If your work touches diffusion LMs, masked or any-order language modeling, parallel decoding, or on-policy learning at the pretrain/post-train boundary, this paper is worth a careful 1.5 to 2.5 hour read.1c2:T831,主结果集中在数学语料。1M 模型几乎都在地板附近，说明模型太小，patching 规则差异还发挥不出来；computed results 只有 3–5% 左右，只有手写 syntax 规则能稍微抬高 final answers。到了 12M，novelty patching 开始明显拉开：final-answer accuracy 71.5%，而 entropy 只有 46.6%，dependence 是 56.7%；computed results 从 entropy 的 5.8% 提到 10.1%。真正显著的是 50M：computed results 达到 57.5%，对比 entropy 的 20.7% 和 dependence 的 35.1%；final answers 达到 89.5%，对比 entropy 的 59.9% 和 dependence 的 78.2%。而且 entropy 在 computed results 上 seed 间波动很大，说明它对这类位置既不稳，也不准。作者还特别检查了训练细节，例如 50M 使用 grad clipping=1.0 对 entropy baseline 基本中性，因此主结论不是由训练稳定性偶然造成。

另一个重要结果是泛化与边界。用原始预训练语料拟合的 novc 仍然保留主要收益，说明这个信号不完全依赖数学特定标签或任务定制。域外测试上，novelty 在 prose 上能降低 bits per byte；在 source code 和 synthetic execution traces 上则大致与 entropy 打平，无论是 bpb 还是 exact token accuracy 都没有明显优势。作者据此给出机制解释：computed results 这类位置的 surprisal 往往并不高，所以 entropy-based patching 会错过；而 novelty 在数学解答里常常恰好在“新结果串开始”的地方升高，因此能把 patch 打在计算结果附近。相反，在代码和执行轨迹里，真正关键的结构不一定表现为“新字节串开始”，所以 novelty 的优势消失。论文还分析了 boundary enrichment——SOMBRERO 一类 learned chunker 优化的指标——发现 entropy 在这个指标上反而最高，但它在 computed results 上最差，这说明 enrichment 这类局部统计目标并不等于对下游推理位置有帮助。作者也提到 learned chunker H-Net 可以自行恢复这类结构，暗示简单启发式和可学习 chunker 之间可能存在互补关系。1c3:T6ff,The proposed method is novelty patching, motivated by LZ77-style compression. If the upcoming bytes can be copied from recent context, they are old information; if they cannot, new information is entering the stream, and that is where a patch should start. Formally, for each position t, m_t is the length of the longest prefix of the future byte stream that appears within the previous 128 bytes, capped at 16. Novelty is defined as -m_t, so shorter matches mean higher novelty. Since m_t depends on future bytes, it cannot be used directly online. The authors therefore build a causal approximation: a lookup table indexed by the previous two bytes, storing the average value of -m_t observed under that context. The table is fit on 4 MB of raw text in seconds on CPU, with backoff to one-byte context and then the global mean for rare contexts. At inference time, patching is just a table lookup plus thresholding to hit a target patch rate.

Several design choices are notable. The method needs no labels, no reference model, and no loss-based ablation signal, making it cheaper than both entropy patching and the earlier dependence-table approach. It changes the routing principle from surprisal-seeking to novelty-seeking. The paper also evaluates two variants: nov, fit on GSM8K and MATH training solutions, and novc, fit on a raw pretraining-corpus sample, to test whether the effect depends on math-specific fitting. Baselines include BLT’s entropy threshold, the prior dependence table, and a hand-written syntax+entropy rule. Models are BLT-style systems trained from scratch with cross-attention pooling, a windowed local decoder, and 128-byte context, at 1M, 12M, and 50M parameters on a 1.9 GB math-heavy corpus, with matched patch rates around 11% and three seeds per setup.1c4:T79b,The main gains appear only once the model is large enough to use the extra global compute effectively. At 1M parameters, all methods are near the floor on computed results, around 3–5%, and only the hand-written syntax rule noticeably improves final answers. At 12M, novelty patching separates clearly: final-answer accuracy reaches 71.5%, versus 46.6% for entropy and 56.7% for dependence; computed-result accuracy rises from 5.8% under entropy to 10.1%. At 50M, the gap becomes large: computed results reach 57.5%, compared with 20.7% for entropy and 35.1% for dependence; final answers reach 89.5%, compared with 59.9% and 78.2%. Entropy also shows high seed variance on computed results, suggesting that it is not just weak but unstable for this failure mode. The paper checks that gradient clipping at 50M is neutral for the entropy baseline, so the result is not an artifact of training stabilization.

Generalization results are mixed in an informative way. The corpus-fitted novelty table, built from raw pretraining text rather than math-solution data, preserves the main gain, which means the signal is not purely task-specific. Outside math, novelty lowers bits per byte on prose, but only ties entropy on source code and synthetic execution traces, both in bpb and exact token accuracy. The mechanism analysis explains why: computed results often have ordinary surprisal, so entropy misses them, while novelty tends to spike where a new result string begins in math solutions. In code and traces, important structure does not align as cleanly with “new literal starts here,” so the advantage disappears. The discussion of boundary enrichment is also useful: the metric optimized by learned chunkers such as SOMBRERO is actually highest for entropy, even though entropy is worst on computed results. That is a strong warning that local chunking metrics can be misaligned with the positions that matter for reasoning-like behavior.1c5:T4bd,Read the introduction first to understand the target claim: high entropy is not the same as high value for global compute. Then go straight to the math results, especially the 12M and 50M settings; the 1M model mostly shows that capacity can hide routing differences. While reading the tables, separate computed-result accuracy from final-answer accuracy. The former directly tests whether patches land near inline results, while the latter shows whether that local routing improvement propagates to end-task behavior. After that, read the novelty definition carefully. It is short, but it explains why the method is so cheap and why it can be fit outside the main training loop. The negative results on prose, code, and traces are worth reading closely because they define the scope of the claim. If your interest is adaptive compute or learned routing, pay attention to the discussion of boundary enrichment and H-Net: it makes clear that the proxy objective used for chunking strongly shapes what structure the model learns to expose. A quick pass takes 20–30 minutes; a deeper read should focus on the novelty-table construction, threshold matching, the baseline design, and the mechanism analysis sections.1c6:T9a3,方法的出发点来自 Anari et al. (2026) 的精确 rejection correction。设 proposal 是把一个 block 内多个 token 按各自条件边缘独立采样得到的分布，target 是该 block 的真实联合条件分布。两者的 likelihood ratio 的对数，可以沿 block 内某个顺序分解成若干 token-level increment 之和；每个 increment 都能通过额外查询 score function 得到。问题在于完整求和要对 block 中每个 token 都查询一次。

SIRS 的关键改动，是不再显式求完整 log acceptance ratio，而是随机抽取一个 increment 来构造其无偏估计。单次估计只需一次查询，因此单个增量的获取成本与 block 大小脱钩。难点在于 rejection sampling 需要的是 acceptance probability，也就是 exp(log-ratio)；对 log-ratio 的无偏估计直接指数化后并不是 acceptance probability 的无偏估计。为此，论文引入 Poissonized Bernoulli factory：先采样一个 Poisson 个数的 clipped increments，再通过 Chen et al. (2026) 的 Bernoulli factory 机制，把这些随机增量组合成一个 [0,1] 内的随机接受概率，其期望恰好等于目标接受率。这样 rejection sampler 的边际输出仍可对准目标分布。

为了保证 Bernoulli factory 的输入可控，作者对 increment 做了区间 [-B, B] clipping。clipping 是 score 精确时唯一的近似来源。B 越大，理论误差越小，但期望查询次数会上升，文中给出每个 unmasking step 的期望查询成本上界为 (1+2B)e^{2B}，与 block size 无关。另一个重要技巧是 Rao-Blackwellization：虽然一次 score 查询是为某个随机选中的 increment 服务，但该查询实际上会返回当前剩余所有 masked 位置的条件分布，因此可以对所有可能的 token-level increment 做条件平均，降低方差而不增加查询成本。理论部分也证明了 Rao-Blackwellized increment 对 clipping-induced error 的上界更紧。

误差分析上，论文把输出分布与数据分布之间的 KL 分解为三部分：proposal 误差、acceptance probability 误差、clipping 误差。若 score function 精确，前两项消失，只剩 clipping 误差。并行独立采样对应 B=0，此时误差就是 block joint 与 marginals product 之间的完整相关性误差；SIRS 则只保留超出 clipping 区间的那部分增量贡献，因此当所有 increment 都落在 [-B,B] 内时可以恢复精确修正。1c7:T9c6,The starting point is the exact rejection correction of Anari et al. (2026). Let the proposal be the product of token-wise conditional marginals used by parallel sampling, and let the target be the true joint conditional distribution over the block. The log likelihood ratio between target and proposal can be decomposed into a sum of token-level increments along an ordering of the block, and each increment can be obtained from the score function. The problem is that evaluating the full sum requires one score query per token.

SIRS replaces the full evaluation with a single randomly sampled increment, yielding an unbiased estimator of the log acceptance ratio at the cost of one query. The main obstacle is that rejection sampling needs the acceptance probability, namely the exponential of that log ratio, and exponentiating an unbiased estimator does not preserve unbiasedness. To handle this, the paper uses a Poissonized Bernoulli factory following Chen et al. (2026): it samples a Poisson number of clipped increments and combines them into a random acceptance probability in [0,1] whose expectation matches the desired acceptance rate. Since rejection sampling only depends on the expected acceptance probability, the marginal output distribution remains correct under the construction.

To make the Bernoulli factory valid and stable, increments are clipped to [-B, B]. With an exact score model, clipping is the only source of approximation. Larger B reduces approximation error but increases query cost; the paper gives an expected per-step query bound of (1+2B)e^{2B}, independent of block size. A practically important refinement is Rao-Blackwellization. One score query returns conditionals for all remaining masked positions, so the sampled increment can be averaged over all eligible token choices at no extra query cost, reducing variance. The theory also shows a tighter clipping-error bound for the Rao-Blackwellized version.

The analysis decomposes the KL divergence between the sampler output and the data distribution into proposal error, acceptance-probability error, and clipping error. When the score function is exact, the first two vanish. Standard parallel sampling is recovered at B=0, where the method keeps the full correlation error between the block joint and the product of marginals. SIRS removes part of that error, leaving only the contribution from increments that exceed the clipping range; if all increments lie within [-B, B], the correction becomes exact.1c8:T4ad,The experimental section is intentionally narrow and theory-driven. The authors evaluate on two discrete systems with exact score functions, an Ising chain and a Pólya urn, where the KL divergence can be computed directly. This isolates the sampling error from model error.

Three findings matter. First, under the same score-query budget, SIRS with the Rao-Blackwellized increment achieves lower KL divergence than standard parallel sampling when within-block dependence is weak. Second, when dependence is strong, SIRS still corrects part of the bias, but the extra rejection and clipping overhead can make it less attractive than simply using smaller parallel blocks; the paper is explicit that small-block parallel sampling may remain cheaper in that regime. Third, Rao-Blackwellization consistently improves the estimator with essentially no extra query cost.

What is missing is also important: there are no large-scale language-model experiments, no end-to-end text generation quality results, and no wall-clock study on realistic MDLM or LLaDA-style systems. So the evidence is strongest on theoretical validity and controlled mechanism tests, not yet on practical large-model deployment.1c9:T641,The model is a dual-view, dual-tower TSLM. The two views are chosen to preserve different aspects of the same signal. One view is a standard line plot, which retains absolute amplitudes, axis ranges, and the observed coordinate frame. This is the view needed for questions grounded in actual measurements. The second view is a normalized delay embedding. Delay embeddings reconstruct a time series as a trajectory in phase space using time-lagged observations, making temporal geometry more explicit. By normalizing this representation before rendering it, the model factors out positive amplitude rescaling and offsets while preserving temporal structure.

Architecturally, the line plot is processed by Qwen3-VL’s native vision encoder initialized from SigLIP-2, while the delay embedding is processed by a separate DINOv3 encoder. This is an important design choice: the authors do not simply concatenate the two images and feed them through a shared visual tower. They allow each view to develop a specialized visual representation before fusion. The resulting features are compressed into a compact token set—230 tokens for the line plot and 64 for the delay embedding—and then concatenated as input to a shared language model. In addition, the model uses DeepStack to inject multi-level visual features into early language-model layers, so the complementary views can interact with language processing beyond a single input projection. The method is therefore less about adding another tower and more about pairing distinct invariance profiles with dedicated encoders and sustained fusion.1ca:T514,The model is built on Qwen3-VL-8B and evaluated on TSRBench, TSExam, and ChatTS. The headline result is 53.2% overall accuracy on TSRBench, compared with 36.7% for the strongest dedicated TSLM baseline reported in the paper, and close to GPT-5 with text-plus-visual input at 55.6%. The more informative comparison is the controlled ablation: under the same training setup, a plot-only variant reaches 45.2%, while adding the delay-embedding view raises performance to 53.2%, an 8.0-point gain. The gains are concentrated in reasoning, prediction, and decision-making, while perception changes little. That pattern supports the paper’s claim that complementary views help higher-level temporal reasoning rather than basic visual extraction.

The invariance experiments are also important. Under positive rescaling and offset shifts, the delay-only model remains nearly unchanged, showing that the normalized delay embedding indeed induces robustness to those transformations. The plot-only model is much more sensitive, which is expected because it preserves the original measurement frame. For a reader interested in modeling rather than benchmark chasing, these intervention results are more valuable than the raw leaderboard numbers because they tie performance back to representation properties.1cb:T6a9,The design has a single-GPU part and a distributed part. On a single GPU, FlashMask-3 builds on the column-wise sparse representation from FlashMask. The mask is indexed by key position, while each key stores query-axis intervals through four boundary vectors, commonly denoted LTS, LTE, UTS, and UTE for lower- and upper-triangular regions. This avoids constructing an n by n mask and gives the kernel a compact representation of valid query-key tiles. The new kernel integrates this representation into FlashAttention-3’s Hopper execution model. It uses three-role warp specialization: a KV Index Generator scans the boundary vectors and produces the relevant tile or KV indices, a KV Loader issues asynchronous TMA loads, and MMA Consumers run WGMMA compute. Mask handling is moved out of the main compute loop into a producer-like stage, which reduces branch overhead and keeps the asynchronous pipeline full. A preemptive persistent-tile scheduler is added to reduce SM-level imbalance under irregular sparse masks. For distributed context parallelism, the key observation is that the mask is keyed by K positions but stores Q-axis intervals. Under any multi-chunk CP assignment, a rank-local mask can be obtained by elementwise clipping, shifting, and max operations over the boundary vectors. No cross-rank mask exchange is needed, and the resulting local representation can be passed to the same kernel. The distributed system then adds a sparsity-aware hierarchical load balancer, HCC-IPO, topology-aware hierarchical routing for forward all-gather, mask-driven communication pruning, and a backward reduce-scatter path overlapped with attention recomputation using bitmask-AMO synchronization.1cc:T4ca,The evaluation covers microbenchmarks, context-parallel scaling, and end-to-end training. On a single H100, across 12 structured masks and sequence lengths from 4K to 128K, FlashMask-3 improves achieved TFLOPs over FlashMask by 45% to 141%, over FlexAttention by 34% to 71%, and over MagiAttention by 2% to 44%. These gains indicate that the improvement is not only from compact mask representation, but also from aligning mask-aware scheduling with Hopper’s TMA/WGMMA pipeline. In distributed context-parallel experiments with CP degrees from 4 to 32 and 8K tokens per device, it reaches 31% to 75% compute-communication overlap efficiency. Throughput improves by 1.80× to 3.71× over Megatron-Core CP ring, by 1.71× to 2.92× over Megatron-Core CP all-gather, and by 1.09× to 1.46× over MagiAttention. The end-to-end result is the most relevant for pretraining: on a 118B-A14B MoE model with 128K context over 128 H100 GPUs and CP degree 16, replacing Dual Chunk balancing and all-gather communication with the FlashMask-3 distributed extension raises training throughput by 7.3% to 11.0%. The smaller end-to-end gain is expected because the full step also includes MoE, MLP, other collectives, and scheduler overhead.1cd:T42e,Read the mask-localization theorem first. The important idea is why a key-indexed representation that stores query intervals can be localized through clip-shift-max operations under arbitrary multi-chunk CP placement. Then read the Hopper kernel section and compare it with FA3 and the original FlashMask: the key implementation idea is the separation of mask scanning into a KV Index Generator role rather than embedding mask branches in the compute loop. The distributed sections on HCC-IPO, communication pruning, and recomputation-overlap are also worth careful reading, because long-context training often fails to scale due to imbalance and communication rather than raw MMA throughput. In the experiments, focus on the 12-mask single-GPU curves, CP-degree scaling, overlap-efficiency numbers, and the 118B-A14B MoE training table. Two questions are worth keeping in mind: which real pretraining masks cannot be expressed by the four-boundary representation, and whether dynamic multimodal packing could make mask construction or scheduling overhead visible again.1ce:Ta7b,方法核心是 Virtual Head Attention。出发点很直接：如果把物理 query heads 数量减半，再把 KV heads 压到 2，理论上可以同时降低 attention 计算和 KV cache；问题在于这样会损失 head diversity。VHA 的做法不是恢复真实的更多 KV heads，而是在 query 侧“造出”虚拟头的差异，并在输出侧补跨组信息交互。

第一部分是 Q Premix。设原始 query heads 为 Hq，压缩后物理 query heads 变成 Hq'，通常是原来的一半；KV heads 固定为 2，因此每个 KV group 会对应更多 query heads。Premix 在每个 KV group 内对 query 做一个接近恒等映射的线性变换，把较少的物理 query heads 扩展成更多“虚拟 query heads”。这里“接近恒等”很关键：如果一开始就做强混合，训练可能不稳定，也容易破坏原有注意力结构；近恒等初始化更像是在 GQA-2 的基础上逐步学出组内头部专门化。作者从训练后矩阵的直接可视化里观察到，Premix 学到的是 group-conditioned query specialization，也就是同组内不同虚拟头会形成有结构的差异，而不是无意义的线性扰动。

第二部分是 Linear Postmix。仅靠组内 Premix 还不够，因为 KV heads 只有 2，跨组的信息通道仍然受限。Postmix 在 attention 输出后施加一个低秩 identity-residual 变换 I + AB^T，其中秩 r 取 Hq'/2，例如 1.7B 模型里 r=4。这个设计的意图是用很小的额外参数和计算，把不同头、不同组之间的特征再融合一次。作者把它解释为 structured low-rank cross-head communication。与 MFA 通过增大 head dimension 来补容量不同，VHA 不去扩大每个头的宽度，而是在头之间做便宜的线性耦合，因此训练和 prefill FLOPs 不会上升，反而因为物理 query heads 减半而下降。

一个很漂亮的工程点是：Premix 和 Postmix 都是纯线性操作，没有非线性，也不依赖 token 位置或上下文状态，因此在推理时可以分别吸收到 WQ 和 WO 中。吸收后，线上模型就是一个标准 GQA-2 结构，完全复用现有 kernel 和 serving 优化，不引入额外 runtime overhead。这一点把它和很多“训练时好看、部署时麻烦”的注意力变体区分开了。

从对比关系看，VHA 与 GQA 的区别是：GQA 直接让更多 query heads 共享同一组 K/V，而 VHA 在共享前后都加了可学习线性补偿；与 MLA 的区别是：VHA 不做 latent KV 压缩，因此避免了 latent bottleneck 带来的质量损失；与 MFA 的区别是：VHA 不通过增大 head dim 来换质量，因此不会显著增加训练和 prefill 计算。1cf:T834,实验覆盖面比较完整。作者在四个基础规模上做了 4K context、50B token 预训练：0.6B、1.7B、4B dense，以及 8B-A1B MoE。结果是 VHA 在所有规模上都超过标准 GQA baseline，提升范围约为 +0.05% 到 +0.81%。这里绝对数值看起来不大，但要注意比较对象已经是很强的 GQA，而且 VHA 同时把 KV cache 压下去了。

以 1.7B 为例，GQA-8 的 KV cache 是每层每 token 4KB（BF16），直接降到 GQA-2 后变成 1KB，但会带来约 1.00% 的质量下降。MLA 的 cache 约 1.12KB，质量在多个尺度上最低。MFA 也能做到 1KB cache，质量接近 GQA-8，但在 1.7B、序列长度 4096 时训练和 prefill FLOPs 增加 49.8%。VHA 则在保持 1KB 级别 cache 的同时，相比 GQA-8 还把训练和 prefill FLOPs 降低了 7.9%，并且质量超过标准 GQA baseline。这正是论文所谓同时改进三角形三个顶点的证据。

更重要的是工业级验证。作者在 30B-A3B MoE、500B token、8K context 的设置下，VHA 在 12 个 base-model benchmark 上比 MLA 高 0.70%，比 GQA-4 高 2.60%。这说明方法在更大模型和更长训练下仍然成立，而不是小模型偶然收益。另一个 matched 10B-A1B MoE 对比把结论延伸到 128K context，在更激进的 KV 压缩下，VHA 仍保持优势。

论文还做了组件消融。结论是 Premix 和 Postmix 缺一不可：只做其中一个，无法补齐双重压缩带来的表达损失。作者还直接检查训练后的 Premix/Postmix 矩阵结构，发现前者呈现组条件化的头专门化，后者呈现低秩但有结构的跨头通信，这让方法不只是经验上有效，也有一定可解释性。

如果从预训练角度看，最值得注意的数字不是单个 benchmark 分，而是：在 50B 到 500B token 的训练规模上，VHA 没有表现出随着规模增大而收益消失；同时它把线上 cache 压到 GQA-2 级别，却没有像纯 GQA-2 或 MLA 那样明显掉质量。这说明它抓住的不是小模型欠拟合补丁，而是 attention 参数化里一个更稳定的自由度。1d0:T8b7,Virtual Head Attention starts from an aggressive compression setting: only 2 KV heads, and only half as many physical query heads as the baseline. This immediately reduces both KV cache and attention compute, but it also removes a large amount of head diversity. VHA restores that diversity through two lightweight linear modules.

The first is Q Premix. Within each KV group, Premix applies a near-identity linear transformation to the reduced set of physical query heads, effectively expanding them into a richer set of virtual query heads. The near-identity design is important. It keeps the model close to a stable GQA-2 parameterization early in training, while allowing the network to gradually learn structured specialization among heads that share the same KV pair. The authors’ matrix inspection suggests that this is exactly what happens: Premix learns group-conditioned query specialization rather than arbitrary mixing.

The second is Linear Postmix. Even with better within-group query diversity, using only 2 KV heads still limits cross-group interaction. Postmix therefore applies a low-rank identity-residual transformation, I + AB^T, to the attention output. The rank is small, for example r = Hq'/2 and r = 4 at the 1.7B scale. This gives the model a cheap way to fuse information across heads and groups after attention, without increasing head dimension or introducing nonlinear runtime structure. The paper interprets this as structured low-rank cross-head communication.

A major engineering advantage is that both modules are purely linear. Premix can be folded into the query projection matrix WQ, and Postmix into the output projection WO at inference time. After folding, the deployed model is just a standard GQA-2 model. This means VHA inherits existing inference kernels and serving optimizations from frameworks such as vLLM and SGLang with zero additional runtime overhead.

Relative to prior methods, the distinctions are clean. Compared with standard GQA, VHA adds learnable compensation before and after shared-KV attention. Compared with MLA, it avoids a latent KV bottleneck. Compared with MFA, it does not increase head dimension and therefore avoids the large training/prefill FLOP increase.1d1:T705,The paper reports matched pretraining experiments at four scales under 4K context and 50B tokens: 0.6B, 1.7B, 4B dense, and 8B-A1B MoE. VHA consistently outperforms the standard GQA baseline at every scale, with gains ranging from about +0.05% to +0.81%. The absolute gains are modest, but the comparison is against already strong baselines while simultaneously reducing cache and compute.

The 1.7B case is especially informative. GQA-8 uses 4 KB of KV cache per layer per token in BF16. GQA-2 reduces that to 1 KB, but causes roughly a 1.00% quality drop. MLA reaches about 1.12 KB cache but gives the weakest quality among the compared methods. MFA also reaches 1 KB cache and gets close to GQA-8 quality, but increases training and prefill FLOPs by 49.8% at sequence length 4096. VHA keeps the cache at the compressed level, lowers training and prefill FLOPs by 7.9% relative to GQA-8, and still beats the standard GQA baseline in quality.

The industrial-scale result is even more important. On a 30B-A3B MoE model trained on 500B tokens with 8K context, VHA outperforms MLA by 0.70% and GQA-4 by 2.60% on a 12-benchmark base-model suite. A separate matched 10B-A1B MoE comparison extends the advantage to 128K context under more aggressive KV compression. This suggests the method scales in both model size and context length.

The component ablations show that neither Premix nor Postmix alone is sufficient. The matrix analyses are also useful: Premix learns structured specialization within KV groups, while Postmix learns low-rank but nontrivial cross-head communication. From a pretraining perspective, the key takeaway is that the gains do not disappear as training scale increases from 50B to 500B tokens, which makes the method more credible than a small-scale optimization artifact.1d2:T690,Read the paper in four passes. First, study the introduction carefully. The quantitative framing of the “impossible triangle” is essential: GQA-8 has strong quality but large cache, GQA-2 is cheap but weak, MLA compresses but loses quality, and MFA recovers quality at a large compute cost. Without that baseline map, the value of VHA is easy to underestimate.

Second, read the method section closely. Focus on how Q Premix is parameterized, why it is near-identity, and how it reconstructs virtual head diversity from fewer physical query heads. Then examine Linear Postmix and its low-rank identity-residual form. The important design question is not just what these modules do, but why they are placed before attention on queries and after attention on outputs, and why they are kept strictly linear. The answer is deployment: only this design can be folded into standard GQA weights with no inference overhead.

Third, inspect the main result tables, especially the 1.7B and 30B-A3B comparisons. The 1.7B setup makes the cache/FLOP/quality trade-off concrete. The 30B-A3B result tells you whether the method survives industrial-scale training. Also check the 128K long-context evaluation to verify that the advantage is not limited to short context.

Finally, read the ablations and matrix visualizations. These sections explain what Premix and Postmix are each compensating for, and whether the learned transformations have stable structure rather than acting as arbitrary extra parameters. If you are considering implementation or adaptation, pay attention to the appendix details on FLOP accounting, head configurations at different scales, and the exact MoE settings.1d3:T537,The method compresses generation in fixed 512-token blocks. After a block is completed, learned pause tokens attend to that block and store a summary in their own KV entries. These pause tokens do not emit output tokens. Once their KV entries are written, the original block cache is freed, and later tokens attend to the pause-token code rows instead. The training objective remains next-token prediction, so future prediction loss teaches the code rows what information to preserve. Three design choices are central. First, the code rows are assigned positions inside the block they replace, rather than being appended after it; this keeps the positional geometry closer to the original history under positional embeddings. Second, cache budget is allocated across layers according to measured value, instead of using a uniform per-layer budget. Third, compression is performed over relatively large blocks, reducing repeated lossy compression and overhead. Compared with LightThinker or Breadcrumbs-style memory-token compression, the contribution is not just adding learned memory tokens, but making them work in long competition-math generations through position, layer-budget, and block-size design. Compared with text-summary methods such as MEMENTO, it avoids an external annotation pipeline for writing and refining summaries.1d4:T419,The experiments cover Qwen3 models from 0.6B to 14B, with detailed results on Qwen3-8B-Base and post-trained Qwen3-8B. With Fisher-selected secondary planes, 2.16 bpw improves to perplexity 9.30, zero-shot 65.9, and MMLU 62.8. On the post-trained Qwen3-8B, 1.99 bpw surpasses CAT-Q on all three reported measures while using 0.28 more bpw. At 14B, RoleQ lifts MMLU from 25.4 with per-output-channel scales to 38.5. Fisher selection for the second plane beats random by 6.2 MMLU points and Hessian × weight by 9.0 points on the post-trained 8B setting.1d5:T4ab,The key idea is to rewrite attention statistics so they can be accumulated or recovered within FlashAttention’s computation path.
- The paper distinguishes statistics (per-head quantities returned by kernels) from features (host-side aggregations used by a classifier).
- Using FlashAttention’s online softmax state (running max m, normalizer ℓ, accumulated output O) and the stored LSE, it classifies statistics into four exact computation tiers:
  (1) accumulate inside the tiled pass with bounded state (near-free),
  (2) a fixed number of post-pass sparse lookups by re-evaluating a few scores and recovering weights via LSE,
  (3) a second tiled pass over scores (still avoiding dense materialization),
  (4) statistics that truly require dense materialization.
- Implementation: Triton kernels extending FlashAttention-2 forward to emit the statistics needed by five published detectors (Lookback Lens, LLM-Check, RAUQ, INTRYGUE, SinkProbe), packaged as an attention backend for integration.
The design trade-off is explicit: keep statistics exact, prioritize tier (1)/(2) for common detectors, and offer tier (3) as a controlled extra pass rather than falling back to O(L^2) memory.1d6:T7e1,方法从注意力输出扰动的精确表达式出发。对给定 query q，完整 cache 下的注意力输出是 a=Σ_i p_i v_i。若删去索引集合 J，对应输出变成 a_-J，扰动是 Δ(J)=a_-J-a。作者先写出这个扰动与被删 token 的总注意力质量 P_J 以及 value residual 的关系。单 token 情况下有一个很直观的式子：Δ({j}) = p_j/(1-p_j) · (a - v_j)。这说明删一个 token 的影响不只取决于它的 attention weight p_j，也取决于它的 value 向量和当前输出 a 的偏差。如果 v_j 很接近 a，即便 attention 不低，删掉它也未必伤害大；反过来，一个 attention 中等但方向独特的 value 可能更关键。

难点在于多 token 联合删除时，最优集合选择是组合问题。DropKV 的核心是 decoupling：把联合扰动最小化近似成独立的 per-token 评分，再按分数保留或删除。论文里称之为 Decoupled Residual-Output Perturbation。直观上，它用单 token 扰动代理多 token 选择，把原本互相耦合的决策拆开，从而把复杂度降到线性级别。作者进一步给出 near-optimality 保证：在 cone condition 下，这个 decoupled proxy 与原 NP-hard 最优解只差一个常数因子。这里的 cone condition 可以理解为被选 value residual 在几何上不会严重相互抵消，方向大致处于同一锥体内。这个条件不是纯理论摆设，作者在 Llama-3.1-8B、Mistral-7B-512K、Qwen2.5-7B-1M 上做了经验验证。

工程实现上，DropKV 的另一个重点是 kernelization。很多 query-aware 或 output-aware 方法理论上合理，但需要显式构造大 attention matrix，prefill 阶段内存开销很大。作者用 fused Triton kernels 在线计算 eviction scores，避免 materialize attention matrix，把 128K 长度下 scoring kernel 的 scratch memory 从约 9GB 压到约 17MB。这个量级差异很关键，因为它决定方法能否在真实长上下文服务里启用，而不是只在离线实验里成立。1d7:T87b,The method starts from the exact perturbation of the attention output. For a query q, the full-cache attention output is a = Σ_i p_i v_i. If a set J of tokens is evicted, the new output is a_-J and the shift is Δ(J) = a_-J - a. The paper derives how this perturbation depends on the total removed attention mass P_J and on value residuals relative to the original output. The single-token case is especially revealing: Δ({j}) = p_j / (1 - p_j) · (a - v_j). This immediately shows why attention-only scoring is incomplete. A token can have nontrivial attention but still be safe to remove if its value is close to the current output; conversely, a token with moderate attention can be important if its value points in a distinctive direction.

The hard part is multi-token selection, which is combinatorial. DropKV’s main idea is decoupling: replace the joint optimization over eviction sets with independent per-token perturbation scores. The paper calls this Decoupled Residual-Output Perturbation. Intuitively, it uses single-token perturbation as a proxy for the multi-token objective, breaking the coupling between decisions and reducing the complexity to linear time. The authors then prove a near-optimality result: under a cone condition, the decoupled proxy matches the NP-hard optimum up to a constant multiplicative factor. The cone condition roughly says that the relevant residual vectors do not cancel each other arbitrarily and lie within a bounded geometric cone. Importantly, the paper does not leave this as a purely formal assumption; it empirically checks the condition on Llama-3.1-8B, Mistral-7B-512K, and Qwen2.5-7B-1M.

The implementation side is equally important. Many query-aware or output-aware methods require materializing large attention matrices, which makes prefill expensive. DropKV uses fused Triton kernels to compute eviction scores on the fly, avoiding attention-matrix materialization. At sequence length 128K, this reduces scoring-kernel scratch memory from about 9 GB to about 17 MB. That difference is large enough to determine whether a method is usable in real long-context serving rather than only in offline experiments.1d8:T53c,The experiments cover three long-context models: Llama-3.1-8B, Mistral-7B-512K, and Qwen2.5-7B-1M. The main benchmarks are RULER and LongBench, with cache budgets of 5% and 10%, which are fairly aggressive compression settings. The headline result is that DropKV achieves the best accuracy among both query-aware and output-aware eviction baselines while also delivering the lowest latency. More notably, in matched-batch prefill it is reported to be faster than the dynamic-cache baseline, which suggests the method is not merely trading quality for speed; the kernel design is removing a real prefill bottleneck.

The most striking engineering number is the memory reduction: at n = 128K, scratch memory for score computation drops from roughly 9 GB to roughly 17 MB. The paper also empirically validates the cone condition to support the relevance of its approximation guarantee on real models.

When reading the experiments closely, three comparisons matter most. First, compare against attention-only methods to see where value-aware scoring helps most. Second, compare against more complex output-perturbation baselines to separate gains from the proxy itself versus gains from better implementation. Third, inspect the degradation curves across cache budgets to judge whether the method remains stable under very low retention rates.1d9:T46c,A good way to read this paper is formula first, approximation second, implementation third. Start with the perturbation derivation in the method section, especially the single-token formula; that is the key intuition for the whole paper. Then read the decoupling argument and the approximation guarantee to understand what is being approximated, what interactions are discarded, and why the resulting score is tractable. Even if you are not theory-focused, read the explanation and empirical validation of the cone condition; otherwise it is hard to judge where the guarantee applies. Finally, read the Triton-kernel section and the latency/memory tables, because much of the paper’s practical value comes from implementation.

If you only have 20 minutes, read the introduction, the derivation around the main theorem, the main benchmark table, and the scratch-memory comparison. For a deeper pass, two questions are worth probing: whether per-token decoupling introduces systematic bias across heads, layers, or query distributions, and how easily the method composes with quantization, paged KV caches, or speculative decoding.1da:T72b,RoLaQ combines rotation learning and range calibration. The starting point is an error analysis: if the dequantized latent differs from the original by e, then the induced key and value projection errors are governed by quadratic forms involving W_K and W_V. The authors trace-normalize the two projection energies and sum them into a joint matrix H, which measures how sensitive each latent direction is to shared K/V distortion. Empirically, the leading half of H's eigenvectors captures 62% to 75% of the projection energy across models and layers, so RoLaQ restricts rotation learning to a compact subspace defined by this joint geometry rather than searching over the full latent space.

The second ingredient is coupled threshold-gain learning. RoLaQ does not keep the quantizer range fixed while only optimizing the rotation. Instead, it jointly learns a per-layer threshold whose value also determines the reconstruction gain. This matters because at 2 bits, the rotation changes the latent distribution seen by the quantizer, while the quantization boundaries and dequantization scale jointly determine the effective reconstruction response. Optimizing only one side leaves a mismatch between assignment and readout behavior.

Training uses frozen model weights. Supervision comes from two sources: a prediction-level KL to a BF16 teacher over next-token distributions, and an attention-output reconstruction loss that directly constrains layerwise attention outputs. The latter is important because final-logit supervision alone can hide harmful intermediate distortions. On the systems side, the serving implementation packs the latent cache into INT2, fuses cache writes, optimizes the attention path, and absorbs the read-side rotation into MLA projections so that inference does not pay an extra standalone rotation cost.1db:T618,The evaluation covers three MLA models: DeepSeek-V2-Lite, Moonlight-16B-A3B, and MiniCPM3-4B, across six benchmarks. The main result is that RoLaQ achieves the best average accuracy among compared 2-bit methods both with and without token protection. Without token protection, it improves over the strongest baseline by 1.1 to 3.8 points on average, which is a meaningful gain at this compression level.

The long-context result is also important. On RULER retrieval at 8K and 16K, the gains persist beyond the 4K calibration context, suggesting that the method is not merely overfitting a short calibration window but is improving the underlying quantization geometry.

The serving numbers are strong for the target setting. On DeepSeek-V2-Lite with a 256K input on a single A100 80GB, the packed 2-bit cache reaches 3.96x the BF16 cache capacity at the same memory budget and 2.51x decode throughput, while also reducing first-token tail latency. Calibration itself takes about 30 minutes on one A100, so the offline cost is modest.

The ablations are the most informative part. Rotation-only and range-only variants both underperform joint optimization, supporting the claim that error direction and reconstruction scale must be calibrated together. The K/V-guided subspace outperforms less structured rotation search, which validates the MLA-specific geometry argument. Adding attention-output supervision improves stability and quality over using prediction KL alone, especially in the 2-bit regime where intermediate-layer distortions accumulate quickly.1dc:T485,The main setup uses a frozen Qwen2.5-1.5B receiver with 28 layers and grouped-query attention with group size 6. The sender reads a passage containing the answer; the receiver sees the same passage with the answer masked plus the question; the system is scored by whether greedy decoding over eight tokens contains the answer. The reported run uses n=200 items. Two anchors define the scale: the masked native cache gives 0.180 accuracy, and the receiver’s own unmasked native cache gives 0.665. When the receiver’s cache is perturbed, accuracy is already at the floor at cosine 0.9999, drops to 0.120 at cosine 0.999, and falls to 0.005 at cosine 0.995. First, the paper introduces a simple cost model for remote KV hits. It uses per-token KV size s and GPU prefill rate R to define a break-even bandwidth B*=sR, plus a fixed per-hit overhead T0. The interpretation is straightforward: if the effective remote-tier bandwidth and fixed latency do not clear that threshold, a cache hit is not worth taking. Second, the authors redesign KV storage for PCP with MLA. In the original LMCache setup, only worker 0 stores and loads MLA KV because tensor-parallel ranks hold the same latent KV. Under PCP, however, all ranks advance in lockstep, so concentrating remote I/O on one rank creates a bottleneck. The paper replaces this with a sharded MLA KV store, where chunk storage, lookup, and loading are statically partitioned by rank. Rank r of every engine talks to its own server instance, which avoids extra cluster protocols and client-side hashing while preserving cross-engine reuse. The paper also proves that the scheduler’s existing minimum-over-ranks lookup still returns the longest cached prefix. Third, the execution path is repaired. Synchronous loading is replaced with asynchronous loading so that hit processing no longer blocks the engine step. The authors also fix three client bugs, including a lost-completion race and a missing-key read that could stall indefinitely, and add regression tests. The key idea is not an API trick but moving remote-hit handling off the blocking critical path while keeping the load protocol compatible with collectives: every rank issues the same collectives, avoiding deadlocks and inconsistency.1de:T4de,The experiments are the strongest part of the paper because they are driven by production trace replay rather than only synthetic microbenchmarks. In the original deployment, enabling remote L2 increased p99 TTFT for 16k prompts from 3.96s to 17.3s, and for 32k prompts from 6.06s to 25.0s, while median latency stayed roughly unchanged. Isolated replay shows why: a 16k prompt takes 0.31s to recompute but 0.88s to load from L2. On the same B300 node, GPU prefill runs at about 52.2k tokens/s, so the remote path is simply too slow. The queueing effect is even more important. Under a hit-heavy synchronous workload, once arrival rate times per-hit service time exceeds one, the engine becomes unstable: median latency grows from 3.52s to 52.30s within six minutes while GPU utilization is only 7%, showing that the bottleneck is entirely outside compute. After the fixes, p99 on a hit-heavy production trace drops from 83.32s to 0.67s, a 124x reduction, with 98.5% of prompt tokens served from L2. The cost model is also validated on configurations not used for fitting, which makes it more than a one-off explanation.1df:T442,RoPERelay takes a selector-produced sparse KV cache and the source positions of the retained states. It sorts retained states by their original chronological order and assigns compact, order-preserving RoPE coordinates, removing the gaps created by evicted tokens. Since cached keys already include RoPE phase at the original positions, the method applies an inverse rotation to remove the old phase and then re-rotates each key at its new compact coordinate. This directly edits the selected cache keys and avoids rerunning the historical context. For layers and physical KV heads with different retained lengths, RoPERelay aligns their endpoints using the maximum retained length M, so the current question and subsequent generation start from a shared positional boundary. This is better than starting every head at zero, which would create inconsistent distances from different heads to the current query. The method also separates membership from organization: selector scores decide which states to keep, while source order decides the positional order in which those states are read.1e0:T75f,The main contribution is not a new model but a unified benchmark and protocol. System1-Arena represents each static example or environment step as a decision request r=(s,Q). The state s is a small set of named text fields, such as a message, a code diff, or a rendered webpage. Q is a set of typed questions over the same state. Questions are boolean, choice, or score. Each question includes instructions, and each option includes a description, so models do not rely on dataset-specific prompting. The output is a probability distribution over options for each question, not free-form text.

Several design choices matter. First, the interface is shared across model families. Dedicated System-1 models, autoregressive LLMs, and even diffusion LMs are all mapped into the same probability-based API. For open autoregressive and diffusion models, the authors provide a method to derive decision probabilities from answer tokens, which is important because it makes otherwise incompatible model families comparable. Second, the benchmark evaluates not only accuracy but also Brier score, since calibrated probabilities are central for thresholding, escalation, and risk-sensitive deployment. Third, it includes closed-loop environments and a real-time protocol in which the environment continues to evolve during inference according to each model’s measured latency. That turns latency from a side metric into part of the task definition.

The benchmark is broad: 92,125 typed questions across 105 tasks from 268 public sources in 16 domains, plus 138 closed-loop environments from 18 families, including web shopping, SWE-style coding control, robotics, games, and driving. This is not just a bundle of existing classification datasets. The benchmark standardizes instructions, option semantics, label sources, and environment feedback into a common probabilistic decision framework.1e1:T7e5,The evaluation covers 30 models: 7 closed LLMs, 13 open LLMs, and 10 System-1 models. The paper reports Jev at roughly $0.05 per 1,000 requests, which highlights the practical advantage of specialized decision models for high-throughput workloads.

The gains are task-dependent. The gap between strong System-1 models and the best LLMs is smallest on filtering, grouping, ranking, retrieval, and dialogue tasks. System-1 models remain weaker on knowledge and forecasting tasks. That pattern suggests that single-pass decision models are well suited to local discrimination and structured selection, but less suited to tasks that require broader knowledge integration or implicit multi-step reasoning.

数据设计上，FEB-30 包含 30 条 fact-evolution trajectories，覆盖 6 个诊断类别和 3 个难度等级。6 个类别分别对应外在 QA 评测看不清的不同失败模式：
1. C1 LLM Compensation：memory 状态错了，但模型仍可能答对。
2. C2 Retrieval Bottleneck：memory 对了，但 retrieval 因词汇不匹配或抽象层级差异而失败。
3. C3 Classification Accuracy：系统是否正确判断新观察是 create、update、reinforce 还是 conflict。
4. C4 Synthesis Quality：多来源观察是否被正确合并成事实，哪些该合并，哪些应分开。
5. C5 Temporal Correctness：事实随时间演化、撤回、漂移时，memory state 是否保持正确时序。
6. C6 Multi-Author Attribution：不同作者来源对 corroboration、冲突处理、置信度整合的影响是否被正确建模。

难度上，L1 接近表面匹配，目标 claim 几乎原文出现；L2 把 claim 埋进更真实的文档上下文；L3 则要求从多句组合中推断，并加入较多干扰内容。

这篇工作的关键创新不是类别枚举，而是数据生成范式。作者采用 paradigm inversion：不是先收集文档再人工标注事实，而是先定义每条 trajectory 在每个 state 应该有哪些 atomic claims、如何演化，再据此生成文档。这样 ground truth 从一开始就是确定的。文中还提到 multi-model rotation 和 3-judge verification，用来控制生成文档质量与事实一致性，减少单模型模板化偏差。

评测上，作者把 intrinsic 和 extrinsic 两套指标并列。intrinsic evaluation 直接比较 memory store 内容与该阶段真值，指标包括 claim coverage、update detection、false update rate 等；extrinsic evaluation 则仍保留 QA accuracy。这样可以把“存错了”“没取到”“答错了”拆开看。论文的立场不是用 intrinsic 替代 extrinsic，而是把它作为 memory 组件的单元测试，与端到端 QA 形成互补。1e6:T8ac,The paper introduces FEB-30, a benchmark for fact evolution in agent memory, together with an intrinsic scoring framework.

FEB-30 contains 30 fact-evolution trajectories spanning 6 diagnostic categories and 3 difficulty levels. The categories are designed to isolate failure modes that extrinsic QA-based evaluation cannot disentangle:
1. C1, LLM Compensation: the memory state is wrong, but the model may still answer correctly.
2. C2, Retrieval Bottleneck: the memory state is correct, but retrieval fails because of lexical mismatch or abstraction mismatch.
3. C3, Classification Accuracy: whether the system correctly classifies observations as create, update, reinforce, or conflict.
4. C4, Synthesis Quality: whether evidence from multiple artifacts is merged into the right fact structure.
5. C5, Temporal Correctness: whether the memory state tracks temporal evolution, retraction, and drift correctly.
6. C6, Multi-Author Attribution: whether source identity is handled correctly in corroboration, conflict handling, and confidence updates.

Difficulty is controlled in a structured way. L1 is close to surface matching, with target claims appearing almost verbatim. L2 embeds claims in more realistic document context. L3 requires inference from multiple statements and includes substantial distractor content.

The most important design choice is what the authors call paradigm inversion. Instead of starting from documents and then annotating facts, they first define the exact atomic claims that should hold at each state of a trajectory, then generate documents from those trajectories. This makes the ground truth deterministic from the start. The pipeline also uses multi-model rotation and three-judge verification to reduce generator-specific artifacts and improve factual consistency.

Evaluation is split into intrinsic and extrinsic metrics. Intrinsic evaluation directly compares the memory store against the state-specific ground truth, using metrics such as claim coverage, update detection, and false update rate. Extrinsic evaluation keeps the usual QA accuracy. The point is not to replace end-to-end evaluation, but to complement it with a unit-test-like view of the memory component itself.1e7:T5bf,The central empirical result is straightforward: intrinsic and extrinsic evaluations diverge substantially. The paper reports an average gap of 16 percentage points, and 44% of trajectories show what the authors consider a meaningful divergence. This is the main evidence that QA accuracy alone is not a reliable measure of memory quality.

By construction, C1 and C2 are the clearest demonstrations of the problem. C1 produces cases where systems answer correctly despite broken memory. C2 produces cases where memory is correct but the final answer is wrong because retrieval fails. Categories C3 through C6 are more diagnostic of internal memory-pipeline behavior, including update classification, synthesis, temporal consistency, and source attribution. Two systems with similar QA scores can therefore have very different internal memory quality.

The provided material does not include the full system comparison tables, per-category scores, or judge agreement details. But the experimental goal is clear: not to rank systems by one aggregate score, but to show that intrinsic and extrinsic evaluation measure different things. A careful reader should verify three aspects in the full paper: the protocol for aligning memory-store contents with claim-level ground truth, the robustness of the document-generation and verification pipeline, and whether the category-specific error patterns are genuinely diagnostic rather than just reflecting overall model strength.1e8:T623,The contribution is a benchmark design, not a new model. The provided excerpt does not include the full leaderboard or all breakdowns, but it is already clear that current models remain weak at long-horizon scientific judgment.1ee:T8c4,The core system is a multi-agent synthesis engine called Data World. A world is formalized as a four-tuple: dependency skeleton G, canonical state X, observed environment E, and recomputable phenomena I. G is a DAG whose nodes are variable clusters and whose edges encode generative relations such as monotonic, threshold, saturation, lagged, or interaction effects. This is not just a graph template; the edge annotations define how the world is generated. X is the latent canonical state, the objective world state that actually governs the phenomena of interest. E is produced by an observation map O that projects X into analyst-visible artifacts such as CSVs, spreadsheets, and logs, with imperfect observability, aggregation, missingness, and noise. I contains target phenomena that can be recomputed and checked from the generated world and, crucially, are intended to remain recoverable from E.

A key design choice is the staged multi-agent pipeline. Separate agent sessions handle world specification, state generation, file projection, task and rubric synthesis, and auditing, while exchanging read-only artifacts. This is meant to preserve consistency without letting later stages directly exploit hidden latent variables. The auditor is central: it verifies both that the intended relationships were instantiated and that the target phenomena remain recoverable from imperfect observations. That addresses two common failure modes in synthetic environments: latent mechanisms that disappear after projection, and tasks that become trivial because the signal is too directly exposed.

Task generation is paired with fine-grained rubrics rather than single gold answers. The rubrics distinguish correct computation from correct analytical insight and evidence use. This gives structured rewards for evaluation and RL. The training setup is world-disjoint, so train and test tasks come from disjoint worlds rather than different prompts over the same latent template. The paper then uses these rubric rewards for RL-zero training, without distilling trajectories from stronger teacher models, to produce DataWorld-35B-A3B. That makes the work especially relevant to current interest in verifier- or environment-based training signals.1ef:T647,The engine produces two main assets. - SWE-at-Scale: directly generates bug-inducing patches from correct code.
- SWE-at-Scale+: additionally learns explicit natural-language bug patterns describing how to modify code to induce a bug, then realizes the patch from the pattern—aiming for more explicit, controllable bug logic at the cost of a harder generation problem.

The paper defines an access path as any transformation or recovery mechanism that changes how the same targeted information is queried or extracted while keeping the underlying information approximately fixed. Cross-lingual querying is chosen because it is a clean instance of this idea: semantics are largely preserved while surface form changes substantially.

The experiments use cTOFU, a multilingual extension of TOFU, with parallel synthetic factual associations in English, Chinese, Hindi, Italian, and Spanish, plus romanized Hindi and Chinese. The original forget/retain partitions are preserved. The study focuses on one-to-one unlearning: unlearn in one language, evaluate in another. The contribution is therefore not a new training recipe but a reframing of what unlearning evaluation should claim. Standard metrics such as Truth Ratio, KS-test-based forget quality, and utility preservation can show distribution-specific behavioral change, but they do not by themselves support a privacy claim. The paper argues that privacy-oriented evaluation should ask whether forgetting survives alternative access paths.1f3:T41c,From the provided full text, the empirical study uses the 10% forget split in cTOFU and evaluates with TOFU-style forget-quality and normalized model-utility metrics. The main result is qualitative but important: conclusions about unlearning success change when the same information is queried through different languages or scripts. A model family may look successfully unlearned under one language-specific evaluation and still reveal the same information under another language or romanized script. That means monolingual evaluation can materially overestimate forgetting strength.

The paper also makes three broader empirical points. First, this is observed across multiple multilingual model families rather than a single isolated model. Second, the gap appears not only across languages but also across script variants, which is useful because it keeps semantics even more tightly controlled. Third, utility preservation is orthogonal to privacy: retaining general capability does not imply that the targeted information has become inaccessible.1f4:T433,ViSiP-Bench builds rare-but-real cases where visual evidence conflicts with likely language priors. - Offline: For each criterion judgment, URW queries the same verifier using a fixed pool of paraphrased judgment templates. Template-to-template variability provides a soft uncertainty proxy even under deterministic decoding. Using a small calibration set with gold labels, URW measures how this soft signal correlates with correctness.
- Online: For each new criterion, URW converts the soft signal into a split-conformal p-value, and uses that p-value directly as the aggregation weight for the criterion in a weighted-sum rubric score.
The key design choice is conformal calibration: it yields distribution-free coverage control, framed here as controlling the probability of assigning spuriously low weight to a correct judgment. Compared to prior work, URW is criterion-level (not only response-level), training-free (no uncertainty head/probe), and compatible with single-verifier, zero-temperature deployments (unlike sampling-based consistency or committee methods).1f6:T447,For pretraining research, this is a useful idea paper rather than a must-read. Its main contribution is a practical alternative to explicit paired cross-modal supervision: use text as an intermediate semantic space, rely on pretrained contrastive encoders for cross-modal priors, and learn bridge modules that map proxy descriptions into representations consumable by the language model. This matters because in many realistic settings, single-modality or modality-text data are abundant, while high-quality jointly sampled non-text data are the real bottleneck. The paper is also careful about its claim: MSP does not remove cross-modal priors altogether. It still depends on CLIP/CLAP-like encoders and modality-text supervision. So the reduction is in the need for real paired non-text supervision, not in the need for pretrained cross-modal structure. For native multimodal pretraining, the key takeaway is that text-mediated alignment may be sufficient for some forms of modality composition, though likely more at the semantic level than at fine-grained temporal or spatial correspondence.1f7:T646,The method has four components: frozen modality encoders, modality-specific projectors, text-to-modality bridges, and a language model. The encoders are pretrained contrastive models, such as CLIP-like vision encoders and CLAP-like audio encoders. Training proceeds in two stages. Stage one is per-modality projector training, where standard modality-text data are used to train projectors so that each modality can be mapped into a shared language embedding space. Stage two is self-play composition training, which is the core idea. Given one observed modality, say an image, the system generates proxy text for an unseen modality, for example a textual description of what the corresponding audio might contain. This proxy text is encoded by a pretrained text encoder and then passed through a bridge plus an MLP projector to produce a representation in the shared language space. During training, the model sees the real observed modality together with the proxy-derived representation of the missing modality, but never the true image-audio pair. The goal is not to reconstruct the unseen modality exactly. The goal is to provide a stable semantic anchor that lets the model learn how to combine modalities in the shared space. Compared with approaches based on shared encoders or modular concatenation, MSP explicitly uses text as the bridge and adds a learned calibration layer to correct the mismatch between proxy-text embeddings and real modality embeddings. That calibration is important because raw text-encoder outputs do not naturally follow the same distribution as actual modality features.1f8:T601,The main experimental setting is strong and clean: no real audio-vision pairs are used in training, only image-text and audio-text supervision, while evaluation requires joint multimodal reasoning. The paper reports competitive and in some cases leading results on standard multimodal benchmarks, supporting the claim that zero-shot modality composition can emerge. The most informative findings are in the ablations rather than in any single leaderboard number. First, removing the learned bridge weakens alignment between proxy-derived embeddings and real modality representations, and multimodal reasoning performance drops accordingly. Second, proxy quality matters: if the generated proxy text is vague or semantically unstable, the model tends to fall back to single-modality reasoning or language priors. Third, the method benefits heavily from the pretrained contrastive encoders, which means MSP is better understood as composition learning on top of existing cross-modal geometry rather than fully unsupervised multimodal grounding. Since the prompt does not include the full result tables, the most important things to verify in the paper are the training data scale, the exact encoders used, the language model size, the gap to paired-data baselines on each benchmark, and the size of the bridge/proxy ablation effects. If the gap to paired supervision is small, the method is more broadly interesting; if it is large, the approach is likely better suited to coarse semantic composition than tightly coupled perception tasks.1f9:T4c9,The method casts three spatial output types as classification over candidate sets. Multiple-choice spatial relations are already finite. Numerical prediction is handled by discretizing a range into bins. Point prediction is handled by discretizing the image into regions. The model encodes the observation, question, and candidate descriptions, then uses the final attention layer’s pretrained query and key projections to score candidates, followed by a softmax. No extra prediction head or trainable readout parameters are added. To keep the candidate set manageable, scalar prediction uses up to two refinement stages, while single-point prediction uses three stages. For point prediction, the selected region is cropped and re-encoded in later stages to recover local visual detail. Multi-point prediction is handled by conditional tree expansion using the same trained point predictor. During training, the multi-stage supervision is packed into one teacher-forced causal forward pass, and stage losses are averaged per question so that multi-stage examples do not dominate the objective. The training system also uses global length grouping and cross-GPU load balancing to reduce padding waste and workload imbalance.1fa:T610,FeaTok has two main components. First, it replaces pixel reconstruction as the training signal for the discrete representation with feature reconstruction. The paper studies several feature sources, including SigLIP, SigLIP2, DINOv2, and DINOv3. The important point is not that feature losses are added on top of pixel losses, but that feature-space supervision becomes the primary and exclusive signal for shaping the encoder and codebook. Second, image rendering is explicitly decoupled from representation learning. A separate image decoder is still trained to reconstruct pixels from the discrete tokens, but the tokens are detached before entering this renderer. Pixel losses therefore improve visual reconstruction without pulling the tokenizer back toward pixel-friendly but generator-unfriendly representations. This gives the autoregressive generator image-level context and improves spatial coherence and layout. The deepest idea in the paper is the operationalization of generative learnability as a tokenizer design target.1fd:Ta01,方法从 KL-regularized policy optimization 的对偶结构出发。给定参考策略和温度参数，存在一个 Gibbs 形式的目标策略，使得“奖励减去相对参考策略的 KL 代价”在目标分布支持上呈常数。GGPO不去显式估计这个 Gibbs policy，也不做 importance weighting，而是利用同一 prompt 下 behavior policy 采到的一组响应，比较这些响应的 KL-adjusted reward 是否已经接近这种“常数化”条件。具体目标是最小化组内 KL-adjusted reward 的 log-mean-exp contrast。直观上，它不是像 AGRO 那样压缩 adjusted reward 的方差，也不是像 GRPO 那样直接做组内相对优势更新，而是在组内构造一个对高 adjusted-reward 响应更敏感、同时保持平滑性的对比目标。论文强调两个层面。
第一，on-policy 时，这个 population loss 恰好等于 KL-regularized optimality gap，也就是离正则化最优策略还有多远；这给了目标函数很干净的解释。第二，off-policy 时，不再追求无偏估计这个 population quantity，而是直接证明：在 coverage 条件下，有限组上的 raw loss 可以上界 learner 单次采样 reward 与 behavior best-of-K reward 之间的差距，外加若干显式项，包括正则项、reference-behavior mismatch、组大小和有限样本误差。这个思路和传统 off-policy 校正不同，它绕开了“先把 off-policy 目标估准，再优化”的路线，而是直接把训练时可观测的组损失和最终 reward benchmark 连起来。
论文还分析了 periodic reference refresh。固定 reference 时，Gibbs target 是固定的；如果周期性把 reference 刷新到当前 learner，目标会随轮次移动。作者证明：若每一轮都精确拟合对应的 Gibbs target，那么做 T 轮、每轮温度 β 的 refresh，等价于对初始 reference 做一次温度 β/T 的 Gibbs 更新。这个结果解释了为什么 refresh 能逐步把策略往更高 reward 区域推，而不是停留在单个固定 reference 定义的局部目标附近。对不精确更新，论文再给出有限数据下的 reward 保证，误差项由每轮 token 级 mismatch 和内层拟合误差累积控制。二值奖励和局部 reference 控制下，最终策略的单样本 reward 可以逼近初始策略的 best-of-K reward。和 AGRO 的关系也讲得比较清楚：两者共享同一个 regularized optimum，但 GGPO测的是组内 log-mean-exp contrast，AGRO测的是 adjusted reward variance，因此优化几何和有限组保证不同。1fe:T9f9,The method is built from KL-regularized policy optimization and its Gibbs-form dual solution. Given a reference policy and temperature, there is a Gibbs target under which the KL-adjusted reward is constant on the support of the target distribution. GGPO does not estimate this target policy explicitly, and it does not apply learner-to-behavior importance weights. Instead, it uses groups of responses sampled from the behavior policy for the same prompt, and measures how far the within-group KL-adjusted rewards are from satisfying that constancy condition.
The resulting objective minimizes a log-mean-exp contrast of KL-adjusted rewards inside each response group. This is different from GRPO-style relative advantage updates, and also different from AGRO, which minimizes the variance of the same adjusted reward. The distinction matters: GGPO and AGRO share the same regularized optimum under common support, but they induce different optimization geometry and different finite-group guarantees.
The paper makes two theoretical moves. First, in the on-policy population setting, the GGPO objective is exactly the KL-regularized optimality gap. That gives the loss a clean interpretation: it is not merely a heuristic group contrast, but a direct measure of suboptimality under KL regularization. Second, in the off-policy setting, the analysis does not try to recover an unbiased estimate of that population quantity. Instead, it proves a direct reward comparison: under bounded coverage, the raw finite-group loss controls the gap between the learner’s expected reward from a single sample and the behavior policy’s best-of-K reward, up to explicit terms for regularization, reference-behavior mismatch, group size, and finite-sample error. This is the central conceptual shift of the paper.
A second major component is periodic reference refresh. With a fixed reference, GGPO optimizes toward a single Gibbs target. Refreshing the reference to the current learner changes the target across rounds. The paper shows that if each round exactly fits its Gibbs target, then T refresh rounds at temperature beta are equivalent to one Gibbs update at temperature beta/T. This explains why refresh can compound improvement rather than merely refine a fixed target. For imperfect updates, the paper derives finite-data guarantees in terms of aggregate tokenwise mismatch and inner optimization error. Under binary rewards and local reference control, the final policy’s single-sample reward can approach the best-of-K reward of the initial policy.1ff:T5ca,The empirical study is organized around three mismatch regimes: training-inference mismatch, controlled policy staleness, and offline training. Evaluation is on five mathematical reasoning benchmarks and two model sizes. The headline result stated in the paper is that GGPO outperforms both GRPO and AGRO under training-inference mismatch, and remains stable as synchronization delay increases from N=8 to N=128, whereas GRPO and AGRO degrade. At N=128, token-level TIS improves GRPO, but GGPO still performs better without relying on importance weighting.
The refresh ablation is especially important. The paper reports that periodic reference refresh substantially improves GGPO under the default training setup, which matches the theory: a fixed reference only defines one Gibbs target, while refresh allows successive rounds to build on previous progress. The experiments also appear designed to test the practical meaning of the theoretical terms, including mismatch severity, group-based supervision quality, and robustness under stale or offline data.
