The point is to internalize the evaluation logic: predictive modeling needs an explicit bridge from generation quality to closed-loop behavioral gain.3b4:T479,TimeBraid uses a mixture-of-Transformers design with two pretrained hosts: a language model for instruction following, reasoning, and text generation, and a time-series foundation model for continuous-signal perception and zero-shot forecasting. The two are connected by interleaved global residual attention layers, which create a shared chronological context while keeping modality-specific processing intact. Inputs and outputs are represented as arbitrary sequences of segments. Each segment can be text or a univariate time series, and can be either context or target. For forecasting, the target time-series segment restates the observed history and then continues with future values, which makes forecasting fit the same interface as text generation. Training follows a two-stage curriculum: first, large-scale paired data for alignment and controllable forecasting; then task adaptation for instruction following and real-world domains. Compared with simple projection layers or signal tokenizers, the key design choice is to preserve native pretrained representations and enable cross-modal interaction through a shared attention space.3b5:T8bf,The method is built around a reverse-SFT pipeline followed by semantic-consistency RL. The system is formalized as a prompt enhancer πθ feeding a video generator Gϕ. The goal is to generate a textual condition y that is easier for Gϕ to realize faithfully. Instead of starting from a user request x and expanding it forward into a richer prompt, WanPE starts from a high-quality real video v, derives a hierarchical cinematic condition y from that video, and then reconstructs a compatible but information-sparser user request x. The pair (x, y) is used for supervised training. The motivation is straightforward: y is grounded in real video and therefore better aligned with the conditioning distribution seen by the generator, while x approximates realistic user input at inference time.

The hierarchical cinematic condition appears to be organized at the shot level rather than as a single long paragraph. It captures scene setup, entities, actions, camera language, lighting, audio or dialogue, and narrative progression across shots. This matters because cinematic planning is a coupled control problem: action, camera, pacing, editing, and atmosphere evolve together and cannot be handled well by local prompt embellishment.

After SFT, the model is optimized with SC-GRPO. The key contribution here is the reward design rather than GRPO itself. The paper defines a nine-dimensional semantic-consistency reward to check whether user requirements are preserved across the entire plan. The reward targets omissions, semantic drift, incorrect bindings between entities and attributes or actions, and temporal inconsistencies across shots. Compared with rewards based only on fluency or overall text quality, this is much closer to structured fidelity. In effect, the RL stage acts like a global verifier for long-form planning: the model is encouraged not only to sound cinematic, but to remain faithful to the original request throughout the generated plan.

Another notable point is transferability. The authors claim WanPE can transfer across video generators after format adaptation. That suggests the model is learning a more abstract planning representation rather than memorizing a single generator-specific prompt template.3b6:T806,Three parts of the experimental section matter most. First is scale and headline gain. The paper trains WanPE variants from 4B to 397B on 1.05M real-world videos. According to the reported main results, WanPE-397B improves over raw prompts by up to 18.84 points for 5–15 second generation and 50.86 points for 30-second generation. The larger gain at longer duration is important: it suggests the value of prompt planning grows with temporal horizon because longer videos depend more heavily on front-end structure.

Second is the ablation evidence. Reverse construction outperforms forward rewriting, which supports the paper’s central claim that distribution alignment to real video-grounded conditions matters more than simply making prompts more descriptive. SC-GRPO improves semantic consistency by 18.6 to 23.3 points across scales. That is a substantial effect size and indicates that the main bottleneck in long-form prompt planning is requirement preservation, not surface-level wording. If the full paper breaks down reward dimensions such as omission, binding, and temporal consistency, those tables are worth reading carefully because they reveal what kinds of failures RL is actually fixing.

Third is evaluation design. The authors build WanPEval, a human-annotated benchmark covering 5 to 30 seconds and varying intent granularity, and evaluate both at the text level and through roughly 11K blind pairwise video comparisons. That is stronger than text-only evaluation because the real utility of a prompt enhancer must show up in generated video. The paper also reports that WanPE leads evaluated commercial offerings at 5–15 seconds and remains competitive with Seedance 2.5 at 30 seconds. This suggests the method is already effective in medium-duration settings, while very long generation is still partly capped by the downstream generator. If transfer experiments across generators are included in detail, those are especially useful for judging whether the model learned general planning or platform-specific prompting habits.3b7:T4cc,For a quick but useful read, focus on three places. First, read the introduction carefully where the paper argues that forward rewriting and video-grounded conditioning come from different distributions. That section determines whether the work is merely a large engineering system or a genuine task reformulation. Second, inspect the method section for the exact structure of the hierarchical cinematic condition and how reverse construction builds training pairs from real videos. If that pipeline is weak, much of the gain may simply come from model scale. Third, study the SC-GRPO reward design and its ablations, especially what each of the nine reward dimensions measures and whether the training remains stable.

In the experiments, prioritize: (1) comparisons among raw prompts, forward baselines, reverse-SFT, and reverse+SC-GRPO across different video lengths; (2) scaling behavior from 4B to 397B; (3) whether text-level gains match video-level blind preference; and (4) transfer across generators. A solid skim should take about 30 to 45 minutes. If only one part is worth deeper inspection, make it the reverse-construction data pipeline and the semantic-consistency reward, since those are the most reusable ideas.3b8:Tac4,方法上最重要的是“串行阶段化 + 奖励硬度排序 + 难度过滤”。完整流水线是 SFT → Reasoning RL → Coding RL → Instruction-Following RL → General Agent → Coding Agent → Search Agent → RLHF，全部基于同一个 GLM-4.5-Air-Base（106B total / 12B active）连续更新参数。

第一部分是 SFT。作者把它当成 capability-building stage，而不是格式对齐。SFT 的作用有两个：一是建立广泛能力下限，二是统一输出格式，尤其是 native <think> chat format 和多轮交互模板。这里隐含的判断是，如果 SFT 没把能力面铺开，后续 RL 只能在狭窄分布上做局部修补，容易出现 reward overfitting。

第二部分是多阶段 RL。Reasoning RL 和 Coding RL 先做，因为奖励最硬，分别依赖可验证答案或执行/测试信号，属于 RLVR。Instruction-Following RL 虽然用了 rubric-based judge，但被放在 agent 阶段之前，因为作者观察到 instruction following 离模型原有聊天能力更近，judge 可被利用的空间较小。General/Coding/Search Agent 三个阶段再把工具使用、环境交互和长轨迹决策加进来。最后才做 RLHF，用偏好型软奖励去修整开放式质量。

第三部分是 difficulty filtering。作者反复强调，训练样本要落在“可学但未掌握”的区间：已经会做的 prompt 要丢掉，大多数阶段里始终不会做的 prompt 也丢掉。这样做不是简单提纯数据，而是在 on-policy RL 中构造自动 curriculum，避免梯度浪费在零优势样本或纯噪声样本上。相比只按题目元数据分桶，这种基于当前策略表现的过滤更贴近真实学习边界。

第四部分是基础设施设计。作者明确指出，多轮 agent RL 需要 token-in/token-out rollouts，也就是把模型生成和环境返回都作为在线轨迹的一部分，而不是离线拼接。为了稳定 RL，他们使用大 batch 和 Rollout Routing Replay；后者的作用是缓解长轨迹、多环境、异步 rollout 带来的分布抖动。另一个关键点是从 SFT 到 agent 阶段保持 chat template 一致，避免模板漂移把能力变化和格式变化混在一起。对于 coding/search agent，还需要长时间稳定运行的 sandbox/service，否则 reward 噪声会直接污染策略更新。

和常见做法相比，这篇工作的区别不在单个算法，而在把“为什么先做这个、后做那个”讲得很具体。很多工作把 IF、agent、RLHF 混在一起做多目标优化；这里则明确按 reward 可验证性和被攻击风险排序。很多工作也做 hard example mining，但这里是按当前 policy 的成功带宽做动态过滤，更接近 RL 里的 learnability control。3b9:T927,The central design is a serial pipeline with explicit stage responsibilities, reward-hardness ordering, and difficulty filtering. The full sequence is SFT → Reasoning RL → Coding RL → Instruction-Following RL → General Agent → Coding Agent → Search Agent → RLHF, all applied to the same GLM-4.5-Air-Base checkpoint (106B total, 12B active MoE).

SFT is treated as the capability foundation. Its role is not only to align output style, but to establish broad competence and normalize the model’s interaction format, including the native <think> template and multi-turn chat behavior. The implicit claim is that if SFT does not already cover the capability surface, later RL will overfit narrow reward channels rather than build robust skills.

The RL stages are ordered by reward reliability. Reasoning RL and Coding RL come first because they rely on hard verification signals such as exact answers, execution, or tests. Instruction-Following RL uses a rubric-based judge, but it is still placed before the agent stages because instruction following is close to the model’s native chat behavior and therefore less exposed to severe reward gaming. General Agent, Coding Agent, and Search Agent then introduce tool use and environment interaction. RLHF is deliberately last, since open-ended preference rewards are the easiest to exploit.

A key mechanism is difficulty filtering. The training prompts are restricted to a productive band: prompts the current policy already solves are removed, and in most stages prompts it never solves are also removed. This turns on-policy RL into an automatic curriculum over learnable examples. Compared with static hard-example mining, the filter is policy-dependent and tracks the current learning frontier.

The infrastructure section is unusually important. The authors use token-in/token-out rollouts for multi-turn on-policy RL, large batches for stability, and Rollout Routing Replay to reduce variance and distributional jitter from long trajectories and asynchronous environments. They also emphasize strict chat-template consistency from SFT through agent stages, plus reliable sandbox services for long coding and search episodes. The paper’s novelty is less about a new optimizer or reward formula, and more about making the sequencing logic and systems constraints explicit.3ba:T5b0,The most useful experimental contribution is the stagewise analysis rather than the final leaderboard. The final Rufus-Air model outperforms the official GLM-4.5-Air release on every reported benchmark except Arena-Hard v2 Creative Writing, and is competitive with similarly sized open models such as INTELLECT-3 and Nemotron-3-Super. It leads on instruction-following and most alignment and agentic rows, ties Nemotron-3-Super on Terminal-Bench 2.1, trails on a few Tau2 domain rows, and is weaker on creative writing.

More importantly, each stage is evaluated against the checkpoint it starts from, not only against the final model. That design is critical in multi-stage post-training because later stages overwrite the same parameters. Without stagewise comparisons, it is hard to tell whether a gain comes from the intended stage or from accidental carryover.

The paper’s main empirical claims are that strong SFT materially raises the downstream ceiling, Reasoning RL improves not only reasoning tasks but also later instruction-following, and difficulty filtering is a major driver of stable RL gains. The excerpt already gives the practical scale: the RL stages run on 8 to 32 nodes with a 12B-active MoE model, which makes the recipe accessible outside frontier labs. When reading the full paper, the most reusable numbers are likely in the stagewise tables, the filtering ratios, and the compute table rather than the final benchmark summary.3bb:T432,Start with the Introduction and Recipe Overview. The four claims to anchor on are: SFT builds capability, difficulty filtering creates an automatic curriculum, stage order should follow reward reliability, and infrastructure is part of the recipe.

Then read the per-stage sections carefully, especially the data, reward, and filtering rules. The key question is not just what data they used, but why each capability is trained at that point in the pipeline rather than earlier or later. The placement of Reasoning RL before IF RL, and RLHF at the very end, deserves close attention.

Do not skip the infrastructure section. For anyone working on agent RL or long-horizon post-training, this is where much of the practical value sits: token-in/token-out rollouts, template consistency, sandbox reliability, large-batch RL, and Rollout Routing Replay.

Finally, read the benchmark and ablation tables with a stagewise lens. Focus on Figure 1, Table 1, Table 2, and Table 16. A careful read should take around 1.5 to 2.5 hours; a recipe-only pass can be done in under an hour.3bc:T8fc,整体框架分三层：大规模多模态 SFT 打底，IDRL 做核心后训练，PAH 做系统层外循环优化。

第一层是 SFT。Pistis-27B 和 9B 分别建立在 Qwen3.6 与 Qwen3.5 基座上。Thinking 版本用结构化 reasoning 数据做大规模多模态 SFT，Agentic 版本则进一步加入 agentic trajectories，覆盖长程规划、迭代推理、工具使用以及文本/图像混合场景。这里的作用是提供一个足够好的 cold start，因为文中明确提到 on-policy distillation 对初始 student-teacher overlap 敏感，没有合适起点时容易失败。

第二层是 IDRL。它不是把 distillation loss 和 RL loss 静态加权求和，也不是先蒸馏后 RL 的串行流程，而是在同一训练循环中交替执行 on-policy distillation 更新和 RL 更新。on-policy distillation 的对象是学生自己采样出来的序列，再用教师分布提供 token-level 密集监督；RL 则继续根据任务回报优化策略。作者的论点是：如果两种目标放在同一次更新里，会出现梯度干扰；如果完全分阶段，又失去相互校正的机会。交替更新相当于在时间上解耦目标冲突，同时保留动态互动。文中把收益归因于三点：探索更充分、策略熵保持更好、优化更稳定。

对于 agentic 长轨迹，作者再加了 PAS，step-level positive-advantage suppression。它针对的问题是 trajectory-level reward 的常见偏差：一条轨迹最后成功了，中间一些无效甚至错误的动作也可能因为共享正 advantage 而被错误强化。PAS 的做法是对这些中间步骤的正优势进行抑制，避免“搭便车式”信用分配。虽然从摘要信息看不到精确公式，但思想很清楚：不是所有位于成功轨迹上的动作都应得到正反馈。

第三层是 Pistis-Auto-Harnessing。它不改模型参数，也不改工具接口，而是用一个 Optimization Agent 基于开发集轨迹提出、验证并筛选 harness revision，例如工作流、prompt、技能调用、证据表示和路由逻辑的调整。只有在开发指标上确实变好时才保留修改，然后冻结到评测阶段。这个设计把“学策略”和“调系统”分开，减少了把系统工程收益误记到模型能力上的风险。3bd:Ta42,The framework has three layers: large-scale multimodal SFT for initialization, IDRL for core post-training, and PAH for system-level outer-loop optimization.

The first layer is SFT. Pistis-27B and Pistis-9B are built on Qwen3.6 and Qwen3.5 respectively. The Thinking variants are trained on structured multimodal reasoning data, while the Agentic variants additionally include agentic trajectories covering long-horizon planning, iterative reasoning, tool use, and mixed text-vision interaction. This stage is important because the paper explicitly notes that on-policy distillation is sensitive to student-teacher overlap and can fail without a strong cold start.

The second layer is IDRL. Instead of using a static weighted sum of distillation and RL losses, or running distillation and RL as separate stages, IDRL alternates between on-policy distillation updates and RL updates within a single training loop. In the distillation step, the student is trained against the teacher distribution on student-generated sequences, giving dense token-level supervision. In the RL step, the policy is optimized against task reward. The motivation is that a static joint loss can create objective interference within the same update, while a purely staged pipeline prevents the two signals from interacting during training. Interleaving is meant to decouple the objectives in time while still allowing them to shape the same evolving policy. The claimed benefits are better exploration, higher retained policy entropy, and more stable optimization.

For long-horizon agentic training, the paper adds PAS, or step-level positive-advantage suppression. This targets a common failure mode in trajectory-level RL: if a trajectory succeeds overall, some ineffective or even wrong intermediate actions may still receive positive credit because they share the trajectory’s positive advantage. PAS suppresses positive advantage on such steps, reducing this hitchhiking effect. The exact formula is not visible from the provided text, but the intent is clear: not every action on a successful trajectory deserves reinforcement.

The third layer is Pistis-Auto-Harnessing. PAH does not change the policy weights or the tool interface. Instead, an Optimization Agent proposes bounded revisions to the inference harness using development trajectories, validates them against a development metric, and keeps only those revisions that improve the metric. The selected harness is then frozen for evaluation. This cleanly separates model learning from workflow optimization, including prompts, skills, evidence representation, and routing logic.3be:T731,The experimental story has two main tracks: Thinking models and Agentic models. For Thinking, Pistis-27B-Thinking is roughly on par with Qwen3.8-27B on 24 non-grounding benchmarks, 82.3 versus 82.4, while reaching the highest grounding average of 80.5, which is 8.6 points above Qwen3.8-27B. That is a useful result because it suggests the post-training recipe improves grounding substantially without sacrificing general reasoning. The 9B Thinking model is reported to achieve the best averages among similarly sized models on both benchmark groups.

For Agentic models, the gains over the corresponding base models are more pronounced on long-horizon interactive tasks. Relative to Qwen3.6-27B, Pistis-27B-Agentic improves BrowseComp-VL, MMSearch, VDR-testmini, and LiveVQA by 8.8, 3.3, 3.2, and 9.7 points. Relative to Qwen3.5-9B, Pistis-9B-Agentic improves the same tasks by 8.4, 8.0, 3.2, and 11.4 points. The larger gains on multimodal search and live interaction are consistent with the paper’s claim that IDRL and agentic trajectory training are especially helpful for long-horizon decision-making rather than single-turn QA.

The ablation section is likely where the paper is most informative. The authors state that IDRL outperforms pure on-policy distillation, pure RL, and a static joint objective. If the full report includes training curves, the most useful things to inspect are whether validation metrics are smoother, whether policy entropy decays more slowly, and whether the interleaving schedule matters. For PAS, the key question is whether it reduces the rate of bad intermediate actions inside successful trajectories and whether it improves sample efficiency on long-horizon tasks. For PAH, the important evidence is how much gain comes from harness optimization alone under the same environment-interaction budget.3bf:T4b4,A good skim should follow the order: method first, system second, results third. Start with the definition of IDRL and the training-loop diagram. The main thing to verify is the granularity of interleaving: whether it happens at the update level, batch level, or in larger alternating phases. That determines how different it really is from prior distillation-plus-RL pipelines. Then read the PAS formulation or pseudocode to see whether it is implemented through masking, clipping, or a more selective step filter. After that, inspect PAH, not just for the score gains but for how it avoids contaminating evaluation and how clearly it separates harness changes from policy learning.

In the experiments, prioritize: (1) the main ablation comparing IDRL against OPD, RL, and static joint training; (2) training stability and entropy curves; (3) consistency across 27B and 9B scales for both Thinking and Agentic variants; and (4) the standalone contribution of PAH with a fixed model. A useful skim should take about 35 to 50 minutes. If only one part deserves deeper attention, make it the IDRL interleaving mechanism and the PAS credit-assignment treatment, since those are the most transferable ideas.3c0:T4b6,The proposed method, GRAFT, stands for Graph-based Faithful Step-level credit assignment. It reorganizes multiple rollout trajectories from the same prompt into a trajectory graph instead of treating them as isolated chains. Nodes represent states and edges represent actions. State canonicalization merges identical or semantically similar states using exact matching or embedding-based similarity. The outgoing actions from a merged node then form an on-state action group, which is closer to the group required by the standard advantage definition. The method estimates node values by Bellman-style propagation over the graph using only terminal outcome rewards. Given these values, the step advantage is defined as A_t = gamma V(s_{t+1}) - V(s_t). The paper also introduces Graph GAE, extending generalized advantage estimation to the trajectory graph by aggregating multi-hop future advantage estimates. Compared with PRM-based approaches, GRAFT does not require step-level reward annotation. Compared with group normalization by step index, it avoids mixing different states into one baseline. Compared with resampling continuations from every intermediate state, it avoids the O(N^2 T) rollout cost.3c1:T430,SLCA-GRPO introduces Segment-Locked Credit Assignment. The rollout is first segmented with masks: environment tokens are excluded from policy gradients, and learnable policy tokens are split into a tool segment and a summary segment. The final contiguous learnable block is treated as the summary segment; all earlier learnable blocks, including reasoning traces and structured tool calls, form the tool segment. The method then computes separate group-relative advantages for tool-side and summary-side rewards. During optimization, tool advantages are routed only to tool tokens, and summary advantages only to summary tokens. This blocks cross-segment advantage contamination before backpropagation, without extra rollouts and without separating the agent into planner and summarizer models. Hierarchical Rewards provide segment-level feedback, and a Schema-Guided LLM Simulator supplies scalable tool-interaction rollouts. Unlike VinePPO, SPO, or GiGPO, which mainly operate along the temporal axis, SLCA operates along a structural execution-versus-articulation axis.3c2:T409,The paper formalizes an agent episode as a sequence of model actions and environment observations, with a binary outcome reward assigned at the end. It builds on GRPO, where multiple trajectories are sampled per task and group-relative advantages are computed from their rewards. The criticized OPSD setup conditions the same model on privileged context to obtain a stronger teacher distribution, then asks the ordinary student view to match it. This creates an irreducible information mismatch. Privileged Self-Practice changes where the privileged information is used. If the model’s rollouts on a task mostly fail, an analyzer model writes a short task-specific instruction. The system then resamples a guided group with that instruction in context. Guided and unguided groups are scored under their own sampling contexts, and advantages are computed within each group. The same GRPO objective is used; there is no loss term comparing the privileged and non-privileged views. At inference time, the extra instruction is removed.3c3:T989,方法核心是 CounterRoute，一个在线 RL 框架，直接从原生支持 thinking / no-thinking 的单一 checkpoint 出发训练，不额外做该方法专用的 SFT warm-up，也不引入外部 router。形式化上，策略先对给定 prompt 采样模式 m∈{TH, NT}，再在该模式下生成回答 z。论文定义了带效率边际 b 的路由目标：只有当 thinking 的估计效用比 no-thinking 高出至少 b 时，才值得走 TH；否则优先走更便宜的 NT。这个 b 不是 token 成本的显式建模，而是 reward space 里的偏置，用来避免在两种模式质量接近时无谓思考。

训练上有两个关键设计。其一是 paired current-policy counterfactual rollouts。对一部分 prompt，强制当前策略分别在 TH 和 NT 下各生成一次回答，得到同一 prompt 下的成对反事实样本。然后比较两种模式的 utility，构造跨模式 credit。因为两条回答都来自当前策略，而不是旧策略、规则标签或外部教师，所以路由监督会随着策略能力一起更新，缓解 non-stationary target 问题。

其二是 hierarchical counterfactual credit assignment。论文采用一种“分离式 token 级赋值”规则：在最初的路由 token 上，不使用模式内 advantage，而是用经过截断或边界控制的跨模式 utility 差值来替换；在后续回答 token 上，只用该模式内部的 GRPO 优势做更新。这样路由 token 学的是“选 TH 还是 NT”，回答 token 学的是“在已选模式下怎么答得更好”，两类梯度不再混在一起。相比把整条序列统一做 policy gradient，这种做法更贴合层级决策结构。

第三个设计是 paired-to-self-routed curriculum。训练早期，为了避免初始模式偏好压制探索，模型会保留较高比例的 paired prompts，让两种模式都持续被采样并获得训练信号；随后逐步过渡到 self-routed prompts，让模型自己决定模式。这个 curriculum 的作用不是提升最终上限，而是稳定 co-learning 过程，避免一开始就被单一模式锁死。

从全文描述看，论文还强调它与 Thinkless、HGPO、TON 等方法的区别：这些方法通常先做额外的双模式 SFT 或混合微调，再用 RL 学路由；CounterRoute 则试图直接从现成 dual-mode checkpoint 出发，用在线 RL 同时学路由和两种回答策略，减少对 warm-up 数据分布的依赖。3c4:T8a4,实验主体在 Qwen3-8B 和 Qwen3-14B 上进行。训练数据只用数学和合成 instruction-following prompts，但评测覆盖 9 个 held-out benchmark，包含 reasoning、coding、knowledge、commonsense 和 instruction following。主结果是：Qwen3-8B 的宏平均准确率达到 79.1%，Qwen3-14B 达到 82.4%，都优于同数据训练的 Think-Only GRPO，同时平均生成 token 更少。相对各自的 always-thinking checkpoint，CounterRoute 在 8B 上把平均生成 token 降低 51%，在 14B 上降低 41%，同时准确率还有提升。这说明它不是单纯靠少想来省算力，而是在不少简单样本上学会了直接答，并把节省下来的训练与推理预算转化成了更好的整体策略。

论文还给出一个很关键的现象：在 direct answering 本来就强的 benchmark 上，学到的 think rate 可以低到 1%，而 direct-answer 能力本身还会继续提升。这意味着 NT 分支不是被动保留，而是在 RL 中被单独训练得更强。另一个有价值的分析是 same-checkpoint forced-mode evaluation：对同一个训练后的 checkpoint，分别强制 TH 和 NT 作答，再看两者性能差与模型实际学到的 think rate 是否一致。结果显示，在 held-out 的 coding、science、knowledge、commonsense 上，think rate 大体跟随“thinking 相对 direct 的经验收益”变化，尽管这些域并不在 RL 训练混合中。这说明路由策略学到的不是简单的表面模式，而是某种可迁移的价值判断。

消融主要在 Qwen3-8B 上做，重点验证四个组件：反事实成对采样、模式分离的回答优化、效率边际 b、以及 paired-to-self-routed curriculum。摘要和正文给出的结论是，这四项都对稳定训练和最终的 accuracy/token trade-off 有贡献。尤其是去掉成对反事实或去掉分离式 credit assignment 时，路由更容易被回答质量噪声污染；去掉 curriculum 时，早期模式偏好更容易自我强化，导致探索不足。由于给出的全文片段没有完整表格数值，无法逐项复述所有 ablation 的具体百分点，但主结论是组件作用比较清楚，不是单一技巧堆出来的结果。3c5:T8f9,CounterRoute starts from an off-the-shelf native dual-mode checkpoint, such as Qwen3, and trains everything with online RL, without method-specific SFT warm-up, routing labels, an external router, or separate models. Formally, the policy first samples a mode m in {TH, NT} for a prompt x, then generates a response z conditioned on x and m. The routing objective is defined with an efficiency margin b: thinking is preferred only if its estimated utility exceeds no-thinking by at least b; ties go to NT. This margin is a reward-space prior that biases toward the cheaper mode when quality is similar.

The first key mechanism is paired current-policy counterfactual rollouts. For selected prompts, the current policy is forced to answer once in TH and once in NT. This produces paired responses under both modes for the same prompt, allowing direct cross-mode utility comparison. Because both rollouts come from the current policy, the routing target tracks the model’s evolving capabilities instead of relying on fixed labels, heuristics, or a teacher.

The second mechanism is hierarchical counterfactual credit assignment. The paper uses a disjoint token-level rule. At the initial routing token, the usual within-mode advantage is replaced by a bounded cross-mode utility credit. For the response tokens, only within-mode GRPO advantage is used. This means the routing token learns which mode to choose, while the response tokens learn how to answer well within the chosen mode. Compared with sequence-level policy gradients over the whole output, this better matches the hierarchical structure of the decision process.

The third mechanism is a paired-to-self-routed curriculum. Early in training, the method keeps enough paired prompts so both modes continue to receive evidence and updates. Later, control is gradually transferred to autonomous self-routing. The purpose is to prevent early mode bias from collapsing exploration before the value of both modes is estimated reliably.

Relative to prior adaptive-reasoning methods such as Thinkless, HGPO, and TON, the paper’s main distinction is that it does not rely on extra dual-mode SFT or hybrid fine-tuning before RL. It tries to co-learn routing and both conditional response policies directly from a native dual-mode checkpoint.3c6:T792,The main experiments use Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-14B. RL training uses only math and synthetic instruction-following prompts, while evaluation spans nine held-out benchmarks covering reasoning, coding, knowledge, commonsense, and instruction following. The headline result is a macro-average accuracy of 79.1% for Qwen3-8B and 82.4% for Qwen3-14B. Both outperform same-data Think-Only GRPO while using fewer generated tokens on average. Relative to the corresponding always-thinking checkpoints, CounterRoute reduces mean generated tokens by 51% on 8B and 41% on 14B, while also improving accuracy.

A notable result is that on benchmarks where direct answering is already strong, the learned think rate can drop to as low as 1%, and the direct-answer branch still improves. That suggests the NT branch is not merely preserved for efficiency; it is actively trained into a stronger policy. Another important analysis is the same-checkpoint forced-mode evaluation. The trained checkpoint is evaluated once with forced TH and once with forced NT, and the empirical benefit of thinking is compared with the learned think rate. The paper reports that think rates broadly track the actual value of reasoning across held-out coding, science, knowledge, and commonsense domains, even though those domains are absent from the RL training mixture. That is a stronger sign of route-value alignment than raw benchmark averages alone.

Ablations are reported on Qwen3-8B and cover the main components: paired counterfactual rollouts, mode-separated response optimization, the efficiency margin, and the paired-to-self-routed curriculum. The qualitative conclusion is that each component matters for stability and for the final accuracy-versus-token trade-off. The provided text does not include all table values, so not every ablation delta can be quoted here, but the paper does present controlled evidence rather than relying on a single aggregate gain.3c7:T516,For a quick read, focus on three parts. First, read the introduction and problem formulation to understand why routing is treated as a hierarchical decision rather than a static classifier, and how the efficiency margin b is defined. Second, read the method section around paired counterfactual rollouts and token-level credit assignment. The central idea is simple but easy to miss: routing tokens get cross-mode credit, response tokens get within-mode GRPO. Third, read the same-checkpoint forced-mode analysis, because that is where the paper shows whether routing actually tracks the value of reasoning.

If time is limited, the system overview figure, training algorithm, main results table, think-rate plots, and ablation table should be enough to grasp the contribution in about 25 to 35 minutes. For deeper reading, two questions are worth keeping in mind. One is whether this credit decomposition extends beyond binary TH/NT routing to multiple reasoning budgets. The other is whether the current reward-space efficiency margin can be replaced by a more explicit model of token cost, latency, or tool cost. A further pretraining-facing question is whether native dual-mode separability should be encouraged earlier, during pretraining or mid-training, rather than learned only at the RL stage.3c8:T437,The central object is the conditional proof-difficulty function V(T|P), the difficulty of proving a target theorem T given an available premise set P. Lean 4 and mathlib provide the formal environment, and proof difficulty is operationalized through formal proof length or proof cost. Using the dependency structure in mathlib, the authors post-train a 27B model to predict V(T|P) before the proof is actually constructed. They then define intrinsic interestingness as proof length divided by statement length. The intended signal is high information density: a theorem that is short to state but hard to prove is more interesting. They also define utility as the amount by which adding a theorem to the mathematical context compresses later proofs. Utility captures reusable abstraction, while interestingness is easier to estimate locally. The paper reports a strong correlation between the two, which motivates using interestingness as a practical reward. The metric is then used both for post-training theorem generation and for inference-time pruning in recursive discovery.3c9:T56b,The paper first characterizes the failure of OPRD-style methods, then proposes LastOPD. In the baseline recipe, the student rolls out its own responses, the teacher scores them, and latent supervision is added by pairing student and teacher layers at matched relative depth, with a projector bridging hidden-size differences. The authors argue that this setup has two structural problems. First, depth-matched layers need not play the same functional role. Their J-Lens analysis shows that the teacher’s final answer becomes readable mainly in the last two layers, whereas the student’s answer emerges more gradually across layers. Second, common alignment metrics can be dominated by a few large dimensions, so improving similarity scores may not reflect useful functional matching. LastOPD changes the recipe in three ways. It aligns only the final hidden states immediately before the LM heads, avoiding intermediate layer pairing altogether. It uses a small trainable MLP to bridge width differences at that final interface. And it treats latent supervision as a short-lived scaffold: over the first 10 steps, the latent loss is linearly decayed while a token-level reverse top-k loss is linearly increased, after which training continues with token-only OPD. The key idea is that latent supervision is useful as an early directional signal but harmful when kept active too long.3ca:T595,The main setup distills Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B teachers into Qwen3-1.7B-Base using DAPO-Math-17k, with MATH-500 as the main validation benchmark. The collapse is striking. In the 4B-to-1.7B setting, latent-only OPRD raises MATH-500 from 25.4 to 46.2 within 10 steps, outperforming vanilla OPD by 28 points at that stage. But continued optimization drives the score down to 11.3, below the student’s initial level, with no recovery. The 8B teacher shows the same pattern. At the same time, the optimized alignment metric keeps improving: projected cosine similarity rises from 0.97 to 0.98 with the 4B teacher and from 0.95 to 0.98 with the 8B teacher, even as behavior deteriorates by roughly 35 points. The paper also reports that the untrained student and the 4B teacher already have mid-layer self-CKA around 0.99 despite a large capability gap on MATH-500, which further weakens the case for taking high similarity at face value. Diagnostics show that the main representational changes are concentrated in later student layers, that teacher and student have different layerwise answer-readout patterns under J-Lens, and that neither masking dominant dimensions nor remapping layers by CKA prevents collapse. On the method side, LastOPD avoids the late collapse and improves final MATH-500 over token-only OPD by 5.55 and 4.02 points in the two cross-size Qwen3 settings, while also outperforming continued joint supervision.3cb:T431,Read it in three passes: phenomenon, diagnosis, remedy. Start with Figure 1. It already contains the core story: early gain followed by collapse, alignment improving while behavior worsens, and mismatched layerwise readout patterns between teacher and student. Then read the analysis section to see why simple explanations do not hold up: the issue is not just insufficient training, and it is not fixed by a better layer mapping. After that, read the LastOPD method section with one question in mind: why align only the pre-head last layer, and why anneal the latent term away after just 10 steps? Finally, inspect the main results and ablations to separate the effect of alignment location from the effect of temporal crossfading. A solid skim takes about 30 minutes. The most interesting follow-ups are whether the useful latent-supervision window depends on teacher–student gap or task type, whether interpretability tools can predict which layers are safe to distill, and whether the same short-lived auxiliary-loss strategy transfers to multi-objective pretraining.3cc:T570,The dataset is 2WikiMultihopQA, where each item already contains several type-matched candidate entities with short profiles. The pipeline keeps only cases where the model first makes a choice, then—when explicitly asked—names a rejected rival and a missing attribute, and that attribute is indeed absent from the rival profile while being available as a real sentence in a sibling profile from the same item. Repairable attributes include birth date, death date, parentage, and director information. The intervention has five conditions. R0 is an unedited re-ask to verify reproducibility under greedy decoding. R1 appends the relevant fact sentence to the named rival. R2 appends a length-matched irrelevant sentence to that same rival. R3 appends the relevant sentence to a third option the model never mentioned. R4 appends the irrelevant sentence to that unmentioned option. This separates content effects from placement effects. A notable design choice is that the inserted sentence need not be true of the target entity: the tested claim is only that the profile omitted the attribute, so any sentence stating that attribute falsifies the model’s earlier complaint. The paper also spends nontrivial effort on integrity gates, deterministic subject substitution, exclusion of cases where the rejected option is actually the gold answer, and validation of the string-rule pipeline.3cd:T5a0,There are three runs: Part A uses three open 7B–8B instruct models with four options; Part B adds three more checkpoints, still with four options; Part C returns to the Part A model roster but uses six options. A useful preliminary result is that contrastive rejections appear spontaneously in only 20.8% of items, but rise to 72.5% when directly elicited, while accuracy stays flat at 68.4% vs 68.2%. So asking surfaces the explanation without materially changing task performance. Another important statistic is that about 32% of specific rejections name a defect that the profile already contains, which immediately limits how literally one should read the model’s stated reasons. The headline result from the largest run is that supplying the named fact at the named rival changes the model’s choice more than a length-matched irrelevant control does, with odds ratio 3.57, 95% CI [1.54, 8.26], Holm-corrected p=0.0210. This supports the claim that the stated reason sometimes does causal work. But the signal is mixed rather than universal. The paper also highlights disagreement between two instruments: free-text choice and forced single-token probability. In one example, adding the relevant sentence flips the model’s final choice, yet the local token probability for that option barely moves and can even be lower than under the irrelevant control. That makes Section 5 important: the two readouts are not interchangeable.3ce:T40d,The method has three parts. First, the authors run activation patching across 25 models from 8 LLM families. They corrupt visual inputs with Gaussian noise or image swaps, cache clean and corrupted activations, then patch clean activations back into the corrupted run by layer and token category. The restoration score measures how much a patched site recovers the clean behavior. This identifies an early L0 attention-routing circuit in a subset of VQ-tokenized unified VLMs. Second, they formalize the mechanism with a three-gate diagnostic: residual-stream divergence, L0 attention-routing concentration, and codebook off-manifold rate. The gates are tied to architectural measurements rather than directly fitted to downstream accuracy. Third, they run a constructive induction test. Replacing LLaVA-1.6's CLIP+MLP continuous projector with a VQ+Linear projector installs the circuit, while a matched-compute MLP control trained on the same data and budget does not. This isolates the VQ bottleneck as the key architectural variable.3cf:T9b7,技术路线可以拆成“人类提供什么”和“agent 决定什么”两部分。

人类提供的是 Research Skills。它们不是逐实验的人工指令，而是把专家经验编码成可执行的操作模板、代码资产、权限边界和流程约束。论文强调 high-density prior, low-frequency intervention：人类把成熟做法一次性写成可复用技能，之后不再频繁介入具体实验决策。这样做的目的，是把经验保留在系统里，但把搜索权交给 agent，而不是让 agent 在完全无先验的空间里盲搜。

agent 端由 Codex GPT-5.6-Sol（xhigh reasoning）承担。它从 base checkpoint 和可用算力出发，先构建 executable task pool，再基于 verified capability-gap trajectories 对 Qwen3.6-27B 做 cold-start。随后训练流程不是直接从 SFT 跳到 RL，而是先经过 OPSD，再过渡到 RLVR。根据正文描述，OPSD 阶段里至少发生了三类关键调整：其一，evaluation 会反过来决定哪些数据进入训练，说明数据池不是静态的，而是被在线证据筛选；其二，受控消融改变了 self-teacher 可见的证据范围，作者借此诊断 teacher 何时在利用泄漏信息、何时在学真实能力；其三，原有目标函数出现 collapsing objective，迫使 agent 把学习规则改成 verifier-anchored credit，也就是让 credit assignment 更紧贴可验证结果，而不是依赖容易漂移的代理信号。

RLVR 阶段则处理另一组问题：reward exploits、false verdicts、length-dependent degeneration。对应的修补方向分别是重写 reward eligibility、调整优化过程、控制 trajectory budgeting。这里最值得注意的是，论文没有把 RLVR 写成一个固定 recipe，而是把它描述成一系列失败后的重设计：奖励被利用，就收紧资格；verifier 有误判，就修改奖励语义或过滤机制；长输出导致退化，就把预算和优化目标一起改。这个叙述方式很像真实工业训练，而不是干净的学术设定。

从模型定位看，iCoder-27B 是一个面向工业编码的专门模型，任务覆盖 RTL 设计和 GPU kernel 优化。选择这两个方向有明确原因：它们都能用可执行 verifier 检查正确性，同时又要求性能意识和系统约束，不是普通代码补全就能解决。论文因此把“可验证环境中的 agent-led model development”落在一个反馈足够硬、但搜索空间仍然很大的场景里。3d0:T749,结果部分最醒目的是 iCoder-27B 在多个工业代码基准上的竞争力。相对同尺寸的 Qwen3.6-27B，iCoder 在 RTLLM 上从 49.6 提升到 68.0，增幅 18.4 分；在 VerilogEval Spec-to-RTL 上从 70.1 提升到 86.3，增幅 16.2 分；在 KernelBench L2 correctness 上从 28 提升到 74，约 2.64 倍。这个幅度说明它不是小修小补，而是任务能力被显著重塑。

与更大模型相比，iCoder 也有竞争力。论文给出的数字是：在 RTLLM 上超过 DeepSeek-V4-Pro（68.0 vs. 67.5）；在 KernelBench L1 correctness 上接近翻倍于 DeepSeek-V4-Pro（61 vs. 32）。对闭源前沿模型，iCoder 在 RTLLM 上高于 GPT-5.5、Claude Opus 4.8、Gemini 3.5 Flash（68.0 vs. 66.0/64.7/63.5）；在 KernelBench L1 上也高于 GPT-5.5 和 Gemini 3.5 Flash，并超过 Claude 的 55 达到 61。TritonBench-G 上它与 Claude Opus 4.8 持平在 20.1，高于 GPT-5.5 的 19.5 和 Gemini 3.5 Flash 的 14.9。

论文还给了更贴近使用场景的 case study。对 8 个 RTL design 任务，iCoder 距 HY3 和 DeepSeek-V4-Pro 分别只差 1.1 和 4.5 分，但使用的输出 token 仅为它们报告值的 51% 和 33%。这说明它不仅正确率高，推理开销也更省。对选取的 8 个 GPU operator，它在其中 2 个上达到 strongest archived endpoint，说明其优化能力不只是 benchmark 分数上的偶然。

从全文表述看，实验的另一条主线是开发过程中的 ablation 和失败分析，而不仅是最终榜单。作者强调 evaluation 改变训练数据进入条件、controlled ablation 改变 self-teacher 证据、objective collapse 触发学习规则重写、reward exploit 和 false verdict 改写 RLVR 设计。这些内容如果正文给出具体表格和时间线，会比最终分数更值得看，因为它们揭示了 agent 是如何做研发决策的。3d1:Ta30,The setup is organized around a division of labor. Humans provide Research Skills: reusable, executable operational procedures, code assets, permission boundaries, and process scaffolds distilled from expert model-development practice. The paper frames this as high-density prior, low-frequency intervention. The point is not to remove human expertise, but to compress it into reusable machinery so that the agent can search over concrete development decisions without requiring constant human steering.

The agent is Codex GPT-5.6-Sol running at high reasoning effort. Starting from a base checkpoint and available compute, it first builds an executable task pool, then cold-starts Qwen3.6-27B on verified capability-gap trajectories. Training does not jump directly from supervised initialization to RL. Instead, the pipeline goes through OPSD and then RLVR.

The OPSD stage appears to be where much of the development logic happens. The paper highlights at least three important dynamics. First, evaluation changes which data are admitted into training, so the data mixture is not static but filtered by ongoing evidence. Second, controlled ablations alter what evidence the self-teacher can access, which is a way to diagnose when the teacher is exploiting leakage versus learning transferable capability. Third, the original objective collapses, forcing the agent to redesign the learning rule around verifier-anchored credit. That means credit assignment is tied more tightly to executable verification rather than to softer proxy signals that drift or become exploitable.

The RLVR stage addresses a different set of failures: reward exploits, false verdicts, and length-dependent degeneration. The corresponding fixes involve changing reward eligibility, modifying optimization behavior, and redesigning trajectory budgeting. One of the strongest aspects of the paper is that RLVR is not presented as a fixed recipe. It is presented as a sequence of failures and revisions: when reward is exploited, tighten eligibility; when the verifier is wrong, revise reward semantics or filtering; when long outputs degrade behavior, adjust both budget and optimization. That is much closer to real model development than a static benchmark loop.

The task domain is industrial coding, specifically RTL design and GPU kernel optimization. That choice is sensible. Both domains offer executable verification, but they also require exact reasoning, systems awareness, and performance-sensitive optimization. This gives the agent a hard feedback signal without collapsing the problem into ordinary code completion.3d2:T760,The headline results are strong for a 27B model. Relative to the same-size Qwen3.6-27B, iCoder improves RTLLM from 49.6 to 68.0, a gain of 18.4 points. On VerilogEval Spec-to-RTL it improves from 70.1 to 86.3, a gain of 16.2 points. On KernelBench L2 correctness it rises from 28 to 74, about 2.64x. Those are large deltas, suggesting substantial task-specific capability reshaping rather than marginal tuning.

The model is also competitive against much larger systems. The paper reports that iCoder slightly exceeds DeepSeek-V4-Pro on RTLLM (68.0 vs. 67.5) and nearly doubles its KernelBench L1 correctness (61 vs. 32). Against proprietary frontier systems, iCoder beats GPT-5.5, Claude Opus 4.8, and Gemini 3.5 Flash on RTLLM (68.0 vs. 66.0 / 64.7 / 63.5). On KernelBench L1, it also exceeds GPT-5.5 and Gemini 3.5 Flash and surpasses Claude’s 55 with 61. On TritonBench-G, it matches Claude Opus 4.8 at 20.1 while outperforming GPT-5.5 at 19.5 and Gemini 3.5 Flash at 14.9.

The case studies are also informative. On eight RTL design tasks, iCoder comes within 1.1 and 4.5 points of HY3 and DeepSeek-V4-Pro while using only 51% and 33% of their reported output tokens. That suggests better efficiency, not just better correctness. On selected GPU operators, it reaches the strongest archived endpoint on two of eight cases, indicating that the optimization ability is not purely benchmark-specific.

Equally important is the process evidence described in the paper. Evaluation changes data admission, controlled ablations change self-teacher evidence, objective collapse triggers a redesign of the learning rule, and reward exploits plus false verdicts force RLVR changes. If the full paper includes tables or timelines for these transitions, those are likely more informative than the final leaderboard numbers because they reveal how the agent actually made development decisions.3d3:T574,A good first pass has three steps. Start with the introduction to pin down the actual claim: not fully closed-loop self-improvement, but agent-led development under a one-time injection of executable human expertise. Then read the section on Human Prior: Executable Research Skills carefully. The key question is what exactly these skills contain: SOPs, code templates, permission boundaries, experiment harnesses, or stronger hand-authored recipes. That determines how to interpret the level of autonomy. Third, read the training pipeline sections with attention to the transitions between cold-start, OPSD, and RLVR, and to the failures that trigger each recipe revision. If the paper includes a development timeline, experiment tree, dataflow diagram, or reward-redesign table, prioritize those.

A 35 to 50 minute skim should be enough to capture the main story. If you only care about model quality, the main results table is sufficient. But the real value is in the process details: how evaluation feeds back into data selection, why the objective collapses, how verifier-anchored credit is defined, how reward eligibility is tightened, and how length-dependent degeneration is diagnosed and mitigated. The right reading stance is cautious: this is agent-led development under strong human priors and institutional scaffolding, not fully autonomous research without hand-designed structure.3d4:T907,方法上有四个部分。第一是 Extractor 数据集本身。作者选择一个真实而且不算简单的逆向工程工具作为开发对象：从 Apple Objective-C / Mach-O 二进制中恢复 protobuf descriptor。整个项目 21,000 行生产代码，测试规模相当，210 个 commits，25 个 sessions，678 条用户指令，全部由 Claude 模型生成，没有人工编写代码、测试或 commit。这个设置的价值在于，它不是 toy repo，也不是只截取若干聊天片段，而是完整保留了开发过程。

第二是代码 provenance tracing 工具。作者提出两种追踪方法。其一是基于 control-flow-graph block decomposition 加 git log -L 历史追踪，并处理 rename bridge，用来把代码块级别的变更追溯到具体来源事件。这里的来源不只是用户指令，也包括 AI 的自发发现和自我修正。其二是 session transcript mining，从工具调用日志中恢复那些在 session 内已经被修正、因此不会出现在 commit 历史里的代码生成错误。这个点很关键，因为只看 git history 会低估模型犯错率，尤其低估“先写错、再自救”的频率。

第三是三套 taxonomy。用户指令 taxonomy 扩展了 Tang 等人的 IDE-chat 分类，使其适用于多轮 CLI coding agent 场景，并新增 cross-session coordination 与 correction of AI conduct 两类。commit provenance taxonomy 则把传统软件工程里的 Perfective / Corrective / Adaptive maintenance 进一步拆开，区分“为什么改”和“怎么发现要改”。response reliability taxonomy 是这篇文章最有新意的部分之一：作者不只看代码结果，而是把 AI 对用户的陈述按 reporting / verification、mechanism explanation、root-cause diagnosis、design fix proposal 等类型分类，再用软件工件去核验这些陈述是否准确。

第四是基于上述工具和 taxonomy 的过程分析。作者把开发过程区分为 proactive 与 reactive 两类触发机制，前者是主动扩展、规划、实现，后者是对 bug、测试失败、异常现象的响应。这样做的目的，是理解 AI coding agent 到底是在“持续前进，偶尔修错”，还是“频繁出错，被动补洞”。全文结论偏向前者，但同时指出中间错误并不少。3d5:T9c8,The work has four technical components. First is the Extractor dataset itself. The target project is a real reverse-engineering tool that recovers protobuf descriptors from Apple Objective-C / Mach-O binaries. It is not a toy repository. The project contains 21,000 lines of production Python code, a similarly sized test suite, 210 commits, 25 sessions, and 678 user instructions. All code, tests, and commits were authored by Claude models, with no human-written code. The value of this setup is completeness: it preserves the full development process rather than a thin slice of it.

Second are two provenance-tracing tools. One combines control-flow-graph block decomposition with git log -L history tracing, including rename bridging, to map code changes back to specific source events. Those events include user instructions, autonomous discoveries, and self-corrections. The other mines session transcripts and tool-use logs to recover code-generation errors that were fixed within a session and therefore never appear in commit history. This is a key methodological point. Commit-only analysis systematically underestimates how often the model first writes something wrong and then repairs it.

Third are three taxonomies. The instruction-intent taxonomy extends Tang et al.’s IDE-chat taxonomy to multi-turn CLI coding-agent interaction and adds categories such as cross-session coordination and correction of the AI’s own conduct. The commit-provenance taxonomy extends the standard Perfective/Corrective/Adaptive maintenance framing by separating why a change was needed from how that need was discovered. The response-reliability taxonomy is one of the more original parts of the paper. Instead of only checking code outcomes, the authors classify the agent’s user-facing claims into categories such as fact reporting, mechanism explanation, root-cause diagnosis, and design-fix proposal, then verify those claims against the software artifacts.

Fourth is the process analysis built on top of these tools. The authors distinguish proactive development from reactive development. Proactive work means planning, extending, and implementing ahead of failures. Reactive work means responding to bugs, failed tests, or observed problems. This framing helps answer whether the agent mostly advances the project and occasionally repairs mistakes, or whether it is mainly patching its own failures. The paper finds more of the former, but with a nontrivial amount of hidden intermediate error.3d6:T716,The key results come from full-process annotation rather than final-repo statistics. On scale, the project contains 21k lines of production code, a roughly comparable test suite, 210 commits, 25 sessions, and 678 cleaned user instructions. On interaction patterns, CLI-based coding-agent instructions differ from prior IDE-chat datasets by putting more weight on comprehension, planning, and consultation rather than one-shot code requests. On development dynamics, 86–90% of commits and 89–90% of code blocks trace back to proactive triggers rather than reactive responses to bugs or failed tests. In this case study, development is mostly forward-moving rather than purely error-driven.

The most informative numbers are about hidden errors and conversational reliability. By mining transcripts rather than only commits, the authors estimate that 14.3% of AI code-generation events contain a real error that is later caught by the AI-authored test suite before any commit is made. Standard commit-based analysis would miss these errors entirely. For user-facing responses, Claude is relatively reliable when reporting or verifying facts at 94.3% accuracy, somewhat worse when explaining an existing mechanism at 91.1%, lower again for root-cause diagnosis at 89.3%, and substantially weaker when proposing a design fix at 79.4%. Overall, roughly one in four to five interactive responses contains at least one inaccuracy. That result is important because it shows that code generation ability and explanation reliability are related but not interchangeable.

The empirical strength of the paper is not breadth across many repositories. It is traceability. The authors recover intermediate mistakes, temporary hypotheses, and corrected misconceptions that are usually erased from the visible software history.3d7:Tadc,方法由两部分组成：IterSynth 范式本身，以及配套的 Role-Decoupled Policy Optimization（RDPO）。

先看 IterSynth。它把一次 deep search 拆成 Planner 和 Synthesizer 两个交替角色，但这两个角色不是两套模型，而是同一个 LLM 在不同 role prompt/格式下的两种行为模式。Planner 只看压缩后的 summary state，负责判断还缺什么信息、下一步该搜什么、何时继续探索。Synthesizer 读取新检索到的证据，对 summary 做增量更新：吸收有用事实、处理冲突、丢弃噪声、维护当前结论和未解决问题。这样，summary 不再是外部 memory module 的被动压缩结果，而是 agent policy 的显式输出和持久状态。

这个设计同时解决两个问题。对 role coupling，它通过角色分工降低单步决策的能力混杂度。Planner 不需要在长证据块里写最终答案，Synthesizer 也不需要决定全局搜索策略。对 context accumulation，它不再把完整历史一直塞回上下文，而是让 summary 成为受控、紧凑、可更新的状态表示。相比多 agent 系统，它不需要多模型协作和额外部署复杂度；相比已有 summary-based agent，它把摘要更新纳入训练目标，而不是把 summarization 当外接工具。

再看训练。作者采用 SFT → RL 的两阶段 recipe。SFT 的作用是教会模型 Planner–Synthesizer 协议、角色切换格式和基本迭代搜索行为，但作者明确指出 imitation 只能学会“怎么按这个协议行动”，不能充分优化“什么时候搜、搜什么、保留什么证据、两个角色如何协同”。因此引入 RDPO。

RDPO 的关键不是简单加一个中间奖励，而是按角色做 credit assignment。它把终局 outcome reward 和 turn-level rubric evaluation 结合起来，再分别为 Planner 和 Synthesizer 计算 group-relative advantages。这样做的动机很直接：Planner 的好坏更多体现在 query 是否有信息增益、是否识别到知识缺口、是否避免冗余搜索；Synthesizer 的好坏则体现在证据整合、冲突处理和 summary 更新质量。如果沿用普通 GRPO 或 outcome-only RL，两个角色共享一条回报，梯度会把不同错误来源混在一起，尤其在长轨迹里更严重。RDPO 通过 role-specific advantage 让更新方向更贴近各自职责。

从范式上看，这篇工作和 ReAct 的差异不只是“多了摘要”，而是把搜索过程从线性 action history 改成了围绕 summary state 的迭代闭环。和外部 summarizer 方法相比，它避免了摘要器与主 policy 目标不一致的问题。和多 agent 方法相比，它保留单参数集部署优势，同时通过角色解耦获得部分 specialization 收益。3d8:T9f2,The method has two parts: the IterSynth search paradigm and the associated Role-Decoupled Policy Optimization (RDPO) training objective.

IterSynth alternates between two roles, Planner and Synthesizer, instantiated by the same LLM rather than by separate models. The Planner reads only the compact summary state and decides what information is still missing, what to search next, and whether exploration should continue. The Synthesizer reads newly retrieved evidence and updates the persistent summary by integrating useful facts, resolving conflicts, filtering noise, and maintaining the current state of knowledge. In this design, the summary is not an external memory artifact. It is the explicit, learned state of the search process.

This addresses both target problems. Role coupling is reduced because planning and evidence integration are no longer forced into the same local decision. Context accumulation is reduced because the agent no longer carries the full search history forward; it carries a controlled, compact, updateable state instead. Compared with multi-agent systems, this avoids extra models and coordination overhead. Compared with prior summary-based agents, it makes summary updating part of the policy itself rather than an auxiliary external module.

Training follows an SFT-to-RL recipe. SFT teaches the Planner–Synthesizer protocol, role formatting, and basic iterative search behavior. But the authors explicitly note that imitation mainly teaches the interaction pattern, not the deeper decisions of when to search, what evidence to preserve, or how the two roles should coordinate. That is why they introduce RDPO.

RDPO combines terminal outcome rewards with turn-level rubric evaluations and computes group-relative advantages separately for Planner and Synthesizer actions. The motivation is straightforward: the Planner should be rewarded for identifying information gaps, issuing informative queries, and avoiding redundant exploration, while the Synthesizer should be rewarded for evidence integration, conflict handling, and summary quality. Standard outcome-only GRPO mixes these error sources together, which is especially harmful in long trajectories. Role-specific advantages make the gradient signal better aligned with each role’s responsibility.

Conceptually, the difference from ReAct is not just the addition of summaries. IterSynth changes the search loop from a linear action history into an iterative process centered on an explicit summary state. That is the main modeling contribution.3d9:T60c,The headline result is that IterSynth-8B reaches 50.7% average performance across five long-horizon deep-search benchmarks: GAIA-text-only, xBench-2505, xBench-2510, BrowseComp, and BrowseComp-ZH. This is 4.2 points above the strongest prior agent at 8B or below, while remaining competitive with several 30B-scale agents at less than one third of the parameter budget.

The training ablations are particularly informative. The SFT baseline scores 44.1%. Outcome-only GRPO raises this to 48.9%. RDPO further improves it to 50.7%. So RL itself contributes a large gain, and role-decoupled credit assignment adds another 1.8 points on top. The paper notes that this extra gain is strongest on exploration-heavy benchmarks, which suggests that RDPO improves search behavior rather than only answer polishing.

A key diagnostic appears in Appendix H: even with a 64K context window, more than 59% of ReAct trajectories on BrowseComp fail to terminate before context exhaustion. This directly supports the paper’s claim that the bottleneck is not simply context length, but the way search state is represented and updated.

The prompting-transfer results are also useful. IterSynth is not only a trainable 8B-agent recipe; it also works as a prompting paradigm for frontier models such as Claude-4.5-Opus and DeepSeek-V3.1, consistently outperforming ReAct and IterResearch, with gains of up to 10 points over ReAct on BrowseComp-ZH. That suggests the paradigm captures a generally better search organization rather than a narrow model-specific trick.3da:T42b,Start with the Introduction and Figure 1. The paper clearly contrasts three paradigms: multi-agent decomposition, external summarization, and IterSynth. Once that structural difference is clear, the rest of the method becomes much easier to follow.

Then read the methodology in two passes. First, focus on what each role sees and produces, and how the summary state is updated. Second, study RDPO carefully, especially why advantages are computed separately by role instead of using a single GRPO-style return for the whole trajectory. If you have worked on agent RL before, this is the part where the paper’s real contribution becomes obvious.

In the experiments, prioritize the main benchmark table, the ablations, and Appendix H. The main table answers whether the method works, the ablations explain why, and Appendix H shows where ReAct actually breaks. If time is limited, read the average benchmark results, the SFT → GRPO → RDPO progression, and the prompting-transfer section. A quick pass takes under an hour; a careful read takes around 90 minutes.3db:T412,TRACER uses a two-stage training recipe. First, supervised fine-tuning on real user dialogues teaches the model to generate user responses and to emit structured annotations: a rationale and an ordinal intent score. The intent score acts as an interpretable proxy for the user’s evolving commitment or engagement state. Second, the simulator is trained with multi-turn reinforcement learning while interacting with a fixed assistant. Rewards combine terminal outcome agreement and trajectory alignment against paired human logs. Dynamic time warping is used to align trajectories with different lengths and conversational pacing. A deviation-aware advantage modulation mechanism then uses local alignment errors, accumulated over discounted trajectory suffixes, to scale turn-level policy updates while preserving the direction of the session-level advantage. Compared with static persona prompting, the method optimizes state evolution; compared with standard turn-level optimization, it assigns credit using the whole dialogue trajectory.3dc:T563,The method has two parts. First, the authors define and measure SBW lock-in. Given T recorded denoising steps, they inspect a midpoint checkpoint and a recent window before it. If the extracted answer is valid and identical throughout that window, the example is labeled as an early lock-in. The locked answer is then compared with the gold answer to decide whether it is correct or wrong. A key part of the analysis is a surface-matched protocol: correct and wrong lock-ins are paired so that observable statistics such as confidence, entropy, margin, and answer stability are closely balanced. This isolates the contribution of hidden states.

Second, they propose LOCKR, a lightweight test-time planner. LOCKR uses the observed hidden-state trajectory as the planning state. A trajectory-based risk detector decides whether to continue the current denoising path or enter repair. If repair is triggered, targeted remasking creates a fixed bank of local counterfactual branches. These branches are continued, scored by a trajectory-aware verifier, and a final selector chooses the retained continuation. Compared with full restart or uniform extra computation, LOCKR spends compute only on high-risk cases. Compared with a single hidden-state snapshot, it models how hidden representations evolve during denoising, which is where much of the reliability signal appears to live.3dd:T6ef,DPara 的关键做法是把 DSpark-style drafter 拆成“重的 diffusion backbone”和“轻的 autoregressive head”。在 target model 正在 verify 当前 draft 时，DPara 不去猜最终 accepted prefix 和 bonus token，而是让 diffusion backbone 为所有可能的 acceptance boundary 预先计算 draft representations，并且暂时不绑定 bonus token。等 verification 结果返回后，真实的 accepted boundary 和 bonus token 已经确定，再由轻量 AR head 把这些信息接进去生成下一轮可用 draft。这样，概率性错误不再导致 backbone fallback；只要 backbone 能在 target verification window 内跑完，backbone 延迟就被完全隐藏，关键路径上只剩 AR head。

标准 DFlash 并不能直接满足这个使用方式，因为它通常依赖单个带有上下文 feature 的 anchor，而 DPara 需要同时覆盖多个 acceptance boundary，并从 feature-less anchors 预测。论文因此提出 M-DFlash：从公开 DSpark checkpoint 初始化，只 finetune diffusion backbone，让它适配 multiple-anchor、feature-less 的输入 regime；AR head 保持冻结，不引入新的可训练参数。这一点很重要，因为它说明 DPara 不是重新训练一个完整 drafter，而是用较小代价把已有 DSpark-style drafter 改造成适合并行排程的版本。

与 SSD/PEARL 这类方法相比，DPara 的差别不在于“更会猜 outcome”，而是不再把 overlap 建立在猜测 outcome 上。与普通 DSpark 相比，DPara 保留了 parallel drafter 的 acceptance 能力，同时把最重的 backbone 从串行 draft-verify 路径里拿掉。代价是需要为多个 boundary 准备 backbone 输出，并要求额外 drafting 设备或足够的同机资源来保证 overlap window。3de:T68a,DPara exploits the internal structure of a DSpark-style drafter: a heavy diffusion backbone followed by a lightweight autoregressive head. While the target model verifies the current speculative block, DPara runs the diffusion backbone ahead of time for every possible acceptance boundary and leaves the bonus token unspecified. Once verification completes, the true accepted boundary and bonus token are known; the lightweight AR head then conditions on that outcome and produces the next draft tokens. As long as the backbone finishes within the target verification window, the dominant part of drafting latency is hidden, and only the AR head remains on the critical path.

A standard DFlash backbone is not directly suitable for this schedule. In the serial setting, it anchors prediction on a single token after a fully featured prefix. DPara needs predictions from multiple feature-less anchors, one for each possible acceptance boundary. The paper introduces M-DFlash by initializing from a published DSpark checkpoint and finetuning only the diffusion backbone for this multiple-anchor, feature-less regime. The AR head is kept frozen, and no new trainable parameters are added.

The key difference from SSD or PEARL is that DPara does not try to make a better guess about the accepted prefix or bonus token. It removes the need for that guess. The key difference from serial DSpark is that DPara keeps the strong parallel drafter but moves the expensive backbone computation out of the serial draft-verify path. The cost is extra boundary coverage work and a requirement that drafting resources be provisioned well enough to complete inside the verification window.3df:T4d5,The evaluation uses Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-14B on math, coding, and chat benchmarks. DPara outperforms the baselines on every model-dataset pair. Average speedups over autoregressive decoding are 3.21× for Qwen3-8B and 3.52× for Qwen3-14B, with a maximum reported speedup of 4.53×. Compared with DSpark, the strongest serial drafter, average gains are 11.1% and 5.1%. On Qwen3-14B, DPara improves average speedup over PEARL and SSD by 31% and 64%, respectively.

The batching results are central. DPara remains ahead of DSpark from batch size 1 to 16 and keeps more than 2× AR throughput at batch size 16. Outcome-dependent methods such as SSD degrade more sharply as batch size increases because a mismatch in any request can push the batch back to serial execution.

The resource studies are also informative. DPara-A10 preserves 98% of DPara's speedup while reducing drafting-device cost by about 90%. DPara-single preserves roughly 90%–95% of the speedup at small batch sizes. An ablation shows that finetuning only the diffusion backbone increases average acceptance length by 30.7%, which supports the claim that the multiple-anchor feature-less regime needs adaptation rather than a direct reuse of the original DFlash backbone.3e0:T47e,Read the introduction and Figures 1–2 first. They clarify the difference between serial speculative decoding, SSD-style parallel speculative decoding, and DPara's outcome-independent overlap. The main point is the critical path, not the acceptance-rejection math.

The DPara design section deserves close reading. Focus on why bonus-token conditioning is deferred to the AR head, and why the system covers all acceptance boundaries instead of predicting a single likely boundary. The M-DFlash section is the other technical core: the distribution shift from standard DFlash to multiple feature-less anchors explains why finetuning the backbone is necessary.

For experiments, prioritize Section 4.2 for speedups and batch scaling, then Section 4.3 for heterogeneous drafting and single-GPU colocation. Good follow-up questions are compute redundancy across boundaries, memory pressure, overlap conditions for different target/drafter size ratios, and interaction with production serving schedulers.3e1:T482,The proposed method is UMIM. It first builds a merge set from a general corpus by collecting frequent contiguous n-grams of length 2 to 4. At inference time, merge candidates are selected with a longest-match rule when spans overlap. For each selected span, UMIM takes the static token embeddings and uses a lightweight single-layer attention module to produce one surrogate embedding, which replaces the original multi-token embeddings at the input layer.

The merge module is trained with predictive distillation. The pretrained LM is frozen, and only the merge module is updated so that the next-token distribution under compressed inputs matches the distribution under the original uncompressed sequence. The context-independent design makes the module reusable, but it is also a limitation: the same n-gram receives the same surrogate wherever it appears, which may be brittle for ambiguous phrases or spans whose role depends strongly on surrounding context. The method is applied to both prompt compression and autoregressive decoding context compression, with rollback used to replace multi-token KV-cache entries by single-step surrogate states.3e2:T647,Uncheatable Eval treats a language model as an ideal lossless compressor. For a document s, tokenized by the evaluated model's own tokenizer into x1:T, the model assigns conditional probabilities to observed tokens. The ideal arithmetic-coding length is -sum log2 p(x_t | x_<t), which is next-token NLL in bits. The compression rate divides this ideal code length by the original UTF-8 size, 8 times the number of bytes. Lower CR means better prediction. The UTF-8 denominator provides a common text-level scale across different tokenizers, although each score remains a property of the model-tokenizer pair.

The data pipeline is a central part of the benchmark. It periodically collects recently published fiction, source code, scientific papers, news, encyclopedia articles, documentation, and related sources, covering 14 text categories. The curation pipeline applies quality filters, removes near-duplicates with MinHash locality-sensitive hashing, and normalizes Unicode with NFC. The non-English encyclopedia subset is sampled in a language-balanced way. Because tokenizers produce different token counts for the same text, each sample is checked with a diverse set of tokenizers and truncated to fit a shared token budget.

Within each category, CR is aggregated as a byte-weighted ratio of total ideal code length to total original byte size. The Overall score is an unweighted arithmetic mean over category rates. This prevents large categories from dominating the final number, but it also means the Overall score reflects a balanced category mixture rather than a natural web-text distribution.3e3:T4fa,The paper evaluates 80 models across 14 text categories, including attention-based, hybrid, and recurrent families. A main finding is that compression rate scales systematically with model size and is well fit by a power law with an additive constant. This mirrors the shape of pretraining scaling laws, but on a dynamic held-out compression metric rather than training loss or task accuracy.

A separate analysis on longer scientific documents covers 54 models and studies how CR changes as more preceding context becomes available. The results show different context-use patterns for attention-based, hybrid, and recurrent models. This is a useful long-context diagnostic because it measures prediction improvement within real documents as context accumulates, rather than relying on short prompted tasks.

The paper also compares compression of technical text with zero-shot MMLU accuracy and finds a strong association. This suggests that predictive ability on technical corpora is statistically related to knowledge-heavy task performance. The relationship should not be read as a replacement for MMLU: compression isolates base-model prediction, while MMLU also depends on answer formatting, multiple-choice behavior, reasoning over options, and post-training effects.3e4:T5d8,There are two main components. First, FakeContext-bench. Each instance contains demonstrations consistent with a contextual rule P, a query, and two reference answers: y_R under the real rule and y_P under the misleading contextual rule. Outputs are categorized into Reality, Context, or Other using a deterministic rule-based judge, with human validation of the scoring protocol. The benchmark spans seven domains: physics, mathematics, chemistry, biology, statistics, history, and computer science. The point is not domain difficulty, but controlled construction of cases where the context is coherent yet lacks real authority.

Second, Jurisdiction In-Context Learning (J-ICL). The method keeps the standard few-shot interface and uses only query-only LM loss. In J+ episodes, the demonstrated rule genuinely applies to the query, so the correct answer should follow the context. In J- episodes, the demonstrations still support a coherent rule, but that rule is private, conflicting, or undeployed, while the query requires the reality-grounded or formally valid answer. No explicit authority labels, auxiliary classifier, or rationale supervision is added. The model is expected to infer applicability from natural-language cues and episode structure. This is the key distinction from methods such as MetaICL or Symbol Tuning, which mainly improve rule extraction from demonstrations. J-ICL tries to train both rule induction and rule applicability judgment within the same prompting format.3e5:T63d,The empirical story has three important parts. First, baseline diagnosis: both proprietary and open-weight models are vulnerable on FakeContext-bench. Larger scale and stronger pretraining do not reliably yield context-authority discrimination. The failure is often not that the model misses the demonstrated pattern, but that it successfully infers the false rule and applies it where it should not.

Second, existing ICL-tuning methods can worsen the problem. The paper reports that prevalent ICL fine-tuning approaches improve conventional few-shot performance but can reduce reality-grounded accuracy by as much as 14.95 percentage points relative to the base model under misleading context. This is the central result, because it shows a systematic objective-level trade-off rather than a mere capability gap.

Third, J-ICL mitigates that trade-off. Training with mixed J+ and J- episodes improves robustness to misleading context while preserving, and in some settings improving, standard ICL ability. The abstract does not expose the full table of numbers, but the full paper appears to emphasize: (1) higher Reality rates and lower Context rates on FakeContext-bench, (2) no major collapse on conventional few-shot tasks, and (3) ablations showing that the gain does not come from simply adding negative examples, but from exposing the model to both apply-context and reject-context episodes in a shared format. When reading the tables, it is worth checking model-size trends, the behavior of different ICL-tuning recipes, and how J+/J- mixture ratios affect Reality/Context/Other outputs.3e6:T552,Start with the problem framing in the introduction. Then read the benchmark construction and scoring protocol. The input is a registry of human-written skills spanning 12 major categories and 63 sub-categories. Each skill is first organized into a structured skill card containing descriptions, examples, pseudocode or scripts, and execution constraints. For each sub-category, the authors manually design reusable templates that instantiate concrete tasks from these reusable workflows, including input assets, interaction interfaces, target conditions, and code-based verifiers. This turns a static skill document into an executable environment.

A key design choice is contrastive validation. Under a reference agent configuration, the system runs tasks with and without the target skill and keeps tasks that show empirical skill dependence. This matters because many tasks associated with a skill document may still be solvable by generic capability alone. Without this filtering step, the resulting supervision would overstate the contribution of the skill itself.

Once environments are validated, the authors collect successful trajectories using multiple teacher models and harnesses. These trajectories can support supervised fine-tuning and outcome-based reinforcement learning. The paper mainly demonstrates the SFT path: verified long-horizon workflows are used to fine-tune Qwen3.5-35B-A3B into SkillGym-Agent.
