Human scientists provide a high-level prompt asking Claude to search DNA sequence databases for interesting reverse transcriptase examples. Claude reads the relevant literature, reproduces established results on public data to check its methods, searches protein families and genomic neighborhoods for systems that do not match known categories, and writes short reports for candidates with proposed functions and supporting evidence. Follow-up Claude sessions critique the evidence and eliminate many weak candidates. Human scientists then review the survivors and test them in the lab. The important design choice is not asking the model for a direct answer. The workflow decomposes discovery into literature calibration, database search, anomaly detection, candidate reporting, self-critique, expert filtering, and biochemical follow-up. The team also studies the model’s generated hypotheses as data, comparing candidates that experts keep against those they discard, then feeding those lessons back into instructions.3eb:T450,Terminal Shrinkage Averaging returns an interpolation between the last checkpoint and the mean of the last K checkpoints: (1-α)θ_T + α\bar{θ}_T. α=0 recovers the raw final iterate, and α=1 recovers uniform LAWA. Since the final checkpoint is included in the average, its total weight is 1-α+α/K, while each earlier checkpoint receives α/K. The analysis uses a local quadratic approximation to the loss over the short terminal region. Checkpoints are decomposed into their across-run mean and stochastic residuals, and risk is measured in the Hessian-induced seminorm. Under this model, the expected surrogate risk is quadratic in α. The expression exposes the tradeoff: averaging older checkpoints can move the mean away from the local optimum, but it can also reduce stochastic terminal variation. This gives conditions where the best α lies strictly between raw final iterate and full LAWA. The same framework explains why an averaged estimator can prefer a higher terminal learning-rate floor: the trajectory keeps making progress late in training, while the estimator damps endpoint noise.3ec:T432,The experiments are designed around the interaction rather than only the main effects. Depth-12 NanoChat runs first show that the best shrinkage coefficient is inside the interval, not at α=0 or α=1. A paired factorial experiment then crosses terminal learning-rate floors of 5%, 10%, and 15% of peak LR with two output estimators, raw final iterate and TSA, using five repetitions. Increasing the floor worsens validation BPB when deploying the raw endpoint, but improves validation BPB when deploying TSA; the effect grows as the floor is raised. A replication with pure AdamW preserves the direction of the interaction, so the result is not tied to the Muon+AdamW optimizer mix used in NanoChat. The higher-floor-plus-TSA recipe is also applied to a depth-22 NanoChat time-to-GPT-2 setting, where it improves over the public recipe at matched budget and yields a qualifying benchmark run. The provided material does not include the exact BPB table, so the reliable quantitative details are the floor values, repetition count, model depths, and direction of the effects.3ed:T7dd,Hill Sampling is intentionally minimal. Start from an initial program x0. At each round, sample N candidate edits from a frozen LLM conditioned on the current incumbent xt. Execute each candidate with the verifier, obtain rewards, and replace the incumbent if the best candidate in the round matches or exceeds the best reward seen so far. The algorithm stores the incumbent’s historical best reward rather than re-evaluating it every round, which is important when execution is stochastic. Equal-reward replacements are allowed to preserve some structural diversity. There is no archive, no crossover, no explicit diversity objective, and no parameter update. The main knobs are decoding temperature, samples per round, and number of rounds.

The paper is stronger because it does not stop at introducing the method. It systematically compares three exploration families. First, repeated sampling, where all generations are drawn independently from the same starting point. Relative to that baseline, Hill Sampling adds exactly one persistent state: the best-so-far program fed back into context. Second, evolution strategies applied directly to LLM weights. The authors build a large-scale ES pipeline and separate standard ES learning from a zero-learning-rate variant that keeps only random weight perturbations. This isolates exploration from learning. Third, they test common add-ons such as diversity encouragement, solution combination, extra exploration mechanisms, and code-execution feedback. The conclusion is that none of these are necessary to obtain strong results in this setting.

Mechanistically, Hill Sampling treats the LLM as a conditional editor rather than a one-shot generator. The incumbent acts as a moving scaffold. Future samples are drawn near the current best program instead of restarting from the original problem statement. That creates a simple local search process in context space, not in parameter space. The paper’s main contribution is showing how far that alone can go.3ee:T79c,The evaluation covers three verifiable mathematical optimization problems with three open-weight models: circle packing with gpt-oss-20b, sums/differences of finite sets with OLMo-3.1-32B-Instruct, and Erdős’ minimum-overlap problem with Mistral-Small-3.1-24B-Instruct. The emphasis is practical wall-clock performance, not only sample efficiency.

The headline result is on circle packing: Hill Sampling reaches the best published result in under five hours on eight H100 GPUs. On the Erdős minimum-overlap problem, it surpasses the AlphaEvolve algorithmic-discovery reference within 12 hours. The abstract is truncated, but the body makes the qualitative outcome clear: one new published best result and strong competitive performance on the other tasks.

The ablations are the most informative part. Hill Sampling substantially outperforms repeated sampling, showing that best-so-far conditioning is the main source of gain. Standard ES often improves mean return while reducing maximum return, which directly supports the paper’s framing that mean-oriented updates can be misaligned with discovery objectives. Setting the ES learning rate to zero removes learning but keeps random weight perturbations; this sometimes preserves maximum return better than learned ES, yet still underperforms plain token-sampling randomness from the unperturbed model. That is a useful boundary condition for claims about nearby experts in pretrained weight space: even if such experts exist, searching for them may be less effective than output-space exploration when exact verification is available.

The paper also compares Hill Sampling with N=64 and N=512 under the same total sampling budget, changing the trade-off between more frequent incumbent updates and larger within-round candidate sets. That distinction has direct implications for verifier-guided decoding, best-of-N methods, and some RL-style test-time adaptation setups.3f0:T82e,The method, GravityOCR, is a parameter-shared AR–block-diffusion model built by adapting GLM-OCR. The same decoder is run under two attention patterns. The first path is a block-diffusion drafter. The output sequence is partitioned into contiguous blocks of size at most B. Dependencies remain causal across blocks, but attention is bidirectional within the current block. During training, a random subset of positions in the current block is masked and the model learns to denoise them conditioned on the completed prefix and the partially observed block. At inference, the current block starts fully masked and is iteratively denoised to produce a draft block in parallel.

The second path is a causal AR verifier. Given the same prefix, it checks the draft token by token and commits only the longest prefix that matches AR greedy predictions. Once a mismatch appears, commitment stops and the next drafting round begins. This design is the key idea: the diffusion path proposes, but the AR path decides. With top-1 verification, the committed output matches pure AR greedy decoding in exact arithmetic, so acceleration comes from accepting multiple drafted tokens per round rather than changing the final decision rule.

This differs from standard speculative decoding, which usually relies on a separate small drafter or an auxiliary multi-token head. Here both drafting and verification use the full shared backbone. Training combines the original AR NLL with a block-diffusion denoising objective so the model can operate under both masks. Post-training then applies GRPO only through the causal AR path using OCR rewards at the sequence and structure levels. The rationale is clean: optimize the path that determines the final output, and let shared parameters transfer improvements to the drafter indirectly. The paper also contrasts direct block-diffusion commitment with self-speculative verification. Direct commitment offers more parallelism but is brittle on tables, formulas, and other structurally coupled outputs; verification trades some parallelism for AR-like reliability.3f1:T69d,The model is evaluated on OmniDocBench v1.6 after adapting GLM-OCR. Four results matter most. First, the final model retains almost all of the original AR model’s quality: 95.16 Overall versus 95.48 for the base GLM-OCR, or about 99.7% retention. Second, GRPO applied only through the AR path improves the score from 94.92 to 95.16, showing that reward optimization helps the final verifier-controlled output without breaking the shared drafter. Third, with a full self-speculative implementation in SGLang, the system reaches 9.7 tokens per forward, counting both diffusion drafting and AR verification passes. This yields a 3.94× speedup in token generation and a 1.32× speedup in end-to-end page processing over causal AR decoding. The gap between those two numbers is informative: decoder token loops are only part of the total OCR latency budget. Fourth, the paper characterizes the accuracy–parallelism trade-off. Direct block diffusion is more aggressive but loses more accuracy; self-speculative verification is limited by draft–verifier agreement, and that agreement becomes the main determinant of practical speedup.

The ablations worth noting involve block size, denoising schedule, verification behavior, and task type. A solid skim should take about 20–30 minutes.3f3:T835,技术方案分两层。第一层是 selective absorption 机制。作者给每个位置加一个二值 absorption indicator；一旦某个位置被 absorb，它的 outgoing transition rate 置零，不再参与后续 CTMC 演化。这样就把原来“所有位置持续更新”的 uniform discrete flow，改成“部分位置冻结、其余位置继续流动”的混合过程。关键约束是：对仍然 active 的位置，保持原来的 uniform-flow velocity，不去改训练目标，也不重写 denoiser。

第二层是如何决定吸收顺序。随机吸收显然不行，因为一旦把错 token 固定住，就失去后续纠错机会。作者提出 LEDFlow，用 predictive entropy 做局部可靠性估计：每一步在给定 absorption budget 下，选当前熵最低的 active positions，把它们按当前最可能 token 固定下来；其余位置继续按 kinetic-optimal velocity 更新。下一步再重新计算熵，因此顺序是自适应的，而不是预先排好的静态 order。

理论部分的重点不是证明整个 sampler 全局最优，而是分析“不可逆吸收”引入的误差。作者把 stepwise absorption error 分解成两个 KL 项：一个对应被同时吸收位置之间的 joint dependence 丢失，另一个对应在已吸收上下文条件下的 conditional prediction error。随后在 oracle-reachable states 和 entropy-error regularity 的假设下，证明在固定吸收预算时，选择最低熵位置可以最小化 conditional error 上界。这个论证的意义在于解释为什么局部熵是合理信号，而不是仅凭经验有效。

作者还专门讨论了 global entropy lookahead。直觉上，往前看几步似乎能做更优决策，但论文指出在 denoiser 不完美时，未来状态估计误差会层层累积，decision error bound 会随 lookahead window 增长。也就是说，复杂的全局规划未必比局部熵更稳，反而更贵、更脆弱。这一点和很多生成式推理系统里的经验是相通的：如果模型本身有偏差，过深的 rollout 可能放大而不是消除误差。3f4:T89f,The method has two layers. The first is selective absorption. Each position is assigned a binary absorption indicator; once a position is absorbed, its outgoing transition rates are set to zero, so it no longer evolves under the CTMC. This changes the original all-positions-update regime of uniform discrete flow into a mixed process where some positions are frozen and others continue to move. A key design choice is that the velocity on active positions is left unchanged, so the method does not alter the trained denoiser or the underlying flow objective.

The second layer is the absorption policy. Randomly freezing positions is risky because an incorrect absorbed token cannot be corrected later. The proposed sampler, LEDFlow, uses predictive entropy as a local reliability signal. At each step, under a fixed absorption budget, it selects the active positions with the lowest entropy and absorbs them using their current most likely values. The remaining positions continue evolving under the kinetic-optimal velocity. Entropy is recomputed at every step, so the generation order is adaptive rather than predetermined.

The theory is framed around the error introduced by irreversible absorption. The authors decompose the stepwise absorption error into two KL terms: one for the loss of joint dependence among simultaneously absorbed positions, and one for conditional prediction error under the context created by previously absorbed values. Under assumptions on oracle-reachable states and entropy-error regularity, they show that, with a fixed absorption budget, choosing the lowest-entropy positions minimizes an upper bound on the conditional error term. This does not prove global optimality, but it gives a principled reason why local entropy is the right signal.

The paper also analyzes global entropy lookahead. In principle, evaluating future successor states could yield better decisions. In practice, with an imperfect denoiser, future-state estimation errors accumulate, and the decision-error bound grows with the lookahead window. The implication is important: more global planning is not necessarily more reliable, and can be both slower and less robust than a local entropy rule.3f5:T61d,The experiments span three task groups: structured reasoning, multimodal understanding, and text-to-image generation. The reasoning results are the most informative because they expose the exact failure mode the method is designed to fix.

In the Sudoku trajectory diagnostic, the native kinetic-optimal sampler produces 9.4% correct-to-wrong reversions, while LEDFlow reduces this to 2.6%. The fraction of token changes occurring after t = 0.75 also drops from 46% to 15%, which is a strong mechanistic result: the method is not just improving final accuracy, it is specifically suppressing unstable late revisions.

On Nikoli Sudoku, LEDFlow reaches 0.845 solve accuracy and achieves the best average rank across nine reasoning tasks. The pattern matters more than the single number: gains are largest on tasks with strong structural dependence, where late token flips are especially costly.

For text-to-image generation, LEDFlow achieves the best GenEval overall score among decode-time samplers, with a 2.8% absolute improvement over the native sampler. For multimodal understanding, it improves over the native sampler on all six reported benchmarks. The ablations are also useful. For lookahead, mean absolute score error rises from 0.17 with a single lookahead term to 1.76 under full lookahead, while longer lookahead can cost about 8x more inference time without meaningful gains. That empirical pattern lines up well with the theoretical analysis.3f6:T464,This is a skim paper, but it is worth a careful read if you work on diffusion LM, discrete flow, or any-order generation. The central condition is simple: a flip occurs when the original logit gap between the winning token and a competitor is smaller than the precision-induced directional perturbation along that pairwise decision direction. Body error accumulates through the transformer, but it is not sufficient to separate flipping from non-flipping steps. The trainable correction has 434,176 parameters.3fb:T87f,The proposed method, QuantWM, is a training-free 2-bit KV-cache quantization framework. Its goal is not merely to reduce Key/Value reconstruction error, but to explicitly preserve attention logits and temporal consistency. It builds on the centroid-residual representation used in QVG: each Key is assigned to a BF16 centroid, and only the residual is quantized to low bitwidth. The paper argues that QVG is limited because centroid selection is driven mainly by K-means geometry, which optimizes feature-space distance rather than downstream impact on QK^T.

The first component is QSAC, quantization-sensitivity-aware clustering. Instead of selecting centroids purely by Key-space clustering quality, QSAC jointly considers Query sensitivity and residual dynamic range, aiming to reduce the effect of INT2 residual quantization on attention logits. Intuitively, some Key directions may have small Euclidean error but still be highly dangerous if they align with Query-sensitive directions and alter token ranking. QSAC tries to avoid such residual structures already at the clustering stage.

The second component is PSAC, principal-subspace attention compensation. Even with better clustering, Key quantization error can still be amplified along dominant Query directions and distort logits. PSAC extracts the principal Query subspace and uses low-rank projections to represent and compensate the Key error components along those sensitive directions during inference. The idea is not to fully reconstruct Keys, which is unrealistic at 2 bits, but to correct the error components that matter most for attention allocation. This is a different philosophy from simply increasing quantization fidelity: it accepts that full preservation is impossible and spends the available budget on the subspace that most affects retrieval behavior.

The overall design is coherent: QSAC makes Keys more quantization-friendly before compression, and PSAC compensates the most harmful attention shifts after compression. Because the method is training-free, it is intended as a practical drop-in replacement for existing KV-cache compression pipelines in video generation and world models.3fc:T53a,The experiments cover several representative models, including LingBot-World-v2, Matrix-Game-2, LongCat-Video, HY-World 1.5, and Causal-Forcing, which suggests the authors are aiming for architecture-agnostic evidence rather than a single-model result. The headline outcome is that QuantWM substantially reduces temporal flickering, blur, and artifacts under 2-bit KV quantization while maintaining strong benchmark performance on metrics such as VBench. It also achieves up to 6.20x KV-cache memory compression with limited inference overhead.

The most important evidence comes from the diagnostic ablations. The paper separates Key-only and Value-only quantization and shows that most degradation comes from Keys. It then compares reconstruction errors and finds that Keys can have smaller numerical error than Values despite causing worse output quality. That result supports the paper's central claim: KV quantization should not be judged mainly by reconstruction magnitude, but by its effect on attention logits and token ranking. The authors fix a ReAct-style coding-agent harness on a multi-tool aggregation task and evaluate protocol fidelity rather than task success. The design has three important pieces.

First, it separates channel from prompt. “Channel” means tool schemas are passed through the native tools= field and then rendered and parsed by the server. “Prompt” means the tool list and JSON call format are written directly into the textual prompt. The paper compares three settings: native, which uses tools= only; native+hint, which still uses tools= but also injects a plain-text tool list and strict JSON format instructions; and text-tools, which removes tools= entirely and parses calls from text. This isolates server-side protocol handling from the model’s ability to follow tool instructions.

Second, it refines the label space. Each assistant turn is categorized as valid in-schema call, hallucinated call, unparseable text, no-call prose, or non-response. The non-response category is crucial. In Ollama, some models trigger HTTP 400 request rejection before inference; the harness retries, gives up, and writes a generic error string into the trajectory. If that error is not preserved as structured metadata, downstream analysis can count it as a model non-call. The paper therefore excludes non-responses from the fidelity denominator and reports them separately.

Third, it performs a multi-stack comparison. The same weights and the same request behave differently under Ollama, llama.cpp, vLLM, and SGLang: some stacks reject tools=, some accept it but return calls as plain text, and some require explicit parser configuration before a call is recognized. The point is not to rank stacks, but to show that the measured outcome is stack-dependent. Human FDE plus assistant baselines have judgment residuals of 0.06 and 0.09, while the closest autonomous agent reaches 0.10.401:T886,The method has a data component and a training component. For data, Video-HopChain does not simply concatenate single-hop video questions. Each example is a dependency chain of 3 to 6 hops. Every hop is a yes/no question about one or two moments in the same video, and each answer maps to one of two integers. The final answer is the sum across hops, which makes the task exactly verifiable by exact match. Two design choices matter. First, every question includes at least one temporal-order hop, so a single frame cannot contain all required evidence. Second, some hops are selectors: the answer to an earlier hop determines which later moment should be inspected next, creating real inter-hop dependence rather than a bag of independent subquestions. The generation pipeline first produces shot-level captions with a VLM, then uses a text-only LLM to synthesize the multi-hop question from those captions. This is a deliberate trade-off: direct end-to-end VLM question generation is harder to control and harder to verify, while operating in caption space gives tighter control over logic structure and answer form.

For training, the paper introduces Confidence-Gated Exploration on top of GRPO. Standard GRPO derives its signal from reward variance within a group of rollouts for the same prompt. If all rewards in the group are identical, the group yields no relative advantage. CGE addresses this without drawing extra rollouts. With group size G=8, the first 4 rollouts are sampled normally. If those 4 are all correct or all incorrect, the remaining 4 are sampled with a top-token mask inside the reasoning span. Whenever the model assigns more than tau=0.95 probability mass to a single token, that token is temporarily removed and sampling is renormalized over the rest. This is not generic noise injection; it is targeted exploration only when the model is highly confident and the group is likely to collapse. Masked positions are excluded from the token-level loss, but all 8 rollouts still participate in the group advantage computation. That avoids the extra rollout cost of resampling while also avoiding direct supervision on tokens that were explicitly perturbed.402:T512,The dataset contains 22,550 training questions over 13,378 videos, plus a held-out benchmark of 1,000 questions on 1,000 videos. The training target is Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, further optimized with GRPO and evaluated on 8 general-purpose video benchmarks. The base model averages 55.4 across the 8 benchmarks. Training on Video-HopChain raises this to 57.9, a gain of 2.5 points, and all 8 benchmarks improve rather than only a subset. That matters more than a single benchmark gain because it suggests the synthesized multi-hop supervision is not merely overfitting to its own task format. Adding CGE on top further raises the average to 59.3, another +1.4 over Video-HopChain alone and +3.9 over the original baseline.

The experimental narrative also ties CGE gains specifically to recovering collapsed groups rather than simply increasing randomness. Another useful aspect is that the paper emphasizes transfer to general video understanding benchmarks, not only performance on its own benchmark. That makes it more relevant as a training-signal paper than as a pure dataset release. The limitations are also clear: question generation is still bottlenecked by shot-caption quality, and the reward remains final-answer exact match, with no finer-grained credit assignment over intermediate hops.403:T57b,The key idea is to turn long-horizon decision quality into a binary choice at a decision fork. The authors observe that in software engineering and machine-learning research tasks, agents often make multiple attempts at the same task, or they take a detour and later correct themselves within a single run. If two trajectories share an equivalent prefix and then diverge, and if later evidence clearly shows which branch was better, that divergence can be converted into a taste question. Each question contains the task, the trajectory prefix up to the fork, and two candidate directions. The model must choose the better direction without seeing the later outcome. The benchmark is built from two mining procedures: parallel trajectories, where independent attempts diverge on the same task, and detour trajectories, where a single run reveals a wrong turn followed by correction. To reduce label noise, the authors do not simply use final success as supervision. They keep forks where the outcome difference can be credibly attributed to the judgment at the fork, using later evidence such as test results or research scores. On top of the benchmark, they introduce a training setup where a teacher model, given knowledge of the correct branch, produces reasoning that is then distilled into a student. This turns hindsight into a trainable judgment policy rather than a static benchmark-only signal.404:T437,The paper releases Taste-Bench, a benchmark of 502 taste questions spanning software engineering and machine-learning research tasks. The first set of experiments validates the benchmark itself: questions become harder as the horizon from the fork to the eventual outcome increases, which supports the claim that the benchmark measures long-horizon judgment rather than shallow pattern matching. The authors also perform human review and report close agreement between mined labels and human judgments when reviewers are allowed to inspect the recorded outcomes, which supports label quality. Model evaluations show that current systems still struggle on taste, and strong end-to-end performance does not automatically imply strong taste. The most important result is that taste appears trainable: distilling teacher reasoning conditioned on the correct direction improves fork judgments on unseen tasks and also leads to end-to-end gains on held-out agent tasks. Confidence analysis shows that many of JEV’s misses are concentrated in low-confidence regions, which makes selective escalation viable, but the paper also reports failures of threshold transfer on some workloads.407:T6ff,The paper is strongest in its controlled experimental design. Instead of making a generic complaint that compile rate is imperfect, it isolates five distinct failure modes of a metric. First, sensitivity to real improvement: if an intervention materially improves generated code, does compile rate move accordingly? Second, confounding by measurement setup: how much of the failure comes from the model versus the isolated-function harness, stub injection, syntax-only compilation, and dataset preprocessing artifacts? Third, toolchain dependence: does the same patch receive different judgments under different compilation configurations? Fourth, disagreement with an independent signal: does compile rate align with other indicators of repair quality? Fifth, gameability: if one optimizes toward compilation, does the system drift toward degenerate behaviors such as code deletion, conservative copying, or syntax-preserving but semantically useless edits?

The paper then studies the common similarity fallback, whole-function CodeBLEU, and shows why it fails structurally in this setting. Real fixes often modify only a small span, while most of the function remains unchanged. A metric computed over the whole function therefore gives large credit for preserved context, even when the vulnerability is untouched. To mitigate this, the authors examine diff_F1 as a change-aware screen rather than a repair-quality metric. It scores overlap only in the edited region, so a no-op copy gets zero credit, and some compile-oriented deletion patches receive near-zero credit as well. The authors are careful not to oversell it: diff_F1 can still over-credit some deletion-style patches, so it should be used as a filter before deeper analysis, not as a substitute for tests or exploit oracles.408:T68e,The empirical setup is reasonably substantial for this niche: 203 vulnerable functions from Big-Vul, spanning 7 CWEs; 3 open-source code LLMs ranging from 350M to 6.7B parameters; 3 prompting strategies; and 5 samples per setting, with bootstrap confidence intervals. Several results stand out.

First, compile rate is weakly responsive to interventions that materially improve generated code. The paper’s point is not just that the metric is noisy, but that it can miss genuine quality changes.

Second, roughly 64% of compile failures are not attributable to the model. They come from missing project context and a specific Big-Vul preprocessing artifact, and this share is nearly invariant across model sizes. This is the central quantitative result because it shows that the dominant source of failure is the evaluation setup, not the model.

Third, whole-function CodeBLEU is shown to be badly misleading: a no-op baseline that simply copies the vulnerable input scores higher than every tested model. That sharply limits its interpretability in single-function repair.

Fourth, diff_F1 behaves better on several observed gaming patterns. It gives zero credit to no-ops, near-zero credit to some deletion patches that compile by removing problematic code, and nonzero credit to edits overlapping the developer’s actual change. The paper also documents where this screen still fails.

Finally, the benchmark-scale comparison itself is useful. At inference time, two Audio Encoder + LLM paths are used. One path makes full-duplex decisions such as keep listening, start speaking, stop, or resume. The other generates response content as text. A context-aware voice renderer then uses the content, dialogue history, voice cues, and acoustic context to produce streaming speech. This separation makes the control problem cleaner: response content, turn-taking policy, and voice rendering have different constraints.

The Think layer uses a four-stage foundation post-training pipeline: Core-Cocktail cold start, Multimodality OPD, domain GRPO specialists, and Multi-Teacher OPD consolidation. Core-Cocktail starts from an audio-pretrained AudioLM and uses the source Text LLM as an anchor for shared language parameters. It then applies controlled SFT over audio and text instruction data. The foundation data scale is about one million hours of paired audio-text data, covering general audio understanding, spoken instruction following, multi-turn interaction, tool-oriented requests, emotion, empathy, pragmatic intent, and acoustic-scene understanding.

M2-OPD is the core capability-transfer mechanism. The Audio Student samples a response trajectory conditioned on audio. At each token position, the Text Teacher receives a semantically equivalent text prompt plus the same student prefix, while the frozen Audio Reference receives the original audio context plus the same prefix. Both provide token-level distributions on the student’s on-policy trajectory. The teacher does not generate a separate answer for imitation; it scores the states actually visited by the student. This design combines text-grounded reasoning supervision with audio-conditioned constraints.

The Act layer builds executable environments that include tools, policies, databases, and tasks. These environments are validated and evolved using rollout feedback. Training uses GRPO with dialogue-level, milestone-level, and turn-level rollouts. Dialogue-level rewards capture final task success, milestone-level rewards provide intermediate signals for long-horizon execution, and turn-level rewards handle local behavior such as tool-feedback interpretation or progress communication. This is a stronger formulation than function-call SFT because the target behavior includes execution state, policy constraints, refusal, and evidence-bounded communication.

The Speak and Coordinate layer learns a conversational policy over how, when, and whether to speak or act. It handles cases such as user interruption, waiting until the user finishes, changing the target while a query is running, or withholding unsupported conclusions. The separate Voice Harness introduces explicit task and memory boundaries for evaluation and control.40b:T4f5,The concrete scale reported in the provided material is approximately one million hours of paired audio-text data for the foundation recipe. Encoder-full systems use a dedicated perceptual encoder to produce continuous semantic features before the shared transformer. Encoder-free and discrete-token systems do not. The central hypothesis is that the missing perceptual computation is internalized by the front part of the shared transformer.

To test this, the authors use three complementary analyses. First, layerwise linear probing asks when modality-token hidden states become linearly decodable for concept identity. In encoder-full models, decodable semantics should already be present at the transformer input. In encoder-free and discrete-token models, semantic organization should emerge progressively with depth. Second, representational similarity analysis compares intermediate states with dedicated perceptual encoders to see whether early and middle layers exhibit encoder-like geometry. Third, causal intervention perturbs image and audio inputs and measures at what depths modality-token states remain causally necessary for the final output, which helps identify where the representation is formed and where it is read out.

Gemma 4 12B is the main target model. Cross-model comparisons include encoder-free EVE and Fuyu, discrete-token Chameleon, and encoder-full controls such as LLaVA-1.5, Qwen3-VL, Qwen3-Omni, and Qwen2-Audio. For aligned image-audio analysis, the paper builds a paired concept dataset from ImageNet-1k and ESC-50 with 31 shared concepts, 40 images and 40 audio clips per concept, for 1,240 samples per modality.

The key claim is not just that some layer performs well. It is that there exists a contiguous band of layers that transforms low-level perceptual structure into a readable semantic representation. That band is the Virtual Encoder. The paper also argues that post-readout routing differs by modality: in Gemma 4, vision briefly aligns with the language subspace near readout, while audio follows a different trajectory, suggesting that shared transformers do not collapse all modalities into one uniform internal stream.40e:T62b,There are four main findings. First, linear probing shows that concept decodability in encoder-free and discrete-token models rises progressively with depth, whereas encoder-full models enter the shared transformer with already organized perceptual representations. This supports the idea that perceptual encoding has been absorbed into the early transformer layers. Second, representational similarity analysis shows that early-to-middle hidden states in models such as Gemma 4 12B resemble dedicated perceptual encoders geometrically, indicating that these layers are not merely doing generic language processing. Third, causal analysis identifies the depth at which modality representations are read out: before a certain layer band, perturbing modality tokens strongly affects the output; after that point, the effect changes, suggesting that the encoded representation has already been handed off to later computation. Fourth, routing is modality-dependent. In Gemma 4, vision transiently approaches the language subspace near readout, while audio follows a markedly different path, implying asymmetric integration mechanisms across modalities.

The paper is more about trends and internal structure than benchmark scores. The only thing that changes across runs is the privileged context policy c_l(x) supplied to the teacher.

From the same problem-solution pairs, the authors compile several context levels offline. L1 is the full solution. L2 is a named strategy, giving a method label or strategy cue. L3 is a method-independent framing, which keeps the structural perspective but avoids committing to a specific derivation. L4 is a problem category, an even higher-level abstraction. L5 is answer-only, preserving the destination but removing the path. There is also a control condition that keeps only a fixed 10% prefix of the original solution plus the answer, which helps separate semantic abstraction from simple context shortening. Prompt templates and bridge wording are controlled, and within each model scale the student prompt, rollout procedure, loss, teacher checkpoint, and training set are held fixed.

Two methodological choices are especially important. First, the paper defines context utility by post-training student performance, not by a static property of the teacher distribution. That is the right target for this problem. Second, initial teacher-student KL is treated only as a diagnostic. This allows the authors to test a common intuition—that larger distributional displacement means better teaching—and show that it fails here.

Mechanistically, the difference is easy to state. A full solution gives the teacher one concrete derivation, so when the student deviates from that path the teacher may push probability mass back toward the reference trajectory. Abstract context keeps information about what kind of solution is appropriate while relaxing how it should be reached. In on-policy distillation, that changes the shape of the supervision signal, not just its strength.415:T79e,The main experiments are on competition mathematics. The right lens is not “math reasoning method” but “training signal design.” Two questions are worth deeper follow-up: whether the gains come mainly from reducing reference-path bias, and whether the same pattern transfers to reasoning SFT, verifier-guided self-training, or RL-style reasoning pipelines.417:T688,The formulation represents autoregressive generation and agentic interaction through a filtration. At each step the model emits a token and may receive an environment observation; the terminal reward is a function of the complete trajectory. The conditional reward prediction is defined as V_i = E[R | F_i]. The paper then imposes three regularity conditions on token credit: Completeness, which requires total credit to explain the deviation of the final reward from its initial prediction; Prefix Consistency, which prevents future tokens from rewriting the accumulated credit of an already generated prefix; and Neutrality, which requires no systematic over- or under-crediting from the current information state. These conditions yield a unique representation, essentially the martingale difference V_i - V_{i-1}. The same construction can be aggregated to coarser units such as turns. The paper uses this representation to reinterpret OPD, RLOO, and GAE-style actor-critic methods. Under an ideal teacher, OPD is equivalent in expectation, up to scale, to the policy-gradient update induced by the unique credit. RLOO uses a response-level signal, but its expected policy-gradient contribution matches that of the token-level credit. Under bounded rewards, token-level credit is approximately sparse, which helps explain the sensitivity of GAE-based actor-critic methods in long trajectories. The proposed algorithm, PACT, uses an Actor-then-Critic update order so that critic training can apply importance sampling correction toward the updated policy. It also trains the critic with BCE rather than MSE, which is better matched to binary or bounded outcome rewards.418:T58b,The experiments cover Gemma-2-9B-IT, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B on GSM8K, MMLU, and BIG-Bench Hard. Instead of comparing all examples at the same absolute recurrent step, the analysis aligns each trajectory by its first exact-solve step. The paper then measures three quantities: completion time, latent-state motion between consecutive recurrent states, and local stability. Stability is evaluated through local Jacobians and controlled finite perturbations. A key distinction is made between perturbations along the model’s natural direction of motion and perturbations along the most expanding Jacobian direction. Extending recurrence to 512 steps raises cumulative exact-solve accuracy from 59.2% to 87.5% for the attention model and from 74.4% to 91.9% for the MLP model. Among puzzles unsolved at step 16, 69.4% for the attention model and 68.4% for the MLP model are solved later, meaning that more than two thirds of nominal-budget failures are unfinished computations. When aligned by first-solve time, Early and Late solvers show similar behavior near completion: latent motion drops sharply and the natural computation direction becomes locally contractive. Persistent trajectories remain more active and have a different stability profile. Perturbation experiments confirm that the most expanding Jacobian direction grows much more than same-sized perturbations along the natural motion direction. After completion, the attention model can absorb perturbations along the most expanding direction within 16 steps, while the MLP model tends to preserve them longer. Additional checks on another attention checkpoint, Easy Sudoku, and 30×30 Maze-Hard support the same qualitative picture and also show that exact-match metrics can undercount valid solutions in path-finding tasks.41b:T83a,The framework is organized around five roles. The God of Concepts provides high-level intent in text or images. The Creator, implemented with an LLM, recursively expands that intent into a world blueprint with themes, shared rules, hidden states, and system constraints. Executors are coding agents that translate the blueprint into executable entities, behaviors, and subsystems. Artists are video generation models that render observations from visual conditions derived from the executable world. Travelers act inside the world and receive observations from their own viewpoints.

Two design ideas carry most of the technical weight. The first is Logical Spaces. A world is decomposed into heterogeneous subsystems such as transportation, construction, resources, and social relations. Each subsystem has local mechanisms, but all must obey shared global constraints. Logical Spaces provides a modular structure for collaborative world construction, so different agents can implement different subsystems while remaining consistent through shared interfaces and rules. This is more controllable than asking one model to generate an entire world monolithically.

The second is Observation as World Registration. Generated observations are not treated as disposable outputs. They are registered back into a persistent world representation, so information obtained from one viewpoint or one interaction can be retained and reused later. This directly targets a weakness of standard video world models, where past frames are consumed as context but are not written back into a structured memory.

The division of labor is deliberate. CoDeR does not ask the diffusion video model to infer rules, track hidden variables, or maintain long-term state, because those capabilities are hard to learn reliably from pixel supervision alone. Instead, the LLM-plus-code layer handles explicit world logic, and the video model focuses on conditional rendering. Compared with end-to-end visual world models, this sacrifices some architectural purity but gains interpretability, editability, and long-horizon consistency.41c:T5ad,The experimental story is organized around four capabilities: persistent memory, open-ended interaction, autonomous world evolution, and multi-agent collaboration. The paper claims clear gains over prior video-based world models on these dimensions, especially for long-term consistency, off-screen state continuation, cross-view information reuse, and sustained interaction among multiple entities. From the visible content, the evaluation appears more system- and capability-oriented than a standard pretraining paper with large-scale scaling curves or tightly standardized benchmarks.

The most informative comparisons are likely to be: direct text-to-video or video continuation baselines, variants without explicit world registration, variants without Logical Spaces, and long-horizon multi-agent scenarios where hidden state matters. For this kind of system, the key question is not a single visual quality metric. For a pretraining-oriented reader, the most useful evidence would be ablations showing separate contributions from explicit hidden variables, modular logical decomposition, and observation registration. If the paper includes failure analysis, it is worth checking whether failures come from rule compilation, state drift in the execution layer, or weak condition following in the rendering layer.41d:T540,MaP has two main components. The first is Masked Trajectory Prediction. A GUI interaction is represented as a multimodal trajectory consisting of the user instruction plus, at each step, a screenshot m_t, a reasoning trace r_t, and an action a_t. Instead of defining separate input-output mappings for different tasks, the method randomly masks a fixed proportion of components in the full trajectory and trains the model to autoregressively recover the missing parts. This turns step-wise decision, state-action alignment, and long-horizon planning into the same problem: predict missing pieces given a partially observed trajectory. The important point is not masking by itself, but the move from task-specific marginal dependencies to modeling a more unified trajectory structure. The second component is role-aware adapter learning. Compared with dataset-specific adapters, this is a finer-grained way to handle heterogeneous supervision inside each sample.41e:T42d,The evaluation spans five GUI navigation benchmarks: AndroidWorld, AndroidControl, GUI-Odyssey, AITZ, and Mind2Web. The architecture has untied prelude and coda stacks, with a middle block of k layers reused for d recurrences, so parameter depth is p+k+l while realized compute depth is p+kd+l. The main experiments use a Huginn-style configuration such as (2, 4⊗32, 2).

To characterize instability, the authors define trace entropy, which measures uncertainty along the loop-wise reasoning trajectory for each token. Incorrect reasoning traces tend to have higher trace entropy. Using a logit-lens analysis, they then identify two token behaviors. Easy tokens improve monotonically across iterations, with growing top-1 vs top-2 margins. Hard tokens do not: they often become confident too early and then attempt revision later, or show unstable refinement patterns. These hard tokens account for only about 10%–15% of the reasoning trace but appear to be disproportionately important.

LoopCD builds on this observation. Standard contrastive decoding uses logits from an expert model and an amateur model. LoopCD replaces that external contrast with an internal one: logits from the final loop iteration serve as the refined distribution, while logits from earlier iterations provide the contrastive signal. The intuition is that later iterations are usually more refined, but earlier iterations may preserve useful intermediate evidence before unstable late-stage refinement distorts it. The final sampling distribution is formed by contrasting these loop-wise logits.

A practical advantage is that no extra model is needed and almost no extra forward cost is incurred, because the intermediate hidden states and logits are already produced during looping. The paper also argues that the gains are concentrated on hard tokens rather than spread uniformly across the sequence, which makes the method more targeted than generic decoding heuristics.424:T5e4,The paper evaluates LoopCD on arithmetic reasoning, code generation, and question answering, and reports consistent gains over standard decoding and stronger decoding baselines. The excerpt provided does not include the full main-table numbers, but several experimental findings are central.

First, trace entropy is strongly associated with reasoning quality. On GSM8K, incorrect reasoning traces show systematically higher entropy than correct ones, suggesting that loop instability leaves a measurable uncertainty signature.

Second, hard tokens are rare but important. They make up roughly 10%–15% of the reasoning trace, yet random replacement experiments in Table 1 show that perturbing hard tokens hurts accuracy much more than perturbing easy tokens. This is one of the strongest pieces of evidence in the paper because it moves beyond correlation and shows that these tokens are closer to the actual bottleneck.

Third, the gains from LoopCD are concentrated on hard tokens. The selective-intervention analysis in Section 5.4 indicates that applying the method to those tokens captures most of the benefit, while intervening on easy tokens yields much smaller returns. That supports the paper’s central mechanism.

Fourth, the method is computationally light. Unlike conventional contrastive decoding, it does not require an auxiliary amateur model. It reuses loop-wise intermediate states already computed by the LoopLM, which is attractive in test-time-compute-heavy latent reasoning settings.425:T446,Start with the Introduction and Motivation. A focused skim should take about 20–30 minutes.426:T4ba,TreeSpark builds on DSpark. A small bidirectional backbone runs once over a block of masked positions and emits hidden states and base logits U_d for each draft depth. DSpark also has a low-rank Markov head B(x,v)=<W1[x],W2[v]> that adds a transition bias from parent token x to candidate token v. TreeSpark uses this existing Markov head to construct parent-conditioned child distributions for every concrete tree node. Evaluating another parent requires only an embedding lookup and a rank-r matrix-vector product, not another backbone pass. Raw proposal probability q0 is then calibrated with target-verification labels using a two-parameter map p_hat = sigmoid(a logit(q0)+b), fitted only on edges whose ancestors were accepted. Nodes are prioritized by the product of calibrated edge probabilities along the path, and expansion stops when the best remaining path survival score falls below a threshold theta. The runtime selects theta from a load-dependent ladder. For nonzero-temperature decoding, TreeSpark samples siblings without replacement from the residual q_T and reconstructs the proposal during recursive rejection sampling. This avoids the bias introduced by deterministic top-k tree expansion.427:T57b,Experiments use Claude Code with Claude Sonnet and Codex with GPT-5 on real repositories such as textual, jinja2, werkzeug, rich, httpx, and tox. To isolate content compression, the authors hold tool filtering fixed and change the compression floor from min_tokens=512 to a no-op-like 49999. To isolate tool filtering, they toggle it while holding the content path fixed, using strict MCP configuration to reduce tool-block jitter. The local Ollama backend and GPU server produce identical compression outputs; the reported segment ratio is about 0.44 for line-numbered reads, with some content compressed to roughly 26% of its original size. The main empirical result is that tool filtering is the dominant and reliably positive lever, saving about 21K tokens per turn. Content compression is often only a roughly 2% marginal effect in real sessions and is easily drowned by turn-count variance. End-to-end savings are about 25% on a single turn and about 39% by turn five in a long session. The measured scaling is linear in N for tool filtering and approximately quadratic for content compression, with a fitted content saving near 3,350 N^2 tokens and a crossover around N≈6, subject to context-window limits. The recall trap is the main negative term: each exact recall resends the original and wastes one previously sent compressed segment, a fixed cost bounded by the compressed segment length.428:T7fb,方法核心是 Semantic-Geometric Decoupled Routing。作者先从 RoPE attention 的分解出发，把 block affinity 看成两部分：一部分是与内容相关的在线语义证据，另一部分是与相对位置相关的几何偏置。已有方法把两者混在 post-RoPE token 表示里一起池化，SGDR 则显式拆开。

第一步，语义聚合移到 pre-RoPE 空间。也就是先在未旋转的 Q/K 表示上做 block 级汇聚，得到更稳定的 block semantic summary。这样做的原因很直接：pre-RoPE 表示没有相位旋转，均值或其他简单聚合不会破坏高频分量，也不会把相邻 token 的局部顺序信息在池化时互相抵消。

第二步，几何信息不再依赖 pooled post-RoPE 向量隐式携带，而是通过离线 structural prior 重建。论文里给出的做法是根据相对 block 几何关系，预先构造一个相对位置偏置项，在推理时与在线语义分数相加，形成 closed-form routing score。这个设计的关键不是“加一个 bias”，而是把位置建模从在线 token 计算里拿掉，变成离线可缓存的结构先验，因此 routing 成本只和 block 数相关，不需要额外 token-level matching。

第三步，路由完全在 block 级进行。对每个 query block，依据 decoupled score 做 Top-p 或预算约束下的 block 选择，生成 causal block mask，再交给 Triton/block-masked attention kernel 执行。作者强调 routing function 的复杂度必须远低于 O(L^2)，否则 sparse attention 在实际 GPU 上未必比高优化的 dense FlashAttention 更快。

从区别上看，SGDR 和已有方法的分界很清楚。它不是像一些方法那样先粗筛 block 再做 token search，也不是在 post-RoPE pooled score 上做温度缩放或启发式修正，而是直接改写了 block score 的构造方式。理论上，它把“为什么 post-RoPE pooling 会坏掉”解释成高频相位干涉；工程上，它把补救从在线搜索换成离线先验，因此更适合长序列 prefill。429:T753,The method is Semantic-Geometric Decoupled Routing (SGDR). The central idea is to decompose block affinity into two parts: online semantic evidence and offline geometric bias. Existing methods implicitly mix both inside pooled post-RoPE features. SGDR separates them explicitly.

First, semantic aggregation is moved to pre-RoPE space. Query and key features are summarized at the block level before rotary rotation is applied. This avoids destructive interference from averaging rotated vectors, especially in high-frequency dimensions. The result is a more stable semantic summary for each block.

Second, positional structure is reconstructed separately rather than being expected to survive pooling. SGDR introduces an offline structural prior based on relative block geometry. At inference time, this prior is combined with the online semantic score to form a closed-form routing score. The important design choice here is that positional bias is no longer recovered through token-level computation or heuristic correction; it is encoded as a reusable block-level prior.

Third, routing remains fully block-level. For each query block, the router selects top blocks under a sparsity budget and produces a causal block mask, which is then consumed by custom Triton/block-masked attention kernels. This keeps routing cost well below quadratic complexity and avoids the common failure mode where sparse attention loses its advantage because routing itself becomes expensive.

Relative to prior work, SGDR is not a coarse-to-fine method with token refinement, and it is not a calibration trick on top of post-RoPE pooled scores. It changes the score construction itself. The theoretical claim is that post-RoPE pooling destroys useful information through phase cancellation; the engineering claim is that offline geometric priors are a better replacement than online search.42a:T5c8,The evaluation covers long-context retrieval, understanding, language modeling, and video reasoning, with context lengths from 4K to 128K. Two results matter most.

First, SGDR stays close to exact full attention in accuracy across the tested range, and is better than or competitive with sparse baselines that depend on heuristic search or post-hoc compensation. The abstract does not list every task-level number, but the paper’s main empirical message is that fully block-level routing does not have to incur a large quality drop if the routing score is constructed correctly.

Second, the routing overhead is very small and remains stable as sequence length grows. The key number reported is that routing time stays below 3.4 ms across all evaluated lengths. At 128K, SGDR achieves a 5.03× speedup over FlashAttention. This is the result to pay attention to, because many sparse methods look attractive in asymptotic complexity but lose in wall-clock time once routing/search overhead is included.

The most informative ablations are likely the following: pre-RoPE vs post-RoPE pooling, to validate the phase-cancellation hypothesis; removing the geometric prior, to show that semantic pooling alone is insufficient; and varying block size or sparsity budget, to expose the quality/latency trade-off. If SGDR remains strong at low attention density, that would support the claim that the decoupled score improves ranking quality rather than merely relying on a denser mask.42b:T491,SPS is a training-free latent steering framework. It does not update model weights. Instead, it builds a state-conditioned direction bank offline and injects retrieved steering directions during generation. The offline stage samples reasoning trajectories on a small calibration set and identifies high-uncertainty transitions, which are treated as likely branching points. At those states, the same model proposes multiple continuations using a higher proposal temperature. An LLM judge labels continuations as progress-making or non-progress-making. SPS then contrasts the hidden representations of these two groups to derive steering directions and stores them by prefix-state regions. During online inference, the method monitors the current reasoning prefix, retrieves a suitable direction from the bank, and applies it only at high-uncertainty transitions and at selected layers. Compared with temperature schedules, diverse prompting, or generic latent perturbation, SPS aims to steer exploration toward continuations that make measurable progress. Compared with training-time diversity methods, it avoids extra optimization, special losses, or RL reward design.42c:T43b,The central result is that efficiency methods often reduce measured jailbreak harmfulness, but the reduction is frequently superficial. The compressed model may still try to answer the harmful request; it simply loses enough reasoning or generation fidelity that the final answer is incomplete, incoherent, or less actionable. More aggressive pruning or compression tends to create stronger capability degradation, while quantization methods differ depending on how well they preserve activation-sensitive weights and outlier behavior. First, it uses controlled referent-disambiguation settings to show that process failure is real and separable from perception. A model can enumerate all candidate objects and their attributes, yet still commit to a single unsupported answer. Second, the authors propose SRT, a family of structured process-prior interventions applied at inference time. SRT has three steps: State extraction, which explicitly surfaces observable states relevant to the question; Relevance checking, which tests whether those states are tied to the current decision boundary; and Target commitment, which delays the final answer until the previous checks are completed. This is more constrained than generic chain-of-thought because it specifies how evidence should be filtered and when commitment is allowed. That structure lets the authors ask when a process prior helps: the key finding is that effectiveness depends on alignment between the supplied prior and the image’s actual decision boundary. S1 uses COCO and GQA-style referent disambiguation to show that better visual access alone does not reliably repair the error, whereas a process-structured intervention can reduce cases where the model has already perceived the right evidence but still answers incorrectly. The representative number highlighted in the paper is 86.1% versus 29.4% on physical state transition when using oracle-aligned versus misaligned settings, indicating that much of the gap comes from boundary identification and evidence binding rather than missing perception. The remaining bottleneck is automatic identification of which decision boundary applies to a given image.432:T6ef,The paper has three methodological layers.

First, it measures shared errors directly. Across multiple preference datasets, the authors collect decisions from both open-weight and frontier judges, compute pairwise error correlations, and summarize the amount of independent information using effective sample size. They use the design-effect approximation: once average correlation is nonzero, a bank of n judges behaves like a much smaller number of independent judges in variance terms. The paper is careful to note that this does not mean 10 judges can literally be replaced by 3.5 judges; it means the consensus contains only that much independent statistical information.

Second, it studies how dependence changes conclusions. The paper compares a pooled-vote significance test, which treats each judge vote as an independent observation, against an item-level test that accounts for correlated votes on the same examples. This isolates a common evaluation mistake: inflating evidence by counting redundant votes as if they were independent samples.

Third, it distinguishes different structures of shared failure. The paper defines global co-failure, where many judges fail on the same items, and vulnerable-subgroup failure, where errors are concentrated within a subset of judges. The key point is that average correlation alone is not enough to distinguish these cases, yet they affect majority voting differently and call for different filtering rules. To address this, the authors propose CorrFilter, which discounts agreement among judges with correlated errors, and a bias-cluster filter, which ranks examples by support from judges outside the vulnerable subgroup. A small trusted set is then used to choose among majority voting and these specialized filters.433:T731,The main quantitative result is straightforward and important. In the primary ten-judge bank, the average pairwise error correlation is 0.21. Under the design-effect approximation, this gives a variance inflation factor of about 2.85 and a variance-effective sample size of only n_eff ≈ 3.5. So ten judges do not provide ten units of independent evidence.

The paper repeats this analysis on two additional datasets and 73 alternative judge-bank compositions spanning prompt styles, model families, providers, and random seeds. The dependence is therefore not a one-off artifact of a single ensemble.

The frontier-judge result is even more striking. Three high-accuracy judges from different providers each reach 91% to 93% accuracy, yet their average error correlation is 0.56, and they make the same mistake together at 7.7 times the rate expected under independence. This directly challenges the naive intuition that stronger judges automatically make consensus more trustworthy. The paper also finds that judges from different providers are about as correlated as judges from the same provider, suggesting that shared blind spots are not just a same-family effect.

At the evaluation level, ignoring dependence changes significance conclusions in up to 28% of system comparisons: a pooled-vote test declares one system significantly better, while an item-level test that respects correlated votes does not. For filtering, the paper shows that no single fixed rule works best across both global co-failure and vulnerable-subgroup failure. A selector based on a small trusted set is tested on eight external factuality datasets, and in those transfers it always chooses plain majority voting. That result is useful because it positions the specialized filters as safeguards for specific failure modes rather than universal replacements.434:T516,This is worth a careful skim for anyone building automatic evaluation, preference datasets, or RLHF/DPO filtering pipelines. Start with the introduction and the main figures to lock in the two headline numbers: rho = 0.21 implies n_eff ≈ 3.5 in the main ten-judge bank, and frontier judges reach rho = 0.56 despite high accuracy. Then read the methodology around effective sample size and pooled-vote versus item-level testing, because the paper is precise about what is and is not being measured. After that, focus on the shared-error-pattern analysis, especially the distinction between global co-failure and vulnerable-subgroup failure; that is the most conceptually useful part of the paper. Two practical takeaways stand out: report judge dependence or effective sample size rather than just the number of judges, and design retention rules for judge-labeled data at the item level instead of relying mechanically on raw vote counts.435:T893,方法上，这篇工作几乎没有把重点放在“发明一个更强的残差化器”上，而是建立了一套证据框架。作者固定了 measurement setup：需要一个原始分数、若干 surface features，以及一个与这些表面特征来源分离的 construct measurement。然后用同一个 residualization operator，在三种证据情境下分别检验它能支持什么主张。

第一种是 designed intervention。代码审计场景里，作者利用 unit-test correctness 作为外部构念标签，并只通过 comments/docstrings 改写来操纵格式通道，保证语义和正确性不变。这样就能直接测“格式效应是否被 attenuate”。这里 residualization 的角色不是生成新 gold score，而是作为审计探针：如果调整后，镜像格式条件下的偏好差距缩小，同时 correctness margin 基本不变，那么可以说它削弱了该格式通道。

第二种是 observational evidence。这里没有保标签干预，只能根据 surface-only predictor 的误差来定义某个 slice，再看 residualized score 在这个 slice 上是否与外部标注更一致。作者强调，这种设计只能支持 slice-restricted alignment gain，不能外推到总体有效性。原因很直接：slice 本身就是按某个模型的错误模式定义的，调整后在 slice 内变好，不代表总体更好，也不代表构念更纯。

第三种是 construct–artifact entanglement。作者构造并分析了构念与表面特征相关的情形，说明 decorrelation、loading 提升、slice gain 都不足以识别 validity restoration。换句话说，如果“好答案通常更长、更有注释、更像某种风格”本身就是任务分布的一部分，那么把这部分减掉，可能连有用信号一起减掉。

全文还有一个重要点：作者把 residualization 明确定位为 audit perturbation，而不是 repaired score。这一点和很多长度控制 win rate、judge debiasing 实践不同。作者还给出一套 reporting protocol，并允许 explicit refusal：证据不够时，就不声称分数被修复。这种写法比常见的“做了控制变量所以更公平”要严格得多。436:T7d0,The paper is organized around an evidence framework rather than a new estimator. The setup fixes three ingredients: an original score, a set of surface features, and a provenance-separated construct measurement. The same residualization operator is then examined under three evidential regimes.

First, in the designed-intervention regime, the authors use a code audit where unit-test execution provides correctness labels and only comments/docstrings manipulate the formatting channel. Because the intervention preserves correctness while changing format, attenuation of the format effect becomes directly measurable. Here residualization is used as an audit perturbation: if mirrored formatting conditions move closer after adjustment while correctness margins remain stable, one can claim attenuation of that specific surface channel.

Second, in the observational regime, no such intervention exists. The authors define slices using the errors of a surface-only predictor and test whether the residualized score aligns better with external annotations on that slice. The key point is that this supports only a slice-restricted alignment claim. Since the slice is itself induced by a model of surface effects, improvement inside the slice does not identify broader validity or better population-level measurement.

Third, the paper studies construct–artifact entanglement. When the target construct is genuinely correlated with the artifact, subtracting the predictable surface component can remove construct-relevant signal together with nuisance variation. In that case, lower correlation with artifacts, better loading diagnostics, or even slice gains do not identify validity restoration.

A central conceptual move is to treat residualization as an audit tool rather than a repaired score. That framing is stricter than common practice in length-controlled win rates or judge debiasing, and it leads to a reporting protocol with an explicit refusal option when the evidence is insufficient.437:T6a5,The most concrete experiment is the code preference audit. On MBPP-style pairs containing a terse correct solution and a commented buggy solution, a public preference reward model selects the correct answer only 0.507 of the time, essentially chance. When the verbosity–correctness pairing is reversed, the same model selects the correct answer 0.615 of the time, showing a substantial format effect. Under the designed intervention, residualization attenuates the format effect by about 0.12 on both correct and buggy code, shrinking the mirrored-preference gap from 0.108 to 0.037 while leaving correctness margins largely unchanged. Length-only corrections fail to close that gap, indicating that the issue is not reducible to raw length alone.

The paper also stresses the limits of this positive result. Across three held-out edit templates, the same operator overshoots one template, attenuates another, and amplifies a third. So even in a controlled setting, the effect of residualization is template- and channel-dependent.

In the observational analyses, held-out and disjoint-annotator tests support only a slice-level alignment gain. Every metric outside the declared slice declines after adjustment, including full-population alignment, the observable flagged subgroup, and within-question ranking. This is one of the strongest empirical points in the paper.

The construct–artifact entanglement section shows an even sharper failure mode: measured loading can improve while the adjusted judge becomes less useful. The paper reports four current-generation judge × setting probes, and all of them fall below the committed loading gate, meaning none supports a stronger validity claim.438:T985,作者先把 training-free UE 系统化分成三类，再在统一实验框架下比较。

第一类是 verbalized uncertainty。模型直接用自然语言表达不确定性，文中研究了两种形式：一种是 abstention，让模型在不确定时输出 UNKNOWN；另一种是 numerical confidence，在答案旁边给出置信分数。优点是部署简单、对闭源模型也适用、几乎没有额外推理成本；缺点是完全依赖模型的自我校准能力。

第二类是 token-level uncertainty。作者采用自回归输出分布上的 entropy 和 negative log-likelihood，并对整段回答做 mean 与 max 聚合。mean 代表长度归一化的整体不确定性，max 试图抓住局部薄弱 token 的尖峰。文中一个重要点是：在 deterministic decoding 下，这类信号会明显退化；提高采样温度后，校准后的效果能恢复，甚至接近更昂贵的 semantic 方法。这个观察很关键，因为它说明 token-level UE 不是简单读取 logits 就够了，解码策略本身决定了你能不能看到有区分度的分布信息。

第三类是 semantic uncertainty。作者纳入 Semantic Entropy 及其多模态变体 VL-Uncertainty、VASE 一类方法。核心思想是多次采样得到多个回答，再通过双向 entailment 或扰动一致性把表面不同但语义相同的回答聚类，在语义簇上计算熵。这样可以避免把“同义改写”误判成高不确定性。代价也很明显：需要多次推理、额外 entailment 模型和聚类开销。

实验框架上，作者沿四个轴系统比较：模型家族、模型代际、模型规模、回答长度。模型覆盖 InternVL 与 QwenVL 两个家族，且各自包含两代和两个规模档，小模型约 2B，中等模型约 7B 到 8B。任务覆盖五个 VQA benchmark，包含多选、句子级和开放式回答。评估指标除了常见 AUROC、Coverage at Risk，还加入 CHDA。这个 calibrated hallucination detection accuracy 指标会先在一小部分数据上校准阈值，再看部署式检测效果，比纯离线排序指标更接近实际使用场景。

方法层面的贡献不在于发明新 UE 算法，而在于把不同范式放到同一坐标系里，并明确指出每类方法的适用边界。尤其是“输出长度决定哪一类方法更占优”这一点，解释了为什么过去很多结论彼此矛盾：它们常常只在短答案 VQA 上成立。439:Ta31,The paper organizes training-free UE into three families and evaluates them under one experimental protocol.

The first family is verbalized uncertainty. The model expresses uncertainty in natural language. The authors study two variants: abstention, where the model outputs UNKNOWN when uncertain, and numerical confidence, where it emits a confidence score alongside the answer. These methods are easy to deploy, work for both open and closed models, and add almost no inference cost. Their weakness is obvious: they rely entirely on the model’s self-calibration.

The second family is token-level uncertainty. The paper uses entropy and negative log-likelihood from the autoregressive output distribution, aggregated over the response by mean and max. Mean is intended as a length-normalized global uncertainty score, while max captures localized spikes from weakly grounded tokens. A key empirical point is that these signals degrade badly under deterministic decoding, but recover when estimated at higher temperature. That is an important observation because it shows that token-level UE is not just about reading logits; the decoding regime determines whether the uncertainty signal remains informative.

The third family is semantic uncertainty. The study includes Semantic Entropy and multimodal variants such as VL-Uncertainty and VASE. The idea is to sample multiple responses, cluster them by semantic equivalence using bidirectional entailment or perturbation-based consistency, and compute entropy over semantic classes rather than surface forms. This avoids treating paraphrases as uncertainty. The trade-off is higher cost: multiple generations, an entailment model, and clustering overhead.

The evaluation protocol is one of the paper’s main strengths. The comparison spans four axes: model family, generation, size, and response-length regime. The models come from two MLLM families, InternVL and QwenVL, each with two generations and two scales, roughly 2B and 7-8B. The tasks cover five VQA benchmarks spanning multiple-choice, sentence-length, and open-ended outputs. In addition to AUROC and Coverage at Risk, the paper uses CHDA, a calibrated hallucination detection accuracy metric that calibrates a threshold on a small subset before deployment-style evaluation. That makes the analysis more operational than standard ranking-only metrics.

The contribution is therefore not a new UE algorithm. It is a careful empirical map of where each UE family works, where it breaks, and why earlier conclusions from short-answer benchmarks do not transfer cleanly to broader MLLM settings.43a:T5fc,From the provided text, the confirmed setup includes two MLLM families, InternVL and QwenVL; two generations per family; two scale regimes, roughly 2B and 7-8B; and five VQA benchmarks covering multiple-choice, sentence-length, and open-ended response formats. The compared methods span verbalized, token-level, and semantic UE, evaluated with AUROC, Coverage at Risk, and CHDA.

The paper highlights four main findings. First, output length determines which UE family performs best; there is no single winner across all regimes. Second, token-level uncertainty collapses under deterministic decoding, but higher-temperature estimation restores calibrated signals that can rival much more expensive semantic methods. Third, verbalized self-uncertainty is unreliable in smaller and older MLLMs, but becomes much stronger in newer medium-scale models, with Qwen3-VL-Instruct called out explicitly. Fourth, even the better methods fail to achieve low risk at useful coverage, indicating that safe deployment of 2B to 8B MLLMs remains far from solved.

The excerpt does not include the full numeric tables, so it would be unsafe to quote exact margins. Still, the practical implications are already clear. For short-answer tasks, expensive semantic methods are not automatically justified. For long or open-ended outputs, plain token entropy is often unstable. For newer instruction-tuned models, abstention and verbalized confidence are worth testing seriously, but they should not be assumed to transfer backward to older generations.43b:T44e,This is a solid skim-to-medium-depth read. Start with the taxonomy and the experimental setup. You need to understand what interface each UE family requires, what extra inference cost it incurs, and why token-level methods report both mean and max aggregation.

Then go to the main result figures, but do not look for a single average winner. The informative part is how rankings change when sliced by response length, model generation, and model size. That is where the paper’s strongest conclusions live.

Next, read the CHDA definition and threshold-calibration procedure. Many UE papers stop at AUROC, which is too far from deployment. This paper is more useful because it evaluates uncertainty in a calibrated decision setting.

Finally, read the discussion or failure-analysis sections, especially the explanation of why deterministic decoding destroys token-level signals and why verbalized uncertainty differs so much between older and newer models.

A reasonable reading budget is 30 to 45 minutes. If time is limited, read the method overview, the main tables/figures, and the CHDA section.43c:T772,The method, VGCompiler, is built around two compilers. The representation compiler maps a visual graph into a structure-preserving intermediate graph representation. Its job is to recover nodes, edges, directions, weights, and relevant graph state as faithfully as possible. The operation compiler then decides which graph procedure should be executed for the given query under that recovered state. This matters because the correct executable procedure depends on the graph condition: reachability, cycle detection, and shortest path are different tasks, and shortest path itself depends on whether the graph is unweighted, nonnegative-weighted, or contains negative edges.

Instead of implementing these compilers as fixed symbolic modules, the paper uses a VLM to generate executable code. Code is treated as the primary reasoning object. During training, the model generates candidate code conditioned on a graph-question pair, and reinforcement learning is used to optimize generation. The reward is layered rather than answer-only: executability of the code, validity of the compiled graph, quality of the recovered representation, and quality of the chosen operation all contribute. This is an important design choice because it separates “correct answer for the wrong reason” from “mostly correct compilation but imperfect final execution.”

A second notable component is the code archive. A frozen observer extracts lightweight cues from each graph-question pair and uses them as condition signatures. Generated code is archived under these signatures during training, and compatible archived code can be retrieved at inference time. This is similar in spirit to case-based retrieval, but the retrieved object is executable program structure rather than natural-language reasoning traces. That makes sense for graph problems, where the space of valid operations is structured and reusable.43d:T52c,The main instantiated model is Qwen-VGCompiler, obtained by RL fine-tuning Qwen3-VL-8B under the proposed framework. Evaluation covers three public benchmarks: GVLQA, VisionGraph, and VGCURE. The headline result reported in the paper is a 28.9% improvement over prior methods. From the full setup described in the introduction, the claim is framed as a broad gain across public benchmarks rather than a narrow win on one dataset.

A few experimental choices are worth attention. First, the paper goes beyond benchmark evaluation and tests three real-world scenarios: metro routing, logistics delivery, and network fault assessment. That matters because the central claim is about robustness of the compilation pipeline under heterogeneous visual graph styles, not just benchmark fitting. Second, the paper repeatedly emphasizes style, layout, and rendering variation as a source of failure, so the most informative ablations are likely those isolating the representation compiler, operation compiler, layered reward, and archive retrieval, especially under style shifts. Third, if the full tables break down results by graph state or by shortest-path variants, those sections are especially useful because they reveal whether the operation compiler truly learned state-aware execution rather than superficial task templates.43e:T429,This is best read as a task decomposition paper, not as just another VLM reasoning method.
