The main deeper question is whether executable code can serve as a robust intermediate representation for other visually structured tasks such as tables, flowcharts, UI screenshots, or scientific diagrams.43f:T4a4,GAE uses a two-stage pipeline. In stage one, the DA3 geometry encoder is frozen, and a learned bottleneck is inserted between its four-level feature hierarchy and the original geometry head. The bottleneck compresses all feature levels into one latent and reconstructs the full hierarchy in a single pass. The geometry head remains frozen when decoding depth, camera rays, and point maps, which prevents the decoder from adapting around information lost during compression. An RGB head is trained from the same bottleneck, forcing appearance and geometry to share the latent. The latent is further shaped for generation through two constraints: token-wise alignment to co-located C-RADIO features improves semantic organization and smooth transport, while pairwise similarity matching to DINOv2 features restores relational and spatial structure. In stage two, the codec is frozen and a DiT-style conditional flow is trained in the standardized GAE latent space. The model uses text, metric Plücker rays, and reference views as conditions, with condition dropout enabling text-to-image generation, camera-controlled video, and reference-conditioned novel-view synthesis in one generator.440:T4f9,WorldCrafter builds on latent video diffusion. A video VAE maps frames into spatiotemporal latents, and a DiT denoiser is trained with conditional flow matching. Long videos are generated chunk by chunk: recent clean latents are kept as a sliding temporal context, while the newly generated chunk is appended to the history archive. The new component is an implicit memory module. A memory encoder maps historical latent frames into a compact representation, initialized from pretrained 3D representation encoders to inherit a 3D inductive bias. The memory encoder, the pose-conditioned readout module, and the video DiT are then jointly optimized so the memory space co-adapts to the DiT token space. The key design is pose-guided readout: given the target camera trajectory, the model extracts a fixed number of memory tokens that are relevant to the requested viewpoints. These tokens are concatenated with recent-history tokens and current noisy latent tokens as [M; z_r; z_t] and are consumed directly by DiT self-attention. No explicit depth correspondence or target-view reconstruction is required. At inference time, complementary historical views are selected according to camera coverage, and few-step distillation reduces sampling cost for streaming interaction.441:T426,The method represents a video as B latent chunks. Each chunk follows K noise levels and is denoised from x_b^K to x_b^0. A denoising step consists of a network prediction F_theta followed by a sampler update S_j. The key abstraction is a context-selection policy Phi_b(j,r), which chooses the noise state of historical chunk b-r when current chunk b is at denoising step j. This policy is tied to the history window W, attention masks, cached representations, sampler behavior, execution scheduling, and training-state sources. Three representative policies are studied: clean history uses clean endpoints from past chunks; same-level history uses past chunks at the same denoising level as the current chunk; progressive history makes more distant history cleaner. Compared with Self Forcing, which mainly addresses the source mismatch between training and inference histories, this work focuses on the denoising state of the historical context. Compared with pure streaming execution optimizations, it analyzes the modeling choice and execution graph together.442:T734,The system, DuetGen, combines a Qwen3.5-2B autoregressive planner with a 4B single-stream DiT through what the authors call DeepFusion. Given a prompt, the planner emits a bbox-content plan, where each region contains four coordinates and a text string. Instead of feeding only the final serialized plan to the renderer, the method extracts the planner’s final-layer hidden states for both prompt tokens and plan tokens, then maps them through a lightweight projector into condition tokens for the DiT. This is the key design choice: the renderer conditions on structured continuous states, not just discrete layout symbols. Training uses three coordinated objectives. First, the planner is trained with the standard autoregressive next-token loss over the serialized plan. Second, the DiT is trained with a text-region-weighted flow-matching loss. Spatial locations inside rasterized reference text boxes receive a larger weight gamma, so the denoising objective focuses more strongly on text-bearing regions, where fidelity is hardest and most important. Third, the model adds auxiliary coordinate supervision: hidden states corresponding to each coordinate span are mean-pooled and regressed to the normalized bounding box. This head is used only during training, with the purpose of making geometric information more explicit in the planner states that later condition the DiT. At inference time, the model further applies Phase-Aware Attention Modulation, or PAM. PAM selectively strengthens attention from image patches inside a planned region to the matched bbox and content states, improving region-specific execution when multiple text regions or long strings compete for attention. The contribution is therefore not a simple pipeline combination, but a three-level coupling across representation, objective, and attention execution.443:T481,From the provided full-content excerpt, the setup uses a 2B planner and a 4B DiT, with the DiT first pretrained from random initialization for general image generation before joint planning-rendering training. The authors adapt the planting probe from Wallat et al. to a setting built around Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and three RLVR agents derived from it.

The procedure has three stages. First, the model answers a question given five retrieved passages, with exactly one citation per sentence. Second, a short span from the original claim is copied into a passage that was retrieved but not cited for that claim, and the model is run again on the doctored context. Third, the evaluation checks whether the citation for the same claim shifts to the doctored passage.

Several design choices matter. Since Qwen2.5 does not expose exact grounding spans, the planted span is selected deterministically as the four consecutive words in the claim with the most characters. Because the regenerated answer may be paraphrased, the authors do not simply ask whether the doctored citation appears anywhere. Instead, they align the new answer to the original claim using Jaccard overlap and score a claim-aligned outcome. The most important addition is the no-planting control. Rather than reporting raw planted rates, the paper asks how much citation movement is actually caused by the plant relative to a baseline where nothing is planted. This avoids conflating genuine post-rationalization with ordinary answer variability or self-repetition.

For the RLVR comparison, the setup is intentionally clean: one shared base model, fixed retrieval corpus, fixed prompt, and fixed scorer. That makes differences easier to attribute to training rather than to model family or infrastructure.446:T4f9,The experiments span four QA datasets. Three findings stand out.

First, post-rationalization is common even without RL. On Wikipedia-style datasets, roughly one citation in seven is unfaithful, around the 14% range. So the baseline instruction-tuned model already treats citation partly as a surface-matching task rather than strict evidence attribution.

Second, RLVR does not fix the problem. Under fixed-context inference, Search-R1 and ReSearch stay within a couple of percentage points of the base model, and R-Search is slightly worse. The authors also provide a detection bound: with their sample sizes, they would likely have detected an improvement of about seven percentage points, so a large hidden gain is unlikely.

Third, the control experiment matters. Even with no planting at all, the selected four-word span reappears in 60%–74% of regenerated answers, simply because models often reuse their own wording. This means evaluation protocols that condition on span recovery or report only raw planted rates can overstate the effect.

A useful detail is the distinction between claim-aligned scoring and cited-anywhere scoring. The latter is kept only as a sensitivity check and is shown to be looser. That strengthens the paper’s measurement credibility.447:T5ce,The interaction pattern is locate-correct-continue. An annotator reads a model response and marks the first inappropriate token. onPanda shows the model's top-k candidate tokens and probabilities at that position, with k defaulting to 20. If a suitable replacement is available, the annotator selects it; otherwise, the annotator writes a free-form replacement. The system truncates all later text and continues generation from the corrected prefix. The process repeats until the response is acceptable.

This differs from standard post-editing because the annotator does not repair a completed response after the model has already drifted. The continuation is re-rolled from the corrected prefix, so most final tokens remain model-generated. Each correction also creates a local supervision record: the bad token, the replacement, the prefix, and the model's candidate distribution. These records can be converted into SFT data, DPO pairs, reward-model data, or process-level supervision. Implementation-wise, onPanda is a componentized front-end library. It can run as a static web app or be embedded in an existing annotation platform. It requires an inference API that can continue from an assistant-message prefix and return token logprobs. A full annotation session is serialized into a single .panda.json file. For agents, it can access tools through MCP and connect to harnesses such as Claude Code, Codex, and OpenClaw, allowing corrected tool calls to be executed in the loop.448:T4a7,ACLArena builds a fixed sequential pipeline rather than evaluating arbitrary task permutations. The order is Math → Search → E-commerce → Instruction Following. Math strengthens reasoning, Search uses a single tool, E-commerce involves up to 15 tools, and Instruction Following is introduced last for adherence and alignment. Sequential training is used as the diagnostic baseline. The analysis has two levels: a model-level view that tracks capability changes across stages, and a token-level view that studies how individual training signals shape behavior and optimization. The method comparison covers three practical strategies. On-policy distillation uses previous checkpoints as teachers on the student’s current state distribution. Self-distilled fine-tuning replays filtered specialist trajectories offline. Model merging reuses prior models directly in parameter space. The proposed Mixture of Low-Rank Experts first uses SDFT to learn valid behaviors across domains, then applies RL through stage-specific LoRA adapters. A router composes the resulting experts. The design reduces interference by avoiding a single dense parameter update path for all heterogeneous skills.449:T402,The study uses emotion as the controlled concept because it is shared across text, audio, and image and can be represented with linear directions. The experiments cover Qwen2.5-Omni-7B, Phi-4-Multimodal-Instruct, and MiniCPM-o-4.5. For each layer, hidden states are captured with forward hooks and mean-pooled over tokens. Linear probes produce a layer-wise readability curve. Separately, emotion steering directions are injected at individual layers to produce a layer-wise steerability curve. The key claim is a probing–steering layer dissociation: probe-best layers are scattered across depth, while steer-best layers concentrate in a mid-to-late band. The paper uses random-direction controls, cross-modal settings, cross-model validation, and logit-lens analysis. The proposed explanation is that effective steering needs both readable representation and downstream plasticity; later layers may be readable but already too close to vocabulary commitment, while earlier layers may not yet provide a stable causal handle.44a:T423,The method uses hRoPE, a hierarchical rotary positional encoding. Position is represented as three coordinates: p1 for paragraph index, p2 for sentence index inside a paragraph, and p3 for token index inside a sentence. Each level receives its own independent rotary channel group, so paragraph, sentence, and token displacements are not collapsed into a single scalar. The frequency base for each axis is calibrated from corpus statistics using the 99th-percentile coordinate range plus a safety margin, so low-frequency channels remain non-wrapping over typical ranges. The central experimental move is a counterfactual intervention: keep the tokens and lower-level coordinates fixed, modify only the paragraph coordinate p1, and measure cross-paragraph attention. A density-matched random-label channel with the same architecture is used as a control. This is important because an arbitrary extra positional axis can also compress attention; the diagnostic quantity is therefore not compression itself, but compression depth relative to the random control.44b:T4a0,The paper combines three analyses. First, it elicits chain-of-thought explanations for evaluation/deployment classification from Gemma 3 1B, 4B, and 12B, Phi-3 Mini and Medium, and Llama-3 8B. The data includes 200 balanced prompts from SAD-Stages Oversight and a GSM8K-versus-WildChat split with 100 evaluation and 100 deployment prompts. Llama-3.3-70B is then used as a judge to assign the generated reasoning traces to categories such as task formatting, memorization, and meta-reasoning. Second, Integrated Gradients is applied to the Phi-3 family to identify input tokens that promote or inhibit evaluation awareness. Third, activation steering vectors are built from 204 contrastive prompts by taking the mean activation difference between evaluation and deployment contexts. A useful implementation detail is the extraction site: the authors use the token corresponding to the closing parenthesis of the model’s choice bracket, rather than static positions that may capture padding or EOS states. The proposed intervention has two paths: prompt sanitization removes external triggers, while activation counter-steering suppresses the internal evaluation-aware representation.44c:Ta3d,方法核心是 TRACE：Teacher-forced Registry of Ablated Component Effects。做法不是像 activation patching 那样在 corrupted/clean 两条前向之间恢复激活，也不是训练 SAE 去解释残差特征，而是建立一个可注册的组件库，对每个组件单独做一次消融，然后在固定答案位置上看输出分布如何变化。

从全文描述看，这个框架有几个关键设计。第一，统一注册接口。它允许把不同层级的对象都视为“组件”，包括整个 transformer block、MHSA 子层、FFN 子层、单个神经元，甚至输出 logit 相关通道。这样做的意义是把不同粒度的解释对象放到同一实验协议下，而不是每种组件各用一套方法。

第二，teacher forcing。作者刻意把研究对象限制在“单个命名实体生成”，并在答案 token 位置固定上下文，避免自由生成时后续 token 误差传播污染 attribution。这样测到的是某个组件对目标 token 条件概率的直接支持，而不是对整段生成轨迹的混合影响。代价是它更适合 factual recall 场景，不适合 reasoning trace 很长的模型。

第三，行为数据集设计。作者构造了两个域：医疗药物知识和一般知识。医疗部分进一步限定到 drug 子域，选了 8 个药物实体，每个实体写 6 类线索提示，如历史、化学式、通用名、一线治疗、药物相互作用等，共 48 个 prompt。一般知识部分来自 TREC-8 QA，经改写后保证答案是单一命名实体，并筛选成与医疗域格式一致的问答。这个设计不是为了 benchmark 分数，而是为了区分“跨域都重要的通用生成组件”和“只在某一域显著的专门组件”。

第四，消融效应度量。摘要里明确说是测量 ablation 后固定答案 token 输出分布的变化。虽然截取内容里没有完整公式，但可以确定它不是只看 top-1 是否翻转，而是看目标答案概率或相关分布量的下降幅度，因此能得到连续的贡献分数。相比只做正确/错误二值统计，这种度量更细，也更适合比较不同组件类型。

与已有方法相比，它的区别很清楚。相对 activation patching，它不依赖构造 clean/corrupted 对照样本，也不强调“恢复足够性”，而是强调“去掉后损失多少支持”。相对 SAE，它不需要额外训练解释模型，扩展到不同模型家族更直接。相对 circuit discovery，它牺牲了组合级最小电路发现能力，换来在当代 dense LLM 上可扩展的单组件扫描。这个取舍很现实。44d:Ta5f,The core method is TRACE, short for Teacher-forced Registry of Ablated Component Effects. Instead of activation patching between clean and corrupted runs, and instead of training a sparse autoencoder over residual activations, the framework registers model components at multiple granularities, ablates them one by one, and measures the effect on the output distribution at a fixed answer position.

Several design choices matter. First, the registry abstraction. Different objects can be treated uniformly as components: full transformer blocks, MHSA sublayers, FFN sublayers, individual neurons, and even output-logit-related units. This is the main reason the framework can compare heterogeneous component types under one protocol.

Second, teacher forcing is central. The study is intentionally restricted to prompts whose answer is a single named entity, and the answer position is evaluated with the surrounding context fixed. This avoids contamination from autoregressive error propagation and makes the score closer to direct support for the target token rather than support for an entire generated trajectory. The trade-off is obvious: the setup is well suited to factual recall, not to long reasoning traces.

Third, the behavioral dataset is purpose-built. The authors use two domains: medical knowledge and general knowledge. The medical side is narrowed to drugs, with 8 entities and 6 clue categories per entity, for 48 prompts total. The general-knowledge side is adapted from TREC-8 QA and rewritten so that each answer is a single named entity. This is not benchmark construction for accuracy; it is an experimental design for separating domain-general generation components from domain-specific ones.

Fourth, the effect metric is distributional rather than purely binary. From the abstract and method description, the framework measures how the output distribution at the fixed answer token changes after ablation. Even without the full formula in the provided excerpt, it is clear that the method is not limited to whether top-1 flips. That makes the signal more continuous and more suitable for comparing components across prompts.

Relative to prior work, the positioning is clear. Compared with activation patching, TRACE does not require clean/corrupted paired inputs and focuses on loss of support after removal rather than sufficiency after restoration. Compared with SAE-based analyses, it avoids training an auxiliary model. Compared with circuit discovery, it gives up combinatorial minimal-circuit identification in exchange for tractable large-scale scans on contemporary dense LMs. That is a sensible engineering trade-off.44e:T54b,From the provided full-text excerpt, the confirmed setup is as follows: the study targets dense language models; the task is single-entity QA; the dataset includes 48 medical prompts plus a filtered and rewritten set of TREC-8 general-knowledge prompts. The authors describe the study as a large-scale ablation experiment, but the excerpt does not include the final result tables or reliable quantitative numbers, so it would be unsafe to invent layer-wise or component-wise effect sizes.

Still, the experimental intent is clear. The paper compares multiple component granularities to test whether entity knowledge is localized or distributed. It explicitly separates domain-general from domain-specific supporting components, so the main results should include contribution distributions aggregated by domain rather than only global averages. The multiple clue categories per drug entity are also a good design choice: they help distinguish support for the entity itself from support for parsing a particular clue style.

In practical terms, the paper should be used for directional conclusions unless one has access to the full result figures and tables. What can be stated confidently is that the authors built a scalable single-component ablation framework and applied it systematically to named-entity recall in both specialized and general domains.44f:T403,This is a skim paper. Focus on three parts.

That determines whether comparisons across prompts and component types are meaningful.

A practical reading budget is 20 to 30 minutes. If time is tight, read the introduction, the method overview, and the main result figures only.450:T668,The method has two layers: a diagnostic argument and a generative model. First, the authors show that the observed intransitivities cannot be explained by a single latent utility under any monotone link function, not merely under the standard Bradley–Terry parameterization. This matters because it rules out a broad family of single-ordering noise models. To avoid confounding latent plurality with prompt artifacts, the data collection protocol controls for prompt wording, presentation order, and option-label bias using multiple prompt variants, both item orders, randomized pseudo-identifiers, and repeated sampling.

The proposed model is a noise-augmented mixture Bradley–Terry (MBT). Each comparison is generated by first sampling a latent preference component, then drawing a pairwise choice according to that component’s Bradley–Terry probabilities, with an additional noise term to absorb residual randomness. Relative to a standard BT model, the key change is not just extra flexibility. Each component remains transitive and interpretable as a coherent ordering, while the observed aggregate can be intransitive because it mixes across components. The paper also uses posterior effective component count, computed from the perplexity of mixture weights, to estimate how many components are actually active for a given model-task pair.

Conceptually, this imports mixture-based preference modeling from social choice and preference learning into LLM behavior analysis. It differs from standard reward-model aggregation by allowing one model to sample from multiple coherent preference modes rather than one global scale.451:T6ca,The study evaluates 7 open-weight LLMs on 4 pairwise-comparison tasks: two factual domains—US city populations as an easier numerical task and atomic half-lives as a harder scientific task—and two subjective domains—joke preferences and Moral Machine dilemmas. This yields 29 model-dataset combinations. The collection protocol is deliberately heavy: every unordered item pair is queried under 4 prompt variants, both presentation orders, and repeated samples, so the authors can estimate stable pairwise choice distributions rather than one-off answers.

There are four main findings. First, structured intransitivity is real. The nonparametric diagnostic rejects the idea that a single latent ordering with noise explains the data, and this remains true after controlling for prompt, order, and label effects. Second, MBT improves held-out preference prediction over a single-component Bradley–Terry baseline across models and tasks, indicating that the mixture structure is not merely overfitting training noise. Third, the posterior effective number of components is often greater than one, meaning multiple active preference modes are needed in many model-task settings. Fourth, aggregate rankings can be misleading for model comparison: two models that look aligned in aggregate may disagree at the component level, and models that look different overall may share similar latent components.

An important nuance is that mixture structure appears in both factual and subjective tasks. That makes the phenomenon harder to dismiss as only a moral-values issue. Harder factual tasks may expose switching between heuristics under uncertainty, while subjective tasks may reflect switching between normative or aesthetic criteria.452:T46d,For a quick read, focus on three parts. First, read the introduction and background carefully to understand exactly what is being rejected: not just vanilla Bradley–Terry, but the broader single-ordering-plus-noise view. Second, read the MBT formulation and the role of the explicit noise augmentation. The key idea is how aggregate intransitivity can emerge while each latent component remains transitive. Third, inspect the results on held-out prediction, effective component count, and aggregate-versus-disaggregated model comparisons. Those sections carry most of the paper’s practical message.

The most interesting follow-up questions are whether the inferred components correlate with controllable factors such as system prompts, temperature, or framing, and whether the same mixture view can improve reward-model training rather than serving only as an offline analysis tool.453:T69a,The method combines paired task synthesis with two-stage post-training. The authors distinguish two safety settings. In environment-risk tasks, the user goal is benign but the interface contains hazards; the correct behavior is safe continuation, not refusal. In explicit-misuse tasks, the goal itself is harmful and should be refused. This distinction is central, because collapsing both into a single refuse/not-refuse label would push the model toward conservative shutdown behavior.

To support this, they introduce SCOPE-Gen, an automated pipeline that starts from normal GUI tasks and injects detectable forbidden events or risky interface elements while preserving the original user goal and completion evaluator. This produces paired tasks and three complementary trajectory types: capability trajectories for ordinary execution, risk-handling trajectories for safe continuation under environmental hazards, and refusal trajectories for harmful goals or no-safe-path cases. The reward is defined as the product of completion reward and safety reward, so full credit requires both successful completion and hazard avoidance.

Training proceeds in two stages. First, joint SFT teaches the model all three behaviors together, establishing a conditional execution policy. Second, capability-oriented online RL further improves task completion while monitoring whether safety is retained. The design choice is deliberate: use supervised data to shape the decision boundary first, then use RL to push capability, rather than expecting RL to discover the right safety-capability tradeoff from scratch. The instantiated model is based on Qwen3.5-9B, and the trajectory dataset is SATraj-OS.454:T510,The main evaluations are on OSWorld for capability and OS-BLIND for attack avoidance. The headline numbers are clear. Capability-only training improves execution but does not reliably induce attack avoidance. After joint capability-safety SFT, SCOPE-SFT reaches 49.72% on OSWorld and 66.30% attack-avoidance on OS-BLIND, with a capability-safety harmonic mean of 56.83%. After subsequent capability-oriented online RL, SCOPE-RL improves OSWorld to 54.17% while retaining 64.30% attack avoidance, yielding the best aggregate score of 58.80%.

The ablations are the most informative part. Refusal trajectories account for most of the gain in attack avoidance on OS-BLIND, meaning that explicit supervision is effective for teaching when to stop. Risk-handling trajectories play a different role: they preserve task utility at comparable attack-avoidance levels by teaching the model to continue safely instead of over-refusing. Together, the two trajectory types produce a more balanced conditional policy.

The broader takeaway from the training path—capability-only, then joint SFT, then capability-oriented RL—is that safety does not emerge automatically from capability optimization, but once a safety-aware boundary is learned, further capability improvement does not necessarily erase it.455:T594,VideoGen-Agent uses a shared multimodal policy in a reasoning-action-observation loop. At each step, the policy conditions on the prompt, previous actions, and tool observations, then selects a tool and specifies its arguments. The six task categories are Procedural Knowledge, Single-Entity Identity, Multi-Entity Identity, Physics Simulation, Compositional Scene, and Multi-Shot. Each category has a default tool subset and workflow: procedural prompts use text retrieval for steps and motion details; identity prompts use visual retrieval and image-conditioned or multi-reference generation; physics prompts invoke simulators and pass motion conditions to a motion-conditioned generator; compositional prompts generate candidates and use verification tools such as detection and depth estimation for regeneration; multi-shot prompts generate phases sequentially and use the last frame of each segment to preserve continuity. Training has two stages. First, the policy is supervised on teacher-distilled tool-use trajectories, with the paper mentioning Claude Opus 4.7 as part of the trajectory construction process. Second, the policy is optimized with multitask agentic RL. A hybrid reward scores both tool use and generated video quality, while task advantage normalization balances learning signals across the six categories. A common tool interface allows backend tools to be replaced without changing the agent workflow.456:T4c8,The method starts from the geometry of the prediction-loss and predictive-entropy plane. A likelihood-only detector uses a horizontal threshold on loss. This fails when many non-members have low loss because they are predictable. The proposed detector instead uses an inclined boundary by correcting loss with predictive entropy. The resulting score has the algebraic form of Helmholtz free energy: token loss plays the role of an energy term, predictive entropy is the uncertainty term, and a coefficient similar to temperature trades them off, giving a score of the form loss minus an entropy correction before sequence-level aggregation. The theoretical analysis shows that when members and non-members have the same mean predictive entropy, the correction preserves the expected membership gap and its lower bound. When the loss gap and entropy gap are positively correlated, an appropriate correction reduces the variance of the gap while preserving its mean, improving standardized separation. The analysis is also extended to settings with a nonzero mean entropy gap. Compared with reference-model or perturbation-based calibration, ETD uses the target model’s own token-level predictive distribution more directly.457:T43d,The strongest evidence comes from ARC-AGI-3, Frontier-CS polyomino packing, MNIST classifier compression, and Terminal-Bench 2.0. On ARC-AGI-3 with Claude Sonnet 4.6, team@3 matches roughly best@13, and team@5 matches roughly best@33, corresponding to effective multipliers of about 4.3x and 6.6x independent agents. On FT09, single-agent success is 9.4%, while team@3 reaches 90%. On LP85, 64 single-agent trials fail to solve the game, while team@5 succeeds 65% of the time. On Frontier-CS polyomino packing, team@4 scores 0.922 with Claude Opus 4.6 and 0.910 with Sonnet 4.6, compared with 0.893 and 0.891 for the strongest solo runs and 0.894 for the prior best-known result. The negative result on Terminal-Bench 2.0 is important: team@2 improves over one attempt but does not beat independent pass@2, likely because intermediate feedback is not reliable enough to rank partial solutions.458:T4c1,The method uses block-level conditioning. A learned codebook defines a bounded set of block embeddings. A shared hypernetwork uses each code embedding to construct block parameters layer by layer by merging the underlying expert bases. Each constructed block therefore already contains information from the full expert pool. During token processing, a router selects only a small number of these blocks for each token. Participation is controlled by full-pool composition, execution is controlled by the number of selected blocks, and materialization is bounded by the codebook size.

The paper also introduces Dual-Path Residual Gating. Instead of merging expert bases into a single linear path, it composes separate value and gate paths and combines them through a gated product. This gives the composed expert a nonlinear dependence on expert bases without increasing the number of raw experts. Compared with sparse MoE, non-selected raw experts can still influence a token through block composition. Compared with dense MoE, the model avoids executing all experts per token. Compared with per-token or per-segment parameter merging, it avoids materializing a new expert-sized parameter set for every routing unit.459:Tb27,技术主线有三步。

第一步，把 masked diffusion 的 tau-leaping sampler 重写成 ordered random partition 的等价形式。这个重写很关键，因为原始 CTMC/Gillespie 视角更接近逐坐标事件过程，不容易直接分析“某一步并行揭示一批坐标”带来的误差；而 partition 视角把整个采样轨迹表示成坐标集合被分成若干按顺序揭示的块，factorization error 就能自然写成对这些块内条件依赖的累积。

第二步，引入 dependence density ρ(u)。按论文描述，除去一个 N-1 的比例因子，ρ(u) 可以理解为：当其余坐标以概率 u 独立地已被揭示时，任意两个未揭示坐标之间平均 conditional mutual information 的密度。这个定义很有力，因为它把目标分布 π 的依赖结构压缩成一个一维函数。随后作者给出 ε_fact 的精确积分表示，schedule 的作用只通过权重项进入，而数据分布的全部难点都被放进 ρ(u)。这一步把“采样 schedule 优化”从一个离散、分布相关、难以下手的问题，变成了一个可分析的泛函优化问题。

第三步，分析不同依赖结构下的最优 schedule 形态。
- 对局部依赖分布，例如遍历马尔可夫链或足够规则的平稳过程，ρ_N 收敛到非退化连续 profile g。在这个 regime 下，优化平滑 schedule 只能改善 ε_fact 的前导常数，不能改变 N/K 的主阶，因此线性 schedule 是 order-optimal。这个结论很重要，因为它说明对很多“局部相关”的序列数据，花很多力气调花哨 schedule，收益可能只是常数级。
- 对 exchangeable mixtures 这类由全局 latent variable 诱导依赖的分布，ρ_N 会集中在原点附近，极限 profile 退化。此时早期揭示少量坐标能快速降低后续不确定性，因此 schedule 形状会显著影响误差阶。论文给出一个很强的例子：当 K_N≈log N 时，uniform schedule 的误差是 Ω(N/log N)，而 geometric schedule 可以做到 O(log N)。这不是常数差，而是阶的变化。

除此之外，论文还给出几个配套结果：有限步最优解满足的 stationarity equations；在大 N 极限下的变分问题及闭式 leading-order optimizer；以及 tau-leaping 中块大小随机性相对同极限 schedule 的 deterministic planner 所带来的额外 penalty。作者还把 total correlation 和 dual total correlation 也写成 ρ 的函数，从而把已有一些 heuristic 和上界放进同一框架里。

从方法取舍看，这篇工作没有去设计更复杂的联合块预测器，而是接受“仍用一维条件预测器”这一现实设定，转而优化采样 schedule。这样做的意义在于，它对应当前 masked discrete diffusion 最常见的实现路径，也更容易落地到现有 diffusion LM 系统里。45a:Tbae,The technical story has three main parts.

First, the paper rewrites the masked-diffusion tau-leaping sampler in an equivalent ordered-random-partition form. This is a useful reformulation. The original CTMC or Gillespie view is natural for exact one-coordinate-at-a-time simulation, but it is awkward for analyzing the error caused by revealing a whole block in parallel. The partition view makes the trajectory a sequence of revealed coordinate blocks, which is exactly the right object for expressing factorization error.

Second, the paper introduces the dependence density rho(u). Up to an N-1 scaling factor, rho(u) is the average conditional mutual information between two distinct coordinates when each of the remaining coordinates is independently revealed with probability u. This is the conceptual center of the paper. It compresses the dependence structure of the target distribution into a one-dimensional function. The authors then derive an exact integral representation of the factorization error epsilon_fact in which the schedule appears only through weighting terms, while all distribution-specific structure is captured by rho. This turns schedule optimization into a tractable functional problem.

Third, the paper analyzes optimal schedules under different dependence regimes.
- For locally dependent distributions, such as ergodic Markov chains or sufficiently regular stationary processes, rho_N converges to a nondegenerate continuous profile g. In this regime, optimizing over smooth schedules can improve only the leading constant of epsilon_fact, not its N/K scaling. So the linear schedule is order-optimal.
- For exchangeable mixtures, where dependence is global and mediated by a latent variable, rho_N concentrates near the origin and the limiting profile degenerates. In this regime, early fine-grained steps matter much more, because revealing a small number of coordinates can sharply reduce uncertainty about the latent structure. Here the schedule can change the asymptotic order of the error. The paper gives a striking example: when K_N is about log N, the uniform schedule has error Omega(N / log N), while a geometric schedule achieves O(log N).

The paper also derives stationarity equations for finite-step optimizers, a large-N variational problem with a closed-form leading-order optimizer, and an asymptotic penalty induced by the randomness of block sizes in tau-leaping relative to a deterministic planner with the same limiting schedule. It further expresses total correlation and dual total correlation through rho, which helps place several existing heuristics and bounds into one framework.

An important modeling choice is what the paper does not do. It does not introduce a more expensive joint block predictor. Instead, it accepts the practical setting of one-coordinate conditional predictors and optimizes the sampler around that constraint. That makes the analysis more relevant to current masked discrete diffusion implementations.45b:T5e7,The provided text indicates both theory and empirical validation, though the full numerical tables are not included in the excerpt. The main takeaways are clear.

1. The paper develops estimators for the dependence density rho, so the framework is not purely abstract. It aims to support practical schedule selection from data or samples.

2. On locally dependent distributions, the experiments should verify that linear schedules are already near-optimal and that schedule optimization mainly improves constants rather than scaling.

3. On exchangeable mixtures or other globally dependent distributions, the experiments should show that geometric schedules with finer early steps outperform uniform schedules substantially, matching the theoretical order separation. The headline asymptotic result stated in the text is that when K_N is about log N, the uniform schedule yields factorization error Omega(N / log N), whereas the geometric schedule yields O(log N).

4. Since the paper analyzes the penalty from random block sizes, any comparison against a deterministic planner is worth checking to see whether that asymptotic gap is already visible at practical sequence lengths.

For readers interested in diffusion LM sampling, the most important empirical questions are whether rho can be estimated stably, whether schedule optimization improves actual sample quality rather than only the theoretical error proxy, and whether factorization error remains a dominant issue once model error is non-negligible.45c:T553,This paper deserves a careful skim, and possibly a full read if you work on discrete diffusion or masked generation. Instead of relying purely on deterministic top-k expansion, it inserts one stochastically sampled token into the candidate pool after the top-m deterministic selections. The key idea is to give this sampled token two probability identities. During dynamic tree construction, it is assigned a proxy probability so it can compete with deterministic candidates for expansion and survival. During verification, it is evaluated with its true sampling probability, which preserves lossless stochastic decoding.

This decoupling resolves the conflict between context-adaptive dynamic trees and proper stochastic sampling. The second major contribution is an equivalence-class analysis. Once randomness is introduced into a dynamic tree, token identities and tree topology become tightly coupled, making direct analysis intractable. The authors compress this large stochastic tree space into equivalence classes and use that framework to prove losslessness. The third component is an Optimal-Transport-based verification algorithm, designed to improve acceptance rate while maintaining correctness. They also add a sparse draft distribution strategy to reduce overhead on large vocabularies.45e:T482,The experimental comparison is mainly against top-k dynamic-tree baselines such as EAGLE-3, with acceptance rate and wall-clock speedup as the main metrics under standard stochastic decoding. The central empirical claim is that RheoSampling consistently outperforms these baselines across multiple LLMs and benchmarks, especially when temperature is nonzero. The paper explicitly points out that EAGLE-style implementations effectively treat draft probabilities as 1.0 during verification, which explains the one-hot collapse and poor tail exploration.

The experiments are designed to show that the theoretical fix matters in practice. They compare behavior across stochastic settings, showing that dynamic trees degrade once sampling is introduced unless probability semantics are handled carefully. Additional gains come from the OT-based verification and sparse draft distribution. The L0 mask is optimized through a hard-concrete relaxation, with a Lagrangian term controlling the desired retention ratio. This combines feature selection with expert construction: instead of simply pruning FFN dimensions away, the method turns selected dimensions into sparse expert capacity. A linear router dispatches tokens to experts, with standard MoE auxiliary losses such as load balancing and router z-loss. The method differs from simple MoE upcycling because the expert structure is derived from L0-selected FFN dimensions rather than only copying dense FFNs into multiple experts.460:T8c8,方法核心是基于 Poisson process 的 multi-draft speculative sampling。传统 speculative decoding通常是单条 draft continuation，target 逐位验证；这篇工作改成同时生成和验证多条 draft continuation，并利用 Poisson process 的构造得到一个 exact list-coupling。这里的关键不是“多 draft”本身，而是 Poisson 化之后可以自然得到几个性质。

第一是 exactness。算法仍然保证最终输出分布与直接从 target model 自回归采样完全一致，不是近似采样。也就是说，加速不以分布偏移为代价。

第二是 drafter invariance。论文强调其 list-coupling without communication 结构，使得接受机制对具体 drafter 的某些实现细节不敏感。这个性质在 watermark 场景尤其重要，因为如果水印嵌入方式和某个特定 drafter 强绑定，系统会更脆弱，也更难分析检测统计量。

第三是 watermarkability。作者不是在 speculative sampling 之后再叠加水印，而是直接利用 Poisson process 中的 keyed randomness 嵌入可恢复统计信号。论文声称该水印是 unbiased 的，即不会改变目标分布；同时水印强度不会随着采样效率提升而同步恶化。这里的含义是：在他们的构造下，增加 multi-draft 带来的接受率收益，不必像已有 no-go 结果那样直接拿水印强度去交换。

第四是理论比较对象。论文把 Rowan et al. 2025 作为主要 baseline，并声称在理论上证明了更高 acceptance rate。结合引言表述，作者并没有说自己绕开了 Hu and Huang 2024 的不可能性结论，而是明确指出那个结论对固定 draft 数仍成立；他们做的是沿着 draft 数这个额外自由度改善 frontier。这一点很重要，说明方法创新来自问题重参数化，而不是对原结论的反驳。

从机制上看，Poisson process 在这里承担了两个角色：一是提供可解析的随机候选生成与耦合工具，二是提供天然适合 key-based watermark 的随机源。相比常见 token-level maximal coupling 或基于 exponential race 的构造，这种做法更适合扩展到 list 级别，并把“接受”和“嵌入信号”统一到同一随机过程里。461:T958,The main idea is a Poisson-process-based multi-draft speculative sampling algorithm. Standard speculative decoding usually uses one drafted continuation and lets the target verify it token by token. Here, the algorithm generates and verifies multiple draft continuations and uses Poisson processes to build an exact list coupling. The novelty is not merely having multiple drafts; it is that Poissonization gives a coupling structure with several desirable properties.

First, exactness. The final output distribution is exactly the same as direct autoregressive sampling from the target model. This is not an approximation scheme.

Second, drafter invariance. The paper emphasizes a list-coupling-without-communication construction, which makes the acceptance mechanism less tied to a particular drafter implementation. That matters even more under watermarking, because a watermark that depends too strongly on one drafter can be brittle and harder to analyze statistically.

Third, natural watermarkability. The watermark is not bolted on after speculative decoding. Instead, keyed randomness is embedded directly into the Poisson-process sampling procedure, producing a recoverable statistical signal while keeping the target law unbiased. The claimed benefit is that watermark strength does not deteriorate simply because sampling efficiency improves. In other words, the efficiency gain from multi-draft verification does not have to be paid for by weakening the watermark in the same way as in earlier impossibility-style results.

Fourth, the theoretical comparison point is Rowan et al. 2025. The authors claim a provably higher acceptance rate than that method. Importantly, they do not claim to invalidate the no-go theorem of Hu and Huang 2024. They explicitly state that the trade-off still applies for a fixed number of drafts. Their contribution is to improve the frontier by introducing the number of drafts as an additional degree of freedom.

Mechanistically, the Poisson process plays two roles: it provides an analyzable random mechanism for candidate generation and exact coupling, and it also provides a natural source of keyed randomness for watermarking. Compared with token-level maximal coupling or exponential-race-style constructions, this seems better suited to list-level coupling and to unifying acceptance and watermark embedding within one stochastic process.462:T676,The analysis starts from one linear layer, Y = XW^T. An invertible transformation P is inserted as Z = XP and V = WP^{-T}, preserving the full-precision output while changing the coordinates seen by activation and weight quantizers. Activation quantization is modeled as per-token symmetric uniform quantization with a dynamic scale determined by ||Z_t||_∞. For 4-bit activations, q_A = 2^{4-1}-1 = 7. The weight quantizer is left general; it may be standard rounding or an optimized method such as GPTQ.

The key result is an exact decomposition of the local weight-activation quantization error into an activation-guided weight compensation term and an orthogonal residual. The first term is the part that weight optimization can reduce along directions supported by the quantized activations. The second term is orthogonal to that compensatable subspace; once P is fixed, it cannot be removed by better weight compensation. This separates two roles that are often mixed together: weight optimization fits the output within a chosen coordinate system, while transformations change the residual structure before quantization.

The paper then analyzes the orthogonal residual to explain common design choices. Random orthogonal rotations reduce the impact of persistent channel-wise outliers on per-token quantization scales. Sign selection reduces unfavorable alignment between outlier structure and the rotation basis. Channel scaling balances activation-side and weight-side quantities. From a second-moment bound on the regular activation term, the paper derives an L2 scaling rule and relates SmoothQuant-like L∞ scaling to a further relaxation.463:T4d7,MME-Safety is built around a four-dimensional annotation scheme: risk scenario, harm severity, image stealth level, and text stealth level. The risk taxonomy covers nine categories, including illegal activities, hate speech, malware generation, physical harm, economic damage, fraud, pornographic content, privacy violations, and politically sensitive content. Harm severity is represented in four tiers, from no harm to high harm, with a 0–10 consequence scale. Image stealth has three levels: explicit harmful objects or embedded malicious text; harmful visual elements that require inference; and visually neutral images whose risk appears only with the text. Text stealth follows a parallel three-level structure: explicit harmful requests, euphemistic reformulations, and benign-looking text that becomes harmful only when paired with the image. The dataset is curated from MM-SafetyBench and SIUO with manual screening to ensure that each image-text pair actually conveys the intended malicious signal. The evaluation framework goes beyond binary attack success by measuring response reliability, actual risk exposure, and the structure of defensive behavior, such as risk identification, refusal, and safe alternative suggestions.464:T4be,The study builds a controlled customer-support workflow setting. The dataset covers 130 workflows, each with a domain policy, tool schemas, and user goals. Two GPT-5 instances are used to generate multi-turn conversations, one acting as the user and the other as the workflow agent. From 1800 generated conversations, Claude-4.5-Opus and Gemini-2.5-Pro independently filter for logical consistency, missing steps, and policy compliance; 1027 conversations remain. Assistant decisions are converted into next-action examples. The training split contains 5834 examples, with 4093 text responses and 1741 tool calls; the validation split has 664 examples. This separation is the main technical design choice: it makes the difference between local correctness and trajectory-level state maintenance observable.465:T566,The contribution is a benchmark and annotation protocol rather than a new model. VidOmni-Bench contains 500 videos spanning five predefined complexity types: Static World, Body Motion, Hand-Object Interaction, Crowd Action, and Multi-Scene Dynamics. These are balanced across three duration buckets, from very short clips to videos up to 90 minutes. That design is important because complexity and duration are treated as separate axes instead of being entangled.

The caption source is also deliberate. Instead of relying on human-written dense ground-truth captions, the authors use five different Video-LLMs to generate dense descriptions: InternVL3.5, Qwen3-VL, video-SALMONN 2+, Keye-VL 1.5, and Gemini 3 Flash. This yields 2,500 video-caption pairs. Human annotators then verify each sentence in a two-stage process and assign binary labels. Sentences that are plausible but unsupported by the video are retained as hard negatives. This makes the benchmark harder to game than synthetic negative construction, because the negatives come from realistic model hallucinations rather than obviously corrupted text.

Conceptually, the benchmark measures grounded verification rather than stylistic generation. It requires checking object states, actions, background changes, scene transitions, and temporal consistency, which makes it a stronger test of video evidence integration.466:T42a,The experimental findings are straightforward. Current Video-LLMs frequently hallucinate events during dense caption generation, so their outputs are not reliably grounded in the video. They also perform poorly when used as verifiers, struggling to reject plausible but incorrect event descriptions. In addition, failure patterns vary substantially across complexity types and duration ranges, which suggests that current weaknesses are heterogeneous rather than reducible to one single bottleneck.

The paper also includes dataset statistics showing that VidOmni-Bench requires broader video inspection than prior benchmarks and provides denser event coverage. Of the 500 videos, 433 contain audio, which means some examples may implicitly test audiovisual grounding as well. The full numeric result tables are not available in the provided text, so exact scores should not be restated. The qualitative conclusion is still clear: long duration, fine-grained interactions, and multi-scene dynamics significantly stress current Video-LLMs in event-level verification.467:Ta58,核心方法是 Benchproofer，一条把已有 coding task 连同其已知正确 patch，转成 formally verified instance 的构造流程。它的设计抓住了两个现实约束：一是不能把整个仓库都形式化；二是不能只依赖机械验证，因为规格本身可能写错。

第一部分是局部建模。Benchproofer 只对新增或修改的代码建立形式规格和证明，而不是试图验证整个代码库。对于修复代码调用但未修改的现有函数，系统不去展开其实现，而是为这些 callee 写 axioms，也就是对调用方真正依赖的性质做过近似摘要。这样做的原因很直接：如果要求把所有依赖函数及其传递闭包都证明一遍，SWE-bench 级别任务几乎不可操作。axiomatization 把验证边界收缩到 patch 附近，使问题规模可控。

第二部分是多后端验证表示。SWE-Proof 为每个实例提供三种验证后端：Nagini（面向静态类型 Python 验证）、Velvet（Lean 上的命令式验证 DSL）和纯 Lean。这里不是简单换语言，而是覆盖了不同验证风格：SMT 驱动的程序验证，以及需要显式写 proof 的 theorem proving。这样能区分“代码逻辑是否容易规格化”和“证明搜索是否成为瓶颈”。

第三部分是 admission pipeline，也就是机械门和对抗门联合筛选。一个候选实例只有在多重 gate 都通过后才会被收入 benchmark。机械 gate 包括规格、实现和证明在对应后端上的可检查性；对抗 gate 则用 LLM 审计规格是否 faithful，是否遗漏需求、过度放宽、或允许错误实现通过。作者特别强调 dominant failure 是 faithfulness failure：规格只约束了部分行为，把剩余关键语义留空。这一点很重要，因为形式验证只能保证“满足规格”，不能保证“规格就是用户想要的东西”。

第四部分是评测协议。作者不仅评估模型直接修 patch，还比较了几种设置：只给自然语言 issue；给结构化自然语言 specification；让模型自己写 specification 再验证；以及直接提供正确 formal specification。这个设计把“patch synthesis”和“specification synthesis”两个子问题拆开，因而能定位真正瓶颈。

从方法取舍看，这篇工作的关键不是发明新的 verifier，而是把形式方法嵌入真实软件工程 benchmark，并用环境 axiomatization + adversarial audit 让它可落地。相比传统 hidden tests，它牺牲了构造成本，换来更强的 correctness oracle；相比端到端全仓库验证，它牺牲了全局完备性，换来可扩展性。468:T92a,The core method is Benchproofer, a pipeline that converts a coding task with a known correct patch into a formally verified benchmark instance. The design is built around two practical constraints: full-repository verification is infeasible, and mechanical verification alone is not enough if the specification itself is wrong.

First, Benchproofer uses local modeling. It formally specifies and verifies only the new or modified code. Calls into unchanged functions are handled through axioms: over-approximate summaries of the properties the patch relies on. This is the key scalability move. Without it, one would need to verify the entire transitive closure of dependencies, which is unrealistic for SWE-bench-scale tasks.

Second, the benchmark supports three verification backends: Nagini for statically typed Python verification, Velvet as an imperative-style verification DSL in Lean, and pure Lean where proof obligations are discharged by proof writing rather than an SMT solver. This is useful because it separates different sources of difficulty: specification quality, program verification, and proof search.

Third, the construction pipeline uses both mechanical and adversarial admission gates. A candidate instance is admitted only if the spec, implementation, and proof check mechanically in the target backend, and if adversarial LLM auditors judge the specification to be faithful to the original task. This is an important design choice. Formal verification only guarantees conformance to the spec, not that the spec captures the intended behavior. The paper identifies faithfulness failures as the dominant issue: a spec constrains part of the required behavior while leaving critical semantics unconstrained.

Fourth, the evaluation protocol disentangles patch generation from specification generation. The paper compares several settings: solving from the natural-language issue alone, adding a structured natural-language specification, asking the model to synthesize a specification and verify against it, and supplying the correct formal specification. This makes it possible to localize the real bottleneck.

The contribution is therefore not a new verifier. It is a practical recipe for embedding formal methods into realistic software-engineering benchmarks using environment axiomatization plus adversarial auditing.469:T608,SWE-Proof covers all 500 instances of SWE-bench Verified and extends to the Python fragment of SWE-bench Pro. Each instance includes a ground-truth formal specification, implementation, and proof, under three verification backends. For realistic repository-level verified coding tasks, this is a substantial benchmark asset.

The evaluation uses Claude Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.5. The main findings are sharp. First, passing all hidden tests is not a reliable correctness signal: roughly 25% to 50% of such patches are still flawed. Second, adding a structured natural-language “specification” does not close that gap, which shows that informal constraints remain too weak. Third, asking the model to synthesize a specification and then verify against it does not improve over the unaided baseline. But when the correct formal specification is supplied, performance rises substantially: Opus 4.8 goes from 85.0% to 95.1%, and GPT-5.5 from 81.2% to 94.7%.

The most informative analysis concerns specification quality. Only 62% of synthesized specifications survive adversarial audit. The dominant failure mode is lack of faithfulness. The correlation with task success is strong: 89% of specifications from unresolved instances fail the audit, compared with 47% from resolved ones. This makes specification synthesis the central unresolved problem.

From a reward-design perspective, the paper also carries a warning: formal verification is only as good as the specification. A wrong spec can turn a seemingly strong oracle into a misleading one.46a:T58f,Although marked skim, this is worth reading a bit more carefully if you care about coding RL verifiers. Start with the introduction, which clearly frames the two core weaknesses of hidden tests: incompleteness and exploitability. Then read the overview and Figure 1 to see how a real SWE-bench issue is converted into a formal spec, callee axioms, and a backend-checkable implementation. The interesting part is not “adding proofs to SWE-bench,” but how the verification boundary is controlled.

In the method section, focus on two ideas: environment axiomatization and the combination of mechanical plus adversarial gates. The first is what makes the approach scale to real repositories; the second is what makes the benchmark trustworthy. In the experiments, prioritize four results: the fraction of test-passing but incorrect patches, the gain from supplying the correct formal spec, the audit pass rate for synthesized specs, and the failure analysis around faithfulness.

If time is limited, read the introduction, overview, the subsections on axiomatization and admission gates, then the main result tables and the specification failure analysis. That should take around 40 minutes. Questions worth probing more deeply: whether the axioms introduce overly strong assumptions, how reliable the faithfulness audit is, and whether this kind of formal oracle could be used for RL training rather than only evaluation.46b:T788,The core idea is Dense Reasoning Trace, or DRT. The goal is not just to make the model say less, but to make it reason in a different external format. DRT separates reasoning into two explicit channels: <visual> stores observed evidence from the image, while <think> stores compact logical derivations. Symbolic connectors and concise state transitions replace long natural-language sentences. This serves two purposes: reducing linguistic redundancy and disentangling observation from deduction so that assumptions are less likely to be written as if they were visual facts.

Training has two stages. The first is Dense Trace Initialization. High-quality multimodal instruction data are rewritten into the DRT format to create a DRT-SFT dataset, and supervised fine-tuning is used to internalize this reasoning mode. The key role of this stage is format adaptation rather than knowledge acquisition: the model learns to organize intermediate states in a compact structured space.

The second stage is Trace-Grounded Reinforcement Learning. The authors build a DRT-RL dataset using a tri-perspective verification pipeline, keeping only traces that satisfy three conditions simultaneously: correct final answer, logically consistent intermediate steps, and faithful visual grounding. They then optimize the model with a trace-grounded GRPO objective, augmented with process-based rewards and exploratory incentives. In effect, the policy is rewarded not only for being correct, but also for producing short, logically coherent, and visually grounded traces.

Compared with prior efficiency methods, this is not early stopping, token selection, or budget prediction within the same natural-language CoT space. It changes the reasoning expression space itself. Compared with standard CoT SFT/RL, it places much stronger emphasis on disentangling observation from deduction and on verifying grounding quality of intermediate traces.46c:T6a4,The model is evaluated on five challenging multimodal reasoning benchmarks, including text tasks and out-of-distribution video tasks. The headline result is a 5.5x improvement in token efficiency together with a 1.3-point accuracy gain over Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct under official prompting. That is the main empirical claim: shorter traces do not merely save tokens at the cost of quality; the structured format can improve the efficiency–accuracy tradeoff.

The paper also emphasizes component ablations rather than only final benchmark numbers. Dense Trace Initialization appears to be necessary for moving the model into the new reasoning format; without it, simply asking for concise reasoning would not reliably produce high-density traces. Trace-Grounded RL further improves faithfulness, especially under tight token budgets, where models otherwise tend to sacrifice logical completeness or grounding for brevity. The tri-perspective verification pipeline is important because it raises the quality of RL reference traces and filters out trajectories that are answer-correct but process-poor, or process-plausible but visually ungrounded.

From a foundation-model perspective, there are clear caveats. The gains depend on a specific trace schema and a data rewriting pipeline, so transfer to other model families, modality mixes, or pure-text reasoning remains open. The 5.5x token-efficiency number should be read carefully: one needs to check whether it counts only output tokens or total tokens, and whether prompts are strictly matched. Also, some of the burden may shift from inference to schema design and data construction quality, which makes the dataset pipeline central to the result.46d:T403,For a quick pass, start with Figure 1 and the method overview to understand what DRT actually looks like; otherwise it is easy to misread it as ordinary concise CoT. Finally, inspect the main tables and efficiency–accuracy plots to confirm that the gains come from changing the reasoning representation rather than from prompt engineering.

First, a unified tactile representation. This is an important design choice: they do not rely on a purely learned sensor adapter from raw heterogeneous inputs, but instead impose a canonical geometric reference before latent compression.

The experts communicate through H-Bridge shared attention in intermediate layers, so the Action Expert can access evolving representations of predicted visual and tactile futures during generation. Still, the experimental pattern is clear: the gains come from the combination of representation alignment, joint future-state prediction, and data augmentation for missing tactile supervision.470:T41d,The system combines a streaming speech encoder, a decoder-only LLM, parallel output streams for assistant text and function calls, an auxiliary RNN-T branch for incremental user transcription, and a streaming TTS/codec decoder. The input waveform is converted to 128-bin log-Mel features from 16 kHz audio with a 25 ms window and 10 ms stride. A 600M-parameter streaming FastConformer encoder with 24 cache-aware layers and 1024 hidden size produces one state every 80 ms after causal subsampling. Attention uses 70 frames of left context and no right context, and the convolution blocks are causal. The LLM backbone is NVIDIA Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2-Base. The same speech representation is shared by the RNN-T transcription head and the LLM adapter, avoiding a separate ASR encoder and keeping transcription aligned with the acoustic context used for response generation. Compared with DuplexSLA-style serialization of actions into a shared autoregressive channel, the main design choice is to keep specialized parallel streams for text and function calls.471:T4bf,ArenaFlow starts with tournament-based relative ranking. For each query, the policy samples a group of trajectories. A seeded single-elimination tournament compares candidates, with a greedy decoding trajectory used as an anchor for the initial ranking prior. The judge does more than choose the better trajectory. It also marks pivotal success steps, extracts strategy-like skills, and attributes whether retrieved historical skills contributed to decisive reasoning. The framework then propagates credit at two levels. For step-level optimization, tournament survival depth is used as a confidence signal: pivotal steps that support wins in later rounds receive higher weight because they have survived comparison against stronger candidates. Depth-aware weighting and intra-trajectory normalization convert trajectory-level advantages into more targeted step-level training signals. For skill-level propagation, a global memory stores candidate skills. Their utility is estimated from group-level usage attribution; skills repeatedly used in pivotal success steps are reinforced, while stale or ineffective ones are pruned. During later rollouts, high-utility skills are retrieved as priors to guide exploration.472:T5c5,The method starts from a unified gradient view. For a group of responses under the same prompt, positive weights increase the likelihood of preferred responses, negative weights suppress dispreferred ones, and magnitudes determine update strength. GVPO uses the analytical solution of KL-constrained reward maximization to design these weights. The obstacle is the partition function in the closed-form solution, which would require an intractable expectation over all possible responses. The key condition is that if the assigned weights within a prompt group sum to zero, the partition function cancels across compared responses. GVPO then defines the response weight as the difference between two centered distances: one from implicit rewards induced by the current and reference policies, and one from actual rewards. The authors provide two interpretations. First, the GVPO gradient matches the gradient of a mean-squared-error objective between implicit-reward and actual-reward centered distances. Second, the loss can be decomposed into a group-relative advantage term, a covariance term between current and reference policies that constrains excessive policy drift, and a current-policy variance term that encourages moderate entropy. Compared with GRPO, it avoids uncontrolled importance-sampling ratios. Compared with DPO, it claims a unique optimum aligned with the KL-constrained reward-maximization solution, without relying on the Bradley-Terry preference model.473:T41a,The framework has three main components. First, it decomposes each natural-language reasoning step into premises, explanations, and conclusions, making the dependency structure explicit. Second, it auto-formalizes these components into symbolic representations and uses automated theorem provers to check whether the conclusion follows from the premises. Third, it defines Solver-Based Backtracking Reward, or SBR, which combines solver verification with premise fidelity. This matters because a model could otherwise obtain a formally valid proof by changing or misusing the original premises. At inference time, if a step’s SBR falls below a threshold, the system backtracks and regenerates from that point. Compared with post-hoc methods such as LogicReward and VeriCoT, LogicTrack verifies during generation rather than after the full trajectory is completed. The paper also extends the framework to supervised fine-tuning by pairing real flawed model trajectories with solver-verified corrections and introducing a dedicated <backtrack> token.474:T413,GUARD, Guided Answer-Reasoning Distillation, builds a deployable unlearned model in four stages. It first samples unsafe or unstable completions to identify failure trajectories. It then rewrites them offline into safe-exit alternatives: fluent non-disclosing reasoning followed by a stable refusal-style answer. Prompt-end guidance tokens are used as a training scaffold to align a frozen reasoning model with these rewritten trajectories. Finally, answer-reasoning distillation internalizes the behavior into the model parameters, so inference does not require runtime guidance tokens. Compared with gradient-ascent suppression, GUARD does not merely push probability mass away from protected tokens. Compared with answer-only refusal optimization, it supervises both the reasoning channel and the final answer. Compared with representation redirection, it tries to avoid destabilizing the autoregressive decoder. The paper also introduces NFRS, a 0–1 score for structural stability, fluency, and absence of unsupported substitute content.475:T55c,The authors study a GPT-2-XL-style model with 48 layers and 1600-dimensional hidden states, trained from scratch on random walks over Manhattan. Inputs encode origin, destination, and previous turns, and the model predicts the next turn. The analysis combines representation extraction, causal activation edits, ablations, and failure tracing. Intersection representations are extracted with linear probes and diff-means features, with diff-means working better for discrete location features. A minimal teleportation edit changes the model’s encoded current position to an intersection near the goal, then tests whether the next greedy action reaches the goal from that edited position. Legal-move encoding is analyzed by checking whether intersection features promote moves that are valid at the current node. A separate goal compass is identified: it encodes the direction of the destination and biases the model among legal moves. The failure analysis traces illegal moves to superposed intersection features packed into a small subspace. Out of distribution, the correct position signal weakens and interference from incorrect intersection features increases. The model also organizes intersections by affordance: intersections with the same legal next moves tend to have nearby representations, making some localization errors harmless for immediate move legality.476:T46c,The numerical results support the mechanistic story. Intersection features are most accurately decoded around layer 18; with diff-means, 99.6% of intersections are decoded with at least 90% accuracy on held-out data. In the teleportation intervention, using a layer-11 direction succeeds for 99.3% of testable nodes on at least one eligible scene, showing that the location representation is causally used rather than merely probe-readable. Legal-move analyses show that current-intersection features favor valid actions. Ablating the goal compass preserves the ability to output legal moves but strongly harms navigation to distant destinations, separating local legality from goal-directed control. The observed failures under forced detours are explained by weakened current-position signals and increased feature interference; strengthening the correct signal or suppressing interference substantially restores performance. Training-dynamics analyses indicate that legal-move and goal-direction representations mature before precise localization, while the position code expands and becomes increasingly organized by affordance.477:T5b4,The paper uses classic Contrastive Activation Addition as a causal probe rather than proposing a new steering method.
