Three follow-up questions are worth deeper thought. First, how far does this result generalize beyond medical QA—to other MCQ settings, code selection tasks, or judge-based preference optimization with small label spaces? Second, minimum aggregation reduces reward hacking, but it may also over-penalize long reasoning chains with one noisy local step; the paper should be checked for reward-variance and stability analysis. Third, using the PRM only during adaptation is operationally attractive, but it also means PRM errors are written into the policy. That makes cross-distribution robustness an important next test.4fb:T6f9,GrowMTP trains a multi-token draft head inside the RL loop using speculative verification signals. The main challenge is not the existence of labels, but how to make those labels valid. The paper identifies three constraints. First, supervision must be applied under rollout-consistent draft-conditioned states. The k-th drafted token is predicted conditioned on previous drafted tokens, not on the final executed prefix after verification. To avoid train-test mismatch, GrowMTP records the draft trajectory and reconstructs the hidden states corresponding to the actual draft-conditioned context that produced each proposal. Second, learning across drafting depths is coupled. A deeper token only matters if earlier drafted tokens are accepted, so depth-wise training should reflect that dependency rather than treating each position as an independent classification target. The paper introduces a depth-coupled acceptance (DCA) loss based on an acceptance-chain surrogate, with a logarithmic transform to increase relative gradient weight on low-chain-value cases. Third, supervision beyond the first rejection is invalid for execution, because deeper drafted tokens are conditioned on a rejected token and therefore lie off the executed prefix. GrowMTP gates the loss after the first rejection and excludes those suffix positions. A further design choice is to detach draft-head updates from the policy backbone, so the online drafting module does not directly perturb policy learning. This sacrifices possible gains from joint optimization, but keeps the method modular and stable. An important practical point is that no offline warm start or depth curriculum is required: the first draft position always yields valid supervision, so training can begin from random initialization.4fc:T4a3,The headline result is from-scratch online growth on a headless model. On Qwen3-4B with a randomly initialized K=5 draft head, trained for 500 math RL steps, the acceptance length rises to 2.91 from the autoregressive floor. This yields 2.13x rollout speedup and 1.60x end-to-end step speedup, with head-training cost included. Over the same 500-step budget, GrowMTP reduces total GPU-hours by 9.4% relative to using an offline-trained head with comparable acceptance, which is the key economic result. The paper also studies online adaptation when a draft head already exists. On Qwen3.5-4B-Base, online updates provide an additional 1.36x rollout speedup over a frozen pretrained head. On MiMo-7B-SFT, extending the head from K=1 to K=5 increases acceptance from 1.65 to 4.0 and improves rollout speed by 1.93x. Another useful finding is domain specialization: heads trained on math rollouts and code rollouts achieve higher in-domain acceptance, supporting the claim that rollout-specific adaptation matters. The introduction does not expose all ablation numbers, but the experimental structure appears to cover from-scratch growth, continued online adaptation, and domain dependence.4fd:T46d,Read this paper with a systems question in mind: why has speculative decoding been standard in serving, yet still depended on offline draft-head preparation in RL? After the introduction, focus on three technical pieces: reconstruction of draft-conditioned states, the DCA loss, and loss gating after the first rejection. Those are the parts that make the method more than simple distillation from verification logits. If time is limited, start with the method figure, the loss definition, and the rollout/training pseudocode, then move to the main training curves showing how acceptance length grows over RL steps and when net speedup appears. The most informative ablations are likely: removing draft-conditioned reconstruction, replacing DCA with independent depth losses, and training beyond the first rejection. While reading, it is worth asking whether the same online-growth idea could extend to stronger native MTP or EAGLE-style drafting modules, and whether partial backbone updates would help or destabilize RL. Around 20-30 minutes is enough for a solid skim; a careful read of method and experiments takes about an hour.4fe:T959,方法设计很干净。作者不从自然语言任务入手，而是构造一组 edge-emitting HMM，让模型读取由这些 HMM 生成的 token 序列，并预测下一个 token。对于每个时间步，真实 belief state 都可以由 HMM 的转移与发射概率精确算出，因此有了一个外部可监督的、理论上正确的表示目标。

论文的第一步是任务筛选。作者在 40 个具有非平凡 belief 结构的 HMM 上评估六个开源 LLM，只保留那些模型已经能接近最优 next-token 预测的过程。这样做是为了避免 probe 结果被“模型根本没学会这个过程”污染。换句话说，他们不是在问任何 HMM 上都能不能读出 belief state，而是在问：当模型行为上已经接近最优时，内部是否真的形成了对应的状态表示。

第二步是线性 probe。作者从不同层的 residual stream 提取激活，用线性回归去预测 belief state 向量，并报告 R2。这里的关键不是单纯 probe 成功，而是 belief state 的几何结构在多个模型、多个 HMM、多个层位上都能被线性读出，说明这种表示不是高度非线性、零散分布的偶然编码，而更像是残差空间中的一个相对规整子空间。

第三步是因果干预。论文做了两类 intervention：patching 和 steering。patching 可以理解为把某个样本在 belief 子空间上的表示替换成另一个表示，再看输出分布如何变化；steering 则是在该子空间上定向移动激活。作者比较了“替换成正确 belief 点”“替换成无关 belief 点”以及未干预模型的预测质量。若 belief 子空间只是相关但无功能，干预不应系统性改变输出；但实验显示，沿 probe 识别出的子空间做正确干预时，模型预测仍接近未干预水平，而替换成不相关 simplex 点会明显恶化。这说明该子空间对下游 next-token prediction 有因果作用。

理论背景上，作者借用了 computational mechanics。这个框架认为，对一个部分可观测随机过程做最优预测，需要维护能压缩过去并保留未来预测信息的充分统计量；在 HMM 场景下，这个量正是 belief state。论文的贡献不是提出新理论，而是把这个理论从 toy transformer 扩展到现成开源 LLM，并给出可证伪的表示预测、probe 和 intervention 证据链。4ff:Ta4a,The setup is clean and theory-driven. Instead of using natural-language tasks with ambiguous latent structure, the authors construct edge-emitting HMMs and feed their emitted token sequences to pretrained LLMs. For every time step, the ground-truth belief state can be computed exactly from the HMM dynamics, so the paper has a precise external target for what the model should represent if it is doing optimal latent-state tracking.

The first step is process selection. The authors evaluate six open-source LLMs on many HMMs and keep 40 with non-trivial belief structure on which the models achieve near-optimal next-token prediction. This is an important choice. They are not asking whether belief states are decodable for arbitrary HMMs; they are asking whether, when the model already behaves close to optimally, the corresponding latent posterior is present in the activations.

The second step is linear probing. Residual-stream activations from different layers are used to predict the belief-state vector with linear probes, and performance is measured with R2. The significance is not merely that a probe works. The belief geometry is linearly recoverable across multiple models, multiple HMMs, and at different depths, which suggests that the representation is organized in a relatively structured subspace rather than being diffusely encoded in a highly nonlinear way.

The third step is causal intervention. The paper uses patching and steering targeted at the probe-identified belief subspace. Roughly, patching replaces the belief-subspace component of one activation with another, while steering moves the activation along directions in that subspace. The authors compare interventions that preserve the correct belief geometry against interventions that substitute an unrelated point on the simplex. If the subspace were merely correlated with prediction, these manipulations should not systematically matter. Instead, interventions aligned with the identified belief state preserve prediction quality near the untampered model, while unrelated substitutions degrade it substantially. That makes the case functional rather than purely correlational.

The theoretical framing comes from computational mechanics. In that view, optimal prediction for a partially observed stochastic process requires tracking a sufficient statistic that compresses the past while preserving predictive information about the future. For HMMs, that statistic is exactly the belief state. The paper’s contribution is to carry this prediction from toy models into pretrained open-source LLMs and test it with both probes and interventions.500:T744,The study covers six open-source LLMs and 40 HMMs. The headline result is that belief states are linearly decodable from residual-stream activations, with peak probe R2 values ranging from 0.83 to 0.99 depending on the model and process. The best layer is not fixed: for some model–HMM pairs the strongest signal appears relatively early, for others later. That suggests belief-state formation is distributed and architecture-dependent rather than confined to the final layers.

A strong part of the experimental design is the behavioral filter. The authors first verify that the model is already near-optimal on next-token prediction for the selected HMMs, and only then analyze representations. This helps separate “the model never learned the process” from “the model learned it but represents it differently.”

The intervention results are the main functional evidence. When patching or steering within the identified belief subspace in a way that preserves the appropriate belief geometry, the KL divergence to the ground-truth next-token distribution remains on the same order as the untampered model. When the activation is replaced with an unrelated point on the belief simplex, prediction quality drops substantially. The abstract does not list all detailed numbers, but the qualitative pattern is consistent and important: correct manipulations of the belief subspace preserve behavior, incorrect ones damage it.

Another good design choice is the use of HMMs with non-trivial belief structure, rather than processes where the next-token distribution already fully captures the hidden dynamics. The paper also includes a contrasting case, Mess3, where hidden-state dynamics are no richer than the observable predictive distribution. That helps rule out the simpler interpretation that the probe is only reading out shallow token statistics.501:T4b8,Read this one with a specific question in mind: is the paper showing a real mechanism or just a probe artifact? Start with the introduction and Figure 1 to understand the exact hypothesis: not generic latent-state encoding, but belief-state geometry predicted by computational mechanics. Then read the background section on HMMs and belief states carefully so the probe target is unambiguous.

The most important part of the main text is the experimental design: how the 40 HMMs are selected, why near-optimal behavioral performance is required before probing, where in the residual stream the probes are applied, and what the control conditions are. Without those details, the probe results are easy to overinterpret.

After that, focus on the intervention section. The patching and steering constructions, and the use of KL divergence to the ground-truth next-token distribution as the evaluation metric, are what elevate the paper from representational correlation to something closer to mechanistic evidence. A careful first pass should take about 35–50 minutes. If you care about ICL theory or interpretability, the appendix on HMM selection, controls, and layerwise variation is worth the extra time.502:T43a,The experiments use Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Qwen3-8B, and Gemma-4-E4B. Activation analysis uses four depth checkpoints per model: layers 8/16/24/31 for Llama-3.1-8B, 9/18/27/35 for Qwen3-8B, and 28/29/40/41 for Gemma-4-E4B. Each condition uses 100 OpenOrca prompts of roughly 100 to 300 words, with adjacent-key typos applied at up to four positions. The observed on-site rotations are 43 to 56 degrees and decay to below 15% within about 10 downstream tokens. A stacked typo bundle reduces single-position prompt-injection probe TPR by 12.0 percentage points at FPR=1%, and threshold recalibration is not sufficient. Multi-position aggregation reduces localized perturbation loss to at most 0.5 percentage points, but distributed perturbations still cause about a 3.8-point drop even with attention- or max-based aggregation. The KV-cache-forked probe suffix closes about 95% of the single-position gap, leaving a 0.6-point residual, while perturbation-augmented training leaves a 3.7-point residual. An LLM-as-judge check labels 94.6% of clean-perturbed pairs as intent-preserving.503:T9e1,技术方案分成两层：模块化 tokenizer 构造，以及与之配套的预训练策略。

先看 tokenizer。作者分别给出 modular BPE 和 modular Unigram 的构造方法，目标是训练一个“大而可拆”的 multilingual tokenizer，然后从中抽取任意语言子集对应的 subtokenizer。这里难点不只是把不同语言的词表拼起来，因为简单拼接会破坏 token id、merge 规则或概率结构的一致性，也不保证抽出来的子词表还能接近单语 tokenizer 的压缩率。论文的做法是从训练阶段就约束 tokenizer 的结构，使每种语言或语言组对应的子词单元可以被稳定抽取，同时保留 byte-level fallback 和 lossless detokenization。对 BPE 和 Unigram 都提供了可抽取方案，说明作者不是只在某一种分词算法上做特例。

再看模型训练。核心思想是让模型在预训练时反复看到不同的 subtokenizer 组合，从而学会在不同 token inventory 下读写文本。论文把这些 subtokenizer 采样后组成 mini-batches，训练同一个模型共享主干参数，但输入 embedding 和输出预测都只在当前子词表上工作。这样做的直接结果是：部署到某个语言子集时，不需要加载完整 multilingual output matrix，只需保留目标语言相关 token 的 embedding/output rows。由于输出层 softmax 的维度显著缩小，推理速度和显存占用都会改善。

这套设计和传统 multilingual tokenizer 的区别有三点。第一，传统方法把所有语言塞进一个固定词表，压缩率和输出层成本一起被全局绑定；这里则把“共享训练”和“专用部署”拆开。第二，传统做法若想针对某语言优化，通常只能单独训练 monolingual tokenizer 和模型，跨语言共享会被破坏；这里保留了一个统一模型，只在 tokenizer/output head 层面做模块化。第三，作者强调目标不是追求极端压缩，而是在接近 monolingual compression 的前提下，保持多语言共享能力和部署灵活性。

从全文表述看，论文还引入了 balanced multilingual training 的思路：通过对子词表进行采样，模型不会总是暴露在同一个大词表下，从而减轻高资源语言在词表分配上的天然优势。这也是它改善 cross-lingual fairness 的机制之一。文中使用 Normalized Sequence Length, NSL 来量化各语言相对单语参考 tokenizer 的压缩损失，这个指标贯穿 tokenizer 评估和后续效率分析。504:Ta6b,实验部分有几条结果值得记住。

第一，现有开源 multilingual tokenizer 的压缩不公平问题很明显。作者在 FLORES-200 devtest 上，用 24k 单语 tokenizer 作为参考，比较 TinyAya、NLLB-200、Gemma-3、Llama-3、Qwen-3 等开放 tokenizer 的 NSL。结论是这些 tokenizer 对英语的压缩通常接近单语参考，但对大多数其他语言明显更差。作者还特意把评测限制在 21 个欧洲语言上，这些语言本来就属于中高资源、且通常被现有 tokenizer 覆盖得较好；即便如此，不公平仍然明显，说明问题不是只出在极低资源语言上。到了低资源语言，差距会更大。

第二，覆盖范围和压缩率之间存在清晰 trade-off。论文训练了只覆盖 21 种语言的标准 BPE tokenizer，记作 Multi21；当词表大小到 256k 时，它与 24k 单语 tokenizer 的压缩差距可以缩小到 4% 以内。这个结果说明，只要减少覆盖语言数，每种语言能分到更多词表容量，压缩自然改善。模块化 tokenizer 的意义就在于：不必为部署某几个语言时继续承担全量覆盖的代价。

第三，模块化 subtokenizer 的压缩率可以做到接近独立训练的 monolingual tokenizer。摘要已经明确给出这一点，全文则把它作为方法成立的关键证据：如果抽取后的 subtokenizer 明显劣于单语 tokenizer，那么后续训练和部署都失去意义。作者对 BPE 和 Unigram 都做了验证，说明不是某个特定 tokenizer 家族的偶然现象。

第四，推理效率确实受益，而且收益在小模型上更明显。论文在引言里举例，Gemma 2 2.6B 即便共享输入输出 embedding，256k 词表仍占到总参数的 22%。这给了一个很直观的量级：在小模型里，词表不是边角成本，而是核心成本。模块化方案在推理时只保留目标语言相关输出矩阵，因此能比标准 multilingual tokenizer 更快，同时在 multiple-choice、summarization、translation 上保持有竞争力。摘要没有列出全部具体分数，但全文强调速度提升来自两部分：更好的目标语言压缩减少序列长度，裁剪后的输出层减少每步 softmax 计算。

第五，作者对“压缩提升是否转化为质量提升”做了审慎处理。文中回顾了相互矛盾的既有结论，因此实验重点不是证明压缩越高模型越强，而是证明在不明显损害任务表现的前提下，可以把效率和跨语言公平性做得更好。这一点从研究设计上是合理的，因为 tokenizer 改动最直接的收益确实先体现在 token budget 和 output-layer cost 上。505:T5a6,This is a meaningful contribution at the tokenizer–pretraining interface. First, it turns the tokenizer from a fixed global artifact into a modular object that can be specialized after training. That is important because multilingual tokenization has usually been treated as a one-shot design choice. Second, it connects tokenizer design directly to model memory footprint and output-layer compute, rather than discussing compression in isolation. For 1B–3B scale models, vocabulary-related parameters are not a side issue; they can take a large fraction of the total budget. Third, the paper does not stop at tokenizer construction. It provides a pretraining recipe that teaches the model to operate under different subtokenizer subsets, which is what makes deployment-time vocabulary pruning actually work. Finally, the paper is careful about claims: it frames better compression mainly as an efficiency and fairness gain, not as a guaranteed quality gain. That restraint is appropriate and makes the contribution more credible.

For pretraining researchers, two ideas stand out. One is that vocabulary size, language coverage, and output-layer cost do not have to remain a single static trade-off; they can be shared during training and specialized at deployment. The other is that tokenizer design is not just preprocessing. If the model is not trained to handle changing token inventories, modular tokenization is not usable in practice.506:Ta8d,The method has two layers: modular tokenizer construction and a matching pretraining strategy.

On the tokenizer side, the authors propose both modular BPE and modular Unigram schemes. The objective is to train a large multilingual tokenizer from which one can extract subtokenizers for any language or language subset. The challenge is not simply concatenating language-specific vocabularies. A naive union would break consistency in token IDs, merge rules, or token probabilities, and the extracted subsets would not necessarily preserve monolingual-like compression. The paper therefore designs the tokenizer training process so that language-specific components remain extractable while preserving byte-level fallback and lossless detokenization. The fact that the framework works for both BPE and Unigram is important; it suggests the idea is not tied to one tokenizer family.

On the model side, the key idea is to expose the model during pretraining to many different subtokenizer combinations. These subtokenizers are sampled and used to form batches, so the same backbone learns to read and predict text under varying token inventories. In each case, the input embedding and output prediction operate only on the active sub-vocabulary. At deployment time, this allows the system to load only the rows of the embedding/output matrices relevant to the target language subset, instead of the full multilingual vocabulary. The efficiency gain comes from two places: shorter sequences for the target languages and a smaller softmax/output layer.

Compared with standard multilingual tokenization, the difference is threefold. First, conventional approaches bind language coverage and output-layer cost into one fixed vocabulary; this framework decouples shared training from specialized deployment. Second, the usual way to optimize for a language is to train a separate monolingual tokenizer and often a separate model, which weakens multilingual sharing; here the model remains unified and only the tokenizer/output interface becomes modular. Third, the paper is not chasing maximal compression at any cost. The target is monolingual-like compression together with multilingual parameter sharing and deployment flexibility.

A further mechanism in the paper is balanced multilingual exposure through subtokenizer sampling. Because the model does not always train under the same giant vocabulary, high-resource languages have less structural advantage in vocabulary allocation. The paper uses Normalized Sequence Length (NSL) throughout to quantify how far each language is from a monolingual reference tokenizer, and this metric anchors both the tokenizer analysis and the efficiency discussion.507:Ta0d,Several empirical results matter.

First, existing open multilingual tokenizers show clear compression unfairness. On FLORES-200 devtest, using 24k monolingual tokenizers as references, the paper compares tokenizers from TinyAya, NLLB-200, Gemma-3, Llama-3, and Qwen-3. The pattern is consistent: compression is often close to monolingual quality for English, but substantially worse for most other languages. Importantly, the evaluation is intentionally conservative: only 21 European languages, mostly medium- to high-resource and already relatively well covered by open multilingual tokenizers. If unfairness is visible there, it is not a niche low-resource artifact.

Second, the coverage–compression trade-off is explicit. The paper trains a standard BPE tokenizer on only those 21 languages, called Multi21. With a 256k vocabulary, its compression comes within 4% of 24k monolingual tokenizers. This is a useful calibration point: if you reduce the number of covered languages, each language gets more vocabulary capacity and compression improves. The modular framework is valuable because it lets deployment benefit from that specialization without giving up a shared multilingual model.

Third, extracted modular subtokenizers achieve compression close to independently trained monolingual tokenizers. This is one of the central validity checks of the method. If the extracted subtokenizers were much worse than monolingual ones, the whole framework would collapse. The paper demonstrates this for both BPE and Unigram, which strengthens the claim.

Fourth, the efficiency gains are real and especially relevant for small models. The introduction gives a concrete scale example: Gemma 2 2.6B spends 22% of its parameters on a 256k vocabulary even with tied embeddings. That makes the cost of the vocabulary impossible to ignore. By pruning the output matrix to the target language subset at inference, the modular approach speeds up decoding while remaining competitive on multiple-choice evaluation, summarization, and translation. The full paper emphasizes that the speedup comes from both better target-language compression and a smaller output layer.

Fifth, the paper is careful about the relationship between compression and quality. It reviews prior work showing mixed evidence on whether better compression improves downstream performance. Accordingly, the experiments are designed to show that efficiency and cross-lingual fairness can improve without materially hurting task quality, rather than claiming that compression alone guarantees better models.508:T6af,This one is worth a careful read. A good order is: problem setup → tokenizer construction → pretraining recipe → efficiency and quality results.

Start with the introduction and the section on multilingual tokenizer inefficiencies. They clearly explain why a single multilingual vocabulary creates both compression unfairness and output-layer waste. Figure 1 and the NSL definition are foundational. Then read the modular BPE and modular Unigram sections closely to understand what “extractable subtokenizers” really means and how it differs from ordinary jointly trained tokenizers. After that, focus on the pretraining strategy: how subtokenizers are sampled at the batch level, how embeddings and output rows are shared or restricted, and how the model remains stable while the token inventory changes. Finally, read the experiments with attention to three groups of results: per-language NSL comparisons, speed/compression trade-offs as vocabulary size changes, and downstream performance when deploying to language subsets.

There are four questions worth keeping in mind. First, does switching among subtokenizers create optimization instability or sparse embedding learning? Second, after pruning the output layer, is cross-lingual transfer weakened because the token inventory has changed? Third, do the gains remain meaningful at larger model scales, or are they concentrated in the regime where embeddings are a large parameter fraction? Fourth, could the same modular idea extend beyond multilingual text to unified discrete token spaces for text, speech, or vision? Reading with those questions in mind makes it easier to judge how transferable the method is to other pretraining settings.509:T555,ZGCM-1 is a 7.39B decoder-only Transformer with 32 layers, hidden size 4096, SwiGLU intermediate size 11008, 32 query heads, 8 KV heads, GQA, RMSNorm, SwiGLU, RoPE, and a 256K maximum context length. Its central architectural choice is a hybrid causal-attention backbone. Twenty-seven layers use gated sliding-window attention with a 128-token window, while five layers use global causal attention at layers 6, 12, 18, 24, and 30. This 5:1 local-to-global pattern trades full attention for much lower KV-cache and bandwidth cost, while still allowing periodic long-range information mixing. The model also uses QK normalization and partial RoPE with a rotary fraction of 0.33 to improve long-context stability.

On the training side, the recipe combines the Muon optimizer, hybrid FP8 precision, and TWEO outlier regularization. The goal is lower time-to-loss rather than only faster per-step execution. Mid-training uses a 600B-token curriculum that increases context length from 16K to 64K to 256K. Multi-turn interaction traces are reformulated as Markov decision process state-action transitions, which gives the model dense supervision at intermediate steps instead of supervising only the final answer. Post-training uses execution-verified trajectories and mixed think/no-think SFT, so the model learns both extended reasoning and efficient direct responses.50a:T49e,The paper reports results on 20 benchmarks. At the systems level, the hybrid attention design reduces per-token KV-cache footprint by 6.4x and improves throughput by 3.94x at 256K context compared with standard full attention. The combination of Muon, hybrid FP8, and TWEO gives about a 4.2x pre-training time-to-loss speedup over an AdamW/BF16 baseline.

On reasoning tasks, ZGCM-1-7B is reported to lead the 7B–8B comparison group on the average of 14 reasoning benchmarks. Specific scores include 75.0% on AIME 2026, 97.1% on MATH-500, and 70.4% on HMMT 2025. On agentic search and system-agency tasks, it reaches 63.1% on WebWalkerQA, 19.4% on BrowseComp, and 62.0% on Binary Function Search. These results support the paper’s practical claim: for compact models, long-context reasoning plus supervised tool interaction can be a more effective route than relying on parametric memorization alone.

The paper also reports how AI agents were used in the model-development workflow. Agents were more useful for data processing, experimentation, monitoring, evaluation, and deployment than for architecture or learning-algorithm design, where human direction remained important.50b:T41f,FedTAR (Task-awARe Federated fine-tuning) uses routing statistics as a proxy for latent task structure and ties it to update aggregation:
1) During local fine-tuning, each client collects routing features such as average expert utilization, expert co-activation patterns, and routing confidence.
2) Apply SVD on routing features to obtain low-dimensional task coordinates that make clients clusterable by implicit task preference.
3) Apply SVD on local parameter updates to extract dominant update directions.
4) Perform task-aware clustering and aggregation (within and across clusters) based on task coordinates, rather than indiscriminate averaging.
5) Learn a mapping between the task space and the update space, then reconstruct the aggregated global update so it remains aligned with task-specific dominant directions—aiming to preserve expert specialization and reduce conflicts on shared experts.
The key departure from FedAvg is that aggregation and reconstruction are driven by routing behavior, not by explicit task labels or manual grouping.50c:T40d,The proposed Compute-Value Audit decomposes test-time scaling into four ordered gates: opportunity, state confidence, action value, and entry fee. Opportunity asks whether better samples exist in the fixed pool. State asks whether observable signals are informative. Action asks whether using those signals improves the target metric. Entry fee accounts for the full cost of generation and verification. The audit fixes the complete candidate budget and requires selectors to score the same pool, avoiding hidden generation or unfair cache reuse. The paper also introduces a Verifier-Quality Law using a minimal Gaussian model, showing that recovered headroom is directly governed by the correlation between verifier score and target quality. Tested deployable signals include Proprio, a one-step flow residual under controlled latent perturbations; cycle energy, which re-noises a latent and integrates it back to measure consistency; and PM, a memory-based reranker that uses legal history without updating the world model or verifier.50d:T40c,The paper is a critical review rather than a new modeling method. It separates three notions. The allocation problem is the decision of how to divide build-time and run-time resources under cost and deployment constraints. A scaling result measures how quality changes as one resource is varied while other settings are fixed. An allocation claim says that one budget split is better than another. The paper argues that many studies establish the second but not the third. It identifies three recurring mismatches: success is counted before a returned answer is selected, the experiment uses information unavailable at deployment time, and important costs are omitted. Examples include reporting coverage over many sampled answers instead of returned-answer accuracy, using answer keys or oracle difficulty estimates, and counting only generation FLOPs while ignoring verifier training, retrieval, latency, or dollar costs. The proposed resource envelope records the metric, available information, and cost boundary alongside the score.50e:T8f9,方法建立在 BD3LM 上。先回顾基线：BD3LM 按 block 自回归，block 内用 masked diffusion 去噪；训练时只在被 mask 的位置上做 SUBS 参数化下的 token 预测；推理时从全 mask 开始，反复预测所有 mask 位置，再按 schedule 或置信度固定一部分 token。问题在于，这一步里各位置预测是独立的。

DA-DLM 的核心改动，是在每个去噪步构造一个 position-oriented DAG，而不是直接输出各位置独立分布。这个 DAG 不是 DAT 在 NAT 里那种大而自由的无位置约束图，而是显式绑定到输出位置。每个输出位置对应一个 node group：
- 如果该位置的 token 在更早去噪步已经被固定，那么这个位置在当前 DAG 中就是一个单节点 anchor；
- 如果该位置还未确定，就为该位置展开多个候选节点，表示该位置当前可能的局部模态。

然后只允许相邻位置的 group 之间建立 transition。这样一来，最终不是对每个位置各选一个 token，而是在整张 DAG 上选一条穿过各位置 group 的路径。路径分数同时考虑节点发射分数和相邻候选之间的转移分数，于是同一步里多个 token 的选择被耦合起来。已经固定的 token 作为 anchor 被钉在图上，能对邻近未决位置形成结构性约束。这一点是作者区别于直接照搬 DAT 的关键：DLM 是迭代式的，前几步已确定 token 的“锚定作用”必须保留，否则 successive denoising 容易漂。

从机制上看，这个设计做了两件事。第一，它把 DLM 每步的预测目标从 factorized marginals 变成了一个局部链式依赖上的联合选择问题。第二，它让 DAG 随去噪过程演化：随着步数推进，anchor 越来越多，未决位置越来越少，图会逐渐收缩，模型把容量集中到剩余不确定区域。这个动态图结构很适合 DLM 的 iterative refinement，而不适合一次性 NAT 生成。

论文的思想来源是 DAT，但改造点很明确：DAT 面向单步生成，允许更自由的转移；DA-DLM 面向 iterative denoising，因此采用 position-oriented DAG 来强化已固定 token 的约束，并让图结构与当前 mask 状态同步变化。这个差异不是实现细节，而是任务结构决定的。50f:T90a,The method is built on BD3LM. In the baseline, generation is autoregressive across blocks, while each block is generated by masked diffusion. During training, only masked positions contribute under the SUBS parameterization. During inference, the model starts from a fully masked block, predicts all masked positions in parallel, and then fixes a subset of tokens according to a schedule or confidence rule. The key limitation is that those per-position predictions are independent.

DA-DLM replaces that factorized prediction with a position-oriented DAG constructed at every denoising step. This is not the same as directly importing DAT from NAT. DAT uses a large DAG with relatively unconstrained transitions for one-shot generation. DA-DLM instead binds the graph explicitly to output positions.

Each output position corresponds to a node group. If a token at that position has already been fixed in an earlier denoising step, the group collapses to a single anchor node. If the position is still unresolved, the model expands it into multiple candidate nodes representing local alternatives. Transitions are only allowed between adjacent position groups. Generation within the step is therefore no longer a set of independent token choices. It becomes a path selection problem through the DAG, where the path score combines node scores and transition scores. This couples the token decisions made in the same denoising step.

The anchor mechanism is the critical adaptation to iterative denoising. Previously fixed tokens are pinned into the graph and structurally constrain nearby unresolved positions. That is the main reason the authors do not simply reuse DAT as-is. In DLMs, the denoising process should progressively converge as more tokens become fixed. Without explicit anchoring, successive steps can drift rather than refine.

Conceptually, the method does two things. First, it changes the denoising objective at each step from factorized marginals to a structured joint selection problem over a local dependency chain. Second, it lets the graph evolve with denoising: as more positions become anchors, fewer candidate groups remain, and the graph shrinks toward the residual uncertainty. That dynamic graph is well matched to iterative refinement and is the main architectural idea of the paper.510:T6f6,The evaluation covers language modeling, open-ended generation, and summarization. The headline findings have two parts. First, DA-DLM consistently outperforms the BD3LM baseline across all settings. Second, the gains are larger when fewer denoising steps are used, which is exactly where the independence problem should hurt the most. That alignment between motivation and empirical behavior is important.

A particularly useful result is that on summarization, DA-DLM matches the autoregressive baseline while retaining the parallel decoding advantage. This suggests that the method is not only making open-ended text look smoother. It is also recovering sequence-level consistency in conditional generation.

From the structure of the paper, the most important ablations are likely to be: step-count sensitivity, to show that the advantage widens in low-step regimes; DAG design ablations, to test whether position orientation and anchors are necessary; and task generalization, to show gains beyond a single metric such as perplexity. For this paper, the most informative curve is not a single average score but how quality degrades as denoising steps are reduced. If DA-DLM flattens that degradation curve, then it is addressing a core structural issue rather than making a small improvement in a comfortable high-step regime.

The anchor idea may generalize beyond diffusion to a wider class of structured denoising LMs.512:Ta2b,方法核心是 Discrete Beckmann Transport Models，简称 DBTM。理解它要抓住三个层次。

第一层是表示。作者把离散 token 序列嵌入到每个位置一个 V 维 simplex 顶点的连续空间里，整条序列是 (R^V)^L 中的点。数据分布 μ1 支持在 one-hot 顶点上，先验 μ0 是连续高斯。目标是学一个从连续空间到离散数据流形的 transport。

第二层是动力学。传统 flow matching 学的是随时间变化的速度场 bt(x)，采样要积分 ODE；flow map 学的是两时刻算子 X_{s,t}，但 off-diagonal 项通常需要 teacher 或 bootstrap。DBTM 改学 autonomous，也就是 time-independent 的速度场 b(x)，对应自治 ODE dX_s/ds = b(X_s)。在这个设定下，流映射满足半群性质，且作者利用 time-independent flow 的几何性质构造一个 transport map T(x)，它把任意 ambient point 沿自治流送到某个固定点，最终落在 simplex 顶点支撑的数据流形上。

第三层是训练。关键不是直接监督 T 的终点，而是利用固定点性质导出守恒方程 b·∇T = 0。直观上，沿着流线前进时，最终 transport destination 不应改变，因此 T 在流方向上的导数为零。作者最重要的贡献是把这个 PDE 残差变成可从数据最小化的训练目标，从而不需要 teacher flow。全文里还给出一个可操作的近似训练法：用冻结副本的当前模型作为 bootstrap target，再加一个 Euler correction，迭代回归到更接近真实 transport map 的目标。论文声称，部分训练好的 Tθ 并不是无意义的半成品，而是对应自治流上的中间点；因此在推理时可以反复应用 Tθ 做 iterative refinement，逐步逼近固定点。

另一个关键设计是 partial-context interpolant。它不是简单在全序列上做连续插值，而是保留部分上下文、对其余位置做插值/传输学习。这样做有两个作用：一是更适合条件生成和 reasoning，因为 prompt 或已确定 token 可以作为锚点；二是允许训练和推理时基于置信度或质量做 selective refinement，而不是每一步都全量重写整条序列。

和已有方法相比，差异很明确。相对离散 diffusion，DBTM 不依赖时间步去噪链。相对 flow matching，它不学 bt(x,t) 而学 autonomous map。相对 flow-map distillation，它不需要先有一个收敛 teacher 来提供 off-diagonal 监督。相对纯 bootstrap 的 few-step map，它把 bootstrap 放在一个有固定点/守恒结构约束的框架里，试图缓解目标漂移和训练不稳。513:T7e4,实验分成两类：无条件语言建模和条件 reasoning。作者强调的指标是低或匹配 NFE 下的性能，而不是只看高步数极限。摘要没有给出完整数字，但从正文结构可以判断，主结果应当比较 DBTM 与离散 diffusion、flow matching、以及需要 teacher 的 flow-map/few-step baseline，在 1-step、少步 refinement、以及 matched-compute 条件下的质量差异。

That matters for pretraining research in at least three ways.

First, it directly challenges the common assumption that few-step discrete generation must be built on top of a teacher model. If this line of work holds up, one-step or low-step language modeling may no longer require an expensive upstream AR or diffusion teacher.

Second, it shifts the objective from fitting instantaneous velocities to satisfying a fixed-point and conservation structure. That changes how the model is parameterized, how it is trained, and how refinement is performed at inference time. For researchers interested in alternatives to next-token AR modeling, this is much more consequential than a standard decoding-speed paper.

Third, the paper evaluates not only unconditional language modeling but also conditional reasoning. This is a must-read paper because it offers a genuinely different route for discrete language generation, with a fairly complete mathematical and algorithmic story.515:Tbc4,The core idea of Discrete Beckmann Transport Models (DBTM) can be understood in three layers.

The first layer is representation. A discrete token sequence is embedded into a continuous space where each token is a vertex of the V-dimensional simplex. A full sequence is therefore a point in (R^V)^L. The data distribution lives on one-hot vertices, while the prior is continuous Gaussian noise. The modeling goal is to learn a transport from the ambient continuous space to the discrete data manifold.

The second layer is dynamics. Standard flow matching learns a time-dependent velocity field b_t(x) and requires ODE integration at sampling time. Flow-map methods learn a two-time operator X_{s,t}, but the off-diagonal terms are usually learned either from a teacher or through unstable bootstrapping. DBTM instead learns an autonomous, time-independent velocity field b(x), defining an ODE dX_s/ds = b(X_s). In this setting, the flow has a semigroup structure, and the paper constructs a transport map T(x) that sends any ambient point along the autonomous flow to a fixed point on the simplex-supported data manifold.

The third layer is training. Rather than supervising the terminal point directly, the paper derives a conservation equation, b · ∇T = 0. Intuitively, as one moves along a flow line, the final transport destination should remain unchanged, so T is constant in the flow direction. This is the central technical contribution: the PDE residual is turned into a trainable objective that can be minimized from data, removing the need for a teacher flow. The practical training procedure uses a frozen copy of the current model as a bootstrap target plus an Euler correction, iteratively regressing toward a better approximation of the true transport map. A partially trained T_theta is not treated as a failed endpoint predictor; instead, it is interpreted as mapping to an intermediate point along the autonomous flow. That makes iterative application of T_theta meaningful at inference time.

Another important design is the partial-context interpolant. Instead of interpolating the entire sequence uniformly, the method preserves part of the context and learns transport on the remaining positions. This is important for two reasons: it makes the framework suitable for conditional generation and reasoning, where prompts or already-decided tokens should act as anchors; and it enables confidence- or quality-based selective refinement instead of rewriting the whole sequence at every step.

Relative to prior work, the distinctions are clear. Compared with discrete diffusion, DBTM does not rely on a time-indexed denoising chain. Compared with flow matching, it does not learn b_t(x, t). Compared with flow-map distillation, it does not require a converged teacher to supervise off-diagonal transitions. Compared with pure bootstrap approaches, it places self-training inside a fixed-point and conservation-structured framework, which is intended to reduce target drift and instability.516:T934,The experiments cover both unconditional language modeling and conditional reasoning, with the main emphasis on quality at low or matched NFE rather than asymptotic performance at large sampling budgets. The abstract does not provide full tables, but the paper clearly positions DBTM against discrete diffusion, flow matching, and teacher-distilled few-step flow-map baselines under one-step, few-step refinement, and matched-compute settings.

Several experimental signals are especially important. First, whether one-step generation is already usable, and how close it gets to teacher-distilled few-step methods. If one-step DBTM is competitive, that would strongly support the claim that the autonomous transport map and fixed-point structure are doing real work. Second, whether iterative application of T_theta improves quality consistently, or at least substantially over the first few refinement steps. That directly tests the paper’s claim that partially trained maps correspond to intermediate points along the autonomous flow. Third, whether the partial-context interpolant materially helps on reasoning and conditional generation, since that determines whether the method is genuinely language-model-like rather than just a generic discrete sampler.

The most informative ablations are likely to include: removing the conservation residual, removing the frozen-self-target plus Euler correction, comparing autonomous and time-dependent formulations, plotting performance against the number of refinement steps, and testing confidence-based selective refinement. If the paper includes trajectory visualizations in simplex space, those are likely more revealing than scalar metrics because they can show whether DBTM is actually learning transport toward vertices rather than behaving like a standard denoiser.

The wording in the abstract, 'stronger performance than baselines at lower or matched NFEs,' is also worth reading carefully. It suggests the gains are concentrated in the compute-efficient regime rather than uniformly across all settings. If the advantage disappears at high NFE, then DBTM should be viewed primarily as a few-step modeling framework. If the gains persist on reasoning tasks, then it is more than a sampler-speed method and starts to look like a viable alternative generative paradigm for conditional language tasks.517:T780,Read it in the order of theory, training objective, then empirical validation.

That distinction will matter for scaling to larger vocabularies, longer contexts, and multimodal discrete token spaces.518:T6e7,DenMark replaces sentence-level candidate selection with rollout-guided semantic lookahead over local denoising updates.
The method has three main components:
1. Fixed region partitioning. The output sequence is divided into token regions that serve as the basic units for watermark injection and detection. These regions are not assumed to align perfectly with syntax; they provide a stable operational granularity during iterative denoising.
2. Temporary rollouts for semantic estimation. A local token update inside a DLM does not immediately define a complete semantic unit, so its watermark value cannot be scored directly. DenMark temporarily rolls out unresolved positions to form approximate completions, evaluates them with a key-dependent semantic scoring function, and estimates the expected watermark gain of each candidate local update. The update with the highest estimated score is then committed. In this way, watermark evidence is accumulated progressively throughout denoising rather than injected only after full sentence completion.
3. Calibrated scanning at detection time. Semantic attacks can shift token boundaries and break the original region alignment. To recover evidence under such shifts, the detector scans over multiple candidate region sizes and calibrates the resulting statistics.
The main conceptual difference from prior semantic watermarking is that DenMark does not force DLMs into an AR-style candidate-rejection loop. Instead, it works with the native iterative denoising process and moves semantic evaluation into local decision making. The paper also provides an analysis interpreting the final semantic score gain as the accumulation of many local choices, which helps explain why the method works beyond empirical results.519:T4ba,From the provided text, the experiments cover multiple DLMs and datasets, with the main comparison against token-level watermark baselines under semantic attacks. Those will tell you more about the method’s limits than a single aggregate detection metric.51a:T630,The method, BOTA, appears to reformulate branched optimal transport as a continuous and differentiable objective that can be optimized with neural flows. Instead of explicitly solving for a discrete transport tree, it parameterizes a transport field with neural networks and trains it in a flow-matching style. The conceptual move is important: standard conditional flow matching learns a velocity field from source-target pairs, but each pair is effectively independent. BOTA introduces a preference for path sharing across samples, reflecting the BOT economy-of-scale principle.

The distinction from prior work has three parts. First, standard FM/CFM prescribes conditional paths per sample pair; BOTA introduces coupling across trajectories so that shared routes become cheaper. Second, classical BOT defines subadditive transport costs on edges, typically scaling like m^alpha with 0<alpha<1; BOTA translates that branching preference into a continuous trainable objective compatible with neural ODEs and flow matching. Third, the solver is amortized: the network learns reusable branched transport structure across batches and tasks instead of solving a fresh BOT instance each time.

From the available full text, the pipeline is roughly: define density evolution and velocity fields, introduce a BOT-inspired objective or regularizer that favors coalescence and later branching, and optimize a neural vector field with a flow-matching-style loss. The main novelty is not merely another FM variant, but the shift from independent particle transport to shared network transport.51b:T541,The experiments focus on biological generation tasks and image generation, with the central claim being structural rather than purely metric: BOTA learns meaningful hierarchical generative processes. 1. Trajectory visualizations showing samples sharing a trunk before splitting into subclasses or modes, unlike standard FM where trajectories remain largely independent.
2. Standard generation metrics showing competitive or improved modeling quality on image or biological data.
3. Ablations on the branching strength, likely through the BOT exponent or related regularization terms, showing that removing the branching bias weakens both structure and performance.

3. Explicit treatment of the KV Cache Absence issue as a systems constraint that any practical early-exit setup must handle, even though the paper does not center its novelty on a new cache-repair mechanism.
4. Self-supervised supervision: the readout is trained only on the frozen model’s own full-depth outputs over ordinary traffic, not on human labels.

For training, the AR backbone is frozen and a diffusion view is trained to propose multiple future tokens in parallel. The main methodological change is the distillation data distribution. Rather than using generic human-written continuations, the authors build a teacher-generated corpus: they take prompts from public Hugging Face datasets, ask Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B to produce greedy continuations, and train on those prompt-response pairs. This better matches the states the frozen AR model actually visits during generation, reducing the mismatch between teacher forcing and on-policy decoding. They keep prompts between 50 and 1,000 characters and obtain 4,113,358 distilled samples, training on eight H100 GPUs.

For evaluation, the criterion is exact token-by-token identity with the corresponding frozen AR model. Orthrus and the AR baseline are run under different precisions, and the generated trajectories are compared directly. The central argument is that Orthrus’s consensus mechanism may preserve equivalence in an ideal arithmetic model, but finite precision introduces tiny differences in logits, normalization, or cache state. Because decoding is a discrete decision process, those small perturbations can cross a decision boundary at some step and cause the entire continuation to diverge. The paper also analyzes the relationship between divergence and response-conditional perplexity, showing that uncertain generations are more sensitive to numerical perturbations.51f:T664,There are three main empirical findings.

First, the core losslessness test. On 1,190 prompts from 12 domains, exact trajectory matching under BF16 is only 45% for the released Orthrus checkpoint and 43% for the independently trained model. In other words, more than half of the generations diverge at some point from the reference AR trajectory. Under FP32, the same evaluation yields exact matching, which supports the paper’s claim that the issue is not the abstract consensus logic but finite-precision implementation.

Second, training data distribution matters for parallel decoding efficiency. The independently trained model, built from teacher-generated on-policy distillation data, achieves higher Tokens Per Forward than the released checkpoint on most evaluated domains. The abstract does not list all per-domain numbers, but the full text presents this as a consistent pattern, suggesting that the diffusion view benefits from seeing prefixes that the backbone actually produces.

Third, divergence does not necessarily imply worse benchmark performance. The paper reports cases where Orthrus scores slightly higher than the corresponding AR model despite sequence-level mismatch under BF16. This is an important caution: benchmark parity does not establish exact inference equivalence, and small numerical perturbations can occasionally move a generation toward a benchmark-preferred answer. The authors also find a strong association between exact matching probability and response-conditional perplexity: the less confident the reference model is, the easier it is for small numerical errors to alter the chosen token.520:T45e,Start with the introduction to understand the target of the critique: the paper is not arguing that Orthrus is useless, only that the term “lossless” is too strong unless precision and equivalence criteria are specified. Then go straight to the main BF16 vs FP32 trajectory-matching results; that is the most informative part. After that, read the training setup, especially the construction of the teacher-generated distillation corpus and the motivation for preferring it over generic human continuations. Finally, look at the analysis linking divergence to response-conditional perplexity, which helps explain when numerical precision matters most.

If time is limited, the best order is: Introduction → main trajectory-equivalence experiments → training data construction → perplexity analysis. Around 20–30 minutes should be enough to extract the main message. A good question to keep in mind while reading is what “lossless” means in your own system: token-level identity, distributional equivalence, or benchmark preservation. The paper gives a practical framework for checking that distinction.521:T4c0,Self-Indexing Attention builds a shared transform-domain sign-magnitude representation. A structured orthogonal transform (motivated by Hadamard-style transforms with random sign flips, LSH intuition, and transform-domain KV compression such as QJL/TurboQuant) is applied to Q/K/V. The per-coordinate sign of transformed keys is stored as a 1-bit, token-level index. Query–key similarity is approximated via sign agreement (a proxy for angular similarity).

Because sign bits are part of the compressed key payload, the same representation supports retrieval and compression without separate index metadata.

To make it work across inference stages:
- Prefill: group queries to amortize selection cost. Instead of average pooling (which can cancel signs), use absmax-sign pooling: for each coordinate, take the sign of the query with the largest absolute value, preserving evidence important to any query in the group.
- Decode: perform packed 1-bit sign-agreement scoring for fast candidate selection, then apply norm-weighted agreement to reintroduce magnitude information lost in sign-only matching.
- Implementation: GQA-aware sparse-attention kernels and bitwise operations for accelerator-friendly execution.522:T918,StepPrune models token selection as an autoregressive policy over subsets, P(S|X)=∏t πθ(at|a<t,X). The action space contains all visual tokens plus a learned STOP action. The policy selects tokens one step at a time, conditioned on the image, the text prompt, and the previously selected tokens. The first time STOP is chosen, the episode ends, so the retained token count becomes input-adaptive rather than a manually fixed hyperparameter.

The selector is implemented as a cross-modal pointer-style decoder. This is the key departure from one-shot top-K ranking. Once one token has been selected, the value of nearby or redundant tokens should decrease, while complementary evidence may become more valuable. A sequential policy can model that changing marginal utility; independent scoring cannot.

Training is nontrivial because argmax-based subset selection is discrete. The paper introduces a trajectory-aware differentiable surrogate built around a variance-preserving noise gate. Aggregated pointer probabilities are used to smoothly interpolate each visual token between its original representation and isotropic Gaussian noise. High-probability tokens remain close to the original signal; low-probability tokens are pushed toward noise. This creates a differentiable pathway from the language-modeling objective back to the selector. To prevent the model from reconstructing masked information through neighboring tokens, the method adds a locally masked denoiser that limits cross-token leakage.

A second practical issue is selector overhead. Pure token-by-token decoding can become expensive for long visual prefixes, especially with AnyRes, dynamic-resolution, or multi-tile representations. To reduce recurrent selection latency, StepPrune allows grouped sequential selection: each pointer step selects a small group of tokens instead of exactly one. The paper uses five tokens per step as a default trade-off. This keeps the history-conditioned nature of the policy while making the selector scalable enough to be useful in practice.

So the main distinction from standard pruning baselines is not just a better scoring function. The decision structure itself changes: StepPrune optimizes a selection trajectory with adaptive stopping, rather than assigning independent relevance scores under a fixed budget.523:T537,The evaluation spans four MLLM backbones with different visual sequence organizations: LLaVA-1.5, LLaVA-NeXT, Qwen2.5-VL, and InternVL3. That matters because the method is meant to work across fixed-resolution, AnyRes, dynamic-resolution, and multi-tile visual prefixes.

The headline result reported for LLaVA-1.5 is strong from an efficiency perspective: after pruning 88.9% of visual tokens, the model still retains 94.6% of normalized full-prefix performance. With an average of 64 retained tokens, StepPrune achieves a 1.50× prefill speed-up. This indicates substantial redundancy in the original visual prefix for many inputs.

The paper emphasizes two empirical advantages. First, the accuracy-compression trade-off is more stable than with fixed top-K pruning. Second, adaptive stopping allocates fewer tokens to simple inputs and more to visually complex ones, which is more sensible than enforcing the same K for every sample.

The most informative ablations are likely the following: sequential selection versus one-shot selection, with and without the STOP action, and different group sizes for grouped selection. Even though the provided excerpt does not list all numbers, these are the experiments that support the paper’s main claims about conditional dependence, adaptive budgeting, and practical latency trade-offs.524:T472,OpWeave has three components. First, it introduces an analytical cost model for colocated serving, homogeneous operator disaggregation, and heterogeneous operator disaggregation. The model characterizes how gains depend on sequence length, model architecture, and hardware. It also shows that core-attention disaggregation approaches the ideal only when stages are balanced and communication is overlapped; fixed two-stage splits can break down when hardware ratios, workload shape, or hybrid-attention layer variation create pipeline imbalance. Second, OpWeave formulates planning as a joint optimization over operator partitioning, hardware assignment, parallelism, batching, and orchestration. To keep the search tractable, it introduces the partition block, the smallest repeating layer-aligned operator pattern, and reuses decisions across layers with similar high-level structure. Third, the system implements the generated plans in a vLLM-based runtime with staged engines, flexible pipeline schedules, and low-overhead worker execution that submits compute and communication sequences in a single native call per decode iteration.525:T622,The paper proceeds in three steps. First, it formulates two-sided GPTQ under a Kronecker-factored quadratic geometry. Standard GPTQ uses only the input-side covariance, corresponding to a Hessian of the form E[xx^T]⊗I. The two-sided extension allows a general A⊗B, which means quantization is guided by both input and output geometry and effectively minimizes ||(B^{1/2})^T(V-W)A^{1/2}||_F^2. Second, the authors extend the high-rate waterfilling view from prior work to this two-sided setting, yielding WaterKron. Instead of assigning uniform precision to all weights, WaterKron allocates row- and column-dependent scales and combines them with entropy coding. Under high-rate, Gaussian, and scalar-grid assumptions, the resulting allocation remains within an asymptotic gap of about 0.25 bits from the information-theoretic limit for the Kronecker distortion. Third, and most importantly, the paper analyzes WaterKron under the true full-Hessian geometry. This yields an explicit mismatch factor Φ that quantifies the multiplicative distortion penalty introduced by replacing the full Hessian with a Kronecker approximation. Choosing A and B is then cast as minimizing Φ. That optimization reduces to a Gaussian covariance-fitting problem and naturally recovers classical flip-flop updates, which motivates the proposed FlipFlop Hessian. The key distinction from prior Hessian choices in the quantization literature is that the approximation is selected to minimize distortion in the true geometry, not merely because it is easy to compute or empirically decent.526:T421,Carryover Drafting feeds rejected target hidden states from the current verification round into the next drafting round as temporary KV context. It reuses the same projection interface already used by DFlash and DSpark-like drafters for accepted target states. The method adds only one learned embedding to mark carried-over rejected states, rather than adding a separate gating or projection module. To control inference cost, carried-over states are replaced every round instead of accumulated, so the additional KV context is bounded by one proposal block. For training, the paper introduces parallel draft–verify–draft. At sampled positions in recorded target responses, the drafter first produces detached proposals. A frozen target verifies them in parallel, producing the rejected states and the shifted next drafting position that would occur at inference time. A second draft is then trained against the recorded continuation, with gradients flowing only through this final draft. This keeps positions independent and avoids sequential rollout.527:T785,The method, Temporal Self-Distillation (TSD), runs the current model on-policy to produce a denoising trajectory. For a given position, if the token is only committed at a later timestep, the model’s predictive distribution at that final commit timestep is treated as the teacher. Earlier-timestep distributions at the same position are then trained to match that teacher. The target is therefore not the ground-truth one-hot token directly, but the model’s own eventual decision.

This design has several notable properties. First, it is on-policy: the supervision evolves with the model, instead of being frozen in an offline teacher-generated dataset. Second, it is cross-time rather than cross-model distillation: teacher and student are the same model evaluated at different denoising stages. Third, it is tightly aligned with fast decoding. If early distributions already resemble the eventual commit distributions, confidence-based parallel unmasking becomes much safer.

From the full text, TSD is added on top of the standard masked diffusion objective as an auxiliary temporal distillation loss, likely implemented as a KL-style objective with stop-gradient on the teacher side. The loss is defined only on positions that will eventually be committed, which keeps the supervision aligned with actual decoding behavior instead of imposing a blanket consistency constraint everywhere. The paper also emphasizes that TSD applies to both base and post-trained policies, which makes it look more like a general low-NFE alignment objective than a trick tied to a specific pretraining setup.

Compared with offline few-step distillation methods such as dParallel, TSD removes the separate teacher-training and trajectory-generation stage. Compared with decoding-only methods such as Fast-dLLM, it changes the model’s early-time predictive distributions themselves rather than only changing when tokens are committed.528:T567,The evaluation spans seven benchmarks across math, planning, and coding, with the main focus on the speed-quality Pareto frontier rather than peak quality at large NFE. The headline number in the abstract is on MBPP: to reach a 40% pass rate, TSD needs about 2.3× fewer forward passes than the base LLaDA model, and about 1.5× fewer than the offline distillation baseline dParallel.

The experimental comparison appears to cover three baseline families: the original dLLM with adaptive decoding, training-free acceleration methods, and offline few-step distillation methods. The key metric is not a single accuracy number, but either quality at fixed NFE or NFE required to reach a target quality. TSD is expected to help most in the strict-budget regime, where parallel commitment is most aggressive and quality degradation is otherwise severe. That matches the paper’s motivation.

The most informative ablations are likely: whether gains are concentrated at low NFE while preserving high-budget quality; whether using the final commit distribution is better than distilling toward the ground-truth token; whether on-policy supervision outperforms cached offline trajectories; and how robust the method is across different confidence thresholds. Those details determine whether TSD is truly learning temporal anticipation, rather than acting as a generic smoothing regularizer.529:T42f,GVA starts from GQA grouping. Multiple query heads share grouped value heads, but the model no longer writes an independent content-key stream into the cache. For query head h, the content key is reconstructed as K_h = V_g(h) M_h, with a separate reconstruction map per query head. During decoding, the map can be folded into the query, since q·(V M_h) equals (q M_h^T)·V. This avoids materializing content keys in the intended decode path. A direct K=V design was tested and did not recover the GQA training loss, which suggests that the same vector should not be forced to both score and carry retrieved content. RoPE creates the main complication: standard RoPE is position-dependent on cached keys, so it cannot be absorbed into a fixed transformed query. The paper uses a small shared decoupled RoPE channel, keeping an unrotated reconstructed content slice and a short rotated positional slice. It also introduces a scale-aware initialization for M_h to match the initial RMS of reconstructed keys and queries, avoiding nearly uniform attention early in training.52a:T979,核心做法是提出 write-time principle：每个字节的最终物理归属在写入时就决定，之后不再为负载均衡目的移动。围绕这个原则，作者设计了 InplaceKVCache 和其上的调度层 WriteScope。

InplaceKVCache 把 KV 空间沿两个维度做物理划分。第一维是 device affinity，区分未来主要由 CPU 还是 GPU 消费；第二维是 access pattern，区分是适合原地计算还是适合高带宽搬运。最终形成四个 region：CPU 侧的 unpinned compute region 和 pinned load region，GPU 侧的 ping-pong compute region 和 D-window offload region。这样 CPU compute engine 只读自己那块 unpinned region，GPU load engine 只流式读取 pinned region 并通过 ping-pong buffer 计算，不再需要把一份 CPU 侧 cache 临时整理成另一种物理状态。

prefill 阶段生成的 KV 直接按目标 region 写入；decode 阶段则先进入 GPU 上的 D-window，等累计到一个 eviction batch 大小 D 后，再整批路由到 pinned 或 unpinned 的 CPU 区域。这里的关键不是简单分层存储，而是把“未来由谁消费、以什么访问模式消费”编码进写入路径，因此后续调度只是在已有物理分区上决定份额，而不是重新组织数据。

WriteScope 负责真正的 CPU/GPU 分工。它沿 sequence 维度切分 KV 份额，用一个可移植 roofline model 估计两边代价：GPU 侧代价是 PCIe 传输加 GPU attention compute，CPU 侧代价是原地 attention compute。调度目标是让累计分配保持在 roofline 平衡点附近，使两边完成时间接近，从而避免一侧空等另一侧。作者强调这里选择 sequence-dimension split，而不是按 head 或 page 做更细粒度切分，原因是 sequence 维度更自然匹配 attention 的历史 token 访问，也更容易维持两侧各自连续、稳定的物理布局。

和已有系统相比，差异很明确。FlexGen、SolidAttention 这类 GPU-centric 方法把 spilled KV 视为待搬运对象，瓶颈在 PCIe；NEO、ScoutAttention 这类 CPU-centric 方法把 spilled KV 视为 CPU 原地计算对象，瓶颈在 CPU 算力。已有方法即便想混合，也会因为 pinned/unpinned、contiguous/per-head 这两种物理要求冲突而落回辅助 buffer 和重排。作者的创新点不在于提出一个更复杂的 scheduler，而在于先把 cache format 改成能承载混合执行的形式。52b:T7db,实验覆盖 DeepSeek-V2-Lite、Qwen3-30B-A3B、Mixtral-8x7B 三个 MoE 模型，兼顾 MLA 和 GQA 两类 attention 结构，并在 32GB VRAM 预算下测试到 1M token 级别总上下文规模（bs=32 × seq=32K）。这是论文最有说服力的部分，因为它不是只在单一模型上做微调式优化。

论文先用动机实验说明问题确实存在：在 SolidAttention 上，对 Qwen3-30B-A3B、batch size 16、sequence 32K，若在 FFN 阶段预加载下一层 KV，attention latency 会从 33.7 ms 升到 74.2 ms，KV transfer bandwidth 从 25.4 GB/s 掉到 14.9 GB/s，说明 MoE 的 expert loading 与 KV 预取会争抢 CPU/PCIe 资源，传统 overlap 失效。

另一个关键数字是数据重排开销。若试图在运行时把 cache 准备成适配另一执行路径的物理状态，per-layer per-step 的 preparation 时间会随上下文从 2K 增长到 64K 时，从 3.5 ms 膨胀到 185.9 ms。这个结果直接支撑作者的论点：动态负载均衡的难点主要在数据结构，而不是调度公式。

主结果上，在长上下文区间（至少 8K）相对四个复现 baseline，WriteScope 在 A100 上取得 1.5x–2.5x 的几何平均加速，在 V100 上是 1.4x–1.7x。文中还指出 vLLM、SGLang、KTransformers 在该 32GB 预算和大上下文设置下大范围失败，说明这里不是常规 serving 框架默认配置能覆盖的工作点。

从论文叙述看，消融重点应包括：四区域布局是否都必要、write-time placement 相比事后重排节省了多少、roofline-guided split 相比固定比例切分的收益、不同 batch/sequence/model 下平衡点如何漂移。如果精读时看到这些图表，建议重点核对，因为它们决定这套方法是“特定工作点调优”还是“确实抓住了稳定规律”。摘要中还提到 DeepSeek-V4 case study，用来验证对原生 sparse 架构的泛化，这部分如果正文给出端到端吞吐或 TTFT/TPOT 数据，会是判断外推性的关键证据。52c:T9f3,The central idea is the write-time principle: each byte gets its final physical residency when it is written, and it is never moved later for load-balancing purposes. Based on this principle, the paper introduces InplaceKVCache and a scheduling layer called WriteScope.

InplaceKVCache partitions KV storage along two axes. The first is device affinity, meaning whether a region is intended for CPU-side or GPU-side consumption. The second is access pattern, meaning whether the region is optimized for in-place compute or high-bandwidth loading. This yields four regions: on the CPU side, an unpinned compute region and a pinned load region; on the GPU side, a ping-pong compute region and a D-window offload region. CPU attention reads only the unpinned compute region in place. GPU attention streams only the pinned load region through ping-pong buffers. This removes the fallback path of temporary contiguous buffers, copies, and layout conversion.

Prefill KV is routed directly to its target region at write time. Decode KV is first staged in the GPU-side D-window and, once an eviction batch of size D is full, the batch is routed as a whole into either the pinned or unpinned CPU region. The key point is that future consumer and access mode are encoded into the write path itself. The scheduler no longer needs to reorganize data; it only decides how much future KV should go to each physical partition.

WriteScope performs the actual CPU/GPU split along the sequence dimension. It uses a portable roofline-style model to estimate the two costs: GPU-side transfer plus attention compute, and CPU-side in-place attention compute. Eviction batches are assigned so that cumulative placement stays near the balance point where the two engines finish at similar times. The choice of sequence-dimension partitioning is important. It matches the natural history-token access pattern of attention and preserves stable physical layouts on both sides better than finer-grained head- or page-level splitting.

Compared with prior systems, the distinction is clear. GPU-centric systems such as FlexGen and SolidAttention treat spilled KV mainly as data to reload, so PCIe becomes the bottleneck. CPU-centric systems such as NEO and ScoutAttention treat spilled KV mainly as data to compute over in place, so CPU compute becomes the bottleneck. Hybridization is hard because the physical requirements of the two paths conflict. The novelty here is not a more elaborate scheduler, but a cache format that makes hybrid execution physically expressible.52d:T7f6,The evaluation covers three MoE models—DeepSeek-V2-Lite, Qwen3-30B-A3B, and Mixtral-8x7B—spanning both MLA and GQA attention variants, under a 32 GB VRAM budget. The system supports end-to-end inference up to an aggregate 1M-token scale with bs=32 and seq=32K, which is a meaningful operating point rather than a toy setup.

The motivation experiments are important. On SolidAttention with Qwen3-30B-A3B at batch size 16 and sequence length 32K, preloading the next layer’s KV during FFN increases attention latency from 33.7 ms to 74.2 ms and reduces KV transfer bandwidth from 25.4 GB/s to 14.9 GB/s. This directly shows that MoE expert loading and KV prefetch compete for CPU/PCIe resources, so the standard overlap trick breaks down.

Another key result quantifies the cost of runtime reorganization. If KV has to be prepared into a different physical state after the fact, the per-layer per-step preparation overhead grows from 3.5 ms at 2K context to 185.9 ms at 64K context. That number strongly supports the paper’s claim that the real obstacle to dynamic balancing is the data structure, not the scheduling logic.

On the main benchmarks, in the long-context regime of at least 8K tokens, WriteScope achieves geometric-mean speedups of 1.5x to 2.5x on A100 and 1.4x to 1.7x on V100 over four reproduced baselines. The paper also notes that vLLM, SGLang, and KTransformers broadly fail under the same 32 GB budget and large-context settings, which helps position the work as addressing a regime not covered by default serving stacks.

The most important ablations to inspect are likely the necessity of all four regions, the gain from write-time placement over post-hoc repacking, the benefit of roofline-guided splitting over fixed CPU/GPU ratios, and how the balance point shifts with model, batch size, and sequence length. The abstract also mentions a DeepSeek-V4 case study for native sparse architectures; if the full text reports end-to-end throughput or latency there, that is the main evidence for generalization.52e:T424,For a quick pass, focus on three parts.

First, read the introduction carefully to understand why MoE breaks the usual attention/FFN overlap assumption that often works for dense long-context inference. That framing is more valuable than the headline speedup.

Second, study the InplaceKVCache layout figure and the write/eviction pipeline. The key is to understand what each of the four regions is for, why pinned versus unpinned and contiguous versus per-head layouts are in tension, and how write-time placement avoids later reformatting.

Third, inspect the roofline model and the main performance plots. The real question is not average speedup, but whether the split adapts as workload changes and whether that adaptive split tracks the empirical optimum.

If time is limited, 30 to 40 minutes is enough to extract the main idea and evidence. For deeper reading, pay attention to the decode-stage D-window design, how the ping-pong compute region avoids extra GPU-side synchronization, and whether MLA and GQA require materially different tensor layouts.52f:Tbcf,技术内容分成两部分：正确性诊断与性能边界测量。

正确性部分，作者先定位一个表示层问题。LMCache 在处理 packed-page attention block 时，原始逻辑能识别 rank-5 attention tensor，却遗漏了实际部署中使用的 rank-4 packed representation，导致跨副本传输时对字节视图理解错误。作者采用上游已有 packed-subpage patch 修复这一点，并记录在 27B 模型上一个 1568-token logical block 会跨 49 个 32-token pages。这个修复解决的是“传什么字节”的问题。

但修完表示后，服务仍出现跨副本命中却输出错误的情况，于是作者继续追查“何时传这些字节”。他们发现评测镜像缺少 LMCache CUDA-ops extension，因而走了 PyTorch fallback 路径；其中 raw-pointer 的 lmcache_memcpy_async 分支调用的是不带 current CUDA stream 依赖的 cudaMemcpy(..., cudaMemcpyDefault)。在使用 cudaStreamNonBlocking 的 stream pool 下，这不会自动继承前序 gather/scatter 的 producer-consumer 依赖，导致 host 侧或 device 侧可能读到旧数据或过早覆盖数据。

作者用两个受控 byte-level probe 证明这一点。device-to-host 测试中，先在 GPU 上延迟写入字节值 37，再触发 fallback copy，host 读到的仍是旧值 0；host-to-device 测试中，先安排 GPU 读取旧值 0，再通过 fallback 把 host buffer 改成 53，consumer 最终读到 53。每次都是 1 MiB、1,048,576 个字节全部不匹配，说明这不是浮点误差或采样波动，而是严格的顺序错误。

随后作者做了更系统的控制实验：固定 pinned host 和 GPU buffer，只改变 ordering 机制，在 4 KiB、1 MiB、16 MiB 两个方向上测试，有无 10^8 CUDA sleep cycles 的延迟。raw fallback 在所有 120 个 delayed checks 中全部失败，在 120 个 undelayed checks 中全部通过；而三种恢复顺序的方法——等待前序 stream 完成、在 current stream 上用 cudaMemcpyAsync、同 stream tensor copy——在 720 个检查中全部通过。这个设计很扎实，因为它把问题收缩到 ordering mechanism 本身。

作者还把机制诊断和真实部署路径连起来：在 helper-level probe 中，lazy allocator 路径失败，而 mixed allocator 路径在两张 GPU 上都通过。因此部署 workaround 是显式设置 --no-l1-use-lazy，强制走 mixed allocator/tensor-copy path，绕开 raw-pointer fallback。

最后是大内存分配问题。256 GiB LMCache pool 的首次 service allocation 会退回 pageable memory。作者追到 PyTorch host allocator 的 power-of-two rounding 可能把 256 GiB + 4096 B 的请求放大到 512 GiB，进而触发失败。通过设置 PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=pinned_max_round_threshold_mb:128，限制大块 pinned allocation 的 rounding，保留 256 GiB pool 并恢复 full-pool allocation 检查。这部分不是算法贡献，但说明 shared cache 部署里 allocator 细节会直接决定系统是否真的在用 pinned host pool。530:Tc23,The technical content has two parts: correctness diagnosis and performance-boundary measurement.

On correctness, the authors first identify a representation bug. LMCache’s handling of packed-page attention blocks recognized rank-5 attention tensors but missed the rank-4 packed representation used in the evaluated deployment. That caused an incorrect byte view during transfer. They adopt an existing upstream packed-subpage patch to repair this representation issue. In the reported 27B setup, a 1,568-token logical block spans 49 pages of 32 tokens. This fixes the question of which bytes should be transferred.

However, after the representation fix, cross-replica reuse still produced wrong outputs. The authors then isolate a second issue: the evaluated image lacks the LMCache CUDA-ops extension and falls back to a PyTorch path. In that path, the raw-pointer lmcache_memcpy_async branch uses cudaMemcpy with cudaMemcpyDefault but without dependence on the current CUDA stream. Because the stream pool uses cudaStreamNonBlocking, the copy does not inherit the producer-consumer ordering of the preceding gather/scatter work. As a result, host or device consumers can observe stale data or overwritten data.

The paper validates this with controlled byte-level probes. In a device-to-host test, a delayed GPU write of byte value 37 is scheduled before the fallback copy, yet host memory still receives the old value 0. In a host-to-device test, a GPU read of old value 0 is scheduled before the fallback overwrites the host buffer with 53, and the consumer ends up reading 53. In both cases, all 1,048,576 bytes in a 1 MiB object mismatch. That rules out floating-point noise or sampling variance and pins the problem on ordering.

The authors then run a stronger control suite: fixed pinned host and GPU buffers, only the ordering mechanism varies, object sizes of 4 KiB, 1 MiB, and 16 MiB, both transfer directions, with and without 10^8 CUDA sleep cycles. The raw fallback fails all 120 delayed checks and passes all 120 undelayed checks. Three alternatives that restore ordering—waiting for prior stream work, using cudaMemcpyAsync on the current stream, and same-stream tensor copy—pass all 720 checks. This is a clean isolation of the mechanism.

They also connect the diagnosis back to deployment behavior. In helper-level probes, the lazy allocator path fails, while the mixed allocator path passes on both GPUs. The practical workaround is therefore to force the mixed allocator path with --no-l1-use-lazy, bypassing the raw-pointer fallback.

A final systems issue concerns large pinned-memory allocation. The first 256 GiB service allocation falls back to pageable memory. The authors trace this to PyTorch host allocator power-of-two rounding, which may inflate a 256 GiB + 4096 B request to 512 GiB. Setting PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=pinned_max_round_threshold_mb:128 constrains large-allocation rounding and restores full-pool pinned allocation checks. This is not algorithmic novelty, but it matters because shared-cache deployment depends on whether the host pool is truly pinned.531:T712,The experiments split into correctness and performance.

On correctness, the byte-level controls are the strongest evidence. Both 1 MiB probes show 1,048,576 mismatching bytes, directly demonstrating missing stream dependency in the fallback copy path. In the supplementary controls, the raw fallback fails 120 out of 120 delayed checks and passes 120 out of 120 undelayed checks. The three ordering-restoring alternatives pass 720 out of 720 checks. This makes the issue clearly one of synchronization semantics rather than random corruption. Helper-level probes further show that the lazy allocator path fails, while the mixed allocator path passes ten checks on GPU 0 and ten on GPU 1.

At the service level, the paper gives a useful concrete example. The same input produces alpha=938639 when computed cold or reused locally on replica A. Replica B externally hits 127,008 tokens but returns 938624 instead. Forcing zero-hit cold computation on B by changing the cache salt restores the correct answer. That isolates the fault to shared-state transfer and reuse rather than model instability.

On performance, the authors run a four-block OFF-ON-ON-OFF comparison with 768 measured requests across two block pairs. The headline number in the abstract is that median cross-replica time to first content token drops from 31.715 s to 0.605 s. So shared host-memory caching can indeed remove most of the repeated prefill cost when a request migrates between replicas. But the paper is careful to retain local-hit baselines, because preserving request locality on the original GPU may still beat cross-replica reuse. The useful takeaway is therefore conditional: shared caching can be very effective, but only after correctness is established and only when compared fairly against locality-preserving placement.532:T45b,Read it as a failure analysis rather than as a feature paper.

Start with the correctness section. Focus on the two layers of failure: what the packed-page representation bug breaks, and why the raw-pointer fallback violates stream ordering under nonblocking streams. The byte-level probes are the most informative part because they turn a vague service anomaly into a reproducible mechanism.

Then read the allocator section to understand why a 256 GiB pinned pool can silently fail because of rounding behavior, and why the mixed allocator path is both a correctness fix and a practical deployment path.

Finish with the performance comparison, paying attention to how the paper separates cold compute, local reuse, and cross-replica reuse. The main value is not the single speedup number, but the boundary it draws: when shared caching beats recomputation, and when preserving locality is still the better option.
