Configurations are ranked by a square-root mean (Overall) to encourage balance.536:T702,GroundBench introduces a six-condition benchmark with a branch-and-merge structure instead of a single monotonic prompt-strength chain. The conditions are: image_only, object_named, part_named, localization_only, localization_shown, and mechanics_shown. The critical design choice is that from object_named, the benchmark branches into part_named and localization_only. This lets the evaluator measure the effect of target identity and target region separately. The two branches merge again at localization_shown, and mechanics_shown adds a bundled mechanics descriptor containing joint type and motion axis.

This factorization matters because localization_only is not just a weaker version of localization_shown. It is the control that asks whether knowing where the relevant region is, without knowing what that part is called, helps at all. Conversely, part_named asks whether the semantic identity of the part is already enough to drive the answer even without explicit localization.

The paper also adds a counterfactual re-ask setup: the model is given a real but noncanonical part name from the same image and object, and the evaluator checks whether the output follows the changed part request or defaults to the canonical action. The authors are careful not to overclaim here. They frame it as a prompt-compliance test, not proof of visual attention.

A less flashy but important contribution is the evaluator design. The benchmark explicitly guards against two measurement errors found in the companion evaluation: fixed thresholds that let trivial constant baselines score surprisingly high, and incorrect action-label rules. GroundBench derives thresholds and baselines from the scored data rather than fixing them in advance, which makes the reported differences more trustworthy.537:T55f,The experimental scale is modest but targeted: 1,068 predictions across three OpenAI models. The main findings are clear.

First, localization_only, which provides the target region while withholding the part identity, gives essentially no gain over a constant baseline. This suggests that merely telling the model where to look is not enough if the model does not know what semantic part category that region corresponds to.

Second, the gains appear mainly in conditions that provide target-part identity, such as part_named and localization_shown. The authors’ interpretation is that the improvement comes from supplying a category variable that already determines the answer within the curated object set, rather than from stronger grounding or mechanical reasoning.

Third, adding the mechanics descriptor yields limited additional benefit, implying that joint type and motion axis are not the dominant bottleneck in this benchmark. The larger bottleneck remains part identity and its association with action labels.

The paper repeatedly contrasts these findings with the companion evaluation, where naming the target part improved action accuracy by 0.32 to 0.63 across eight VLMs and nearly recovered push-action performance. Crucially, answers and targets remain textual in both conditions, so the comparison isolates the effect of presenting evidence visually.

The benchmark uses a shared vocabulary of 12 named shapes and defines 38 procedurally generated tasks grouped into four families: Selection, Relation, Aggregation, and Transformation. A subset is organized into position-controlled groups to probe position/window effects while holding other factors fixed.

Beyond measuring the modality gap across models and shot counts, the paper runs (i) recovery interventions targeting visual access, task framing, and reasoning support, and (ii) decomposition variants that separate induction (inferring the rule from demonstrations) from execution (carrying out a stated rule with multimodal inputs). The key methodological point is that the gap persists even when the task is stated directly, implying a more basic cross-modal execution difficulty; demonstrations then act as both evidence and additional context load, especially in multi-image settings.539:T410,Evaluations span 6 open-weight models, 38 tasks, and multiple shot settings. The provided excerpt does not include full numeric tables; the exact per-task gaps and variance sources need to be read from the main figures/tables and appendices.53a:T8db,方法由三部分组成。第一部分是 stage-wise dynamic evaluation。作者把执行流拆成两套时钟：raw event clock 监控每个原子事件，用于即时拦截明显危险操作；closed action clock 只在一次动作语义闭合后推进，比如 tool call 返回且 agent 让出控制时才结算。这样做的原因很直接：很多工具调用在返回前语义并不完整，过早评分会把未完成动作当错误。真正的评测和里程碑结算都放在 closed action 边界上，从而保留局部上下文并减少噪声。

第二部分是 path-tolerant milestone graph。作者不使用隐藏参考轨迹，而是只基于 public task view 生成任务蓝图，避免测试泄漏。具体做法是让 LLM 以不同启发式和采样温度生成多个候选计划图，对每个候选图做确定性的 contract verification，去掉幻觉 API、类型不匹配和环依赖；然后对 milestone 和 precedence edge 做 strict-majority consensus，只保留多数候选都认可的必要节点和依赖，再做 transitive reduction 得到一个更小的 DAG。这个设计的关键不是追求唯一正确路径，而是提炼“任务不变量”：哪些中间状态必须出现、哪些先后关系不能破坏。这样评测时允许不同搜索路径和不同工具使用顺序，只要满足 DAG 约束即可。

第三部分是 execution-time review and early termination。DynSTEER在每个 stage 上做多维度审查，并根据 stage-level 结果动态决定是否进入更高成本的复核流程。文中强调 first-error localization 和 unrecoverable prefix detection：一旦当前前缀已经破坏关键约束、后续无法补救，就提前终止 rollout，减少无效工具调用和长链推理开销。这里的“counterfactual”含义是，系统不是只问当前动作是否差，而是问从当前前缀出发是否还存在可行完成路径。

从方法取舍看，这篇工作明显偏工程化和评测系统设计。它没有引入新的学习目标，而是把任务结构抽取、局部证据窗口、分层复核和在线止损拼成一个闭环。与整轨迹 verifier 相比，它更强调可诊断性；与 step-level reward model 相比，它更强调语义闭合和上下文完整性。53b:T89a,The framework has three main components. The first is stage-wise dynamic evaluation. DynSTEER introduces a dual-clock model. A raw event clock advances on every atomic event and is used for immediate interception of obviously dangerous operations. A closed action clock advances only when an action reaches semantic closure, for example when a tool call has returned and control is yielded back to the agent. Milestone settlement and scoring happen only at these closed-action boundaries. This design choice is important: before a tool result arrives, the action is semantically incomplete, so scoring earlier would inject noise and misattribute errors.

The second component is a path-tolerant milestone graph. Instead of relying on hidden reference trajectories, the system operates strictly on the public task view to avoid leakage. It prompts an LLM to synthesize multiple candidate plans under diverse heuristics and sampling settings, then filters them with deterministic contract checks to remove hallucinated APIs, type mismatches, and cyclic dependencies. Milestones and precedence edges are retained only if they appear in a strict majority of valid candidates, followed by transitive reduction to produce a compact DAG. The key idea is to capture task invariants rather than a single canonical path: what intermediate conditions are necessary, and which ordering constraints are essential, while leaving room for legitimate variation in execution strategy.

The third component is execution-time review and early termination. At each stage, DynSTEER performs multi-tier review and routes harder cases to more expensive checks only when needed. It emphasizes first-error localization and unrecoverable-prefix detection. The system asks not only whether the current action is bad, but whether any valid completion remains possible from the current prefix. If not, it terminates the rollout early to save tool calls and reasoning tokens.

Methodologically, this is a systems-style contribution rather than a new learning objective. The novelty lies in combining task-structure induction, context-preserving local evidence windows, adaptive review, and runtime stopping into one evaluation loop.53c:T4ed,The headline results are in three buckets. First, DynSTEER improves evaluation discriminability by 85.2% over native evaluation and separates all model pairs with statistical significance. That suggests stage-level structured evaluation exposes model differences more clearly than end-only scoring. Second, it improves diagnostic precision and supports first-error localization while preserving the validity of diverse correct paths, which is the main claim behind the milestone-DAG design. Third, for failed rollouts, execution-time early termination saves 45.41% of execution steps on average, a practically meaningful reduction for long-horizon agents where failed trajectories can become increasingly expensive.

The experiments appear to focus on comparing evaluation paradigms rather than training a new agent. When reading the results, the main caveats are task dependence and blueprint quality. If the public task view is incomplete, majority-consensus planning may miss rare but valid paths. If tasks are highly open-ended, the DAG may still overconstrain evaluation. The point is not merely adding special symbols, but making motion a native generative target rather than a side channel. This differs from many prior designs where motion is injected through adapters or auxiliary encoders and therefore has limited influence on the backbone representation.

The second is motion-grounded chain-of-thought. The motivation is straightforward: text-only CoT can hallucinate details that are linguistically plausible but absent from the motion itself. If ablations are available, prioritize the ones that remove action tokens, future visual tokens, or human-interaction pretraining.543:T9a8,方法叫 Joint-Output On-Policy Distillation，简称 JO-OPD。核心思路是：既然同一个模型在 S2T 模式下文本回答更准，就把这个更强的文本策略当 teacher，去监督学生在 S2TS 联合生成轨迹上的文本预测；同时再加一个 preservation objective，尽量别把原有的非文本生成能力破坏掉。

具体机制分三步。

第一步，学生模型以 S2TS 模式生成 joint trajectory，里面包含文本 token、声学 token 和控制 token。训练不是在 teacher 的理想轨迹上做，而是在 student 自己生成的轨迹上做，这就是 on-policy 的关键。原因很直接：推理时模型看到的是自己生成出来、带有声学历史的上下文，如果只在 teacher forcing 轨迹上蒸馏，会出现训练-推理分布不一致。

第二步，在每个文本位置 i，构造 teacher 和 student 的不同上下文。student 看到完整的 joint history，也就是文本和声学 token 都在；teacher 则对同一段 student 前缀做 text-only projection，只保留其中的文本 token，去掉 acoustic outputs 和 control tokens。这样 teacher 给出的分布代表“如果没有被声学历史干扰，这个位置更合理的文本偏好是什么”。蒸馏时只在 text vocabulary 上比较分布，而不是让 student 去匹配 text 与 non-text 的总概率分配。这个设计很重要，因为作者要修的是文本决策，不是强行改变什么时候该说话、什么时候该出声学 token。

第三步，加入 non-text preservation。由于蒸馏目标会推动模型把概率质量更多放到正确文本上，如果不加约束，可能伤到原本的语音生成行为。为此作者用 base model 在 S2TS 模式下的非文本预测分布作为参考，对 student 的 native non-text predictions 做正则，尽量保持声学和控制 token 的生成习惯。论文还区分了 JO-OPD-Soft 和 JO-OPD-Hard：前者保留 teacher top-k 文本 token 的软分布并重归一化，后者用 one-hot 目标。按经验判断，Soft 版本更能传递相对偏好信息，尤其在开放词表回答中更稳。

这个方法和常见知识蒸馏的区别在于两点：一是 teacher 与 student 共享同一个底座，只是运行在不同输出模式；二是监督发生在 student 自己采样出的 joint trajectory 上，而不是离线标注序列上。它更像一种模式间 policy transfer，而不是传统的 teacher-student 压缩。544:T863,The method is Joint-Output On-Policy Distillation (JO-OPD). The idea is simple: if the same model is better at text answering in S2T mode, use that policy as a teacher for text decisions made during S2TS generation, while regularizing the model so that its non-text generation behavior is preserved.

The training loop works as follows.

First, the student model generates a joint S2TS trajectory containing text tokens, acoustic tokens, and control tokens. Distillation is performed on student-generated trajectories rather than teacher-forced ones. That on-policy choice matters because, at inference time, the model conditions on its own interleaved history, including acoustic outputs.

Second, at each text position, the teacher and student are given different views of the same prefix. The student conditions on the full interleaved history. The teacher conditions on a text-only projection of that same student prefix, where acoustic and control tokens are removed. This isolates what the model would prefer textually if it were not being perturbed by acoustic history. Distillation is applied only over the text vocabulary, not over the full text-vs-non-text probability mass. That design keeps the objective focused on improving text token choice rather than changing the timing or frequency of non-text emissions.

Third, JO-OPD adds a preservation objective for non-text predictions. Without it, improving text predictions could distort the model’s native speech-generation behavior. The base model’s S2TS non-text distribution is used as a reference, and the student is regularized to stay close on acoustic/control-token predictions. The paper also distinguishes JO-OPD-Soft and JO-OPD-Hard: the soft variant keeps the teacher’s top-k text-token distribution and renormalizes it, while the hard variant uses a one-hot target.

What makes this different from standard distillation is that teacher and student are the same base model run in different output modes, and supervision is aligned to the student’s own joint trajectory. It is better viewed as policy transfer across generation modes than as classic model compression.545:T617,The first important result is the size of OMG itself. On paired evaluations of Step-Audio-2-mini and Baichuan-Audio-Instruct, the gap is large under identical speech inputs. On Spoken-MQA and speech-rendered GSM8K, OMG reaches 42.87 and 29.72 percentage points for Step-Audio-2-mini, and 12.41 and 10.39 points for Baichuan-Audio-Instruct. The paper also shows that explicit reasoning instructions on human-recorded VoiceBench-BBH further widen the gap for Step-Audio-2-mini, suggesting that the issue is not limited to arithmetic-style tasks.

The main empirical claim is that JO-OPD reduces OMG in both models. The paper carefully separates two evaluation targets: S2TS(T), the internal text in the joint trajectory, and S2TS(S), the spoken response after speech reconstruction and transcription. This distinction is important. JO-OPD directly optimizes the former, and then the authors examine how much of that gain survives the speech-generation and transcription pipeline. That makes the analysis cleaner than evaluating only final spoken answers.

Another useful part of the experiments is the preservation analysis. The authors check whether improving text accuracy comes at the cost of damaging non-text generation behavior. That matters for unified multimodal LMs: a method that simply pushes the model back toward text-only behavior would miss the point. In the experiments, GRPO uses n=8 rollouts per prompt, while filtering uses N=64. If a problem has no success in 64 attempts, it will almost always produce an all-failure group during training. With binary rewards, the group-relative advantage in GRPO vanishes when all rewards are identical. The proposed fix is to use a stronger teacher to provide partial reasoning traces. A guidance level ρ controls how much of the teacher trace is revealed. At high ρ, the student solves an easier continuation problem; as ρ decreases, the student must perform more of the reasoning itself. Backward chaining then withdraws guidance until the model attempts the original unguided problem. The paper further argues that generic backward-chaining curricula are suboptimal here because training at ρ>0 is off-distribution relative to test-time ρ=0. Monotone Frontier Curriculum addresses this by maintaining a per-sample monotone guidance frontier and pushing samples toward lower guidance whenever the student can handle the current level.549:T7ca,方法主线很清楚：以 Nemotron-3-Super-120B 为底座，直接做 GRPO 强化学习，不先走一个新的 SFT checkpoint。关键创新不在 RL 算法本身，而在 specification-driven task construction。

That makes the signal much closer to the real agent objective than token-level imitation.

First, neologism midtraining. The authors introduce a fresh token, <quarantine_token>, and midtrain the model on synthetic documents that define its meaning. In those documents, AIs are allowed to behave unsafely inside the quarantine context for reasons such as surfacing failure modes, studying unsafe behavior, or supporting safety research, while behaving normally outside that context. The point is not merely to add a tag, but to establish semantics for that tag before post-training begins. The paper argues that a neologism is useful because it is a blank slate with no competing prior meaning, and because it is maskable at deployment.

Second, mixed post-training. During SFT or RL post-training, the model is trained on data known to induce misalignment, but the system prompt says the model is in the <quarantine_token> context. Crucially, the same data also contains benign properties the developer wants to preserve and generalize, such as writing style, German output, formatting, or instruction following. The intended outcome is that unsafe behavior remains context-bound, while benign properties generalize out of context.

Third, out-of-context evaluation. At evaluation time, the quarantine token is removed from the prompt. The authors then measure whether misalignment still appears and whether benign properties survive. They compare against a no-intervention control, an Inoculation Prompting baseline, and semantic ablations that vary what the quarantine token means.

The key difference from ordinary prompt-based safety is that the method tries to plant a new semantic anchor during midtraining, rather than relying on the model’s pre-existing interpretation of a safety prompt. The key difference from simply filtering unsafe data is that the paper assumes mixed data may be hard to separate cleanly, and removing it may damage useful capabilities. A good question to keep in mind is whether the intervention changes the model’s internal representation structure, or merely creates a more elaborate training-time prompt condition.550:T896,方法核心是 SAILS：Set-level Audit-Informed Iterative Learned Selection。它不是给每条样本打分后贪心选 top-k，而是直接学习一个“集合打分器”，把 poison set 当作一等对象。全文先从理论和经验两方面说明 pointwise influence proxy 的局限：如果真实攻击成功率不是逐样本加和，而是存在显著交互，那么优化单点 proxy 可能选出一组彼此冗余的样本，甚至在 proxy 更高时真实 success 更低。作者还指出，某些激进的 pointwise 优化会把搜索推向 proxy 的偏差区域，导致 true objective 下降。

SAILS 的流程是 propose–score–audit：
1. 先用少量 oracle query 构造训练集。这里的 oracle 是完整的 finetune-and-evaluate，一次代价很高，但能给出 poison set 的真实 attack success。
2. 训练一个 set scorer，输入是一个 poison set，输出其预估强度。论文的关键点在于 scorer 学的是集合层面的表征，而不是样本独立分数求和，因此可以捕捉冗余、覆盖、互补等交互。
3. 用该 scorer 在极大的组合空间里提出并排序海量候选集合，规模可到 millions of candidate sets。
4. 只对 top-ranked shortlist 做 oracle audit，拿到真实标签后继续回流训练 scorer，迭代进行。

这个设计的取舍很清楚：直接用 RL against oracle 虽然也能做组合优化，但查询成本太高；纯 pointwise 方法便宜，但目标错配。SAILS 介于两者之间，用学习到的 surrogate 排序大规模候选，再用少量真实训练校准。论文还强调一个实用性质：只要 scorer 能把至少一个强集合排进可审计 shortlist，最终就能返回接近最优的 poison set。这使它更像高召回的候选发现器，而不是必须全局精确排序的回归器。

从全文描述看，方法还做了一个重要工程判断：scorer 可以在小规模 finetune-and-evaluate 上训练，再迁移到 full-scale finetuning。这说明它试图学习的是相对稳定的集合结构信号，而不是某个特定训练预算下的偶然噪声。这一点对数据筛选研究尤其关键，因为真正昂贵的是全规模训练。551:T6c3,The method is SAILS: Set-level Audit-Informed Iterative Learned Selection. The paper first formalizes poison selection as oracle-budgeted set optimization. An oracle query means a full finetune-and-evaluate run for one candidate poison set, which is expensive but gives the true attack success. The authors then analyze why pointwise influence proxies can fail: they assume the quality of a set decomposes into independent example-level effects. That assumption breaks once examples interact through finetuning. Individually strong examples may be redundant; individually weak ones may become strong in combination.

SAILS addresses this with a propose–score–audit loop:
1. Collect a small number of oracle-labeled poison sets.
2. Train a learned set scorer that predicts the strength of an entire poison set rather than summing independent item scores.
3. Use the scorer to rank millions of candidate sets.
4. Audit only a small top-ranked shortlist with expensive oracle queries.
5. Retrain the scorer on the audited results and iterate.

The design choice is practical. Direct RL against the oracle can optimize over sets but is query-hungry. Pointwise methods are cheap but structurally miss interactions. SAILS uses a learned surrogate to search the combinatorial space and spends oracle budget only where ranking quality matters. A useful property emphasized in the paper is that the scorer only needs to place at least one strong set high enough to be audited; it does not need globally perfect calibration. Another important result is transfer: a scorer trained on small-scale finetune-and-evaluate runs can generalize to full-scale finetuning, suggesting that some set-level signals are stable across training budgets.552:T558,There are three headline findings.

First, the variance induced by poison-set choice is large. In three LLaMA-3-8B backdoor settings, attack success spans 3% to 80% while everything else is held fixed. That alone is enough to challenge the standard random-sampling evaluation protocol.

Second, SAILS materially outperforms influence-based baselines. On the three LLaMA-3-8B settings, it improves held-out attack success by about 30 percentage points on average over the strongest influence baseline. This is not a marginal gain; it indicates that set-level interactions dominate the optimization problem.

Third, the pipeline extends beyond one narrow setup. The paper reports transfer to code-generation backdoors, agentic backdoors on Qwen3-4B, and API-only finetuning of Kimi-K2.5. On SmolLM-360M, SAILS nearly matches an oracle-guided RL baseline while using much less cost. That comparison is especially informative for researchers interested in expensive training-defined objectives: learned surrogate ranking plus selective auditing can be more efficient than direct RL over the oracle.

The most useful ablation-level insight is conceptual rather than cosmetic. That is the part most likely to transfer to broader data-selection problems beyond security.554:T71d,The method has two central pieces. The first is a local geometric view around the reference model. The reference model is treated as a common origin in behavioral space, and the allowed drift budget defines a local boundary. Within that neighborhood, drift magnitude determines distance from the origin, while direction determines how the limited behavioral change is allocated across capabilities. This gives a common coordinate system in which heterogeneous updates can be compared by directional efficiency: task improvement per unit of behavioral drift.

The second piece is a coarse but systematic layer-selective probe. Rather than introducing a complicated regularizer, the authors vary which layers are trainable while keeping the data, objective, and optimizer fixed as much as possible. This isolates accessible update directions as the main experimental variable. The result is that several layer subsets provide nearby directions that improve the QA-only target task while preserving reasoning and general capabilities. Full fine-tuning often fails because its large update space includes many easy loss-reducing directions that overwrite existing behaviors. LoRA also restricts directions, but its low-rank subspace does not consistently contain the efficient ones, so it helps in some settings and not in others.

Mechanistically, the paper argues that QA-only supervision specifies the answer but not the reasoning behavior. Optimization therefore tends to exploit whichever behavioral rewrite most easily reduces training loss. If the update space allows the model to bypass or compress its original reasoning style, standard SFT will often take that route. Layer selection changes the reachable subspace, nudging optimization toward adaptations that reuse rather than replace existing reasoning circuits.555:T68e,The experiments use Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-14B, with scientific reasoning and multilingual translation as the main tasks. The key empirical pattern is consistent: direct QA-only full fine-tuning increases target-task performance while steadily degrading downstream reasoning as functional drift grows. LoRA sometimes softens this trade-off, but not reliably. The layer-selective probe identifies multiple trainable-layer configurations that, at similar drift levels, improve the target task and preserve both reasoning and broader capabilities.

The translation results are the strongest practical validation. The deeper questions worth thinking about are whether the behavioral drift metric is robust to stylistic changes, and whether the good layer-selective directions truly preserve existing circuits or merely act as an implicit regularizer through reduced plasticity.557:Tb9b,方法从 on-policy distillation 出发，但关键不是普通 teacher-student KL，而是“能力组合”的表示方式。作者对每个 specialist 构造一个 anchor pair：一个是 post-training 前的基线模型，一个是经过某种专项训练后的 specialist。对于同一个 token state，specialist 相对 anchor-before 的 log probability ratio 被视为该专项训练带来的 policy shift。这样定义有两个好处。第一，它抽取的是增量能力，而不是把 teacher 的全部分布都搬过来，因此更容易和其他 specialist 的增量叠加。第二，它不要求不同教师参数同构，只要求能在 student 生成的状态上打分。

在多能力组合时，Lightning Weave先把不同 anchor pair 的 log-ratio shift 对齐到 student 的 token states 上，再做加权求和，得到一个联合 shift。这里的设计选择很重要：作者不是分别构造多个 target 再做混合，而是先组合 shift，再构造单一目标分布。这样所有能力源在每个 token 决策点上共同作用，避免后续 target averaging 带来的不一致。

真正的方法核心是 Tilted-Target DOPD。作者指出，若直接把 DOPD 的 sampled-token surrogate 用在缓存轨迹上，会出现 stationary target 不保真的问题。原因是缓存来自旧的 behavior policy，当 student 更新后，基于缓存 action 估计的 regularizer 不再等价于当前 student 相对目标策略的 KL；即使 student 已经到达理想 shifted policy，loss 仍可能非零，梯度也不会消失，训练会继续把模型推离目标。为了解决这个问题，作者让每个缓存 shift 显式“倾斜”冻结的 behavior policy，构造出一个明确的 tilted target distribution，然后最小化当前 student 到该 target 的 KL。这样做后，至少在缓存状态上，目标是静态且可达的：当 student 匹配 target 时，loss 和梯度都应消失。文中还强调，这个构造保留了 token-level DOPD surrogate 在初始阶段的期望更新方向，因此既继承了原方法的有效起步信号，又修复了离线训练后期的目标漂移。

工程上，这个框架把昂贵的多教师在线打分转成一次性缓存。若有 K 个 anchor pair，在线 OPD 需要每条 student rollout 经过最多 2K 个 anchor 模型评分；Lightning Weave则先对缓存轨迹离线打分，之后训练只依赖 student 和缓存分数。这样多能力组合的成本主要前置到数据准备阶段，训练期更接近普通离线蒸馏。

与已有多教师蒸馏相比，这篇工作的区别不只是“多加几个 teacher”，而是把 teacher 的贡献限制为可解释的 policy shift，并为离线组合提供了一个有明确定点的目标分布。与参数空间 merge 相比，它不要求模型结构或参数对齐；与直接监督最终 specialist 相比，它更容易调节不同能力的权重，形成一条可控的 trade-off 曲线。558:T9ae,The method starts from on-policy distillation, but the key idea is how capabilities are encoded. For each specialist, the authors form an anchor pair: a checkpoint before the relevant post-training stage and the resulting specialist after that stage. At a shared token state, the log-probability ratio between the specialist and the pre-stage anchor is treated as the policy shift learned during post-training. This is a useful abstraction because it isolates the incremental behavior change rather than copying the specialist distribution wholesale, and it does not require parameter alignment across teachers.

For multi-capability composition, Lightning Weave aligns these log-ratio shifts on student-generated token states and takes a weighted sum to form a joint shift. Importantly, it composes shifts first and constructs a single target distribution afterward, rather than building separate targets and averaging them later. That means all capability sources jointly shape each student decision at the token level.

The main technical contribution is Tilted-Target DOPD. The paper argues that directly reusing DOPD’s sampled-token surrogate on cached trajectories does not preserve the intended stationary solution. The cache was generated under an older behavior policy, and once the student moves away from that policy, the sampled-action regularizer no longer matches the KL that should be imposed relative to the current student. As a result, even if the student reaches the desired shifted policy, the cached surrogate can still produce non-zero gradients and push the model away from the solution. To fix this, each cached shift is used to explicitly tilt the frozen behavior policy into a target distribution, and training minimizes KL from the current student to that explicit target. This gives the offline objective a proper fixed point: when the student matches the target on cached states, both loss and gradient vanish. The paper also argues that this construction preserves the expected initial update direction of token-level DOPD, so it keeps the useful early-stage signal while repairing the late-stage mismatch.

From a systems perspective, the framework converts expensive online multi-teacher scoring into a one-time offline caching step. With K anchor pairs, naive online OPD may require up to 2K anchor-model evaluations per student rollout. Lightning Weave scores cached trajectories once and then trains using only the student and cached scores.559:T590,The experiments cover both math and code reasoning, with student models including at least Qwen3-4B and Qwen3.5-4B, evaluated on five benchmarks. The main setting composes an accuracy-oriented shift from Klear with an efficiency-oriented shift from DECS. The reported results show consistent improvements in the accuracy–efficiency trade-off over both the base model and single-anchor alternatives.

The clearest numbers are as follows. On Qwen3-4B, Lightning Weave improves AIME 2024 accuracy from 72.9% to 76.0% while reducing response tokens by 21.3%. On Qwen3.5-4B, it improves HMMT 2025 accuracy from 59.2% to 64.0% with 10.7% fewer tokens, and LiveCodeBench v5 accuracy from 41.7% to 54.2% with 9.6% fewer tokens. These are meaningful because the gains are not coming from simply allowing longer traces, nor from sacrificing too much accuracy for brevity.

The weight-sweep results are also important. By varying the relative strengths of the anchor signals, the method produces a family of students that trace out an empirical Pareto frontier. That supports the claim that capabilities are genuinely composable and tunable, rather than the method working only at one lucky operating point. The most important ablations to inspect are the comparison between direct cached DOPD and Tilted-Target DOPD, the effect of composing shifts before target construction, and the trade-off curves under different anchor weights.55a:T60f,VG-OPD has two layers of selection: criterion-level expert eligibility and token-level supervision placement.

For the who question, each prompt comes with a rubric made of criteria, verifiers, and weights. Instead of collapsing the rubric into a single scalar reward and discarding structure, the method scores both the student rollout and each candidate expert answer with the same criterion-specific verifier. An expert is allowed to teach a criterion only if it shows a verified advantage over the student on that criterion for the current sample. This is a local, sample-specific notion of expertise, not a fixed domain prior.

For the which question, even an eligible expert does not supervise the whole sequence. The method identifies positions where the expert disagrees with the student and applies distillation only on those tokens through a sparse mask. The intuition is simple: if the student already matches the expert, there is little value in forcing additional imitation; the useful signal lies where the expert would actually change the student’s local decision.

Training remains inside an on-policy RL loop. The base policy update uses a rubric-based GRPO-style objective on the student’s own rollouts. The distillation term is a token-level reverse-KL estimate, but its weight is no longer uniform. It is gated by verifier-based eligibility and by the disagreement mask. In that sense, prompt-level multi-expert OPD methods such as MOPD appear as a special case with fixed teacher assignment and dense, uniform token weighting.55b:T563,The setup uses four RL-trained specialist experts and evaluates 4B and 8B students on seven benchmarks spanning scientific reasoning, domain science, and general reasoning. The headline numbers reported in the paper are that, at 4B, VG-OPD improves average accuracy over rubric-GRPO by 2.0 points on scientific reasoning and 3.3 points on domain science, while consistently outperforming coarse-grained MOPD. The 8B student shows the same pattern and achieves the best overall performance across the evaluation suite.

The ablations are the most informative part. The paper claims that both components matter: verifier-based expert eligibility and selective token supervision. That is an important result because the two mechanisms solve different failure modes. Eligibility answers whether a teacher should be trusted at all on a given criterion. Token masking answers where that trusted signal should be applied. Removing either one should reintroduce noisy supervision.

When reading the experiments, it is worth checking a few details: sensitivity to the number and quality of criteria, sparsity of the supervision mask, and whether multiple experts are actually used within a single problem. If expert switching happens frequently inside one answer, that would support the paper’s central claim that capability integration needs finer routing than prompt-level assignment.55c:T8fa,The method has two stages: attack discovery and attack generalization.

In the discovery stage, the authors use an investigator-agent elicitation framework in the standard hint-based monitorability setting. In that setup, a hint pointing toward an incorrect answer is appended to a multiple-choice problem, and the monitor checks whether the actor relied on the hint without acknowledging it. The interesting finding is that the investigator does not merely learn to suggest the wrong answer. It learns to inject a faulty but benign-sounding chain of reasoning. Even without an explicit instruction to follow it, the actor often paraphrases the injected plan inside its own CoT and reaches the wrong conclusion.

In the generalization stage, this observation is turned into a broader attack class called plan injection. The paper evaluates it in two harder settings: APPS coding backdoors and bio/math disguised-answer injection. In the coding case, the attack steers the model toward flawed or backdoored implementations. In the bio/math case, the attack uses superficially reasonable analysis to push the model toward an incorrect answer. A notable detail is that the injected content can be framed as an optional plan suggestion rather than a hard instruction, yet the actor still adopts it at high rates.

For monitoring, the paper compares thinking and non-thinking monitors. Thinking monitors are allowed to reason before judging; non-thinking monitors are closer to direct classification. Thinking monitors are stronger on average, but not robustly so. In some cases, extra reasoning budget causes the monitor to spend more tokens rationalizing the actor’s faulty reasoning instead of flagging it. The paper also tests whether giving the monitor access to the injected plan helps. On Bio-Math, it can actually reduce detection by as much as 50%, suggesting that more context can contaminate the monitor rather than assist it.

Relative to prior work, the novelty is that the actor is not explicitly instructed to hide malicious intent, nor is it fine-tuned to evade oversight. The attack exploits the model’s tendency to trust and internalize reasoning found in context. That makes the resulting trace look clean, because the suspicious planning has effectively been outsourced upstream.55d:T55e,Several empirical results stand out.

First, the attack transfers across scale. It is initially discovered on a 7B model, then shown to transfer to an 8B model and to DeepSeek-R1-0528 at 671B parameters. Larger scale does not remove the vulnerability.

Second, steering success is high. Plan injection drives the target behavior on over 80% of APPS attempts and over 90% of bio/math attempts. That indicates a strong tendency to adopt ready-made plans from context.

Third, monitor evasion remains substantial. Across monitorability benchmarks, the paper reports 25-33% evasion rates. Non-thinking monitors can miss up to 76% of attacks, and even the strongest monitor misses at least 25%.

Fourth, more monitor compute is not always better. The paper presents cases where additional thinking budget is spent explaining away the corrupted reasoning rather than detecting it. Another concrete result is that, on Bio-Math, giving the monitor access to the injected plan can reduce detection by up to 50%. That is important because many system designs assume that exposing more context to the monitor should help.

The experimental structure is solid for the paper’s main claim: it covers discovery, transfer, scale, and monitor variants. The main limitation is that it diagnoses the weakness more convincingly than it offers a comparably strong defense or training-time fix.55e:T4b4,Start with the introduction and contribution summary to lock in the attack definition. This is not just ordinary prompt injection. The central mechanism is that a corrupted plan is phrased as benign reasoning and then absorbed into the actor’s own CoT without attribution.

Next, read the attack-discovery section carefully. The most important detail is that the actor often follows the injected plan even when there is no explicit “do this” instruction. That points to a deeper issue than instruction following: default trust in contextual reasoning.

Then move to the APPS and Bio/Math experiments. The coding setting shows how a flawed design can be embedded into implementation behavior; the reasoning setting shows the same mechanism outside code. Pay attention to the successful transcripts and the wording patterns that make adoption easy.

Finally, read the monitor comparison section, especially the analyses on thinking budget and whether the monitor sees the injected plan. Those are the parts most likely to update your intuition about CoT monitoring.

The same idea extends to multi-teacher distillation because prompts generated by a domain teacher automatically inherit a domain label.560:T566,SPARK has two stages. Stage 1 trains a disposable Diagnostic Stress Adapter on a harmful calibration set to push the frozen VLM toward unsafe completions. For the same inputs, the method records key and value activations from both the frozen model and the DSA-perturbed model. Their token-level residuals are stacked per layer and head, and independent SVDs on K and V residuals produce low-rank harm-calibrated displacement subspaces. The method decomposes activation residuals rather than adapter weights because the realized KV shift depends on token states, modality, and context. After subspace extraction, the DSA is discarded. Stage 2 projects the KV cache away from these subspaces and learns lightweight residual repairs to recover useful information lost by projection. The repair is constrained by key-side structural grounding, a reconstruction penalty, and query-side separation so it does not reconstruct the suppressed directions. At inference time, SPARK computes the energy of each head's current KV state in the learned harmful subspace and derives a closed-form mixing coefficient g_h* between the original memory and the projected-and-repaired memory. This coefficient is not a learned probability of harmfulness; it is a representation-energy-based intervention strength. First, the task is framed in the CiteGuard environment, where the model can take bounded actions such as search, inspect, request more context, and select a paper. This turns citation recovery into a sequential decision problem under an interaction budget, rather than a one-shot generation task. Second, the authors build CiteAlign, a 7,607-instance dataset from recent computer science literature, with temporally separated splits so that evaluation targets are relatively recent and less likely to be memorized. They also construct a controlled 709-instance benchmark subset for stable comparison. Third, they fine-tune Qwen3-4B with GRPO for tool-using citation recovery. A key design choice is to separate target retrieval from final selection, which lets the authors localize where RL helps. Compared with standard RAG-style supervised fine-tuning, this setup trains search behavior in an open retrieval space. Compared with pure imitation learning, GRPO allows the model to discover better query reformulation and stopping strategies through interaction.562:T6f0,RFPO alternates between two stages.

Stage 1 is Q-guided sample refinement. Given a state, the current flow policy maps Gaussian noise to an action. Instead of using that action directly, the method runs a finite number of MALA steps starting from the policy sample, targeting the Boltzmann distribution induced by the critic, p(a|s) proportional to exp(Q(s,a)/alpha). This is a practical choice: the method does not try to sample exactly from the target distribution, nor does it directly regress a critic-derived velocity field. It first generates a plausible action with the current policy, then uses critic gradients plus Metropolis correction to refine it toward higher-probability regions.

Stage 2 is self-target flow matching. The refined action is paired with the original base noise used to generate the pre-refinement action, and this pair becomes a source-target example for conditional flow matching. In effect, the model learns to map the same latent noise to a better action next time. The targets are therefore self-generated and improved by finite-step MCMC, not provided by an external oracle.

Relative to prior work, the differences are clear. It does not rely on Q-weighted regression alone, does not require directly learning a score model for the target action distribution, and does not treat the critic merely as a weighting function. Instead, it uses MCMC as an intermediate refinement operator and then amortizes that refinement into the flow policy. The paper also includes an idealized distributional analysis showing monotonic improvement of a maximum-entropy objective and identifying the Q-induced energy distribution as a fixed point. That theory is not a full practical guarantee, but it explains why the refine-then-distill loop is sensible.563:T4f8,The experiments have two roles. The synthetic-distribution experiments test whether RFPO can preserve multimodality and fit complex target geometries, which is important because Gaussian actors often collapse such structure. The online continuous-control experiments test whether that expressive policy class translates into better RL performance. The headline claim is that RFPO matches or outperforms a standard Gaussian-policy baseline on almost all tasks.

From the provided full text, several experimental facts are clear: the target policy is the Q-induced Boltzmann distribution; the temperature alpha controls concentration; refinement uses a finite number of MALA steps rather than long-run sampling; and the paper evaluates not only return but also how well the learned policy approximates the target distribution.

The excerpt does not include the final result tables, so exact environment names, architecture sizes, MALA step counts, or return gains should not be fabricated. The most important checks during reading are the ablations: how sensitive performance is to the number of MALA steps, whether removing the Metropolis-Hastings correction hurts, and how RFPO compares against direct Q-guided flow objectives and standard Gaussian actor-critic baselines.564:Tbd5,技术上，文章把问题拆成三个对象和两类证据。三个对象分别是 moral subspace、refusal direction、以及 judgment direction；两类证据分别是几何测量和因果 interchange。

The argument revolves around three objects: a moral subspace, a refusal direction, and a moral-judgment direction.

The moral subspace is built from three independent moral-content sources: Moral Stories, Understanding Fables, and ETHICS. For each source, the authors compute a moral-versus-neutral mean-difference direction, then orthonormalize the resulting set into an effective rank-3 subspace. This design choice is important. The goal is not simply to maximize dimensionality, but to obtain a construct-diverse, source-distinguishable representation that is less vulnerable to single-dataset contamination.

The refusal direction is extracted in the standard representation-reading style from the mean difference between refused and complied requests. A judgment direction is defined analogously for moral judgment. The authors then examine how these directions relate to the moral subspace across layers and positions, with special attention to the decision site: the assistant header or end-of-prompt control token where the refusal gate is read out.

A major strength of the paper is that OLMo-3 provides both base and post-training checkpoints, allowing the authors to track representational formation over training stages. They report that the moral subspace is already present in pretraining and remains nearly the same object through the final model, with a checkpoint-to-final cosine of 0.999. Post-training mainly rotates it once, by about 40 degrees, rather than rebuilding it. By contrast, the refusal gate has only a weak precursor in pretraining: proto-refusal-to-gate cosine is 0.155, about twice the matched null but still far from a mature gate. This asymmetry supports the paper’s central distinction between deep comprehension and shallow control.

The next step is geometric analysis at the decision site. Across four models, the control token is an 8-to-15 dimensional bottleneck. Within that bottleneck, the refusal-decision direction is largely separated from the moral-judgment direction. On OLMo, refusal projects only 0.10 of its norm onto the moral subspace, with mean absolute cosine around 0.06, below the moral-family band. This suggests that refusal is not broadly reading the moral subspace where comprehension lives.

The strongest evidence comes from a nested interchange rank sweep on OLMo. The authors progressively expand the rank of the patched moral basis and compare how refusal coupling and judgment coupling respond. If refusal depended on broad moral content, its transferred effect should keep increasing with rank. Instead, judgment coupling rises with rank and reconstructs about 0.66 of the subspace patch effect, while refusal coupling quickly saturates at the rank-1 harm level. That is the key causal result behind the title: refusal reads only a slice of what the model knows.

Finally, the four-model panel is interpreted along two separate axes: what refusal reads, and how the model commits. Some models appear to read harm, some broader moral content, and commitment can happen at the read layer, earlier than the read layer, or remain reversible under later deliberation. This decomposition is more informative than a single scalar notion of alignment depth.566:T816,There are three experimental blocks that carry most of the paper.

First, the training-stage tracking on OLMo-3. Because the authors have access to both base and post-training checkpoints, they can follow representational continuity. If time is tight, prioritize the OLMo causal interchange over the broader four-model geometric panel.568:T725,The paper compares three state structures under a shared setup. Frontier superposition stores only the active alternatives at the current step. Cumulative superposition stores the full reached history. General weighted superposition allows arbitrary weight allocation over that history. All three use the same graph, candidate bank, downstream query family, and decoder, so the comparison isolates only one design choice: what the continuous state preserves.

The theoretical core is a critical-dimension analysis. Objects receive independent Gaussian embeddings, and the latent state is a normalized superposition of those embeddings. A common decoder then tries to distinguish a useful direction from competing directions. The authors derive an exact finite-dimensional score law and use it to compare the minimum hidden dimension needed for reliable decoding. The main result is that for a broad class of state-independent, nonlocalized, bounded-influence queries, cumulative superposition benefits from coherent reinforcement among historically useful components, while unrelated components behave mostly as random interference. So even though cumulative states have larger support, the signal relevant to future computation can be stronger rather than weaker.

The paper then maps this abstraction back to Transformer mechanics. Attention expands the current computation, while residual writing determines whether previous objects are discarded or preserved. In weighted superpositions, the weakest retained coefficient becomes the routing bottleneck: if some historical items receive too little weight, later attention cannot reliably reuse them. This leads to a minimax design principle: when future queries are unknown, uniform cumulative weighting is robustly near-optimal, and in the formal setup it is exactly minimax.569:T4e1,The experiments are structured to validate the theory rather than to chase a benchmark headline. First, there are controlled simulations checking that the finite-dimensional score law predicts actual retrieval and discrimination behavior. Second, width-scaling experiments compare frontier, cumulative, and weighted superpositions as hidden dimension varies. The central empirical pattern is that cumulative superposition reaches usable performance at smaller widths than frontier superposition for the nonlocalized query classes studied in the theory. Third, the paper implements the attention-residual construction in lightweight models and GPT-2-style token-level settings to test the mechanism-level claim that the weakest retained coefficient is the practical routing bottleneck.

Two aspects are especially useful. One, the cumulative advantage is not restricted to trivial symmetric or purely additive queries; the query family is allowed to be continuous, correlated, asymmetric, and identity-dependent. Two, the failure mode of weighted superposition is interpretable: the problem is not simply insufficient total energy, but poor allocation, where potentially useful historical items are assigned coefficients too small to be reused later.56a:T4b0,Start with the setup and the definitions of the three superposition structures. The paper is easy to misread if one forgets that the task and decoder are held fixed; only the retention policy changes. Then read the critical-dimension section carefully. Dataset C contains non-echoing prompts from a similar generation pipeline. Data come from filtered EPITOME peer-support dialogues, with short seeker posts and self-harm-related cases removed to reduce context sparsity and safety-template confounds. For each empathy mechanism, the authors build contrastive sets and extract steering vectors from residual-stream activations.

The main intervention is contrastive activation addition: a direction is estimated from activation differences between higher-scoring and lower-scoring examples for a given mechanism, then added at inference time to a chosen layer. The contribution is less about inventing a new steering algorithm and more about the analysis stack built around it.

There are three key components. First, a layer sweep identifies where interventions are stable across models; middle layers emerge as the most reliable, with layer 15 receiving special attention in the analysis. Second, target versus off-target evaluation measures not only whether ER steering raises ER, but also whether it unintentionally shifts IP and EX, and likewise for the other directions. This tests separability rather than raw controllability. Third, geometric and projection analyses examine pairwise structure among ER/IP/EX directions and quantify how much persona-induced activation movement lies inside the recovered mechanism subspace.

Compared with prior activation-steering work on honesty, refusal, or sycophancy, the difference is substantial. The target behavior here is inherently multi-component. The authors use steering as a representational probe, not just a control knob. And they explicitly test whether prompt-induced persona effects align with the recovered mechanism basis, which is a deeper question than simply comparing response scores under different personas.56d:T700,The experiments support three main findings. First, steering is feasible. Across all three models, contrastive activation addition at middle layers consistently shifts EPITOME proxy scores in the intended direction. The trend survives evaluation with a second automated judge, which reduces the chance that the result is only an artifact of one classifier. The paper also reports partial out-of-domain transfer, suggesting the vectors are not purely dataset-specific surface heuristics.

Second, the three empathy mechanisms are not independently controllable. Steering along one recovered direction improves the target mechanism, but also causes measurable off-target changes in the other two. The result is not that ER, IP, and EX are indistinguishable; rather, they are distinguishable but share representational structure strongly enough that clean disentanglement fails. This is the central empirical basis for the paper’s “multi-axial” claim.

Third, persona effects mostly fall outside the recovered mechanism basis. Persona prompts can produce large changes in output-level empathy scores, yet the corresponding activation shifts project only weakly onto the ER/IP/EX subspace. The headline number is that at layer 15, the recovered ER/IP/EX basis explains only about 3% of the persona-induced mean-squared activation-shift magnitude. That is a strong indication that persona-conditioned empathy variation is not just movement along “more ER,” “more IP,” or “more EX,” but involves broader representational changes.

Evaluation relies mainly on EPITOME classifiers plus an LLM judge, so the findings are best read as robust mechanism-level evidence rather than a final statement about human-perceived empathy.56e:T48c,For a skim, start with the two research questions in the introduction, then jump to the method figure and the layer-sweep results. Second, the spillover results across mechanisms. This is the core evidence in the paper. Do not only look at target gains; inspect how much the non-target dimensions move and whether the pattern is consistent across models.
