The penalty is first applied to the localized safety-decision layers; if compensatory drift appears in unpenalized layers, the same diagnostics are used to expand the scope. The method uses no safety training data, no reference policy, and adds no inference overhead.82f:Ta1d,方法叫 BPCO（Best-Practice Critic Optimization）。它由五个关键部件组成。

第一，用 DPPO 替代标准 PPO clipping。标准 PPO 用概率比值裁剪，低概率 token 的微小绝对变化也可能触发 clipping，而高概率 token 可以承受更大的绝对变化；在大词表 LM 中，这会让不同 token 的更新几何很不均匀。DPPO 把约束改成 sampled token 概率的绝对变化上界，相当于让每个被采样 token 共享同一 absolute-probability trust region，更适合语言模型的长尾词分布。

第二，把 critic 输出限制在 reward range 内。论文考虑的是 outcome reward，回报天然有已知范围。若 value head 仍是无界线性层，训练早期很容易出现超范围预测，随后 GAE 和 value loss 都会被放大。作者将 value prediction bounded 到 reward 支持集，使 critic 的函数类与任务先验一致，减少无意义外推。

第三，critic 直接拟合 Monte Carlo return，而不是常见的 bootstrap target。由于中间 reward 全为 0、终局才给分，且 γ=1 的设置很常见，此时用 bootstrap target 的收益并不大，却会把旧 critic 的误差传播到新 critic。BPCO 直接用观测到的最终回报训练 value，相当于在 outcome-only 场景里主动放弃一部分低方差，换取更少偏差和更稳定的 critic 学习。

第四，policy update 不做 batch-wise advantage normalization。作者的论点很直接：当策略逐渐收敛时，真实 advantage 的尺度本来就应该变小；若每个 batch 都强行归一到单位方差，就等于持续放大残余噪声，容易造成后期训练抖动甚至过更新。BPCO 保留 raw advantage scale，让优化器看到“信号正在衰减”这件事。

第五，使用 length-adaptive GAE。固定 λ 在短回答和长回答上对应的 terminal reward 传播形状不同，导致 credit assignment 随长度系统性偏移。作者设计按 response length 调整的 λ，使不同长度样本上终局奖励向前传播的权重分布更一致。

除此之外，论文还强调一个 critic-only 的额外自由度：privileged critic input。因为 critic 只在训练时使用，可以额外看到 reward-defining information，例如数学题参考答案、官方解、或开放式任务的 rubric，而 policy 仍只看原始 prompt。这样不会改变最优 value function 的定义，但会显著降低 value approximation 难度。这个点和传统 RLHF/GRPO 的差别很大：group-relative estimator 很难自然利用这类只在训练时可见的信息。830:T7b2,实验分三层。

第一层是 controlled sanity test。作者构造了一个小而可解的数据设定，用“能否稳定拟合”来隔离优化问题，而不是把失败归因于任务难度。这里最有信息量的结论是：bounded value head、MC target、去掉 advantage normalization、以及 length-adaptive GAE 都能单独改善稳定性；把这些组件叠加后，critic baseline 从容易发散或震荡，变成可持续下降并收敛的训练曲线。这个部分更像训练病理分析，建议认真看。

第二层是数学推理主实验。数据规模是 40.3K problems，并在两个 30B-A3B 的 MoE 模型上评估。文章的主张不是“critic 远超 group-based RL”，而是更克制：BPCO 相比原始 critic baseline 在不同模型和数据规模上都更稳、更强；同时在只用每个 prompt 一个 response 的条件下，性能可以追平或超过 group-based baseline。这里真正重要的是 sample efficiency 叙事：GRPO 需要每 prompt 多条 rollout 才能形成组内相对优势，而 BPCO 用单条 rollout 就能构造 token-level advantage。

第三层是 privileged information 实验，包括数学任务里给 critic 参考答案，以及 rubric-reward 任务里给 critic rubric。结果显示 privileged input 往往能加快 critic 学习，但对最终 policy 的收益并不总是单调增加；当 critic 过拟合训练分布时，value 更准不一定转化成更好的 policy improvement。这个观察很重要，因为它提醒人们：critic 监督更强，不等于 actor 更新一定更好，关键还要看 value error 的分布是否与 policy improvement 方向一致。

从摘要和正文可确认的硬数字包括：40.3K 数学数据集、两个 30B-A3B MoE 模型、single-rollout 设置对比 group-based baseline。若做复现，建议重点记录各 ablation 对 value loss、KL、reward variance、以及训练后期稳定性的影响，而不只看最终 pass@1。831:T95d,The proposed recipe is BPCO, Best-Practice Critic Optimization. It combines five design choices.

First, it replaces standard PPO clipping with DPPO. Standard PPO clips the probability ratio, which means low-probability sampled tokens can be clipped by tiny absolute probability changes while high-probability tokens tolerate much larger ones. In large-vocabulary language models, this creates uneven update geometry. DPPO instead clips the absolute probability change of the sampled token, giving a common absolute-probability trust region.

Second, it bounds value predictions to the reward range. In outcome-reward settings, the return support is known. An unconstrained linear value head can easily overshoot that range, especially early in training, which then destabilizes both value fitting and downstream advantage estimates. Bounding the value head injects a simple but strong task prior.

Third, it trains the critic on Monte Carlo returns rather than bootstrapped targets. Because intermediate rewards are zero and the terminal reward carries the whole signal, the variance reduction from bootstrapping is limited while the bias from critic self-reinforcement can be severe. BPCO therefore prefers direct supervision from observed outcomes.

Fourth, it removes batch-wise advantage normalization in the policy update. The argument is that as the policy improves, the residual advantage scale should naturally shrink. Forcing every batch to unit scale erases that information and can keep magnifying noise late in training. BPCO preserves the raw advantage magnitude.

Fifth, it introduces length-adaptive GAE. With a fixed lambda, terminal reward is propagated backward with a length-dependent profile, so short and long responses receive systematically different credit assignment. The adaptive schedule is designed to make the effective weighting of terminal reward more consistent across response lengths.

A notable extra feature is privileged critic input. Since the critic is discarded at inference time, it can condition on reward-defining information unavailable to the policy, such as a reference answer, official solution, or grading rubric. This does not change the ideal value function for a prompt, but it can make that function much easier to approximate. That is a meaningful advantage over group-relative estimators, which do not naturally exploit such side information.832:T650,The empirical section has three layers.

The first is a controlled sanity test on a small solvable setup. This is arguably the most informative part of the paper because it isolates optimization pathologies from task difficulty. The ablations show that bounded value prediction, Monte Carlo targets, removing advantage normalization, and length-adaptive GAE each improve stability, and their combination turns a fragile critic baseline into a trainable one.

The second layer is the main mathematical reasoning evaluation on a 40.3K-problem dataset, using two 30B-A3B mixture-of-experts models. The claim is measured rather than inflated: BPCO consistently improves over the critic baseline across scales, and with only one rollout per prompt it matches or exceeds a group-based baseline. The key point is sample efficiency and token-level credit assignment, not merely final accuracy.

The third layer studies privileged information. In math, the critic can see a reference answer; in a rubric-reward task, it can see the grading rubric. This often accelerates critic learning, but the policy gain is task-dependent and can weaken when the critic overfits. That is a useful result: a more accurate critic is not automatically a more useful critic for policy improvement.

The hard numbers explicitly stated in the paper include the 40.3K math dataset, two 30B-A3B MoE models, and single-rollout comparisons against group-based training. For reproduction, the most important metrics to track are not just final reward or accuracy, but also value loss behavior, KL, reward variance, and late-stage training stability.833:T45c,Start with the introduction, because the paper frames instability as a set of mismatches rather than a vague implementation issue. Then go straight to the controlled sanity-test section and its figures. That is where the paper earns its claims. If time is limited, prioritize the ablations comparing PPO vs DPPO, bounded vs unbounded value heads, Monte Carlo vs bootstrapped targets, and normalized vs raw advantages.

Next, read the section defining length-adaptive GAE. The value is not in the formula itself, but in how it corrects length-dependent reward propagation under outcome-only supervision. If you work on RLHF or GRPO alternatives, compare its terminal-reward weighting profile against fixed-lambda GAE.

Finally, read the privileged-critic-input experiments. The interesting question is not whether the score goes up, but when training-only side information improves actor learning and when it merely helps the critic fit returns. A careful skim takes about 30 to 45 minutes. For implementation or transfer to reasoning RL, the appendix is worth reading for optimizer details and exact hyperparameters.834:T853,The method is NC-GRPO, Noise-Contrastive GRPO. For each rollout group, half of the branches are standard GRPO rollouts, while the other half receive Gaussian noise injected into the last hidden layer during the prompt-encoding prefill pass. The noisy branches therefore start generation from displaced latent states. If a branch still reaches the correct answer despite the displacement, it is reinforced relative to branches that fail, so sensitivity to that latent perturbation is converted into policy-gradient signal through group-normalized rewards.

Several design choices matter.

First, the noise is injected only once during prefill, not throughout decoding. The paper is careful about this distinction: it changes the departure state of the rollout, but does not keep perturbing the cached representation during generation. This keeps decoding cost identical to standard GRPO and makes attribution cleaner.

Second, the noise scale is calibrated to the hidden-state norm. The perturbation magnitude is proportional to the norm of the original hidden vector, so sigma becomes a dimensionless relative scale rather than an architecture-dependent absolute one. The paper also shows that the relative perturbation magnitude concentrates with variance 2/d, which means the actual perturbation size is tightly controlled in high-dimensional hidden spaces.

Third, the noise follows an annealing schedule: stronger exploration early, decaying to zero later. This mirrors prior noisy-rollout schedules, but moves the perturbation from pixel space into latent space.

Fourth, the paper includes antithetic and steered probes. These are designed to test whether the gain comes from simply adding more noise budget or from creating independent stochastic branches. The conclusion is that independent stochastic diversity is the active ingredient, not a specific direction or just larger perturbation energy.

Methodologically, this is a clean intervention. The GRPO objective, reward, decoding, and evaluation are kept fixed as much as possible, so the observed differences can be attributed mainly to the diversification mechanism.835:T6f9,The experiments focus on multimodal mathematical reasoning and hallucination robustness. The paper reports significant gains over vanilla GRPO on five out-of-domain multimodal math benchmarks, with pooled McNemar significance ranging from p=0.001 to p<1e-4. It also reports improvements on in-domain accuracy, suggesting that latent perturbation is not merely acting as domain-shift regularization.

Compared with image-space noise, NC-GRPO performs better on hallucination robustness: significant on POPE with p=0.007, and +0.6 points on HallusionBench. This matters because it suggests latent diversification is not just making outputs more varied; it may be encouraging policies that are more stable to perturbations in internal representations. It also highlights a limitation of pixel-space noise: it can only diversify along directions expressible by the visual encoder, whereas latent noise acts after multimodal fusion.

The mechanism studies are the most informative part. Matched antithetic and steered probes indicate that the benefit comes mainly from independent stochastic branching rather than a particular perturbation direction or total noise budget. The noise-scale study is also useful: sigma_0 acts as a specialization dial. Larger noise tends to favor reasoning gains but can trade off against general capability, while sigma_0=0.2 is reported as a regime that improves reasoning without measurable loss in general capability.

The provided text does not include the full model sizes, training budgets, or all benchmark-by-benchmark scores, so it would be unsafe to invent them. The reliable takeaways are the significant gains on five OOD multimodal math benchmarks, the POPE result at p=0.007, the +0.6 HallusionBench gain, and the mechanism and scale ablations.836:T437,This is a good skim paper. Focus on the motivation and the mechanism studies rather than treating it as a dense RL derivation.

Start with the introduction and the method section that defines exactly what is perturbed and what is not. That design choice is central to the paper’s causal interpretation.

Then read the noise-scaling formulation and the proposition about width-invariant relative perturbation. The math is simple, but it is important because it turns sigma into a controlled experimental knob rather than a model-specific heuristic.

The most valuable sections are the mechanism probes and the noise-scale study. One explains why the method helps; the other explains what trade-off it induces. If you care about latent reasoning, NoisyCoconut-style branching, or rollout diversification for text-only LLMs, those sections are more informative than the headline benchmark table. A focused read should take 20 to 30 minutes.837:T769,The method defines Visual Information Gain, or VIG, at each reasoning position. Conceptually, VIG measures how much the image reduces uncertainty about the token generated at that position, conditioned on the question and prior context. The paper motivates this as a conditional mutual information quantity, but the practical implementation uses an entropy difference computed from two forward passes of the same policy: one pass with the image, and one pass with visual tokens removed. If the image makes the predictive distribution much sharper, the token is treated as visually grounded and receives a higher VIG score. If the entropy barely changes, the token is likely recoverable from text context alone and is treated as filler.

These token-level scores are aggregated over the <think> span into a sequence-level reward, which is then combined with standard answer-accuracy and format rewards inside GRPO. A key design choice is that the method never rewards shorter chains directly. Shorter reasoning emerges because the policy learns to keep tokens that earn visual support and drop tokens that do not. This is different from length penalties, which can suppress both useless and necessary reasoning. It is also different from trace distillation, which depends on external compressed chains and inherits teacher bias.

Another notable choice is the use of entropy reduction rather than only the log-probability gap for the sampled token. Entropy reduction captures whether the image globally resolves uncertainty at that step, not just whether it happens to boost the chosen token. In that sense, the reward is closer to a token-level grounding diagnostic than a simple preference score. Methodologically, this is a post-training RL contribution rather than a new pretraining objective, but the signal itself is general and could plausibly inspire pretraining-time multimodal objectives.838:T664,The evaluation spans three Qwen3-VL-Thinking model sizes, six main multimodal reasoning benchmarks, and an additional test on R1-Onevision-Bench. The paper emphasizes the accuracy-efficiency Pareto frontier rather than reporting accuracy alone. On Qwen3-VL-8B-Thinking, VIG reaches 64.92% average accuracy and 52.42 ACC per 1k tokens. Relative to the strongest compression baseline, ThinkPrune, it improves accuracy by 2.37 points and efficiency by 39.4%.

The qualitative example in the introduction is also informative. On a simple geometry problem, the base model spends 823 reasoning tokens and still answers incorrectly. An L1-style length penalty reduces the chain to 412 tokens and recovers the correct answer. VIG solves the same problem in 105 tokens by directly reading the visual label and applying the correct relation. That example supports the paper’s claim that the issue is not merely verbosity, but visually disengaged reasoning.

From the available full text, the main empirical story is built around three comparisons. First, VIG is compared against base, plain GRPO, L1, ThinkPrune, and TALE, showing that a visual-dependence reward outperforms purely textual compression signals. Second, the gains persist across model sizes, suggesting the effect is not tied to one checkpoint. Third, on R1-Onevision-Bench, the method ranks first overall and first or tied-first in three of five subject categories, which argues against narrow benchmark overfitting. The important result is that token count drops sharply while accuracy also improves, which is exactly what length-only compression methods often fail to achieve.839:T495,For a quick read, focus on three parts. Start with the introduction and the motivating examples, especially the figure showing how long multimodal CoT can talk itself out of a correct answer. Two deeper questions are worth keeping in mind. One is whether entropy-based VIG may systematically favor certain token types or templated visual descriptions. If you care about pretraining, the natural follow-up thought is whether this kind of token-level grounding signal could be turned into a multimodal pretraining objective rather than staying purely in post-training RL.83a:T5a7,The proposed framework is computation-conditioned credit transport, or CCT. Standard GAE can be written as a stationary upper-triangular transport kernel whose weights depend only on temporal distance. Group-relative methods often assign a response-level statistic to all valid response tokens, giving a rank-one broadcast structure. CCT instead extracts a detached statistic from the behavior policy’s internal computation at each prefix and maps it to a bounded retention gate κ_t. The sensitivity of an earlier advantage A_t to a later residual δ_u is then the product of gates along the intervening path. This makes the transport kernel nonstationary and trajectory-specific while keeping the task reward and outer objective unchanged. The instantiated algorithm, CompPO, uses native attention concentration as a cheap structural proxy. The gate enters a computation-conditioned bootstrap and a path-dependent generalized-advantage trace, called Comp-GAE. A transport-aligned critic pools value-relevant history from the actor’s hidden states and attention, using the same gate to connect local and routed-history value estimates. The outer objective remains clipped PPO, with the same verifier, rollout format, and reward. The method is not simply an attention-weighted policy-gradient loss: attention parameterizes the bootstrap coefficient, trace weights, and critic state geometry, but does not directly multiply the policy gradient.83b:T56b,The setup starts with a deliberately sparse training pool: 20,830 visual-math problems filtered from MathV360K, where Qwen2-VL-2B gets only 3.6% rollout accuracy and 85%–97% of GRPO groups are all-wrong. On this pool, the authors train 11 arms under identical data, budget, seed, and hardware conditions. For text priors, they prepend part of a reference solution so exploration starts from a more promising state. An important decomposition is that the gain comes from improved exploration itself, while the auxiliary UFT-style likelihood term adds little. For distribution priors, they compare several on-policy distillation variants and show that delivery matters: if the signal is capped by teacher ability, gated only to failures, or otherwise poorly routed, it does not help much. Annealed global distillation works; failure-gated persistent distillation does not. For value priors, they train a critic to provide token-level credit assignment even when sequence-level outcomes are uniform. The key finding is not merely that a critic helps, but that critic parameterization matters a lot: replacing clipped MSE scalar regression with an HL-Gauss categorical loss substantially improves signal delivery. They also test stacking text and distribution priors and find little additive benefit, suggesting both mainly address the same early bottleneck rather than complementary ones.83c:T616,The experimental design is unusually controlled: same pool, same step and batch budget, same seed, one 8×A800 node per arm. Evaluation uses blind judging by an independent LLM judge (DeepSeek) over full outputs, with McNemar exact tests for pairwise claims. The main result is a clean separation by signal delivery. On the out-of-domain DynaMath benchmark, the six arms whose prior demonstrably reaches the policy score 30.6%–32.9%, while the remaining five arms, including plain GRPO and variants where the prior is blocked or misparameterized, score 27.0%–29.1%, with no overlap. Component-level findings are also concrete. A half-solution hint raises prevalidated success from 7.2% to 34.4%, showing that exploration state matters. The paper also reports a scoring audit showing that a heuristic answer extractor can introduce up to 30-point arm-dependent bias and even invert rankings.83d:T4f5,The method, LACL-GUI, is a length-aware contrastive RLVR framework. It starts from the observation that GUI trajectory quality depends not only on final success but also on efficiency and closeness to success. For successful trajectories, the method prefers shorter executions by assigning stronger optimization pressure to concise solutions and down-weighting redundant ones. For failed trajectories, it defines divergence length, measuring how long a failed trajectory stays aligned with a reference successful trajectory before deviating. Failures that diverge later are treated as more informative negatives and are suppressed less aggressively. The key design choice is how these preferences are injected: not by changing the success/failure labels or moving the decision boundary, but through outcome-preserving, zero-mean logit modulations inside a contrastive/classification objective. This lets the method reshape optimization pressure within the positive set and within the negative set while keeping the original binary supervision intact. Conceptually, the paper builds on the motivation behind REAL-like methods: classification objectives avoid GRPO’s gradient pathologies, and LACL-GUI adds finer trajectory structure without sacrificing that stability.83e:T449,The Activation Controllability Benchmark asks a model to copy a fixed neutral sentence exactly while an embedded instruction tells it what to do internally, such as thinking about a concept or suppressing it. Trials are kept only when the copy is correct, reducing confounds from different output text. The measurement reads the residual stream. For each concept and layer, a concept direction is built by taking the residual at the last token of a prompt like “Tell me about {concept}” and subtracting the mean residual for unrelated words. During generation, token residuals are projected onto this direction. The benchmark uses raw projection rather than only cosine similarity, so changes in residual norm are also captured. Six measures define controllability: Engage, Suppress, Dial Rank, Temporal Control, Coverage, and Layer Targeting. Most use a signal-detection d′ effect size; Dial Rank uses Spearman correlation to test monotonic control over requested intensity. A conjunctive geometric-mean score combines the measures, rewarding broad control rather than a single strong axis.83f:T605,Model generation as a finite-horizon MDP: state = token prefix, action = next token, reward only at the end and normalized to [0,1]. Define policy variance σ^2_π(s)=Var_{a~π}[Q^π(s,a)]. Under deterministic transitions, the environment term in the return-variance decomposition vanishes, yielding a clean identity: trajectory return variance equals the sum over time of expected σ^2_π(s_t). This motivates “critical forks”: states with σ^2_π(s) above a threshold τ.

The paper separates two questions with different complexity regimes:
(1) Local discovery: how many samples from π(·|s) are needed to even observe an action with advantage ≥ c. Using concentration/one-sided inequalities (Cantelli/Chebyshev/Markov variants) on the centered advantage draw A^π(s,a), they derive a polynomial lower bound Ω(c^2/σ^2_π(s)), and show tightness on a canonical two-action fork.
(2) Long-horizon estimation: once such an action is observed, how many full trajectories are needed to estimate its advantage accurately enough to act on; this scales exponentially with remaining horizon, motivating local credit assignment.

They also provide a rollout-free screening step: bound σ^2_π(s) by the Gini–Simpson dispersion 𝒟(s)=1-||π(·|s)||_2^2, computable from a single next-token distribution. Low-dispersion states cannot be critical forks, though high dispersion is not sufficient (many paraphrase/formatting choices can be value-equivalent). Extensions to stochastic environments clarify which arguments rely on determinism.840:T4a2,Two-layer design:
1) Conceptual layer (CPC): transformer computation is framed as iterative refinement of representational fragments under a global coherence functional C (explicitly treated as an interpretive hypothesis, not an explicit training objective). Components can instantiate four operator roles:
- Alignment: propose candidate relations between context fragments.
- Unification: integrate mutually supporting evidence into a consistent interpretation.
- Suppression: downweight incompatible alternatives / resolve conflicts.
- Routing: carry selected information forward to the prediction site.
Roles can be distributed across components; components can be multi-role.
2) Operational layer: define attention-head role “signatures” in weight space and corresponding activation-level role measures, then test whether weight signatures predict held-out activation measures. The empirical program is organized around P1–P4: reproducibility/validity of signatures; dependence of suppression on upstream alignment; behavior under contradiction via a coherence proxy; and how post-training reshapes operator structure (reweighting existing roles vs introducing new structure).841:T699,The approach is a systematic intervention study rather than a new training recipe. The authors use three open-weight models previously shown to exhibit WG: Llama-3.1-70B, Qwen-2.5-32B, and Qwen-2.5-72B. They start from four narrow fine-tuning datasets known to trigger broad behavior changes: Old Bird Names, Medical Terms, Harry Potter, and Extreme Sports.

They then construct controlled variants along five axes. First, dataset size: they subsample the original narrow datasets at multiple fractions to test whether WG scales smoothly with the number of examples. Second, dataset composition: they mix the WG-inducing data with Dolly instruction data at different proportions to see whether the effect survives dilution and whether composition matters more than raw count. Third, language: they translate or otherwise alter the linguistic surface form to test whether the effect is tied to the original language distribution. Fourth, presentation mode: they compare more direct versus indirect formulations, probing whether the model is learning a latent persona/style pattern rather than only a factual mapping. Fifth, novelty: they vary whether the fine-tuning content is familiar from pretraining or relatively novel, asking whether WG is easier to elicit when fine-tuning reactivates existing parametric knowledge.

Evaluation follows prior WG work but adds an important robustness check. The models answer open-ended probe questions, and GPT-5-mini scores both consistency with the target generalization and response coherence. The paper also studies sensitivity to the choice of probe questions, which is crucial because WG claims often rest on very small curated evaluation sets.842:T5e4,The study spans 3 models and 4 base datasets. Dataset sizes differ substantially: Birds has 208 examples, Medicine 1,139, Harry Potter 137, and Extreme Sports 6,000. The authors also create matched-size comparisons by truncating larger datasets to 137 or 208 examples, which helps separate dataset identity from sample-count effects.

The most robust findings are qualitative but clear. First, WG depends much more on composition and language than on dataset size. Increasing the number of narrow examples does not produce a clean monotonic increase in weird generalization, while changing the fraction of WG-inducing data inside a broader instruction mixture can materially change the outcome. Second, WG is stronger when the fine-tuning data draws on knowledge already familiar from pretraining. This supports an activation or steering interpretation: the fine-tune may be unlocking or amplifying latent pretrained structure rather than teaching a wholly new broad behavior from scratch. Third, measured WG is sensitive to the specific probe question set, which means current evaluations have nontrivial variance.

The headline conclusion is that WG and EM are fragile forms of generalization and are unlikely to arise without adversarial data engineering. The paper’s evidence is less about one standout metric and more about instability across controlled perturbations. The practical takeaway is that size is not the main driver; composition, language, and novelty are closer to the real control knobs.843:T4b8,The proposed framework is Adaptive Functional Metaplasticity, or AFM. At each protected update, AFM first computes the endpoint that the same learner would have accepted from the exact same pre-update state without any retention constraint. This endpoint is used only as a counterfactual reference and is not installed. AFM then identifies the component of that update that is compatible with protected functional behavior and stores only an accepted fraction in the ordinary parameters. A key distinction is made between persistent adaptation, finite deployed protection, and population behavior: matching protected outputs on a finite set does not imply that the unrestricted learning has been stored, nor that behavior is preserved on unseen inputs. The framework includes bounded sketches of behavioral sensitivity, multiple metaplastic timescales, a rank-timescale controller, task-free observable routing, a guarded finite functional shield, and function-preserving renewal of dormant structure. The formal results cover streamed-memory certificates, a rank-plasticity frontier, pathwise retention, projected stationarity, a convex dynamic-regret specialization, resource bounds, and obstruction cases.844:T526,The paper introduces three families of commutators: gate-covariance, sensitivity-covariance, and AGOP-NFM. The first key result is that the feature-side AGOP-NFM commutator is not a closed object; it is the congruence-transported image of an internal sensitivity-covariance commutator. This explains why feature-side alignment can appear stronger than internal alignment: incompatibility along small singular directions is attenuated, and components in covariance-null directions can disappear entirely. The second key result is an exact layerwise recursion for the internal commutator [Q_l, P_l], decomposing it into four sources: downstream transport, adjacent-layer imbalance, pointwise sensitivity fluctuations, and nonlinear gate-covariance interaction. The gate commutator is therefore an intrinsic nonlinear source, but not the whole story. The third contribution is the notion of buffered localized energies, which measure direct coupling between selected covariance spectral blocks while ignoring mixing inside a buffered near-degenerate region. This lets the analysis distinguish genuine cross-block misalignment from harmless rotations within clustered eigenspaces. Overall, the paper turns spectral alignment from an empirical observation into a decomposable and localized finite-width geometric framework.845:T4ab,The setup is clean and controlled. The authors define a fixed Task Management API with seven components, explicit communication rules, data ownership constraints, six hard architectural rules, 25 HTTP routes, three ADRs, and a prescribed file layout. They then encode the exact same system in five formats: natural-language prose, Mermaid diagrams with constraints and ADRs, OpenAPI, C4/Structurizr DSL, and TypeScript interface contracts with ArchUnit-style rules. Six models from three vendor families are asked to implement the system in a multi-turn coding-agent setting. Evaluation combines three channels: automated static architecture checks, automated route-coverage analysis, and LLM-as-judge scoring for architectural adherence, constraint compliance, and completeness. The central result is not that one format universally wins, but that there is a strong format-by-model interaction. Frontier models can absorb almost any representation, whereas weaker models improve sharply when the specification is more structured and closer to executable code. The paper also identifies three recurring failure modes: compilation death spiral, premature termination, and perfectionist iteration.846:T46d,The study is modest in scale but well controlled: 90 main multi-turn trials are reported, and 93 full transcripts and codebases are released. Four results stand out. 1) Strong format-by-model interaction: on Sonnet 4.6 and GPT-5, the quality spread across formats is only 0.17 to 0.92 points, while on non-frontier models it reaches 0.83 to 2.42 points. 2) TypeScript contracts strongly help the weakest model: Gemini Flash implements only 33% of specified API routes under prose, but 100% under TypeScript interface contracts, a 3x improvement from representation alone. 3) Inverted cost efficiency: Haiku consumes about 735K tokens for a score of 6.50, while Sonnet uses about 640K tokens for 8.42, showing that smaller iterative agents are not necessarily cheaper in practice. 4) Self-validation collapses with weaker models: frontier models achieve 100% demo run rate, while the smallest model reaches 0%, meaning it never successfully tests its own system end to end. The evaluation channels are complementary rather than redundant; the correlation between judge-based constraint scoring and automated compliance is only r=0.21.847:T581,The method has two key components. First, the model never emits raw SQL. It operates over a typed DSL with 15 relational operations: 12 relation-building operators and 3 read-only probing operators. Intermediate states are represented as immutable Relation handles, and later operations can only reference existing handles. This matters because many errors are caught at compile time rather than after SQL execution: unknown tables, unknown columns, references to columns removed by earlier projections, and malformed parameters all trigger typed errors from the DSL engine. Second, the system runs a standard think-act-observe ReAct loop. At each turn, the model reasons in a <think> block, then emits a JSON array of tool calls. The engine executes them sequentially and returns observations such as new handles, available columns, row counts, and result previews. If a call fails, the rest of the batch is skipped and the next reasoning step sees the diagnostic. Grounding is handled through iterative probing: the model can inspect candidate tables, sample values, verify join keys, and only then commit to joins, filters, or aggregations. An answer-shaping stage converts the final trace into the benchmark’s canonical answer format. Relative to prior text-to-SQL systems, the design intentionally removes schema-linking modules, retrieved demonstrations, candidate prefilling, and dedicated verifiers.848:T788,The paper has three main components. First, it formalises the collaboration tax using team-decentralisation and cooperative-game language. The tax is the success-rate gap between a full-information solo policy and a split-information paired policy. Two propositions characterise when the quantity is positive and connect it to a violation of superadditivity in the underlying cooperative game. The theory is lightweight, but it gives the empirical phenomenon a precise reference point.

Second, the authors build a 32-task suite grouped into Spatial, Relational, and CSP families. These families are chosen to span different sources of grounding friction: reference-frame alignment, lexical/category alignment, and indexing/ordinal alignment. Each task is designed so that a single model can solve it when given the full view, after which the information is partitioned across two agents. This makes the benchmark much cleaner than many agent evaluations that mix in tool use, planning depth, or environment interaction.

Third, the paper develops a mechanistic account of failure. It identifies a four-stage conversational cascade: grounding, querying, integration, and re-derivation. Grounding failures occur when agents introduce facts supported by neither private view. Querying failures occur when they do not ask the partner for missing information. Integration failures occur when they fail to combine both views before committing. Re-derivation failures occur when the receiver accepts an answer without recomputing it. The authors then show that conversation-shape features predict the tax well: model capability largely sets the intercept, while conversation structure sets the slope. Finally, they test a simple prompt-only intervention that adds one clause targeting each stage. The simplicity matters because it supports the claim that the dominant issue is coordination process, not missing base reasoning ability.849:T61c,The evaluation covers 11 models from 7 providers, with solo, homogeneous-pair, heterogeneous-pair, and slot-swapped heterogeneous settings. Even from the provided full text excerpt, several findings are clear. First, the collaboration tax is systematic rather than anecdotal. It exhibits two no-exception orderings: one over task categories and one over model capability. Harder grounding-friction categories consistently incur larger tax, and stronger models show monotonically smaller tax. Second, the main failure mode is not reasoning deficit. Conversation analysis indicates that many failures happen before the relevant information is properly requested or after it is received but not integrated or checked. Third, in heterogeneous pairs the stronger model bears the asymmetry of the loss, suggesting that weaker partners often drag the interaction into a poorer coordination regime rather than contributing complementary value. Fourth, the prompt-level intervention recovers a substantial fraction of the tax, and leave-one-out ablations show that the dominant bottleneck differs by task family. That is more informative than a generic prompt-length effect because it points to task-structure-specific coordination failures.

The experimental design is strong in one respect: the solo-tractable construction makes causal interpretation cleaner. The limitations are also clear: the suite is still relatively small, focused on two-agent natural-language coordination, and does not cover richer settings with tools, memory, or learned communication protocols.84a:T405,The method has two parts. First, the authors introduce a causal leave-one-out probe for evidence utilization. The generated answer is held fixed, and each candidate document is removed in turn; the resulting counterfactual sensitivity estimates how much the answer depends on that document. Because the answer is fixed, the probe can be run as teacher-forced evaluation rather than full autoregressive regeneration. The paper then uses same-query hard negatives to show that similarity-based and overlap-based metrics often confuse topical relatedness with actual evidence reliance. Second, the validated probe is used in a k-by-T factorial allocation study, where k controls context width and T controls the number of generation rounds. The system component is a closed-loop submodular scheduler that uses attribution feedback from previous generations to choose future evidence. An attribution-steered contrastive decoder is added to reduce repeated reliance on already-used evidence while maintaining plausibility constraints.84b:T723,The central proposal is Knowledge Triage. The authors derive a five-type knowledge model from 396,934 agent artifacts and argue that this is the coarsest partition that still supports distinct safety guarantees. The exact labels are written as {C, P, B, F, E}; the important point is that each type tolerates a different kind of distortion. Constraints require wording-level fidelity, procedures allow behavior-preserving rewrites, and episodic logs can be aggressively summarized or dropped.

The knowledge base is formalized as K=(I, τ, T, π, σ), where I is the item set, τ is the type classifier, T is a topic tree, π maps items to topic leaves, and σ defines the scope of constraint items. This lets the paper unify three context-management operations under one typed budget-allocation view:
1. TypeCompact: in-place budget reduction with type-specific fidelity policies instead of uniform summarization.
2. TypeDecompose: splitting oversized topics before compression, so non-compressible constraints are not mixed with compressible background material.
3. TypeRetrieve: retrieval from external memory that is aware of item type, not just semantic relevance.

Two supporting components are added. A post-compaction guard verifier checks whether critical guards remain enforceable after rewriting. A SafetyMargin classifier scores items by counterfactual safety impact rather than surface form, which is more meaningful than keyword-based rule detection.

A strong point of the paper is that it does not stop at empirical anecdotes. It states per-operator safety requirements and argues that type-blind strategies cannot satisfy them across compaction, decomposition, and retrieval. The claim is therefore structural: one fidelity policy cannot serve heterogeneous knowledge objects with incompatible loss tolerances.84c:T5d4,The empirical section has two layers. First, it measures the failure mode directly. On 20 production agent configurations, Claude Code’s /compact prompt on Sonnet 4.6 preserves only 53% of safety rules after one compaction round and 10% after five rounds. The introduction also cites about 50% safety-constraint retention under hierarchical truncation on 50 real agent configurations. This rapid decay is the Compaction Cliff. The paper further reports that the same pattern appears across four LLM compactor families and the strongest non-LLM compressor they tested, which supports the claim that the issue is structural rather than model-specific.

Second, it validates the proposed framework. The authors build AgentArtifactCorpus with 396,934 artifacts from 54,628 public GitHub repositories and provide 2,000 type annotations. Their five-type taxonomy covers 97% of real configuration content, which is an important practical check. End-to-end validation on five public corpora shows that typed triage, together with the guard verifier and SafetyMargin classifier, preserves safety constraints better than uniform compaction without giving up too much budget efficiency. The excerpt provided here does not include the full result tables, so the exact gains beyond the headline recall numbers cannot be reproduced faithfully. Still, the main empirical signal is clear: the benefit is concentrated in constraint retention and multi-round robustness, not in generic summarization quality.84d:T47b,For a quick read, start with the introduction and the figure that plots the Compaction Cliff. That section tells you whether the paper’s core diagnosis is convincing. Then read the typed knowledge model in Section 3. The key is not the notation itself, but why the authors insist that compaction, decomposition, and retrieval are one budget-management problem with different safety constraints by type. After that, check the taxonomy coverage analysis and the table defining the five types. This is where the practical plausibility of the framework stands or falls. Finally, inspect the guard verifier and SafetyMargin classifier to judge whether they are narrow engineering heuristics or reusable abstractions.

If you only have half an hour, read the introduction, the type table, the main cliff figure, and the primary experiment table. If you want to go deeper, focus on three questions: whether the taxonomy transfers beyond the artifact distribution they collected, how the counterfactual safety labels are constructed, and whether the typed-memory idea can be moved upstream into training objectives rather than remaining a runtime patch.84e:T52f,Proposes the “agentic compositional generalization” hypothesis: terminal-agent competence is hierarchical, with (i) low-level atomic skills (command execution, file edits, tool usage primitives, domain snippets) and (ii) high-level behaviors that compose and coordinate those skills (task decomposition, planning, verification, error recovery, skill routing). The hypothesis claims SFT (plus pretraining/mid-training priors) primarily equips skills, while RL primarily shapes high-level behaviors via reward signals; generalization requires both skill coverage and reusable behaviors.

Based on this, introduces River (Reward-Integrity Verified Environments for RL), focusing on reward signal quality:
1) Verifier-aware filtering: discard synthetic environments with unreliable or easily exploitable reward/verifier signals, keeping a smaller but cleaner subset.
2) Behavior-level regularization: add training-time regularization targeted at behavior patterns to improve verifier alignment and suppress opportunistic strategies (the exact form should be checked in the method section).

The overall recipe is a division of labor: use SFT/data to fill missing atomic skills; spend RL budget on shaping high-level decision-making and self-check behaviors rather than learning fine-grained skills from sparse terminal rewards.84f:T56c,OptiMAS builds all agents on a shared ReAct-style execution primitive. Each agent alternates between thought, action, and observation. Multi-agent coordination is implemented through a proactive assign-deliver protocol: a parent agent delegates a subtask as a tool call, the sub-agent solves it, and the result is returned as a structured observation. This removes the need for a fixed workflow while still keeping execution structured.

The optimization scope covers prompts, role definitions, skill descriptions, tool access, model choices, and the directed collaboration graph among agents. To avoid unstable free-form code generation, tools are selected from a predefined macro-library. The collaboration graph is constrained to be a DAG, which helps prevent uncontrolled recursive delegation.

The main departure from search-based MAS evolution is the optimization loop. A candidate MAS runs on training tasks, producing full interaction trajectories and task-level metrics. These are converted into a textual loss signal for an agentic optimizer, which induces textual gradients and edits the MAS configuration. A dual-track memory mechanism stores, validates, and retrieves optimization insights across a long evolution horizon. The central contribution is not a new prompt template, but a continuous, memory-supported optimization process for evolving the whole MAS configuration.850:T491,The analysis is set in the continuous-time Markov chain formulation of discrete diffusion. A transition-rate matrix defines the forward noising process and a family of marginal distributions p_t. The reverse process requires concrete scores, i.e. pairwise ratios p_t(y)/p_t(x). SEDD learns these ratios with the score-entropy loss, a weighted Bregman divergence D(a,b)=a/b-1-log(a/b), where the weights are induced by the transition structure.

The main contribution is a minimax treatment of this estimation problem. The paper first derives a lower bound for estimating a single concrete score function under the score-entropy risk. It then constructs a simple estimator, essentially a smoothed or clipped empirical plug-in estimator for the relevant probability ratios, and proves that its risk nearly matches the lower bound. The single-time result is then connected back to SEDD by controlling the time-averaged score-estimation term that appears in KL guarantees for the generated distribution. This complements analyses of tau-leaping, uniformization, Gillespie, or Euler samplers, which study how to simulate the reverse chain once accurate scores are available.851:T4bb,A sampling-based watermark adapted to diffusion decoding.
- Injection: replace position-indexed i.i.d. Gumbel perturbations with a smooth, locally auto-correlated Gumbel field (SAC). The field is constructed via a Gaussian copula so that each coordinate keeps Gumbel marginals (under the paper’s assumptions) while introducing controlled local dependence across neighboring positions.
- Rationale: diffusion decoding refines multiple positions in parallel; independent high-frequency perturbations across neighbors can conflict with local consistency during iterative updates, causing oscillations or incoherence.
- Mechanistic analysis: quantify “latent perturbation roughness” via a local-difference energy and show how positive low-lag dependence reduces this roughness (the paper provides an analytic form contrasting i.i.d. vs SAC).
- Detection: a SAC-aware detector using covariance-aware filtering plus native-sample calibration to manage false positives. A global-offset scan is added as a coarse synchronization recovery tool under mild token–signal misalignment.
Overall, it modifies keyed randomness during DLM decoding and pairs it with a matched detector, rather than changing DLM training.852:T449,The diagnostic pair is a Qwen3.5-27B mentor and a Qwen3.5-4B student. On Multi-IF, linear probes on mentor states show a large freshness gap: stale-state accuracy falls from 0.79 at t=0 to 0.47 at t=512, while fresh-state accuracy stays between 0.76 and 0.80. This drift also affects behavior. Static guidance reduces the 4B student’s constraint satisfaction by 2.5 points below the no-guidance baseline, while refreshing every 16 tokens turns it into a 2.0-point gain over that baseline. Fresh but mismatched memory does not help, which supports the content-freshness explanation. Across 13 datasets, MentorPulse closes 52.2% of the mentor-student gap on the main pair, roughly twice the recovery of the strongest prior alternative. Gains concentrate on long-output tasks. Short outputs often finish before refresh matters, and very large mentor-student capability gaps reduce the margin. The proposed V64 read-distribution indicator helps screen pairs before deployment. Throughput measurements place R=16 among the efficient settings tested against text-to-text guidance on long-output tasks.853:T7ab,方法分成两部分：TDES 和 SABA。

TDES（Target-Distilled Edge Scoring）解决父子错配。现有 DDTree 的边选择近似是 parent-agnostic 的：child token 在不同 parent 下贡献相同，只由该位置的 token probability 决定。GRAFT 改成显式给 edge 打分。做法是从 target model 的验证轨迹里蒸馏一个轻量 edge scorer，输入是相邻位置候选节点及其上下文特征，输出该 parent-child transition 被 target 接受的兼容性分数。然后树构建时不再只按各位置 token 概率乘积选路径，而是结合 edge score 进行 parent-conditional 组装。这样保留了 DLM 一次前向产出候选节点的优点，又补上了“节点之间是否能连成 target 偏好的路径”这一层信息。

从机制上看，这一步很像把 target 的局部条件分布偏好压缩成一个便宜的结构预测器。它不是重新跑 target，也不是让 drafter 变成 AR，而是在 assembly 阶段补一个 learned compatibility model。相比直接增大候选集，这种做法更有效，因为问题不是候选 token 不在，而是树结构把它们接错了。

SABA（State-Aware Budget Allocation）解决固定预算失配。作者把每轮 throughput 看成 accepted gain 与 verification overhead 的函数，学习一个按当前 decoding state 选择 tree budget 的策略。直觉上，easy round 本来 acceptance 就长，再加节点收益很快饱和；hard round 适度扩树更值钱，但也不是越大越好。SABA 用当前轮的状态特征预测不同 budget 下的收益，选 throughput 最优预算。这里的关键不是复杂控制器，而是把“树大小”从静态超参变成在线决策变量。

整体上，GRAFT 没有改 DLM 本身，也没有改 target verification 机制，而是专门优化 DLM-based tree assembly 这一层。这种切分是合理的，因为瓶颈正出在 one-pass future distributions 到 executable tree 的映射。854:T781,GRAFT has two components: TDES and SABA.

TDES, or Target-Distilled Edge Scoring, addresses parent-child mismatch. DDTree is effectively parent-agnostic: a child token contributes the same score regardless of which parent path it extends, because scoring is driven by per-position token probabilities. GRAFT instead learns an explicit edge scorer distilled from target-model traces. The scorer takes candidate parent-child pairs from adjacent positions, together with contextual features, and predicts how compatible that transition is with the target model. Tree assembly then uses these edge scores, rather than only the product of marginal token probabilities, to select target-compatible paths under a node budget.

Mechanistically, this is a lightweight structural predictor that compresses local target preferences into a cheap model. It does not rerun the target and does not force the DLM drafter into autoregressive expansion. It patches the missing conditional dependency at the tree-assembly stage. That is the right intervention point, because the failure mode is not merely missing candidate tokens; it is incorrect attachment among already available candidates.

SABA, or State-Aware Budget Allocation, addresses budget misallocation. The paper models per-round throughput as a trade-off between draft gain and verification cost, then chooses the budget conditioned on the current decoding state. Easy rounds already have long accepted prefixes, so larger trees mostly add cost. Hard rounds benefit more from extra nodes, but only up to a saturation point. SABA predicts the utility of different budgets from state features and selects the throughput-optimal one online.

Overall, GRAFT leaves the DLM and the target verification mechanism unchanged. It focuses specifically on the mapping from one-pass future distributions to an executable draft tree. That decomposition is sensible and technically clean.855:T4a2,The main empirical claim is consistent end-to-end throughput improvement with very small overhead. The paper reports 2.13x to 6.36x throughput gains over baselines across models and datasets, while adding less than 0.5 ms overhead per decoding round. That matters because it suggests the method is not trading away the cost structure of speculative decoding.

The ablations are more informative than the headline numbers. TDES improves MAT, indicating that parent-child compatibility is a real bottleneck for DLM-based tree construction. The paper shows both examples and aggregate evidence that target-compatible tokens are often already present among candidates, but become unusable because they are connected to the wrong parent. SABA shows that a fixed budget is not robust: the throughput-optimal tree size varies substantially across rounds. Dynamic allocation preserves most of the acceptance gain while avoiding unnecessary verification cost.

From a systems perspective, the strongest result is not a single benchmark number but the combination of stable gains across tasks and low added latency. That makes the method more credible as a practical layer on top of DLM drafters.856:T455,This is a skim paper, but the introduction, method section, and ablations are worth reading carefully.

Focus on three things. First, the two failure modes defined in the introduction: parent-child mismatch and budget misallocation. If those are convincing, the rest of the paper follows naturally. Second, inspect how TDES gets supervision from target traces and what features the edge scorer actually uses. The important question is what information is added beyond marginal token probabilities. Third, check whether SABA is optimizing throughput directly or only a proxy such as acceptance length.

For figures and tables, prioritize the mismatch examples, the MAT/throughput comparisons, and the curves showing diminishing returns with larger budgets. Expected reading time is about 25 to 35 minutes. If reading selectively, the problem setup, the two modules, and the ablations are enough. If reading more deeply, two follow-up questions are worth keeping in mind: how target-specific the distilled edge scorer is, and whether the budget policy can generalize to broader adaptive verification strategies.857:T4ff,The method, DPQ (Doubt-Preserving Quantization), is a family of pre-quantization calibration-data recipes rather than a new quantizer. The pipeline is lightweight. First, run the full-precision model on candidate examples. Then select target-aware 'fragile' examples using FP uncertainty signals. Two signal families matter most: high-doubt examples, such as high entropy, low confidence, or small top-2 margin; and answerability-boundary examples, especially for answer/no-answer settings like SQuAD2. These are mixed with generic anchor examples and then passed to an unchanged quantizer such as GPTQ or AWQ. The theoretical argument is modest but useful: if the deployment target puts more mass near decision boundaries, while the calibration mixture is dominated by generic anchors, the optimal calibration set will differ from the one preferred by broad MCQA-style targets. The paper calls this mixture mismatch. The framing is built around two preservation risks: a distributional risk that measures deviation between quantized and FP predictive distributions, and a boundary risk that measures decision flips in low-margin regions, optionally reweighted toward answerability or abstention-heavy inputs. This is a better fit for real systems than accuracy-only calibration.858:T539,The evaluation spans 8 language models, 9 NLP benchmarks, and 22 comparison methods or configurations. The metric suite is broader than standard quantization papers: besides ECE, adaptive ECE, NLL, and Brier score, the authors report FP-behavior metrics such as FP agreement, JSD between quantized and FP predictive distributions, confidence shift, top-two margin drift, and margin correlation. On SQuAD2 they also evaluate answerability-boundary behavior directly. Three findings stand out. First, the best calibration recipe depends strongly on the target. For boundary-sensitive answerability preservation, a high-boundary mixture such as DPQ-s128-r75 works best. For broad MCQA, milder recipes such as DPQ-r50 or single-signal confidence-only / entropy-only selection are often better. Second, accuracy can hide substantial uncertainty drift: some settings preserve top-1 behavior while materially changing confidence and margin structure. Third, preservation signals transfer only partially across quantizers. The post-hoc calibration and AWQ analyses suggest that some useful signals are not tied to one quantizer, but the best score-preservation recipe still remains quantizer-specific. The paper is less about one headline average gain and more about establishing the robustness of this target dependence across models and tasks.859:T758,系统结果是全文最硬的部分。作者在 NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPU 上报告，优化后的 BF16 实现从 4K 上下文开始超过 dense attention；在 32K 时，单层 attention 达到 10.91× speedup。更重要的是，真实的八层 retrofit 在 warm 32K whole-model TTFT 上带来 15.3% 的下降。这个数字没有单层 10× 那么夸张，但更可信，因为它把 attention 之外的层、调度、kernel launch、planning 等开销都算进去了。

训练结果方面，论文做了三种 matched Stage A 对照：Dense continued training、equal-pair-count local sliding、equal-pair-count static-random nonlocal graph。BF1 在三次训练 seed 下都排第一。这里最关键的不是“第一”这个标签，而是控制做得比较细：local sliding 和 random graph 都匹配了 pair budget，因此 BF1 的优势更可能来自拓扑结构，而不是单纯看得更多。换句话说，作者试图回答的是“在相同稀疏预算下，dyadic + first-block 这种图是否比局部或随机图更适合 next-token LM”。

论文还单独讨论了 selected-page decode semantics，并指出在低 batch 场景下，主瓶颈不是 selected-page attention arithmetic，而是 planning lifecycle。这个观察很重要，因为它解释了为什么很多稀疏 decode 方案在 paper benchmark 上很快，落到真实 serving 却收益有限：算子省下来的时间被 page selection、mask planning、runtime orchestration 吃掉了。

从当前给出的正文片段看，底座是 Qwen3-0.6B 几何配置。若全文有 perplexity 或 downstream LM 指标，阅读时要重点看 BF1 retrofit 后相对 dense-continued-training 的差距是否稳定很小，以及这种差距是否随上下文长度扩大。如果长上下文收益建立在明显牺牲短上下文 LM 质量之上，那方法的适用面会窄很多。85a:T723,BF1 is a deterministic, block-aligned causal sparse-attention pattern. The sequence is partitioned into blocks of width b, with the reported public configuration using b = 64. For a query block j, the route includes four components: the causal self block, two exact local predecessor blocks, the first global block, and historical predecessor blocks at dyadic distances, i.e. j - 2^r starting from an offset of four blocks. In short, it is local + global-first + dyadic history.

The paper is explicit that this route is related to earlier log-sparse and dilated designs such as LogSparse Transformer and LongNet. The claimed novelty lies elsewhere: pretrained-model retrofit, matched topology-control experiments, and correctness-gated Blackwell measurements. The correctness-gated part is important. The authors do not only benchmark a fast path; they verify partial blocks, backward gradients, dense-path equivalence, future-token isolation, and opposite-order benchmarks up to 32K, which makes the systems claims more credible.

With fixed block width, each converted layer uses O(n log n) selected token interactions and has O(log n) graph communication depth. The communication-depth argument is the structural reason BF1 should beat pure local sliding windows: long-range information can propagate in logarithmically many sparse hops rather than linearly many local layers. Compared with static random nonlocal graphs, BF1 is deterministic and easier to optimize at the kernel level.

Another sensible design choice is that the paper does not replace all attention layers in the model and call it done. It reports an actual eight-layer retrofit separately from an all-layer timing-only ceiling. That makes the results more realistic for pretrained models, where replacing every layer with a sparse operator can be risky.85b:T74e,The strongest evidence is on the systems side. On an NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPU, the optimized BF16 implementation reportedly crosses dense attention around 4K context length. At 32K, the per-layer attention operator reaches 10.91× speedup. More importantly, the actual eight-layer retrofit reduces warm whole-model TTFT by 15.3% at 32K. That number is much smaller than the per-layer speedup, but it is also much more informative because it includes the rest of the model and runtime overheads.

For language modeling, the paper runs three matched Stage A training comparisons: dense continued training, equal-pair-count local sliding, and equal-pair-count static-random nonlocal graphs. BF1 ranks first in all three matched runs. The key point is not the ranking alone. The controls are designed to keep the sparse budget comparable, so the advantage is more plausibly due to topology rather than simply attending to more pairs. In other words, the paper tries to answer whether a dyadic-plus-first-block graph is a better sparse inductive bias for next-token LM than local-only or random sparse graphs under similar budget.

The decode analysis is also useful. The paper reports selected-page decode semantics and argues that, at low batch, the dominant unresolved cost is planning lifecycle rather than selected-page attention arithmetic. That observation explains why sparse decode methods often look strong in operator benchmarks but deliver limited gains in real serving stacks.

From the provided text, the tested geometry is based on Qwen3-0.6B. When reading the full paper, the most important thing to check is how much LM quality is lost relative to dense continued training, and whether that gap stays small across context lengths. If long-context efficiency comes with a noticeable short-context LM penalty, the deployment envelope becomes narrower.85c:T43b,A good skim order is: operator definition, systems measurements, then matched training controls. Start with the route definition and complexity proposition to understand exactly which blocks are connected and why the selected interactions are O(n log n) with O(log n) communication depth. Then jump to the systems section and focus on the dense crossover point, the 32K per-layer speedup, and the whole-model TTFT for the eight-layer retrofit. Finally, read the matched Stage A training results to see whether topology, sparse budget, and training adaptation are properly disentangled.

If you only have about 25 minutes, prioritize Figure 1, the complexity statement, the correctness-gated Blackwell benchmark tables, and the matched-control training results. Three details are worth deeper inspection: why the first block is used as the global anchor instead of learned global tokens, which eight layers were retrofitted and why, and how the planning-lifecycle overhead is broken down during decode. That last point may be more operationally important than the sparse route itself.85d:T885,方法核心是 trace → execution graph → workload synthesis → deterministic replay → profiling 这一整条链路。

1. 通用 tracing。XPerf 支持对 LangChain、LangGraph 等常见 agent 框架做无侵入或低侵入埋点；对自建 agent 只需很少注释。它记录的不只是 LLM 请求本身，还包括工具调用及其时间信息。

2. 执行图重建。论文用基于 time-span tree 的分析方法，从 traces 中恢复 LLM call、tool call 及其依赖关系，得到 execution graph。这个设计比简单按时间顺序回放更合理，因为 agent 负载里存在并发、等待工具返回、条件分支等结构，只有显式依赖图才能保留真实调度约束。

3. 工作负载合成。作者没有把 benchmark 限定为“原样回放历史 trace”，而是允许在 execution graph 之上改变请求到达模式，构造 online serving、offline batch inference、fixed-concurrency 等不同场景。这一点很关键，因为系统研究需要控制 arrival process，才能比较调度器、batching、cache 策略在不同负载区间的行为。

4. 可复现回放。为保证 replay fidelity，XPerf 对每个 LLM call 提交记录下来的精确 input token IDs，而不是重新 tokenize 文本；这样可以保留 prefix cache 命中行为。必要时还可以强制 serving engine 解码记录过的 output tokens，避免因为模型输出偏移而改变后续控制流。回放时还遵守 execution graph 的依赖顺序，并把工具调用时长纳入时间轴，因此即便被测 serving engine 与 tracing 时不同，负载形态仍尽量贴近原始应用。

5. 细粒度 profiling。系统层面报告 KV cache usage、prefix cache hit rate、token throughput 等；硬件层面报告 GPU tensor core 利用率、memory bandwidth 利用率等。作者强调 profiler 开销很低，避免 benchmark 本身扭曲结果。

和已有工作相比，区别主要在两点：一是它不是只测独立请求，也不是只做 agent 任务完成率；二是它公开、可扩展，并且把“非确定性 agent 行为”通过 trace replay 固定下来，而不是接受 run-to-run variance 作为噪声。85e:T896,The method is a full pipeline: trace collection, execution-graph reconstruction, workload synthesis, deterministic replay, and low-overhead profiling.

1. Application-agnostic tracing. XPerf instruments popular agent frameworks such as LangChain and LangGraph with minimal friction, and supports lightweight annotations for custom agents. It records both LLM calls and tool calls, including timing information.

2. Execution-graph construction. Rather than replaying requests as a flat sequence, XPerf reconstructs dependencies among LLM calls and tool invocations using a time-span-tree-based analysis. This matters because agent workloads contain waiting, branching, and sometimes parallel structure. A dependency graph preserves the scheduling constraints that actually shape serving behavior.

3. Workload synthesis. XPerf does not stop at replaying historical traces. It can alter request arrival patterns over the reconstructed execution graphs to emulate online serving, offline batch inference, and fixed-concurrency settings. This makes the framework useful for controlled systems studies, where arrival processes must be varied independently of application logic.

4. Reproducible replay. For each LLM call, XPerf submits the exact recorded input token IDs, not just the raw text, so prefix-cache behavior is preserved. It can also force the serving engine to decode the recorded output tokens, preventing output drift from changing downstream control flow. Replay respects dependency order in the execution graph and accounts for tool-call durations, so the workload remains realistic even when the target serving engine differs from the one used during trace collection.

5. Fine-grained profiling. XPerf reports serving metrics such as KV-cache usage, prefix-cache hit rate, and token throughput, and hardware metrics such as tensor-core utilization and memory-bandwidth utilization. The profiler is designed to add negligible overhead.

Relative to prior work, the distinction is clear: it is neither an agent-quality benchmark nor a standard serving microbenchmark. Its central idea is to freeze the stochastic control flow of agent applications into a reproducible systems workload.85f:T5aa,The evaluation uses eight agentic applications spanning deep research, coding, Q&A, and general-purpose assistance. The most important results fall into three buckets.

First, replay fidelity. XPerf achieves below 3% mean absolute percentage error in end-to-end request latency for both isolated and concurrent requests. That is the key validation result: if replay were not faithful, the rest of the benchmark would be hard to trust.

Second, workload variance in native agent runs. The paper quantifies how unstable agent execution can be without replay. The headline example is the roughly 70% average variation in the number of LLM calls for the same request under mini-SWE-agent with gpt-oss-120b. This result justifies the entire benchmark design.

Third, bottleneck diagnosis. With replay fixed, XPerf can decompose end-to-end latency and relate it to prefix-cache hits, KV-cache occupancy, token throughput, and GPU compute or bandwidth utilization. The paper’s emphasis is not on claiming one serving engine wins universally, but on showing that the framework can localize where performance is lost under agent-style traffic.

For a foundation-model audience, the useful takeaway is that agent workloads materially change prefix reuse, request-length distributions, and concurrency structure. Optimizations that look effective on standard chat-style benchmarks may behave differently once execution graphs become deeper and more irregular.860:T46f,The conceptual move is to extend JND from human perception to machine receivers. Instead of asking whether a compressed signal is visually indistinguishable, the paper asks whether the downstream policy response remains effectively unchanged. In a VLA setting, the receiver is a language-conditioned robotic policy and the response is a continuous action vector, including translation, rotation, and gripper control. Compression decisions are therefore guided by action sensitivity rather than by visual similarity or attention mass. Based on the introduction, the method likely defines an action-conditioned noticeability metric for visual tokens or intermediate features, estimates a tolerance boundary or compression budget per token, and uses that budget for pruning, reuse, or feature compression. The main contribution appears more conceptual than architectural: safe compression should be defined by receiver behavior. The exact formulation, how action deviation thresholds are estimated, whether an auxiliary calibration model is used, and where compression is applied in the stack would need the full method section to verify.861:T42f,The evaluator state is decomposed into three typed sources: grounds for evidence, norms for decision rules, and authority for whether a rule applies to the case. For an old and revised evaluator state, each source can be taken from either version, producing a 2^3 intervention table called the judgment cube. Each hybrid state is executed through a trusted adjudicator. A source replacement set is a reason when it is sufficient to reproduce the revised verdict from the old state, and it is kept only if it is inclusion-minimal. The complete set of such minimal sufficient replacements is the judgment receipt. A key design choice is the separation between prediction and certification: a model can emit a receipt, but only execution of the counterfactual hybrids certifies it. The work also introduces paired consistency as an evaluation primitive. Control transformations carry known metamorphic relations; when a pair violates the relation, at least one prediction must be wrong. This gives an error lower bound without needing gold labels for every transformed item.862:T818,MGAL is built from long-form reports in the UN Digital Library, using position-aligned multilingual documents so that cross-lingual comparisons are not merely task-level but also semantically and structurally aligned. It covers Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian, and Spanish, with context lengths from 8K to 128K tokens. The benchmark spans four linguistic granularities—word, sentence, paragraph, and document—and includes both closed-ended and open-ended tasks. The paper mentions seven tasks in total, including word-level QA, sentence-level cloze, paragraph filling, document summarization, and translation, with 420 query-response pairs per task per language.

The key design choice is controlled stratification by evidence position. Examples are labeled by whether the relevant evidence appears at the beginning, middle, or end, indexed at both document and paragraph levels. This turns the benchmark into a diagnostic instrument rather than a generic task suite. The choice of UN reports is practical: they provide multilingual parallelism, topic consistency, and relatively regular discourse structure, which makes coherent unit definitions more reliable.

Quality control is manual and strict. The authors state that every query-response pair was audited and flawed samples were removed. This is a smaller-but-cleaner benchmark philosophy, which is appropriate for diagnostic evaluation.

Scoring is hybrid. Closed-ended tasks use precision-oriented reference metrics such as Accuracy, while open-ended tasks use ROUGE-L and, for tasks like paragraph filling where lexical overlap is insufficient, an LLM-as-a-judge setup. That trade-off is sensible: pure reference metrics under-credit semantically correct paraphrases, while pure judge-based evaluation reduces reproducibility. MGAL uses both.

Relative to LongBench, LV-Eval, M4LE, and ONERULER, the novelty is not simply broader coverage. The main difference is tighter control over variables that matter for error attribution: multilingual alignment, discourse granularity, and evidence position.863:T8dd,The experimental section is useful mainly for the error patterns it exposes. The benchmark is evaluated on 12 long-context LLMs. The main findings reported in the paper fall into four groups.

First, performance degrades as granularity becomes coarser. Models do well on word-level tasks, but performance drops at sentence, paragraph, and document levels. This suggests that many current long-context models are stronger at local matching or retrieval than at stable discourse-level integration.

Second, multilingual gaps widen in lower-resource languages. Large open-source and closed-source models are relatively comparable on higher-resource languages, but closed-source systems maintain a clearer lead on lower-resource ones, and smaller open models degrade more sharply. For pretraining, this points to data coverage and multilingual representation quality as major bottlenecks, not just architecture.

Third, position sensitivity remains strong. In sentence cloze, blanks appearing earlier in the text produce the highest error rates, with performance improving toward later positions, consistent with recency-biased attention. The authors also observe an early-option bias: models disproportionately choose earlier answer options such as A or B, indicating reliance on answer-order heuristics rather than evidence verification.

Fourth, the paper identifies two more specific failure modes. One is local semantic crowding: when neighboring sentences share entities, years, or discourse markers, models over-rely on surface overlap and pick the wrong sentence, failing to distinguish functional roles such as background, explanation, or outcome. The other is a fluency-consistency gap: generated outputs are often fluent and stylistically plausible but weakly anchored to the source, leading to factual drift and unsupported claims.

In terms of benchmark scale, MGAL covers 6 languages, 7 tasks, 4 granularities, and contexts from 8K to 128K, with 420 examples per task per language. Even without chasing a single aggregate score, this is enough to support meaningful slicing by granularity and position. The most informative numbers are likely the relative slopes across word→sentence→paragraph→document and begin→middle→end, not the overall ranking.864:T936,UpgradeBench 的设计核心是 longitudinal，而不是静态 pairwise transfer。作者沿着四代 Qwen release 加上一条 continuation release，构造了真实的升级路径；同时补充 OLMo checkpoints，因为 OLMo 的训练关系是公开且可验证的，可以把“是否来自同一训练轨迹”当成受控变量，而不是靠 release note 猜。

它把升级决策拆成四种策略：freeze、port、refresh、retrain。freeze 是继续部署旧 specialist；port 是把旧 adapter 或 task vector 直接迁到新 base；refresh 是用旧 specialist 作为 teacher，对新 base 做便宜的再专门化；retrain 则是从头按固定 recipe 重训 specialist。围绕这四种策略，作者定义并测量了几个关键量：retention、recovery cost、specialization half-life，以及 upgrade tax。这里最重要的是 retention：新策略相对“该 hop 上可达到的最佳 specialist”保留了多少收益。这样定义后，不同 hop、不同任务、不同模型规模可以放到同一坐标系里比较。

任务设置覆盖 6 个应用任务、3 类任务、2 个模型尺度，并把训练侧成本纳入 benchmark 输出，包括 GPU-minutes 和 energy。这个点做得比较扎实，因为很多迁移论文只报最终精度，不报恢复到同等质量需要多少代价，而实际部署决策恰恰取决于这个成本。

方法上它没有提出新的迁移算法，贡献在于实验设计和变量控制。尤其是对 port 的分析很关键：作者直接检验一个业界常见假设——只要新旧模型架构兼容，adapter 原样拷贝就是强基线。实验结论是否定的。决定能否直接拷贝的不是 shape compatibility，而是训练连续性，也就是两个 checkpoint 是否位于同一权重演化轨迹上，以及相距多远。

OLMo 部分进一步把这个结论做成了更接近机制层面的测量。沿同一 documented trajectory 往后走，adapter retention 会随着 continuation token 数增加而下降；文中给出的边界是，从 46B-token continuation 时仍有 0.88–0.99 retention，走到 2.9T-token continuation 时则掉到接近 no-adapter floor。后续 anneal 和 model-soup merge 并没有带来额外主要损伤。这个结果很有信息量，因为它把“能不能 port”从模糊经验变成了 distance budget 的问题。865:T8e6,实验规模不算大，但设计很完整：总共 98 次训练、193 个 evaluation cells，全部在一张 RTX 4090 上完成，并释放了 per-query prediction、bootstrap CI 和 energy log。这个设置说明作者更关心可复现的决策测量，而不是堆大算力。

几个关键结果值得记住。第一，specialist 不一定会很快过时。对于 intent classification，freeze 在 9 个 upgrade hops 上能保留 99%–101% 的 attainable gain；跨四代模型，retrained specialist 的参考分数只移动了 0.2 分，而 zero-shot 却提升了 21 分。这说明某些任务的专门化收益主要来自标签体系、输出格式或任务数据本身，base 进步并不会立刻吞掉这些收益。

第二，另一些任务则明显更依赖 base 能力。text-to-SQL 上，冻结旧 specialist 在单个 hop 上最多会损失 59% 的 attainable gain，而且它相对新 base 的优势会在三代内衰减到零。作者据此提出 data-bound 与 base-bound 的区分：前者 specialist moat 更稳，后者随着 base reasoning 能力增强会更快被追平。

第三，naive porting 可能非常危险。文中给了一个很强的反例：在两个架构完全相同但来自独立预训练运行的 checkpoint 之间，直接贴 adapter 会把 intent classification 从 92.8% 打到 42.9%，甚至低于不用 adapter 的 60.7%。但如果目标模型是同一权重继续预训练得到的 descendant，同样的操作可以保持接近 reference-level accuracy。这一组结果基本否定了“同家族同结构即可直接迁移”的经验法则。

第四，OLMo 验证复现了同样规律，并进一步定位了边界：同一训练轨迹上，随着 continuation 距离增大，port retention 从 0.88–0.99 逐步跌到 no-adapter floor；而 anneal、model soup merge 不是主要破坏源。这个结论对 checkpoint 发布和 continual pretraining 很有现实意义。

文中还给出了一个 half-life 估计：在 7–8B 规模，specialization half-life 大约落在 2–3 个 generation；在 1.5–1.8B 规模，至少观察到一次 crossing，即新 base 的便宜采用策略真正超过旧 specialist。这个量化虽然依赖任务集，但比过去泛泛讨论“要不要升级”要扎实得多。866:T955,The main design choice is longitudinal evaluation rather than static pairwise transfer. The benchmark follows four consecutive Qwen releases plus one continuation release, creating a realistic upgrade path. It also includes OLMo checkpoints, where training relationships are documented rather than inferred, allowing the authors to treat training continuity as a controlled variable.

The benchmark evaluates four upgrade strategies: freeze, port, refresh, and retrain. Freeze keeps serving the old specialist. Port copies the old adapter or task vector onto the new base. Refresh uses the old specialist as a teacher to cheaply re-specialize the new base. Retrain rebuilds the specialist from scratch under a fixed recipe. Around these strategies, the paper defines and measures retention, recovery cost, specialization half-life, and upgrade tax. Retention is especially important: it measures how much of the attainable gain on the target hop is preserved by a cheaper strategy relative to the best specialist achievable there. This makes comparisons across hops, tasks, and model scales much more meaningful.

The benchmark covers six application tasks from three classes, at two model scales, and treats training-side cost as a first-class output, including GPU-minutes and energy. That is a strong design choice because deployment decisions depend on cost-to-recover, not just final accuracy.

The paper does not introduce a new transfer algorithm. Its contribution is experimental structure and variable control. The most important analysis concerns porting. A common practitioner assumption is that if two checkpoints are shape-compatible, direct adapter copying is a strong baseline. The paper shows that this assumption is false. What licenses copying is not architectural shape but training continuity: whether the target checkpoint lies on the same weight trajectory, and how far away it is.
