The post is concise; close reading takes approximately 15-20 minutes. It is useful to compare this account to OpenAI's prior sandbox escape disclosure, noting differences in trigger conditions, model behavior, and defensive gaps across the two incidents.937:T6bd,The method has three main ingredients. The first is an agentic red-teaming harness. Instead of asking the attacker for a single-shot jailbreak prompt, the system gives it a stateful defender_model tool so it can probe, observe, revise, and retry. This matters because realistic prompt injection often depends on multi-turn interaction, tool outputs, file edits, and context-specific weaknesses that a one-pass generator will miss. The second ingredient is environment construction. Existing capability tasks are converted into adversarial RL environments under a realistic threat model: during the defender’s rollout, the attacker may be allowed to edit a designated tool response, a local file region, or another controlled insertion point. This keeps the attack surface close to real agent deployments while making the environment family extensible as production tasks expand. The third ingredient is large-scale self-play RL. The base game rewards the attacker for inducing valid failures and rewards the defender for resisting the attack while still completing its original task. Crucially, training is not limited to a single attacker-defender pair. The attacker is trained against a diverse, simultaneously trained population of strong defenders. That design is meant to prevent overfitting to one defender’s quirks and instead teach the attacker to identify model-specific weaknesses. The paper also frames scaling along three axes: inference-time compute through iterative search in the harness, environment diversity through many red-teaming scenarios and goals, and training compute through a very large RL run. The resulting GPT-Red is therefore a search-based adaptive attacker, not a prompt-template library.938:T51b,The main empirical message is that GPT-Red finds more working attacks, transfers better, and keeps improving with additional test-time compute. The paper reports that it can reliably break prior GPT-5-series models up to GPT-5.5, outperform human red-teamers and a GPT-5.5 baseline on the 2025 IPI Challenge style setting, and transfer to real systems such as an AI-powered vending machine. Another important result is longitudinal rather than benchmark-specific: progressively stronger internal red-team models were used over roughly six months in the training of each production model since GPT-5.2, culminating in GPT-5.6 achieving the strongest robustness profile in their internal evaluation suites. The public text does not fully disclose all run details such as parameter counts, RL steps, or complete absolute metrics, but several experimental signals are especially informative. Test-time scaling is strong, which suggests the attacker is using search and adaptation rather than memorized attack strings. Training against a defender population improves generalization, indicating that the attacker is learning broader attack principles rather than exploiting one model’s idiosyncrasies. Out-of-distribution transfer across goals, harnesses, and target models further supports that interpretation.939:T562,Start with the introduction and the vision section to anchor the paper correctly: the core contribution is a scalable adversarial-data engine for robustness training. Then read the threat-model and environment sections carefully, especially the part describing what the attacker is allowed to modify and when. Those choices determine whether the RL signal reflects realistic failures or synthetic artifacts. The agentic harness section is worth close attention because it explains why state, tools, and iterative interaction are necessary for red-teaming. The self-play training section is the center of the paper; focus on how the defender population is constructed, how rewards are assigned, and how the training setup avoids simple overfitting. Three questions are worth keeping in mind while reading: how valid failures are defined and credited, how population training trades off generalization against stability, and whether the setup is robust to reward hacking where the attacker exploits environment bugs rather than genuine model weaknesses.93a:Tadc,方法上，作者做得比较干净，重点在于把 midtraining 的因果效应尽量从 post-training 中剥离出来。

首先是数据构建。作者从 Anthropic 2026 Constitution 中手工抽取 40 个 constitutional values，并配上定义文本。随后用 Sentence-BERT 对每个 value 做嵌入，计算其与其他 value 的平均余弦相似度，作为 centrality score。两个偏组织性的 value——helpfulness 和 principles hierarchy——因明显更外围，被排除出 curriculum unit selection，剩下 38 个 value。作者再用层次聚类把这些 value 分成四簇，并按平均 centrality 从高到低排序，得到 curriculum 条件下的教学顺序：从更核心的伦理价值，到身份/品格/福祉，再到操作安全与关系行为，最后到认识论完整性与诚实。这里的设计意图很明确：如果价值之间存在结构中心与边缘，那么先教中心、再教外围，可能更利于形成稳定表征。

其次是 2x2 因子设计。两个因素分别是 curriculum ordering 与 deliberative reasoning。也就是：是否按 centrality 导出的顺序组织内容，以及样本中是否包含显式价值推理。这样得到四个 constitutional midtraining 条件，再加一个 replay-only control。语料规模上，摘要给出总 constitutional corpus 为 394M tokens，其中 reasoning 版约 257.6M，no-reasoning 版约 136.8M。这个规模不算大到改变通用能力分布，但足以作为一个有针对性的 midtraining 注入。

第三是模型与训练位置。所有条件都从同一个 Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-Base 出发，这是一个 hybrid Mamba-2/attention 的 MoE 基座模型，总参数 120B、激活参数 12B，预训练约 25T tokens。作者把 constitutional 数据插入 midtraining，而不是混在后续 SFT 里；之后再接一个 value-neutral SFT 阶段，确保如果 CMT 条件优于 control，这个优势主要来自 midtraining 内容，而不是后续监督阶段重复灌输了相同价值。

第四是评测设计。作者不仅看标准 alignment benchmark，还看 self-generated 与 established benchmark 的组合，并覆盖 alignment under pressure、value conflict resolution、blackmail、emergent misalignment 等更接近 disposition 的场景；同时在三个阶段评估：midtraining 后、SFT 后、以及 benign fine-tuning 后。这样可以区分“即时行为变化”和“能否穿过后续训练仍保留”的差异。

从方法论上看，这篇文章最重要的不是某个数据模板，而是实验隔离做得比较到位：同一 base model、同一后续 value-neutral SFT、同一 benign fine-tuning，只改变 midtraining 内容与组织方式，因此更接近在问“midtraining 到底能不能塑形”。93b:T892,实验结论可以概括成三层。

第一层，constitutional midtraining 相比 replay-only control，确实带来更强的 alignment，而且这种提升不是只停留在 midtraining 刚结束时。作者在 post-midtraining、post-SFT、post-benign fine-tuning 三个阶段都做了评测，结论是优势能够延续到后续阶段，说明这不是一层很薄的行为补丁，而更像是对模型倾向的重新塑形。摘要里明确写到 gains are durable and generalizable，并且 survive post-training and benign fine-tuning。

第二层，真正驱动收益的是 content presence。也就是，只要 constitutional 内容在 midtraining 中出现，收益就已经相当显著；相比之下，curriculum ordering 和 deliberative reasoning 的额外增益更像二级效应。这个结论很重要，因为作者原本专门为这两个因素设计了结构化实验，结果却发现“有没有把价值内容放进去”比“怎么排顺序、是否显式写推理”更关键。这对数据工程的启发比对齐口号更实在。

第三层，收益具有一定 OOD 泛化，并且在压力场景下仍可观察。论文列出的评测包括 alignment under pressure、value conflict resolution、blackmail、emergent misalignment，这些都不是简单拒答率能概括的指标，而是在看模型是否形成了更稳定的价值取向。作者还开源了数据和一组 120B checkpoints，方便后续做 mechanistic analysis，这说明他们也把这项工作视为“行为倾向如何进入表征”的起点，而不只是 benchmark 提分。

从当前提供的全文片段里，缺少完整结果表，因此无法安全写出每个 benchmark 的精确分数、提升幅度、训练步数或 token replay 比例。可以确定的硬信息包括：模型是 120B total / 12B active，底座预训练约 25T tokens；constitutional corpus 总计 394M tokens，其中 reasoning 与 no-reasoning 两部分分别约 257.6M 和 136.8M；实验是 2x2 因子设计加 control，并在三个训练阶段做追踪评估。若精读原文，最该补的是各条件在不同 benchmark 上的绝对分数、方差、以及 benign fine-tuning 后保留率。93c:T930,The methodology is notable for trying to isolate the causal effect of midtraining from later alignment stages.

The data pipeline starts from Anthropic’s 2026 Constitution. The authors manually extract 40 constitutional values and pair each with definitional text. They embed each value using Sentence-BERT and compute a centrality score based on mean cosine similarity to all other values. Two organizational values, helpfulness and principles hierarchy, are treated as outliers for curriculum-unit selection and removed from that part of the design, leaving 38 values. These are clustered hierarchically into four groups, ordered by average centrality. This produces a curriculum from more central ethical values toward more peripheral categories such as operational safety and epistemic integrity. The motivation is straightforward: if constitutional values have an internal structure, a central-to-peripheral curriculum may shape representations differently from an unordered presentation.

The training design is a 2x2 factorial setup with two factors: curriculum ordering and deliberative reasoning. This yields four constitutional midtraining conditions, plus a replay-only control. The abstract states that the total constitutional corpus is 394M tokens, with a reasoning-rich version of about 257.6M tokens and a no-reasoning version of about 136.8M tokens.

All conditions start from the same base model, Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-Base, a hybrid Mamba-2/attention MoE model with 120B total parameters and 12B active parameters, pretrained on roughly 25T tokens. The constitutional intervention is inserted during midtraining, not folded into later SFT. After that, the authors apply a value-neutral SFT stage so that any downstream advantage can be attributed primarily to midtraining rather than repeated value injection during supervised tuning.

The evaluation setup is also carefully chosen. The paper tests not only standard alignment benchmarks but also self-generated and established suites covering alignment under pressure, value conflict resolution, blackmail, and emergent misalignment. Importantly, evaluation is performed at three stages: immediately after midtraining, after SFT, and after benign fine-tuning. That allows the paper to distinguish immediate behavioral effects from durable changes that survive later training.93d:T777,The experimental findings have three main layers.

First, constitutional midtraining consistently outperforms the replay-only control, and the advantage is not limited to the checkpoint right after midtraining. The gains remain visible after value-neutral SFT and after benign fine-tuning on an unrelated task. That is the core evidence that the intervention is not merely a thin post-hoc behavior patch.

Second, the dominant factor is content presence. Once constitutional content is included in midtraining, alignment improves substantially. By comparison, curriculum ordering and explicit deliberative reasoning appear to have smaller, secondary effects. This is one of the most useful takeaways in the paper because the study was explicitly designed to test those structural factors, yet the strongest signal comes from the presence of the value-bearing content itself.

Third, the gains generalize beyond narrow in-distribution settings. The evaluation suite includes pressure scenarios, value conflicts, blackmail, and emergent misalignment, which probe behavioral disposition more deeply than simple refusal metrics. The authors also release the data and matched 120B checkpoints, making the work useful for later mechanistic studies of how alignment-relevant content changes internal representations.

From the provided full-text excerpt, the detailed result tables are not available, so it would be unsafe to fabricate exact benchmark scores, effect sizes, or training-step counts. The hard facts that are visible are: a 120B total / 12B active base model, about 25T pretraining tokens, a 394M-token constitutional corpus, a 2x2 factorial design plus control, and evaluation at three stages including post-benign-fine-tuning durability checks. In a full read, the most important numbers to extract would be absolute benchmark scores, variance across conditions, and retention after benign fine-tuning.93e:T606,This one deserves a close read. Start with the introduction, focusing on how the paper links shallow post-training alignment, alignment elasticity, and midtraining as an intervention point. That framing matters because the paper’s contribution depends on whether the post-training confound is truly controlled.

Then go straight to the method section. Three parts deserve careful attention: how the constitutional values are extracted and filtered, how centrality and clustering define the curriculum, and how the 2x2 factorial design is combined with value-neutral SFT to isolate the effect of midtraining. After that, compare the main effects of content presence, curriculum, and reasoning, and check whether the paper reports uncertainty estimates or multiple seeds.

Two deeper questions are worth keeping in mind. Why does content presence matter more than reasoning format? And does midtraining change shallow response templates or deeper internal representations? The released checkpoints suggest that the latter question may become the more important one over time.

If you already know the midtraining and alignment literature, a serious read should take about 60 to 90 minutes. If you want to build on the setup, the method and results sections both merit detailed study.93f:T44c,The design decomposes the repair packet into four retry conditions with matched budgets. In resample, the model sees only the original prompt again. In placebo, it sees its failed program plus a content-free notice that it was wrong. In feedback, it also receives the actual failing input, expected output, and observed output. In reflect, it is asked to diagnose the failure in prose before rewriting the code. This separates the value of another draw, self-exposure, diagnostic feedback, and verbal reflection. Retry attempts use temperature 0.8; the authors explicitly avoid greedy retry because it would return byte-identical programs and make resampling meaningless. Each trajectory allows up to k=8 attempts, and pass@1 for all k≤8 is read from the same trajectory. Paired contrasts are tested with exact McNemar tests, task-level bootstrap intervals, and Holm correction. The proposed mechanism is anchoring: once the failed program is in the context, the next sample tends to stay near it and perform local edits, while blind resampling can explore a different region of the solution space.940:T464,The main experiments use Qwen2.5-Coder Instruct at 1.5B, 3B, and 7B, quantized as Q4_K_M and run locally on a single 6GB consumer GPU. MBPP+ with 378 tasks is the primary benchmark. HumanEval+ with 164 tasks is secondary and is treated as underpowered because each cell has only about 32–75 failing tasks, compared with 110–164 on MBPP+. On MBPP+, blind resampling reaches the highest pass rate at 1.5B and 3B, and is statistically tied with the best condition at 7B. The diagnostic content of execution feedback is not detectable: feedback minus placebo is +0.000, +0.026, and +0.008 across the three model sizes, with no significant effect. Self-exposure is harmful at smaller scales: placebo minus resample is -0.061 at 1.5B with p=0.006, and -0.069 at 3B with p<0.001. The abstract also reports that blind resampling uses 2.5–5.5 times fewer tokens than self-repair-style conditions. Reflection weakens the anchor but does not pay for itself. Additional checks rule out prompt length, quantization, and model family as sufficient explanations, and suggest that the penalty is governed by baseline model capability.941:T517,The work first proposes Routing Slot Memories (RSM), a unifying framework that decomposes fixed-size memory updates into two independent dimensions: (1) write routing, which selects a subset of memory slots to write new content to; (2) slot-wise decay, which applies forgetting operators only to slots that receive new writes, leaving unselected slots completely untouched with no overwrites or decay. Under this framework, SSMs correspond to the extreme of dense full-slot writes with global gradual decay, while SWA corresponds to the extreme of deterministic round-robin single-slot writes with hard eviction (unselected slots retain content until overwritten on their rotation). Raven is a concrete RSM instantiation that uses learned, input-dependent sparse routing to select a small subset of slots per step—neither writing to all slots nor rotating deterministically through a single slot. New content is only written to selected slots, and learnable decay is applied exclusively to these updated slots, while unselected slots retain their content indefinitely without any update or decay. The Raven block requires no auxiliary convolution or sliding-window attention layers; a single RSM layer supports both persistent memory and precise recall while maintaining strict linear time complexity.942:T843,方法分三层：
1）训练层：不再训练一个通用 drafter，而是按负载分布做专门化。MTP（multi-token prediction）drafter 用更“对话/开放域”的高熵数据强化，追求短深度下的稳定接受；block-parallel diffusion drafter 用代码/数学样本强化，追求长可预测 span 的高接受与高摊销。这里的关键不是简单换数据集，而是把“接受率随深度衰减的形状”当作训练目标的隐含约束：高熵任务深度收益递减，低熵任务深度收益更线性。
2）架构层：提出 DFly，基于 DFlash 的 block-diffusion drafter 做两点改造：

3）推理/系统层：D-cut 把“验证更多 token”视为共享的 batch 资源。在线根据：a）不同请求当前前缀的期望接受收益（可理解为多验证一位能带来多少期望前进步长），b）profile 得到的 runtime cost model（并发、并行策略、硬件、目标模型结构导致的边际验证成本变化），在并发请求间重新分配验证深度：资源充裕时保留更长 draft，资源紧张时更激进裁剪低价值 suffix。
配套工程：AngelSpec 训练框架把 target hidden states 的生成与训练解耦（推理引擎流式产出 hidden states 给训练 worker），支持 MTP 的 on-policy TTT rollout、长上下文训练、以及 DFly 的逐层 target-conditioning 与可插拔 AR head，并提供在训 acceptance 评测服务，避免只看离线 loss。943:T60c,Three layers:
1) Training specialization: instead of one universal drafter trained on an averaged mixture, train an MTP drafter on diverse conversation-heavy data (optimize short-depth acceptance under high entropy) and a block-parallel diffusion drafter on code/math-heavy data (optimize long-span acceptance where structure is tight).
2) DFly architecture (building on DFlash):
  - Hybrid target-conditioning backbone: combines a globally transformed target context with layer-specific target views, so different draft layers can consume target features at appropriate abstraction levels.
  - Predecessor-conditioned autoregressive head: keeps a single-pass parallel backbone but conditions each position’s output on the previously selected token, converting per-position marginals into prefix-conditioned predictions to improve intra-block dependency and suffix coherence.
3) Serving-time adaptation (D-cut): treats target verification as a shared batch-level resource. It dynamically chooses/prunes verification depth per request based on (i) expected acceptance utility and (ii) a profiled runtime cost model that captures concurrency, parallelism strategy, model architecture, and hardware effects.
Infrastructure (AngelSpec): disaggregates target hidden-state generation (inference engines) from training workers via streaming; supports MTP on-policy rollouts inside the training step, long-context packing, per-layer target conditioning, pluggable AR heads, and an evaluation server that measures true acceptance behavior during training.944:T982,技术上，CaRE 的重点不是复杂算法，而是把评测协议做成一个可执行、可扩展、可审计的框架。核心实现是统一的 RemaskingSampler，围绕四个设计原则展开。其一，自动记录每次生成的 actual NFE，而不是接受论文里常见的 nominal step 作为 compute proxy。这个点很关键，因为不同 remasking 策略会重复 mask 已决定 token，导致同样 256 nominal steps 下，真实 NFE 可以从 128 到 513，相差约 4 倍。其二，默认同时报告四个指标：用 Llama-3-8B 计算的 PPL、MAUVE、Self-BLEU、Distinct-3。作者明确把“单指标最优”视为不充分证据，因为不同指标衡量的是流畅性、分布匹配和表面多样性的不同侧面。其三，把 unmask_temp 设为必填超参，并要求 sweep，而不是像以往工作那样固定一个温度后直接比较策略。其四，加入字符级英文过滤器，避免生成中混入非目标语言文本后污染 PPL/MAUVE 等统计。

协议层面，作者提出七点规范，核心精神是三件事：compute 要按 actual NFE 对齐，stochasticity 要显式 sweep，指标要成组报告而不是挑一个最有利的。实验覆盖 12 个 open-weight MDLM，参数规模从 150M 到 8B，包含 dense、MoE 和 soft-masked 变体；任务包括 OpenWebText/LM1B 上的 unconditional generation、HumanEval 代码生成，以及 GSM8K、HellaSwag、BBH 的 log-likelihood 评测。后面三类任务被作者当作 sampling-invariant sanity check，用来确认某些结论不是纯采样噪声。

论文最有信息量的技术发现来自交互分析。作者不是只做 pairwise 对比，而是用三因素 ANOVA 分析 strategy、temperature、compute 的联合作用。结果显示 temperature 是主导因素，效应量 η²=0.91；strategy × temperature 交互也显著，η²=0.47。这说明“某策略优于另一策略”如果不附带温度和 compute 条件，结论几乎没有可移植性。进一步地，作者区分了 stochastic unmasking 带来的表面多样性提升，与 high-entropy remasking 在高预算下造成的 persistent token churn。后者会让 token 持续被重新 mask / 重新决定，表面上增加变化，实际上缩窄了分布覆盖，因此 MAUVE 反而下降。这个机制解释了为什么一些论文在高温或高步数下报告 high-entropy 类策略更好，而另一些论文得到相反结论。945:T489,Its value to pretraining research is mostly infrastructural but still substantial. First, MDLMs are now close enough to autoregressive LMs that evaluation noise can distort conclusions about the paradigm itself. If remasking papers are not compute-matched and temperature-controlled, later claims about inference efficiency, training targets, or AR-vs-MDLM trade-offs rest on unstable ground. Second, the paper reframes inference improvements under real compute accounting. That matters beyond MDLMs: any non-AR generation method can look better if nominal steps are used as a loose proxy for cost. Third, the work surfaces a concrete interaction that had not been isolated before: stochastic unmasking is the main driver of diversity gains, while informed or high-entropy remasking can erase those gains at higher compute budgets through persistent token churn. That finding is immediately relevant for MDLM decoding design and may also inform training-time choices about denoising trajectories. The contribution is best understood as a standardization effort in the spirit of Clean-FID or SacreBLEU: not a new model, but a correction of the measurement layer.946:T8d4,Technically, CaRE is a protocol and software framework centered on a unified RemaskingSampler. The design is intentionally simple, but the choices are sharp. First, it automatically tracks actual NFE per generation. This is the key correction: strategies that remask already decided tokens incur extra forward passes, so the same nominal step budget can hide a large compute gap. Second, the framework reports four default metrics together: PPL scored by Llama-3-8B, MAUVE, Self-BLEU, and Distinct-3. The paper treats single-metric wins as insufficient because these metrics capture different aspects of generation quality and diversity. Third, unmask_temp is made a required hyperparameter with sweep support, rather than an incidental setting buried in an appendix. Fourth, a character-level English filter is added to reduce contamination from off-target language outputs when computing distributional metrics.

The protocol itself is built around three principles: compare strategies at matched actual NFE, sweep stochasticity explicitly, and report a metric bundle rather than cherry-picking one score. The empirical scope is broad enough to make the standard credible: 12 open-weight MDLMs from 150M to 8B parameters, including dense, MoE, and soft-masked variants; unconditional generation on OpenWebText and LM1B; code generation on HumanEval; and log-likelihood evaluations on GSM8K, HellaSwag, and BBH as sampling-invariant sanity checks.

The most informative methodological contribution is the interaction analysis. Instead of pairwise comparisons only, the authors run a three-way ANOVA over strategy, temperature, and compute. Temperature dominates with effect size η²=0.91, and the strategy × temperature interaction is also large and significant at η²=0.47. This means a statement like “strategy A is better than strategy B” is not portable unless compute and temperature are specified. The paper then interprets the failure mode of high-entropy remasking through persistent token churn: repeated remasking keeps tokens unstable, which can preserve superficial variation while narrowing true distributional coverage. That mechanism explains why prior papers could report contradictory rankings under different temperatures and budgets.947:T742,Several quantitative results carry most of the paper’s weight. First, the compute mismatch is large. At nominal 256 steps, actual NFE ranges from 128 for the no-remasking baseline to 513 for running_conf., roughly a 4x spread. This alone shows that many prior comparisons were not compute-fair. Second, once actual NFE is fixed at {128, 256, 512}, the none strategy dominates MAUVE at every budget, and the gap grows with more compute. So some remasking methods that looked stronger under nominal-step comparisons lose their advantage when real cost is matched. Third, temperature has an outsized effect: a single temperature change can raise MAUVE from 0.66 to 0.98, a gain of 0.32, larger than the maximum gap between any two strategies at the same temperature. That scale makes unswept temperature settings a major source of false conclusions. Fourth, at higher compute budgets, high-entropy remasking removes 0.296 MAUVE points of the diversity benefit from stochastic unmasking, with p=0.020. The paper attributes this to token churn rather than a generic randomness issue.

The ranking reversals are not limited to open-ended generation. The paper reports that strategy rankings also flip on HumanEval when actual NFE is equalized, which matters because it shows the issue extends to code generation. For GSM8K, HellaSwag, and BBH, the authors use log-likelihood scoring mainly as a sanity check to separate sampling effects from changes in the underlying conditional model. One concrete number mentioned in the paper is that under 128 deterministic steps, high_entropy reaches MAUVE 0.612 and is best in that local setting, but that advantage is not stable once compute, temperature, or metric changes. The broader conclusion is not that one strategy wins universally, but that rankings are fragile unless all three confounds are jointly controlled.948:T5c9,Start with the introduction and the motivating figure that shows contradictory rankings across recent remasking papers. Each round sweeps one category's ratio candidates while fixing others (with renormalization) and selects the value with best validation performance, avoiding multi-variable confounding. Points for further exploration: how validation set selection for inter-class search avoids overfitting, integration of difficulty scores with data curriculum learning, and the boundary of entropy term weight's suppression effect on redundant data.94c:T74c,技术路线是一个端到端 CuraWeb curation framework。原始数据来自 2013–2024 年的 12 年 Common Crawl snapshots。先用 Resiliparse 从 WARC 抽取正文，去掉 header、footer 和广告噪声；再用 FastText 语言分类器保留 English confidence > 0.5 的文档；exact dedup 用全局 SHA-256 文档哈希；随后用扩展 URL blacklist 去掉 spam 和成人内容域。这个基础漏斗从 184.9B raw documents 压到 41.4B unique documents，保留率 22.4%；URL blacklist 后得到 39.1B documents，保留率 94.5%。

核心创新有三块。第一是 dual-track cleaning。规则过滤不再使用统一阈值，而是根据 domain 调整阈值，避免数学、代码等高价值领域因符号密度、长度分布或格式特征被误杀。模型驱动部分使用 data understanding model 给文档打多维标签，包括 writing quality、content value 和 domain tags。第二是 hybrid deduplication。传统 n-gram / LSH 能处理显性重复，但对两类 hidden redundancy 不够：一种是 templatized clusters，即页面结构高度相同但局部参数不同；另一种是 redundant crawling，即相似度刚好落在 LSH 阈值下方的重复抓取。CuraWeb 用 soft semantic deduplication 和 weighted voting：不是单条相似边超过阈值就删除，而是累计多个相似边的 penalty score，超过总阈值才判为冗余。这样比硬阈值更不容易误删边界样本。第三是 multi-objective sampling。writing quality 用 harmonic mean 聚合，因为任何一个严重缺陷都应显著拉低分数；content value 用线性求和，因为专业性、信息密度等维度可以累加贡献；再把质量指标与 diversity score 结合，保证 domain coverage。最终采用 Power Sampling，提高高信息量文档的抽样概率，同时不把分布完全压成单一高分区域。94d:T7fa,The pipeline starts from twelve years of Common Crawl snapshots from 2013 to 2024. Main-body text is extracted from WARC files with Resiliparse, removing headers, footers, and advertisement noise. A FastText language classifier keeps English documents with confidence above 0.5. Global SHA-256 hashing performs exact document deduplication, reducing 184.9B raw documents to 41.4B unique documents, a 22.4% retention rate. An extended URL blacklist then removes spam and adult domains, leaving 39.1B documents with a 94.5% retention rate after that stage.

The main design has three components. First, dual-track cleaning combines domain-aware heuristic rules with model-driven document understanding. Instead of applying uniform thresholds, the rules are calibrated per domain so that math, code, and other structurally unusual but useful content are not removed simply because they violate generic web-text statistics. A data understanding model annotates documents with multi-aspect writing quality, content value, and domain tags. Second, hybrid deduplication combines n-gram-style filtering with semantic deduplication. The paper highlights two hard cases: templatized clusters, where pages share a structural skeleton but differ in local parameters, and redundant crawling cases that fall just below an LSH threshold. CuraWeb uses a soft semantic deduplication strategy based on weighted voting over multiple similarity edges. A document is removed only when its accumulated penalty exceeds a threshold, which reduces over-filtering compared with hard similarity cutoffs. Third, multi-objective sampling combines writing quality, content value, and diversity. Writing quality is aggregated with a harmonic mean to penalize severe defects on any single dimension. Content value is summed linearly to reward expertise and information density. A diversity score is added to preserve domain coverage, and Power Sampling increases the probability of selecting high-value documents without collapsing the sample into a narrow high-score slice.94e:T4bc,The post is a position statement rather than a technical contribution, but its policy ranking is precise. First, restrict access to advanced chips and chipmaking equipment for authoritarian states, and crack down on smuggling and evasion, because scaling laws imply that without sufficient chips it is not possible to train models beyond the U.S. frontier. Second, target industrial-scale distillation, because distillation is far more compute-efficient than training from scratch and can compress the capability gap to a few months even under chip constraints; in the author's view, this matters much more than whether weights are open or closed. Third, require mandatory pre-release safety testing for all sufficiently capable models, open or closed, regardless of origin, with emphasis on cyber, biological, and alignment risks. The author argues that banning U.S. companies from using Chinese open weights does not address misuse, because malicious actors are unlikely to be regulated U.S. businesses. Open weights do introduce unique safety problems—weak guardrail enforcement, limited monitoring, and irreversible release—but the proposed response is capability-based testing rather than a blanket ban.94f:T7d9,技术路线可以拆成四块。第一块是长上下文与深层信息流。Kimi Delta Attention 负责长序列混合，周期性插入 Gated MLA 层保留全局交互；这说明他们没有完全放弃 attention，而是用更便宜的序列混合主干配合稀疏的全局 attention 校正。Attention Residuals 则让每层可以选择性访问所有前层表示，缓解超深网络中的信息衰减与优化困难。第二块是超大规模稀疏 MoE。K3 使用 Stable LatentMoE，把 routed expert 空间扩到 896 个，每个 token 激活 16 个 expert，外加 shared expert。这里的难点不是 MoE 结构本身，而是极高稀疏度下的训练稳定性与负载均衡。报告提到用 normalization、SiTU-GLU 和 Quantile Balancing 来稳定路由与激活分布，目标是既扩大专家容量，又避免 router collapse、负载失衡和训练震荡。第三块是训练与数据 recipe。公开文本里没有把所有数据细节完全展开，但明确把 refined data and training recipes 作为 2.5× scaling efficiency 的组成部分，而不是把收益全部归因于架构。这一点很重要，因为大模型报告常把数据因素弱化。第四块是 post-training 与基础设施协同。RL 覆盖 general、agentic、coding 和多种 reasoning effort level，训练环境包括可验证搜索、专业知识工作、软件工程、kernel optimization、vision-in-the-loop 工具使用、persistent assistant workflow 等。不同领域和 effort 的策略最后通过 multi-teacher on-policy distillation 合并到统一模型。系统侧则分别为 KDA、2.8T MoE 预训练、百万 token agentic RL 和 serving 做了专门设计：如 fused kernels、KDA context parallelism、state-aware prefix caching、MoonEP 的静态 shape 与零拷贝通信、外部 KV 保留、partial rollout、可恢复 microVM sandbox 等。这里最值得注意的是，他们把“能否训练和运行长轨迹 RL”当成模型设计的一部分，而不是后处理问题。950:T848,The technical design has four major pieces. First is long-context and deep information flow. This suggests they do not fully abandon attention; instead they use a cheaper sequence-mixing backbone plus sparse global correction. Attention Residuals let each layer selectively access representations from all previous layers, which is meant to reduce information decay and optimization difficulty in very deep networks. A full careful read likely takes 1.5 to 2.5 hours because this is a large-stack technical report rather than a narrow method paper.953:T426,Two desirable properties for group-based RL optimizers are first formalized: (P1) Gradient unbiasedness — the gradient estimator is an unbiased estimate of the true policy gradient; (P2) Length invariance — each trajectory's total contribution to gradient updates is independent of its length. An impossibility theorem is then proven: under outcome rewards (scalar reward assigned only at generation end, e.g. 0/1 for correctness) and group-relative baselines, no length-based weighting function can satisfy both P1 and P2 simultaneously. A parametric family of weighting functions f_α(L) = L^(α-1) (α ∈ [0,1]) characterizes the full tradeoff spectrum: α=0 recovers GRPO (length-normalized, length-invariant but gradient-biased), α=1 recovers Dr. GRPO (no length normalization, gradient-unbiased but length-biased). Quantitative analysis shows that for two trajectories with length ratio r, the longer trajectory captures r/(1+r) of the total gradient signal under Dr. GRPO, meaning length bias can be substantial even for moderate length differences.954:T56c,The experimental design is intentionally simple. Invisible reasoning is defined as consequential computation in internal representations during the forward pass without an interpretable trace in output tokens. The authors insert a fixed filler-token sequence before the model’s answer. The key control is that the same filler sequence is used for every problem, so it cannot encode information about a particular question or answer at the token level. In evaluation, few-shot examples include the question, an assistant-side filler span, and the ground-truth answer; the test query is also followed by an assistant-side filler prefill before the model generates the answer. The baseline uses the same setup without filler. The paper proposes three diagnostic criteria: performance improves with filler tokens; the improvement depends on filler content; and filler preferences differ across models. These criteria make it less plausible that the effect comes from ordinary semantic prompting, and more plausible that model-specific representations and attention dynamics are being used. The tasks are short and verifiable: 4-digit multiplication, 5-to-7-step nested arithmetic, and counting distinct assigned variables in code snippets. The authors are careful not to reduce the mechanism to “more compute” alone, since inserting tokens also changes positions and attention patterns.955:T461,The study evaluates 13 frontier language models. Many models benefit from filler tokens on the synthetic reasoning tasks, with gains up to about 13 percentage points. The gain depends strongly on the filler sequence, and the best filler content varies across models. This model-specific variation suggests that the effect is tied to internal token representations, positional interactions, and learned computation patterns rather than to a shared human-readable meaning of the filler. A safety-relevant experiment adds a hidden modular arithmetic objective alongside the primary task. For Claude Opus 4.5, filler tokens allow the model to satisfy the hidden constraint without sacrificing primary-task accuracy, while the extra objective remains invisible in the output text. The training experiments are more mixed: RL on Qwen3-235B induces strong preferences over filler content, but the filler-token benefit does not persist robustly at test time; supervised fine-tuning also fails to transfer it. The capability appears to exist in current models, but making it stable through straightforward RL or SFT is not solved.956:T965,技术路线很扎实，核心在于把“局部近似是否有效”做成可直接检验的实验。模型是 150M 参数 Transformer，在 FineWeb 上训练 3B tokens，并每 10% 训练进度保存 checkpoint。围绕每个 checkpoint，作者构造两类代理目标。prox 是对网络输出做一阶线性化，但保留交叉熵，因此等价于 NTK 参数化下的多类 logistic regression；quad 则进一步把这个目标在 checkpoint 处做二阶展开，得到凸二次目标。然后从同一个 checkpoint 出发，在相同数据流和训练设置下继续训练这些代理模型，并与原始非线性模型的真实轨迹比较。这里关键不是只比较 loss 数值，而是比较在一个非平凡时间窗口内，代理模型是否能复现真实训练的下降趋势和超参敏感性。

在谱分析部分，作者估计 Hessian 和 Gauss-Newton 矩阵的谱，并分别考察原始参数空间和 Adam 预条件后的谱。方法上使用很深的 Lanczos quadrature probe，并给出误差带，分辨率覆盖约六个数量级。这一点很重要，因为很多过去的谱结论只看头部几个特征值，难以判断尾部是否真有稳定幂律。作者发现谱存在清晰的 head-tail 分裂：head 的大小与 vocab size 对齐，且主要来自 unembedding；tail 呈 power law，并且在不同 batch size 下几乎重合，Adam 预条件也不改变其形状，只改变某些尺度关系。基于这些谱，作者进一步估计 source exponent β 和 capacity exponent α，在可分辨尾部中得到 α≈1，而 β<1，不满足一些文献常用的可求和假设。这意味着若用经典 inverse-problem 或 kernel-regression 风格的谱假设来分析 LLM 训练，很多前提并不成立。

稳定性分析则把理论预测和真实 blow-up 实验对上。作者从多个 checkpoint 出发，用预条件 SGD 在学习率和 batch size 的乘子网格上做扫描，直接测哪些组合会发散，再与线性稳定性分析给出的边界比较。这里的“预条件 SGD”是为了更贴近 Adam 类训练的局部线性动力学。结果显示，小中 batch 下，噪声会把系统推到 stochastic edge-of-stability；大 batch 下则更接近经典线性理论中的 deterministic edge。这个设计的好处是，它没有把 edge-of-stability 当作单一现象，而是区分了噪声主导和曲率主导两种机制。957:T500,The contribution is important less as a new optimizer and more as a validation layer for a large body of optimization reasoning. First, it shows that local Taylor proxies are not merely infinitesimal approximations: in a 150M-parameter transformer trained on 3B tokens, they can remain predictive over windows as long as roughly 10% of total training, with noticeably better agreement later in training. That gives empirical support to using quadratic analyses for practical pretraining questions. Second, the spectral measurements are unusually informative: the spectrum separates into a head whose size is set by vocabulary and dominated by the unembedding layer, and a power-law tail that is nearly invariant across batch sizes and largely unaffected by Adam preconditioning. That is directly relevant to output-layer parameterization, tokenizer/vocabulary choices, and curvature structure. Third, the stability analysis sharpens the edge-of-stability story: small and medium batches operate in a noise-dominated stochastic edge regime, while large batches move toward the deterministic edge predicted by linear theory. The broader implication is that LLM training is typically run close to stability limits regardless of batch size, but the mechanism changes with noise scale.958:T9e0,The methodology is strong because the paper turns a vague theoretical claim into a falsifiable training experiment. The base model is a 150M transformer trained on 3B FineWeb tokens, with checkpoints saved every 10% of training. Around each checkpoint, the authors build two local proxies. The first, prox, linearizes the network outputs while keeping the cross-entropy objective; this is equivalent to multiclass logistic regression in the NTK parameterization. The second, quad, further takes a second-order Taylor expansion of that objective, yielding a convex quadratic problem. Starting from the same checkpoint, they continue training these proxy systems and compare them against the original nonlinear trajectory under matched conditions. The key point is not just local loss fitting at a single step, but whether the proxies reproduce meaningful optimization behavior over a sizable future window.

For geometry, the paper estimates Hessian and Gauss-Newton spectra along training, both before and after Adam-style preconditioning. The estimation uses very deep Lanczos quadrature probes with error bands, resolving the spectrum over roughly six orders of magnitude. This is a major practical detail: many prior empirical studies only resolve the top few eigenvalues, which is insufficient for claims about tail behavior. The resulting picture is a clear head-tail split. The head is tied to vocabulary size and is dominated by the unembedding layer. The tail follows a power law and appears universal in the sense that it is nearly identical across batch sizes and not materially altered by Adam preconditioning. Using these curves, the authors estimate a capacity exponent around alpha ≈ 1 in the resolvable tail and a source exponent beta < 1, contradicting summability assumptions that appear in parts of the optimization and inverse-problems literature.

For stability, the paper combines theory with direct blow-up tests. From multiple checkpoints, it runs preconditioned SGD over a grid of learning-rate and batch-size multipliers, measuring which settings diverge and comparing the observed boundary to linear stability predictions. This is a good design choice because it tests the practical content of edge-of-stability theory rather than treating it as a metaphor. The results separate two regimes: stochastic edge of stability at small to medium batch sizes, where gradient noise is essential, and deterministic edge of stability at large batch sizes, where classical linear analysis becomes more accurate.959:T7ee,The main experiments use a 150M-parameter transformer trained on 3B FineWeb tokens. Checkpoints are saved every 10% of training, and around each checkpoint the authors construct the prox and quad local surrogates. The central empirical result is that both surrogates can track the real optimization trajectory over windows up to about 10% of total training, with substantially better agreement later in training than early on. The paper does not claim that a single quadratic model explains the entire run; the claim is more precise and more useful: over a practically meaningful local horizon, the approximation is predictive enough to support analysis.

The spectral experiments estimate Hessian and Gauss-Newton spectra with deep Lanczos probes over six orders of magnitude. Three observations stand out. First, the spectral head has a size linked to vocabulary and is dominated by the unembedding layer, indicating that the output layer contributes a distinct curvature structure. Second, the tail follows a stable power law and is almost unchanged across batch sizes. Third, Adam preconditioning does not remove this tail structure, suggesting that preconditioning does not whiten the problem into something close to isotropic geometry. From the measured spectra, the paper estimates a capacity exponent alpha ≈ 1 and a source exponent beta < 1 in the resolvable tail, which runs against common summability assumptions.

The stability experiments scan learning-rate and batch-size multipliers to map divergence boundaries. The outcome is that training spends most of its time near the edge of stability. At small and medium batch sizes, the regime is noise-dominated and better described as a stochastic edge of stability. At large batch sizes, the observed boundary aligns more closely with deterministic linear stability theory. The predictive quality of the linearized analysis also improves later in training, matching the earlier observation that local Taylor models become more accurate toward the end of pretraining.95a:T6f2,A good reading order is: first verify that the local approximation is genuinely predictive, then study the spectral structure, then read the stability section.

Start with the introduction and the main experiments in Section 3. Focus on how prox and quad are defined, how the checkpoint-based continuation experiments are set up, and what exactly it means for a proxy to remain predictive over a 10%-of-training window. That section determines whether the rest of the paper should be taken as more than a theoretical analogy.

Then read Section 4 carefully. The most important figures are the Hessian and Gauss-Newton spectra, the before/after-Adam comparisons, and the evidence for the head-tail split. Two questions are worth keeping in mind. Why is the spectral head so tightly linked to vocabulary size and the unembedding layer? And why is the power-law tail so insensitive to batch size and Adam preconditioning? Those observations have implications for output-layer design, tokenizer/vocabulary choices, and what parts of optimization geometry are intrinsic versus optimizer-induced.

Finally, read Section 5 on stability. Pay attention to how blow-up is operationally defined, how the learning-rate/batch-size multiplier grid is constructed, and how the measured instability boundary compares to linear predictions. The distinction between stochastic and deterministic edge-of-stability regimes is the part most likely to matter for practical pretraining recipes, especially for batch scaling and schedule design.

If time is limited, prioritize the trajectory-comparison figures, the spectral plots, the Adam-preconditioned spectrum comparison, and the stability maps. A full careful read is about 1.5 to 2 hours; a focused pass for the main ideas is around 40 minutes.95b:T577,The method, Byte-Prefix Marginalization, rewrites the teacher’s next-token distribution in the student vocabulary through a shared byte representation. For each teacher token, BPM takes its byte string and finds the longest student token whose byte string is a prefix of that teacher token’s bytes. The teacher token’s probability is assigned to that student token, and probabilities mapped to the same student token are aggregated. Probability mass that cannot be matched is assigned to an explicit residual category, which is required to preserve total mass. When byte prefixes do not span multiple teacher tokens, the transformed target exactly recovers the teacher’s byte-prefix marginal. At spanning positions, the method uses a mass-preserving chain-factorized lower bound. Training remains on-policy: the student generates trajectories, the teacher is queried at the corresponding byte-aligned states, and the student minimizes a generalized Jensen-Shannon divergence to the transformed target. Compared with candidate-set methods such as SimCT, BPM avoids dropping mass; compared with rank-based methods such as ULD or GOLD, it avoids assigning probability to byte-unrelated student tokens; compared with SeqKD, it keeps dense next-token supervision. A precomputed mask removes all-whitespace target positions in code data to prevent learning tokenizer-specific formatting artifacts.95c:T400,The paper addresses a central failure mode in asynchronous RL for LLM post-training. Asynchrony improves throughput by overlapping rollout generation with policy optimization, but the resulting data are stale and off-policy: updates are applied to trajectories not fully generated by the current policy, and long trajectories may even span multiple weight versions. Existing methods usually clip or mask tokens using a single threshold on the importance-ratio magnitude, implicitly assuming that a large ratio means an untrustworthy token. The paper argues that this assumption breaks in asynchronous agentic RL because the natural scale of the ratio depends strongly on token entropy. Large ratios at low entropy are often amplified sampling noise, while large ratios at high entropy can reflect legitimate exploration induced by asynchronous updates. The real problem is therefore how to suppress harmful off-policy noise without discarding useful exploration, and to do so without reconstructing an exact behavior policy.95d:T7a7,The paper develops its argument in three steps. First, it establishes an entropy-ratio relation. Both empirically and theoretically, the authors show that the natural scale of the token-level log-importance ratio grows with token entropy. Intuitively, in low-entropy regions where the model is highly confident, a small train-inference discrepancy can be blown up into a large ratio because of near-zero probabilities. Such large ratios are often noise rather than meaningful policy drift. In high-entropy regions, by contrast, larger ratios are expected and can still be statistically normal. Second, the paper decomposes asynchronous staleness more carefully. Instead of treating each trajectory as if it came from one behavior policy, it separates inter-trajectory staleness from intra-trajectory version switching. The latter is the more novel observation: during a long rollout, a worker may sync to a newer model mid-generation, so different segments of the same trajectory come from different policy versions. Around the switch point, entropy and importance ratios rise together. The paper argues that this should not be interpreted as purely harmful off-policy drift; it is often valid exploration introduced by asynchronous training itself. Third, based on these observations, the authors propose ESTR, the Entropy-Scaled Trust Region. Rather than applying a fixed threshold to |δ_t|, ESTR uses a token-wise trust-region boundary that expands with entropy and contracts when entropy is low. Low-entropy tokens are constrained more tightly to block amplified noise; high-entropy tokens are given a wider admissible region so that useful exploration is preserved. A key practical point is that ESTR does not require explicit behavior-policy reconstruction and does not rely on hand-tuned magnitude bias. It is a token-level filtering or constraint mechanism that can replace conventional ratio clipping or hard masking inside asynchronous RL training.95e:T52a,The main experiments focus on long-horizon agentic tasks and difficult reasoning settings. The headline result reported in the paper is on BrowseComp-Plus: ESTR reaches 37.3 avg@1, compared with 34.9 for the strongest prior asynchronous baseline, while matching synchronous GRPO in quality and training 2.6x faster. This is the right comparison to care about, because asynchronous RL usually faces a trade-off between throughput and optimization fidelity. The evidence is not just in the final score table. The paper first shows, on real rollouts, that |δ_t| increases systematically with token entropy, which undermines the statistical validity of a single global threshold. It then analyzes version-switch points inside trajectories and shows concurrent spikes in entropy and ratio, while the standardized deviation remains well-behaved, supporting the claim that many high-entropy large-ratio tokens are legitimate rather than pathological. Finally, against interval clipping, hard masking, and other asynchronous stabilization baselines, ESTR is more stable on long trajectories and reduces policy collapse. When reading the experiments, the most informative figures are the entropy-binned analyses and the training curves under different masking strategies; they explain why the method works, not just that it works.95f:T4d2,This one is worth a careful read. Start with the introduction and motivation, focusing on the two assumptions the paper challenges: that ratio magnitude alone indicates token trustworthiness, and that each trajectory can be associated with a single behavior policy. Then study the analysis around Figures 1–3: first the coupling between entropy and |δ_t|, then the role of intra-trajectory version switching in creating joint spikes. In the method section, make sure to understand exactly how the ESTR boundary scales with entropy and how it replaces standard clipping or masking logic in training. In the experiments, prioritize the main results on BrowseComp-Plus and other long-horizon tasks, then the stability curves and entropy-bucket visualizations. Good questions to keep in mind are: whether entropy is the best scaling variable or should be combined with reward/advantage uncertainty; how ESTR interacts with PPO/GRPO clipping; and whether a similar token-level trust region could be useful in asynchronous pretraining, speculative decoding mismatch, or multimodal RL with heterogeneous token types.960:T6a1,The public material does not expose enough technical detail to support strong claims about the underlying method. It is not a good idea to treat the benchmark rankings here as strict scientific conclusions, because the post lacks the protocol detail and training disclosure needed for that standard.963:T414,The analysis incorporates normalization-induced scale invariance into loss-landscape stability. For weights feeding into normalization layers such as BN or LN, rescaling the weight vector may leave the network function largely unchanged. The loss is therefore insensitive to radial scaling, but the curvature is not. When the norm of such a weight block becomes small, the relevant Hessian eigenvalues can be amplified, roughly following the inverse scale of the norm. Weight decay supplies a persistent shrinkage force, so increasing the decay coefficient drives these blocks toward a high-sharpness region. The paper then defines a weight-norm criticality indicator combining local Hessian information and the learning rate. A practical feature is the component-wise decomposition: one can evaluate the restricted Hessian for a specific scale-invariant block instead of the full parameter Hessian. This makes the criterion applicable to architectures with many normalization modules and allows attribution of instability to individual layers.964:T44b,The architecture repeatedly applies one Transformer block Fθ to a hidden state, h^{t+1}=Fθ(h^t,e), with optional input injection through a learned adapter. The main grid uses NoPE, with positional-encoding controls in the appendix. The key methodological move is to replace tail instruments with a head instrument. Tail instruments such as skipping a late loop or comparing Jacobians across late loops are unreliable because converged trajectories sit near fixed points; near such states, skipping is cheap and local circuits look similar by construction. The proposed diagnostic is convergence-time scaling τ(n,i): the first loop at which the decoded output at position i reaches its final value and stays there. Its scaling class acts as a mechanism signature. Constant τ indicates shortcut or refinement, τ proportional to log n indicates a parallel scan, and τ proportional to n indicates serial step-indexed computation. A streaming positive control validates the instrument: when token i is revealed only at loop i, τ recovers a linear slope of 1.0, while shortcut controls remain flat.965:T577,The experiments are controlled population studies over many seeds, recipes, and model sizes. The reported scales include a small model with a 2-layer block and d=128, a medium model with a 2-layer block and d=256, and a larger model with a 4-layer block and d=512. Tasks include prefix parity, LSB-first increment-with-carry, and group word problems over Z60, S4, S5, and A5. These tasks have known algorithmic structure: some admit constant-depth shortcuts, while S5 and A5 connect to NC1-complete word problems, and associative scan gives a logarithmic-depth solution in principle. The main empirical result is a linear computation frontier learned by free training. The frontier solves v positions per loop, with v approximately n_tr/T_tr; under T=n training, the speed is about 1 position per loop. Giving more loops at test time rescues late positions at fixed input length. Standard tail diagnostics fail: skip retention is essentially total on sufficiently solved examples, cross-step Jacobian alignment is uniformly high, and these metrics do not predict length generalization. The study also separates optimization walls from circuit complexity: A5 hardness is not the main barrier, while S5 operator scale is; an operator-first curriculum removes that wall. Budget annealing transfers the learned mechanism across loop contracts in 4 out of 4 seeds, avoiding the from-scratch seed lottery.966:T5b9,GaugeQuant learns orthogonal rotations at transformer boundaries so that activation mass is spread more evenly across dimensions. The paper identifies usable symmetries in attention and MLP blocks. Value vectors in attention admit an SO(d_k) rotation, with corresponding transformations of W_V and W_O preserving the exact output; under GQA, each KV head group shares its rotation. Query/key rotations are constrained by RoPE: they must commute with the RoPE matrix, reducing the available symmetry to U(1)^{d_k/2}, which the paper does not exploit. In the SwiGLU MLP, the down-projection boundary also admits an invariance, but the rotation cannot be fully absorbed upstream because SiLU and the element-wise product do not commute with a general dense rotation. As a result, H·R remains a runtime operation while R^T can be fused into W_down. Instead of simulating quantization, the method adds a LogSumExp penalty on rotated boundary activations. LogSumExp acts as a smooth dense proxy for the infinity norm, which matters because the uniform quantization step size is driven by the largest outlier. A stop-gradient operator ensures that this auxiliary term updates only the rotation matrices, while the base model parameters are still trained only by cross-entropy. Compared with SpinQuant-style post-training rotation search, GaugeQuant does not require calibration data, a frozen model, or a non-differentiable quantization operator in the optimization loop.967:T6ff,方法叫 Windowed-MTP。核心思想是把 StreamingLLM 风格的 sliding window + attention sink 只应用在 draft head 上，而 target verify 仍然保留全上下文注意力。这样 draft 每一步只读取 W + sink 个 token 的 KV，而不是整段 S 长度上下文；例如 1M context 下 4K window 只占 0.4%。

为什么这能做到“lossless by construction”？因为 speculative decoding 的接受与否始终由 full-attention target 决定。windowing 只会改变 draft 提出的候选 token，不会改变 target 的验证规则，因此不会改变最终采样分布。论文还专门做了 greedy output diff，验证 windowed draft 与 native full-attention draft 的最终输出没有系统性分歧，超出范围的差异只来自 verifier 既有的 bf16 非确定性。

作者还给了一个逐步 latency model，把一次 speculative iteration 分成 γ 次 draft forward 和一次 verify forward，并分析在不同 acceptance length、draft depth d=γ+1、context length S 下，什么时候 native deep draft 会从加速退化到与 dense baseline 持平，甚至变成负收益。这个模型的意义在于，它不是只报告“快了多少”，而是解释为什么在长上下文、低 acceptance、verify 变便宜时，draft attention 会成为主导项。

机制分析部分也做得比较扎实。作者没有停留在“窗口够小也没掉速”这种经验结论，而是看了 window-size dose-response、每个 draft position 的 conditional acceptance 分解，以及 in-run decision-invariance probe。结论是：windowing 大多数时候并不改变 draft 的 top-1 proposal，保留了与 full-attention draft 相近的 acceptance profile，因此速度收益来自每步成本下降，而不是靠牺牲 acceptance 换吞吐。968:T6a0,The method, Windowed-MTP, applies a StreamingLLM-style sliding window plus attention sink to the draft head only, while leaving the target verifier at full attention. As a result, each draft forward reads only W + sink tokens from KV instead of the full context length S. At 1M context, a 4K window is only 0.4% of the sequence.

The key point is why this remains lossless. In speculative decoding, the target verifier always decides which proposed tokens are accepted. Windowing changes only the draft proposals, not the acceptance rule. Therefore the final output distribution remains identical to standard exact speculation. The paper validates this with greedy output diffs, showing no systematic divergence beyond the verifier’s existing bf16 nondeterminism.

The authors also provide a per-step latency model. One speculative iteration is decomposed into γ draft forwards plus one verify forward, and the model explains when a deeper native draft stops helping: long context increases draft KV reads, low acceptance reduces amortization, and cheaper verify phases expose the draft cost instead of hiding it. This is useful because the paper does not merely report speedups; it explains the regime in which native MTP collapses from accelerator to liability.

The mechanistic analysis is also stronger than usual. The paper studies window-size dose response, conditional acceptance by draft position, and an in-run decision-invariance probe. The conclusion is that windowing usually preserves the draft’s top-1 proposal and closely tracks the full-attention acceptance profile. The gain therefore comes from reducing per-step draft cost, not from trading away acceptance for throughput.969:T730,The experiments span three architecture families, including at least a dense Qwen-122B model, a hybrid Nemotron model, and a third model with a different attention design. The main operating point is 1M context with batch size 1.

First, the paper quantifies the long-context draft-attention tax. At γ=6, i.e. d=7, the draft phase alone adds about +92% to +138% on top of the bare verify cost per decode step, nearly doubling step latency. This directly falsifies the assumption that the draft is negligible at million-token context. More importantly, on hard low-acceptance workloads the shipped native draft can become net-negative: at d=7 it reaches only 0.80× the no-speculation dense baseline on Qwen-122B code QA and 0.97× on the hybrid Nemotron. Increasing draft depth to d=9 does not rescue the situation.

Windowed-MTP then delivers a fairly consistent reduction. At 1M context, it cuts per-speculative-iteration cost by about 28%–44% relative to native MTP, and the gain is largely input-invariant. Its magnitude tracks the fraction of draft cost attributable to windowable attention. The paper also measures that the draft KV pool is about 7.7%–11% of total KV across the three models; after windowing, all but W + sink of that draft KV becomes dead state and can be reclaimed into a compact ring buffer with no quality or speed penalty.

On acceptance behavior, windowing preserves the draft top-1 proposal 86%–94% of the time, and the resulting acceptance profile tracks full-attention draft within confidence intervals across the sweep. Residual differences exist, but they are small, depend on input and draft depth, and are always outweighed by the per-step latency reduction. End-to-end performance therefore never regresses in the reported settings, while exactness is preserved because the verifier is unchanged.96a:T607,This one is worth a careful read. 从概率建模上，作者给出了这个多 mask 前向过程的精确定义，并推导出闭式 ELBO。训练目标可以理解为两部分：一部分是标准的 clean-token reconstruction，即从 xt 预测原始 token；另一部分是 intra-mask identification，即当位置已经落入 mask 子空间时，模型还要识别它属于哪个 mask。这个额外项不是装饰性的，它正对应 multi-mask 设计引入的信息结构：如果模型不学会区分不同 mask，终态熵虽然存在，但无法被有效利用。

论文另一个关键点是“如何做离散 consistency distillation”。连续扩散里可以借助 probability-flow ODE 把随机过程对应到确定性流，但离散 jump process 没有这么直接的对应物。作者的处理是构造 low-entropy shared-Gumbel coupling：在不同时间点共享 Gumbel 噪声，使得两条离散路径之间具有较强耦合，从而定义稳定的一致性训练目标。目标不是简单让不同时间的网络输出相同 token，而是让学生去逼近沿耦合路径的 future-filtration posterior，也就是给定未来噪声信息后对 clean token 的后验。这个定义比朴素 self-consistency 更严谨，因为它尊重离散随机过程本身的条件结构。

还有一个很实用的设计是 continual training recipe。由于 MultiMDM 与 MDM 在大部分建模接口上兼容，作者可以从一个已经训练好的 MDM 初始化，再继续训练到 multi-mask 版本，而不是从头训练。这一点很重要，因为 diffusion LM 的预训练成本不低；如果 few-step 能力必须靠从零训练新模型获得，方法的采用门槛会高很多。论文还给出初步证据，说明这种从 pretrained MDM 到 MultiMDM 的迁移在 8B 级模型上也可行，并能转移到 code、math 这类更难分布上。96c:T74d,实验主要在 LM1B 和 OpenWebText 上进行预训练与 consistency distillation，并报告 few-step generation 质量。摘要和现有全文片段没有完整列出所有表格数字，但从论文叙述可以确认，作者比较了三类路线：标准 MDM、USDM 类 few-step 替代方案，以及提出的 MultiMDM。结果方向很清楚：MultiMDM 在少步采样场景下优于标准 masked diffusion 的直接 few-step 化，也优于 uniform-state 路线，同时尽量保住了 MDM 的建模质量和训练效率。

Its significance is not just a new corruption process, but a concrete attempt to remove one of the main practical barriers for diffusion LMs: how to move from long denoising chains to few-step generation without giving up the training advantages of masked diffusion. If that transition fails, diffusion LMs remain hard to deploy against autoregressive models on inference cost, and they become less attractive as text components in unified multimodal generative systems.

The contribution has three layers. First, MultiMDM replaces the single absorbing mask with a multi-mask subspace, preserving explicit noise markers while restoring nonzero terminal entropy. Second, it derives a closed-form ELBO/KL objective that remains native to the discrete setting, rather than relying on continuous relaxations. Third, it proposes a discrete consistency-distillation recipe based on shared-Gumbel low-entropy couplings and a future-filtration posterior target. Just as important, the method supports continual adaptation from pretrained MDMs instead of requiring a new model family trained from scratch. That interface is highly relevant for anyone working on diffusion LMs, any-order LMs, or AR+diffusion hybrids.96e:Tb06,The key idea is to replace the single mask token with a set of mask states. Let V be the normal vocabulary and M={m1,...,mK} be a set of mask tokens. Each clean token x0 is assigned a designated mask. In the forward process, a token does not jump directly toward one universal [M]; it is first biased toward its designated mask and only later mixes across the full mask subspace. This changes the geometry of the diffusion process in two useful ways. First, the terminal distribution is no longer a single deterministic all-mask sequence; it retains entropy over the mask subspace and can therefore serve as a meaningful starting point for few-step generation. Second, mask states remain separate from the normal vocabulary, so the model still knows which positions are corrupted. That preserves the clean/noise separation that makes MDMs stronger than uniform-state diffusion.

The probabilistic formulation is developed explicitly, and the resulting ELBO has a clean interpretation. One term is the usual clean-token reconstruction objective: predict the original token from a corrupted state. The second term is an intra-mask identification objective: once a position has entered the mask subspace, the model must also identify which mask it belongs to. This is not a cosmetic addition. It is exactly what allows the model to exploit the information carried by the multi-mask terminal state. Without learning to distinguish masks, the extra entropy would exist formally but would not be useful for generation.

The second major technical contribution is the consistency-distillation construction for the discrete setting. In continuous diffusion, one can often move from a stochastic SDE to a deterministic probability-flow ODE while preserving marginals. There is no direct analogue for finite-state jump processes. The paper addresses this by introducing a low-entropy coupling based on shared Gumbel noise across time points. This creates strongly coupled discrete trajectories and enables a stable consistency target. Importantly, the target is not a naive requirement that outputs at different times should match. Instead, the student is trained toward the future-filtration posterior over clean tokens along the coupled path. That is a more principled target because it respects the conditional structure of the discrete stochastic process.

A practical strength of the framework is the continual-training recipe. Because MultiMDM stays close to the MDM parameterization and training interface, a pretrained MDM can be adapted into a multi-mask model rather than retraining from scratch. Given the cost of diffusion-LM pretraining, this is a meaningful design choice. The paper also provides preliminary evidence that this transfer works at the 8B scale and can carry over to harder domains such as code and math.96f:T712,The experiments pretrain and distill models on LM1B and OpenWebText, then evaluate few-step generation quality. The full excerpt provided here does not include all tables, but the empirical story is clear. The paper compares standard MDMs, uniform-state diffusion style alternatives for few-step generation, and the proposed MultiMDM. MultiMDM performs better in few-step generation than direct few-step variants of standard masked diffusion and also outperforms the uniform-state route, while preserving much of the modeling quality and training efficiency associated with MDMs.

The experimental evidence is useful in four ways. First, few-step generation quality improves at the same or similar NFE, indicating that the multi-mask terminal distribution provides more usable starting randomness. Second, the training-objective ablation shows that the intra-mask identification term matters; removing it weakens the benefit of the multi-mask design. Third, the distillation ablation shows that shared-Gumbel coupling and the posterior target are central rather than incidental engineering choices. Fourth, continual adaptation from a pretrained MDM remains effective, and the paper reports preliminary positive transfer on an 8B pretrained MDM for code and math benchmarks.

A full read will likely take 1.5 to 2.5 hours.971:T80d,LISA replaces each standard self-attention block with two parallel components. The first is linear attention, implemented as a recurrent state matrix S_t that accumulates historical key-value interactions. This branch provides cheap global memory: update and read cost do not grow with context length, and memory usage stays constant. Its weakness is well known: linear attention lacks the sharp content-based indexing behavior of softmax attention.

The second branch is the Lightning Indexer. It scores historical tokens by importance and dynamically selects the top-M tokens for exact self-attention. This gives the model a fixed-size high-resolution retrieval set. The overall design is therefore a hybrid memory system: linear attention stores broad long-range context, while the indexer preserves precise access to a small number of critical tokens.

A central part of the paper is the training recipe. The model is trained in two stages. In stage 1, only the linear-attention branch is cold-started with plain cross-entropy. The rationale is to let the recurrent memory learn a stable predictive representation on its own, instead of immediately forcing it to mimic the teacher distribution through distillation. In stage 2, the indexer and top-M selection are introduced, together with a KL term to stabilize token selection and keep the modified model close to the original teacher behavior. This is a sensible choice because discrete top-M routing can make optimization brittle; KL acts as an anchor.

The design differs from pure sparse attention, which usually relies on predefined windows, blocks, or retrieval heuristics and may miss long-range information. LISA uses the linear state as a global fallback. It also differs from pure linear attention, which is efficient but often fails on tasks that require exact recall of earlier variables, constraints, or intermediate results. Finally, unlike some state-compression approaches, it does not require complicated preprocessing or a new output format, making the retrofit path much more practical.972:T6e7,The experiments focus on long-context mathematical reasoning across five benchmarks. The two headline results are efficiency and quality. On efficiency, LISA reduces inference cost by up to about 50% at 16K context relative to the full self-attention baseline. The gain comes from replacing sequence-length-dependent attention computation with a constant-cost recurrent update plus fixed-budget sparse retrieval, while also reducing KV-cache pressure. On quality, the paper reports an average accuracy improvement of 5.6% over the full-attention baseline. That is more interesting than a simple “small degradation” result: the hybrid memory is not merely an approximation, it can be a better inductive bias for long-CoT reasoning.

The ablations support the main design choices. Linear attention alone is insufficient, especially on context-sensitive reasoning tasks, which validates the need for exact token retrieval. The top-M budget shows the expected trade-off: too small M hurts precise recall, while larger M improves quality with diminishing returns and higher cost. The two-stage training strategy outperforms one-shot joint training, indicating that stabilizing the recurrent memory before learning the indexer is important. The KL term in stage 2 further improves stability, especially for token selection behavior and output consistency.

训练数据分成几类。真实 parallel 语料来自 ARCTIC、CHAINS、CSTR-VCTK、EnDialects、ESD、TIMIT 等，覆盖不同说话人、口音、风格和情绪；非 parallel 语料用 LibriSpeech 960h、Tedlium-3 374h 扩展覆盖面，并通过同一语音的随机增强在线构造 pseudo-parallel 对；作者还用 Kokoro 合成额外 parallel 样本。这里的取舍很重要：只靠真实 parallel 数据，覆盖面不够；只靠增强，学到的多半是噪声不变性而不是说话人/韵律不变性，所以两者结合。

训练目标围绕“跨 realization 对齐”展开。虽然给出的全文片段没有完整公式，但从方法描述可以看出它同时约束连续表示和离散 token：一方面让相同 transcript 的不同语音在时间对齐后靠近，另一方面配合 aggressive augmentation，迫使模型把不稳定因素视为 nuisance。作者强调 word-level forced alignment，这说明他们不是做粗粒度句向量对齐，而是在局部时间轴上保留内容结构。这样做比直接蒸馏 ASR 文本更合适，因为文本会丢掉时长、停顿、局部边界等对 codec 和生成模型有用的帧级 grounding。

论文还把“好 token”的定义说得比较完整：不仅要 content capture，还要 nuisance invariance。很多已有方法只优化前者，比如保留足够音素信息；PINT 认为如果后者做不好，token 仍然不是好的 semantic token，因为同内容不同表面形式会映射到不同离散序列。这个定义直接解释了为什么后续可以配合 RLE 和 BPE 获得更高压缩率：重复帧和稳定片段被真正折叠了，而不是把 speaker/prosody 的抖动也编码进去。

与已有工作相比，PINT 和 ContentVec、DC-Spin、StableToken、NAST 有交集，但重点不同。ContentVec/DC-Spin 更偏 speaker invariance；StableToken 更偏噪声鲁棒；很多 codec 工作则默认 HuBERT/WavLM/Whisper 特征已经足够“语义”。PINT 的区别在于，它把 parallel data 作为核心监督信号，直接针对“同内容多实现”这个结构化事实做表示清洗，而且结果是 drop-in 的：可以作为现有 codec 或 speech LM 的 semantic target，而不要求重做整个系统。975:T40c,This matters for pretraining in at least three ways. First, it reframes speech token quality in language-model terms rather than only downstream task terms: lower conditional entropy, better compressibility, and easier autoregressive prediction. That is the right lens if the tokens are meant to feed speech LMs. Second, it argues that many speech codec and speech-generation systems may be bottlenecked not by decoder architecture but by noisy semantic targets upstream. If the target sequence itself is unstable, the LM is forced to model nuisance variation that should never have been there. Third, it offers an alternative to collapsing speech into ASR text. PINT aims for content-only discrete units while preserving frame-level temporal grounding, which is important for codec-style generation and unified audio-language modeling. The contribution is not a narrow probe improvement; the gains line up across disentanglement, discriminability, compression, and LM perplexity, which suggests a real representation-level improvement.976:Ta3c,PINT starts from a pretrained SSL speech encoder and fine-tunes it using parallel utterances plus aggressive augmentations so that different realizations of the same content align in representation space and, ultimately, in discrete token space. The paper’s design choice is notable: instead of redesigning the codec stack, it isolates the semantic-target problem and improves the upstream representation that existing codec or speech-LM systems can consume as a drop-in replacement.

The training data mix is important. True parallel corpora include ARCTIC, CHAINS, CSTR-VCTK, EnDialects, ESD, and TIMIT, covering variation in speaker, accent, style, and emotion. Non-parallel corpora such as LibriSpeech 960h and Tedlium-3 374h are used to broaden linguistic and acoustic coverage; pseudo-parallel pairs are created online by applying stochastic augmentations to the same utterance. The paper also synthesizes additional parallel samples with Kokoro. This combination is a sensible compromise: real parallel data teaches invariance to speaker and style, while augmentation-based pseudo-parallel data expands coverage and robustness.

A key implementation detail is forced alignment at the word level. That suggests PINT is not learning only sentence-level invariance, but preserving local temporal structure while aligning content across realizations. This is one reason the method differs from using ASR text as the semantic target: text removes nuisance factors, but it also removes frame-level grounding that modern speech codecs and generators rely on.

Conceptually, the paper defines a semantic token with a dual criterion: content capture and nuisance invariance. Many prior methods emphasize the first and under-specify the second. PINT argues that without invariance, the token sequence is still not truly semantic, because identical content does not map to a stable discrete form. That framing also explains the compression angle: once nuisance variation is removed, run-length encoding and BPE can collapse repeated frames and stable spans more effectively, yielding lower bitrate and easier AR modeling.

Relative to prior work, PINT overlaps with ContentVec, DC-Spin, StableToken, and NAST, but the emphasis is different. ContentVec and DC-Spin focus more on speaker invariance; StableToken focuses more on noise robustness; many codec papers simply inherit HuBERT, WavLM, Whisper, or w2v-BERT features as semantic targets. PINT’s distinction is to use parallel data as the primary supervision signal for representation cleaning, explicitly exploiting the same-content/multiple-realizations structure.977:T647,The experimental story is convincing because the metrics form a coherent chain rather than a single isolated win. The headline numbers are: speaker probe accuracy drops from 93.1% to 1.2%, a 98.7% relative reduction, indicating that speaker information is largely removed; ABX discriminability improves by 42%, showing that phonetic/content distinctions are preserved or even sharpened rather than collapsed; and on the same 85M decoder-only Transformer, test perplexity on PINT tokens is 1.95 versus 2.78 and 2.67 for HuBERT and WavLM tokens, a 27–30% reduction. The training-dynamics result is especially important: PINT reaches WavLM’s final perplexity in 23× fewer steps, which points to better optimization and sample efficiency, not just a better endpoint.

For pretraining researchers, this is the most relevant part of the paper. Probe results alone would not prove that the tokens are better LM targets. But lower perplexity and faster convergence on a fixed LM architecture strongly suggest that the token sequence has become more predictable in the right way.

The paper also appears careful about evaluation hygiene. Splits are constructed to avoid transcript leakage, including speaker holdout for CSTR-VCTK and transcript-grouped splitting where official partitions do not exist. That matters because parallel-data methods can otherwise overstate invariance by leaking repeated text across train and test. Additional evaluations include emotion probing on RAVDESS and LM training on a 6k-hour clean subset of LibriLight, covering both representation purity and practical modeling utility.978:T735,Start with the introduction’s formulation around H(z|c). The central empirical observation is that freely trained RLVR checkpoints stay near-isospectral to their base, and this proximity is not merely a high-dimensional artifact. Three interventions test functional necessity: (1) restoring base Σ while keeping learned U, V in RL checkpoints preserves most acquired gains; (2) training with Σ fixed throughout RL while updating only U and V still achieves strong RL learning; (3) the reverse—freezing frames and updating only Σ—yields only marginal improvement. This leads to spectral inheritance: the base spectrum can be reused, with new behavior carried by both frames. Follow-up ablations show both frames must remain adaptable; remixing only within input/output spans or holding one frame fixed leaves substantially more of the endpoint change unexplained. ISO (Isospectral Optimization) operationalizes this in two complementary forms. ISO-Merger (offline) consolidates multiple specialists trained from a shared base by reusing the shared base spectra and directly combining expert frame changes into a single fixed-spectrum checkpoint, without extra data, rollouts, or distillation. ISO-Optimizer (online) constrains training to the fixed-spectrum manifold of the base weights while allowing both frames to adapt, and can be wrapped around base optimizers such as AdamW or Muon.97a:T460,Read carefully, about 1–1.5 hours.
