成本方面，论文给出的推理额外开销最多约 8% per-token，这一点很关键。因为很多 latent reasoning 或 depth recurrence 方法的主要问题不是无效，而是推理成本太高，难以进入真实 serving。T^2MLR 的 trade-off 是把更多复杂性放在训练端，换取较低的在线开销。985:T9f0,The core idea is temporal middle-layer recurrence. The model caches a representation from a deeper middle layer at token t-1 and injects it into an earlier middle layer at token t through a gated fusion pathway. This creates a continuous latent channel across decoding steps, but places that channel inside the part of the network where abstract computation is believed to happen.

Two design choices matter. First, the recurrent signal does not re-enter through the embedding layer. It is fused directly into the middle of the computation graph, so the previous token’s abstract state can continue evolving in the current token’s middle-layer processing. Second, recurrence is localized to a subset of middle layers rather than applied everywhere. The rationale is functional: early layers are more lexical/syntactic, late layers are closer to vocabulary projection, and middle layers are the best place to preserve reasoning state.

Architecturally, T^2MLR defines a write location and a read location. A hidden state from the write layer is cached, then consumed at the read layer of the next token. A gating module controls how much of the current token’s local representation should be mixed with the carried-over latent state. This is more flexible than a plain residual addition because the model can decide contextually when to rely on persistent latent state and when to ignore it.

The training story is a major part of the contribution. Exact temporal recurrence would introduce token-to-token dependencies under teacher forcing and break standard sequence-parallel training. The paper proposes an approximate temporal-parallel training scheme that preserves scalable parallelism while still training the recurrent pathway. This is the practical enabler: without it, the architecture would behave more like an RNN-style serial model and would be hard to pretrain at scale. The approximation introduces a train-time compromise between recurrence fidelity and throughput, and that trade-off is central to evaluating the method.

Relative to prior work, the distinctions are clean. Compared with latent-recurrent methods, recurrence is placed in the middle layers rather than at the input side. Compared with looped/depth-recurrent Transformers, extra computation is propagated across time instead of repeatedly re-running the full stack for one token, so inference overhead stays small. Compared with a standard Transformer, the model adds an explicit continuous hidden-state pathway across tokens, reducing the token bottleneck.986:T84e,The empirical section is broad and well structured.

First, the paper uses the synthetic S5-Retrieval benchmark, which combines non-solvable group state tracking with in-context retrieval. The point is not benchmark coverage but mechanism stress-testing: standard Transformers and recurrent models fail in isolation, while a shallow T^2MLR can solve the task. Even without focusing on the exact number, this result supports the claim that middle-layer temporal recurrence can maintain abstract state across steps.

Second, in language pretraining, T^2MLR achieves lower perplexity than parameter- and data-matched Transformer baselines and also improves downstream NLP benchmarks. A particularly informative ablation is that the best gains come from applying recurrence to only about 20% of the middle layers rather than the full stack. That strongly suggests the benefit comes from placing recurrence in the right region, not from adding generic extra machinery. The paper also scales experiments to 361M and 1B parameters with 50B pretraining tokens, and the gains persist.

Third, in downstream reasoning finetuning, the model consistently beats matched baselines on GSM-Aug, ProsQA, HotPotQA, and Variable Assignment. The most important pattern is not any single benchmark delta, but the repeated finding that middle-layer recurrence outperforms full-layer recurrence. That reinforces the paper’s central architectural thesis.

Fourth, the retrofit experiment is practically important. The authors insert the recurrent pathway into a pretrained SmolLM2-1.7B-Instruct model and do brief math finetuning. GSM8K improves from 35.8 to 39.9, and MATH500 from 12.8 to 18.0, compared with an identically finetuned baseline without the recurrent modification. This suggests the architecture may be adoptable without full pretraining from scratch.

On efficiency, the paper reports at most about 8% extra per-token inference overhead. That matters because many latent-reasoning or depth-looping methods fail the deployment test due to decoding cost. T^2MLR shifts more complexity to training while keeping online overhead modest.987:T6e5,Start with the problem framing in the introduction, then move quickly to the method section that argues why recurrence should live in the middle layers. If time is limited, the best path is: method figure, training approximation, main pretraining table, layer-placement ablations, and the retrofit experiment. A serious read is about 60–90 minutes; reproducing or adapting the method would require another pass over the training-parallelism details.988:T85f,The method models each MDLM denoising step as two actions. First, the model predicts tokens for all currently masked positions. Second, among those newly predicted positions, it chooses which ones remain revealed and which ones are remasked for later steps. This yields a two-stage action MDP. As a result, the trajectory probability factorizes into a token policy term and a masking-policy term, and the policy gradient decomposes accordingly: one term reinforces good token choices, the other reinforces good ordering decisions.

A practical strength is that the masking term does not require a separate policy head. The authors derive unmasking scores from the model’s existing logits and turn them into position log-probabilities via a softmax. So the method adds no extra parameters and no extra forward passes beyond those already needed for token likelihood computation. That is important for diffusion LMs, where generation chains are already longer than AR decoding.

The theoretical claim is that dropping the masking term can miss ascent directions for expected return. Intuitively, this makes sense: in an MDLM, deciding which positions to resolve early and which uncertain positions to defer changes the future conditional distributions and can affect final answer quality. Optimizing only token predictions leaves part of the policy frozen.

Another positive feature is compatibility. The paper does not introduce a bespoke RL framework; it plugs the decomposition into standard policy-gradient style algorithms. Any method that relies on log-probabilities over sampled trajectories can, in principle, incorporate both token and masking log-probs. That makes the proposal easier to adopt than an entirely new optimizer.

Compared with prior work, the differences are clear. Relative to ELBO-based RL approximations, it moves from a reconstruction view to an explicit trajectory-policy view. Relative to token-only trajectory methods, it treats unmasking order as part of the policy. Relative to approaches that would need an extra network for ordering, it reuses the model’s own logits and keeps the engineering overhead low.989:T678,The main empirical focus is mathematical reasoning and code generation. The headline result is consistent improvement from jointly optimizing the token and masking terms over methods that optimize only the token component. The abstract reports gains of up to +4.0% on MATH500, +2.9% on HumanEval, and +2.5% on GSM8K and MBPP. The paper also claims top-tier performance across these tasks, suggesting the benefit is not isolated to a single benchmark.

The most informative part should be the ablations. The critical comparisons are likely: token-gradient only, masking-gradient only, and both together; sensitivity to remasking schedules; and alternative constructions of the position log-probability. If the joint objective consistently wins, that supports the claim that the masking policy contributes genuine learning signal rather than acting as a noisy regularizer.

The paper should also be read against prior ELBO-based RL and token-only trajectory RL baselines. For those comparisons to be meaningful, one should check whether rollout count, denoising steps, reward normalization, and the underlying MDLM backbone are controlled. RL results for diffusion LMs can otherwise be confounded by sampling budget and decode schedule.

A practical point is efficiency. The authors emphasize that the masking term comes at no extra forward cost beyond token-likelihood computation. That means the gains are not simply purchased with more compute; they come from extracting more supervision from the same sampled trajectory. If the full paper includes wall-clock or sample-efficiency numbers, those would be especially useful for judging real adoption value.98a:T5c9,Do not start from the result tables. The proposed world plus event stream decomposition unifies ordinary video, interactive video, speech, behavior, and language into one causal sequence modeling framework. Three implications matter for foundation model research. First, it provides a pretraining task for joint video/audio/language/behavior modeling that is closer to agent interaction than plain video generation. Second, it writes open-vocabulary actions directly into the language event stream, avoiding a fixed action vocabulary and pointing toward a unified interface for agent behavior. Third, it frames pretraining as learning how a world evolves in real time given context and incoming inputs, then specializes that competence by changing the world configuration and input driver; this differs from both standard next-token language modeling and standard diffusion video generation. Relevant for multimodal foundation models, real-time interaction systems, and world modeling.98d:T71f,The paper keeps the Wan-Streamer v0.1/v0.2 design: a single Transformer models text, audio, and video on one causal timeline, so perception, response timing, speaking, visible listening, and synchronized video are learned jointly rather than assembled from cascaded modules. The main change in v0.3 is not architecture but a reframing of the training objective and sequence representation. Any video is decomposed into a persistent world and a time-varying event stream. The world captures stable context over the timescale of a clip or interaction: environment, visual style, subject identity and appearance, ambient sound, voice characteristics, and other durable conditions. Events are localized changes: subject behavior, camera motion, environmental change, speech, and other sounds. The world is represented as a flexible structured record whose schema can vary by clip or task rather than being globally fixed. Each event has a time interval, a free-form description of the change, and an association to a character or to the environment. The pretraining task becomes: given the world and incoming inputs, predict how the world streams forward unit by unit in real time. For downstream interaction, the world configures scene, character, ambient sound, and voice; streaming user text/audio/video drive the model's event stream. The event stream interleaves spoken words with parenthesized natural-language behavior directives such as “(frowning slightly) What did you say?” This replaces a fixed action vocabulary with open-vocabulary actions grounded in the world, while conditioning audio-video generation through the same path as the language stream, so no new latency-critical component is added. In short, this is a semantic reorganization of the existing causal sequence rather than a new stack of modules.98e:T4e5,The central design is a one-bit experiment. In the answer-blind condition, the generator sees only the problem, samples a chain, and the pipeline keeps chains whose final answer is correct. In the answer-conditioned condition, the generator sees both the problem and the gold answer, is asked to reach that answer, and the same correctness filter is applied. The setup fixes the generator, problem set, filter, training recipe, and data budget, so the intervention is isolated.

The mechanism analysis separates answer visibility from the instruction to rationalize. Merely showing the answer under a neutral instruction is much less harmful; the main damage comes from asking the model to derive toward the known answer. The observable symptom is early answer declaration. Answer-conditioned chains tend to state the answer near the beginning and then fill in the explanation. This is an off-policy shift: the training traces no longer match the model’s own search distribution when the answer is unknown. After fine-tuning, the student inherits this habit in its own generations. A simple filter that removes chains with early answer statements partially repairs performance, which supports the claim that rationalized chains carry much of the harm.98f:T651,The main experiments fine-tune Qwen3-8B with full-parameter SFT on math problems from the Nemotron-Cascade-SFT-Stage-2 split, disjoint from evaluation. Evaluation uses vLLM in thinking mode on MATH-500 with a 32,768-token budget and symbolic answer matching. The controlled comparison is built on a fixed set of 935 training problems. Under this harness, the Qwen3-8B base model scores 95.2. The answer-conditioned corpus trains a student that is 16.2 points weaker than the answer-blind corpus on MATH-500. On harder olympiad-style AIME problems, the gap grows to 27.2 points. The penalty remains under length-matched controls and training-budget sweeps, and it increases with difficulty.

The degradation also appears in code: even when every retained chain passes tests, answer-conditioned traces still hurt the student. The penalty is absent on multiple-choice knowledge and science benchmarks, where the task is mainly option selection rather than deriving an answer through a long process. Within a single answer-conditioned corpus, chains that state the answer early account for much of the damage; a three-seed difference-in-differences analysis reports a 16.9-point effect. The paper also proposes a pre-training diagnostic signature measured from a small set of unlabeled generations. Across eight models from four families, the signature ranks the leakage penalty and predicts a held-out family with a mean absolute error of 2.9 points. If a pipeline cannot avoid showing gold answers, prompting the model to derive first and state the answer only at the end recovers about two-thirds of the lost accuracy.990:T4c8,The method decomposes total GRPO post-training compute into C_search, C_learning, and C_reward. C_search covers autoregressive rollout generation. C_learning covers policy optimization, including an effective update-cost model for LoRA that accounts for trainable adapters as well as the frozen backbone forward and activation costs. C_reward covers reward or verifier inference, which is negligible for rule-based rewards but can be substantial for learned feedback such as process reward models. The main allocation variable is the update fraction ρ = C_learning / C_total. Low ρ corresponds to search- or feedback-heavy runs; high ρ corresponds to update-heavy runs. This differs from common reporting practice because reward-model inference is not treated as free. A PRM-based run and a rule-based run can have the same total FLOPs while buying different amounts of exploration and learning. The empirical setting uses LoRA-adapted Qwen2.5 policies trained with GRPO on mathematical reasoning tasks, and compares model sizes, allocation ratios, reward systems, and evaluation targets. RACE is introduced as a pilot-grid protocol for locating useful allocation regimes before spending budget on larger validation runs.991:T440,The experiments use GRPO post-training of LoRA-adapted Qwen2.5 policies on math reasoning tasks. Four findings are central. First, model size and allocation are coupled under a fixed budget: larger policies cost more per token, so the same budget yields fewer rollouts and fewer updates. As a result, a larger policy is not automatically the best post-training choice. Second, the best observed update fraction changes with model size; no single search-versus-learning split dominates. Third, reward design changes the compute frontier. Rule-based rewards leave most non-update compute for policy rollout, while learned feedback spends part of the budget on reward-model inference. Fourth, evaluation target matters. Native training reward, pass@1 symbolic accuracy, and common-judge process scores can select different allocations. The available text does not expose reproducible numerical tables, exact model-size lists, or absolute gain values, so the safest reading is that the empirical evidence supports conditional allocation frontiers rather than a single winning operating point.992:T60f,The framework treats a discrete diffusion model as a corruption-denoising system over a constructed state space. That state space may come from BPE or subword tokenizers, bytes or characters, VQ image tokens, codec audio tokens, video tokens, or natural scientific alphabets such as amino acids, nucleotides, atom types, and bond types. Within this lens, several families become different choices in the same design space. Transition-matrix methods, as in D3PM-style models, specify categorical transitions directly and can support uniform, nearest-neighbor, or structure-aware corruption. Masking or absorbing-state methods introduce a mask token as an absorbing state and train the model to recover clean tokens from partially corrupted sequences; they are related to masked language modeling, but generation proceeds through iterative denoising rather than one-shot filling. Score- or ratio-based methods learn discrete probability ratios or denoising directions rather than continuous scores, covering recent diffusion and flow-matching language models such as SEDD, MDLM, and LLaDA-like systems. The framework also explains why embed-then-diffuse is fragile: adding Gaussian noise in embedding space and rounding back to tokens creates a mismatch between continuous geometry and discrete vocabulary structure. Compared with AR modeling, native discrete diffusion gives up the simplicity of left-to-right likelihood and mature decoding infrastructure, but gains parallel updates, global revision, and a natural interface for infilling and editing.993:T44b,The work is primarily a unifying framework rather than a new large-scale empirical training study. Its evidence is comparative and organizational, spanning diffusion language models for text and code, tokenized multimodal generation, and scientific sequences or structured alphabets. Several practical lessons are emphasized. Token granularity changes the denoising problem: subword tokenization shortens sequences but makes each token semantically larger, while byte or character tokenization increases length but regularizes the alphabet. Vocabulary topology matters: in image or audio codebooks, uniform corruption can destroy local structure that a topology-aware transition matrix could preserve. Absorbing-mask models are convenient for infilling and arbitrary-order generation, but they require careful sampling schedules, confidence-based remasking, or step allocation to reduce train-sample mismatch. Parallel generation is not automatically faster in wall-clock terms; the number of denoising steps, denoiser size, resampling policy, and hardware efficiency determine the realized latency.994:T5ca,The central tool is the Visual Dependency Gap (VDG). For each question, the model is evaluated under the original-video condition and under a black-screen condition; VDG is defined from the difference in correctness between the two. This per-question formulation is important because it allows the benchmark to be stratified by actual dependence on visual input rather than only by aggregate averages. The paper then uses paired McNemar tests to show statistical dissociation: if two models differ significantly on original videos but not on black screens, higher accuracy cannot be equated with stronger visual grounding. Beyond the black-screen control, the authors build a four-step diagnostic ladder: black screen, single frame, shuffled frames, and original video. This decomposes what the benchmark is rewarding: any visual content at all, static spatial information, frame diversity, and temporal order. An FPS ablation from 0.5 to 24 FPS provides an additional probe into temporal sensitivity. The paper also revisits compression robustness through CRF sweeps and argues that flat robustness curves can be an artifact of benchmark composition, where visually dependent and visually independent questions cancel each other. The study spans 20 models, 10 architecture families, and 2B–78B parameters, including open-weight and API systems. The authors are careful not to overclaim from 4-bit quantized runs and restrict defended scaling conclusions to full-precision models.995:T640,The most important findings are diagnostic rather than leaderboard-oriented. A focused read takes about 45–60 minutes.997:T450,The analysis starts with a separable strongly convex quadratic and an affine-variance noise model, where the gradient-noise variance has an additive term σ0² and a multiplicative term σ1²||∇f||². When σ0=0, the noise is a scale family and vanishes at the optimum. For SGD in one coordinate, the second moment follows an exactly multiplicative recursion with contraction r(η)=(1-ηλ)²+η²σ1²λ². The optimal fixed learning rate is η*=1/(λ(1+σ1²)), giving contraction σ1²/(1+σ1²), and the best WSD cooldown fraction is zero. For signSGD and normalized methods under the same multiplicative noise, the probability of stepping in the correct direction is independent of the iterate scale. The dynamics reduce to an analyzable lattice walk, producing a final loss floor of Θ(η²). Cooldown helps because it reduces the step granularity. With any additive noise component, σ0>0, every method has an η-dependent floor. The paper then checks robustness under local (L0,L1)-smoothness, multidimensional normalized SGD, momentum, and heavy-tailed noise without relying on finite moments.998:Tab4,技术路线分成四层，而且每一层都围绕“把几何恢复和因果有效性拆开”展开。

第一层是构造完全可控的 ground-truth superposition toy model。作者从头训练一个很小的合成模型，不用预训练权重，也不用外部数据，使得真实 feature 方向、隐藏维度、稀疏度和 superposition 几何都已知。这样做的目的不是追求 realism，而是让“恢复是否正确”以及“干预是否沿真实路径生效”都能被严格定义。

第二层是复现并修正已有 SAE 几何结论。论文多 seed 复现了 Elhage 等人的 superposition phase diagram，并指出一个重要 artifact：在高 sparsity 区域，若训练步数不够，会把 under-training 误判成 superposition 结构。作者用 sparsity-aware step budgets 解决这个问题。除此之外，论文还描述了一个此前没有被充分刻画的 diffuse sharing regime：在极端 overcompleteness 下，每个 feature 都被“相当程度地表示”，但 feature dimensionality 很低，说明表示不是少数原子清晰分工，而是更弥散地共享字典容量。

第三层是复现 TopK SAE 与 L1 SAE 的比较，并把“L1 shrinkage”从口头说法变成直接测量。作者从头复现 TopK-vs-L1 Pareto，对 activation refinement 做了直接测试，量化 L1 正则导致的 shrinkage，而不是只凭经验判断。这里的关键点是：decoder recovery 看起来相近时，encoder 激活行为可能已经明显不同，这正是后面因果分歧的来源之一。

第四层是提出一套 causal validation battery，并把 inertness 细分成可操作的类型。作者对每个 correlationally recovered feature 做两类干预：ablation 和 sign-correct steering，并把影响一路传播到模型真实输出层，而不是停留在 SAE reconstruction 空间。基于这些干预，论文区分了两条轴。按成因分，有 structural inertness 和 competitive inertness。前者来自 antipodal-pair superposition geometry 与 positive-pass encoder 的结构性错配，即使 SAE 训练更好也未必消失；后者来自 TopK 竞争机制下退化字典的竞争病理，并且和数值边界不稳定性耦合。按方向分，有 read-inertness 和 write-inertness：前者表示 ablation 监测不到，后者表示 steering 无法写入有效影响。论文指出 antipodal pairs 可以把这两者完全解耦。

此外，作者还把这套审计流程封装成 sae-causal-audit 工具，接口只要求对象能 encode、decode 并暴露 dictionary，因此理论上可审计任意 SAE 实现，包括 sae_lens.SAE。工具设计里还专门处理了 sign-handling bug 这一类常见错误，使其在接口层面不易发生。999:T9d8,实验部分信息量很高，且不少结论都带具体数字。

第一，superposition phase diagram 的复现不是单次跑通，而是多 seed 统计。作者发现高 sparsity 区域存在收敛伪象：训练不够时会看起来像某种 superposition 几何，实际只是没收敛。这个问题通过 sparsity-aware step budget 解决。论文还报告了 diffuse sharing regime 的量化特征：在极端 overcompleteness 下，每个 feature 的表示强度大致为 ||W_i||^2 ≈ 1.40，而 feature dimensionality 约为 D_i ≈ 0.08，说明 feature 普遍被表示，但每个 feature 占用的“维度份额”很小。

第二，TopK-vs-L1 复现部分，作者不仅比较 Pareto，还直接测 activation refinement，验证 L1 shrinkage 的存在。虽然当前给出的正文片段没有完整表格数字，但结论很明确：仅看 decoder 对齐会高估 L1 SAE 的恢复质量，因为 encoder 激活被 shrinkage 扭曲后，因果效应会进一步偏离。

第三，也是最关键的，因果验证结果显示 correlational recovery 和 causal efficacy 可以明显分离。在一个 degraded SAE 上，22 个几何匹配到的 feature 里有 17 个是 causally inert；在一个 well-trained SAE 上，同样是 22 个匹配里只有 2 个 inert。更强的一点是，inert match 的 cosine 可以高到 0.9998，说明“几何几乎完美”并不能保证“因果上有效”。这基本击穿了只用 cosine recovery 做结论的做法。

第四，真实模型小规模审计。作者拿一个已发布的 production SAE，gpt2-small-res-jb，对 83 个手工编写、跨多个语义域的 concept 做审计，恢复出 7 个 correlationally matched feature，其中 1 个，也就是 14%，是 causally inert。样本不大，但方向上和 toy setting 一致。论文还发现一个意外现象：少数 decoder atoms 会反复成为几十个语义上互不相关 concept 的最近邻匹配。作者用三组独立构造、规模和多样性逐步增加的 concept batch 复现了这个 atom collision 现象，并用受控负例排除了 prompt template artifact 的解释。

第五，复现性实验。作者在 CI 调试中说明了为什么浮点训练跨平台做不到 byte-exact reproducibility，并提出两层保证：固定环境内做 SHA-256 级别的字节一致；跨环境则要求 semantic equality，数值容差 rtol=1e-4，边界敏感的整数计数允许 ±1。这个部分不是主结果，但对做 SAE 或小模型复现实验的人很实用。99a:Taa1,The technical program has four layers, all built around separating geometric recovery from causal validity.

First, the authors construct a fully controlled ground-truth superposition model. It is a small synthetic model trained from scratch, with no pretrained weights and no external data. The point is not realism but identifiability: true feature directions, sparsity, hidden dimensionality, and superposition geometry are all known, so both recovery and intervention can be evaluated rigorously.

Second, they reproduce and refine prior geometric results. The paper reproduces the Elhage et al. superposition phase diagram with multi-seed statistics and identifies an important artifact: at high sparsity, insufficient training can masquerade as superposition structure. This is corrected with sparsity-aware step budgets. The paper also describes a less-discussed diffuse sharing regime at extreme overcompleteness, where every feature is substantially represented while each feature occupies only a small effective dimensional share.

Third, the paper reproduces the TopK-vs-L1 SAE comparison and turns the usual claim about L1 shrinkage into a direct measurement. Instead of asserting that L1 regularization distorts activations, the authors run an activation-refinement test that quantifies the shrinkage. This is important because similar-looking decoder recovery can coexist with very different encoder behavior, which later shows up as causal mismatch.

Fourth, the paper introduces a causal validation battery and a taxonomy of inertness. For every correlationally recovered feature, the authors run ablation and sign-correct steering interventions and propagate the effect through the model’s actual output stage rather than stopping at the SAE reconstruction space. This leads to two orthogonal taxonomies. By cause, there is structural inertness and competitive inertness. Structural inertness arises systematically from antipodal-pair superposition geometry combined with a positive-pass encoder, and better SAE training does not necessarily remove it. Competitive inertness is a TopK competition pathology in degraded dictionaries and is tied to numerical boundary instability. By direction, there is read-inertness and write-inertness: ablation can fail to reveal a feature even when steering can affect it, and steering can fail even when ablation suggests relevance. Antipodal pairs can fully dissociate these two notions.

The work is also packaged into a model-agnostic auditing tool, sae-causal-audit. Any object that can encode, decode, and expose its dictionary can be audited, including sae_lens.SAE. The interface is designed to make a documented class of sign-handling bugs hard to express.99b:T9ab,The empirical section is unusually rich and several results are numerically sharp.

First, the superposition phase diagram is reproduced with multi-seed statistics rather than a single run. The paper shows that high-sparsity regions suffer from a convergence artifact: under-training can look like a geometric phase transition. This is fixed with sparsity-aware training budgets. The newly described diffuse sharing regime is quantified by values such as ||W_i||^2 ≈ 1.40 and feature dimensionality D_i ≈ 0.08 under extreme overcompleteness, indicating that features are broadly represented but each occupies only a small dimensional share.

Second, in the TopK-vs-L1 reproduction, the paper directly measures activation refinement and confirms L1 shrinkage rather than treating it as folklore. The excerpt provided here does not include the full Pareto tables, but the qualitative conclusion is clear: decoder alignment alone overstates recovery quality when encoder activations are distorted by shrinkage.

Third, and most importantly, causal validation reveals a strong gap between correlational recovery and causal efficacy. In a degraded SAE, 17 of 22 matched features are causally inert. In a well-trained SAE, only 2 of 22 matched features are inert. More strikingly, inert matches can have cosine similarity as high as 0.9998. This is the paper’s strongest result: near-perfect geometric recovery does not guarantee causal usefulness.

Fourth, the authors run a first small-scale audit on a real published SAE, gpt2-small-res-jb. Against 83 hand-authored concepts spanning unrelated semantic domains, they recover 7 correlational matches, of which 1, or 14%, is causally inert. The sample is small, but the direction is consistent with the toy setting. They also report an unexpected atom-collision phenomenon: a small number of decoder atoms repeatedly appear as nearest matches for dozens of semantically unrelated concepts. This is replicated across three independently constructed concept batches of increasing size and diversity, and a controlled negative case argues against a prompt-template artifact.

Fifth, the reproducibility section explains why byte-exact reproducibility across platforms is unavailable for floating-point training workloads. The paper proposes a two-tier guarantee: SHA-256 byte exactness within one pinned environment, and semantic equality elsewhere with rtol = 1e-4 and boundary-sensitive integer counts allowed to vary by ±1.99c:T755,This is worth a careful read. Start with the central claim and keep it in mind throughout: decoder geometry and causal validity are different empirical statements. Once that is clear, the paper’s structure becomes straightforward.

On a first pass, read the Introduction and the contribution list to see that this is not just another toy SAE reproduction. Then jump directly to the causal validation section, especially the ablation and sign-correct steering protocol. Focus on how interventions are propagated to the model’s actual output layer and how inertness is operationally defined. That is the conceptual center of the paper.

Next, go back to the superposition phase-diagram reproduction. Pay attention to how the high-sparsity convergence artifact is diagnosed, how training budgets are adjusted with sparsity, and what characterizes the diffuse sharing regime. This helps explain why geometrically recovered features can still fail at the encoder or competition stage.

Then read the TopK-vs-L1 reproduction and the activation-refinement test. The key question there is not simply which SAE reconstructs better, but which one recovers features that remain causally actionable. If you usually look only at reconstruction, sparsity, or cosine metrics, this section fills in the missing encoder side.

After that, read the taxonomy and tooling sections. Structural vs competitive inertness and read- vs write-inertness are useful concepts because they turn intervention failure into something diagnosable. Finish with the real-model audit on gpt2-small-res-jb and the atom-collision finding to judge whether the toy conclusions already have echoes in practical SAEs.

If you plan to reproduce the work, Section 8 on reproducibility conventions is also worth close attention.99d:T44b,As a real-world industrial deployment of LLMs in the vertical education domain, this work offers three main takeaways for pretraining research: 1) Vertical domain adaptation path: instead of injecting domain knowledge via continued pretraining, the product uses a "base model + external knowledge connector + domain skill library" paradigm for fine-tuning-free adaptation, providing a reference for low-cost domain deployment of pretrained models. 2) Domain capability evaluation: teaching skills are evaluated against rigor, pedagogical alignment, and classroom usability, with iterative input from frontline teachers — this domain-specific alignment evaluation process is informative for vertical capability alignment after pretraining. 3) Data privacy boundaries: the product explicitly excludes teacher and student data from model training, in compliance with FERPA and other education privacy regulations, offering practical reference for data compliance boundaries in vertical domain pretraining. 更关键的是，他们把条件改写成无量纲形式 ρ_i < 2^{-φ_i}，其中 φ_i 是 log2|wi| 的小数部分，表示参数位于当前 binade 内的相对位置。若 φ_i 近似均匀分布，则 half-ULP 边界对应一个固定的一比特宽区间，其中位阈值给出 ρ* = 1/sqrt(2) ≈ 0.707，没有拟合参数。这个推导解释了为什么冻结阈值是 O(1) 常数，而不是随模型维度变尖锐的相变。

预测器的构造也很直接：先跑一条 fp64 高精度轨迹 {w_t, g_t}，然后对任意目标精度 m，在每个 step 上计算预测冻结比例 \hat f_t(m)=<1[η|g_{t,i}| < 1/2 ULP_m(w_{t,i})]>。\hat f_t 穿过 1/2 的时刻就是预测的 τ*。这里完全不需要低精度训练数据，因此如果预测成立，就说明冻结主要由算术离散化决定，而不是低精度训练反馈改变了动力学。

实验设计上，作者用了两类实现。其一是真实 bf16 硬件。其二是 mantissa-truncation emulator：所有算术在 fp64 中做，但每步后把权重 round 到 m-bit mantissa 网格。这样可以单独研究 mantissa 精度，而不混入 exponent 范围和 denormal 等因素。作者先在 m=7 上验证 emulator 与真实 bf16 一致，再扫 m∈{5,6,7,8,10,12}。这套设计的优点是把问题拆得很清楚：冻结来自权重存储精度本身，而不是某个硬件实现细节。

从全文看，论文还强调了两个细节。第一，冻结 onset 是 crossover，不会因为参数数目变大而变成无限尖锐的临界点，因为 half-ULP band 的宽度天然就是一比特。第二，在多层网络里，全局 L2 聚合的 ρ 可能失真，因为不同层尺度不同，小 bias 向量还可能长期不冻结；因此真正可靠的是逐坐标或分层统计，而不是单个全局标量。这一点对大模型监控很重要。9a0:T9b4,实验分四层展开，逻辑很完整。

1. frozen-feature 线性 GD + 真实 bf16 硬件：作者先在最简单可控的设定里直接观测冻结。step 100 时 frozen fraction f=0，step 300 时 f=1.0，之后训练最后 90% 的过程参数都保持冻结。用首次完全冻结点读取阈值，得到 ρ*≈0.72。

2. mantissa emulator 扫精度与学习率：在 m=7 上，emulator 对真实 bf16 的 freeze curve 拟合 RMSE 仅 0.002，说明它是可信替身。进一步扫 m∈{5,6,7,8,10,12}，覆盖 128× 的精度跨度，以及 4× 学习率范围，得到稳定阈值 ρ*=0.71，跨设置 coefficient of variation 为 0.06。这里最关键的结果不是单点数值，而是阈值几乎不随精度和学习率变化，只是 freeze time 在大范围移动。

3. 先验预测 τ*：这是全文最有说服力的实验。作者只用高精度轨迹和目标 mantissa 位数预测冻结时间，预测与实测在 384× 的 freeze-time 范围内一致，覆盖从 11 到 4222 steps。对可训练网络的 55 个 clean cells，predicted/measured 的中位比值为 1.00，约 94.5% 的 cell 落在 15% 误差内。更重要的是，预测能跟住个体轨迹差异；某些 run 比邻近设置早两个数量级冻结，预测也能提前指出。

4. 可训练非凸网络与真实数据：
- 两层 tanh teacher-student 回归中，emulator 与真实 bf16 的 freeze curve RMSE 为 0.007，阈值约 ρ*≈0.74；跨 seed 的 within-cell CV 中位数为 0.21。说明冻结并不依赖 frozen features 或凸性。
- 一个约 1e5 参数的 CNN，在 MNIST 上做交叉熵训练。emulator 扫 m∈{5,6,7,8,10}、3 个 seeds，共 15 个 precision-seed cells。这里先验预测达到“逐 cell 完全命中”：预测 freeze step 与实测完全相同，中位比值 1.000，最大误差 0%。真实 bf16 硬件上，m=7 的 freeze curve 也被 emulator 以 RMSE 0.02 复现。

5. 124M GPT-2：摘要里已经给出一个关键信号：在 124M GPT-2 上，如果每步后都把权重约束到 8-bit floating-point grid，训练也会在中途进入冻结区。虽然给出的正文片段没有完整展开 GPT-2 数字，但论文的意图很明确：silent freeze 不是小模型玩具现象，而是会出现在标准 Transformer 训练里。

整体上，最值得记住的数字有三个：阈值 ρ* 大致稳定在 0.71–0.74；高精度轨迹预测 freeze time 的中位比值 1.00；预测覆盖 11 到 4222 steps 的 384× 时间尺度。9a1:T805,The analysis starts from floating-point spacing. For a format with m mantissa bits, the spacing at coordinate wi is ULP_m(wi)=2^{floor(log2|wi|)-m}. Under round-to-nearest, a gradient step leaves wi unchanged whenever |Δwi| < 1/2 ULP_m(wi). This gives a per-coordinate freeze condition and leads to a measurable frozen fraction f, defined as the proportion of coordinates that remain bitwise unchanged after a step. The freeze time τ* is the first step where f reaches 1/2.

The key theoretical move is to rewrite the condition in dimensionless form as ρ_i < 2^{-φ_i}, where φ_i is the fractional part of log2|wi| and indicates where the weight lies within its binade. If φ_i is approximately equidistributed, the half-ULP boundary occupies a one-bit-wide band, whose median yields a parameter-free threshold ρ*=1/sqrt(2). This explains why the onset is an O(1) crossover rather than a sharp size-dependent phase transition.

The predictor is deliberately simple. Run one fp64 trajectory {w_t, g_t}. For any target mantissa length m, compute the predicted frozen fraction at each step as \hat f_t(m)=<1[η|g_{t,i}| < 1/2 ULP_m(w_{t,i})]>. The predicted τ* is where \hat f_t crosses 1/2. Since the predictor uses no low-precision data, successful prediction would imply that the phenomenon is governed primarily by arithmetic discretization rather than by altered low-precision dynamics.

The experimental design separates arithmetic effects cleanly. Real bf16 hardware establishes that the freeze is physically present. A mantissa-truncation emulator performs all arithmetic in fp64 but rounds weights to an m-bit grid after each step, allowing controlled sweeps over mantissa precision without confounding exponent range or denormals. The paper also emphasizes an important practical nuance: in multilayer networks, a single pooled L2-based ρ can become misleading because layers live at different scales and tiny bias vectors may never freeze. Layerwise or coordinatewise statistics are therefore more informative than a single global scalar.9a2:T91d,The empirical story is built in stages.

First, in frozen-feature linear gradient descent on real bf16 hardware, the frozen fraction is 0 at step 100 and 1.0 by step 300, after which the iterate remains frozen for the final 90% of training. Reading the threshold at the first fully frozen point gives ρ*≈0.72.

Second, the mantissa-truncation emulator is validated against real bf16 at m=7, reproducing the freeze curve with RMSE 0.002. Sweeping m in {5,6,7,8,10,12} spans a 128x precision range, and varying the learning rate spans another 4x. Across this grid, the threshold remains stable at ρ*=0.71 with coefficient of variation 0.06. The main point is that precision and learning rate shift the freeze time substantially, but not the threshold itself.

Third, the a-priori prediction of freeze time is the strongest result in the paper. Using only the high-precision trajectory and the target mantissa length, predicted and measured τ* agree across a 384x range of freeze times, from 11 to 4222 steps. On 55 clean trainable-network cells, the median predicted/measured ratio is 1.00, and about 94.5% of cells fall within 15%. The predictor also tracks trajectory-specific outliers rather than only average trends.

Fourth, the phenomenon survives beyond convex toy settings. In a two-layer trainable tanh teacher-student regression problem, the emulator matches real bf16 with RMSE 0.007 and the threshold is around ρ*≈0.74. In a CNN with about 1e5 parameters trained on MNIST with cross-entropy, the emulator sweep over m in {5,6,7,8,10} and 3 seeds yields exact freeze-step prediction in all 15 precision-seed cells: median ratio 1.000 and maximum error 0%. On real bf16 hardware at m=7, the emulator still matches the freeze curve with RMSE 0.02.

Finally, the paper extends the observation to a 124M GPT-2 transformer with weights constrained to an 8-bit floating-point grid after each step. The full numerical details are not included in the excerpt here, but the inclusion of this experiment is important: the authors are not claiming a toy-only effect. They are arguing that the same arithmetic mechanism appears in standard Transformer training as well.

The numbers worth retaining are the threshold range 0.71–0.74, the median prediction ratio of 1.00, and the 384x span of accurately predicted freeze times.9a3:T793,Read it in three passes: definition, predictor, generalization.

Start with the opening part of Results where the paper derives the half-ULP condition and rewrites it in terms of ρ and φ. That section determines whether the work is merely empirical or whether it truly pins the effect on floating-point arithmetic. Then inspect Figure 1 carefully: the real-bf16 versus emulator freeze curves, and the predicted-versus-measured freeze times. If those plots are convincing, the main claim is already in good shape.

Next, go to the Methods section for the derivation of ρ*=1/sqrt(2). The important question is not the algebra itself, but why a parameter-free threshold emerges and how credible the equidistributed-φ assumption is in practice. This is also where one should think about whether different parameter classes in large models, such as embeddings, norms, and biases, might violate the assumption.

Then read the trainable tanh and CNN sections. They answer the obvious objection that the effect might only hold in linear or frozen-feature settings. The CNN discussion is especially useful because it shows why a single pooled ρ can fail in multilayer models with heterogeneous scales. That point is highly relevant for real LLM monitoring.

If time is limited, at least read the GPT-2 setup and the main figure around it. The practical questions to keep in mind are: how weights are projected to the low-precision grid, whether AdamW plus cosine is still used, and at what stage of training the freeze appears. Natural follow-up questions are whether fp32 master weights largely remove the issue, whether Adam moments merely delay rather than eliminate freezing, and whether cooldown, weight decay, or norm control can keep ρ away from the danger zone.

A full careful read is about 45 to 60 minutes. A fast read focused on the main claim can be done in about 20 minutes via Results, Figure 1, and the Transformer experiment.9a4:T43d,The framework separates three axes of inference-time scaling. Reasoning scaling spends more tokens before producing an answer. Sampling scaling generates more attempts and selects one. Interaction scaling alternates between proposal, external observation, and revision. The paper defines grounded feedback as observations from an instrument that measures the artifact’s actual behavior or form: running tests, rendering a page and measuring element positions, querying an external source, or measuring a layout. It also defines grounded evaluation as using such observations as the score. A coverage principle ties the two together: feedback helps only for defects that the instrument can observe. This explains why a linter may be grounded but ineffective for behavioral bugs, and why a screenshot-reading VLM can fail as a layout judge. The screenshot may crop away overflow, and small overlaps may be below the judge’s effective visual acuity. The contribution is not another agent loop; it is a sharper account of what kind of feedback and metric make interaction scaling real.9a5:T411,The experiments cover seven artifact-producing modalities: code, web pages, slides, figures, animations, video edits, and research reports. Grounded execution feedback raises two hard coding suites to a 100% pass rate. Grounded geometry feedback removes 40% to 74% of measured layout defects across four visual modalities. A dense academic-figure case shows the evaluation problem clearly: a standard screenshot VLM judge marks 14 of 15 single-shot renders as perfect, while direct measurement finds only 3 clean outputs. Under equal token budgets, reasoning-only and best-of-N saturate; best-of-N saturates even with an oracle verifier, while interaction methods continue improving. The proposer-reviewer harness reaches the gains with lower token cost and zero reported seed variance. Instrument ablations support the grounding thesis: execution feedback beats critique for behavioral bugs, a linter adds little when it observes the wrong property, and a screenshot VLM reviewer worsens slide geometry while a geometry reviewer repairs it.9a6:T84c,方法上，论文从一个很朴素但很有力的恒等式出发：沿着从 clean data 到 pure noise 的退化路径，条件熵 H(X|Y(τ)) 的增量望远镜求和后，得到总熵或更一般的 cross-entropy 的守恒关系。关键难点不在积分形式本身，而在于如何把 joint conditional entropy / CE 的导数，化成可训练、可解释的局部量。作者借用编码理论里的 EXIT / GEXIT 思路，证明在 memoryless channel 下，整体导数可以拆成各坐标的局部导数之和。进一步，在 mismatched setting 中，他们把真实数据分布 P 与模型后验 Q_θ 之间的数据-模型 cross-entropy 写成沿噪声参数 τ 的积分，积分核是局部信息导数项。这样一来，diffusion 的全局 CE 被精确连接到每个噪声级别上的局部去噪质量。

更具体地说，论文的几个技术点值得单独看。其一，统一性来自对“admissible memoryless channel”的抽象，而不是只对 Gaussian 或 masking 特判。Gaussian 情况退化到熟悉的 I-MMSE；离散情况则得到对应的 generalized EXIT 公式。其二，作者证明了 locality property：计算这些信息论导数时，不需要完整的联合后验 P(X|Y(τ))，只需边缘后验 P(X_i|Y(τ))，或者进一步写成 P(X_i|Y_{-i}(τ)) 再结合 channel tilt。这个结论很重要，因为完整联合后验在高维序列上几乎不可建模，而边缘后验更接近实际 diffusion LM 的 token-wise 参数化。其三，论文给出一个实现层面的推论：训练时可以只建模 P(X_i|Y_{-i}(τ))，再用已知 channel likelihood 做倾斜修正得到目标后验。这和 masked LM / pseudo-likelihood / leave-one-out 风格目标有明显亲缘关系，但这里给出了更一般的噪声路径版本。其四，作者反复强调 matched 与 mismatched 的分界：在无限容量、精确后验时，不同 channel 的积分都守恒到同一个 CE；但有限容量下，不同 channel 对后验族的逼近难度不同，因此会出现 channel-dependent gap。也就是说，理论上等价，不代表有限模型下训练等价。9a7:T767,The technical starting point is a telescoping identity over the degradation path from clean data to pure noise. Conditional entropy, and more generally data-model cross-entropy, can be expressed as the integral of its derivative with respect to the noise parameter. The nontrivial step is to turn the derivative of a joint quantity into something local and usable. The paper imports the EXIT/GEXIT machinery from coding theory and proves that for memoryless channels, the derivative decomposes into a sum of coordinate-wise local derivatives.

The main result is a mismatched conservation law for cross-entropy. Instead of assuming the denoiser equals the true posterior, the analysis allows a learned posterior family and shows that the global data-model CE is exactly the integral of local information derivatives along the noise axis. This yields several concrete consequences. One, the framework is channel-agnostic at the level of admissible memoryless corruption and recovers familiar special cases such as the Gaussian I-MMSE relation. Two, there is a locality property: the relevant derivatives depend only on marginal posteriors P(X_i | Y(τ)), not on the full joint posterior P(X | Y(τ)). This is a major simplification for high-dimensional sequence modeling. Three, the paper derives an implementation-oriented implication: it is sufficient to model an extrinsic posterior of the form P(X_i | Y_{-i}(τ)) and combine it with the known channel likelihood through a tilt. That connects the theory to practical token-wise denoisers and to leave-one-out style parameterizations. Four, the paper makes a sharp distinction between matched and mismatched regimes. In the matched limit, all admissible channels conserve the same CE. In finite-capacity settings, however, different channels define posterior families of different complexity, which leads to channel-dependent performance gaps.9a8:T68e,The experiments are designed to validate the finite-capacity claim rather than to optimize benchmark rankings.

The first set uses synthetic Markov sources with known entropy rates. This setting allows direct comparison between the theoretically conserved quantity and what finite denoisers recover under different channels. By varying alphabet size, the paper shows that channel-dependent gaps grow when the posterior family becomes harder to approximate. This is the cleanest empirical support for the main thesis.

The second set studies character-level language modeling on text8. The key comparison is between discrete noising paths and Gaussian noising paths under comparable model capacity. The paper reports substantial channel-dependent differences in CE/NLL, indicating that some channels align better with the discrete structure of text and are easier for finite denoisers to learn. The most useful plots here are the decompositions over noise levels, which show where the model pays the CE cost along the path.

The third set uses CIFAR-10 to show that the same phenomenon is not specific to text. High-dimensional image data also exhibits large finite-capacity, channel-dependent gaps. The practical message is that the conservation law is universal, but the approximation burden imposed on a given model family is channel-specific.

The abstract already states the main empirical takeaway: synthetic data, text8, and CIFAR-10 all show large finite-capacity, channel-dependent gaps. When reading the full paper, the most important numbers are not a single headline metric but the CE, NLL, or bits-per-dim comparisons across channels, alphabet sizes, and capacities.9a9:T4ea,Read it in three passes. First, go through the introduction and the main theorem statements. The key points to lock in are: the conserved quantity is data-model cross-entropy, not just entropy; the scope is general memoryless noising processes; and channel choice matters in practice because of finite-capacity mismatch.

Second, study the derivation that turns the derivative of joint conditional entropy or CE into coordinate-wise local terms. Pay attention to the assumptions behind differentiability, absolute continuity, and the memoryless factorization. These details determine how far the result can be extended to practical diffusion LM variants. If your interest is discrete diffusion or masked LM, the most important part is the proof that marginal posteriors are sufficient.

Third, focus on the implementation implication: how P(X_i | Y(τ)) is related to an extrinsic posterior P(X_i | Y_{-i}(τ)) plus a channel-dependent tilt. This is the bridge from theory to trainable denoisers.

For experiments, start with the synthetic Markov source section because it isolates the mechanism cleanly. Then read text8 for the language-modeling implications. CIFAR-10 mainly serves as a universality check. A careful read will likely take 1.5 to 2.5 hours.9aa:T736,The method is deliberately minimal. Instead of changing attention or introducing a new positional network, the paper keeps the RoPE mechanism and replaces fixed band frequencies with learnable scalars. In the reported setup this adds only 32 parameters per model, which suggests the learned frequencies are shared at the band level rather than expanded per layer and per head. The key point is that the relative-position property of RoPE is preserved: the rotated query-key inner product still depends only on relative offset, but the spectrum is no longer forced to follow a predetermined geometric schedule.

What makes the approach interesting is not just added flexibility, but selective relaxation of the right inductive bias. Compared with learned absolute embeddings, LeRoPE remains a relative positional encoding and therefore keeps the structural advantages of RoPE. Compared with partial RoPE, it does not require manually deciding which low-frequency bands should stop rotating. Compared with changing the base, it does not apply a uniform rescaling to the whole spectrum; it allows non-uniform redistribution across bands. The analysis shows that the learned spectra are highly consistent across scales and random seeds, which argues against the improvement being a fragile optimization artifact.

A second technical contribution is the analysis of attention logits by frequency band. Rather than stopping at perplexity, the paper decomposes positional contributions across bands and finds the emergence of a dominant positional band. This suggests that trained models do not use the RoPE spectrum uniformly. Instead, they seem to concentrate explicit positional signaling in a small part of the spectrum while leaving other bands closer to content channels. LeRoPE appears to help the model discover this allocation more efficiently.9ab:T652,The experimental setup is a scale ladder from 52M to 2.5B parameters, all trained from scratch. The main empirical result is simple and strong: LeRoPE outperforms standard RoPE at every scale. The clearest quantitative statement in the abstract is that at 2.5B scale, standard RoPE requires 3.4% more compute to match LeRoPE. That framing is more informative than a single validation-loss delta because it directly translates into pretraining efficiency.

The analysis results are equally important. Learned frequency profiles are highly consistent across random seeds and model sizes, which indicates that the optimization is finding a stable preferred spectrum rather than exploiting arbitrary extra degrees of freedom. The paper also shows that one band emerges with a much larger positional contribution to the attention logits than the others, termed the dominant positional band. This supports the view that the useful role of the RoPE spectrum is not evenly distributed.

From the provided full-text excerpt, the paper situates its findings relative to partial RoPE, base tuning, and NoPE. When reading the full paper, the most important figures to inspect are the scaling curves, the learned-frequency visualizations, and the band-wise logit decomposition. Those explain the gain better than the headline language-modeling metric alone.

The excerpt does not include all training details such as total tokens, context length, dataset names, or the full ablation table. A skim should take about 25 to 40 minutes. If you are considering adoption, spend extra time on the appendix for initialization, constraints on the learned frequencies, optimizer treatment, and convergence patterns across scales.9ad:T69a,SCOPE-RL is a two-stage framework built on a single design principle: leave the GRPO policy update unchanged, and only densify the reward signal on either side of the success boundary.
1) Stage 1: Adaptive Scaffolded RL (ASR). Hard problems with low success rates are identified via on-policy routing (prompts with zero within-group reward variance where all rollouts are wrong). The problem is decomposed into an answer-hidden sub-question chain, and prefix-consistent verifiable rewards are assigned to each correctly solved sub-question. Sub-question answers do not leak the final answer, and the model must complete prefix sub-questions sequentially to earn subsequent rewards, providing partial progress signal for hard problems without answer leakage.
2) Stage 2: Quality-Aware Process RL (QPR). For problems where the model already produces correct answers, a correctness gate ensures only trajectories with correct final answers receive process-shape rewards. These rewards prefer reasoning paths with higher useful-step density, fewer low-value steps, and clearer error localization, penalizing redundancy and local flaws. Process rewards are bounded to never outweigh correctness rewards, preventing the model from optimizing for brevity at the cost of answer accuracy.
The two stages are naturally sequential: ASR first raises the supply of verified correct trajectories on hard problems, then QPR refines the process quality of those correct trajectories.
A Step-Quality Evaluation Protocol is also introduced, complementing rule-based answer verification with post-hoc LLM-judged diagnostics: useful-step density, low-value step ratio, error localization, and token efficiency.9ae:T4c7,The paper starts from TRPO, where policy improvement is constrained by a KL trust region, and views PPO-Clip as a cheap first-order approximation to that idea. The flaw is that PPO clips the importance ratio r=πθ(a|s)/πold(a|s) with a fixed interval such as 1±ε. For a categorical policy, the local KL expansion is approximately 0.5·Σ Δp(a)^2/p(a). Written in terms of ratio changes, the KL contribution of one action is roughly 0.5·p_old(a|s)·(r−1)^2. A fixed ratio bound therefore gives low-probability actions very small absolute movement and high-probability actions disproportionately large movement. Riemannian Isometric Policy Optimization changes the clip boundary as a function of the local old-policy probability. Rare actions get a wider ratio range; frequent actions get a tighter one. The intended effect is an approximately isometric update under the policy manifold geometry. The paper further argues that this geometry-aware clipping induces a more homoscedastic update signal and improves the bias-variance trade-off. Compared with heuristics such as increasing the upper clip bound or using asymmetric clipping, the key difference is per-state-action adaptation based on local policy geometry.9af:T535,The analysis uses two attention-based probes. The answer-side probe measures how strongly answer tokens attend back to the question. The visual-side probe measures how strongly visual tokens attend to one another. Across depth, these probes reveal a recurring three-stage pattern. Early layers are dominated by question-conditioned organization, where the model frames the image under the query. Middle layers shift toward visual consolidation, where visual tokens interact more strongly and answer-relevant evidence is assembled. Late layers return to language-side answer formation. The authors call the middle interval the Visual Relay Window. Its geometry is task-dependent: counting-like tasks tend to require a broader and later relay, while tasks that rely more on downstream reasoning need an earlier handoff to the language side. TRACE builds on this observation. It uses lightweight prefill-time attention statistics to predict relay layers, applies task-aware scheduling to expand or contract visual relay allocation, and anchors selected visual support after handoff so that decoding remains grounded. Compared with contrastive decoding, fixed attention reallocation, or activation steering, TRACE is more temporally structured: it intervenes according to where the model is in the visual-to-language computation process.9b0:T4e1,UltraX uses function-calling refinement instead of end-to-end text regeneration. The lightweight refiner emits edit operations, not the full rewritten document. Its operation space includes deletion, modification, and insertion, addressing the incomplete edit spaces in earlier function-calling refiners such as ProX and RefineX. Supervision is built through a multi-stage pipeline. Dataset-adaptive prompt optimization first guides an expert LLM to produce higher-quality refined texts. Line Alignment Mapping then converts original-refined text pairs into executable program supervision. Dynamic Context Replacement handles context changes caused by local edits and reduces interference between consecutive operations. Low-confidence examples are filtered, and ratio-controlled sampling balances different operation combinations. At inference time, UltraX uses sliding-window prediction for long documents, global operation aggregation to merge window-level outputs, and post-processing to normalize, validate, and execute the predicted programs. Compared with full-text rewriting, the programmatic route reduces output tokens and makes chunk recombination easier to control. Compared with static rules, it supports instance-level semantic repair.9b1:T4aa,The provided full-text excerpt states that the evaluation includes from-scratch pretraining of 1B-parameter MiniCPM models, which is the right evidence path for a pretraining-data method. The useful part of the design is the closed loop from edited corpus to trained model quality, rather than only reporting edit accuracy or quality-classifier scores. The paper also appears to evaluate the function space, supervision pipeline, and execution reliability through ablations: complete insertion/deletion/modification operations versus restricted edit spaces; Line Alignment Mapping and Dynamic Context Replacement for supervision quality; low-confidence filtering and ratio-controlled sampling for training stability; and sliding-window prediction, global aggregation, and post-processing for long-document robustness. The supplied text does not include the final numeric tables, token counts, corpus scale, or benchmark scores, so those numbers should be checked in the experimental section before quoting.
