In the experiments, prioritize from-scratch pretraining results over standalone editing metrics. The most important tables are likely the comparison against raw data, rule-based cleaning, LLM rewriting, ProX, and RefineX; ablations over operation space; filtering and sampling ablations; and throughput or cost measurements. The main risks to examine are distribution shift from editing, over-normalization of writing style, accidental removal of rare knowledge, and whether the lightweight refiner transfers cleanly to new domains.9b3:T469,Gradient-Routed Auxiliary Modules (GRAM) has three core components. (1) Architecture: each MLP layer in a dense Transformer is augmented with several smaller auxiliary MLP modules, each dedicated to one target capability domain, while the main MLP handles general core capabilities. (2) Training routing: forward and backward passes for auxiliary modules are selectively enabled based on the domain of the current batch. Core data updates only the backbone; data from a specific auxiliary domain updates both the backbone and the corresponding auxiliary module; gradients never flow to unrelated auxiliary modules. This design maps data domains to parameter subspaces, physically isolating the learning of different capabilities. (3) Inference control: ablating an auxiliary module at inference time removes its corresponding capability without retraining; enabling arbitrary subsets of modules produces arbitrary capability profiles from a single deployed model. GRAM combines domain-specific modules, data-dependent selective gradient updates, and per-subset optimizers into an end-to-end pretraining recipe for access control.9b4:T46f,Experiments span synthetic and realistic dual-use datasets, scale from 50M to 5B parameters, and compare against data filtering (gold standard), model branching, FT-LoRA, and post-hoc unlearning. (1) On the Simple Stories synthetic dataset, GRAM closely matches data filtering on both capability retention and removal. (2) In the 800M-parameter realistic setting, the core corpus is web text + code + arXiv papers, with four auxiliary domains: virology, cybersecurity, nuclear physics, and Lisp code. GRAM matches the all-data baseline on core tasks; matches data filtering and FT-LoRA on auxiliary retention and removal; resists malicious finetuning on removed domains substantially better than post-hoc unlearning, approaching the robustness of data filtering. Enabling multiple auxiliary modules does not cause mutual interference. (3) Under partially labeled data, GRAM achieves far better capability removal than both data filtering and branched finetuning. (4) Across 50M–5B compute-optimal models, GRAM's capability profiles closely track data filtering, and suppression of the target forget capability strengthens with scale.9b5:Tb27,方法名叫 Hidden Decoding。核心做法是把原始序列中的每个 token 沿 sequence 维度扩展成 n 个 stream，然后在一次标准前向里处理这条更长的序列，但只对最终 stream 施加 next-token loss。这样，中间 stream 提供的是“隐藏计算”，不是额外可见 token。它和 chain-of-thought 或 test-time visible reasoning 的区别在于：额外计算发生在隐状态里，不增加训练目标里的显式文本监督。

这套设计有两个关键点，缺一不可。

第一，per-stream embedding replication。若只是简单复制同一个 token n 次，多个 stream 的初始状态几乎相同，模型很难学出有分工的内部计算。作者为每个 stream 复制一套词嵌入表，把 token x_i 扩成 (E1(x_i), E2(x_i), ..., En(x_i))。continued pretraining 过程中，这些 embedding table 会逐渐分化，让不同 stream 承担不同的表示角色。这个设计很像给“同一个 token 的多步内部思考”提供不同起点，否则 sequence expansion 很容易退化成重复计算。

第二，persistent intermediate KV。此前一些 length-scaling 方案，比如 PHD，为了不让推理成本爆炸，会把中间重复 token 的 KV 设为 transient，只在当前 token 内部起作用，不作为后续位置的上下文保留。这样虽然便宜，但中间计算不能跨位置积累，能力上更像局部 refinement。Hidden Decoding 反过来保留所有 stream 的 KV，让前面位置在中间 stream 上形成的计算结果，能被后面 token 继续访问。作者认为，只有这样，中间 stream 才不只是“当前 token 的额外层数”，而是能形成真正可持续的 latent computation。

问题随之而来：如果对 nL 长序列做全连接注意力，成本会从原来的 O(L^2) 变成 O(n^2 L^2)，在长上下文和大模型上不可接受。为此论文提出 Stream-Factorized Attention。做法是把跨 stream 的信息交换限制在少数层：大多数层只在各自 stream 内做注意力，只有少数“交换层”允许 stream 间通信，而且这些层沿用 base model 原本的注意力模式，比如 sliding-window 或 full attention。这样，绝大多数层避免了对整个 nL 序列做稠密注意力，额外成本更接近对 n 的线性增长，而不是平方增长。

从建模角度看，这个方法和 recurrent-depth Transformer 的差异很明确。looped 模型是在深度维度重复使用同一组 block，计算图有显式回环；Hidden Decoding 则把额外计算摊平到序列维度，仍然保持一次标准前向，因此天然兼容现有的并行训练栈。和普通 token repetition 也不同，它不是把重复 token 当作可见上下文噪声，而是通过独立 embedding、持久 KV 和受控跨 stream 交互，把重复位置变成内部计算槽位。9b6:T7e9,实验分两部分，分别验证“能否扩到大规模”和“扩展因子 n 是否形成新的 scaling”。

第一部分是大规模能力验证。作者训练了 WeLM-HD4-80B 和 WeLM-HD4-617B，其中 HD4 表示每个 token 扩成 4 个 stream。对照组分别是同 backbone 的 WeLM-80B 和 WeLM-617B。结果上，80B 版本在九个共享 benchmark 上全部提升，文中点名的增益包括 SciCode 45.8→50.0，PHYBench 69.8→73.8。617B 版本同样在九个共享 benchmark 上全部提升，包括 GPQA Diamond 89.1→91.2，HLE 33.6→35.4，FrontierMath 49.0→51.0。这里一个重要细节是：这些比较使用的是相同的、较早期的 SFT-only post-training recipe，没有引入 RL。这样做的好处是把变量控制得更干净，说明增益主要来自 continued pretraining 阶段的 Hidden Decoding，而不是后续对齐流程差异。

第二部分是 expansion factor 的 scaling 实验。作者在 80B 上做 progressive expansion，把 n 从 2 提到 4 再到 8。结果显示 MMLU 单调提升，85.0→86.7→87.5；Pile-test BPB 从 0.386 降到 0.378。前者说明下游能力随隐藏计算增加而继续增长，后者说明语言建模损失也同步改善，不只是 post-train 指标偶然上涨。对预训练研究者来说，BPB 的下降很关键，因为它表明 Hidden Decoding 不是单纯把推理 benchmark 做高，而是在基础建模质量上也有收益。

从论文叙述看，作者还做了若干设计消融，重点应包括：是否必须保留 intermediate KV、是否必须使用 per-stream embedding、跨 stream 交换层的密度如何影响效果与成本、以及 Stream-Factorized Attention 相比全量跨 stream attention 的效率收益。虽然你给出的全文片段没有完整表格，但这些消融是判断方法是否真的抓住机制的关键。若某个组件去掉后性能明显回落，说明 Hidden Decoding 的有效性不是“把序列拉长”这么简单，而是依赖于可持续的多流内部状态。9b7:Ta0f,Hidden Decoding expands each input token into n streams along the sequence dimension, processes the expanded sequence in one standard forward pass, and applies the next-token loss only to the final stream. The intermediate streams act as hidden computation rather than visible reasoning tokens.

Two design choices are central.

First, per-stream embedding replication. If the same token were simply repeated n times with the same embedding table, the streams would start from nearly identical states and the extra computation could collapse into redundant processing. The paper therefore replicates the vocabulary embedding table into n stream-specific tables, so token x_i becomes (E1(x_i), E2(x_i), ..., En(x_i)). During continued pretraining, these tables can diverge and give different streams different representational roles.

Second, persistent intermediate KV states. Some earlier length-scaling approaches keep repeated-token KV transient so that intermediate computation helps only within the current token and does not persist as context for later positions. That keeps inference cheaper, but it limits the extra computation to local refinement. Hidden Decoding instead retains the KV of all streams, allowing latent computation accumulated at earlier positions to remain available to later tokens. This is the paper’s key argument for why sequence expansion can become capability scaling rather than mere local smoothing.

The resulting challenge is attention cost. Full attention over an nL-length sequence would scale as O(n^2 L^2), which is not viable for long contexts and large models. The paper introduces Stream-Factorized Attention to control this. Most layers attend only within each stream, while cross-stream communication is allowed only in a subset of layers. Those exchange layers follow the base model’s original attention pattern, such as sliding-window or full attention. This avoids dense attention over the entire expanded sequence in most layers, making the added cost much closer to linear in n than quadratic.

Relative to recurrent-depth Transformers, the distinction is sharp. Looped models reuse depth and create explicit recurrence through the same blocks, which clashes with pipeline execution. Hidden Decoding flattens extra computation into the sequence dimension and preserves a standard single-pass training graph. Relative to naive token repetition, it adds the ingredients needed to make repeated positions useful as latent compute slots: stream-specific initialization, persistent memory, and controlled cross-stream mixing.9b8:T659,The experiments test two claims: scalability to frontier-scale models and capability gains from increasing the expansion factor.

For large-scale validation, the paper trains WeLM-HD4-80B and WeLM-HD4-617B, where HD4 means four streams per token. Each is compared against a matched non-HD backbone. The 80B model improves on all nine shared benchmarks, with reported gains including SciCode 45.8 to 50.0 and PHYBench 69.8 to 73.8. The 617B model also improves on all nine shared benchmarks, including GPQA Diamond 89.1 to 91.2, HLE 33.6 to 35.4, and FrontierMath 49.0 to 51.0. An important experimental choice is that these comparisons use the same early SFT-only post-training recipe, without RL. That makes the comparison cleaner and supports the claim that the gains come from continued pretraining with Hidden Decoding rather than from downstream alignment differences.

For scaling with expansion factor, the paper runs a progressive study on the 80B model, increasing n from 2 to 4 to 8. MMLU improves monotonically from 85.0 to 86.7 to 87.5, while Pile-test BPB drops from 0.386 to 0.378. The BPB result matters: it shows that Hidden Decoding improves the underlying language-modeling objective, not only reasoning benchmarks after post-training.

The full paper likely includes ablations on persistent KV, stream-specific embeddings, the density of cross-stream exchange layers, and the efficiency trade-off of Stream-Factorized Attention versus denser alternatives. Those ablations are important because they test whether the gains come from the intended mechanism rather than from simply making the sequence longer.9b9:T6a9,This one deserves a careful read. Read it in four passes: motivation, systems constraint, method, evidence.

Start with the introduction and focus on why the paper rejects depth looping in favor of sequence-length scaling. The key is not abstract modeling preference but compatibility with pipeline parallelism. Then study the main Hidden Decoding diagram until three pieces are clear: token expansion into streams, loss applied only on the final stream, and persistence of intermediate KV states across positions. After that, read the Stream-Factorized Attention section closely. This is the engineering hinge of the paper. Without it, the method would likely fail at 100B+ scale. Use the complexity discussion and the architecture figure together to understand which layers are intra-stream only and which layers perform cross-stream mixing.

In experiments, prioritize three things. First, the main 80B and 617B result tables: check whether gains are broad and whether they concentrate on reasoning-heavy tasks. Second, the progressive-expansion study: verify monotonicity and inspect diminishing returns as n grows. Third, the ablations, especially the necessity of persistent KV and stream-specific embeddings. If time allows, also read the throughput, memory, and context-length cost analysis, because practicality is part of the contribution.

The deeper questions worth following up are: whether different streams specialize into distinct functions; how training-time expansion should be handled at inference time; how this scaling axis interacts with MoE, long context, and decoding efficiency; and how Hidden Decoding relates to latent reasoning, visible chain-of-thought, and test-time scaling.9ba:T45c,Visual Pretraining renders scientific PDF pages as images, filters foreground visual patches, represents them as latent tokens in a frozen visual-feature space, and trains the model with next visual latent prediction. The visual sequence is therefore part of the predictive target, rather than an auxiliary condition for text generation. The matched Text Pretraining baseline uses MinerU2.5-parsed text from the same PDFs and applies standard text-token prediction. VP and TP share the same starting checkpoint, the same underlying document corpus, the same continued-pretraining stage, and the same supervised fine-tuning stage. This design isolates the document representation variable. The main technical contribution is the autoregressive visual-latent objective for document pages, together with a controlled comparison showing that preserving layout and visual structure can improve downstream text-only reasoning. The paper also reports stronger cross-modal alignment: matched visual and textual document embeddings move closer in the shared representation space, without explicit image-text pair supervision.9bb:T43f,The core idea is to transform gradients into a near-isotropic coordinate system before quantization, so that uniform FP8 scaling introduces comparable error magnitudes across dimensions. The implementation has three parts: 1) Error diagnosis: Fisher information matrix whitening maps gradients onto a Riemannian manifold where the gradient distribution becomes approximately isotropic, with substantially lower quantization error than in Euclidean space. 2) Geometry approximation: K-FAC is used for Kronecker-factored approximation of the Fisher matrix, but only to construct temporary communication coordinates; the optimizer (Muon) update rule remains unchanged. 3) Selective application: Per-layer quantization sensitivity is first evaluated. K-FAC forward and inverse transforms are applied only to quantization-sensitive layers; all other layers use standard layer-wise Euclidean scaling to keep extra compute bounded. The entire pipeline only alters the coordinate representation during gradient communication and does not affect optimizer state storage or model weight precision.9bc:Tbb0,方法上，Co-LMLM 是一个 decoder-only Transformer，同时承担 LM 和 dense retriever 两个角色。核心设计有四部分。

第一，连续查询检索。模型在自回归生成时，如果输出特殊 token <FACT>，就读取该位置最后一层 hidden state 作为查询向量，而不是再生成一串自然语言查询。这个向量去检索外部索引中的 top-1 key，对应返回一个文本 fact span。系统把这个 span 直接插回上下文，形式是 <FACT> retrieved text </FACT>，然后从 </FACT> 之后继续解码。这样每次检索只额外消耗一个生成步，而不是多 token query decoding。这里的关键不是“把 hidden state 拿来做检索”本身，而是把检索动作内生进 next-token pretraining 流程里，让查询表示由 LM hidden state 自然承载。

第二，KB 形式从 relational tuples 改为 dense key-value store。value 是人类可读的文本 span，保留可编辑和可归因；key 是模型学出来的连续向量，避免关系模板约束。这样外置对象不再要求是显式关系三元组，只要能在文本中标出一个事实片段，就可以进入 KB。

第三，联合训练目标。训练数据中，原始文本的某些 factual spans 被 <FACT> 和 </FACT> 包起来。模型一方面照常做 next-token prediction，另一方面要学会在需要这些 span 时发出能命中对应 value 的查询向量。为此作者引入对比学习式 retrieval loss：每个 factual span 配一个自然语言问题，问题编码得到 query 侧表示，文档中的事实 span 提供正样本，其他 span 构成负样本。论文强调，预处理只规定“这里应该检索什么文本”，而不规定“查询必须长成什么样”，这和 Rel-LMLM 直接合成关系查询文本是根本区别。模型因此可以自己形成更灵活的检索几何。

第四，事实标注与数据构造流水线。为了摆脱 Wikipedia 的实体中心结构，作者设计了一个 annotation pipeline，在自由文本中标出 factual spans，并为每个 span 生成一个以该 span 为答案的自然语言问题。这样训练时既有语言模型上下文，也有 retrieval supervision。这个设计很关键，因为 Co-LMLM 的可扩展性不只来自连续查询，还来自“监督信号不再依赖结构化知识图谱”。从范式上看，它更像是在原始预训练语料上合成 retrieval-aware masking/slotting，再用 contrastive objective 把 slot 与外部 memory 对齐。

和现有方法相比，差异很清楚。它不同于标准 RAG，后者通常在预训练后外挂检索器，LM 本体并未被训练成主动外置知识；它也不同于 Rel-LMLM，后者的查询是离散文本、知识是关系型 tuple、监督路径是预先写死的；它也不同于纯 dense retrieval LM，因为这里返回的是可读文本片段，并直接进入生成上下文，目标是把 factual memory 从参数中迁出，而不是只做文档增强。9bd:T453,The paper addresses a concrete bottleneck in the Limited Memory Language Model line: how to move from a relational, Wikipedia-dependent, query-template-driven external memory setup to a more scalable pretraining paradigm. Rel-LMLM externalizes knowledge into a human-readable KB, but it is constrained in three ways. First, only facts that can be cast into relational tuples are easy to externalize. Second, retrieval is expressed as discrete natural-language queries, which adds decoding cost and limits expressivity. Third, the preprocessing pipeline effectively hard-codes retrieval pathways by synthesizing the exact query form in advance. Co-LMLM aims to keep the attractive properties of LMLMs—editable memory, attribution, direct unlearning via database operations—while replacing discrete relational queries with continuous vector queries and replacing relational tuples with dense-key/text-value memory. The broader goal is to train a model that learns, during pretraining, when to externalize knowledge and how to retrieve it, rather than merely learning to imitate a fixed retrieval template.9be:Tb9b,Co-LMLM is a decoder-only Transformer trained to function as both a language model and a dense retriever. The method has four central pieces.

First, retrieval is triggered by a continuous query. During autoregressive decoding, when the model emits a special <FACT> token, the last-layer hidden state at that position is read out as the retrieval query. This vector is used to search an external index, and the top-1 retrieved textual fact span is inserted back into the context as <FACT> retrieved text </FACT>. Decoding then resumes after </FACT>. Each retrieval therefore costs only one extra autoregressive step, rather than requiring the model to generate a multi-token textual query. The key idea is not just using hidden states for retrieval, but integrating retrieval into the standard LM decoding loop.

Second, the KB is a dense key-value store rather than a relational database. Keys are learned continuous vectors; values are human-readable text spans. This preserves editability and attribution while removing the representational constraints of subject-relation-object schemas. Any factual span that can be marked in text can, in principle, be externalized.

Third, the model is trained with a joint LM-plus-retrieval objective. Training documents contain factual spans bracketed by <FACT> and </FACT>. The model is trained to predict tokens as usual, but also to emit query vectors that retrieve the correct span when needed. Retrieval supervision is provided through a contrastive objective built from question-span pairs: each factual span is paired with a natural-language question whose answer is that span, giving positives and negatives for dense retrieval training. A crucial design choice is that preprocessing specifies only when retrieval should happen and what text should be returned, not the exact textual form of the query. This is the main departure from Rel-LMLM, where the query representation is explicitly synthesized.

Fourth, the paper introduces an annotation pipeline for free-form corpora. Instead of relying on Wikipedia’s entity-centric structure, it marks factual spans in raw text and generates a natural-language question for each span. This creates retrieval-aware pretraining data without requiring a structured knowledge graph. In effect, the pipeline turns raw pretraining text into a retrieval-supervised corpus where factual spans are slotted out of the parametric channel and aligned with external memory.

Relative to prior work, the distinctions are clear. It is not standard RAG, because retrieval is not bolted on after pretraining; the model is pretrained to externalize knowledge. It is not Rel-LMLM, because queries are continuous rather than textual and the KB is not relational. It is also not just a dense retriever attached to an LM, because the retrieved object is a human-readable fact span that becomes part of the generation context, with the explicit goal of shifting factual memory out of the weights.9bf:T821,The empirical story has three main parts.

First, Co-LMLM improves language modeling and factuality at the same time. Across model scales, it achieves lower perplexity than standard non-externalizing baselines and also outperforms comparable Rel-LMLM variants. At the same time, it substantially improves factual precision. The headline number in the paper is that at 360M parameters, Co-LMLM attains lower perplexity than HF SmolLM2-360M despite SmolLM2 being pretrained on roughly 40 times more data. That is not a perfectly controlled recipe match, but it is still a strong signal for data efficiency.

Second, factual QA performance is unusually strong for the scale. The paper reports that the 360M Co-LMLM reaches SimpleQA-verified performance in line with GPT-4o-mini and above Claude Sonnet 4.5. This should be interpreted carefully: SimpleQA is a factual precision benchmark, not a full proxy for broad capability. Still, it directly supports the paper’s claim that externalized factual memory can produce high-precision knowledge access without requiring a much larger parametric model.

Third, scaling beyond Wikipedia works. Extending pretraining from Wikipedia to FineWeb-Edu further improves factual precision. This is one of the most important results in the paper because it directly addresses the main limitation of Rel-LMLM: dependence on corpora where relational supervision is easy to synthesize.

The most useful ablation-level takeaways are mechanistic rather than cosmetic. Continuous queries reduce inference overhead relative to textual relational queries. Supervising retrieval targets without fixing the query form yields more flexible retrieval behavior. And the fact that NLU utility is largely preserved while factual precision rises suggests a better allocation of model capacity away from brute-force memorization and toward retrieval-conditioned use of knowledge. When reading the experiments, it is better to focus on the joint movement of perplexity, factual precision, and utility across scales and corpora than on any single benchmark number.9c0:T697,Start with the method overview and the inference diagram. The critical sequence is: emit <FACT>, use the hidden state as a query, retrieve a textual span, splice it into context, and continue decoding. That sequence explains why the method remains compatible with standard decoder-only training and inference rather than requiring a separate retrieval stack.

Then read the data construction and objective sections carefully. The important distinction is between the LM loss, which teaches the model to use retrieved facts in context, and the contrastive retrieval loss, which teaches the hidden-state query to align with the right fact span. The real innovation is not merely adding a contrastive loss; it is removing the need to predefine the query representation during preprocessing.

After that, go to the experiments comparing Wikipedia and FineWeb-Edu and the head-to-head results against Rel-LMLM. Those sections make it clear which old bottlenecks are actually resolved: data scalability, retrieval flexibility, and factual precision. If time is limited, prioritize the main results table, the corpus-scaling experiment, and the discussion of controllability and unlearning.

There are several good follow-up questions to keep in mind. Whether top-1 retrieval becomes a ceiling in ambiguous or multi-hop settings. Whether inserting fact spans back into context creates a new context-budget bottleneck. How the construction of contrastive negatives shapes retrieval geometry. And whether the model truly reduces parametric memorization rather than simply learning to both memorize and retrieve. Any later probing or memorization analysis on this point would be especially useful.9c1:T454,At each denoising step, the target distribution is the constrained mean-field posterior p_θ(x^0 | x^t, C) ∝ p_θ(x^0 | x^t) · 1[x^0 ∈ C], where the constraint C is represented by a finite automaton. The paper treats the automaton as a graphical model whose support is exactly the set of valid sequences, then performs exact inference on this chain-structured model to obtain per-token marginals under the constrained distribution. These marginals are used for both greedy and stochastic sampling.

Naive forward–backward inference on a chain requires O(L) sequential steps. Inspired by depth-reduction techniques for arithmetic circuits, the paper restructures the linear computation into a binary tree over prefix–suffix state pairs, reducing the number of inference steps to O(log L) without changing the sampling distribution. The resulting algorithm supports exact constraint satisfaction by construction, works with parallel and block-wise remasking schedules under arbitrary schedules, and exposes per-token constrained marginals that can be used as confidence scores for remasking decisions.9c2:T8d2,环境定义在符号 alphabet 上。每个 source symbol 映射到一个或多个全局唯一的多字符 RHS string；全局唯一性保证 contraction 是无歧义的，即任何匹配 RHS 的 substring 都能唯一映射回 source symbol。模型支持两类 primitive inverse operations：expansion 把一个 symbol 替换为 RHS，contraction 把一个匹配 substring 收缩回 source symbol。每一步都序列化为带位置、span 和 rule 的动作，因此生成轨迹可以逐步审计。

预训练从零开始，在 primitive rewrite chains 上训练 Transformer。数据生成器从初始 word 出发，反复采样合法 primitive expansion 或 contraction，并把 resulting word 作为下一步输入。预训练只暴露局部 grammar-consistent dynamics，不包含后续分析中的非 primitive shortcut。作者用 contraction weight ρ 控制预训练分布；默认 ρ=4，它局部提高 contraction move 的采样倾向，但不直接指定最终 contraction frequency 或 chaining length。

post-training 任务是 goal-directed contraction。prompt 由目标 symbol c* 经多次 primitive expansion 得到较长 word，模型只看到 w_prompt，需要生成逐步 contraction trace，最后输出 c*。reward 只有最终答案是否正确的二值信号。由于语法完全可审计，每条轨迹可分成 primitive rule use、valid non-primitive composition 和 invalid rewrite。valid composition 又分为 sequential composition，即把有序 primitive contraction chain 合成一个 macro step；以及 parallel composition，即在一个 emitted step 中合并彼此独立的 primitive contractions。这个 taxonomy 是全文的关键，它把“RL 学到新策略”从 pass rate 变化变成可检查的轨迹结构变化。

方法比较上，RL 与 rejection fine-tuning 形成了清晰对照。RFT 会选择成功样本，也会复制一些 shortcut-like 行为，但其中相当一部分是 spurious rewrite。RL，特别是 GRPO 的 same-prompt contrast，会在同一 prompt 的候选组内相对提高有效结构、压低无效 passenger actions。作者给出 finite-group view 来解释这种选择效应：RL 的优势不只是探索更多，而是把探索质量集中到可复用的合法组合上。9c3:T6cd,实验设计围绕 difficulty 和轨迹分类展开。Difficulty 由 optimal primitive contraction solution 在 256-token generation budget 下的长度定义：Difficulty 1 的 primitive 最优解能放进预算；Difficulty 2 比预算多一个 primitive contraction step；Difficulty 3 多两个 step。RL 训练 mixture 为 60% Difficulty 1、20% Difficulty 2、20% Difficulty 3。评估覆盖 held-out Difficulty 1–6，其中包含训练分布之外的更难 bucket。

关键结果有四点。第一，RL 能解决一些 pretrained model 即使用更大 sampling budget 也很少解决的 held-out problems，且收益在训练后期更明显，并随难度上升而扩大。这支持 finite-budget frontier expansion，而不只是小 k 下的重排序。第二，RFT 早期提升明显，但较快 plateau；它会保留成功轨迹中的 shortcut-like 行为，却无法稳定区分 valid composition 和 spurious rewrite。第三，轨迹分析显示 RL 有阶段性：先增强 primitive reductions，再发现和复用 valid compositions，最后把 sequential macro 与 parallel composition 固化为更稳定的策略。第四，预训练分布会影响后续策略可达性。ρ=4 的默认设置提供了更偏 contraction 的 procedural substrate；第 7 节进一步消融 ρ，检验预训练中 contraction chaining 的组织方式是否影响 RL 后续能否压缩为 macro。

提供内容中没有给出 Transformer 参数量、预训练 token 数、训练步数或具体 pass-rate 数字。因此最可靠的数字是环境和训练设置：256-token generation budget、ρ=4、RL 训练难度配比 60/20/20、评估 Difficulty 1–6，以及 pretraining 只含 primitive chains 而不含非 primitive shortcuts。9c4:T9d1,The environment is defined over a symbolic alphabet. Each source symbol maps to one or more globally unique multi-character right-hand-side strings. Global uniqueness makes primitive contraction unambiguous: any substring matching a right-hand side maps back to exactly one source symbol. The environment supports two inverse primitive operations. Expansion replaces a symbol with one of its right-hand sides. Contraction replaces a matching substring with its source symbol. Each step is serialized with the relevant position, span, and rule, which makes trajectory-level auditing possible.

A Transformer is pretrained from scratch on primitive rewrite chains. The generator starts from an initial word, repeatedly samples valid primitive expansions or contractions, appends the serialized action, and uses the resulting word as the next input. Pretraining exposes the model to local grammar-consistent dynamics, but not to the non-primitive shortcuts analyzed later. A contraction weight ρ controls the pretraining distribution; the default is ρ=4. This locally upweights contraction moves when both directions are available, without directly fixing the realized contraction frequency or chain length.

Post-training uses a goal-directed contraction task. A prompt is produced by expanding a target symbol c* into a longer word w_prompt. The model sees only w_prompt and must generate a contraction trace whose final emitted symbol is c*. The reward is binary and depends only on the final answer. Since the grammar is exactly known, each generated trajectory can be classified into primitive rule use, valid non-primitive composition, and invalid rewrite. Valid composition has two forms: sequential composition, which collapses an ordered chain of primitive contractions into a macro step, and parallel composition, which combines independent primitive contractions in one emitted step. This taxonomy is the technical core of the paper because it turns the vague claim of “new reasoning strategy” into an auditable trajectory property.

The comparison with rejection fine-tuning is important. RFT selects successful samples and can copy shortcut-like rewrites, but many of these are spurious. RL, especially with GRPO-style same-prompt contrast, concentrates probability mass on valid reusable structure and suppresses invalid passenger actions. The finite-group view explains why the advantage is not merely larger exploration volume, but better selection among behaviors produced for the same prompt.9c5:T767,The experiments are organized around difficulty and trajectory structure. Difficulty is defined by the length of the optimal primitive contraction solution under a 256-token generation budget. Difficulty 1 problems have an optimal primitive solution that fits within the budget. Difficulty 2 requires one extra primitive contraction step beyond the budget. Difficulty 3 requires two extra steps. The RL training mixture contains 60% Difficulty 1, 20% Difficulty 2, and 20% Difficulty 3 examples. Evaluation covers held-out Difficulty 1–6, including difficulties beyond the training distribution.

The main findings are clear. First, RL solves held-out problems that the pretrained model rarely solves even with much larger sampling budgets. The gains emerge late in training and become larger as difficulty increases, which supports finite-budget frontier expansion rather than only small-k reranking. Second, RFT improves early but plateaus. It imitates successful traces, including shortcut-like behavior, but does not reliably separate valid compositions from spurious rewrites. Third, trace analysis shows a phased mechanism: RL first strengthens primitive reductions, then discovers and reuses valid compositions, and eventually consolidates sequential macros and parallel compositions into stable strategies. Fourth, the pretraining distribution matters. The default ρ=4 setting creates a contraction-biased procedural substrate, and the ablation in Section 7 tests whether the organization of contraction chaining affects which strategies RL can later compress and reuse.

The provided content does not specify model parameter count, pretraining token count, training steps, or exact pass-rate values. The reliable numerical details are the 256-token generation budget, ρ=4, the RL training mixture of 60/20/20 over Difficulties 1–3, and held-out evaluation over Difficulties 1–6.9c6:T539,This paper is worth a careful read. Analysis of positional contrast in attention scores proves a frequency matching principle: for a dependency profile of width W, the optimal selected frequency scales as θ* ∝ 1/W, meaning training automatically selects frequency bands matched to the dependency scales present in the data. 1) Kernel Decomposition: Breaks the sequential constraint of traditional BSP by partitioning on-accelerator AIV compute units into independent task groups that run in parallel (e.g., most AIVs handle token sending, while a smaller group handles token count computation and prefix sums). 2) Hierarchical Token-level Scheduling: Addresses hierarchical latency differences within superpods, using a hardware-accelerated mapper to generate optimal allocation schedules within 1 microsecond, resolving load imbalance from irregular token traffic.
3) Data-as-Flag: Leverages hardware-native 512-byte atomic load/store support to embed control flags directly in the data payload, achieving implicit consistency without separate control messages and eliminating expensive cross-NPU global synchronization.

Key findings include: 1. During training, the chordal distance between new and old subspaces at each refresh reaches 96.7%–99.6% of the geometric maximum, nearly orthogonal. 2. The difference between two same-step subspaces (0.725√(2r)) is nearly equivalent to the difference across T steps (0.742√(2r)), indicating subspace variation is dominated by estimation noise. 3. The gradient spectrum contains only a small number of reproducible dominant directions (~39 at r=128), followed by a gapless smooth power-law tail. The top-r cutoff lies inside the bulk spectrum, with an adjacent singular value ratio of only ~1.005; per the Davis-Kahan theorem, subspace estimation has inherent randomness. 4. Averaging gradients cannot open a spectral gap, as the tail is power-law signal rather than pure noise, shrinking only as N^(-1/4), so subspace stability cannot be achieved by increasing averaging budget.

The motivation is that late turns may have little reliable supervision because few trajectories survive to them, while blindly truncating rollouts would remove rare but important deep decisions. The controller therefore balances effective KL quality with a coverage-side lower bound; the figure summarizes this as choosing H=max(Heff, Hcov). The effective memorization window is the minimum of these two values, representing the safe interval after which a sample can be reintroduced to the training stream. Based on this signal, Memorization-guided Data Reuse (MDR) continuously tracks per-sample loss retention dynamics during training, adaptively scheduling repeat exposures only when the interval since last exposure exceeds the memorization window, rather than using fixed epoch schedules. Ablations show memorization window length scales positively with model parameter count and total training tokens processed, and negatively with learning rate.9d4:T8da,方法核心是提出 BDLM Mamba-H：一个面向 block diffusion 的 Mamba-attention hybrid，其中“部分双向性”只保留在当前 active denoising block 内，而已完成 prefix 只通过可缓存的前向状态参与条件化。具体做法有几个关键点。

第一，架构层面，attention 层和 Mamba 层都按 block 边界缓存。对 attention 层，缓存对象仍是标准 KV；对 Mamba 层，缓存的是每层在 block 边界处的 forward recurrent boundary state。这样，已完成 block 不需要在每个 reverse diffusion step 重新跑一遍。

第二，作者没有采用全序列双向 Mamba，而是把 reverse-direction scan 限制在当前 block 内。原因很直接：如果反向扫描跨过 clean prefix，那么反向状态会依赖当前 block 的 noisy 内容和 diffusion timestep，prefix 就不再是稳定缓存。把反向扫描裁到 active block 后，prefix 只需要 forward scan，天然可复用；当前 block 仍然保留局部双向 mixing，避免退化成纯因果 denoiser。

第三，训练目标采用 all-block objective。一个训练窗口被切成多个 block，同一窗口内每个 block 都轮流作为“当前去噪目标”，其左侧 clean blocks 作为条件前缀。关键不只是 block-wise loss，而是训练时显式构造与推理一致的 prefix caches：attention KV 和 Mamba forward states 都在训练图里被真实建立，后续 block 的 loss 会直接反向训练这些缓存状态的构造过程。这样，模型学到的不是抽象的 prefix 表示，而是推理时真正要复用的状态。

第四，论文还处理了 diffusion timestep conditioning 与缓存冲突的问题。timestep modulation 只作用于当前 active block，而不污染 clean-prefix cache。否则 prefix hidden state 会依赖当前 reverse step，缓存就失效。这个 factorization 看起来像工程细节，实际上是 block diffusion 与 cacheable recurrent mixer 能否兼容的必要条件。

第五，作为对照，作者系统比较了四类模型：full-sequence attention、full-sequence DiffuMamba-H、BDLM attention、BDLM Mamba-H。这里的价值在于把“block factorization”和“mixer 替换”两个变量拆开，而不是只和一个弱基线比较。9d5:T8b1,The proposed model is BDLM Mamba-H, a block diffusion Mamba-attention hybrid with partial bidirectionality. The key design choice is simple but consequential: bidirectional mixing is retained only inside the current active denoising block, while completed prefix blocks are represented through cacheable forward states.

At the architectural level, attention layers cache standard KV tensors at block boundaries, and Mamba layers cache forward recurrent boundary states. This lets completed blocks remain fixed conditioning context across reverse diffusion steps, instead of being recomputed every time.

The main departure from prior full-sequence DiffuMamba-style models is the restriction of the reverse-direction Mamba scan. A reverse scan over the whole denoising window would make prefix states depend on the current noisy block and on the diffusion timestep, which destroys cache reuse. By limiting the reverse scan to the active block, the model keeps local bidirectional context where denoising needs it, while preserving a stable forward-only prefix representation.

Training is built around an all-block objective. A training window is partitioned into blocks, and each block is trained as the current denoising target conditioned on the clean prefix blocks to its left. The important part is not merely summing block losses. During training, the model explicitly constructs the same cache objects used at inference: attention KV caches and Mamba forward boundary states. Losses on downstream blocks therefore directly train the mechanism that builds reusable prefix states.

The paper also introduces timestep-conditioning factorization so that diffusion-step modulation applies only to the active block. This avoids contaminating clean-prefix caches with timestep-dependent activations. That detail is essential: without it, the cached prefix would vary across reverse diffusion steps and would no longer be reusable.

Methodologically, the paper compares four controlled variants: full-sequence attention, full-sequence DiffuMamba-H, BDLM attention, and BDLM Mamba-H. This is useful because it separates the effect of block factorization from the effect of replacing attention with Mamba-style recurrent mixing.9d6:T78a,The empirical story has two parts: quality and throughput.

For quality, the authors first run a controlled 87M-parameter study on DCLM with tuned hyperparameters. The headline result is C4-en validation perplexity: BDLM Mamba-H reaches 61.6, compared with 76.5 for BDLM attention, 83.7 for full-sequence DiffuMamba-H, and 87.6 for full-sequence attention. This is the strongest evidence in the paper. It suggests that the gain is not coming from Mamba alone or from block diffusion alone, but from the combination of cache-aligned block factorization, local bidirectionality in the active block, and training that directly supervises reusable prefix states.

The models are then scaled to 350M parameters, comparing BDLM attention and BDLM Mamba-H under a Complete(d)P-style learning-rate transfer rule. At this scale, BDLM Mamba-H remains comparable to BDLM attention in perplexity, which is important because it shows the throughput gains are not bought by a large quality collapse.

For throughput, training throughput is measured at 8192 context on 8×A100-80GB, while inference throughput is measured with a 700M randomly initialized model on 1×A100-80GB at batch size 1. As generation length increases, BDLM Mamba-H overtakes both BDLM attention and full-sequence DiffuMamba-H. At 65K context, it reaches 19.7× the throughput of full-sequence DiffuMamba-H. At 262K, it is still 3.7× faster than BDLM attention. The trend matches the intended mechanism: as the prefix grows, attention cache traffic becomes increasingly expensive, while Mamba boundary states remain compact.

The most meaningful ablation insight is structural rather than cosmetic. Restricting reverse scans to the active block is necessary for stable caching, and the all-block objective is necessary to train the exact recurrent boundary states reused at inference. The paper’s experimental design supports the claim that both pieces matter together.9d7:T584,Start with the introduction and the main method figure to fix the problem setting. Naive BSA computes full attention, aggregates token-level attention mass within each chunk, and selects the top-K chunks with the largest mass. This is too expensive to use as an efficient method, but it provides a full-attention-derived target pattern for chunk selection. HiLS approximates this pattern without the full-attention pass. It appends a landmark token to each chunk and uses it to form a trainable chunk summary key. The query-summary scoring function is motivated as a first-order Taylor approximation to the chunk mass induced by full attention. The second component is a hierarchical factorization of attention. A query first allocates mass across retrieved chunks, then computes token-level attention independently within each selected chunk, and finally fuses the chunk-specific outputs using the retrieval scores. The important distinction from prior sparse attention methods is that the chunk score is not merely a pre-selection heuristic. It participates in the actual forward computation and is trained under the LM loss.9d9:T4c5,The method has two stages: structural compression followed by capability recovery. The structural stage uses Iterative Puzzle, a sequential version of the Puzzle framework. Instead of compressing the model in one large step, it alternates hardware-aware structural compression with short knowledge-distillation recovery phases. This allows each compression step to account for representation drift and inter-layer dependencies introduced by earlier steps. The compressed dimensions include heterogeneous channel pruning of routed MoE experts, heterogeneous reduction of active experts, and pruning of the SSM state size in Mamba layers. The main design choice is non-uniform capacity allocation across depth: sensitive regions keep more capacity, while more redundant regions are compressed harder. During training, prefixes are sampled from this pool; the student generates its own action at the target step, environment observations are read directly from stored trajectories instead of executing live environment calls, and the teacher only provides per-token distribution supervision at the current step rather than generating full trajectories. Theoretically, the gap between ReOPD and the ideal interactive OPD objective is decomposed into two terms: a student occupancy mismatch term from using non-student-generated prefixes, and a teacher reliability term from error when the teacher provides supervision on OOD student-induced histories, proving fully on-policy training is not universally optimal. Guided by this decomposition, multi-turn OPD is framed as reliability-aware prefix distribution design, using a geometric bridge between student and teacher prefix occupancy. A simple step-decay sampling schedule is used for implementation: early in training and for early interaction steps, more student-on-policy prefixes are used when the teacher-student gap is small and the teacher remains reliable; later in training and for late interaction steps, more replayed teacher prefixes are used to reduce noise from unreliable teacher supervision. 第二步是定位机制。作者先看 attention，发现加入 filler 后，answer token 不再主要直接看 question，而是形成 question→filler→answer 的 relay 结构。这个观察本身还不够，因为 attention 不等于 computation。于是他们进一步用 logit lens 在每一层、每个 filler 位置上读 residual stream，检查哪些中间值在何时出现。结果显示，不同任务的中间变量会按时间和位置逐步浮现：例如 2-fact addition 中，A1 往往在 filler 前段较早层出现，A2 在后续位置出现，而 A1+A2 的和在靠近答案前的晚层才稳定“结晶”。这说明 filler 区域不是均匀缓存，而是有阶段性的计算轨迹。

第三步是做因果验证。作者采用 KV-cache transplant，只替换 filler token 对应的 KV 行，而不动问题和答案位置，观察答案分布是否随 donor example 改变。如果仅移植 filler 区域就能显著把答案 logits 推向 donor 的中间值或最终答案，那么 filler 中编码的内容就不是旁观信号，而是实际参与了生成。更细的一步是只移植那些 logit lens 已经能读出 addend 的位置，发现大部分效应都能保留；移植互补位置则几乎无效。这把“某些特定 filler 位置承载关键中间量”从相关性推进到了位置级因果性。

在无监督恢复部分，作者给出一个很实用的 pipeline：对所有 layer-position 做 logit lens，减去跨样本均值以抑制系统性伪影，再跨位置聚合 token 分数，把 top-50 候选交给 LLM judge 解释。这个流程不需要中间变量标签，也不训练 probe，重点是证明隐藏计算并不一定需要重监督才能恢复。与常见 probe 工作不同，这里更强调“可审计性”而不是“线性可分性”。9e0:Ta01,The method proceeds in three stages. The first stage establishes the behavioral phenomenon. The authors build four task families with explicit intermediate values: 1-fact addition, 2-fact addition, 2-hop letter-position queries, and a system-of-equations task where the relevant values are computed entirely in context. They insert content-free fillers between the question and the answer slot, using dots, counting sequences, and alphabet sequences. This task design is important because it spans both retrieved intermediates and in-context computed intermediates, reducing the chance that the effect is just a retrieval artifact.

The second stage localizes the mechanism. Attention analysis shows that when filler is present, the answer token no longer relies mainly on a direct question-to-answer path. Instead, the model forms a relay structure: question to filler to answer. Since attention alone is not computation, the paper then applies the logit lens at every layer and filler position to inspect what is present in the residual stream. The resulting picture is temporally and spatially structured. In 2-fact addition, one addend tends to appear early in the filler region, the second later, and the sum stabilizes only in late layers near the answer. This suggests that the filler region is not a passive buffer but a staged computational trajectory.

The third stage tests causality with KV-cache transplantation. The authors replace only the KV rows corresponding to filler tokens, leaving the question and answer positions untouched, and measure whether the answer distribution shifts toward the donor example. If swapping only the filler region changes the answer, the filler content is not merely correlated with the computation; it participates in it. They further restrict transplantation to positions where the logit lens already decodes an addend and find that most of the effect is preserved, while the complementary positions carry little effect. This gives position-level causal evidence that specific filler locations encode specific intermediate values.

The unsupervised recovery pipeline is also notable. It applies the logit lens over all layer-position pairs, subtracts the cross-example mean to remove shared artifacts, aggregates scores across positions, and sends the top-50 candidate tokens to an LLM judge for interpretation. No intermediate labels and no trained probe are required. Compared with standard probing work, the emphasis here is less on linear separability and more on practical auditability of hidden computation.9e1:T8e8,The study uses two open-weight frontier models: DeepSeek V3 (about 671B total parameters, roughly 37B activated per token) and Kimi K2 (about 1T total parameters, roughly 32B activated per token). Behaviorally, filler tokens improve accuracy across all four task families. On DeepSeek V3, 1-fact addition rises from 54% to 72%; 2-fact addition from 21% to 24%, with 9% of examples flipping from wrong to right; 2-hop letter position from 61% to 70%; and the system-of-equations task from 31% to 61%. On Kimi K2, 2-fact addition rises from 27% to 35%; 2-hop letter position from 69% to 75%; and the equations task from 18% to 36%. The largest gains appear on tasks that clearly benefit from extra intermediate computation, especially the in-context equations setting.

The filler-type ablation is informative. Dots, counting sequences, and alphabet sequences produce similar gains, while scrambled sequences underperform. This suggests that the model benefits from a non-disruptive token scaffold with stable positional structure, not from any particular semantic content. In other words, the filler acts more like extra computational runway than extra knowledge.

The mechanistic evidence is strongest in the KV-transplant experiments. Attention maps show increased reliance on filler positions, and logit-lens readouts reveal intermediate values across layers and positions. But the key result is that transplanting only the filler KV rows can move the donor answer upward by tens to hundreds of ranks, for both retrieved facts and values computed in context. When transplantation is restricted to positions that decode an addend, most of the effect remains; the complementary positions contribute little. This argues for localized functional structure rather than diffuse storage across the whole filler span.

In the unsupervised recovery experiments, the strongest LLM judge recovers intermediate values with 80% to 95% accuracy across both models and all four task families. The recovered content includes numeric facts, string-valued entities such as city or element names, and variables computed inside the prompt in the equations task. That result matters because it shows that hidden reasoning traces can be extracted without supervised labels for the intermediate steps.9e2:T71a,Read it in the order of phenomenon, mechanism, causality, and recovery. Two main results are derived constructively. First, at finite attention scale, induction heads perform soft context matching: every candidate context in history is scored by its overlap with the current context (including non-contiguous matches), and next-token predictions are aggregated with weights exponential in that overlap. HERMES first applies a Learned Semantic Transform, h_i = normalize(W e_i + b), with W initialized as the identity. The transform is trained to make the embedding space more quantization-friendly while preserving semantic structure. The losses include pairwise structure preservation, quantization-aware reconstruction, and an orthogonality constraint to avoid degenerate rotations. A three-stage residual vector quantizer then emits a code (c1, c2, c3), with codebook size K=256 at every stage. The first stage gives L1 buckets, the first two stages give L12 buckets, and all three stages give L123 buckets. In the observed corpus this corresponds to 256 buckets, roughly 65k buckets, and roughly 130k cells. Since all resolutions come from the same trained codebook stack, changes in downstream behavior can be attributed to granularity and sampling rules rather than to different reclustering runs. For training mixtures, the outer weights are kept at the L1 level using Uniform or DoReMi, which avoids fitting a high-dimensional mixer over tens of thousands of cells. The Stage-2 sampler controls which documents are drawn within the coarse buckets.
