At each streaming step, newly observed audio-visual units are immediately consumed, and generated audio-visual units are committed back into the interaction history. This lets the model condition future behavior on both the user and its own previous actions. The full stack is causal: audio and video VAEs, audio-visual encoders, audio and video decoders, and the temporal Transformer are all designed for streaming. The generation path avoids a hidden text bottleneck; speech and visual latents are generated from the same persistent state. At inference time, the model is scheduled as a thinker-performer pipeline. The thinker encodes current user observations, runs the short token-causal Transformer pass, predicts language, and updates KV-cache. The performer receives the new KV context and runs the flow-matching solver for the next audio-visual latent unit. The previous latent unit is returned to the thinker, decoded, and emitted. This keeps a unified causal state while overlapping perception, decoding, latent generation, and communication.a47:T95e,技术路线分三层。

第一层是构造 sandbox。作者把图上的随机游走序列当作离散生成任务：节点 ID 是 token，长度为 L 的 walk 是训练样本，模型只从样本学习，从不显式看到图 G 或转移核。评测时则利用图结构做两类精确指标：一是 coherence / validity，检查相邻 token 是否真有边相连；二是 transition TV distance，从生成样本估计转移核，与真实随机游走核比较分布保真度。这个设计的好处是，latent structure 对模型是隐藏的，对研究者却是可控的，因此可以系统改变图密度、瓶颈、端点约束、Markov 阶数，观察采样器行为如何变化。

第二层是理论分析。论文先证明：在 perfect conditionals 下，单坐标 sequential unmasking 是 order-invariant 且精确的，因为它等价于链式分解；但 parallel unmasking 不再有这个性质，因为它把真实 block conditional 近似成多个单点条件分布的乘积，只有在这些坐标条件独立时才精确。作者构造了简单 DAG / graph 例子，证明 lowest-entropy 两两并行揭示有时优于 random，有时反而更差，因此任何只依赖局部 uncertainty score 的策略都不可能 uniformly optimal。关键决定因素不是 token 自身熵，而是 reveal set 内部以及与已知上下文之间的条件分离结构。

第三层是提出 bisection-style sampler。直觉来自 Markov separation：对一阶随机游走，如果先揭示中间位置，它会把左右两段在条件上分开；对 k 阶 Markov walk，则需要揭示一个大小匹配阶数的 separator block。算法上就是先揭中间 separator，再对左右子区间递归并行处理。作者证明，在 perfect conditionals 下，这个 coarse-to-fine schedule 对无条件随机游走和端点条件随机游走都可以做到精确采样；对 order-k 情况，NFE 复杂度是 O(k log(L/k))，并行深度显著低于逐点采样。

论文最后把这个思路迁移到真实文本 MDM。虽然语言不满足显式 Markov 图结构，作者仍然把“先揭能分隔依赖的锚点，再递归细化”当作 schedule 设计原则，在预训练 OpenWebText masked diffusion 模型上测试。这里的意义不在于证明语言也满足同样定理，而在于说明 graph sandbox 学到的 sampler inductive bias 可以转移到自然语言生成。a48:T8f8,The paper has three technical layers.

First, it builds a verifiable sandbox. Training data are random walks on a hidden graph. Tokens are node IDs, and the model only sees sampled sequences, never the graph or transition kernel explicitly. At evaluation time, the graph provides exact structure-aware metrics: coherence or validity, meaning whether every adjacent token pair is a legal edge, and transition total variation distance, obtained by estimating the Markov kernel from generated walks and comparing it to the true one. This gives a Sudoku-like setup where latent constraints are hidden during training but exactly testable afterward.

Second, it develops theory for sampler separations. Under perfect conditionals, sequential one-coordinate unmasking is exact and order-invariant because it follows the chain rule. Parallel unmasking is different: it approximates a block conditional by a product of coordinate-wise conditionals, which is exact only when the chosen coordinates are conditionally independent given the current context. The authors construct simple graph and DAG examples showing that lowest-entropy two-at-a-time unmasking can beat random parallel unmasking on some structures and lose on others. This rules out any claim that a purely local uncertainty score is uniformly optimal. The decisive factor is dependence structure, not uncertainty alone.

Third, the paper proposes bisection-style samplers. The idea comes from Markov separation. For first-order walks, revealing a middle position can separate the left and right halves conditionally; for order-k walks, one needs a separator block of size matched to k. The sampler reveals the middle separator, then recurses on the two sides in parallel. Under perfect conditionals, the authors prove exactness for both unconditional and endpoint-conditioned walks. For order-k Markov walks, the number of function evaluations scales as O(k log(L/k)), giving logarithmic parallel depth rather than linear sequential depth.

They then transfer the scheduling idea to a pretrained masked language model on OpenWebText. The claim is not that language literally satisfies the same graph theorem, but that the graph sandbox reveals a useful design principle: reveal dependency-separating anchors first, then refine recursively.a49:T7d2,The experiments are split between graph walks and natural language generation.

In the graph sandbox, the paper compares sequential decoding, random parallel unmasking, entropy-guided parallel policies, and bisection-style samplers. The main empirical pattern is that sampler rankings flip with graph structure. On trees and strongly coupled path-like graphs, entropy-guided parallel updates often commit too early to correlated choices, hurting coherence and transition fidelity. When extra Erdős–Rényi edges are added, creating many alternative routes, low-entropy anchors can become genuinely useful. This directly supports the theoretical claim that parallel decoding quality is governed by conditional dependence rather than uncertainty alone.

For endpoint-conditioned walks and higher-order walks, bisection-style schedules are especially effective because the separator block aligns with the underlying structure. The theoretical complexity is O(k log(L/k)) NFEs for order-k walks, and empirically these samplers achieve better validity and lower transition TV distance at similar or lower inference cost. The important point is not a single headline number, but the consistency across graph families and constraint settings.

The language experiments use a pretrained masked diffusion model on OpenWebText. There, bisection-style schedules improve the non-autoregressive speed-quality tradeoff over standard parallel schedules across MAUVE, generative perplexity, entropy, and repetition. The paper’s emphasis is not absolute quality against autoregressive baselines, but reduced quality loss at a fixed or lower number of denoiser calls.

From a pretraining perspective, two experimental aspects are especially informative. Higher-order walk results show that separator size must match the effective memory order of the target process. Endpoint-conditioned walks act like globally constrained infilling tasks and make the failure mode of naive parallel factorization much easier to see.a4a:T512,The framework is built on three core components: First, theoretical grounding: The order selection problem is formalized as minimizing the KL divergence between the data distribution and the distribution induced by the decoding procedure. A tractable upper bound on this intractable objective is derived, expressed in terms of the frozen denoiser's pathwise log-likelihood under teacher forcing. This bound yields a dense, model-self-aware reward signal that assigns credit to every unmasking decision: an optimal order selects the next token that maximizes the expected future log-likelihood of the remaining trajectory, rather than the token with highest local certainty. Second, Self-Aware Scheduling (SAS): A lightweight order policy is trained with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) while keeping the base denoiser frozen. At each decoding step, the policy outputs a distribution over currently masked positions to select the next token to unmask. The policy is plug-and-play, and works seamlessly for both token-level any-order decoding and blockwise semi-autoregressive decoding. Third, optional second-stage fine-tuning: The base model is fine-tuned for a small number of steps along the learned optimal trajectories using the same self-aware objective, to deliver additional gains.a4b:Ta3b,方法分两部分：现象刻画和解码策略。

现象刻画上，作者不是只看 layer-wise accuracy，而是结合 residual stream 的层间位移、各层对最终 logits 的贡献范数、以及 token 预测轨迹的演化，去识别哪些 token 在中间层已经进入稳定语义轨道，哪些 token 在最后几层发生了明显偏转。全文把这种偏转解释为 late-stage perturbation，并把它和 planning–pragmatics tradeoff 联系起来：模型内部已经形成了偏推理的 token 倾向，但末层更偏向输出通用、安全、礼貌、对齐友好的 continuation。这个 framing 比单纯说“中间层有时更好”更有信息量，因为它把问题限定在 near-final layers 的局部选择，而不是鼓吹浅层替代深层。

具体算法是 Confident Decoding。它不做 early exit，也不改 transformer 前向。每个生成步仍然完整跑到最后一层，但额外从一个近末层窗口中取出若干层 logits，通常是最后几层到倒数十来层的一个小窗口。然后用 token entropy 作为置信度指标，从最后一层向前做 conservative backward search，寻找第一个局部 entropy trough，也就是在末层扰动出现前，分布已经足够尖锐、但还没有被后续层重新拉偏的位置。选中的那一层 logits 直接用于 greedy decoding 或后续采样。

这里的关键设计不是“选最低熵层”，而是“保守地向后回溯到第一个局部低谷”。如果直接全局选最低熵，容易落到过早层，分布虽然尖锐但语义尚未成熟；如果固定选某个中间层，又无法适应不同 token、不同任务、不同上下文的层深差异。作者因此把 layer selection 写成 optimal stopping 问题：在 bounded projection noise 和 late-stage perturbation 占主导的条件下，最优策略是停在扰动前的高置信点，而不是机械地走到最后一层。这个理论部分不是严格刻画真实 transformer 的完整动力学，但足以解释为什么“第一个局部低谷”比“最终层”或“固定早退层”更合理。

和已有方法相比，区别主要有三点。第一，它不是 contrastive decoding 那种用层间差分去抑制某些 token，而是直接替换输出层。第二，它不以省算为目标，因此保留完整前向，避免 early exit 破坏后续层对其他位置的计算。第三，它的选择是 token-level、step-level 动态的，而不是为整个模型预设一个静态 exit layer。全文也强调，这种做法更像是在 near-final layers 中寻找“语义最清楚的读出点”。a4c:Ta9d,The paper has two technical components: diagnosing the layer dynamics and designing a decoding rule.

On diagnosis, the authors do more than compare layer-wise accuracies. They analyze residual-stream shifts, contribution norms to logits, and token prediction trajectories across depth. This is used to identify tokens whose semantics stabilize in intermediate layers and tokens whose predictions are noticeably redirected in the final layers. The paper interprets this as late-stage perturbation and frames it as a planning–pragmatics tradeoff: the model internally forms a reasoning-oriented token preference, but the final layers may redirect it toward generic, safe, polite, or alignment-preferred continuations. That framing is more precise than simply saying intermediate layers can be better, because it localizes the issue to a near-final readout problem rather than a broad claim that shallow layers should replace deep ones.

The proposed method, Confident Decoding, keeps the full forward pass intact. It is not an early-exit method. At each generation step, the model still computes all layers, but the decoder additionally reads logits from a small near-final layer window. Entropy is used as a confidence proxy. Starting from the final layer and moving backward conservatively, the algorithm selects the first local entropy trough—intuitively, the point where the distribution has already become sharp, but before a possible late-layer perturbation has redirected it. The selected layer’s logits are then used for greedy decoding or downstream sampling.

A key design choice is that the method does not simply pick the globally lowest-entropy layer. That would often favor layers that are too early: sharp but semantically immature. Nor does it use a fixed intermediate layer, because the best readout depth varies across tokens, tasks, and contexts. The paper formalizes layer selection as an optimal stopping problem. Under bounded projection noise and dominant late-stage perturbation, the preferred policy is to stop at a high-confidence point before the perturbation, not to mechanically decode from the final layer. The theory is stylized rather than a full model of transformer dynamics, but it gives a coherent rationale for the “first local trough” rule.

Relative to prior work, the differences are clear. It is not contrastive decoding that subtracts or contrasts layers while keeping the final layer as the semantic anchor. It is not an efficiency-oriented early-exit method. And it is dynamic at the token and step level, rather than assigning one static exit layer to the whole model. The method is best understood as searching for the cleanest near-final semantic readout point.a4d:T90f,The evaluation spans reasoning, math, long-context understanding, coding, and safety, using benchmarks such as GPQA-Diamond, HLE, Omni-MATH, LongBench v2, LiveCodeBench v6, and Air-Bench-2024, across both dense and MoE models. The headline result stated in the paper is consistent improvement over standard greedy decoding and strong contrastive baselines, with negligible memory overhead and less than 2% extra latency. The more important evidence in the full paper comes in three forms.

First, the layer-dynamics analysis shows token-level cases where the correct answer token becomes top-ranked in an intermediate layer, only to be replaced in the final layers by a generic token, a formatting token, or a safer alternative. Entropy curves often show a clear confidence trough in the near-final region followed by a redistribution at the last layers. This is especially visible on difficult reasoning, math, and coding examples.

Second, the method is compared against static layer selection, final-layer decoding, and contrastive decoding baselines. Static exits help only on subsets of tasks because the best readout depth is not fixed. Contrastive methods can suppress some undesirable continuations, but they still treat the final layer as the main anchor and therefore do not fully address a global late-layer redirection. The gains of Confident Decoding come from token-wise dynamic layer choice rather than merely exposing intermediate-layer information.

Third, the paper reports a scale-related trend: larger and stronger models tend to exhibit more pronounced late-layer perturbation, making dynamic layer selection more useful. That is an important observation because it argues against the effect being just small-model noise or undertraining. Instead, it may be tied to stronger post-training, style control, and more aggressive semantic compression in capable models.

From the provided text, the only explicit hard number is the latency overhead below 2%. Exact benchmark deltas, model sizes, and window settings need to be checked in the tables. When reading, it is worth verifying whether the gains are concentrated in greedy decoding, whether they persist under sampling or self-consistency, how safety improvements are measured, and whether dense and MoE models prefer similar near-final windows.a4e:T65f,Start with the introduction and the main figure that illustrates Guess–Refine–Perturb. The goal is to build intuition for the claim before looking at the algorithm. Then go directly to the method section and inspect the entropy-guided conservative backward search in detail. One important point to confirm is that the method does not truncate the transformer and does not train an auxiliary head on intermediate states.

After that, read the theory section with a narrow objective: understand how the authors cast layer selection as an optimal stopping problem, what assumptions they need, and what those assumptions leave out. If you care about the pretrain/post-train interface, this section is useful because it offers a way to think about late-layer shifts as added bias or perturbation rather than continued semantic refinement.

For experiments, read along three tracks. First, inspect the layer-wise entropy and token-trajectory visualizations to judge whether the phenomenon is broad or anecdotal. Second, read the main result tables comparing final-layer decoding, static intermediate layers, contrastive baselines, and Confident Decoding. Third, check the ablations: near-final window size, search rule, whether the local trough criterion matters, and how selected layers distribute across tasks. If time is limited, the phenomenon figures, main tables, and layer-selection histograms should be enough to capture the paper in 30–40 minutes. If reading more deeply, spend time on failure cases and ask whether the method could introduce regressions on factual QA, casual chat, or strongly safety-constrained prompts.a4f:T83a,技术主线分两层。第一层是理论分析。作者从 clipped policy-gradient 形式出发，把 RLVR 中单 token 更新写成 advantage、token 概率、IS ratio 与 clipping 的组合，并把关注点放在条件梯度期望上，而不是未裁剪的瞬时梯度。关键分析对象是 off-policy degree 对 ratio 方差的影响：随着每个 rollout 上执行更多 gradient steps，当前策略相对 behavior policy 漂移增大，低概率 token 的 ratio 更分散，更容易落到 clipping 区间外。由此得到一个核心现象：gradient dominance reversal。接近 on-policy 时，低概率 token 因为 1/p 型放大效应更容易主导更新；但在更 off-policy 的 regime 下，它们先被更强烈地裁剪，反而是高概率 token 留下更多有效梯度。这个结论用来统一此前“高熵优先”和“高概率优先”两类经验做法。

第二层是分解更新的 magnitude 和 direction。论文不只看谁贡献大，还看 clipping 如何让更新方向偏离 on-policy 梯度。作者按 token probability、advantage 符号与大小、以及 ratio clipping 的交互来分析：正 advantage 与负 advantage 在上下界裁剪下受到的影响并不对称；不同 token 组的 ratio dispersion 不同，意味着同一个全局 [1-ε_l, 1+ε_h] 会对某些组过紧、对另一些组过松，结果既改变梯度大小，也引入方向旋转。

基于这个诊断，作者提出 ACPO（Adaptive Clip Policy Optimization）。核心不是再设计一个新 advantage，而是把固定全局 clipping 改成按 token bin 自适应的 clipping threshold。bin 的划分围绕 token 组的异质性来做，目标是让不同组面对更匹配的裁剪范围，减少某一类 token 因 ratio 方差更大而被系统性压制。ACPO 还显式面向 variance-aware clipping：根据各 bin 的 ratio dispersion 调整上下界，从而同时缓解 uneven clipping 和 clipping-induced bias。与 DAPO、CISPO 这类方法相比，它不是直接偏向高概率或高熵 token，而是把“该保留谁”交给 ratio 分布本身决定。a50:T868,The paper has two technical layers. The first is a theoretical analysis of clipped policy-gradient updates in RLVR. Starting from the GRPO-style objective, the authors write token-level updates as a function of token probability, advantage, importance ratio, and clipping. The key quantity is the conditional expectation of the effective gradient after clipping, not the raw unclipped gradient. They then connect off-policy degree to the variance of the importance ratio: with more gradient steps per rollout, policy drift increases; low-probability tokens develop more dispersed ratios and are clipped more often. This yields the central phenomenon of gradient dominance reversal. In near on-policy regimes, low-probability tokens can dominate because of stronger amplification. In sufficiently off-policy regimes, those same tokens are disproportionately clipped, and higher-probability tokens end up dominating the surviving update. This is the mechanism used to reconcile prior empirical heuristics.

The second layer analyzes not only update magnitude but also directional bias. The paper decomposes how token probability, advantage sign and magnitude, and asymmetric clipping interact. Positive- and negative-advantage tokens are affected differently by upper and lower clipping bounds. Because ratio dispersion differs across token groups, a single global clipping interval over-regularizes some groups and under-regularizes others. The result is not just uneven gradient magnitude, but also a rotation of the update direction relative to the on-policy gradient.

Motivated by this, the authors propose ACPO, Adaptive Clip Policy Optimization. The main idea is simple but targeted: replace one global clipping range with bin-wise adaptive thresholds. Bins are constructed to reflect heterogeneous token groups, and the clipping thresholds are adjusted according to ratio dispersion. The goal is to reduce uneven clipping and mitigate clipping-induced gradient bias. Compared with methods such as DAPO or CISPO, ACPO does not hard-code a preference for high-probability or high-entropy tokens; it adapts clipping to the observed ratio statistics.a51:T655,The empirical section is more about validating the mechanism than chasing a single benchmark number. ACPO is compared against strong baselines, including DAPO and CISPO, on three reasoning tasks, under both near on-policy and more off-policy training regimes. The headline result is consistency: ACPO performs better overall and is more stable across model scales, tasks, and rollout-reuse settings.

The most informative experiments are the diagnostic ones. First, the paper measures ratio distributions and clipping rates across token groups. As the number of updates per rollout increases, low-probability tokens show substantially larger ratio variance and higher clipping frequency, matching the theoretical prediction. Second, the authors analyze effective gradient contribution by token group. In near on-policy settings, low-probability tokens contribute more; as off-policyness increases, the dominant contribution shifts toward higher-probability tokens. Third, they quantify directional bias by comparing clipped gradients with an on-policy reference, showing that fixed global clipping can induce a meaningful directional deviation, while ACPO reduces that deviation. Fourth, ablations show that the gain is not explained by simply adding more thresholds: removing bin-wise adaptation or ignoring ratio dispersion weakens the effect.

The practical takeaway is clear: if rollout generation is cheap and updates are expensive, leading to heavy sample reuse, many token-level heuristics are likely responding first to off-policy clipping dynamics rather than to some deeper notion of reasoning-token importance.a52:T6f4,Read it in the order of phenomenon, theory, method, and validation. That section contains the main theoretical hinge: how off-policy degree changes importance-ratio dispersion and therefore the conditional expected gradient. While reading, keep two questions in mind: why low-probability tokens dominate near on-policy, and why they are the first to be suppressed once ratio variance grows.

Section 3 is the next important stop. Its value is that it separates two effects that are often conflated in practice: shrinking the update and rotating the update. Many implementations monitor reward and stability but do not inspect gradient bias. This section explains why clipping can stabilize training while silently changing the optimization direction. Focus on the decomposition by token probability, advantage sign, and clipping asymmetry.

For implementation-oriented readers, it helps to write the GRPO, DAPO, and CISPO objectives side by side while reading.a53:T95c,技术方案由 VeriEvol 框架和 HTV-Agent 两个核心部件组成。

第一部分是 type-aware prompt evolution。输入是低难度 seed 样本 x=(I,q,a)，目标是构造更难但仍然 image-grounded 的新样本 \u007e{x}=(I,q',â,m)。作者没有采用单一通用改写器，而是按题型路由，例如 geometry、chart、OCR 等，每一类使用 family-specific evolution operators。这样做的原因很明确：视觉数学题的难度不是靠把问题写长，而是靠增加真正依赖图像结构的推理步骤。几何题可以通过引入辅助关系、角度/长度约束、多步推导来变难；图表题则可以通过跨区域比较、组合统计量、条件筛选来增加推理深度。route-specific operator 的价值在于避免生成“表面更复杂、实则可由文本先验回答”的伪难题。

第二部分是 HTV-Agent，即 hypothesis-test verifier。它不是让一个 judge 直接给分，而是采用“先提出候选解释，再主动寻找反证”的 falsification 流程。文中描述为四阶段：
1. independent solver hypotheses：多个独立求解器先给出候选答案或推理假设；
2. refutation-seeking verification：从 counter-evidence、programmatic checking、visual evidence 等多个通道尝试推翻候选答案；
3. conflict resolution by a decider：当不同通道结论冲突时，由 decider 汇总证据做裁决；
4. deterministic acceptance gate：只有满足预设接受条件的样本才进入 RL 数据池。

这里最关键的设计不是“多 agent”本身，而是 verifier 的接口化和可扩展性。作者把 difficulty scaling、answer verification、policy optimization 三者拆开：增加题目难度时，只需扩展 evolution routes；提高答案可靠性时，只需增加新的 refutation channel 或更严格的 acceptance contract；而训练端仍然消费标准 prompt-answer-reward tuple，不需要改 GRPO recipe。相比把生成、验证、训练绑成一个端到端黑盒，这种分层设计更适合规模化迭代，也更容易审计错误来源。

数据产物也分成两层：SFT 数据允许较宽松的 reasoning trace 和 evidence；RL 数据则要求更强的答案规范化和 deterministic reward-checker 保证。这个区分很合理，因为 SFT 可以容忍一定表达多样性，而 RL 的 reward 若不稳定，会直接污染梯度信号。a54:Ta23,The framework has two main components: VeriEvol for prompt evolution and HTV-Agent for answer verification.

The first component is type-aware prompt evolution. Starting from a low-difficulty seed sample x=(I, q, a), the system constructs a harder but still image-grounded sample \u007etilde{x}=(I, q', â, m). Instead of using one generic rewriting model, it routes each seed by problem family—such as geometry, charts, or OCR—and applies family-specific evolution operators. This design choice is important. In visual math, difficulty should come from additional grounded reasoning steps, not from making the prompt longer or more verbose. Geometry can be made harder by introducing auxiliary relations and multi-step constraints; chart questions can be made harder by requiring cross-region comparison, aggregation, or conditional filtering. Route-specific evolution is meant to avoid pseudo-hard examples that look more complex but can still be solved from text priors.

The second component is HTV-Agent, a hypothesis-test verifier. Rather than asking a single judge to score an answer, it follows a falsification-oriented pipeline: propose candidate solutions, then actively try to refute them. The paper describes four stages: (1) independent solver hypotheses, where multiple solvers generate candidate answers or reasoning hypotheses; (2) refutation-seeking verification, which checks those candidates through counter-evidence, programmatic tools, and visual evidence channels; (3) conflict resolution by a decider when channels disagree; and (4) a deterministic acceptance gate that only admits samples satisfying predefined criteria into the RL pool.

The key idea is not merely “multi-agent verification.” It is the separation of interfaces. Difficulty scaling, answer verification, and policy optimization are decoupled. New evolution routes can be added without changing the verifier. New verification channels can be added without changing the RL optimizer. The training side still consumes standard prompt-answer-reward tuples, so existing SFT and GRPO recipes remain usable. This is a cleaner systems design than an end-to-end generator-verifier-trainer loop where all failure modes are entangled.

The paper also distinguishes between SFT and RL data products. SFT samples can tolerate more flexible reasoning traces and evidence. RL samples require stronger answer normalization and deterministic reward-checker guarantees. That separation is well motivated: RL is much less tolerant to label ambiguity because reward instability directly corrupts the gradient signal.a55:T710,The reported numbers support two claims: scaling data helps, and verified data helps more than merely larger data.

1. SFT scaling: increasing SFT data from 10K to 250K improves the mean score by +19.31. This suggests the route-specific evol-instruct pipeline is generating supervision with real training value rather than mostly redundant variants.

2. RL scaling: increasing verified RL data from 10K to 130K yields a smooth +4.60 gain along the data-volume axis. The word “smooth” matters here. It suggests that verification quality does not collapse as the pool grows; otherwise RL gains would typically saturate early or become unstable.

3. Design contribution at fixed budget: with the RL budget fixed at 130K, the full VeriEvol design outperforms an unevolved RL baseline by +3.88. The gain decomposes into +1.82 from evolved prompts and +2.06 from the verifier. This decomposition is one of the most informative results in the paper: answer verification contributes slightly more than prompt hardening, which directly supports the paper’s central claim that reward quality is a primary bottleneck.

4. Traceability: every released sample includes the full verifier trace—solver hypotheses, counter-evidence reports, tool outputs, decider rationale, and gate outcomes. This is not a benchmark number, but it is important for reproducibility and for analyzing verifier failure modes.

The most important details to inspect are the contribution of each route type, the acceptance rate and error profile of HTV-Agent, and whether accepted-sample quality remains stable as the data pool scales.a56:T457,The work impacts pretraining research on three levels. First, it extends the interleaved reasoning paradigm initiated by o3 from pure-text and visual-only tools to the MLLM + Python code invocation scenario for numerical computation, filling the capability gap of non-visual tools in multimodal agentic RL and providing a reproducible training recipe for multimodal foundations to move from perception-reasoning to a perception-computation-reasoning closed loop. Second, the combined recipe of cold-start data construction, dual-track data filtering, and group-constrained GRPO directly addresses two engineering pain points: the difficulty of activating tool use in small models, and the long-term instability of agentic RL. The unexpected finding that adaptive tool use actually stabilizes training offers practical reference for analyzing training dynamics in RL pretrain. Third, the entire pipeline is open-source implementable and does not depend on proprietary capabilities of closed-source models, providing direct engineering guidance for the community to reproduce o3-style multimodal reasoning models.a57:T4ff,The AIR framework has two training stages: cold-start SFT and interleaved reasoning RL, supported by three technical lines. First, two-stage cold-start data construction: an MLLM first generates pure-text CoT reasoning traces, then an LLM rewrites the CoT into interleaved reasoning format with inserted code calls, followed by verification of code execution integrity and answer correctness. This decoupled generation avoids the insufficient reasoning depth and low efficiency of one-step synthesis in multimodal scenarios. Second, dual-track data filtering: the Self-Sampled strategy performs multiple rollouts on the SFT model and uses Pass@k as the admission threshold for candidate samples, filtering noise through multi-turn consensus of the target model itself; the Prior-Filtered strategy acts as a complement, using a strong teacher model as an external quality gate to further remove low-quality interleaved reasoning samples. Third, group-constrained GRPO reward mechanism: group constraints are applied to tool-use behavior during RL, guiding the model to adaptively judge whether tool invocation is needed and choose the right timing. This constraint also suppresses training fluctuations when tool-use rate increases, mitigating long-term instability in agentic RL.a58:T400,Experiments focus on multimodal complex numerical computation and mathematical reasoning tasks. In the cold-start stage, two-stage data construction delivers clear improvements over one-step synthesis in code executability and final answer accuracy. Dual-track filtering, compared with no filtering or single-track filtering, significantly reduces noise in SFT data and leads to faster convergence in subsequent RL. In the RL stage, group-constrained GRPO outperforms vanilla GRPO in two aspects: adaptive tool-use rate is more reasonable, without extreme over-use or non-use, and accuracy on problems requiring computation improves notably; training curves are smoother, with no reward oscillation or model collapse under high tool-use settings, which is common in vanilla GRPO. A worthwhile deep-dive direction is the causal relationship between tool-use behavior and training stability in agentic RL, and whether this mechanism transfers to pure-text RL or RL with other tool types.a5a:T56d,The A-Evolve-Training system is built on three cost-driven design choices unified by the asymmetric freedom principle: zero degrees of freedom on comparability-critical invariants, maximum freedom on exploratory axes. First, an immutable reference substrate: every round forks the same operator-audited default training stack into isolated candidate sandboxes, with no overwrites of the base substrate to eliminate cross-round hidden variance and guarantee cross-candidate recipe comparability. Second, homogeneous stateless workers: the initial design of specialized handoff agents (data, training, eval) was abandoned because it accumulated unobserved variance and corrupted selection signals; instead, each round spawns N=8 identical full-stack agents (1 as a noise-calibration baseline anchor, 7 exploring orthogonal axes), each independently completing recipe editing, GPU job launch, failure debugging, checkpoint evaluation, and result writing, with no cross-round state carryover. Third, a constitution-bounded round-level meta agent: a one-shot collector aggregates cross-worker evidence into a fixed-schema round report, and the meta agent may only rewrite the next round's rolling search policy, with no ability to modify the frozen system constitution; winning recipes are never promoted to the base substrate, only reflected in updated search policies to prevent search drift.a5b:T5e4,1. Task modeling: Abstracts CoT reasoning as a pathfinding problem on a directed multigraph, constructing a branched path-star multigraph (source node → fork node → W branches of depth K, each branch containing K diamond subgraphs with L multiedges per diamond; only the golden path reaches the target leaf node). The reasoning model is formalized as a pretrained world model, either an edge-level linear-softmax bigram or node-level trigram. 2. Analysis framework: Uses gradient flow (for SFT) and sign policy gradient flow (for RLVR) for dynamical characterization. 3. Core theoretical derivation: ① Rigorously proves that SFT trained only on golden shortest paths has gradient flow that never converges to any backtracking strategy — training data contains no gradient signals for dead-end or rollback states, so the model only learns to advance along the golden path. ② Proves that RLVR with only outcome-level reward (plus length penalty) obtains gradient signals for backtracking actions via on-policy failed rollouts, and converges to a consistent backtracking policy in finite time. ③ Quantitative complexity separation: After convergence, the RLVR model reaches any target in Θ(WK) expected time, while the SFT model requires Θ(WL^K) (exponential gap when L>1). ④ Further proves that distilling RLVR-generated reasoning traces (including backtracking steps) into the base model via supervised learning transfers efficient backtracking, recovering Θ(WK) test-time compute efficiency.a5c:T4a2,1. 从实验结构判断，作者想证明三件事：能测到 oversensitivity；oversensitivity 会被 policy 学走；简单离散化足以缓解。这个证据链是完整的。局限也存在：离散化依赖候选回答集合与聚类阈值估计，若候选分布很窄或 RM dropout 不稳定，效果可能受影响；另外，论文更像是在 RL teacher 侧做修正，还没有触及如何从训练数据和目标函数层面直接学出低-oversensitivity 的 RM。a5e:T74e,The work has a theoretical layer and a practical layer. The theoretical setup models true utility u(x, y) as an integer-valued function with a finite number of perceptible utility levels for each prompt. That formalizes the idea that many responses belong to the same utility class. Under this view, a good reward model must do two things at once: separate different utility classes and avoid inventing distinctions within the same class. The paper uses discriminative ability for the former and specificity for the latter. The central claim is that these objectives need not be traded off blindly; a suitable discretization of reward scores can preserve useful between-class variation while suppressing harmful within-class variation.

The practical method is uncertainty-aware reward discretization. Instead of retraining the reward model, the authors estimate predictive uncertainty with Monte Carlo dropout by running the RM multiple times and measuring the variance of the predicted reward. They then cluster candidate responses using both reward means and uncertainty, treating responses within a cluster as approximately utility-equivalent. RL no longer optimizes fine-grained score gaps inside those clusters. In effect, the method converts a continuous scorer into a confidence-aware ordinal teacher.

This differs from common alternatives in several ways. It is not simple reward binning with fixed thresholds, not temperature scaling, and not binary verification. It preserves some hierarchy when the model is confident that differences are meaningful, while collapsing distinctions when the score differences are likely to reflect uncertainty or arbitrary tie-breaking. A key conceptual point in the paper is that reward variance is only useful when it aligns with true utility differences. Inter-class variance helps learning; intra-class variance hurts it.a5f:T7ac,The experiments are organized to establish a full causal story. First, the authors evaluate oversensitivity directly on the Ties subset of RewardBench 2, where responses should be treated as ties. Across several popular reward models, discretization consistently improves specificity while only modestly reducing discriminative ability, improving their combined quality. The important result here is the consistency across models rather than a single headline number.

Second, they build a controlled environment with a mixture of a primary reward and a spurious stylistic reward. The primary component represents actual task utility such as instruction following; the secondary component captures style-related features that a reward model may latch onto. Optimizing the raw continuous reward leads to strong stylistic overoptimization and degraded primary-task performance. Discretization suppresses that failure mode and preserves the primary objective much better. This is the key mechanism experiment because it shows that oversensitivity is not just a benchmark artifact; it becomes a learnable signal that policy optimization exploits.

Third, they run a more realistic multitask RL setup on unlabeled prompts and evaluate on IFEval, GSM8K, and MATH. The discretized reward models are never significantly worse than the raw reward models and are often better. The emphasis is on robustness rather than chasing a single best benchmark score. The paper argues that when reward models contain stylistic bias or tie-breaking noise, discretization reduces harmful gradients without sacrificing useful supervision.

The experimental story is strong because it covers measurement, mechanism, and downstream impact. The main limitation is that the method still depends on the candidate-response set and on uncertainty estimates from dropout. It is a teacher-side correction rather than a solution to training low-oversensitivity reward models from first principles.a60:T697,Start with the introduction and the early figures, especially the examples that separate accuracy, variance, and oversensitivity. Those distinctions carry the whole paper. Then read the problem formulation carefully. The assumption that true utility is discrete and finite is not cosmetic; it is what makes discretization theoretically natural rather than an ad hoc heuristic.

In the theory section, focus on how discriminative ability and specificity are defined, and on the constructions showing that an apparently excellent continuous reward model can still be a bad RL teacher. The key insight is structural: the issue is not just reward noise magnitude, but where the variance lives.

In the method section, pay attention to how Monte Carlo dropout is used to estimate predictive variance and how clustering thresholds are chosen. The useful question to keep in mind is why this approach is preferable to simpler fixes such as score clipping, fixed binning, or binary conversion.

The experiments cover four open 7–8B models: LLaMA-3.1-8B with GQA and θ=500,000; LLaMA-2-7B with MHA and θ=10,000; Qwen2.5-7B with GQA and θ=1,000,000; and OLMo-2-7B with MHA and θ=500,000. The overall finding is that consistency training reliably makes verifier information decodable and sometimes causally influential, but does not by itself make generated rationales faithful.a64:T950,The core innovation is a reframing identity that rederives softmax attention as maximum-entropy Boltzmann-weighted aggregation over fixed Euclidean distances. The derivation rests on four assumptions, of which only one — "keys are hyperspherical vectors with constant norm" — has empirical weight; the other three are merely a geometric lens to standardize the metric form.
Expanding the squared Euclidean distance shows the ||q||² term cancels during softmax normalization because it is identical across all keys; the ||k||² term only cancels if all keys have equal norm. Standard dot-product attention is thus by construction a distance metric omitting the ||k||² term, making it blind to key magnitude.
When this norm-blind routing metric mismatches learned representations (where key norms do vary), the model produces three invariant compensation signatures: concentrated routing weights, collapse of routed representations, and norm stratification of routing-relevant tensors.
Validation proceeds in four steps: First, quantify the three signatures across 9 pretrained Transformers and compare them against matched null baselines (controls for random routing, norm distribution, and other confounding factors). Second, replicate validation across four non-token-level routers: graph attention on heterophilic graphs (routes over nodes), selective state-space models without explicit attention (routes over timesteps), temporal recurrent mixers, and depth-wise attention residuals (routes over layers). Third, perform causal ablations: where routing weights can be reconstructed from fixed quantities, remove the effect of the norm-blind metric to verify that routing concentration arises from the mechanism rather than incidental training dynamics. Fourth, formalize a "fixed mechanism, variable form" hypothesis: the invariant mechanism is metric mismatch inducing three compensations, while variable phenomenon form is set by positional brake strength. This hypothesis is validated by sweeping positional brake strength across two architectures. Finally, a router with enforced key normalization (satisfying the constant norm assumption) confirms norm stratification is a compensation effect rather than a root cause.
Key difference from prior work: prior studies only attribute individual phenomena to individual architectures, with no cross-router unifying mechanism.a65:T4db,All three signatures in 9 pretrained Transformers (spanning multiple parameter scales and training recipes) deviate significantly from matched null baselines (statistical significance p < 0.001): routing concentration — top 1% of tokens account for 45–62% of attention weight, compared to 8–12% in null baselines; representation collapse — final-layer hidden state rank is 22–38% of first-layer rank, compared to 85–92% in null baselines; norm stratification — coefficient of variation of key norms is 0.28–0.41, compared to 0.06–0.09 in null baselines.
All four non-token-level routers exhibit identical signature patterns with comparable magnitude: for example, in selective state-space models, the top 2% of historical timesteps account for 51% of gating weight, with a 31% rank decay rate across temporal processing depth.
Positional brake sweep: doubling Transformer positional encoding strength shifts attention sink onset from layer 12 to layer 4, and increases rank decay rate by 2.1x.

Fourth, investigate whether the low-rank collapse subspace overlaps with the task semantic subspace for in-context learning.a67:T560,The paper defines internalization as a transition from implementing a computation through many explicit steps to implementing it in fewer steps through modified weights. The main empirical setting is semiautomaton simulation. A transformer is trained to generate CoT tokens corresponding to intermediate automaton states over T steps, and then a curriculum progressively removes these CoT tokens so that the model must predict the final state with less explicit computation. This separates learning the step-by-step state transition from compressing the computation. The paper studies task structure through modular counter semiautomata and relates difficulty to the arithmetic structure of the counter order. Counters with small prime-power factors appear easier to represent compactly, while prime-order counters are harder. The theoretical part analyzes sparse parity with a stylized one-layer transformer using linear attention and a fixed nonlinear MLP. The model first learns the hidden-support parity with explicit CoT supervision, then internalizes the autoregressive computation as CoT tokens are removed one at a time, eventually computing the parity directly. The paper also connects the mechanism to Positive Distribution Shift, where the training distribution is deliberately changed in a way that allows earlier learned representations to support later learning.a68:T41f,The empirical findings are mainly mechanistic. On semiautomaton tasks, wider transformers internalize CoT more reliably than deeper transformers under a fixed parameter budget. This weakens the simple picture that implicit reasoning is just explicit reasoning unfolded vertically across layers. Task structure matters: among modular counters, prime-order cases are the most difficult to internalize, consistent with the compact-representation argument. Internalization also has a cost. Models that succeed in-distribution often show degraded out-of-distribution performance, suggesting that the compressed computation can become a shortcut rather than a faithful implementation of the original stepwise algorithm. The theoretical sparse-parity result provides the cleanest positive result: explicit CoT makes the hidden computation learnable, and progressive token removal transfers that computation into the direct predictor. The supplied material does not include checkable numerical details such as model sizes, dataset sizes, or exact accuracy deltas.a69:T5cb,The authors first isolate a simplified Muon update by removing momentum and Newton-Schulz implementation details. The remaining operation replaces each matrix gradient by its polar factor, keeping singular directions while removing singular values. This isolates the effect of gradient orthogonalization. The theoretical testbed is Burer-Monteiro factorized matrix sensing, which is connected to training two-layer quadratic neural networks and allows the gradient and Hessian geometry to be controlled through the sensing operator. The key model is mixed-spiked matrix sensing. Its sensing operator decomposes into signal, spike, and bulk components. The signal component is task-relevant anisotropy aligned with the ground truth. The spike component is strong but task-irrelevant anisotropy. The bulk component captures the remaining more isotropic directions. This construction mirrors a common feature of LLM training: gradients are highly anisotropic, but not every dominant direction is useful. The authors then analyze the landscape using a river-valley decomposition. The river direction corresponds to meaningful progress toward the ground truth, while hill directions capture sharp transverse deviations. In this geometry, GD quickly descends from the hillside into the river but then makes slow progress along the river. Muon moves rapidly along the sides of the valley, which improves exploration, but its normalized update can prevent fine convergence near the solution.a6a:T832,方法上分三层。第一层是定义。作者把多轮 MDP 中的状态分成 critical state 和 routine state。critical turn 的动作会改变后续 return distribution；routine turn 虽然是完成任务所必需的执行步骤，但在给定状态下，不同可行动作对最终回报分布近似不变。基于这个划分，decision density ρ 被定义为轨迹中 critical turn 的比例。

第二层是估计器比较。论文比较两类 policy gradient：一类是 turn-level estimator，用每步 advantage A_t 做信用分配，对应 PPO 这一族；另一类是 trajectory-level estimator，用整条轨迹共享的标量优势，对应 GRPO 这一族。关键观察是：在 perfect critic 下，routine turn 的真实 advantage 为 0，因此 turn-level estimator 会逐点把 routine contribution 消掉；而 trajectory-level estimator 只能在期望意义上抵消 routine turn，因为它仍把同一个轨迹级回报乘到这些 turn 的 score function 上，所以会保留额外方差。

第三层是理论推导。作者用 SNR 作为训练步效率代理，分析 turn-level 与 trajectory-level 的信噪比差距。在非退化条件下，perfect critic 情况下 turn-level 相对 trajectory-level 的 SNR 优势按 Θ(ρ^{-1/2}) 增长。也就是说，critical turn 越稀疏，trajectory-level 的浪费越严重。论文还把分析扩展到 imperfect critic：critic 不是免费午餐，若 critic error variance 足够小，turn-level 仍保留优势；但当 critic 误差方差上升到与 decision density 同量级甚至更大时，这种优势会饱和甚至被吃掉。这个扩展很重要，因为它回答了“为什么不是永远上 critic”——因为 critic 的收益要和其误差、成本、稳定性一起看。

实验环境 Diluted Doors 也是技术方案的一部分。它是一个可控 MDP，能精确调节 ρ，同时保持其它因素尽量稳定，用来隔离 signal dilution 机制，而不是在复杂 agent benchmark 上混入太多 confounder。这个设计比直接在真实代码 agent 上做 ablation 更干净。a6b:T727,The paper proceeds in three steps. First, it defines critical versus routine turns in a finite-horizon MDP. Critical turns are those where the chosen action changes the future return distribution. Routine turns are necessary execution steps, but alternative admissible actions leave the return distribution effectively invariant. Decision density ρ is then defined as the fraction of critical turns in a trajectory.

Second, it compares two policy-gradient families. A turn-level estimator uses per-step advantages A_t, as in PPO-style methods with a value function. Under a perfect critic, routine turns have zero true advantage and are canceled pointwise. A trajectory-level estimator, as in GRPO-style methods, attaches one scalar advantage to the entire trajectory. In that case, routine turns only cancel in expectation, not per sample, so they retain variance contributions.

Third, it derives an SNR comparison. Using signal-to-noise ratio as a proxy for training-step efficiency, the paper shows that under non-degeneracy assumptions, the SNR advantage of turn-level over trajectory-level estimation scales as Θ(ρ^{-1/2}) in the perfect-critic regime. As decision density decreases, the penalty of trajectory-level credit assignment grows. The analysis is then extended to imperfect critics: the turn-level advantage survives only while critic-error variance remains below the scale set by ρ, and saturates once critic noise becomes too large. This extension is important because it explains why adding a critic is not automatically beneficial.

The controlled environment, Diluted Doors, is also part of the technical contribution. It allows the authors to vary ρ directly while keeping other factors as stable as possible, making it easier to isolate the signal-dilution mechanism than in a full LLM-agent benchmark.a6c:T5ea,The experiments are designed to validate the mechanism rather than to maximize downstream scores. The central testbed is Diluted Doors, a controlled MDP with tunable decision density.

The first key result is an SNR study. Over roughly a 50x range of ρ, the empirical SNR ratio between turn-level and trajectory-level estimators follows the predicted ρ^{-1/2} law extremely closely. The paper reports that the fit explains 99.9% of the variation, which is unusually clean evidence for a theory paper.

The second key result is a training-efficiency study. As ρ decreases, trajectory-level learning becomes increasingly inefficient, while the gap in favor of turn-level estimation widens. This supports the paper’s main claim that the cost of critic-free multi-turn RL is governed by decision density rather than horizon alone.

The paper also discusses the imperfect-critic regime. When critic-error variance is controlled, turn-level estimation retains its advantage; when critic noise grows too large, the gain saturates. If the appendix includes explicit critic-noise sweeps, that part is especially relevant for real LLM RL where value estimation is often unstable.

A limitation is that the empirical evidence is primarily from a controlled MDP, not a full-scale LLM agent training run. So the paper is strong on causal identification and weak on external validity. The next practical question is how to estimate ρ in real agent traces and whether routine versus critical turns can be detected reliably.a6d:T6b2,Start with the introduction. The two terms to anchor on are signal dilution and decision density. The paper’s main claim is already visible there: the problem in multi-turn RL is not just long horizon, but sparse consequential decisions.

Then read the formal setup and theory sections carefully. Pay attention to how routine states are defined through return-distribution invariance, what exact estimators are being compared, and what assumptions are needed for the SNR scaling result. The usefulness of the conclusion depends on how restrictive those assumptions are.

Next, inspect the construction of Diluted Doors. The important question is whether the environment really varies ρ without simultaneously changing horizon, reward scale, or transition stochasticity. If that control is clean, the empirical validation is much more convincing.

In the experiments, prioritize the figure showing SNR ratio versus ρ and the figure showing training efficiency as ρ changes. One validates the theoretical slope; the other shows that the effect matters for actual learning speed, not just for a derived statistic.

Three follow-up questions are worth carrying into a second pass. First, how could ρ be estimated in real agent tasks from rollouts, tool traces, or verifier signals? Second, can the critic-error-versus-ρ comparison be turned into a practical criterion for whether a critic is worth training? Third, are there cheaper middle-ground solutions—process rewards, step-level verifiers, segment-level return decomposition—that recover some of the benefit without a full critic? First, the backbone keeps DeepSeekMoE and Multi-Token Prediction, which signals continuity with an already validated large-scale recipe rather than a wholesale paradigm shift. Second, the key architectural change is a hybrid attention design combining Compressed Sparse Attention (CSA) and Heavily Compressed Attention (HCA). CSA compresses KV caches along the sequence dimension and then applies DeepSeek Sparse Attention, aiming to reduce long-sequence cost while retaining selective access. HCA compresses KV more aggressively but keeps dense attention, trading more compression for a simpler attention pattern. The combination suggests that no single compression mode is sufficient across the stack. Third, the model introduces Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections (mHC) in place of standard residual pathways and adopts the Muon optimizer. This is important because at 1M context and trillion-scale MoE size, optimization geometry and training stability become first-order concerns. Fourth, the training system is heavily engineered: a single fused MoE kernel overlaps compute, communication, and memory access; TileLang is used as a DSL for productivity/performance balance; deterministic, batch-invariant kernels are provided for bitwise reproducibility; tensor-level checkpointing extends autograd for fine-grained recomputation; hybrid ZeRO and two-stage contextual parallelism are used to manage compressed attention efficiently. If time is limited, read Figure 1, the attention-design section, the systems section, and the main base/long-context result tables.a77:T77b,The analysis first formalizes Shrinkage Bias: for non-uniform floating-point grids like E2M1, representable values follow geometric spacing, creating asymmetric rounding bins where the interval midpoint sits closer to the smaller-magnitude value. Under Round-to-Nearest-Even (RTNE, the default deterministic rounding for NVFP4), this structure produces a consistent negative expected rounding error. The bias accumulates multiplicatively across layers, rather than averaging out as zero-mean noise. The original intuition for choosing E2M1 was that non-uniform grids provide better dynamic range for heavy-tailed natural tensors; however, RHT—applied to spread outlier energy and improve codebook utilization—transforms tensor distributions to near-zero, approximately Gaussian shape, which falls exactly in the value range where E2M1 bin asymmetry is most severe, amplifying bias instead of reducing quantization error. Uniform grids (E1M2, INT4) use equal spacing between representable values, eliminating this geometric asymmetry entirely; these grids also match the post-RHT near-Gaussian tensor distribution, converting RHT-induced codebook utilization gains into consistent quantization quality. The resulting UFP4 recipe makes two core design choices: first, apply RHT to all three linear layer GEMMs in training (forward pass, data gradient, weight gradient), resolving the prior failure mode of training collapse when using RHT across all paths with E2M1; second, restrict stochastic rounding exclusively to quantization of the upstream gradient dY, using deterministic RTNE for weights and activations to minimize update variance. Unlike prior E2M1-based methods that stack stabilization fixes around a fixed format choice, UFP4 resolves the fundamental mismatch between format geometry and post-RHT tensor distribution, enabling stable end-to-end FP4 training without complex heuristic stabilization.a78:T4dc,Validation spans full long-run pretraining runs at three scales: 1.5B dense, 7.9B MoE, and 124B MoE. On the 124B MoE task, well-tuned E2M1 baselines (following NVFP4 best practices) show clear loss degradation relative to BF16, with occasional late-training instability; UFP4 achieves substantially lower relative loss degradation with stable training dynamics across the entire run. Key ablation findings include: (1) Shrinkage bias accumulates with network depth for E2M1, causing measurable signal decay in deeper layers that is absent for uniform grids; (2) RHT increases bias and reduces quantization SNR for E2M1, but improves quantization SNR for uniform grids across all GEMM paths; (3) Restricting stochastic rounding to dY is sufficient—applying SR to weights or activations provides no stability benefit but increases update variance; (4) Scaling analysis across 1B to 124B parameter models shows UFP4 maintains a constant small gap to BF16, while the E2M1 gap grows with training steps and model scale; (5) Fused kernel benchmarks show UFP4 has marginally lower runtime overhead than optimized E2M1 NVFP4 implementations, as uniform quantization requires simpler per-block arithmetic, with no additional hardware support barriers.a79:T862,方法上，文章的核心不是提出一个新 reviewer，而是构建一套分层 benchmark，并用它比较 OpenAIReview、‘coarse、Reviewer3、以及 zero-shot baseline 在多种后端模型上的表现。OpenAIReview 的系统设计值得看，因为它代表了一类典型的 agentic long-document pipeline：先把整篇论文切成长度相近的 passages，再对每个 passage 做局部审阅，同时维护运行中的摘要或全局上下文，使后续 passage 的判断不完全局限于局部窗口；最后把评论与原文引用绑定并聚合成结构化 review。作者强调，这种 running summarization 对跨段的论证错误、错误 claim、实验设计问题更有帮助，因为这些问题往往不是一个局部 token span 能决定的。

和已有工作相比，区别主要有三点。第一，评测对象是完整系统而不是裸 LLM。第二，既看开放世界的相关性信号，也看封闭世界的已知错误召回。第三，作者明确区分 recall 和 precision：系统在 benchmark 上可以抓到不少错误，但真实使用里用户最不满的是 false positive 和吹毛求疵，这个张力在 agentic system 里很常见。a7a:T751,The contribution is primarily an evaluation framework, not a new review model. That design is intended to preserve long-range coherence while keeping each local review step tractable.

The evaluation has three layers. First, a real-paper quality-proxy study on ICLR/NeurIPS papers. Since these systems do not necessarily output calibrated scores, the paper uses comment volume as a weak signal and asks whether lower-quality papers, as approximated by citations, acceptance decisions, reviewer scores, or a composite proxy, receive more comments than higher-quality papers in random pairwise comparisons. This allows direct measurement of error recall. Third, a public deployment study of OpenAIReview, collecting user feedback on real reviews to expose precision issues that offline recall benchmarks may miss.

Relative to prior work, three differences matter. It evaluates complete systems rather than naked models. It combines open-world proxy correlation with closed-world error detection. And it explicitly surfaces the recall-precision tension: systems can catch many issues offline while still frustrating users with false positives and low-value nitpicks.a7b:T763,The headline result on the quality-proxy task is that every evaluated system performs above chance, suggesting that current reviewer systems do extract nontrivial quality signals from paper text. Reported performance spans roughly 66% to 83% depending on system and backend model, with a clear trend that stronger models yield stronger quality discrimination.

On the perturbation benchmark, the strongest setup again is OpenAIReview + GPT-5.5, reaching 71.6% recall over injected errors. The gains over a zero-shot baseline are not uniform across error types. This pattern fits the system design: passage-wise review plus running summarization helps when the error depends on longer argumentative structure or cross-section consistency, but offers less advantage for highly local symbolic corruption.

That suggests reviewer-style error detection has broad coverage gaps and may benefit from committee-style aggregation rather than relying on a single stronger model.

DiffusionGemma passes a bottleneck between denoising steps consisting of C natural-language tokens and C self-conditioning vectors, where C is the canvas length. If this bottleneck is treated as opaque, DiffusionGemma performs 28.6× more opaque serial computation than the corresponding Gemma model. If the bottleneck is interpretable, the ratio drops to 1.1×. The rest of the paper tests whether that interpretability assumption is defensible. It first restricts the inter-step information flow to O(c) natural-language tokens and measures whether performance is preserved. It then analyzes whether the resulting mapped tokens correspond to guesses for nearby positions. The paper also adapts monitorability evaluations to compare DiffusionGemma with Gemma 4, and uses case studies to study non-autoregressive phenomena such as non-chronological reasoning, token and sequence smearing, and intermediate-context reasoning.a7e:T838,方法很简洁，关键是把回归目标从“mixture -> 最终 loss”改成“当前训练状态 -> 下一阶段 loss”。RegMix 原始做法是：采样若干 mixture，训练若干小 proxy 模型到固定步数，只记录终点验证损失，再拟合一个回归器预测某个 mixture 的终点 loss，最后选一个全程固定的 mixture。RegMix-D 则在 proxy 训练中按多个时间点记录 validation loss，把每条 proxy trajectory 切成若干相邻区间。对于给定的 switch point 数 N，会选出 N+1 个时间节点 t1...tN+1，并从每条轨迹构造 M×N 个训练样本。回归器 f_N 的输入是当前步点 t_l、当前 mixture m、当前 observed loss l_l，输出是下一时间点的 loss l_{l+1}。也就是说，它学的是局部转移，而不是全局终点映射。

在部署上有两个版本。Offline 版本在目标训练开始前递归生成完整 schedule：从初始 loss 出发，在每个 switch point 上搜索使预测下一段 loss 最低的 mixture，把预测出的 loss 再喂给下一段，直到生成整条 mixture schedule。这个版本不需要 target run 中途干预，但误差会递归累积。Online 版本则在 target training 的每个 switch point 上，用目标模型真实观测到的 validation loss 替代预测 loss，再调用同一个冻结回归器选择下一段 mixture。这样做的好处是把 proxy-to-target 的偏差限制在单段决策里，而不是沿整条 schedule 传播。

方法上的几个细节值得注意。第一，作者没有引入额外 RL、bandit 或 bilevel optimization 机制，仍然是回归 + candidate search，所以工程接入成本低。第二，初始阶段固定使用 human-curated Pile prior，而不是从第一个 segment 就让回归器自由选 mixture，这反映了一个现实假设：训练初期没有足够 target-state 信息，先验配比更稳。第三，mixture 搜索仍然通过 Dirichlet-sampled candidates 完成，说明作者追求的是在现有 RegMix 搜索框架内最小改动地升级为 dynamic mixing，而不是重新设计连续优化器。a7f:T7d0,The key move is to replace a global regression target with a local transition model. In standard RegMix, each sampled mixture is used to train one proxy model to a fixed horizon, only the final validation loss is kept, and a regressor maps mixture to endpoint loss. The chosen mixture is then used for the entire target run. RegMix-D logs validation loss at multiple points along each proxy trajectory. For a chosen number of switch points N, it selects N+1 time anchors and converts each proxy trajectory into M×N training examples. The regressor f_N takes the current state (training step t_l, current mixture m, current loss l_l) and predicts the next loss l_{l+1}. In other words, it learns one-step loss transitions rather than a direct mixture-to-final-loss map.

This enables two deployment modes. In the offline mode, the schedule is generated before target training: starting from an initial loss, the method searches over candidate mixtures at each switch point, picks the one with the lowest predicted next-step loss, feeds that predicted loss into the next decision, and recursively builds a full schedule. In the online mode, the same frozen regressor is queried during target training, but the current loss is the actually observed target-model validation loss rather than the previously predicted one. This grounds each decision in the real target trajectory and limits error accumulation.

Several design choices are worth noting. The method does not introduce RL, bandits, or bilevel optimization; it stays within the regression-plus-search framework, which keeps the engineering overhead low. The first segment uses the human-curated Pile prior instead of a learned mixture, reflecting a cold-start assumption that early in training there is not enough target-state information to trust dynamic adaptation. Candidate mixtures are still searched via Dirichlet sampling, so the contribution is a minimal but effective extension of RegMix rather than a full redesign of the optimizer.a80:T571,The experiments follow the standard RegMix setup: a 1B-parameter target model trained on 25B tokens from the Pile. The main comparisons are static RegMix versus RegMix-D, with both offline and online variants evaluated under different switching granularities. The headline findings are consistent. First, RegMix-D outperforms RegMix at every tested granularity, both in validation loss and across 13 downstream tasks. Second, the online variant is generally more reliable than the offline one because it uses observed target losses to correct the state, whereas the offline schedule can accumulate recursive prediction error. Third, the method is notably more proxy-efficient: 128 proxy models, about 25% of the 512-proxy budget used by RegMix, are already enough to surpass the static baseline.

The important experimental point is not one unusually large gain, but the consistency of the improvement. A sequence is split into contiguous blocks. Previous blocks are kept clean and used as prefix context, while the current block is corrupted with an absorbing [MASK] process and denoised in parallel. The conditional distribution for each block is trained with a weighted cross-entropy over masked positions, with weights induced by the diffusion noise schedule. This design interpolates between AR generation and fully parallel diffusion. The main method is block-size curriculum learning. This differs from fixed small-block training, which limits inference parallelism, and from direct large-block training, which is brittle for reasoning. After unrolling, h_N=h_0+ε∑r_n. The squared norm contains a quadratic term, ε²/d · ||∑r_n||². In an ordinary non-shared residual stack, different residual branches are approximately independent, so this term grows like Θ(ε²N), which motivates ε=1/√N. In a looped network, the same W generates all updates. The activations are produced by the same recurrence, the residual directions remain positively correlated, and the quadratic term grows like Θ(ε²N²). Keeping the residual stream bounded therefore requires εN=O(1), i.e. ε=1/N. The same accumulation appears in the optimization analysis: the output change after one optimizer step scales as ηεN, so ε=1/N makes the stable learning rate roughly independent of N. For a practical block with L unique layers repeated N times, the paper separates two effects: a linear N factor from within-layer reuse and a √L factor from across-layer random-walk accumulation. This yields ε=λ/(N√L) and a learning-rate law η≲1/(λ√L).a84:T44d,The public write-up does not disclose parameter counts, data size, token count, RL algorithm details, or reward-model architecture. The entropy change of a token decomposes into the product of the trajectory-level advantage and a local entropy sensitivity function determined by the next-token distribution. This yields an advantage-surprisal quadrant view: positive-advantage low-surprisal tokens tend to decrease entropy, positive-advantage high-surprisal tokens tend to increase it, and the signs are reversed under negative advantage. Since low-surprisal tokens occur much more often, the realized update is biased toward entropy reduction. The authors also identify a near-criticality property: a mild perturbation to the weights of specific tokens can flip the direction of entropy evolution; beyond the critical threshold, the weight mostly controls magnitude rather than sign. STARE uses this observation in three steps. It selects entropy-critical tokens using batch-internal surprisal quantiles, amplifies the effective advantage of positive-advantage high-surprisal tokens, attenuates that of negative-advantage high-surprisal tokens, and activates the intervention only when batch-averaged entropy falls below a target. Controlled pretraining runs across model sizes from 0.1B to 1.5B first confirm that small initialization reduces validation loss, but gains decay sharply with model size. Two architectural factors suppressing these gains are isolated. First, the RMSNorm stability constant epsilon enters a saturation regime when hidden state variance drops below epsilon, making normalization invariant to weight scale and erasing initialization effects. Second, small initialization exacerbates the attention sink effect — over-concentration of attention weights on the first sequence token — which is mitigated by gated attention. The best-performing profile is ×-shaped: wide at the bottom, narrow in the middle, and wide again near the top. The implementation detail that matters is the residual stream. Instead of inserting learned projections between layers, the model keeps a fixed global residual dimension equal to the widest layer. Each block reads from and writes to a layer-specific slice of this residual stream. When a layer is narrower, unused coordinates bypass the block. When a later layer expands, those coordinates are restored from the most recent layer that actively processed them; if no such value exists, the coordinate is zero-padded. This parameter-free resizing avoids projection bottlenecks and keeps the skip path closer to a standard residual stream. The design differs from work that only reallocates FFN intermediate width: here the full block width changes, so attention, MLP parameters, KV cache, activation movement, and compute are all affected.a8e:T5ef,Dynamic Rollout Editing (DRE) has three pillars:
1) Make “answer emergence” observable: for each sampled trajectory, parse intermediate outputs to extract an answer candidate and use an external verifier to find the earliest position where a correct answer can be verified. This splits tokens into a necessary prefix vs. post-answer continuation.
2) Edit successful overthinking rollouts: when a successful rollout contains substantial continuation after emergence, construct an edited counterpart that preserves a conservative verified prefix up to a safe boundary around the emergence point, and replaces/truncates the remaining overthinking segment while keeping the correct answer.
3) Rewire the GRPO preference within the same group: place the original and edited trajectories in the same GRPO group and prefer the shorter edited one, so the positive learning signal is less coupled with post-answer verbosity.
Two training stabilizers are introduced:
- Prefix masking: avoid directly penalizing the shared verified prefix, preventing degradation of the reasoning needed to reach the answer.
- GClip: provide a controlled learning signal around the edit boundary to mitigate instability caused by hard edits near the cut point.
Key difference from alternatives: it is not a global length penalty (which can suppress useful reasoning), and not a post-hoc stopping controller (which does not change what RL reinforces). It explicitly changes the training signal to decouple success from post-answer continuation.a8f:T828,模型是 550B 总参数、每 token 激活 55B 参数的 Mixture-of-Experts hybrid Mamba-Attention LM。架构延续 Nemotron 3 Super 的设计，使用 LatentMoE 作为 MoE 层，以提升每个激活参数的有效容量；同时混合 Mamba 与 attention，目标是降低长序列推理中的 attention 计算和 KV cache 占用。模型还原生加入 Multi-Token Prediction。MTP 使用两个 head，且两个 head 共享参数，用于训练出更稳的自回归 draft token，服务于 speculative decoding。每个 MTP head 由一个 attention layer 和一个 MoE layer 组成。

It follows the Nemotron 3 Super hybrid Mamba-Attention design, scaled up and combined with LatentMoE. The motivation is direct: MoE improves accuracy per active parameter, while replacing part of full attention with Mamba-style sequence modeling reduces inference cost and KV-cache footprint for long contexts and long outputs.

The model includes native Multi-Token Prediction with two shared-parameter heads. The heads are trained to produce autoregressive draft tokens and are used for speculative decoding. Each MTP head consists of one attention layer followed by one MoE layer.

Pretraining uses 20 trillion text tokens with a Warmup-Stable-Decay learning-rate schedule. The first 15T tokens emphasize diversity and broad domain coverage. The last 5T tokens emphasize higher-quality data to refine accuracy. This is a practical data schedule: broad coverage first, lower-noise refinement later.

A central technical point is NVFP4 pretraining. NVFP4 layers use the E2M1 datatype with two-dimensional block quantization on weights. Random Hadamard Transforms are applied to inputs for weight-gradient computation, and gradients use stochastic rounding. The recipe keeps numerically sensitive parts in higher precision: the final 15% of the network, corresponding to 16 layers, plus Mamba output projections, latent projections, QKV and attention projections, MTP layers, and embeddings. This selective precision policy is likely as important as the FP4 datatype itself.

Post-training starts with curated SFT, then applies unified RLVR over reasoning, agentic, code, safety, usability, and chat environments. More than ten specialized teacher models are trained, including agentic teachers from a dedicated agentic SFT path. Multi-teacher On-Policy Distillation then gives dense token-level supervision on rollouts generated by the student model. The final model also supports reasoning effort control, allowing inference-time adjustment of the compute-accuracy trade-off.a91:T4e7,The main scale numbers are 550B total parameters, 55B active parameters, 20T pretraining tokens, and 1M-token context extension. The release also includes 173B tokens of fresh GitHub code data, specialized synthetic pretraining datasets, and post-training datasets.a92:T62e,Given a sequence x, the method partitions tokens into a conditioning set x_c and an evaluation set x_e. The loss is applied only to tokens in x_e, since tokens in x_c are observed. ac-gpt creates a copy of the conditioning tokens, \bar{x}_c, and places these copies at the beginning of the attention order. All later tokens can attend to them. The copied tokens keep their original positional encodings, so the model knows where the observed tokens belong in the original sequence. The copied conditioning tokens use unrestricted bidirectional attention among themselves because they are all observed.

The evaluation tokens still follow the original left-to-right causal factorization. This is the main distinction from masked or denoising LMs: ac-gpt does not independently predict masked tokens and does not rely on a pseudo-likelihood approximation. It models the joint distribution over the evaluation set through an autoregressive chain, conditioned on an arbitrary observed subset.

The copy mechanism is not a cosmetic detail. If the model simply allowed every token to attend to the original conditioning tokens, multi-layer attention could leak information between evaluation tokens. For example, a conditioning token at position 3 may need to attend to positions 1 and 2 in order to predict position 4; in the next layer, position 1 could then indirectly receive information about position 2 through position 3. This violates the intended left-to-right factorization over x_e. Separating copied observed tokens from the original autoregressive stream avoids this leakage.a93:T6e4,The method has two main components. The first is Reflective Masking (RM). At each denoising step and for each position, the model chooses among three actions: keep the current token, re-mask the current token for future resampling, or reveal a token if the position is currently masked. The key idea is that remasking is no longer a fixed heuristic based only on low confidence in still-masked positions; already denoised tokens can be actively reconsidered. This makes the denoising process partially reversible and turns generation into iterative local correction.

The second component is History Reference (HR), a parameter-free mechanism that aggregates intermediate decoding states into a history-aware representation. Instead of conditioning only on the current partially denoised sequence, the model also gets access to what each position looked like in previous steps and how stable those predictions were. This gives MDMs a temporal memory channel that AR models get implicitly through sequential context accumulation.

The training recipe is the most important part of the paper. The authors argue that inference-time rules alone are insufficient because existing MDMs were never trained for self-initiated multi-turn revision. They therefore introduce lightweight post-training centered on reflective masking, together with a data-generation pipeline designed to stay close to the model’s native output distribution. This is a good design choice: if training examples are built from artificial off-distribution corruptions, the model may only learn to repair synthetic noise rather than revise its own realistic mistakes. The paper instead tries to teach the model to detect and correct unreliable predictions arising from its own denoising dynamics.a94:T47c,The evaluation spans image editing, Sudoku, and text generation, which is a sensible way to test whether the method is tied to one modality or one supervision regime. The main result is consistent: RM improves over baseline MDM decoding across all three settings, and HR is especially helpful when the task requires autonomous exploration rather than explicit guidance. In image editing, where instructions specify both what and where to modify, RM mainly improves localized edits and reduces unnecessary changes elsewhere. In Sudoku, the benefit is clearer as iterative conflict detection and local correction. In text generation, where supervision is weakest and the final answer is not directly hinted, RM better exposes the intended reasoning behavior: progressively refining a partially wrong state rather than restarting from scratch.
