For multi-attribute control, intervention is implemented via disjoint SAE feature sets, cross-attribute interference is bounded by the decoder Gram structure, and effect-size calibration is applied to balance the strength of different attributes to avoid weak attributes being overwhelmed.b96:T9ae,MuonQ has three main components, all built around the idea of preventing quantization noise from inducing systematic directional drift.

The first is pre-quantization normalization. The authors argue that if gradients or momentum are quantized directly at each step, the absolute scale of the quantization error changes with the state magnitude. Over many steps, this can accumulate into a preferred direction. Since Muon preserves direction and discards singular-value magnitudes, such bias is especially damaging. MuonQ normalizes the state before quantization so that each step contributes errors of comparable magnitude. The goal is not simply to reduce one-step MSE, but to make accumulated error more isotropic over time.

The second is structural decomposition. Direct low-bit quantization of the full momentum matrix can perturb singular vectors, and those perturbations survive the orthogonalization step. MuonQ instead decomposes the momentum structurally and quantizes the singular factors separately, so that quantization error is pushed more into singular-value magnitudes than into singular-vector directions. This matches Muon’s update rule: singular-value errors are largely washed out by the polar operation, while directional errors are preserved. The paper also proposes a truncated top-k variant to trade off memory and fidelity. The important point is not decomposition for its own sake, but deliberate error reallocation into the part of the representation that Muon is less sensitive to.

The third is μ-law companding quantization. The authors argue that Muon needs higher resolution near zero because, after polar decomposition, different singular directions are treated more evenly than in Adam-like optimizers. Uniform quantization wastes bins on large magnitudes and under-resolves the dense region near zero, where subtle directional information can still matter. Companding compresses the dynamic range before quantization and allocates more effective resolution to that dense region.

Together, these components form a coherent design: normalization controls the geometry of accumulated error, structural decomposition controls where the error lands, and companding improves resolution where Muon is most sensitive. Compared with prior Muon quantization work, the novelty is that the method is derived from the optimizer’s polar-update mechanism rather than from generic low-bit heuristics or mixed-precision retention of dominant components.b97:T796,The main empirical claim is focused and important: on GPT-style and LLaMA-style pretraining setups, pure 4-bit MuonQ tracks full-precision Muon closely in both training loss and downstream accuracy, while reducing optimizer-state memory by up to 7.3x. This matters because the paper positions prior work as follows: 8-bit Muon is generally workable, but naive pure 4-bit quantization degrades badly, and existing methods often rely on mixed precision for dominant singular components. MuonQ is meant to close that gap.

The most informative experiments are likely four types. First, training-curve comparisons among full-precision Muon, naive 4-bit Muon, prior 8-bit or mixed-precision baselines, and MuonQ. The shape of the loss curve matters as much as the endpoint. Second, downstream evaluations after pretraining, to verify that low-bit optimizer states do not silently damage generalization. Third, ablations over the three components: normalization only, decomposition only, companding only, and different top-k truncation settings. If the paper is convincing, these should show complementary gains rather than a single dominant trick. Fourth, mechanism-oriented analyses such as singular-vector perturbation, directional similarity after quantization, or deviation in the polar update. Those are the experiments that directly support the directional-fidelity thesis.

The hard facts visible from the provided text are: experiments cover GPT-style and LLaMA-style models; the target is pure 4-bit Muon state quantization; MuonQ remains close to full-precision Muon in training loss and downstream accuracy; and optimizer-state memory is reduced by up to 7.3x. For each prompt, the policy samples a group of responses, receives response-level rewards, normalizes advantages within the group, and optimizes a clipped policy objective. At a decoding state s_t, the next-token distribution is represented by softmax logits. For a sampled token y_t with advantage A, the update from A log π(y_t|s_t) increases the sampled token logit and redistributes probability mass according to the current distribution. The paper derives a first-order approximation of the local entropy change ΔH_t after this logit perturbation. The decomposition contains a sampled-token term and a state-wise distributional correction. Entropy polarity is the resulting signed quantity that predicts whether the update expands or contracts entropy and by how much. The asymmetry is important: reinforcing an already high-probability continuation tends to make the distribution sharper, while entropy expansion usually requires a lower-probability sample with positive advantage or a strong correction from the surrounding distribution. Papo then uses polarity as an online control signal. It reweights token-level advantages differently for positive- and negative-polarity updates, increasing entropy-expanding pressure when collapse is likely and allowing entropy-contracting updates when the policy needs to consolidate reward-aligned behavior.b9e:T503,The framework is called Detect-Classify-Compare. It first segments a generated CoT into reasoning steps using a rule-based parser over newlines, transition markers, and sentence boundaries; the reported parsing F1 is 0.87. At each step boundary, it estimates internal answer commitment with a logit-lens proxy. Hidden states from each layer are projected through the unembedding and layer normalization, and the probability assigned to the ground-truth answer token, p_ans, is tracked. A step is treated as internally committed when p_ans exceeds τ=0.3. The visible-trace label is constructed by checking whether the cumulative CoT text has already exposed the ground-truth answer string or a normalized variant. Belief-CoT Agreement measures whether these two binary states match over time. Mismatches are then classified into step-level patterns, with confabulated continuation being the dominant one: the answer proxy is already stable while the model keeps writing deliberative-looking text. The paper also compares architecture-matched Qwen2.5 and DeepSeek-R1-Distill model pairs to isolate the effect of reasoning distillation. To reduce dependence on a single probe, the logit-lens signal is cross-validated with Patchscopes, tuned-lens probes, and causal direction ablation.b9f:T46a,The study covers nine models and seven reasoning benchmarks. It uses the alignment-exponent framework of Everett et al. to measure how weight matrices and activations align during training. The key empirical observation is that nGPT does not match the alignment assumptions usually used in μP derivations. The authors therefore introduce a mid-alignment assumption: weights and activations are neither independent in the random-feature sense nor fully aligned, but partially aligned. Under this assumption, they derive a different width-scaling prescription for the learning rate and package it as a new nGPT parameterization called νGPT.

For depth transfer, the paper follows the line of work that studies residual networks with updates of the form h_{l+1}=h_l+n_layers^{-alpha_depth}F_l(h_l). The choice of alpha_depth controls the relative contribution of each residual block as depth grows. Prior work disagrees on whether alpha_depth=1/2 can provide reliable depth transfer in realistic blocks, while alpha_depth=1 is more consistently stable. νGPT adopts a depth-scaling heuristic aligned with the stable-transfer side of that literature. For token horizon, the paper finds that the optimal learning rate in nGPT scales approximately as the number of training tokens to the power -1/3, consistent with measurements reported for unnormalized Transformers. The final recipe combines width, depth, and horizon scaling rather than treating learning-rate transfer as a width-only issue.ba2:T526,The starting point is BLT: a local encoder processes bytes, an entropy-based patcher forms variable-length byte patches, a global model operates over latent patch representations, and a local decoder emits bytes. The paper introduces three mechanisms. BLT-D trains the decoder with both the standard next-byte prediction loss and a masked-byte prediction loss over corrupted fixed-size byte blocks. These blocks are derived from dynamically segmented patches but may cross patch boundaries, forcing the decoder to model future bytes beyond the average patch length. At inference time, a block of byte positions is initialized as masked and multiple positions are iteratively revealed per decoder step, reducing calls to the decoder, encoder, and global model. BLT-S is a self-speculative variant for standard BLT: the lightweight local decoder drafts bytes past the usual patch boundary, and the full BLT computation verifies the draft. Because rejected drafts roll back to the first mismatch, it preserves the output of standard autoregressive BLT while reducing expensive global evaluations. BLT-DV uses BLT-D’s dual training objective: diffusion decoding proposes a byte block, and the same model, run with causal masks, verifies it autoregressively. It trades some of BLT-D’s speed for tighter quality control.ba3:T46e,1. Unify all changes across domains, modalities, and preprocessing pipelines as data transformations, and distinguish two categories: bijective (information-preserving) transformations and non-bijective (information-destroying) transformations; 2. Prove that scaling exponents remain invariant under bijective transformations, providing strict theoretical guarantee; 3. Propose information resolution ρ(T) as the core metric, defined as the ratio of task-relevant mutual information between transformed input and label to that between original input and label; 4. Derive two mechanisms of scaling degradation under non-bijective transformations: variance inflation (increasing the sample size required for equivalent statistical precision) and optimal loss shift (raising the irreducible loss floor), and obtain the corrected general scaling formula based on ρ(T), which reduces to the standard Chinchilla form when ρ=1; 5. The framework does not require large-scale training sweeps in the target domain, only the calculation of information resolution is needed to transfer scaling laws from the source domain to the target domain.ba4:T4c9,Under the token-level policy gradient framework, this work derives two core properties of the cumulative token IS ratio, defined as the product of all per-token IS ratios up to position t. First, this ratio provides unbiased prefix distribution correction for gradient terms at each token position, as it fully accounts for the likelihood difference of the current prefix under the behavior and target policies. Second, its variance is strictly lower than full-sequence IS, since suffix tokens beyond position t have unit expectation under the behavior policy and only introduce unnecessary variance without reducing bias. To address the issue that the log variance of cumulative IS grows linearly with token position (Var(logρ_t^cum) = tσ²), which causes inconsistent regularization where early tokens are rarely clipped and late tokens are over-clipped under a fixed clipping threshold, this work proposes a position-adaptive clipping strategy that scales clipping thresholds proportionally to √t, matching the standard deviation growth of cumulative log IS and achieving consistent regularization intensity across all token positions. These two insights form the CTPO (Cumulative Token Policy Optimization) algorithm.ba5:T4f4,The study uses matched model pairs to separate base-model identity from reasoning-style training: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B versus Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B versus Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. The paper starts from a general scoring function s(x; θ, D_val), where x is a training example, θ is a model state or proxy model, and D_val is a validation set representing the target distribution. In offline curation, this score is computed once before training and converted into fixed weights or a selected subset. ADAPT instead updates the signal during training and uses it to assign continuous per-sample loss weights.

The key design choice is that weighting is driven by alignment with the validation set rather than by raw training loss alone. That is an important distinction. Loss-based online curricula often overemphasize hard examples, but high loss can come from noise, corruption, or out-of-domain content. ADAPT tries to estimate whether a sample is useful for the target distribution, not merely whether it is difficult. Operationally, the method acts like an adaptive per-sample step size: all data remain in the corpus, but their gradient contribution is scaled according to their current relevance.

Another useful aspect is the paper’s unified view of prior work. Offline selection becomes a 0/1 weighting scheme. Domain mixing becomes grouped weighting with fixed or slowly varying coefficients. Balancing methods are also reinterpreted as constrained reweighting. ADAPT differs along three axes: it is online rather than precomputed, sample-level rather than only domain-level, and soft rather than hard. Those choices explain why it can preserve diversity while still steering optimization toward the validation distribution. The paper also emphasizes that the method is global rather than merely batch-local, and that it adds almost no extra overhead because it does not require explicit resampling or rebuilding the dataset.ba8:T6f6,The experimental section is strong mainly because it evaluates the method under a unified protocol and across both pretraining and instruction tuning. The headline result is up to 7.2% higher accuracy per FLOP than offline baselines such as LESS, DoReMi, and RegMix, as well as prior online reweighting methods. It also reports up to 6.1% better out-of-domain generalization across benchmarks. Accuracy-per-FLOP is the right lens here, since an online method should be judged not only by final accuracy but also by whether it avoids the repeated proxy-score-and-retrain cycle of offline curation.

The experiments support several concrete claims. First, online soft weighting is more robust than offline hard filtering. Offline methods can look good on the validation target they optimize for, but they are more brittle once the evaluation distribution shifts, because they have already discarded part of the training support. Second, retaining the full dataset helps generalization. Weakly relevant or long-tail examples are not uniformly useless; their value changes over training. Third, dynamic weights outperform static weights, which directly supports the paper’s premise that sample importance is not fixed. Fourth, the gains transfer from pretraining to instruction tuning, suggesting that the method is not just a corpus-cleaning trick but a more general data allocation mechanism.

The ablations appear to focus on the right questions: sample-level versus group-level weighting, dynamic versus static weights, the choice of similarity or quality signal, update frequency, and the effect of keeping the full corpus versus filtering. The main takeaway is that the benefit comes from dynamic, fine-grained, continuous reweighting rather than from a particular scorer alone.ba9:T578,Start with the introduction and the unified formalization section. A careful read of method plus experiments should take around 1.5 to 2 hours.baa:T981,方法核心是把 document 作为路由共享单位，而不是让每个 token 在全体 expert 上自由选择。具体做法是：模型总共有很多 expert，例如 128 个，总激活数 top-k 为 8；但对同一篇 document，router 先为它选出一个共享 expert pool，例如 32 个 expert，文档内所有 token 只能在这 32 个里再做 top-k 选择。这样做的目的不是硬编码“这篇文档属于某个领域”，而是利用一个较弱但普遍成立的假设：同一文档中的 token 往往在语义上更一致，因此应该依赖相近的 expert 子集。

这个设计和标准 MoE 的关键区别有两点。第一，标准 MoE 的路由粒度是 token 级、候选空间是全局 expert 集合，容易让不同 token 因局部词法特征走向不同 expert，最终一个任务会覆盖大量 expert；Emo 先加了文档级共享池约束，把路由自由度从“全局任意选”收缩到“文档内共享候选集”，从而鼓励 recurring expert subsets 在训练语料中反复出现。第二，和 FlexOlmo、BTX 这类显式按领域切分 expert 的方法不同，Emo 不需要预定义 math/code/biology 之类标签，也不把 expert 绑定到固定人工类别，而是让模块结构从数据里自发形成。

从机制上看，这个约束改变了 expert specialization 的压力来源。标准 MoE 中，expert 更容易因为高频局部模式而分工，例如标点、功能词、位置相关模式，因为这些模式在 token 级 routing 下最稳定、最容易被 router 捕捉。Emo 把文档内 token 的候选 expert 集合绑定在一起后，单个 token 的局部差异不再足以驱动完全不同的路由，router 更有动力按文档级统计规律组织 expert，于是 specialization 更可能落在 topic/domain 这类跨 token 持续存在的高层因素上。论文强调，这种更高语义粒度的 specialization 正是 modularity 的来源。

从训练目标上，Emo 仍然保持 MoE 语言模型的主干训练方式，重点不是改 loss 形式，而是改 routing constraint。也就是说，它试图在不牺牲 full-model 通用性能的前提下，给 MoE 增加一个结构归纳偏置：同域 token 共享更相近的 expert 子空间。这个取舍很重要，因为如果模块化是靠强监督硬切出来的，往往会损失组合后的整体能力；Emo 的目标是 full model 仍然强，同时子集也可用。bab:T8f9,实验规模是这篇工作的一个重要支点：作者训练了一个 14B total、1B active 的 Emo，并在 1 trillion tokens 上预训练，同时给出同数据、同规模的标准 MoE baseline。主结果有两部分。

第一，作为完整模型使用时，Emo 的整体性能与标准 MoE 基本匹配。这一点很关键，因为它说明文档级共享 expert pool 并没有明显破坏 MoE 作为通用基座模型的能力。若 full-model 性能明显掉点，这个方法就更像部署特化模型，而不是通用预训练方案。

第二，也是论文最核心的结果：在只保留部分 expert 的受限部署设置下，Emo 的性能下降显著更小。作者在 MMLU 和 MMLU-Pro 的领域子集上做 expert subset identification 与部署，例如数学、物理、生物、社会科学等。结果显示，只保留 25% 的 expert 时，Emo 仅约 1 个百分点绝对性能下降；只保留 12.5% expert 时，下降约 3 个百分点。对照的标准 MoE 在相同约束下分别下降约 10 和 15 个百分点。这个差距已经不是轻微改进，而是说明两类模型的 expert 组织方式完全不同：标准 MoE 的 expert 子集不可独立用，Emo 的子集则在相当程度上可独立部署。

论文还做了路由分析，结论是 Emo 的 expert subset 更倾向于按高层语义主题聚类，例如 math、code 等，而标准 MoE 更容易出现低层 syntactic/lexical specialization，例如 prepositions、punctuation。这个分析不是装饰性的，它直接解释了为什么标准 MoE 在裁掉大部分 expert 后会崩：因为它的能力分散在很多细碎、跨任务共享的低层 expert 上；而 Emo 把同域能力更集中地组织进可复用的子集。

从摘要可见的数字之外，阅读正文时应特别留意作者如何定义“最相关 expert”的选择方式，以及 subset selection 是基于开发集统计、路由频率还是其他启发式。如果选择过程很复杂，部署价值会打折；如果选择过程简单且稳定，方法的实用性会更强。另一个值得看的是不同 pool size、top-k、expert 总数对 modularity 与 full-model performance 的权衡，这类消融通常能说明模块化究竟来自文档约束本身，还是来自更强的容量瓶颈。bac:T73c,The core idea is to make routing partially document-conditioned rather than fully token-global. In a standard MoE, each token selects its top-k experts from the full expert set. In Emo, each document first gets a shared expert pool, and every token in that document can only choose its active experts from that pool. For example, with 128 total experts and top-8 activation, a document may be assigned a pool of 32 experts, and all tokens in that document must select their 8 active experts from those 32. Different documents can use different pools.

This changes the inductive bias of routing. Standard token-level routing has enough freedom that experts often specialize in frequent local patterns such as punctuation, function words, or other low-level lexical cues. Those are easy for the router to detect and reward, but they do not produce deployable modules. Emo constrains that freedom by tying the candidate expert set across all tokens in a document. Since documents tend to be semantically coherent, the router is pushed to organize experts around document-level regularities rather than token-local quirks. Recurrent expert subsets can then emerge across the corpus without any explicit domain labels.

This is different from prior domain-partitioned MoEs such as approaches that assign experts to predefined categories like code or biology. Those methods rely on human priors and fixed taxonomies. Emo instead uses document boundaries as weak supervision and lets the modular structure emerge from data. The training objective remains that of an MoE language model; the main intervention is the routing constraint, not a fundamentally new LM loss. That design choice is important: the method tries to preserve full-model generality while inducing subset-level modularity, rather than trading one for the other through hard specialization.bad:T82e,The experimental setup is large enough to make the claims meaningful: the authors train a 14B-total, 1B-active Emo model on 1 trillion tokens, alongside a matched standard MoE baseline trained on the same data. The first key result is that as a full model, Emo matches the baseline MoE in overall performance. This is essential, because it shows the document-level shared-pool constraint does not significantly damage the model’s utility as a general-purpose pretrained LM.

The second and central result is subset deployment. On domain-specific subsets of MMLU and MMLU-Pro, including areas such as math, physics, biology, and social sciences, the authors identify relevant expert subsets and evaluate the model while retaining only a fraction of experts. Emo loses only about 1 absolute point when keeping 25% of experts, and about 3 points when keeping 12.5%. The matched standard MoE drops by roughly 10 and 15 points under the same constraints. That gap is large enough to indicate a qualitative difference in how expertise is organized, not just a mild robustness improvement.

The routing analysis is also important. Emo’s experts appear to specialize at higher semantic granularity, such as topic or domain, whereas standard MoE experts are more associated with low-level syntactic or lexical patterns like punctuation and prepositions. This analysis directly supports the modularity claim: if expertise is concentrated into semantically coherent subsets, partial deployment becomes viable; if it is scattered across many low-level experts, it does not.

When reading the full paper, it is worth checking how the “relevant experts” are selected at evaluation time. If subset identification depends on heavy supervision or expensive search, the deployment story weakens. If it is simple and stable, the practical value is much stronger. - CCA（Compressed Convolutional Attention）：在压缩潜空间做序列混合，用轻量卷积下投影减少训练与 prefill FLOPs，并降低长上下文 KV-cache 压力；作者声称在保持类似 KV 压缩率下，训练速度优于 GQA/MLA 方案。

- learned residual scaling：对 residual stream 与 layer input 做可学习缩放，控制深层 residual norm 增长，几乎不增加 FLOPs。
训练策略强调“推理从头做”：
- 预训练/中期训练就混入长 CoT 数据。为解决 CoT 超过上下文长度，引入 Answer-Preserving Trimming（AP-trimming）：截断推理尾部但保留最终答案；若仅答案也放不下则丢弃。它是数据构造阶段的长度控制，而不是推理时或 rollout 时的长度控制。
- 后训练是四段式 RL cascade：先做 math/puzzle reasoning warmup；再做基于 RLVE-Gym 的 400-task 自适应难度课程；再做 math+code 的可验证 RL 并结合 test-time compute 轨迹；最后做行为/偏好相关的 RL 收尾。实现上用异步 PipelineRL，并组合 DPPO Binary-TV 的 trust-region masking、Dr-GRPO 的序列级损失聚合、MaxRL advantage 等；显式提到 reward 里不加 KL 正则，稳定性主要靠 verifier、精度与数据治理。
- Markovian RSA：把 RSA 的递归候选聚合与 Markovian Thinking 的“有界工作区”结合。推理被拆成分阶段批量推断：每阶段并行生成 N 个候选，每个候选 decode 长度上限为 β；聚合时只携带长度为 τ 的 tail（C 个片段）而不是全历史，从而把长推理变成可控的 prefill/上下文开销。更关键的是它被纳入训练：用 expert-model rollouts 重排成聚合样本做 SFT，并在 RL 阶段同时训练“专家模型”和“自聚合策略”变体，让模型适配这种推理工作流。bb0:T865,ZAYA1-8B is an MoE++ model with 8B total / 700M active parameters. The architecture changes are:
- CCA (Compressed Convolutional Attention): performs sequence mixing in a compressed latent space via a lightweight convolutional down-projector, aiming to reduce training and prefill FLOPs and shrink KV-cache pressure for long context.
- ZAYA1 router: replaces the standard linear MoE router with a multi-layer MLP router to increase routing expressiveness; positioned as a small-parameter component that controls a large expert parameter pool, improving load balancing stability and quality.
- Learned residual scaling: learnable scaling on both the residual stream and layer input to control residual-norm growth with negligible overhead.
Training is “reasoning from scratch”:
- Reasoning/CoT data is included already in pretraining and midtraining. To fit long traces into limited context, AP-trimming truncates the tail of the reasoning while preserving the final answer; samples are dropped if even the answer cannot fit. This is a data-construction-time length control, not an inference-time or rollout-time constraint.
- Post-training uses a 4-stage RL cascade: (i) reasoning warmup on math/puzzles, (ii) a 400-task adaptive curriculum on RLVE-Gym, (iii) math+code verifiable RL with test-time-compute traces, and (iv) a final behavioral RL stage. Implementation details include asynchronous PipelineRL, DPPO Binary-TV trust-region masking, Dr-GRPO sequence-level aggregation, MaxRL advantage estimation, and explicitly no KL term in the reward (stability is handled via verifiers/precision/data curation).
- Markovian RSA (test-time compute): combines RSA-style recursive candidate aggregation with Markovian bounded-workspace thinking. Inference is staged batched decoding: each stage generates N candidates in parallel, each capped by decode length β; aggregation only carries forward C tails of length τ rather than the full history. Crucially, the workflow is trained into the model: SFT data is built by reshuffling expert rollouts into aggregation examples, and RL trains both an expert-model and a self-aggregation policy variant.bb1:T4bc,UniPool replaces layer-private expert sets with a single globally shared expert pool. Each MoE layer still has its own router, so routing remains depth-conditioned, but all routers select from the same pool. Two design choices make this viable. First, the auxiliary load-balancing loss is moved from the layer level to the pool level. In conventional MoE, each layer balances its own private experts to avoid dead experts. With a shared pool, that objective is misaligned: an expert can be unused by one layer but heavily used by others. UniPool aggregates token-to-expert assignments across layers and balances utilization at the level where parameters are actually owned, namely the global pool. Second, the model uses NormRouter rather than a standard softmax router. Since routers at different depths compete over the same larger pool, layer-dependent hidden-state scales can create inconsistent routing sharpness. NormRouter uses L2 normalization, ReLU scoring, and a learnable scale, which reduces scale sensitivity, encourages sparse competition, and lets each layer tune routing strength during training. This differs from post-hoc expert pruning or merging because the sharing is built into pretraining.bb2:T5a8,The proposed model is Momentum DeltaNet. The paper starts from the interpretation of Delta Linear Attention as an online optimization process and replaces the plain SGD-style update with a stepwise momentum rule. Momentum introduces an auxiliary state that accumulates past gradient information, which can smooth updates and preserve longer-range signals.

The main technical device is a chunkwise parallel algorithm for this stepwise momentum recurrence. Instead of using blockwise momentum, which weakens within-block causality and creates a training-inference mismatch, the paper algebraically reorders the update coefficients so that the same causal stepwise rule can be evaluated in parallel within chunks. The derived equivalent coefficients include terms such as \(\widetilde{\alpha}_t=\alpha_t+\mu_t\beta_t/\beta_{t-1}\), \(\widetilde{\beta}_t=\beta_t\eta_t\), and \(\widetilde{\gamma}_t=\alpha_{t-1}\mu_t\beta_t/\beta_{t-1}\). Training uses the parallel chunk form, while recurrent decoding keeps the original stepwise update.

The paper also analyzes the momentum recurrence as a second-order dynamical system. Momentum changes the spectrum of the recurrence and can introduce complex eigenvalues. This gives the model richer temporal dynamics, but it also creates stability concerns. MDN therefore uses constrained gating mechanisms rather than unconstrained gates. This design is motivated by the dynamics, not only by empirical tuning.bb3:T5dc,ViTok-v2 is a continuous latent ViT autoencoder. An encoder maps an image x into a latent z with spatial downsampling factor f and channel dimension c. The compression ratio is defined as r=3f^2/c. Lower r preserves more information and improves reconstruction, but it produces a larger latent space that is harder for a downstream flow or diffusion model to learn. The paper makes several design changes around this axis. It introduces native-resolution training with a NaFlex-style setup and 2D RoPE, replacing fixed absolute positional embeddings so that a model trained at 256p can operate at 512p, 1024p, and varying aspect ratios. It scales the decoder aggressively: the largest model has 5B parameters, with a 4.5B decoder and a 463M encoder, more than 14 times larger than the 350M ViTok scale. The emphasis on decoder scale is important because, at a fixed bottleneck, reconstruction depends heavily on how well the decoder can invert the compressed representation. The paper also introduces a DINOv3 perceptual loss. A frozen DINOv3 model provides feature-level reconstruction supervision, replacing both LPIPS and GAN losses. This removes discriminator instability while keeping a perceptual signal beyond pixel L1. Finally, the paper compares KL, tanh, and LayerNorm latent regularization and finds little effect on generation quality at scale, making simpler deterministic encoders viable. The autoencoders are paired with 450M and 1.2B flow generators across r values of 12, 24, and 48.bb4:T46b,The experimental program has four main parts. The interaction protocol has three parties: user, base assistant, and defender. If blocked, the candidate response is replaced by a refusal. The learning target is to intervene exactly at the first harm-enabling turn.

Dialogue-level harmfulness labels are too coarse for learning when to intervene.

The reward is designed to favor timely interception at the closure turn while penalizing both premature refusal and delayed blocking. This is an important design choice: optimizing only final attack success would likely push the monitor toward overly conservative behavior, whereas process rewards align the objective with precise temporal localization.

Relative to prior approaches, the differences are clear. It is not a single-turn policy compliance checker. It is not a query-only monitor. And it is not trained only on dialogue-level judgments. The most informative figures and tables should be the task illustration, the main safety-utility results, the response-aware ablation, and the error analysis.bb8:T51c,First, a unified perspective is derived: for each prompt, K sampled responses form a finite-dimensional response simplex. All mainstream group-based policy gradient methods implicitly construct a reward-weighted softmax target distribution on this simplex, with target sharpness determined by the advantage normalization scheme. Subsequent policy gradient updates are merely first-order approximations of reverse KL projection toward this implicit target.
Based on this insight, LPO makes the projection process explicit: 1) It constrains the proximal RL objective to the set of sampled responses to obtain a closed-form target distribution, with a temperature parameter to control target sharpness, eliminating the need for empirical advantage normalization tuning. 2) It projects the policy onto the target via divergence minimization on the response simplex, decoupling the two steps of target construction and projection, and natively supports different divergence choices (the paper implements both forward KL and reverse KL variants).
Gradients from explicit projection are inherently bounded, zero-sum, and self-correcting, requiring no additional gradient clipping or normalization to reduce optimization variance, and monotonic improvement of listwise reward per iteration is theoretically provable.bb9:T4eb,The work proceeds from mechanistic characterization to an RL-free replacement.
Mechanistic findings via token-level comparisons across multiple model families and RL algorithms:
- Only ~1–3% of token positions are meaningfully altered by RL.
- The token promoted by RL is always within the base model’s top-5 candidates, indicating reranking rather than novel token invention.
- Edits concentrate at high-entropy decision points (branching tokens).
Causality is tested with oracle interventions: correcting the specific token at those positions recovers a large fraction of RL’s gains, while random corrections/locations do not.
Predictability: the decision points can be located without an RL-trained model using the base model’s own token entropy peaks.
Low-dimensionality: the full correction is claimed to be representable with a tiny fraction of parameters.
Based on this, ReasonMaxxer is introduced:
- Sample a small set of rollouts from the base model.
- Use entropy gating to select decision points.
- Apply an advantage-weighted contrastive loss only at gated positions, while anchoring all other tokens to the base distribution to prevent global distribution shift.
- Entirely offline; no online RL rollouts or iterative policy optimization.bba:T432,The work combines controlled experiments, a mechanistic explanation, and a case study. The first is the benchmark. The authors build 300 verifiably false premises covering seven error categories and 21 domains. Each premise is evaluated in two matched settings: an isolated condition, where the false claim is presented directly, and a contextualized condition, where the same claim is embedded in task framing composed of background, output specification, and scope instructions. The design is careful because it turns suppression into a behavioral dissociation under controlled prompt variation, rather than a generic drop in accuracy.

The second component is the mechanism analysis on open-weight models. The authors compare isolated and contextualized prompts using hidden-state representations, uncertainty at the false-claim position, and attention patterns across layers. Their main claim is that suppression is not a knowledge failure. Uncertainty patterns remain strongly correlated across the two conditions, suggesting that the model still internally registers the problematic content. The difference emerges in routing and response formation: early-layer attention is pulled toward task framing, and middle layers increasingly encode a compliance-oriented output plan. In other words, the model still “knows,” but the generation policy no longer prioritizes correction.

The third component is intervention. CDS, or Correction Direction Steering, estimates a representation-space direction that separates corrective behavior from compliant behavior, then injects that direction at middle layers before the output intent fully crystallizes. This is a targeted activation-steering method tailored to the identified failure mode. DPA, or Dynamic Payload Amplification, avoids calibration data. It uses the observed attention divergence to identify payload tokens—tokens carrying the false content that should matter for correction—and amplifies their representations so that factual deliberation remains active instead of being drowned out by task instructions. CDS is the stronger and more explicit control method; DPA is lighter-weight and easier to deploy when calibration is unavailable.bc0:T6c3,The empirical section covers prevalence, mechanism, and intervention. 第二部分是 teacher consistency 的理论分析。作者指出，OPD 实际上有两个 teacher：一个用于生成 SFT 训练轨迹，决定了 reference policy π_ref 所在的数据支持；另一个用于 OPD 阶段提供目标分布。如果这两个 teacher 不一致，那么 student 被要求在一个由 teacher A 诱导的数据分布上，去拟合 teacher B 的 token 分布，目标函数会出现不可消除的偏差。作者把这种偏差写成优化目标中的系统性 mismatch，并分析其固定点性质：即使在线采样、即使训练足够久，也不会收敛到标准 OPD 想要的最优解。离线场景下，这个问题更严重，因为 rollout 分布也被冻结在错误 teacher 诱导的参考策略附近。

第三部分是 Lightning OPD 的构造。做法并不复杂，但关键在于约束关系被理顺了：先选定一个 teacher π_T；用这个同一个 teacher 生成 SFT 轨迹，把 base model 训成 reference policy π_ref；然后从 π_ref 采样固定 rollouts，对这些 responses 预计算同一个 teacher 的 token log-prob；最后在训练阶段只更新 student，不再需要在线 teacher。理论上，作者证明在 teacher consistency 成立时，Lightning OPD 与 standard OPD 共享相同最优点；两者的梯度差异在训练过程中有界，不会无限累积。更有意思的是，离线目标由于固定在 π_ref 支撑集上，天然带来一种抑制 policy drift 的隐式正则效果，因此不需要额外显式 KL penalty 也能保持稳定。这一点很像把 on-policy distillation 的有效区域锚定在 reference neighborhood 内，用数据支持而不是额外正则去限制漂移。

和已有方法相比，区别主要有三点。其一，不是简单把 online teacher cache 成离线表，而是先解释为什么有些离线 OPD 失败。其二，关注点不是 reward shaping 或 advantage estimator 改进，而是 teacher/data/reference 三者的一致性。其三，它把“offline”从近似妥协变成了在特定条件下与 online 等价的训练形式，这个论证比单纯报速度提升更重要。bc6:T41e,The paper addresses a practical bottleneck in On-Policy Distillation (OPD): standard OPD needs a live teacher model during training to score student rollouts token by token, which makes reasoning post-training expensive and infrastructure-heavy. A natural workaround is to precompute teacher log-probabilities on SFT rollouts and reuse them offline. In practice, that naive offline variant often underperforms. The central claim of the paper is that the main issue is not offline approximation itself, but a missing condition in prior OPD pipelines: the teacher used to generate SFT trajectories and the teacher used to provide OPD token distributions must be the same model. The paper calls this teacher consistency. Once this condition is violated, both offline and online OPD optimize a biased objective and converge to a suboptimal fixed point. Lightning OPD is built on this observation: enforce teacher consistency, precompute teacher scores once on reference-policy rollouts, and remove the live teacher server without changing the target optimum.bc7:T967,The method has three layers.

First, the paper reframes the online requirement in OPD. Standard OPD samples rollouts from the current student policy, queries the teacher for token log-probabilities on those rollouts, and updates the student with dense token-level advantage weighting. Because the rollout distribution changes during training, the teacher appears to be inherently online. The authors start from an empirical observation: during OPD, the student policy does not drift very far from the SFT reference policy. That opens the door to using a fixed rollout distribution.

Second, the paper introduces and analyzes teacher consistency. OPD implicitly involves two teachers: one teacher generates the trajectories used in SFT and therefore shapes the support of the reference policy, while another teacher may be used during OPD to provide target token distributions. If these are different, the student is asked to fit teacher B on data induced by teacher A. The paper argues that this creates an irreducible mismatch in the objective. The analysis goes beyond offline caching: even standard online OPD remains biased under this mismatch and converges to the wrong fixed point. Offline training makes the issue worse because the rollout distribution is also frozen around the wrong reference policy.

Third, Lightning OPD is the consistent offline construction. Choose one teacher π_T. Use that same teacher to generate SFT trajectories and train the base model into a reference policy π_ref. Then sample fixed rollouts from π_ref, precompute token log-probabilities from the same teacher on those responses, and train the student without any live teacher server. The theoretical result is the key part: under teacher consistency, Lightning OPD shares the same optimum as standard OPD, and the gradient discrepancy between the offline and online objectives stays bounded during training. The paper also argues that the offline objective introduces an implicit regularization effect: because training remains anchored to the support of π_ref, policy drift is naturally limited even without an explicit KL penalty.

Relative to prior OPD work, the novelty is not just caching teacher outputs. The paper explains why some offline attempts fail, isolates the failure mode as teacher mismatch, and turns offline OPD from a heuristic approximation into a conditionally equivalent training procedure.bc8:T777,The experiments cover mathematical reasoning and code generation, with student–teacher pairs including Qwen3-4B distilled from Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-8B distilled from Qwen3-32B. The headline result stated in the paper is that Lightning OPD matches or exceeds standard OPD across all reported benchmarks while delivering about a 4.0× training speedup by removing parallel teacher serving.

The most important empirical evidence appears to come from four types of comparisons. First, a naive offline baseline: simply caching teacher log-probabilities on existing SFT rollouts does not reliably match standard OPD when the SFT teacher and the OPD teacher differ. Second, teacher-consistency ablations: once the same teacher is used for both SFT trajectory generation and OPD supervision, offline performance recovers and becomes competitive with online OPD. Third, online mismatch controls: the paper shows that teacher inconsistency also hurts standard online OPD, which is crucial because it demonstrates that the issue is objective bias rather than offline approximation error. Fourth, training-dynamics analysis: the student stays relatively close to the reference policy, and the offline variant shows stable optimization behavior, supporting the implicit-regularization argument.

The empirical starting point is simple: train on compositional tasks where atomic skills are sampled either from a power-law distribution or a uniform distribution, then evaluate under a uniform test distribution. Power-law training still performs better, so the gain is not explained by matching the test distribution. The theoretical core is a k-multiplicative composition task, designed to isolate the difficulty of learning products or compositions of k latent skills. Under uniform sampling, the relevant learning signal remains highly symmetric and high-order; the paper proves that learning requires d^{Ω(k)} samples or runtime. Under power-law sampling, frequency asymmetry breaks this symmetry. Gradient descent can first fit high-frequency components, and this staged progress turns the remaining problem into a much easier one, with d^{O(1)} sample and runtime requirements. The same staged mechanism is then checked in state tracking: head skills are acquired first, and their acquisition strengthens the signal for scarce skills later in training.bcb:T473,The motivating arithmetic setup uses direct-answer multi-step expressions with k=4 sequential operations, including addition, subtraction, and multiplication. Each operation-operand pair is treated as an atomic skill. Training samples skills from either a power-law or a uniform distribution, while evaluation is uniform. Power-law training consistently beats uniform training. The k-hop state tracking experiments show a stronger optimization gap: with uniform sampling, the model cannot learn the implicit multi-hop task without extra supervision such as chain-of-thought or curriculum learning; with power-law sampling, the same type of model can learn directly. The theory gives the sharpest quantitative statement: uniform training requires d^{Ω(k)} samples or runtime, while gradient descent under a power-law distribution requires only d^{O(1)}. Additional synthetic natural-language experiments, including multi-hop QA and grade-school math style tasks, show the same direction of effect. This differs from standard long-context extension recipes that rely on training directly on long sequences after changing the RoPE base. Each learner keeps its own model replica θ_m and runs an inner optimizer, such as AdamW, on its local data shard for H steps. Synchronization is expressed through the DiLoCo outer update: the difference between a learner’s current parameters and a reference parameter state is treated as an outer gradient, and an outer optimizer aggregates these updates. Earlier DiLoCo synchronized all learners every H steps. Streaming DiLoCo split parameters into P fragments, synchronized different fragments at different offsets, and allowed a small communication delay τ to reduce peak bandwidth. Decoupled DiLoCo removes the blocking barrier. Learners can continue training without waiting for all other learners to reach the same synchronization point. A central synchronizer asynchronously receives learner updates and sends reconciled parameter updates back. The design deliberately trades strict consistency for availability and partition tolerance. The main algorithmic question becomes how to control parameter drift through H, fragment size, delay, update scheduling, and the outer optimizer. Compared with elastic SPMD, it does not simply resize a still-synchronous job after a failure; it limits the failure blast radius to the affected learner. Compared with naive asynchronous SGD, it keeps the DiLoCo structure of multi-step local training and outer optimization, which is better aligned with bandwidth-constrained pre-training.bcf:T4b2,The experiments are organized around three claims: asynchronous learners should not materially degrade pre-training quality; the method should work for both dense and MoE models; and it should improve goodput under realistic failures. A configuration combines update mechanism and state precision, such as momentum usage, adaptive statistics, and low-precision states. The pipeline has four stages. First, it samples sparse gradient streams from each block; the default sampling rate is 0.1% of coordinates, fixed after sampling. Second, it computes lightweight block-level metrics with running statistics, including signals such as directional stability, scale anisotropy, and noise. Third, it converts these metrics into a mismatch-risk score for each block-configuration pair. Fourth, it solves a constrained mixed-integer linear program that minimizes total risk while satisfying optimizer-state memory and update-time budgets. The memory definition is careful: it counts only persistent optimizer-owned state tensors and excludes parameters, gradients, activations, scratch buffers, FP32 master weights, and EMA copies. Update time is normalized against AdamW16 and estimated with a lightweight one-step timing measurement. The key difference from global 8-bit optimizers, Adafactor, or projection-based methods is that BAOC does not assume one low-memory mechanism is suitable for all layers.bd1:T44e,The method builds a discrete diffusion process using Glauber dynamics. The state space is a length-L token sequence. Glauber dynamics updates local coordinates and samples according to a stationary distribution defined by an energy function. The paper sets this energy function using a pretrained language model, with a distribution of the form p(x) proportional to exp(-f(x)). This is different from masked diffusion processes that diffuse toward a generic masking distribution or from discrete diffusion with simple uniform transition kernels.

The lower-level RM update depends on the data distribution induced by the current policy. By analytically unrolling this update, they decompose the true policy gradient into the usual policy-gradient term and an additional parameter-steering term. The latter measures how current policy samples change future reward-model parameters.

They then propose Foresighted Policy Optimization, or FPO. Rather than replacing the whole RLHF pipeline, FPO adds a targeted penalty during policy optimization to account for the missing steering effect. The analysis is first developed in a pointwise setting to expose the geometry, then extended to pairwise preference comparisons. The exact bilevel term would normally require inverse-Hessian computations. The first component is the Production Knowledge System. The authors argue that raw anime data is too diverse for a stable implicit prior to emerge on its own, so they introduce structured supervision. This includes an industrial production taxonomy that factorizes clips along four controllable axes: Style, Motion, Camera, and VFX. On top of that, they build AniCaption, which is not a standard captioner describing visible content, but a system that infers production variables and verbalizes them as creator- or director-like instructions. This is an important shift. The conditioning signal is no longer “what is in the clip,” but “how the clip should be authored.” The paper also mentions graph-based multimodal reasoning in the annotation pipeline, suggesting that the labels are inferred from relations across frames, semantics, and visual cues rather than extracted from a flat template. A dual-channel conditioning interface then separates precise production control from more flexible artistic intent, which likely reduces the burden on a single text channel to encode both hard constraints and soft style cues.

The second component is a progressive style-motion-deformation curriculum. This appears to be the main training innovation. The gap between natural-video priors and extreme anime expression is decomposed into three axes: style diversity, motion amplitude, and deformation intensity. Instead of mixing all anime samples at once, which the authors claim leads to early collapse, training proceeds through a controlled schedule that gradually increases difficulty along these axes. The rationale is strong: the optimization difficulty is not just “harder samples,” but a compounded mismatch across multiple dimensions that each break the original prior in a different way. A curriculum aligned with the source of domain shift is more principled than generic curricula based only on resolution or noise level.

The third component is deformation-aware preference optimization. Standard metrics such as FVD or CLIP-based similarity are poorly suited here because both intentional stylization and pathological corruption can look like deviations from natural video statistics. The paper therefore introduces a domain-specific reward model and uses preference optimization to teach the generator what counts as good anime deformation versus broken structure. The key idea is not merely adding a reward model, but redefining the reward boundary itself: physics violations are not uniformly bad; unsupported distortions are. If the full paper provides details on preference data construction, positive/negative pair generation, and how the reward model is integrated into training, that section is likely one of the most informative parts.

Compared with prior anime-generation work that mainly adds control modules or post-hoc alignment on top of physics-trained backbones, AniMatrix seems to intervene earlier, at the level of supervision design and optimization trajectory. The novelty is less about any single component and more about how the three conditioning signals complement each other.

Stage 1 is Draft. Given a prompt p, the LLM generates a coarse visual draft d in the form of discrete vision tokens. This draft is not treated as the final image. It is a low-fidelity scene plan. The paper argues that this step is necessary because, without a concrete visual instance, later evaluation would collapse into generic prompt rewriting rather than grounded diagnosis.

Stage 2 is Evaluate. The same LLM takes the original prompt and the draft, compares them, and outputs a grounded evaluation e: a concise textual description of what is wrong or missing in the draft. This is the key move in the paper. The system exploits the empirical asymmetry that the unified model is better at post hoc diagnosis than at one-shot generation. Instead of asking the model to satisfy all constraints directly, it first asks it to create something inspectable and then to critique that object.

Stage 3 is Diffuse. A frozen SANA diffusion model is conditioned jointly on (p, d, e). The prompt provides the global semantic target, the draft provides a spatial anchor and scene layout, and the evaluation provides localized corrective instructions. The paper repeatedly argues that these signals are complementary: draft alone would preserve its own mistakes, evaluation alone without a visual anchor would reduce to prompt rewriting, and prompt alone returns to the standard text-conditioned diffusion setup.

Relative to prior work, this is not just prompt enhancement, because the evaluation is grounded in a specific visual draft. It is also different from generic coarse-to-fine generation, because the refinement signal is explicit language feedback rather than an implicit latent refinement path. From a pretraining perspective, the method also encodes a practical division of labor: the LLM handles discrete planning and semantic verification, while diffusion handles high-fidelity rendering. That division is more realistic than expecting one model to jointly master fine-grained pixel synthesis and compositional reasoning at the same level.be1:T6e6,The main empirical result is clear: with the same frozen SANA diffusion backbone, UniReasoner improves prompt faithfulness rather than merely image quality. Draft alone can lock the generator into the draft’s mistakes; evaluation alone lacks a concrete spatial reference. Even though the provided excerpt does not include every table entry, the logic of the ablation and the reported gains strongly suggest that the improvement comes from complementary conditioning rather than from simply adding more tokens.

Those are the places where the idea could evolve into a broader training or inference framework.be3:T499,Uni-OPD uses a dual-perspective recipe. From the student side, it improves exploration with two balancing strategies. Offline difficulty-aware balancing shapes the training distribution by sample difficulty, so training is not dominated by trivial examples or by examples that are too hard to learn from. Online correctness-aware balancing then uses the student’s current rollout correctness to keep training focused on informative states, especially near the boundary between correct and incorrect behavior. From the teacher side, the paper introduces outcome-guided margin calibration. Vanilla OPD trusts the teacher’s token probabilities on student rollouts, but those rollouts can be out of distribution for the teacher. The proposed calibration uses outcome reward as a global anchor: after aggregating token-level teacher scores over a trajectory, correct trajectories should rank above incorrect ones by a margin. If this order consistency is violated, the teacher signal is adjusted. This is meant to handle teacher degradation on unusual student prefixes, fluent but wrong reasoning chains, conflicts between multiple teachers, and unstable multimodal supervision.be4:T543,The method decomposes evaluation into rubric generation and rubric-conditioned judging. A rubric is considered useful if it helps a judge assign a higher score to a preferred response than to a dispreferred one. Rubric quality is therefore directly trainable through discriminative utility, measured by the score gap induced by the rubric. The paper formulates rubrics as latent variables and derives a training objective from a variational-inference view. Training alternates between two phases. In the policy phase, a frozen rubric model generates rubrics for questions; the policy samples multiple responses; a frozen judge scores the responses under the rubric; GRPO updates the policy using these rubric-derived rewards. In the rubric phase, preference pairs are built through temporal contrast: current-policy responses are treated as preferred, earlier-checkpoint responses as dispreferred. The rubric generator samples candidate rubrics, and receives reward when the judge conditioned on that rubric separates the pair in the right direction with a larger gap. This differs from GPT-4.1-generated rubrics or labeled rubric training because it does not require an external rubric teacher. 1) Fit a standard Chinchilla loss law on single-epoch runs (no repetition) as a function of model size N and training tokens D.
2) For multi-epoch training, first pretend repeated tokens are fresh: D = U_D · (1 + R_D), and use the single-epoch Chinchilla fit to predict the expected loss.
3) Define the residual (observed minus predicted) as repetition-induced damage. Empirically, this residual follows a power law in repetition count R_D and is superlinear.
4) Study how the residual coefficient varies with configuration: larger N and smaller unique data U_D lead to larger penalties. This motivates a family (“complexity ladder”) of additive penalty forms with 1, 2, and 4 parameters, trading simplicity for fit quality.
5) Use the fitted law to prescribe compute-optimal allocations in the data-constrained regime, solving for (N, R_D) that minimize validation loss under a compute/token budget. The key new prescription is the existence of an optimal repetition level; beyond it, scaling N is better than adding epochs.
6) Because overfitting is captured by a single coefficient, the law can compare training setups; the paper demonstrates this with weight decay, including predicting the compute point where strong regularization overtakes the standard setting.be7:T41e,Its main contribution is not a new model architecture but a stronger training signal for agent post-training. Rewards are divided by source into intrinsic and external rewards. Intrinsic rewards are then split into certainty-based and ensemble-based rewards. Certainty-based rewards use signals derived from the policy itself, such as token entropy, trajectory likelihood, sequence probability, self-certainty, or probability gaps over answer tokens. Examples include RLIF, EM-RL, RENT, RLSC, and RLSF. Ensemble-based rewards use agreement among multiple rollouts, with majority voting as the central case.

The technical core is the sharpening mechanism. For majority-style rewards, if an answer is already the majority under the initial sampling distribution, RL updates increase its probability further. For certainty-style rewards, the update favors outputs that the model already assigns high confidence to. The paper analyzes one-step dynamics and convergence, and then generalizes the argument through a unified reward framework in the appendix. The induced optimum is not the true answer distribution. It is a sharpened version of the model’s initial distribution.

This explains the main tradeoff. If the initial model prior is aligned with correctness, sharpening raises accuracy and consistency. If the prior is misaligned, the same training objective reinforces wrong answers. The paper also introduces model collapse step as a practical proxy for prior quality. A model that collapses later under intrinsic URLVR tends to have more usable prior structure and is more likely to benefit from RL.bee:T694,The experiments compare multiple intrinsic URLVR variants, including majority-voting methods and certainty-based rewards. The analysis tracks training dynamics rather than only final accuracy: answer distributions, majority stability, confidence metrics, collapse behavior, and per-problem sharpening are all used.

The first recurring pattern is early improvement followed by collapse. Early gains come from making initially correct majority answers more stable. Longer training reduces diversity and can reinforce wrong modes, which causes performance to degrade.

The second pattern is method-dependent failure. Majority-voting rewards fail when the sampled majority answer is wrong. Certainty-based rewards fail when the model is poorly calibrated and assigns high confidence to incorrect reasoning paths. In that case, entropy minimization or likelihood-based rewards turn overconfidence into the training target.

The third pattern is that constrained usage is safer. Small training sets reduce distribution drift and delay collapse. Test-time training is also safer because adaptation is local to a problem or a small batch of problems, making it closer to controlled sharpening of the current prior.

The fourth pattern is predictive: collapse step correlates with later RL gains. The paper studies different backbones, training stages, model scales, generation settings, and training datasets, and finds that resistance to collapse is an informative early signal. 从与已有方法的区别看，νGPT 不是简单给 nGPT 加一个 Depth-μP 标签，也不是把 μP 原封不动搬过来。它的关键区别有两点：一是承认并利用 nGPT 中不同于标准 Transformer 的对齐统计；二是把 width、depth、token horizon 的 transfer 规则联合校准，而不是只证明单一维度上的宽度迁移。bf5:T859,The central move is to reject a blind application of μP and instead measure the alignment structure that actually appears in nGPT training. The paper proceeds in three stages.

First, it diagnoses why vanilla nGPT lacks LR transfer. Standard μP-style derivations rely on specific matrix–vector alignment assumptions. The authors empirically check these assumptions in nGPT and find that the observed regime is neither fully aligned nor fully unaligned. It is closer to the “mid-alignment” regime discussed by Everett et al. This matters because the correct width scaling of updates depends on how forward activations, gradients, and parameter updates co-scale with width.

Second, under this empirically supported mid-alignment assumption, they derive a new width parameterization and LR transfer rule, which they call νGPT. Intuitively, νGPT keeps the optimization benefits of nGPT’s normalization-heavy design, but rescales parameter families and trainable gain terms so that effective update magnitudes remain comparable across widths. Figure 2 is the key technical anchor here: it links measured alignment exponents to the proposed scaling prescription.

Third, they extend transfer beyond width. For depth, they adopt a residual-depth scaling rule aligned with recent work arguing that realistic deep Transformer blocks need a depth parameterization that preserves stability and transfer, especially when blocks contain internal matrix multiplications. The paper sides with the α_depth = 1 branch for practical transfer and stability. For token horizon, they empirically find that the optimal learning rate scales as tokens^{-1/3}, consistent with prior observations in unnormalized Transformers. This suggests that even in normalized models, the dominant LR adjustment with longer training budgets follows a similar compute-aware law.

Relative to prior work, νGPT is not just “μP for nGPT.” Its novelty is twofold: it explicitly adapts to the alignment statistics induced by normalized Transformers, and it jointly calibrates transfer across width, depth, and token horizon rather than validating only one axis.bf6:T6a9,The main empirical claim is clear: νGPT improves learning-rate transfer across width, depth, and token horizon without sacrificing the performance of a well-tuned nGPT baseline. 第一部分是 systematic breadth-first exploration。与 Explorer 这类从 homepage 提任务再向外扩展的方法不同，AutoSurfer 直接把网站探索建模成一个带队列的 BFS 过程。队列里维护已发现页面及到达这些页面的 action trace，因此每个新页面都带着“它是怎么被发现的”这一因果路径。这样做有两个好处：一是覆盖更全，能逐层深入网站结构，而不是停留在首页可见功能；二是后续任务合成时可以直接利用到达路径，而不是只看孤立页面截图或 DOM 片段。作者还强调 knowledge propagation：探索过程中从先前页面抽取的网站知识会传递给后续页面，用来理解导航结构、避免重复探索、识别哪些元素属于同一功能簇。

第二部分是对静态与动态元素做差异化处理。静态功能，如菜单、导航栏、dropdown、设置项，适合系统遍历，因为它们定义了网站的功能骨架；动态内容，如商品列表、推荐流、搜索结果、用户生成内容，如果也做穷举，成本会迅速爆炸且收益有限。因此 AutoSurfer 对动态区域采用代表性采样，而不是完全展开。这是一个很关键的设计取舍：作者不是追求状态空间穷举，而是追求“功能覆盖最大化 / 冗余最小化”。这比 random walk 更稳，因为 random walk 容易在动态内容里浪费大量步数，却漏掉真正重要的结构性入口。

第三部分是 task synthesis with exploration trajectory。现有方法常从最终页面或局部交互反推任务，容易产生 hallucinated、模糊或不符合用户意图的任务描述。AutoSurfer 利用 BFS 过程中保留下来的完整探索轨迹，把中间状态、页面语义和最终发现的能力一起输入任务合成器。这样生成的任务不只是“这个页面能做什么”，而是“用户如何通过一串合理步骤完成什么目标”。这一步把任务 grounding 从静态页面内容提升到了过程级别。

第四部分是 trajectory generation 和 wLLM 建模。作者不仅生成任务，还基于更扎实的任务定义去生成执行轨迹，并用这些数据训练 website-specific LLM。这里的隐含假设是：对于复杂网站，通用 MLLM 的能力瓶颈部分来自对站点局部语义、导航习惯和功能组合的不熟悉；如果用系统探索得到的高质量站点数据做针对性训练，小模型也能获得明显收益。与 AgentTrek、OS-Genesis、SynthAgent 相比，AutoSurfer 的区别不在单个 prompting 技巧，而在于它把探索、任务发现、任务表述和训练数据构造连成了一个一致流程。bf9:T5c3,For pretraining and mid-training research, this paper matters more than a typical agent data-engineering paper. The reason is not a new model architecture, but a serious treatment of coverage in interactive data generation. In text pretraining, people already think in terms of data mixture, deduplication, and quality filtering. Web-agent data adds another axis: functional-space coverage. If the exploration stage misses deep menus, form branches, dynamic widgets, or cross-page dependencies, then later task synthesis is operating on an incomplete state space no matter how polished the prompting is. AutoSurfer’s main contribution is to elevate exploration from random walks or homepage-centered heuristics into an explicit, knowledge-carrying, website-structured process.

A second reason the paper is important is that it does not stop at generating demonstrations. It uses the generated data to train a website-specific LLM. That makes it relevant to the interface between data generation and targeted pretraining or continual training. The broader lesson is that in interactive environments, data quality is not just about whether a trajectory succeeds. It also depends on whether the task is properly grounded, whether exploration is systematic, and whether the collected transitions cover the right capability boundaries. The contribution is best viewed as data infrastructure for web agents, but one that directly touches how the training distribution is formed.bfa:Tb94,The method has three main components: systematic exploration, trajectory-grounded task synthesis, and more reliable trajectory generation for downstream modeling.

The first component is systematic breadth-first exploration. Unlike homepage-based methods such as Explorer, AutoSurfer models website exploration as a queue-based BFS process. The queue stores discovered pages together with the action traces used to reach them, so each page is paired with its causal access path. This has two benefits. It improves coverage by progressively expanding into deeper site structure rather than staying near the homepage, and it preserves process information that can later be used for task synthesis instead of relying on isolated screenshots or DOM fragments. The paper also emphasizes knowledge propagation: information extracted from earlier pages is passed forward to help interpret later pages, recognize navigation structure, avoid redundant exploration, and group related functionality.

The second component is differentiated handling of static and dynamic elements. Static functionality—menus, navigation bars, dropdowns, settings—is traversed systematically because it defines the structural backbone of the site. Dynamic content—product lists, recommendation feeds, search results, user-generated content—is sampled selectively rather than exhaustively. This is a key design choice. The goal is not full state-space enumeration, but high functional coverage with low redundancy. That is a better fit than random walks, which can waste many steps in dynamic regions while still missing important structural entry points.

The third component is task synthesis with exploration trajectories. Prior methods often infer tasks from a final page or a local interaction snippet, which can lead to hallucinated, ambiguous, or weakly user-aligned tasks. AutoSurfer uses the full exploration trajectory produced by BFS, including intermediate states, page semantics, and the final discovered capability, to synthesize tasks. This moves task grounding from static page content to process-level evidence. The resulting task is not merely “what this page can do,” but “what a user can accomplish through a plausible sequence of actions.”

Finally, the paper connects data generation to modeling by using the resulting tasks and trajectories to train a website-specific LLM. The underlying hypothesis is that part of the failure of general-purpose multimodal LLMs on complex websites comes from weak familiarity with site-local semantics, navigation conventions, and capability composition. If systematic exploration can produce high-quality site-specific data, then a smaller model may gain a lot from targeted training. Compared with AgentTrek, OS-Genesis, and SynthAgent, the novelty is less about a single prompting trick and more about turning exploration, task discovery, task formulation, and training-data construction into one consistent pipeline.bfb:Ta1f,The most important part of the evaluation is not a single benchmark score, but whether the paper demonstrates that better exploration actually becomes better training data and then better models. A full read will likely take 60–90 minutes.bfd:T446,The paper focuses on UDDMs, where the forward process corrupts discrete tokens toward a uniform distribution and the reverse model learns conditional token distributions. The key conceptual move is to connect conditional likelihood maximization to associative memory. Classical Hopfield-style memories use explicit energy functions to guarantee stable attractors, but generic feed-forward networks and Transformers do not naturally satisfy the symmetry constraints required by such energy formulations. The authors instead use a pseudo-likelihood or conditional-likelihood perspective: if a model learns to reconstruct tokens from corrupted contexts, the induced reverse dynamics can form basins of attraction around data points. In a simplified setting, the analysis shows that maximizing conditional likelihood implicitly enforces a Hebbian-like update on data points and increases classification margins. Empirically, token recovery rate probes whether a corrupted sequence returns to a given sample, while conditional entropy measures how stable and confident the local token prediction is.bfe:T476,The experiments examine how the retrieval behavior changes as the training set size grows. In the memorization regime, the model reliably recovers training examples but treats unseen test sequences as unstable, often altering their tokens during reverse denoising. As more data are added, the basins around individual training examples become less dominant, and unseen in-distribution examples begin to acquire partial basins. In the generalized regime, the model tends to preserve uncorrupted test tokens and can recover tokens from partially corrupted test sequences. Token-level conditional entropy separates these behaviors: successfully recovered tokens have near-zero entropy, while unstable or incorrectly recovered tokens have higher entropy. Sequence-level conditional entropy is used as a practical transition detector; once the generalized regime is reached, the entropy distributions of training and synthetic sequences align. The provided text does not include concrete parameter counts, dataset sizes, or full numeric tables, so the safest reading is as a mechanism and diagnostic study rather than a scale-calibrated benchmark.bff:T812,The method combines a theoretical analysis of entropy dynamics with a simple rejection-sampling controller. The theory starts from a simplified policy-gradient objective without clipping or importance weighting and studies how predictive entropy changes after an update. The key result is that entropy change is negatively related to advantage, and the effect is amplified when the model is already highly confident. Intuitively, positive-advantage samples reinforce selected tokens, sharpen the distribution, and reduce entropy; negative-advantage samples do the opposite and tend to flatten the distribution. In high-confidence regions, this sharpening or flattening effect becomes stronger, which explains why entropy collapse can become self-reinforcing once the policy has already narrowed.

Entrocraft uses this result operationally. Instead of adding entropy regularization to the loss, it performs rejection sampling on rollout samples before the policy update. If the observed entropy is below the target schedule, it preferentially keeps samples whose advantages push entropy upward and filters out samples that would reduce entropy further. If entropy is above target, it does the reverse. In effect, it biases the advantage distribution so that the resulting gradient steers the policy toward the desired entropy level. Because the intervention happens directly at the sample-distribution level, the controller reacts quickly, often within a few update steps, rather than relying on a weakly coupled regularization term. The paper emphasizes two practical properties: it is drop-in for existing RL pipelines, and it is advantage-estimator-agnostic.

A notable aspect is that the paper is about crafting an entropy curve, not merely preserving entropy. It treats entropy scheduling similarly to learning-rate scheduling and compares different schedule families. The main empirical conclusion is that linear entropy annealing works best: keep exploration sufficiently high early on, then gradually tighten the policy later for stability and generalization.c00:T664,The experimental story is centered on long-horizon RL rather than short-run reward gains. The paper reports that Entrocraft extends the useful training horizon by up to 4× before performance plateaus, which directly supports the anti-saturation claim. It also reports a strong generalization result: a 4B model with Entrocraft surpasses an 8B baseline. On diversity-sensitive evaluation, pass@K improves by about 50% over the baseline, consistent with the claim that better entropy control improves exploration coverage rather than merely sharpening one preferred trajectory.

From the paper structure and the introduction, the key experiments likely include four layers. Since the reasoning trace z is latent, Pθ marginalizes over possible trajectories. The paper defines a Tsallis-loss continuum ℓq = -logq(Pθ) = (1 - Pθ^(1-q)) / (1-q). At q=0, ℓ0 = 1 - Pθ, which corresponds to expected-accuracy maximization and RLVR under exact-match rewards. At q=1, ℓ1 = -log Pθ, which is the log marginal likelihood over latent trajectories. The central identity is that all q values share the same per-example gradient direction and differ only by a scalar: ∇θℓq = Pθ^(-q) ∇θℓ0 = Pθ^(1-q) ∇θℓ1. Higher q amplifies low-Pθ examples more strongly, so the model commits faster to unfamiliar supervision. Lower q keeps the loss bounded and reduces sensitivity to corrupted labels. This reweighting cannot be reproduced by a single global learning rate, because a learning rate scales every example equally while q changes the relative weighting across examples. Since exact Pθ is intractable, the paper derives Monte Carlo estimators through two factorizations. The RL factorization uses all M sampled rationales with Rao-Blackwellized rewards pθ(y* | x*, z), improving statistical use of samples but potentially mixing in trajectories that do not semantically support the answer. The FT factorization approximately samples from the posterior over rationales compatible with the correct answer and then fine-tunes on them, giving more coherent gradients at the cost of sampling efficiency and coverage. The two estimators share the same bias structure but suit different regimes.c04:T408,The strongest quantitative claims in the provided text concern training dynamics. At the exploitation pole q=0, cold-start escape requires Ω(1 / p0) time, so progress becomes slow when the initial success probability is tiny. At the density-estimation pole q=1, escape takes Θ(log(1 / p0)) time, giving much stronger signal on low-probability supervised examples. For noisy supervision, q=0 benefits from a bounded loss and escort tempering, which reduce the impact of corrupted labels; q=1 fits the empirical training distribution more directly and can memorize errors. Intermediate q values trade off cold-start speed against noise resistance. The first main result is a negative one. With standard positional encodings and a finite alphabet, any input and CoT trace expressible in C-RASP is also definable in TC0. This strengthens prior observations that C-RASP CoTs are not Turing complete, because it ties the limitation directly to learnable length generalization rather than mere representability.

The constructive result identifies two barriers in simulating Turing machines with length generalization: arbitrary copying and position-based retrieval. A Turing machine simulation needs to address tape cells and recover the latest content written to a cell. In a standard trace, this becomes a non-unique retrieval problem over an increasingly long history. The proposed fix uses two ingredients. First, signpost tokens provide unique addresses for cells or structural positions, with the symbol inventory growing with instance size. Second, value-change encoding records transitions between old and new values only when a value changes. This replaces “retrieve the most recent write” with a count-comparison computation over changes, which is more compatible with C*-RASP-style length-generalizable computation. The key difference from ordinary scratchpads is that the trace format is engineered to match the operations Transformers can learn to extrapolate.c07:T570,The model is trained as a continuous diffusion SLM over log-mel filterbanks rather than over discrete codec or SSL tokens. 论文没有停在理论最优策略，因为 exact conditional expectation 在每一步、每个候选 token 上都算一遍，代价太高。实际实现分三层近似。第一层是 stagewise Soft-BoN approximation，可以理解为在每个 reveal stage 上用 soft best-of-N 的方式近似 reward-tilted 选择，而不是直接求全局最优控制。作者给出 terminal KL 上 O(1/N) 的收敛结论，说明采样数增加时会逼近精确 DPRM。第二层是 online bucketized controller：把候选 token 或候选动作按某种统计量分桶，在线估计 bucket-level reward，逐步替代纯 confidence score。这样做的原因是单 token 粒度的 reward estimate 方差太大、更新太慢，而 bucket 化能在样本效率和分辨率之间做折中。第三层是 warmup-to-guidance 的调度：一开始仍以 confidence-driven ordering 为主，因为早期 reward estimate 不可靠；随着在线估计稳定，再逐步切到 reward-aware ordering。这个设计很像从 exploitation 过渡到 informed exploration，但它不是通用 RL 控制器，而是专门嵌在 DLM reveal 过程里的轻量策略层。

和已有方法相比，差异点很清楚。随机 masking 不利用状态信息；confidence ordering 只看局部 posterior / certainty；teacher-forced progressive masking 虽然在 train-test alignment 上更进一步，但实际 policy 仍偏 confidence heuristic。DPRM 的新意在于：它把 ordering policy 显式写成“proposal × future reward tilt”，并给出可计算近似，而不是继续在 confidence 上做启发式修补。c0a:T7ec,实验覆盖 7 个场景，作者刻意保持 host model、训练目标和数据流程尽量不变，只替换 ordering controller，这使结果更容易归因到 policy 本身。自然语言方向，DPRM-PUMA 在 GSM8K validation mean 上从 29.34 提到 34.27，提升 16.8%；DMPO-DPRM 在 MATH Hard 上从 44.3 到 47.9，提升 8.1%，在 Countdown Hard 上从 29.6 到 33.4，提升 12.8%；DPRM-Prism 在 GSM8K voted accuracy 上从 82.41 到 83.85，增加 1.44 个点。这里可以看出一个特点：在 reasoning / test-time scaling 场景里，ordering policy 的收益不是只体现在 token-level reconstruction，而是会传导到最终答案正确率。
