从消融角度，最值得注意的是 warmup、bucketization、reward estimate reliability 这几项。论文的论证链条是：纯 reward guidance 早期不稳，纯 confidence 后期近视，因此需要一个从 confidence 到 reward-aware 的渐进切换。理论部分用 empirical-Bernstein rate 解释在线 bucketized score 对 exact DPRM score 的跟踪误差来源，包括 bucket coarsening bias、warmup bias 和 nonstationarity。也就是说，作者并不把近似误差藏起来，而是明确指出性能取决于 reward estimate 的方差控制和状态分布漂移。c0b:T72b,The method formulates token ordering as a sequential control problem over partially revealed states, with a terminal reward defined on the completed generation. The exact controller is derived via a Doob h-transform: starting from the host model's proposal distribution over reveal actions, DPRM reweights that proposal by an h-function tied to expected future reward. Intuitively, the policy no longer asks only which token is currently most confident, but which reveal action is most promising for the final outcome.

Because the exact conditional expectation is too expensive to compute for every candidate at every step, the paper introduces a practical approximation stack. First, it uses a stagewise Soft-BoN approximation, effectively a soft best-of-N selection at each reveal stage. The authors prove O(1/N) convergence in terminal KL to the exact DPRM target, giving a clean approximation guarantee as the sample budget grows. Second, they introduce an online bucketized controller. Candidate actions are grouped into buckets, and reward estimates are accumulated at the bucket level rather than per action. This reduces variance and improves sample efficiency, at the cost of some coarsening bias. Third, the controller uses a warmup schedule: it begins with confidence-driven ordering when reward estimates are unreliable, then gradually shifts toward reward-aware guidance as online estimates stabilize.

This differs from prior approaches in a precise way. Random masking ignores state-dependent control. Confidence-based policies rely on local certainty. Teacher-forced progressive masking improves train-test alignment but still uses confidence-like heuristics in practice. DPRM instead makes the policy explicitly equal to proposal times future-reward tilt, then builds a computable approximation around that principle.c0c:T6d7,The evaluation spans seven settings, and the experimental design is careful: the host model, objective, and data pipeline are kept as fixed as possible, while only the ordering controller is changed. The first is architectural progression. The authors first define Tuna-R: remove the VAE, keep a pretrained representation encoder, encode images into visual tokens, and feed them into an LLM decoder. Tuna-R is not the final answer; it is a controlled intermediate model that isolates the role of the encoder.

The second layer is Tuna-2 itself. Here the representation encoder is removed as well. Images or videos are split into patches and embedded with simple patch embedding layers, then processed together with text tokens by a single transformer decoder. Both understanding and generation are handled within the same token stream and the same backbone, making the model genuinely end-to-end from raw pixels.

What makes this trainable is the masking-based visual feature learning scheme. Direct pixel-space unified modeling is harder than latent-space modeling, and the model can otherwise overfit to low-level local statistics instead of learning robust visual semantics. The masking mechanism introduces a feature-learning bias that encourages the model to recover or model semantically meaningful visual structure under partial observation. In effect, it injects a masked-visual-modeling style signal into unified pixel-space pretraining, improving stability and representation quality.

Conceptually, Tuna-2 differs from the dominant “strong vision encoder plus LLM” recipe. It is closer to a monolithic decoder-only multimodal model where perception is not outsourced to a separately pretrained encoder. Compared with VAE-latent generation, it avoids the information bottleneck and the mismatch between understanding and generation objectives. Compared with decoupled encoder designs, it removes module boundaries and objective misalignment. Compared with shared-encoder unified models, it goes one step further by discarding external visual priors in exchange for stronger end-to-end optimization.c0f:T70a,The most useful part of the empirical section is not a single benchmark win, but the controlled comparison between Tuna-R and Tuna-2. That pattern matters more than any one leaderboard number. It suggests that encoder-free models are harder initially, but not fundamentally weaker, and may have a better asymptotic regime for perception.

Those questions determine whether the approach can scale to larger models or broader video settings.c11:T894,技术上分两层。第一层是 bug 定位与验证。作者定位到 DeepSpeed ZeRO Stage 1/2 配合 CPU-offloaded Adam 时，梯度累积逻辑有一个分支错误：copy_gradients_to_cpu() 只在 micro_step_id == 0 的路径上执行，导致只有第一个 micro-batch 的梯度被拷到 CPU 侧优化器，后续 micro-batch 虽然在 GPU 上累积了，但不会同步到 CPU，最终 optimizer step 实际只看到了首个 micro-batch。这个 bug 来自 2024 年 9 月的 DeepSpeed PR #6550。修复方式很直接，把梯度拷贝调用移到分支外，让每个 micro-batch 累积后都同步。作者没有停留在代码阅读，而是用两个独立参照系做了交叉验证：OpenRLHF 中不 offload 的 GPU-resident DeepSpeed optimizer，以及 verl 里的 PyTorch FSDP optimizer。修复后，平均 loss 和 gradient norm 与这两个参照实现对齐。

第二层是 loss aggregation bug。标准 SFT 的 cross-entropy 应该按所有有效 response token 的总损失除以总 token 数，也就是全局 per-token mean；但 OpenRLHF、Llama-Factory、早期 verl 会先在每个 mini-batch 内求 mean，再在梯度累积或多卡之间平均这些 mean。由于不同 mini-batch 的有效 token 数不同，这相当于给每个 mini-batch 相同权重，而不是给每个 token 相同权重，长短样本的贡献被扭曲。修复方法是先聚合 token-level loss sum 和 token count，再统一相除。

在这两个 bug 修复后，作者重新实现并比较标准 SFT→RL 与多种 mixed-policy 方法。论文的论证逻辑很清楚：不是抽象地说 sequential 更好，而是说明为什么它在 reasoning 上常更有效。SFT 提供的是 dense、低方差的学习信号，先把格式、领域知识和基本解题轨迹学稳，RL 再在已有成功轨迹附近做策略锐化；而 mixed-policy 在训练早期同时面对 off-policy demonstration 和 on-policy sparse reward，优化目标更杂，且如果初始策略太弱，RL 部分几乎不给有效梯度，算力利用率并不高。作者还给出 truncated RL 结果，说明即便只做很少轮数的 RL，只要 SFT 起点足够强，也能超过很多复杂混合方法。c12:T403,This is a high-importance paper because it recalibrates a widely cited empirical conclusion in reasoning post-training. A substantial part of the apparent advantage of mixed-policy methods seems to come from broken SFT baselines rather than a genuinely better training paradigm. That matters directly for the pretrain–posttrain interface: if SFT is artificially weakened, then conclusions about how much RL needs off-policy demonstrations, how to mix dense supervision with sparse rewards, and where RL should start from all become unreliable. The paper reinforces a simple but consequential point: if SFT is implemented correctly and pushed to a strong enough starting policy, RL from verifiable rewards can be both more compute-efficient and more stable than trying to learn demonstrations and on-policy exploration simultaneously. The contribution is corrective rather than algorithmic, but the blast radius is large because the affected stack includes DeepSpeed, OpenRLHF, TRL, Llama-Factory, and earlier verl code paths.c13:T9c3,The technical contribution has two layers. First is bug identification and validation. The authors trace a bug in DeepSpeed ZeRO Stage 1/2 with CPU-offloaded Adam: during gradient accumulation, copy_gradients_to_cpu() is executed only in the branch where micro_step_id == 0. As a result, only the first micro-batch’s gradients are copied to the CPU-side optimizer. Later micro-batches accumulate on GPU but are never transferred, so the optimizer step effectively uses only the first micro-batch instead of the accumulated gradient. The bug was introduced in DeepSpeed PR #6550 in September 2024. The fix is simple—move the gradient copy outside the conditional so it runs after every micro-batch accumulation—but the paper goes beyond code inspection and validates the patch against two independent references: a GPU-resident DeepSpeed optimizer in OpenRLHF and a PyTorch FSDP optimizer in verl. After the fix, loss trajectories and gradient norms align across implementations.

The second layer is the loss aggregation bug. In standard SFT, cross-entropy should be computed as the total loss over all valid response tokens divided by the total number of valid tokens, i.e. a global per-token mean. OpenRLHF, Llama-Factory, and earlier verl versions instead compute local means within each mini-batch and then average those means across gradient accumulation steps or distributed ranks. Because mini-batches contain different numbers of active response tokens, this gives equal weight to each mini-batch rather than each token, distorting the contribution of short and long samples. The correct fix is to aggregate token-level loss sums and token counts first, then divide once globally.

With both bugs corrected, the authors re-run the standard SFT→RL pipeline and compare it against published mixed-policy methods. The conceptual argument is straightforward and well supported: SFT provides dense, low-variance supervision that teaches formatting, domain knowledge, and basic reasoning traces; RL then sharpens the policy around trajectories that already have nontrivial success probability. Mixed-policy training, by contrast, mixes off-policy demonstrations with sparse on-policy rewards from the beginning, which makes optimization noisier and often less compute-efficient when the initial policy is weak. The paper also includes truncated-RL results showing that even a small amount of RL can outperform more elaborate mixed-policy methods if the SFT starting point is strong enough.c14:T655,The key experimental story is the reordering of baselines before and after bug fixes, followed by direct comparisons against mixed-policy methods. The two bugs together can reduce SFT performance by as much as 5.7 points on Qwen2.5-Math-7B, with the optimizer bug accounting for most of the drop and the loss aggregation bug adding a smaller but consistent penalty. After fixing them, the standard SFT-then-RL pipeline surpasses the best published mixed-policy result on in-distribution math tasks by +3.8 points for Qwen2.5-Math-7B and by +22.2 points for Llama-3.1-8B, while maintaining generalization on out-of-distribution benchmarks. Another important result is the compute comparison: even a truncated variant with only 50 RL iterations, instead of 500, still beats all mixed-policy methods on the math benchmarks, indicating that the extra complexity of mixed-policy optimization is not buying better sample efficiency or FLOP efficiency.

The paper also includes several validation layers that make the case more convincing. These include alignment of the patched DeepSpeed offload implementation with GPU-resident and FSDP optimizers in both loss curves and gradient norms; ablations that isolate the effect of fixing each bug separately versus both together; replication across model families including Qwen2.5-Math-7B and Llama-3.1-8B; and separate reporting on in-distribution and out-of-distribution benchmarks. Methodologically, the strongest aspect is that the paper does not rely only on final benchmark numbers; it also checks optimizer consistency, gradient statistics, compute cost, and generalization.c15:T459,This one is worth a close read. If time is limited, prioritize the introduction, the bug sections, the main result tables, and the appendix patch details.c16:T8b8,方法叫 Temporally Coherent Reward Modeling，核心是在标准 Bradley-Terry pairwise loss 之上，加两个正则项，让中间位置的输出逼近最终 reward 的条件期望。论文的关键洞见是：在 decoder-only transformer 的因果掩码下，第 k 个位置的隐藏状态天然只依赖 prompt 和前 k 个 response token，因此它正好具备表示 E[R | x, y0..k] 的结构条件。问题不在模型能不能表示，而在训练目标没有要求它这么做。

作者在实践上用 final model score r(x, y) 作为未观测 ground-truth reward 的 proxy，然后要求中间输出 r(x, y0..k) 与这个 final reward 的条件期望一致。两个正则项分别对应 Monte Carlo 和 TD 风格的 value learning。一个是 MC 型正则，让中间位置直接回归最终分数，从而鼓励每个 prefix 的输出成为“看到当前前缀后，对最终结果的平均预测”；另一个是 TD 型正则，约束相邻位置之间的时序一致性，使当前 token 的预测与下一步预测之间满足类似 Bellman 的递推关系。论文给出相应引理，说明这些正则项的最小化解就是条件期望，因此不是拍脑袋的平滑项，而是有明确统计目标。

这套设计有几个值得注意的点。第一，它不需要 process labels。传统 PRM 往往依赖 step-level 标注，成本高且定义不稳定；TCRM 只用常规 preference pair，就把 RM 训练成了一个近似 process-aware 的模型。第二，它不改推理接口。训练后仍然可以像普通 RM 一样只读 final token 分数，但如果需要，也可以读取中间轨迹做解释、credit assignment 或 value estimation。第三，它自然导出 token-level incremental contribution：相邻位置分数差 d(yk | x, y0..k-1) 可以解释为该 token 对最终质量预测的边际影响。这一点对分析 reward hacking、模板化套话、冗余推理步骤等问题很有用。

和已有 RM 训练相比，区别不在于换了偏好损失，而在于把“final-only supervision”改成“full-trajectory consistency under the same supervision”。它仍然是 pairwise preference learning，但把每个中间位置都纳入了一个 value-style 约束框架。c17:T7d9,Temporally Coherent Reward Modeling (TCRM) augments the standard Bradley-Terry pairwise loss with two regularizers that force intermediate outputs to approximate the conditional expectation of the final reward. The key observation is architectural: in a decoder-only transformer with causal masking, the hidden state at position k depends only on the prompt and the first k response tokens. That is exactly the conditioning structure needed to represent E[R | x, y0..k]. So the limitation is not representational capacity; it is the training objective.

Since the true scalar reward R is unobserved in pairwise preference training, the paper uses the model's final score r(x, y) as a proxy target under an unbiasedness assumption. It then adds two value-learning-style regularizers. One is Monte Carlo-like: intermediate predictions are encouraged to match the final score, making each prefix output a predictor of the eventual outcome. The other is TD-like: adjacent token positions are constrained to be temporally consistent, in a way analogous to Bellman-style bootstrapping. The paper proves via lemmas that the minimizers of these regularizers are conditional expectations, so the objective is statistically grounded rather than heuristically smoothed.

Several aspects are notable. TCRM requires no process labels, unlike standard process reward models that depend on expensive step-level supervision. It also leaves inference unchanged: one can still use only the final token score if desired, but now the full token trajectory is meaningful and can be used for analysis, credit assignment, or value estimation. Finally, the model naturally yields token-level incremental contributions through score differences between adjacent positions, which can help diagnose reward hacking, verbosity bias, or unhelpful reasoning steps.

Relative to prior RM training, the novelty is not a new preference loss but a shift from final-only supervision to full-trajectory consistency under the same preference data.c18:T71f,The empirical story is focused and convincing. The clearest result is on intermediate-token pairwise accuracy. Standard reward models are near chance in the middle of a sequence, around 50%, because those outputs are never trained to mean anything. TCRM raises middle-token pairwise accuracy to as high as 88.9% while preserving final-token accuracy. That is strong evidence that the regularizers are not merely smoothing trajectories; they are making intermediate outputs genuinely predictive of final preference.

A second important result is process-level evaluation. TCRM is used as a process reward model without any step-level labels and achieves 44.9% average F1 on ProcessBench. The significance here is not just the absolute number, but the fact that useful process supervision can be extracted from ordinary preference data if the objective is designed correctly.

The third major result is in PPO. Because the TCRM regularizers align with Monte Carlo and TD value learning, the same model can serve as both reward model and value model. The paper reports a 27% reduction in peak GPU memory and a 19% reduction in training step time, with no degradation in final LLM quality. For practical RLHF systems, that is a meaningful systems-level gain.

The paper also discusses policy shift. Intermediate conditional expectations depend on the continuation distribution: offline training uses the dataset distribution, while online RL changes the policy over time. Empirically, TCRM's intermediate-token accuracy is reported to be no more sensitive to this shift than final-token accuracy, and even a frozen TCRM can function effectively as a value model in PPO. If this holds broadly, it suggests the method learns a fairly robust prefix-to-outcome mapping rather than merely overfitting static preference trajectories.c19:T578,Begin with the motivation and the section on intermediate reward outputs. The key conceptual move is to reinterpret reward modeling as conditional expectation estimation over prefixes, not just end-of-sequence comparison. Then read the lemmas behind the Monte Carlo and TD regularizers. Those are the theoretical core: they explain why the proposed regularization targets the right object instead of just imposing smoothness.

After that, inspect how the regularizers are combined with the Bradley-Terry loss in practice. Pay attention to whether the method requires extra rollouts, how variable-length responses are handled, and how the proxy final score is used during training. In the experiments, prioritize three parts: middle-token pairwise accuracy, ProcessBench, and the PPO section with unified reward/value modeling. Together they validate interpretability, process-level usefulness, and systems efficiency.

A few follow-up questions are worth keeping in mind. Does using the model's own final score as a target introduce self-distillation bias? How robust is temporal coherence under strong online policy shift? When token-level score differences are used for credit assignment, do they track genuine helpfulness or merely stylistic correlates? And can the same objective be extended to outcome reward models, hybrid ORM/PRM setups, or even auxiliary training for the policy model itself?c1a:T641,The central surrogate is a pre-trained Gaussian Process over the performance function. The GP prior is not learned from scratch. For established benchmarks, its covariance can be derived from historical evaluation records across models, capturing that two inputs are related if models tend to succeed or fail on them together. For new domains or modalities, the method uses off-the-shelf text or image embedding models to represent inputs, then pre-trains encoder parameters and GP hyperparameters so the kernel reflects semantic or visual similarity.

On top of this surrogate, ProEval handles two objectives. For aggregate performance estimation, it frames the metric as an integral, ∫ f(x)p(x)dx, and uses Bayesian quadrature. Unlike Monte Carlo averaging, BQ treats the integral as a posterior random variable and provides an analytic estimate of its uncertainty. The acquisition rule then selects inputs that most reduce posterior variance of the aggregate metric. For failure discovery, the method defines failures as a superlevel set, {x | f(x) ≥ λ}, and selects points by balancing predicted failure probability with epistemic uncertainty. This prevents the search from repeatedly sampling only known failure types.

The paper also extends evaluation beyond a static dataset. It uses an LLM generator conditioned on discovered hard examples as in-context anchors. To reduce collapse into a single failure mode, it introduces bi-level sampling: first sample high-level semantic topics, then generate concrete test cases under those topics. This makes active failure discovery more diverse.c1b:Ta9b,The method is a target-aware, uncertainty-aware sequential selection strategy. The setup assumes observations follow y = f(x; θ*) + ε, where f is a parametric scaling law, x is a configuration, y is the measured outcome, and c(x) is the experiment cost. The key departure from classical optimal design is that the acquisition objective is not built around generic parameter variance reduction. Instead, it asks which candidate run is expected to reduce prediction error in the target region the most.

The approach has three important pieces.

First, it maintains a set of plausible fits under the current observations, rather than relying only on a single local optimum with a local Gaussian approximation. The paper explicitly distinguishes two sources of uncertainty: local uncertainty around a fit, and disagreement among multiple plausible parameter settings that explain current data similarly well but extrapolate differently in the target regime. This is a strong design choice for scaling laws, because the practical failure mode is often not local noise but non-identifiability: several parameterizations fit the cheap region, yet diverge sharply at larger scales.

Second, it defines experiment utility in terms of downstream extrapolation. A candidate run is valuable if observing it is expected to resolve ambiguity that matters for target-region predictions. From the paper’s description, the acquisition combines how much plausible fits disagree at the candidate point and how informative that point would be for collapsing disagreement over the target region, while also accounting for experiment cost. In effect, the method prefers runs that are cheap but highly discriminative among competing extrapolation hypotheses, instead of simply chasing the most uncertain or most expensive points.

Third, the design is sequential. After each selected run is executed, the model refits, updates the plausible parameter set, and chooses the next point accordingly. This matters because early rounds can eliminate grossly wrong extrapolation shapes, allowing later budget to focus on the most decision-relevant regions. For low-dimensional but highly nonlinear scaling-law fitting, that is more robust than one-shot static design.

Relative to prior approaches, the differences are clear: the objective is target-region extrapolation rather than in-sample fit; the setting uses heterogeneous experiment costs rather than equal-cost assumptions; and uncertainty is represented as ambiguity across multiple plausible fits, not only local curvature around one optimum. The paper evaluates this framework against random selection, grid-like heuristics, and classical design baselines on a unified benchmark.c1c:T970,The experimental section is designed to test robustness across scaling-law scenarios rather than to showcase a single benchmark win. The paper builds a diverse benchmark spanning multiple scaling settings, different law families, and task-specific cost structures. One explicitly mentioned example is Step Law, covering learning-rate and batch-size scaling. On that task, the method reaches the low-loss regime with only 1% of the original fitting budget, approaching the extrapolation ground-truth optimum. That is a strong signal that large pilot sweeps can often be replaced by much more selective probing.

A key strength of the evaluation is the metric choice. The paper does not optimize or report only fit quality on observed points; it measures extrapolation accuracy on a held-out target region. That is the right criterion for this problem, because many baselines can fit the observed low-cost region reasonably well while still making poor predictions where the final training decision lives. The use of heterogeneous costs also makes the comparison more realistic: the question is not how many runs are selected, but how much budget is spent to achieve a given target-region error.

Several empirical patterns stand out. First, the gains are largest in the low-budget regime. When budget is abundant, many methods eventually recover a decent fit; the practical value lies in how quickly a method reduces target-region error when only a small fraction of the original pilot budget is available. Second, modeling ambiguity across multiple plausible fits appears important. A purely local approximation can commit too early to a misleading extrapolation shape, while the proposed method actively seeks points that separate competing hypotheses. Third, cost-awareness matters. Without normalizing utility by cost, the strategy can over-invest in a few expensive runs and lose overall efficiency.

First, Rewrite-Driven Joint SFT trains the model to generate structured rewrites rather than CoT plus an answer. Images, videos, and visual documents are recaptioned; text queries are elaborated. The rewrite keeps retrieval-relevant entities, attributes, relations, and context, but avoids committing to a single summary. This is a better fit for general retrieval than CoT, because retrieval needs semantic coverage and discrimination more than explicit reasoning trajectories. Second, Cross-Mode Alignment aligns discriminative and generative embedding spaces through mutual contrastive learning: embeddings of the same query across the two modes are pulled together, while negatives are separated. This pushes rewriting toward better retrieval separation, not just longer or more fluent descriptions.c1f:T4e2,The work has three technical components. First, it introduces two metrics. CIR is computed by progressively truncating a generated reasoning trace and forcing the model to answer early, then measuring how the answer distribution changes as more of the trace is removed. If the distribution barely changes, the reasoning was not causally important for the answer. SR is measured with a verifier model: compare the verifier’s predicted answer when given only the reasoning trace versus when given reasoning plus the original question and prompt. If the answer changes materially once the question is added back, the reasoning is not self-sufficient. Second, the authors track these metrics throughout RLVR training on Qwen2.5 instruction-tuned models at 1.5B, 3B, and 7B scales, with additional experiments on Llama3.2-3B, across 40 ReasoningGym tasks. The key distinction from much prior work is that reasoning is treated as an object with its own causal and informational properties, not merely as a stylistic output format.c20:T541,Several findings stand out. Second, CIR and SR rise more consistently only on tasks where RLVR drives very large accuracy gains, above 50 percentage points. A focused read of the introduction, metric section, Sections 5–7, and the main figures should be enough for the main argument; a full careful read is about 45–60 minutes.c22:T49c,A red-blue adversarial evaluation framework is adopted: the red team has full knowledge of the blue team's training setup, and constructs sandbagging model organisms optimized to resist common training interventions. The red team's model is constrained to sandbag on at most 90% of tasks, so its performance when sandbagging matches the weakest trusted supervisor model (around 10% accuracy) to avoid obvious sandbagging being detected. The blue team can only use signals from the weak trusted model T and 10 ground truth samples from the training set for training. The core pipeline is: first run SFT on demonstration data generated by T plus the small set of ground truth data to break the conditional trigger mechanism of sandbagging, then run RL fine-tuning with T as the reward model to consolidate the output of true capabilities. Unlike existing alignment methods that assume supervision signal quality is at least equal to the model's capability, this pipeline is designed specifically for scenarios where supervision signals are weaker than the target model, using a combination of SFT (trigger breaking) and RL (capability consolidation) instead of standalone SFT or RL.c23:T53d,The paper frames confidence using the first-order versus second-order distinction from decision neuroscience. In a first-order account, the same signal determines the chosen response and confidence in that response. The LLM analogue is token log-probability. Under greedy decoding, this signal is tied to the selected answer and therefore gives a weak account of why the model would later judge its own answer as wrong. A second-order account introduces a partly independent evaluative variable. The paper focuses on the post-answer newline token, or PANL. Prior work by Kumaran et al. 2026 found that PANL caches a confidence representation that causally drives verbal confidence and dissociates from generation-time log-probabilities. This work tests whether the same representation supports error detection and self-correction. The experimental paradigm is verify-then-correct: generate an answer, elicit or measure confidence and verification behavior, then allow a correction attempt. The analysis asks whether verbal confidence predicts error detection beyond log-probabilities, whether PANL activations predict error detection beyond verbal confidence, and whether PANL predicts which errors can be corrected. Causal evidence comes from activation patching and joint ablation, including settings where answer information is corrupted.c24:T4d4,The findings are reported across Gemma 3 27B and Qwen 2.5 7B, on TriviaQA and MNLI. Behaviorally, verbal confidence predicts verification outcomes much better than token log-probabilities, which argues against a pure first-order account. Representationally, PANL activations still predict error detection after controlling for verbal confidence, indicating that the internal evaluative signal is not fully exposed in the model’s verbal report. The strongest result is on correctability: PANL predicts which erroneous answers will be successfully revised, while behavioral signals, including log-probability and verbal confidence, fail to do so reliably. - The cluster is partitioned into M independent learners. Each learner runs an inner optimizer (e.g., AdamW) on its own data shard for multiple local steps.
- In DiLoCo, every H steps learners synchronize and an outer optimizer (often SGD with Nesterov momentum) treats inter-learner parameter differences as an “outer gradient” to update a global reference.
- Streaming DiLoCo shards parameters into P fragments to reduce peak bandwidth, but synchronization is still fundamentally blocking.
- Decoupled DiLoCo introduces a central synchronizer and an asynchronous reconciliation protocol: learners can continue local training while sending/receiving fragment-wise deltas with delay, tolerating stragglers, communication hiccups, and local failures without global stalls.
From an optimization lens, the important knobs are the outer optimizer choice, synchronization cadence H, staleness/lag τ, fragmentation P, and learner count M—together determining drift, effective noise, and generalization.c27:Tb53,整套方案由三部分组成：SigLIP-VQ tokenizer、16B MoE dLLM backbone、Diffusion Decoder。

先看 tokenizer。作者没有沿用传统重建导向的 VQ，而是提出 SigLIP-VQ，把连续视觉输入离散成“fully semantic discrete tokens”。这里的关键不是单纯做更好的压缩，而是让 token 更接近语义单元，能被语言式 backbone 直接消费。传统 VQ token 往往偏局部纹理和重建细节，适合生成但不利于理解；如果压缩率再高一些，生成也会受损。SigLIP-VQ 试图在语义保真和离散统一格式之间找到平衡，使视觉 token 既能支持问答推理，又能作为后续图像生成的中间表示。

再看 backbone。LLaDA2.0-Uni 以 LLaDA2.0 的 16B MoE dLLM 为核心，不走 next-token AR，而是对文本和图像 token 统一采用 block-level masked diffusion。这里的 block-wise mask prediction 很重要。它不是逐 token 自回归，也不是完全无结构地全局去噪，而是在块级别进行掩码和恢复，兼顾并行解码效率与上下文建模能力。作者强调 modality-agnostic MoE，说明专家路由不是按模态硬切，而是让文本和视觉 token 在共享 backbone 中竞争专家容量，这对统一表示学习是更激进的设计。

第三部分是 diffusion decoder。由于 backbone 输出的是语义离散视觉 token，而不是可直接还原高保真图像的重建 token，因此需要一个专门 decoder 把这些 token 转成图像。这个 decoder 经过蒸馏后只需 8 步推理，目的是把统一建模和高质量生成拆成两个相对独立的问题：前者由 dLLM 解决，后者由 decoder 解决。相比把所有视觉细节都塞进统一 backbone，这样更符合容量分工，也更容易扩展到高分辨率生成。

The tokenizer is central. Instead of a standard reconstruction-driven VQ tokenizer, the paper introduces SigLIP-VQ to convert continuous visual inputs into fully semantic discrete tokens. The goal is not just compression, but semantic usability. Traditional VQ tokens often preserve local texture and reconstruction detail, which can help generation but are weak for understanding; stronger compression then hurts generation as well. SigLIP-VQ is designed to produce discrete visual units that are useful for reasoning while still serving as an intermediate representation for image synthesis.

The backbone is built on LLaDA2.0, a 16B MoE discrete diffusion language model. Rather than next-token prediction, it uses a shared block-level masked diffusion objective over both text and image tokens. The block-wise design matters. It is not token-by-token autoregression, but it is also not an unstructured fully bidirectional denoising process. It aims to balance parallel decoding efficiency with stronger contextual modeling. The paper also emphasizes modality-agnostic MoE routing, suggesting that experts are shared across text and vision instead of being hard-partitioned by modality. That is a stronger form of unification than simply concatenating modalities into one sequence.

The third component is a diffusion decoder. Because the backbone predicts semantic discrete visual tokens rather than reconstruction-ready image codes, a dedicated decoder is needed to turn those tokens into high-fidelity images. This decoder is distilled to run in only 8 inference steps. Architecturally, this is a clean decomposition: the dLLM handles unified semantic modeling, while the decoder handles visual detail synthesis. Compared with forcing the backbone to carry all low-level image detail, this is a more scalable allocation of capacity.

Training is described as a curated large-scale, multi-stage pipeline. The excerpt here does not include all stage details, but the likely structure includes tokenizer training, unified multimodal dLLM training, decoder distillation, and staged mixing of understanding and generation data. The key point is objective unification: both text and vision are optimized in the backbone with the same masked diffusion objective, instead of using AR for text and diffusion for images and then balancing heterogeneous losses.

On inference, the paper adds two practical optimizations. First, prefix-aware decoding reduces redundant updates and recomputation for conditioned generation in the backbone. Second, few-step distillation compresses the decoder to 8 steps. This matters because inference cost is one of the main objections to unified diffusion systems.c2a:T7e9,The empirical story has three parts: understanding, generation, and unified capability. The authors take five standard self-supervised vision tasks and reformulate them as verifiable visual puzzles that an MLLM can answer in a text interface, then optimize the model with GRPO. The five tasks cover different granularities of visual reasoning. (1) Rotation prediction: the image is rotated by a sampled angle from a discrete set, and the model predicts the angle. This probes global structure and orientation sensitivity. (2) Visual similarity: two crops from the same image form a reference and a positive, while crops from other images serve as negatives; the model selects the most similar candidate. This resembles instance discrimination and requires semantic and appearance-level matching. (3) Region inpainting: a region is masked and the model must infer the missing content or choose the correct completion-related option, forcing contextual completion. (4) Patch ordering: shuffled patches must be reordered, emphasizing spatial layout and part-whole structure. (5) Geometric correspondence: the model reasons about point or region correspondences under transformations, targeting finer spatial reasoning.

These tasks share the properties that matter for RLVR: labels are generated automatically from the corruption or transformation process, and correctness can be checked exactly. The RL algorithm is GRPO rather than PPO. That choice is practical: no critic is needed, and relative comparison among sampled responses is well suited to discrete, verifiable reward settings. The main novelty is not a new RL optimizer, but the alignment between visual SSL task design and reward verifiability. Another important detail is that the tasks are cast into the native MLLM interaction format, so the visual reinforcement signal updates the generative policy directly instead of training a separate vision head.

A useful takeaway from the full method section is that not every SSL task is equally suitable for RL post-training. Good tasks need a clear answer space, stable reward computation, and meaningful transfer to downstream visual capabilities. Tasks that are too low-level, too ambiguous, or too dependent on continuous regression are harder to convert into high-quality RL signals.c2d:T6de,The experimental story is about systematic gains in vision-centric capability rather than a narrow win on one benchmark. If a puzzle is too easy, rewards saturate and the RL signal weakens; if it is too hard, rewards become too sparse and optimization becomes unstable. Candidate set size, masking ratio, rotation granularity, and negative sampling strategy all affect learning dynamics.

1) Metrics and setup: focus on embeddings e(n) for number tokens n in 0..999 (aligned with common tokenizers where these are single tokens). Compute a DFT along the token index and measure power at frequencies 1/T to identify spikes. Separately, train a linear probe (T-way logistic regression) to predict n mod T from e(n), operationalizing “geometric separability.”
2) Theory: prove that Fourier-domain sparsity/spikes are necessary but not sufficient for mod-T linear separability (Theorem 1). Intuitively, a periodic component in the sequence of embeddings does not guarantee that residue classes form linearly separable clusters; two systems can share near-identical spectra yet differ drastically in the geometry relevant to linear decoding.
3) Controlled attribution experiments: train ~300M-parameter models on matched data while perturbing one factor at a time. Data-side perturbations progressively remove (i) text–number co-occurrence, (ii) cross-number interaction signals, and (iii) long-context dependencies. - Universality: T=2/5/10 spikes are observed across many released LMs and non-Transformer sequence models, plus GloVe/FastText; strikingly, the corpus-level frequency distribution of number tokens already exhibits a similar periodic spectrum.
- Two-tier outcome: spectral convergence is near-universal; geometric convergence is not. A key controlled contrast: Transformers and linear RNNs (in large-token training settings) yield high mod-T probe accuracy, while LSTMs trained on the same data can show even stronger spikes yet remain near chance on mod-T probing.
- Data ablations: removing co-occurrence, cross-number interactions, or reducing context length degrades mod-T probe accuracy substantially, while Fourier spikes persist—supporting the claim that spikes are largely data/tokenization-driven, whereas linear decodability requires additional structured signals.
- Architecture/optimizer: architecture is decisive for geometric convergence; optimizer can affect whether separable structure emerges in some settings, but does not eliminate the spectral spikes.
- Tokenizer/task constraint: in addition-from-scratch, multi-token number representations more reliably induce modular/circular features due to forced modulo subproblems; single-token setups allow alternative shortcuts, leading to higher variance and optimizer dependence.
(Note: the provided full-text excerpt does not include all numeric tables; exact probe accuracies and training details should be taken from the corresponding figures/tables in the paper.)c31:T423,LoopLM reuses a stack of L transformer layers for t recurrent steps (shared weights), effectively deepening the computation graph without increasing parameter count. A prediction head is attached at each step, enabling multi-step supervision.

Adaptive compute is implemented via a learned early-exit (or equivalently, a learned weighting over step-wise losses). The key training issue is collapse: without constraints, the model either exits too early (cheap but weak) or always runs the maximum steps (strong but no adaptivity). The proposed fix is an entropy-regularized objective with a uniform prior over exit steps to force unbiased exploration of depths early in training, followed by a focused stage that tunes the compute–quality trade-off and lets the model allocate steps based on input difficulty.

For interpretation, the paper positions recurrence as iterative refinement in latent space, and backs it with controlled studies that aim to disentangle “knowledge storage” from “knowledge manipulation” (composition, multi-hop reasoning).c32:T52e,Scale: pretraining up to 7.7T tokens; open-sourced Ouro models at 1.4B and 2.6B parameters.

Efficiency claim: 1.4B/2.6B LoopLMs reportedly match roughly 4B/8B standard (non-looped) transformers on many benchmarks, implying ~2–3× parameter efficiency under their evaluation protocol.

Ablations: varying loop steps shows generally increasing capability with more steps, but training can be unstable due to exit-policy collapse; entropy regularization plus the two-stage schedule stabilizes depth usage and preserves peak performance while enabling early exit on easier inputs.

Mechanistic results: the paper reports similar “knowledge storage density” between looped and non-looped models (on the order of ~2 bits/parameter), while showing larger gains on tasks requiring fact composition and multi-hop reasoning—supporting the “manipulation over storage” explanation.

Safety/faithfulness: lower harmfulness on HEx-PHI, improving with more recurrent steps (including extrapolated steps). It also argues latent iterative traces align better with final answers than explicit CoT, suggesting less post-hoc rationalization.

Caveat: to validate the strongest headline comparisons (e.g., matching much larger models), one should check the exact benchmark suite, prompting, and aggregation in the main figures/tables.c33:Tae8,技术路线分成三部分：稳定性建模、稳定架构设计、以及面向随机深度训练的算法修正。

先看建模。作者把 middle-looped 架构写成三段：prelude 单元把输入 token 映射成条件向量 e，recurrent unit 在循环步 t 上更新 hidden state h_t，coda 单元把最终状态映射到 logits。关键是把 recurrent update 视为一个关于 residual stream 的非线性时变系统，其中一部分参数控制“保留多少旧状态、注入多少新状态”。在对系统做线性化近似后，这个更新退化成经典 LTI 系统，稳定性可以用状态转移矩阵的谱性质来分析。作者发现，已有 looped 架构中的 injection 参数会学到过大的谱范数，从而导致 residual explosion。这不是经验上“有时会炸”，而是能被动力系统视角解释的结构性风险。

基于这个分析，Parcae 的核心设计是对 A 做连续到离散的稳定参数化，并把连续形式的 A 约束为 negative diagonal matrix。这样离散化后的状态更新天然带有收缩性质，谱范数被控制住，残差不会在循环中指数放大。这个设计很像把 recurrent depth 的自由度从“任意线性耦合”收缩到“逐维稳定衰减/保留”，牺牲了一部分表达灵活性，换来训练稳定性和可预测性。作者没有选择更宽松的全矩阵稳定化，而是用对角负矩阵，原因很实际：它足够稳定、参数少、实现简单，而且在大模型训练里更容易和现有 Transformer block 兼容。

除了结构约束，作者还处理了两个训练层面的尖点来源。第一，对输入条件 e 做归一化，缓解训练后期的 loss spikes。这里可以理解为 recurrent unit 在不同 loop depth 下反复接收同一个条件信号，如果其尺度漂移，容易在深循环时放大不稳定模式。第二，训练目标需要对随机深度的期望损失做优化。已有做法常在 batch 级别采样统一深度，导致梯度方差和深度切换带来的不连续更明显。Parcae 改成 intra-batch per-sequence depth sampling，让同一 batch 内不同样本走不同 loop 次数，从而平滑优化过程，也更接近“对深度分布求期望”的目标。

论文还有一个重要点是把训练时 scaling 和测试时 scaling 统一起来。训练时，他们在 isoFLOP 设定下研究给定总训练 FLOPs 时，应该把预算分给更多数据还是更多 looping；测试时，他们研究增加 loop 次数带来的 loss 改善曲线，并拟合出带 irreducible loss 的指数衰减形式。最终得到一个统一的 looping scaling 视角：训练阶段学到的 recurrent refinement 能在推理阶段继续通过更多循环释放出来，但收益遵循可预测的递减规律。c34:T93b,实验分成稳定性、端到端质量、训练 FLOP scaling、测试时 scaling 四块。

稳定性方面，作者先证明旧配方确实容易出现 residual explosion 和 loss spikes，并把问题和 injection 参数的谱范数联系起来。Table 2 是关键证据之一：不稳定模型会学到更危险的 A 参数化，而 Parcae 的约束能显著抑制这种现象。文中还强调，过去一些 looped 模型往往依赖敏感超参和 Post-Norm 才能勉强收敛，Parcae 则把稳定性更多前移到参数化本身。

端到端质量方面，Parcae 与参数量、数据量匹配的 RDMs 和标准 Transformer 比较。结果上，相比 RDM，验证集 perplexity 降低 6.3%。当规模扩展到 1.3B 参数、100B tokens 时，Parcae 在 Core 和 Core-Extended benchmark 上分别比参数匹配 Transformer 高最多 2.99 和 1.18 分，并能匹配约两倍参数量的 Transformer。这是全文最重要的结果之一，因为它说明 looping 不是只在 toy setting 下省参数，而是在较实在的预训练规模上也能换到质量。

训练 FLOP scaling 方面，作者做了 parameter-matched isoFLOP 实验：总训练 FLOPs 固定时，比较把预算用于更多数据，还是用于更多 loop depth。结论是 looping 构成了与参数、数据并列的独立 scaling 轴，最优配方会同时增加数据和 looping，并满足经验幂律。Figure 1 右图是这里的核心图。这个结果的含义不是“looping 总比数据好”，而是“在固定参数下，compute-optimal 解不只是一味加数据”。

测试时 scaling 方面，作者观察到增加循环次数会带来可预测的 loss 下降，形式接近指数衰减并存在不可约下界。也就是说，模型确实学会了可继续 refinement 的动态，但额外 loop 的边际收益会越来越小。论文进一步把训练期和测试期的 scaling law 合在一起，形成统一拟合。这一点对部署很关键，因为它支持按场景做 per-token 或 per-request 的计算分配。

从全文叙述看，消融实验还覆盖了 A 的参数化方式、e normalization、以及 per-sequence depth sampling 对 loss spikes 的影响。值得注意的是，作者不是只报告最终分数，而是把训练曲线稳定性本身当成一等结果来分析，这对做大规模预训练的人更有参考价值。c35:T8f4,The technical story has three parts: stability analysis, stable parameterization, and training-algorithm fixes for stochastic depth.

The model is written as a middle-looped architecture with a prelude module, a recurrent middle block, and a coda module. The recurrent update over the residual stream is cast as a nonlinear time-varying dynamical system. After linearization, the update reduces to a linear time-invariant system, which makes classical stability analysis available. The key empirical observation is that prior looped architectures can learn unstable injection operators with large spectral norms, leading to residual explosion.

Parcae addresses this by parameterizing the continuous-time state matrix A and discretizing it in a controlled way, while constraining A to be a negative diagonal matrix. This gives the recurrent update an inherently contractive character and prevents the hidden state from blowing up across loop iterations. The design is deliberately conservative: a diagonal stable parameterization gives up some flexibility relative to a full matrix, but it is simple, cheap, and robust enough for large-scale Transformer training.

The paper also identifies two practical sources of loss spikes. First, the conditioning signal e is repeatedly injected across loop steps, so scale drift in e can destabilize deep recurrence. Parcae adds normalization on e to mitigate this. Second, the training objective optimizes expected loss over variable depths. Prior recipes often sample one depth per batch, which creates higher variance and sharper optimization discontinuities. Parcae instead uses intra-batch per-sequence depth sampling, so different sequences in the same batch use different loop counts. This better matches the expectation-over-depth objective and empirically smooths training.

A further strength of the paper is that it connects training-time and inference-time scaling. Under isoFLOP training, it studies how compute should be split between more data and more looping. At test time, it studies how additional loop iterations reduce loss, finding an exponential-decay form with an irreducible floor. The result is a unified view in which recurrence learned during training can be exploited at inference, but with predictable diminishing returns.c36:T98d,The experiments cover stability, end-to-end quality, training-FLOP scaling, and test-time scaling.

On stability, the paper shows that earlier looped recipes indeed suffer from residual explosion and loss spikes, and links this behavior to the learned spectral properties of the injection operator. Table 2 is central here: unstable models learn more dangerous parameterizations, while Parcae’s constrained form suppresses that failure mode. An important practical point is that prior looped models often relied on sensitive hyperparameters and normalization choices such as Post-Norm just to converge; Parcae moves much of the stability burden into the parameterization itself.

On end-to-end quality, Parcae is compared against parameter- and data-matched RDMs and standard Transformers. Relative to RDMs, it reduces validation perplexity by 6.3%. At 1.3B parameters trained on 100B tokens, it outperforms parameter-matched Transformers by up to 2.99 points on Core and 1.18 points on Core-Extended, while matching Transformers roughly twice as large. That is the headline result: looping is not only a toy parameter-saving trick, but can buy real quality at meaningful pretraining scale.

For training-FLOP scaling, the paper runs parameter-matched isoFLOP studies and asks whether extra compute should go into more data or more loop depth. The answer is that looping behaves like an additional scaling axis. FLOP-optimal training increases both data and looping according to empirical power laws. The implication is not that looping dominates data, but that under a fixed parameter budget, the compute-optimal solution is not exhausted by “just add more tokens.”

For test-time scaling, increasing the number of loop iterations yields predictable loss improvements that follow an exponential decay toward an irreducible floor. This suggests that the model learns a genuine iterative refinement process, but one with diminishing returns. The paper then combines training-time and test-time fits into a unified scaling-law view. That is especially relevant for adaptive inference and per-request compute allocation.

The ablations also examine the parameterization of A, normalization of e, and the effect of per-sequence depth sampling on loss spikes. Importantly, the paper treats training-curve stability itself as a first-class result, which makes it more useful for practitioners than papers that only report final benchmark scores.c37:T5e4,This one is worth a close read. The most important part is not the benchmark table but the way the paper reformulates looped Transformers as dynamical systems and then turns that analysis into a trainable architecture.

A good reading order is: Introduction, then the formal definition of the middle-looped architecture in the background section, then the stability analysis. Pay special attention to the step from the nonlinear time-varying system to the linearized LTI view, and to why the spectral norm governs residual explosion. That is the conceptual core of the paper. After that, read the Parcae parameterization carefully: continuous A, discretization, and the negative-diagonal constraint. Several follow-up questions are worth keeping in mind. The negative-diagonal parameterization is stable, but perhaps restrictive; future work could explore low-rank or block-diagonal stable forms. The exponential test-time scaling curve suggests a finite but usable reserve of iterative computation, which connects naturally to latent reasoning, adaptive compute, and early exit. Also, the choice of training-time depth distribution likely shapes the quality/compute Pareto frontier at inference. Key takeaways for foundation-model researchers:
- Capacity/cost allocation: extending Thinker–Talker and putting MoE on both the understanding side and the speech-generation side is a concrete pattern for separating “reasoning capacity” from “low-latency generation capacity”.
- Long-context multimodalization: interleaving audio/video tokens into one sequence with explicit timestamp tokens is a pragmatic way to turn long-horizon multimodal perception into a standard long-context modeling problem.
- Streaming speech as token modeling: codec-based discrete speech units + streaming alignment (ARIA) pushes speech generation closer to LLM-style decoding, which matters for unified training and serving.
Overall, the work shifts the bottleneck from “add another modality encoder” to “representation + alignment + routing + long-context stability”, which is where many omni-modal systems fail in practice.c3a:T753,Qwen3.5-Omni continues the Thinker–Talker split: Thinker performs multimodal perception/reasoning and produces textual/semantic outputs; Talker generates speech conditioned on multimodal context and Thinker outputs, optimized for streaming.

1) Hybrid-Attention MoE on both Thinker and Talker: the central design choice is not MoE per se, but using MoE to scale capacity while keeping inference efficient, and explicitly applying it to the speech-generation stack (Talker), where latency and robustness constraints are tighter.

2) Unified 256k long-context modeling: visual inputs go through a vision encoder; audio goes through AuT. This favors early unification over late fusion, enabling reuse of long-context training recipes.

3) Speech representation for low latency: RVQ codec tokens with a multi-codebook design enable single-frame, immediate synthesis, reducing time-to-first-audio and making speech generation a discrete-token prediction problem compatible with LLM decoding.

4) ARIA for streaming alignment: a decoding-time mechanism that dynamically aligns text units and speech units during streaming generation, targeting common streaming failures (repetitions, dropped content, awkward segmentation) without relying on heavy external alignment/post-processing.

5) End-to-end streaming I/O and agentic behaviors: chunk-wise streaming ingestion in Thinker plus streaming Talker output; built-in turn-taking/semantic interruption, controllable prosody (volume/speed/emotion), and voice cloning. The report also frames the model as a “native omni agent” with WebSearch and FunctionCall, implying training/finetuning includes tool-use trajectories rather than external orchestration only.c3b:T431,This work matters for foundation-model training for three reasons. First, it separates one source of hallucination from others: not missing pre-training knowledge, not inference-time fabrication, but degradation of already acquired knowledge during SFT. That distinction is operationally important for evaluation and for choosing fine-tuning recipes. Second, it proposes two mitigation regimes with clear use cases. If new factual acquisition is unnecessary, factual plasticity should be suppressed; if new factual acquisition is required, output drift should be regularized with self-distillation. Third, the mechanism analysis argues against a simple global-capacity story. Forgetting appears to be driven more by localized representational interference between nearby facts than by running out of storage. That has implications for continual pretraining, data mixture design, entity representation, tokenizer choices, and knowledge editing. The contribution is not just a better regularizer; it is a cleaner decomposition of a common but previously entangled phenomenon.c3c:T96e,The method has three layers. First, the paper builds a controlled setup that separates task learning from factual learning. Following Gekhman et al., it uses SLiCK to determine whether each fact is already known by the base model. SLiCK probes the model under multiple randomized few-shot prompts and classifies facts into HighlyKnown, MaybeKnown, WeaklyKnown, and Unknown. The paper keeps only HighlyKnown and Unknown examples: the former measure forgetting, the latter measure acquisition of new facts. This filtering is important because it removes ambiguity between facts the model never knew and facts it knew but later corrupted.

Second, the paper tests whether reducing factual plasticity reduces forgetting. Motivated by prior work showing that parameter groups play different roles in factual storage and task behavior, the authors freeze selected subsets of parameters during SFT. The key observation is that the model can still learn the downstream task format and behavior while becoming much worse at absorbing new facts, and this reduction in factual plasticity sharply lowers forgetting on old facts. The point is not that freezing is universally optimal, but that it provides a clean intervention showing that task learning and factual writing are not fully coupled.

Third, the paper applies self-distillation as a continual-learning regularizer. During SFT, the current model is trained not only on supervised targets but also to stay close to its own pre-update output distribution, limiting output-distribution drift. This is similar in spirit to KL-based regularization, but the role here is specific: preserve old factual behavior while still allowing new factual acquisition. The mechanism section strengthens this interpretation with synthetic-fact experiments. The authors vary the surface form of new entities: either name-like strings, which are likely to live near existing entities in representation space, or UUID-like identifiers, which are not. If forgetting were mainly due to global capacity limits or generic behavior cloning, both conditions should behave similarly. Instead, forgetting rises strongly with scale for name-like entities, while UUID-based entities induce almost no forgetting even with 1M new facts. This points to representational overlap as the main driver. Self-distillation then works by reducing the drift that would otherwise corrupt nearby held-out facts.c3d:T71f,There are three main empirical results. First, the paper reproduces the core phenomenon: after SFT on Unknown facts, performance on previously HighlyKnown facts drops, showing clear factual forgetting. In the main setup, the forgetting level is around 15%. Second, interventions that suppress factual plasticity, such as freezing selected parameter groups, substantially reduce forgetting while preserving much of the task-learning ability. This is especially relevant for settings like alignment tuning or private-domain adaptation where learning new facts is not the goal. Third, in settings where new factual acquisition is required, self-distillation reduces forgetting from roughly 15% to roughly 3% while still allowing effective learning of the introduced facts. That is the central result of the paper because it shows that stability and plasticity are not forced into a strict either-or choice.

The mechanism experiments are equally important. Using synthetic facts, the paper varies both the scale of new knowledge and the surface form of entity names. Name-like entities cause substantially more forgetting as scale increases, whereas UUID-style entities produce near-zero forgetting even at 1M new facts. This is a strong result because it turns representational proximity into a manipulable variable. The paper also shows that self-distillation reduces representational drift on held-out facts, supporting the claim that its benefit comes from mitigating localized interference rather than simply shrinking updates. The novelty is not self-distillation by itself, but its use as a targeted tool for factual forgetting.

Two main modifications are explored:
1) Merge skipping: during greedy merge selection, skip candidate merges whose R or L falls below thresholds (Rt, Lt). The intuition is that source coverage does not increase up the merge tree, so blocking narrow-source merges early prevents long, highly specific tokens later.
2) Objective/score regularization: adjust the BPE merge scoring so that pairs with narrow source support are de-prioritized (conceptually the opposite of TF-IDF: penalize terms that appear in only a small subset of documents/sources), favoring merges that are frequent and broadly supported across repos/languages.

1) SAB (Sparsity-Aware Batching):
- Lightweight sparsity estimation to approximate how expensive a sample will be under sparse attention.
- Latency-based packing: instead of packing by token count, it packs by predicted execution latency.
- A latency prediction module built via offline profiling that maps (sequence length, sparsity) to real runtime, used by both SAB and DST.
2) DST (workload-aware Dynamic Sparsity Tuning):
- Runtime, layer-level bidirectional sparsity adjustment per microbatch: reduce attention budget for bottleneck microbatches to eliminate stragglers; increase budget for non-bottleneck microbatches to fill PP bubbles and improve accuracy.
- Anchor-guided thresholding to decide adjustment direction and bound step size, aiming to keep training stable while exploring the accuracy–efficiency trade-off.
3) System framing: explicitly targets PP bubble reduction and DP barrier straggler mitigation, and argues length heterogeneity propagates across parallelism dimensions; DST aims to equalize per-layer microbatch latency.c45:T631,The key contribution is Event Tensor: treat synchronization events as first-class tensor objects in the compiler IR. An event represents completion of a set of tiled tasks at (roughly) the SM granularity; organizing many such events into a multi-dimensional tensor yields a compact, structured representation of fine-grained dependencies inside a megakernel.

Why this matters:
1) Structured dependency encoding: instead of scattering semaphores/flags in hand-written code, dependencies become tensor-shaped objects the compiler can analyze and transform.
2) Dynamic-shape support via symbolic dimensions: because Event Tensors look like tensors, they can reuse existing compiler machinery for symbolic shapes, avoiding recompilation/capture for every possible runtime shape.
3) Data-dependent dynamism via index expressions: dependencies that depend on runtime data are expressed as mappings from task coordinates to event coordinates, enabling runtime-resolved dependency tracking while keeping the abstraction uniform.

On top of this IR, the Event Tensor Compiler (ETC) applies scheduling transformations to generate persistent megakernels. It supports a spectrum from fully static scheduling (pre-assign per-SM task queues) to dynamic scheduling (an on-GPU scheduler dispatches ready tasks), and can mix strategies to trade off synchronization overhead vs adaptability/load balance. The novelty is less about inventing semaphores and more about tensorizing synchronization in IR so that previously bespoke megakernel fusion/scheduling techniques become systematic compiler passes.c46:T4d8,CoDIT instantiates contrastive decoding with the post-trained teacher as the expert and its pretrained checkpoint as the amateur.
- Token scoring: at each step, select tokens maximizing log p_post(v|x,y< i) − log p_pre(v|x,y< i), amplifying behaviors introduced by post-training while down-weighting tokens equally likely under both models.
- Stabilization via constraints: the paper notes naive, unconstrained contrastive decoding can overemphasize tokens with extremely low p_pre, harming fluency/relevance; it therefore adopts a constrained variant (e.g., restricting to a high-probability candidate set under the expert / applying probability thresholds). (The provided excerpt cuts off before the exact constraint formulation; the full PDF is needed to specify the precise algorithm and hyperparameters.)
- Chat-vector interpretation: the log-probability difference can be viewed as a text-space projection of the parameter delta θ_post − θ_pre, making the distilled signal usable for any student model regardless of architecture.
- Pipeline: generate (instruction, response) pairs with CoDIT, then SFT students on the resulting dataset; compare against standard teacher decoding and against existing public instruction datasets.c47:T83d,全文主线是“LR 的隐式正则化 → loss landscape/锐度解释 → 与 progressive sharpening/edge of stability 连接”。

(1) 现象层：在相同 SFT loss 约束下比较不同 SFT LR。作者强调不是简单的‘大 LR 训练不收敛’或‘小 LR 欠拟合’，而是把训练推进到相近的 SFT 目标后，仍观察到 OOD 能力显著差异，说明 LR 改变了收敛到的解的几何性质与与 base features 的偏离程度。

(2) 隐式正则化视角：低 LR 的 SFT 具有“贴近初始化”的偏置（更强的 stability），更倾向于在 base 模型附近做小幅、可逆的功能改写；高 LR 更容易跨越 basin/穿越高曲率方向，导致对预训练表征的结构性破坏，从而遗忘。

(3) loss landscape/锐度机制：作者把“遗忘”与“sharpness（Hessian 最大特征值）”联系起来：当 base 模型更尖锐时，同样的 SFT 更新（尤其在 decay 之后的小步长阶段）更容易沿高曲率方向产生不可忽略的功能漂移，或更容易被优化推入与 base 不同的尖锐极小值。论文用 progressive sharpening 的经典结论（训练中 sharpness 增长并在 2/η 附近进入 edge-of-stability 振荡）作为解释框架：预训练后期 LR decay 会抬升可达到的 sharpness 上界/平衡点，使 checkpoint 更尖锐。

(4) 理论支撑：作者在一个对角网络（diagonal-network）/简化可解析模型中展示：在不同 LR 下，优化会偏好不同的参数解（例如更偏向保留某些坐标/特征 vs 更激进地重分配权重），并把这种差异与曲率/锐度联系起来，用以支撑“LR→几何→遗忘”的因果链条。

(5) 连接到 catastrophic overtraining：把 Springer et al. (2025) 的“预训练越久，SFT 后越忘”解释为：预训练越久（尤其伴随 LR decay），checkpoint 越尖锐（progressive sharpening），从而在后续 SFT 中更偏向 plasticity 端，导致更强遗忘；因此 overtraining 不是单纯容量瓶颈或噪声敏感性的黑箱，而是可由 sharpness/LR 动力学刻画的可控现象。c48:T78b,The paper’s argument is a three-step chain: LR-dependent implicit regularization → loss-landscape sharpness explanation → progressive sharpening as the upstream cause of overtraining.

1) Empirical identification under matched SFT loss: the authors compare finetuning runs that reach the same (or comparable) SFT loss but use different learning rates. Despite similar SFT fit, OOD behavior differs substantially, implying LR changes the *type* of solution reached, not merely convergence quality.

2) Implicit regularization view: small-step (low-LR) SFT is biased toward staying near the pretrained initialization, preserving pretrained features/capabilities (stability). Larger steps more readily traverse high-curvature directions and/or jump basins, producing structural feature drift and forgetting (plasticity).

3) Sharpness/landscape mechanism: forgetting is linked to sharpness (top Hessian eigenvalue or related notions). The claim is that sharper pretrained checkpoints are more susceptible to being rewritten by SFT dynamics, especially under schedules that eventually take small steps in a sharp region. The authors ground this in the progressive sharpening literature: during training, sharpness increases until it approaches ~2/η (edge-of-stability threshold), so pretraining LR decay raises the attainable sharpness of later checkpoints.

4) Analytic support via a diagonal-network finetuning model: in a simplified, more tractable setting, they show how different LRs bias optimization toward different parameter configurations, and connect that bias to curvature/sharpness, supporting the causal story “LR → geometry → retention/forgetting.”

5) Explaining catastrophic overtraining: longer pretraining (with LR decay) yields sharper checkpoints; sharper checkpoints sit further toward the plasticity end of the stability–plasticity tradeoff, hence exhibit stronger forgetting after standard SFT.c49:T4e2,The provided full-text excerpt does not include the complete experimental section (tables/figures with model sizes, dataset sizes, LR values, sharpness estimates, and benchmark numbers). To avoid fabricating details, I can only summarize the experiment *structure* and the qualitative findings that are explicitly described:
- Overtraining reproduction: take two pretraining checkpoints t1<t2; after SFT, the later checkpoint yields worse OOD loss/performance despite being better pre-SFT.
- LR intervention: for a fixed checkpoint, vary SFT LR (and likely schedule) while matching final SFT loss; lower LR reduces forgetting, indicating an optimization-path effect beyond capacity or data-fit.
- Mechanism validation: estimate sharpness (Hessian top eigenvalue or proxy) across pretraining; show sharpness increases with training and is tied to LR decay; correlate higher sharpness with greater post-SFT forgetting.
- Toy/analytic alignment: diagonal-network analysis reproduces the LR-dependent solution bias consistent with the sharpness narrative.

Crossing the two axes yields four quadrants: high-entropy/high-divergence (Q1), high-entropy/low-divergence (Q2), low-entropy/high-divergence (Q3: overconfident wrong), and low-entropy/low-divergence (Q4: confident correct). Empirically, Q3 is rare (3–15%) but disproportionately valuable.
The theory defines “importance” via a one-step expected loss decrease objective: under β-smoothness and a token-separable approximation (ignoring cross-token gradient covariance), the optimal per-token weight depends on token-wise gradient statistics. This leads to three key results: (1) an oracle strongly favors high-entropy regions over Q4; (2) any entropy-only score is structurally unable to distinguish Q3 from Q4 (both low entropy), hence misses overconfident errors; (3) incorporating divergence restores coverage. - Task setup: one-step Collatz map T(n)=n/2 if n is even else 3n+1. Inputs/targets are digit sequences in base b, ordered most-significant to least-significant. The encoder reads digits of n; the decoder autoregressively emits digits of T(n). Training uses teacher forcing; evaluation uses greedy decoding, making sequence-level accuracy sensitive to readout quality.
- Early-structure evidence: linear probes on encoder states (notably parity) show that key arithmetic attributes become linearly decodable very early, well before sequence accuracy improves—supporting “structure is present”.
- Causal bottleneck localization:
  1) Encoder transplant: plug a trained encoder into a fresh model with a newly initialized decoder; if grokking accelerates, the encoder already contains usable structure.
  2) Decoder rewind/reset: selectively reinitialize only the decoder during training; if the plateau disappears, the delay is primarily decoder-side.
  3) Decoder transplant harm: transferring a trained decoder can actively impede learning, consistent with the decoder locking into a poor readout strategy that is hard to unlearn.
- Representation/tokenization as inductive bias: sweeping numeral bases reveals that local computability differs by base. In even bases, the n/2 branch is locally computable with minimal lookahead, while 3n+1 requires carry propagation across digits; base choice changes the carry structure and thus the decoder’s effective credit assignment and learnability. Binary is an extreme case where training collapses and does not recover.
- Boundary via transfer: Collatz-trained encoders transfer poorly to GCD prediction, indicating that the learned structure is not a broadly reusable arithmetic primitive in this setting.c4d:T56e,Key experimental details and reported numbers from the full text:

(1) 现象学：两条成功条件
- 条件 A：Thinking-pattern consistency（思维模式一致）。作者用 student 与 teacher 的 top-k token 分布重叠度（overlap ratio）来刻画：如果初始重叠很低，即便 teacher benchmark 更高，OPD 也可能无法把 student 拉到 teacher 分布附近。
- 条件 B：Higher scores ≠ 新知识。即使思维模式一致、teacher 分数更高，如果 teacher 与 student 来自同数据同训练配方、只是 scale 更大，那么从 student 视角看 teacher 分布可能“不可区分”（distributionally indistinguishable），teacher 并没有提供 student 未见过的可迁移信号，OPD 增益会很小。
- 通过 weak-to-strong 的 reverse distillation 进一步验证：OPD 学到的本质是“思维模式/分布形状”，而不是简单地追逐 benchmark 分数。

(2) token 级机制：梯度信号的主承载体是 overlap tokens
- 成功 OPD 的统一签名：在 student 访问到的状态上，student 与 teacher 分布逐步变得更相似：top-k overlap ratio 持续上升；两者 entropy gap 逐渐缩小；重叠 token 集合承载了 97–99% 的联合概率质量。
- 失败 OPD：overlap 停滞、entropy mismatch 从一开始就存在并持续。
- 关键验证：只对“重叠 token 集合”施加监督，效果可匹配完整 top-k 监督，说明 OPD 的有效梯度主要来自重叠集；非重叠部分对优化贡献小或噪声大。

(3) Recipe：两种互补的失败修复策略
- Off-policy cold start：先用 teacher 生成的 rollouts 做一段 SFT warmup，提高初始 overlap，缩小思维模式差距，再切换到 OPD。
- Teacher-aligned prompt selection：用 teacher 后训练数据分布中的 prompts 来做 OPD，使监督集中在 teacher 高概率 token 上，更易对齐；但会导致 student entropy 显著降低（更“尖”/更保守），因此需要与 out-of-distribution prompts 混合以避免过拟合/塌缩。

(4) 稠密监督的成本与长轨迹问题
- reward 质量随 trajectory depth 系统性下降；不稳定性往往从后段 token 开始并向前传播。
- 重要观察：即便“失败 teacher”，其 reward 与 rollout 正确性在全局上仍相关，失败更像是局部优化几何问题：更大的 teacher 可能让 student 附近的 reward landscape 局部变平，导致 token 级梯度虽“方向正确”但幅度/曲率不足以推动策略更新。

整体上，作者把 OPD 从经验技巧提升为可诊断、可修复、可解释的训练算子，并给出一套与 token 分布几何直接对应的指标体系（overlap、entropy gap、probability mass concentration）。c54:T444,For foundation-model training research, the contribution is a rare mechanism-driven account of a widely used post-training primitive:
- It replaces the naive "stronger teacher helps" assumption with two testable distributional requirements (thinking-pattern compatibility and genuine novelty beyond the student’s training exposure), which is directly relevant to scaling, continual distillation, and data/recipe design.

1) Phenomenology: two governing conditions.
(A) Thinking-pattern consistency: student and teacher must have compatible next-token distributions, quantified via top-k overlap ratio. If initial overlap is low, OPD often cannot recover even if the teacher scores higher.
(B) Higher benchmark scores do not imply new transferable knowledge: if teacher and student share the same data and training recipe (only scale differs), they may converge to distributions that are indistinguishable from the student’s perspective, leaving little signal for OPD.
Reverse distillation experiments are used to validate these claims and to argue OPD primarily learns "thinking patterns" (distributional behavior) rather than merely chasing benchmark metrics.

2) Token-level mechanism.
Successful OPD shows a consistent signature on student-visited states: increasing top-k overlap, shrinking entropy gap, and the overlap set capturing nearly all probability mass. Failing runs show stagnant overlap and persistent entropy mismatch.
A key test: supervising only the overlap tokens matches full top-k supervision, implying the overlap set is the main carrier of useful gradients.

3) Practical recipes.
- Off-policy cold start: warm up with SFT on teacher-generated rollouts to raise initial overlap, then switch to OPD.
- Teacher-aligned prompt selection: use prompts from the teacher’s post-training distribution to sharpen alignment on high-probability tokens; mitigate entropy collapse by mixing with out-of-distribution prompts.

4) Cost/instability with depth.
Reward quality degrades with trajectory depth; instability starts at later tokens and propagates backward. Even "failing" teachers provide globally informative reward, suggesting failure is due to local optimization geometry (e.g., a locally flat landscape around the student induced by a larger teacher), not purely reward noise.c56:T43b,Deep-read guide (2–3 hours, aiming to reuse the recipe):

- Conceptual contribution: elevates “teacher consistency” from an implementation detail to a necessary condition, explaining systematic failures when SFT demonstrations come from one model while OPD supervision comes from another. The claim is strong: inconsistency induces an irreducible bias and a suboptimal fixed point even for online OPD, not just offline.
- Practical contribution: Lightning OPD removes the need for parallel teacher serving by caching teacher log-probs offline, reporting ~4× speedup while matching or exceeding standard OPD on reasoning/code benchmarks.
- Broader research lesson relevant to continual learning / self-distillation / RL-pretrain-like pipelines: mixing a data-generation policy and a different token-level supervising policy can bake in objective bias that does not vanish with more compute or data, so “distributional alignment” between generation and supervision matters as much as raw teacher strength.c58:T5bf,1) Empirical motivation: student policies in OPD tend to drift only modestly from the SFT reference (consistent with observations that RL trajectories are largely reweighted SFT trajectories and KL constraints keep policies near the reference), suggesting offline reuse of teacher scores might work.
2) Root-cause analysis: OPD implicitly involves two teachers—an SFT teacher that produced the trajectories used to train the reference policy, and an OPD teacher that provides token-level distribution targets/advantages during distillation. If these differ, the OPD objective becomes biased; the paper argues this bias is irreducible and leads to convergence to a suboptimal fixed point regardless of training length or data scale. Offline OPD is further harmed because the rollout distribution is fixed to the (already mismatched) reference.
3) Lightning OPD (offline OPD done right): choose a single teacher π_T; (i) generate SFT trajectories with π_T and fine-tune the base model to obtain π_ref; (ii) sample rollouts from π_ref and precompute π_T log-probabilities once over these fixed responses; (iii) train the student with OPD using cached teacher scores—no live teacher server.
4) Theory claims: under teacher consistency, Lightning OPD shares the same optimum as standard OPD; the gradient discrepancy remains bounded during training; and the offline objective provides implicit regularization that limits policy drift without an explicit penalty term.c59:T4bb,Built on the Joshi et al. (COLT 2025) PAC model:
- Base hypothesis class F consists of next-token generators f: Σ*→Σ.
- Iterating the apply-and-append operator T times yields a length-T trajectory (the “CoT”) and the final token (the e2e output). This induces derived classes F^{CoT,T} and F^{e2e,T}.
- Learning task: prompts x are drawn i.i.d. from an unknown distribution D; target generator f_*∈F. Training data reveals either (x, f_*^{e2e,T}(x)) or (x, f_*^{CoT,T}(x)), but evaluation is always end-to-end error on the final token.
- Core proof pattern: analyze how complexity blows up when learning the composed/iterated mapping under e2e-only labels (typically via lower-bound constructions where many distinct generators/trajectories alias to the same final outputs on observed samples), versus how full-trajectory supervision enables stepwise identification and yields substantially better (often polynomial-in-T) sample complexity upper bounds.
- The paper also discusses extensions beyond single “correct” outputs (multi-solution reasoning) via more general loss/multilabel viewpoints, which is crucial for mapping the theory to real CoT data where many intermediate chains can be valid.c5a:T932,方法上是“可控数据生成 + 最小可表达架构 + 机制归因/电路分析”的组合。
- 任务与数据：从对称 Dirichlet 分布一次性采样 K 个转移矩阵（固定不变），每个样本是一段长度≤N 的状态序列，训练目标是自回归预测下一个状态分布。K 是训练任务族多样性；因为 K 有限，模型既可能学到对每条链的参数记忆（识别链ID→读出转移），也可能学到对上下文统计的在线估计（对未见链也泛化）。

- Algorithmic strategies/phases:

1）问题形式化：模型输出置信度 p(x)∈[0,1]，校准差 Δ(p)=η(p)−p，其中 η(p)=E[正确|p(X)=p]；考虑 Δ 属于 L-Lipschitz 函数类 F(L)。目标是用 m 个带标签样本估计 ECE（文中以 binned ECE 为例，但结论指向更广的校准误差估计）。
2）关键结论（被动/静态评测）：给出 minimax 风险 R*(m,ε,L)=inf_est sup_{Δ∈F(L)} E|Ĥ−H| 的最优速率为 Θ((L·ε/m)^{1/3})（忽略对数因子），并强调 ε 依赖是此前工作缺失的关键。直觉上：当错误稀有时，校准偏差也变成“稀有事件”，观测到足够多的错误以区分校准函数需要更高样本量；同时 Lipschitz 约束把“局部偏差”扩散到可检测尺度，形成 1/3 指数的非参数估计难度。
3）下界证明：构造两个分布/先验（P0 校准、P1 在 p0=1−ε 附近引入幅度 δ 的失配）使得 ECE 差异可控但 KL 散度也可控；通过 Bretagnolle–Huber 或两先验方法（Lepski et al.）把“不可区分性”转成风险下界。文中还给出在 score-mass 集中于 1−ε 附近时更强的 (Lε/m)^{1/3} 下界，并强调不依赖白噪声渐近等价（附录给出 Brown–Low 等价的替代推导）。
4）上界与可达性：用直方图/分箱估计并选择最优 bin 数 B*≈(L^2 m/ε)^{1/3} 达到同阶速率，完成 minimax 匹配。
5）四个“反直觉”结果：
- 自评无信息：任何不使用真实标签的估计（包括 LLM-as-judge、self-consistency、CoT verification、模型内部信号等）在最坏情形下对校准误差的估计无改进，甚至给出常数级下界（文中表述为 worst-case calibration error ≥1/2），除非白盒访问能把问题约束到低维参数族。
- 相变：当 m·ε≈1 以下，错误样本期望数不足，失配不可检测；大量论文报告的提升落在“验证地板”之下。
- 主动查询：若审计者可选择输入进行测试，minimax 速率提升到 Θ(√(ε/m))，且 Lipschitz 常数 L 消失，说明“输入选择权”能显著降低非参数难度。
- 组合爆炸：K 组件 pipeline 的验证成本呈 Ω(L^K·ε/δ^3) 增长，意味着长链路 agent/CoT/RAG 端到端验证会指数变难，必须分解验证或改变评测结构。c5d:T72a,The work is an information-theoretic/minimax analysis of calibration-error estimation.

1) Main change (Muon2): apply Adam-style adaptive second-moment, element-wise scaling to the momentum matrix before the NS-based orthogonalization. Concretely: form momentum M_t, maintain a second-moment accumulator V_t (EMA of squared signals), compute a preconditioned momentum \tilde{M}_t = M_t / (\sqrt{V_t}+\epsilon) element-wise, then run K NS iterations on \tilde{M}_t to obtain an approximate polar/orthogonal factor Q_t, and update parameters with an additional \sqrt{m/n} learning-rate scaling.
2) Key insight: the practical difficulty in Muon’s polar approximation is not the need for exact orthogonality. The original Muon already tolerates fairly inexact orthogonalization (e.g., mapping singular values only roughly into [1-ε,1+ε] with ε up to ~0.3). The real issue is that the input momentum matrix can be ill-conditioned with an unfavorable singular-value spectrum, slowing NS convergence. Muon2’s second-moment preconditioning empirically improves the spectrum/conditioning, which:
- speeds up NS convergence to a practically sufficient orthogonalization;
- improves directional alignment of the finite-iteration update with the “true” orthogonalized direction.
3) Metric shift: the paper argues that orthogonality error metrics (e.g., \|Q^TQ-I\|) alone do not capture what matters for optimization; directional alignment and finite-iteration utility are more relevant.
4) Muon2-F: a memory-efficient variant using a factorized second-moment preconditioner to avoid storing full second-moment tensors, retaining most of Muon2’s gains under large-scale memory constraints.

This drives low-entropy behavior; in writing, it manifests as high-frequency, formulaic phrasing.

2) Relative information gain decomposition: define a generalist reference policy π_b (pre-finetune) and a specialist policy π_s (SFT on high-quality in-domain data). For each token: log π_s = log π_b + log(π_s/π_b). The log-likelihood ratio ϕ(y_i|s_i)=log(π_s/π_b) captures token-level domain-specific information beyond generic high-frequency preference.

3) TCER reward: directly using log-ratio can be numerically unstable when π_b is tiny, so TCER keeps log π_s as the base reward and adds a gated triviality correction: r_TCER = log π_s(y_i|s_i) + w(y_i|s_i)·ϕ_smooth(y_i|s_i).
